# WP-OSS: Research on block themes for independent creatives

> Initial research: what you can build on native WordPress block themes, who would use each one, and **~310 theme ideas across 31 sectors**, each based on real, live sites.
> Scope: **block themes only** (FSE: `theme.json`, `templates/*.html`, `parts/*.html`, `patterns/*.php`, `styles/*.json`). No classic editor or page builders. Every plugin must be free/OSS, block-native, and essential.
> Audience: small independent users (artists, architects, musicians, makers, tiny studios, micro-shops, local businesses, tradespeople, clinics, clubs, co-ops, collectives, schools, campaigns, individuals), not enterprise.
> Aesthetic: **current (2025–26), hand-crafted, and distinctive.** Art-school and brutalist directions are the house accent, not a uniform. Each idea has its own explicit style brief.

### Ground rules (non-negotiable)
1. **Grounded in reality.** Every idea, template list, pattern, and signature feature comes from real live sites of that type. Each entry cites them ("Real-world basis", "seen on"). Nothing speculative.
2. **Nothing vibe-coded.** See `ANTI-VIBE.md` (263 traits, 53-question sniff test), `ANTI-VIBE-FIELD-STUDY.md` (65 measured AI-built sites, 40 lint rules) and `ANTI-AI-WRITING.md` (writing tells, zero em dashes, `copylint`): no purple gradients, no shadcn-default cards, no pill-badge heroes, no icon-in-a-circle feature grids, no filler marketing copy. Every theme is checked against the sniff test before release.
3. **Explicit style per idea.** A named direction, exact free fonts, hex palette, layout, imagery, motion, and a live example of the style.
4. **Native only.** Block themes (like Automattic's), core blocks first, and a plugin only when it is essential.
5. **Screenshots.** Every reference deep link is captured (desktop + mobile) into `screenshots/NNN-k.jpg`.

## Part 1: What stock WordPress can do in 2026 (no plugins)

This is the base every theme is built on. If core already does something, don't add a plugin for it.

| Capability | Core feature | What it unlocks for these themes |
|---|---|---|
| Whole-site templating | Site Editor, `templates/`, `parts/` | Every page type ships as an editable HTML template |
| Design tokens | `theme.json` (v3): palette, fluid type, spacing scale, shadows, layout widths | The brutalist system: hard grids, raw colour, huge fluid type |
| Theme variations | `styles/*.json` | 3–5 looks per theme (e.g. "Riso", "Blueprint", "Terminal", "Newsprint") |
| Section styles | Block style variations in `theme.json` (6.6+) | Inverted, outlined, and "exposed grid" sections applied per group |
| Patterns | `patterns/*.php`, synced patterns, pattern overrides (6.6+) | The "50+ pre-made blocks" promise. Overrides let a user reuse one case-study layout with new content |
| Starter page patterns | `Block Types: core/post-content` patterns | "New page → pick a layout" modal (About, CV, Pricing, FAQ, Press…) |
| Dynamic lists | Query Loop, Post Template, pagination, "sticky" handling | Works grids, news lists, exhibition archives |
| Lightbox | Image block "Expand on click" (6.4+) | Enlarged work previews without a plugin |
| Custom fields → blocks | Block Bindings API (6.5+, UI 6.7+) | Bind "Year / Medium / Dimensions / Client" meta to Paragraph/Heading/Image/Button blocks |
| Interactivity | Interactivity API (6.5+) | Filters, type testers, cursor-follow previews, countdowns, audio players, all declarative and server-rendered |
| Fonts | Font Library (6.5+), `fontFace` in theme.json | Self-hosted grotesks and monos. No Google calls (GDPR-friendly) |
| Footnotes | Footnotes block (6.3+) | Essays, poets, academics, curators |
| Details/Accordion | Details block. Accordion block landed in 6.9 | FAQ, CV sections, colophons |
| Navigation | Navigation block + overlay | Index-style menus, full-screen overlay menus |
| Media | Cover (video bg), Video, Audio, Embed (Bandcamp, Vimeo, YouTube, SoundCloud, Mixcloud, Spotify) | Reels, discographies, mixes |
| Access control | Password-protected posts/pages | Client proofing, gallery viewing rooms, press areas |
| Time | Post date + Query Loop order | Newsletter/blog/journal |

**Main gap in core:** no custom post types, no meta-based querying in the UI, and no front-end faceted filtering. Those are the only places we need plugins (see Part 2).

**Rule from the WordPress.org theme directory:** themes may not register CPTs or other functionality. Content models live in either (a) one shared `wp-oss-companion` plugin for the whole library, or (b) Secure Custom Fields JSON that ships with each theme. Recommendation: **one small companion plugin** that registers opt-in CPTs (Work, Project, Exhibition, Event, Release, Episode, Book, Case Study, Person, Stockist) plus meta and bindings sources. It also provides 6–10 custom Interactivity-API blocks that the whole library shares.

## Part 2: Essential plugin toolkit (free, OSS, block-native)

Use as few as possible. Each theme lists which of these it needs.

| Need | Plugin | Why this one |
|---|---|---|
| Commerce | **WooCommerce** | Fully block-based cart/checkout, Product Collection, Product Filters, mini-cart, and block templates themes can override. Supports simple/variable/grouped/external/downloadable products |
| Content model (if not using companion) | **Secure Custom Fields** (WordPress.org fork of ACF) | CPTs, taxonomies, fields. Works with Block Bindings |
| Meta/date queries in Query Loop | **Advanced Query Loop** (Ryan Welcher) | "Upcoming vs past" exhibitions, events, and tour dates; order by meta |
| Front-end filtering | **Query Filter** (Human Made) | Taxonomy/post-type filter blocks for Query Loop ("Painting / Drawing / Print") |
| Masonry/mosaic | **Jetpack Tiled Gallery** *or* a theme block style (CSS columns) on Gallery/Post Template | Masonry works grids. Prefer the theme block style to keep zero dependencies |
| Forms | **Jetpack Forms** | Native-feeling contact, commission, and booking-request forms |
| Newsletter / paid posts | **Jetpack Newsletter + Paid Content**, or **MailPoet** | Writers, labels, zines |
| Events & tickets | **The Events Calendar** + **Event Tickets** (RSVP + Woo) | Venues, theatres, supper clubs. Alternative: companion "Event" CPT + Advanced Query Loop for lightweight cases |
| Courses | **Sensei LMS** (Automattic, block-based) | Ateliers, music teachers, online courses |
| Podcast | **Seriously Simple Podcasting** or **PowerPress** | RSS feed + episode blocks |
| Donations | **GiveWP** or Jetpack Donations block | Nonprofits, residencies, artist-run spaces |
| Subscriptions (free) | **Subscriptions for WooCommerce** (WP Swings) or Jetpack recurring payments | Coffee, CSA boxes, zine subscriptions |
| Pickup/delivery dates | WooCommerce Local Pickup (core Woo) + **Order Delivery Date (Lite)** | Bakeries, florists, farm shops |
| Maps | **Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap** | Murals, stockists, food truck spots. No Google API key |
| Code highlighting | **Code Block Pro** | Creative coders, devs |
| Booking | **Cal.com embed** (OSS) or **Simply Schedule Appointments** | Tattoo, music lessons, studios, therapists |
| Age gate | **Age Gate** | Wine, brewery, hot-sauce (sometimes), tattoo |
| Multilingual | **Polylang** | Translators, EU studios |
| Hotel | **MotoPress Hotel Booking Lite** | Guesthouses |
| Theme dev | **Create Block Theme** (Automattic) | Build and export themes from the Site Editor. The main dev tool for this whole project |

## Part 3: The full list of site types (granular)

This is the full list to pick from. The 100 ideas in Part 4 are selected from it. Keep the rest as a backlog to reach "5+ templates per type".

### 3.1 Independent e-commerce: 32 types
1. Illustration / art-print shop

## Part 4: The 310 theme ideas

**How to read each entry**
- **For:** who exactly would use the theme.
- **Templates:** block templates in `templates/`, taken from the page lists of the real sites studied. WooCommerce templates are included when there is a shop.
- **Patterns:** the pre-made block library for that theme, using the words real sites of that type use.
- **Content model:** content types, taxonomies and fields from the `wp-oss-companion` plugin, shown through Block Bindings.
- **Plugins:** only what is essential, from the toolkit in Part 2 unless noted and checked.
- **Signature:** the one feature that makes the theme worth choosing, with a link to the real site where it already works ("seen on").
- **Nice-to-haves:** small, practical touches across buying confidence, trust, conversion, owner tools, local information, seasonal operations, aftercare, community, accessibility and owner quality of life. Recurring ones become shared blocks (Part 5).
- **Real-world basis:** the 3–5 live sites studied to write the entry.
- **Style:** a named direction with exact free fonts (unique display face per theme, see `FONT-REGISTRY.md`), a hex palette, layout, imagery, motion, and a live example of why it is current.
- **Style variations:** three `styles/*.json` variations.
- **Refs:** the 2–3 best deep links to learn from.
- **Screens:** desktop and mobile captures of each Ref, stored in `screenshots/` (click to enlarge). Pages behind bot checks are left out.

Ideas 001–084 were first drafted from memory, then rewritten from scratch against real sites. Every feature that could not be found on a live site was replaced.

### I. Visual art

<a id="001"></a>
#### 001 · Illustrator: Portfolio + Shop (`ink`)
**For:** freelance illustrators who sell prints, publications and the odd original, and take private commissions alongside editorial work.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-work (portfolio) · single-work · taxonomy-work-category (editorial / posters / packaging / books) · page-art-for-sale (originals) · page-commissions · page-about · page-contact · Woo: archive-product (shop with Prints / Publications categories) · single-product · cart · checkout · order-confirmation · 404
**Patterns (~45):** portfolio grid with category links (Editorial · Posters · Packaging · Product · Exhibitions), work caption (client, publication, year), originals-for-sale list (title, medium such as "ballpen and correction fluid", drawing size, paper size, price or RESERVED), "how to buy an original" steps (email title + postal address, pay by request, arrives within 21 days), shop category row (Prints · Publications), product card with "Sold out" label, commission options table (digital print vs painted, size and price range), commission process list (form, contract + 40% deposit, sketch and colour study, final, balance), commission FAQ (sizing, reference photos, copyright), books list with publisher and retailer links, newsletter block, contact with agent line.
**Content model:** `work` CPT (client, publication, year, `print_product_id`); taxonomy `work_category`. Originals are Woo simple products with stock 1 and a "Reserved" status tag.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce, Jetpack Forms.
**Signature:** an "Art for sale" page that lists each original drawing with medium, drawing and paper size, one flat price and a RESERVED state, and explains in three lines how to buy and when it arrives (seen on: [Tom Gauld: Art for Sale](https://www.tomgauld.com/art-for-sale)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Operational/seasonal: "Order by 15 Dec for Christmas delivery" banner with UK / EU / rest-of-world cut-off dates that switches itself off after the last date.
- Buying confidence: print shown at scale beside an A4 sheet, plus a "ships rolled in a tube / flat in board" packing note on every print.
- Conversion helper: "Commissions open / closed" state that swaps the commission form for a waitlist line (process and 40% deposit terms seen on: [Ellen Surrey: Commissions](https://www.ellensurrey.com/commissions)).
- Local & practical: postage-included note by region and "arrives within 21 days" delivery promise (seen on: [Tom Gauld: Art for Sale](https://www.tomgauld.com/art-for-sale)).
- Owner-side quality of life: ready-made commission T&Cs page covering copyright and reproduction rights.
**Real-world basis:** [Tom Gauld: Art for Sale](https://www.tomgauld.com/art-for-sale) · [Tom Gauld: Shop](https://www.tomgauld.com/shop) · [Jean Jullien: Works](https://www.jeanjullien.com/works/) · [Ellen Surrey: Commissions](https://www.ellensurrey.com/commissions)
**Style: Sketchbook grotesk**
- Type: Headings: Bricolage Grotesque 800 (opsz 96) at 88px, tracking 0; body: Bricolage Grotesque 400 (opsz 14) 18px/1.6; captions and prices: Sometype Mono 400 15px
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF (paper), text #151515 (ballpen), accent #E0422F (correction-red, prices and links), surface #F3F1EC (sketchbook), line #CFCBC2
- Layout: 12-col grid; portfolio as a ragged-row grid of mixed aspect ratios with a caption under each; shop as a plain 4-column product list, 0 radius; top nav "Work · Shop · Art for sale · Commissions · About"; home leads with one large recent commission at 8/12 plus a short list of what is for sale at 4/12
- Imagery: flat scans on white, no mockups or frames; process shots of pencil roughs next to finals
- Motion: none on scroll; image opens in the core lightbox; link underline thickens on hover (inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)
- Why it fits now: illustrators are dropping Behance-style grids for plain, fast sites where the drawings do the talking and buying is one email away ([Tom Gauld: Portfolio](https://www.tomgauld.com/portfolio))
**Style variations:** Night desk: #141414 bg, #F2EFE8 text · Blue pencil: #2B4C9B accent on white · Newsprint: #ECE9E1 bg, #111 text
**Refs:**
- [Tom Gauld: Art for Sale](https://www.tomgauld.com/art-for-sale): originals listed with medium, sizes, one price and a RESERVED state; buying instructions in plain words
- [Tom Gauld: Shop](https://www.tomgauld.com/shop): two-category shop (Prints / Publications) with honest "sold out" labels left in place
- [Jean Jullien: Works](https://www.jeanjullien.com/works/): portfolio split into client categories (Editorial, Posters, Packaging, Product) on WordPress, shop kept separate

<a id="002"></a>
#### 002 · Painter: Studio & Available Works (`oil`)
**For:** painters who sell originals directly and through galleries and need a searchable record of their whole output.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-work (all works, filterable) · taxonomy-medium (paintings / drawings / prints / monotypes) · single-work · archive-exhibition · single-exhibition · page-about (CV) · page-journal · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** work index grouped by year, filter panel (medium, subject, series, availability, price range, year), work card (image, title, year), work detail (title, year, medium such as "oil on wood", size in cm and inches, Available / Unavailable), price line or "price on request", sold marker on the listing, exhibitions list (solo / group, venue, dates), CV blocks (education, solo shows, group shows, collections, bibliography), articles and reviews list, journal post, gallery representation line, studio-visit enquiry.
**Content model:** `work` (year, medium, dimensions_cm, dimensions_in, series, subject, price, availability available/unavailable/sold, gallery); `exhibition` (dates, venue, type solo/group). Taxonomies `medium`, `series`, `subject`.
**Plugins:** Query Filter (medium / series / subject / availability), Advanced Query Loop (current vs past exhibitions), Jetpack Forms. WooCommerce optional for works sold direct.
**Signature:** a complete works archive filterable by medium, subject, series, availability, price range and year, where every work page shows size in both cm and inches and a plain Available / Unavailable line (seen on: [Tom Hammick: Paintings](https://tomhammick.com/work/paintings)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Local & practical: dimensions stored once and shown as "25.4 × 20.3 cm / 10 × 8 in" (seen on: [Tom Hammick: Autumn Moon](https://tomhammick.com/work/autumn-moon)).
- Trust & proof: sold works stay online with a "Sold" label and their last price, so the archive doubles as a price record (seen on: [Tom Climent: Paintings](https://tomcliment.com/product-category/paintings/)).
- Content the owner gets for free: one-click CV PDF generated from the exhibitions and collections data, plus a bibliography page (seen on: [Tom Climent: Bibliography](https://tomcliment.com/bibliography/)).
- Conversion helper: "Enquire about this work" form pre-filled with title, year and size, sent to the studio or the representing gallery.
- Accessibility & inclusion: image descriptions on every painting, written by the artist, shown under a "Describe this work" toggle.
**Real-world basis:** [Tom Hammick: Paintings](https://tomhammick.com/work/paintings) · [Tom Hammick: In Home](https://tomhammick.com/work/in-home) · [Tom Climent: Paintings](https://tomcliment.com/product-category/paintings/) · [Tom Climent: Kingdom Map](https://tomcliment.com/product/kingdom-map/) · [Hughie O'Donoghue: Exhibitions](https://www.hughieodonoghue.com/exhibitions2-1)
**Style: Catalogue raisonné**
- Type: Headings: Gloock 400 at 80px; body: Libre Franklin 400 18px/1.6; captions and dimensions: Libre Franklin 500 15px with tabular figures
- Palette: bg #F4F5F5 (cool gallery white, the wall the work hangs on), text #1C1B19, accent #8C2F23 (sold/red-dot oxide, used only for "Sold" and links), surface #ECEAE3, line #C9C5BA
- Layout: 12-col grid; works index as a dense grid grouped under large year headings, filters in a left column at 3/12 on desktop and a drawer on mobile; work page puts the painting at 8/12 and the caption block at 4/12, 0 radius; nav "Work · Exhibitions · Journal · About · Contact"
- Imagery: straight-on, colour-true photographs of each canvas, cropped to the edge of the painting; occasional studio shots at 3:2
- Motion: filter results swap with a 150ms opacity cross-fade; none on scroll; reduced-motion users get an instant swap
- Why it fits now: mid-career painters are building full searchable archives in place of a gallery-style "selected works" page ([Tom Hammick: Paintings](https://tomhammick.com/work/paintings))
**Style variations:** Salon: #2D2A26 bg, #F2EEE6 text · Linen: #EDE8DC bg, #3D3A33 text · Ultramarine: #1F3A8A accent on white
**Refs:**
- [Tom Hammick: Paintings](https://tomhammick.com/work/paintings): year-grouped works archive with medium, subject, series, availability and price filters
- [Tom Hammick: Autumn Moon](https://tomhammick.com/work/autumn-moon): single-work caption with cm and inch sizes and an availability line
- [Tom Climent: Paintings](https://tomcliment.com/product-category/paintings/): WordPress and WooCommerce shop for originals that keeps sold paintings visible with prices

<a id="003"></a>
#### 003 · Fine-Art Photographer: Series & Editions (`silver`)
**For:** photographers who work in long projects, publish photobooks and sell signed, editioned prints.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-project (projects list by year) · single-project (sequenced series) · page-prints (editions) · single-print · page-books · page-calendar (talks, shows) · page-information (bio, CV, press) · page-workshops · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** projects list with year ranges ("GOOD MORNING, AMERICA 2012–2024"), series opening text or epigraph, vertical image sequence with plate captions ("Peter's Houseboat, Winona, MN, 2002"), book block (publisher, year, specs, buy link), print list (title, series, sizes, edition), edition note ("edition of 7 + 2 AP"), "prices on application" line, open-edition print card (8×10 in, fixed price), signed books row, calendar of talks and exhibitions, press list with publication and date, CV sections, workshops list, other-series thumbnail row at the foot of each project.
**Content model:** `project` (years, publisher, book specs); `print` (project, sizes, edition size, APs, price band, status); `event` (date, venue, type).
**Plugins:** WooCommerce (signed books and open editions), Jetpack Forms (print enquiries), Advanced Query Loop (upcoming calendar).
**Signature:** series pages that run as a single vertical sequence of plates, each with a place-and-year caption, closing with the book and "other series" (seen on: [Alec Soth: Sleeping by the Mississippi](https://alecsoth.com/photography/projects/sleeping-by-the-mississippi)); editioned prints are listed "price on application", with prices that step up as an edition sells (seen on: [Mark Power: Prints](https://bookshop.markpower.co.uk/collections/prints)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Buying confidence: each print lists both sizes, paper and edition, with a note that "prices rise as an edition sells" (seen on: [Mark Power: Prints](https://bookshop.markpower.co.uk/collections/prints)).
- Conversion helper: a cheap open-edition tier alongside collector editions (8×10 in, one price) (seen on: [Matt Stuart: Prints](https://www.mattstuart.com/prints)).
- Content the owner gets for free: an Information page that carries bio, collections, exhibitions and a dated press list, reusable as a CV (seen on: [Bryan Schutmaat: Information](https://www.bryanschutmaat.co/information)).
- Community & loyalty: calendar of talks, signings and shows with past events kept below (seen on: [Alec Soth: Calendar](https://alecsoth.com/photography/calendar)).
- Owner-side quality of life: Product and VisualArtwork schema on print pages so edition details show in search.
**Real-world basis:** [Alec Soth: Sleeping by the Mississippi](https://alecsoth.com/photography/projects/sleeping-by-the-mississippi) · [Rob Hornstra: Sochi Singers](https://www.robhornstra.com/stories/sochi-singers) · [Mark Power: Projects](https://www.markpower.co.uk/Projects) · [Mark Power: Prints](https://bookshop.markpower.co.uk/collections/prints) · [Matt Stuart: Prints](https://www.mattstuart.com/prints)
**Style: Darkroom plate list**
- Type: Headings: Author 300 (Fontshare) at 76px, tracking 0; body: Source Serif 4 400 18px/1.65 (opsz auto); plate captions: Source Serif 4 italic 15px
- Palette: bg #FBFBFA, text #111111, accent #5E6B73 (selenium-toned grey-blue, links only, 7.1:1 on bg), surface #EFEFEC, line #D6D6D2
- Layout: single centred image column at 10/12 for sequences, one plate per viewport with caption below-left; projects list as text rows (title left, years right); 0 radius; nav "Projects · Books · Prints · Calendar · Information"
- Imagery: plates never cropped or overlaid; full frame at their native ratio, generous white margins like a book spread
- Motion: none; the only transition is a View Transition cross-fade between project list and project page, disabled under reduced motion
- Why it fits now: photographers are returning to book-like sequencing on the web after years of Instagram grids ([Rob Hornstra: Sochi Singers](https://www.robhornstra.com/stories/sochi-singers))
**Style variations:** Gallery black: #0E0E0E bg, #EDEDED text · Fibre: #F2EFE9 bg, #1A1A1A text · Cyanotype: #1F4E79 accent on white
**Refs:**
- [Alec Soth: Sleeping by the Mississippi](https://alecsoth.com/photography/projects/sleeping-by-the-mississippi): one-plate-at-a-time sequence with place and year captions, book cover first
- [Rob Hornstra: Sochi Singers](https://www.robhornstra.com/stories/sochi-singers): series page that mixes plates with quotes, then book specs, exhibition format and other series
- [Mark Power: Prints](https://bookshop.markpower.co.uk/collections/prints): editioned prints "price on application" with an honest note on how edition pricing steps up

<a id="004"></a>
#### 004 · Wedding & Portrait Photographer (`vow`)
**For:** solo documentary wedding, family and portrait photographers.
**Templates:** front-page · page-weddings (approach + pricing) · page-families · page-portraits · archive-story (wedding stories) · single-story · page-about · page-testimonials · page-gift-vouchers · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** full wedding story post (venue and place in the title, 40–80 images in sequence), story list by venue, coverage price list ("Elope from £400 · Full day from £1,900"), "what's included" list (edited images, online gallery, film add-on), albums block (materials, from price), engagement shoot card, "how booking works" steps (call, contract, non-refundable deposit), delivery timeline (sneak peek in 72 hours, full gallery in about 6 weeks), backup promise paragraph, testimonials as full quotations with date and venue, gift voucher block, date-check enquiry form (date, venue, guest count).
**Content model:** `story` (wedding date, venue, location, suppliers list); taxonomy `venue`. Client galleries stay on the photographer's delivery platform and are linked, not rebuilt.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms, WooCommerce (gift vouchers only, optional).
**Signature:** a pricing page written as a plain price list with "from" prices per coverage length and a clear delivery timeline (sneak peek in 72 hours, private gallery after), in place of package cards (seen on: [Ryan Brenizer: Services](https://ryanbrenizer.com/services/) and [Katherine Ashdown: Weddings](https://katherineashdown.co.uk/weddings/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Operational/seasonal: "Now booking 2027 · 2026 Saturdays full" line driven by a simple year/status list.
- Trust & proof: backup paragraph (dual cards, on-site copy, cloud sync) set as a plain promise (seen on: [Ryan Brenizer: Services](https://ryanbrenizer.com/services/)).
- Conversion helper: gift vouchers for engagement and family sessions (seen on: [Katherine Ashdown: Gift vouchers](https://katherineashdown.co.uk/gift-vouchers/)).
- Care & aftercare: "What happens after the wedding" timeline: sneak peek, full gallery, album design, reprints.
- Local & practical: "No travel fees within the UK" note next to the price list (seen on: [Kevin Mullins: Wedding photographer](https://www.kevinmullinsphotography.co.uk/wedding-photographer-kevin-mullins)).
**Real-world basis:** [Katherine Ashdown: Weddings](https://katherineashdown.co.uk/weddings/) · [Ryan Brenizer: Services](https://ryanbrenizer.com/services/) · [Ryan Brenizer: Central Park Boathouse wedding](https://ryanbrenizer.com/blog/central-park-boathouse-wedding-babi-and-john/) · [Kevin Mullins: Wedding photographer](https://www.kevinmullinsphotography.co.uk/wedding-photographer-kevin-mullins) · [Jonas Peterson: Sicily wedding](https://jonaspeterson.com/gallery/sicily-wedding/)
**Style: Contact-print documentary**
- Type: Headings: Bodoni Moda 500 (opsz 96) at 84px, roman only; body: Figtree 400 18px/1.6; dates and venues: Figtree 600 15px
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #1B1A1F, accent #7A2E3A (wine, links and the enquiry button), surface #F4F0EE, line #D9D2CE
- Layout: stories as full-bleed image sequences broken by pairs of portrait frames; pricing page as a two-column definition list (coverage left, price right) at 7/12; 0 radius on images, 2px on buttons; nav "Weddings · Families · Stories · About · Check your date"
- Imagery: unposed black-and-white and colour mixed as delivered, never retouched for the site; no overlays or text on photos
- Motion: none on scroll; images load with native lazy-loading and a flat #F4F0EE placeholder
- Why it fits now: documentary wedding photographers win work with long honest stories and clear prices, not styled hero slideshows ([Ryan Brenizer: Central Park Boathouse wedding](https://ryanbrenizer.com/blog/central-park-boathouse-wedding-babi-and-john/))
**Style variations:** Film: #F1ECE4 bg, #262320 text · Monochrome: #111 text, #777 lines only · Garden: #3E5B3A accent on white
**Refs:**
- [Katherine Ashdown: Weddings](https://katherineashdown.co.uk/weddings/): coverage tiers with "from" prices, film and album add-ons, gift vouchers (WordPress)
- [Ryan Brenizer: Services](https://ryanbrenizer.com/services/): price range stated in one sentence, 72-hour sneak peek, deposit and backup explained plainly
- [Ryan Brenizer: Central Park Boathouse wedding](https://ryanbrenizer.com/blog/central-park-boathouse-wedding-babi-and-john/): wedding story post titled by venue, the core content unit of the theme

<a id="005"></a>
#### 005 · Sculptor / Installation Artist (`plinth`)
**For:** artists whose work is spatial, time-based, participatory or site-specific.
**Templates:** front-page (text index) · single-work · archive-edition · single-edition · page-books · archive-news · page-exhibitions · page-about (bio, CV) · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** year-grouped text index (year heading, then plain linked titles), work page header (title, year, type such as "walking tours, posters, badges"), commissioner and partner credits, materials and dimensions caption, installation-view sequence, "documentation" image run with photographer credit, editions list (title, year, format, edition size), books list, news feed with category labels (Exhibition · Read · Watch · Listen), exhibitions list (upcoming / past), CV blocks, gallery representation line.
**Content model:** `work` (year, type, materials, dimensions, commissioner, location, collaborators, photographer); `edition` (format, edition size, price, availability); taxonomy `work_type`.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (upcoming vs past exhibitions), Jetpack Forms.
**Signature:** a front page that is only a text index of works grouped under year headings, no thumbnails, each title linking to a full documentation page (seen on: [Oliver Laric](https://oliverlaric.com/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Trust & proof: commissioner, partner and funder credits on every work page as structured fields (seen on: [Ruth Ewan: Dreadnoughts](https://www.ruthewan.com/dreadnoughts/)).
- Conversion helper: small editions section (badges, posters, multiples) that funds the practice (seen on: [Ruth Ewan: Feminist Beer Mats](https://www.ruthewan.com/edition/feminist-beer-mats/)).
- Content the owner gets for free: news feed labelled Exhibition / Read / Watch / Listen that doubles as a press archive (seen on: [Katie Paterson](https://katiepaterson.org/)).
- Accessibility & inclusion: plain-language summary and audio description field on each work, for durational or dark-room pieces.
- Local & practical: "where to see it now" line on public and permanent works, with address and opening times.
**Real-world basis:** [Oliver Laric](https://oliverlaric.com/) · [Ruth Ewan](https://www.ruthewan.com/) · [Ruth Ewan: Dreadnoughts](https://www.ruthewan.com/dreadnoughts/) · [Katie Paterson](https://katiepaterson.org/) · [Lakwena: Work](https://www.lakwena.com/work)
**Style: Plain archive index**
- Type: Headings and index: Archivo 500 (width 100) at 20px for index rows, Archivo 800 (width 62, condensed) at 96px for work titles; body: Archivo 400 18px/1.6; captions: Archivo 400 15px
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #0F0F0F, accent #0038A8 (index links on hover and focus), surface #F2F2F0, line #DADAD6
- Layout: front page is a single left-aligned column at 6/12 with year headings hanging in the left margin; work pages break out to full-bleed installation views between text blocks at 7/12; no cards; 0 radius; nav "Works · Editions · Books · News · About"
- Imagery: documentation photos uncropped at 3:2 and 16:9, video stills with running time in the caption
- Motion: none; hover on index titles only changes colour and underline
- Why it fits now: artists with complex practices are moving to text-first archives that load fast and read like a catalogue ([Oliver Laric](https://oliverlaric.com/))
**Style variations:** Concrete: #E9E8E4 bg, #1A1A1A text · Blueprint: #0038A8 bg, #FFFFFF text · Rust: #9A3B1B accent on white
**Refs:**
- [Oliver Laric](https://oliverlaric.com/): whole practice as a year-grouped list of linked titles, nothing else on the page
- [Ruth Ewan: Dreadnoughts](https://www.ruthewan.com/dreadnoughts/): project page with type, date, commissioner and documentation of a participatory work (WordPress)
- [Lakwena: Work](https://www.lakwena.com/work): works listed by year with location, medium and dimensions for large public pieces

<a id="006"></a>
#### 006 · Ceramicist: Shop Updates & Kiln Openings (`kiln`)
**For:** potters who sell in small batches, online in scheduled shop updates or in person at kiln-opening sales.
**Templates:** front-page · page-shop (Woo shop, open or closed state) · single-product · page-kiln-opening (sale dates) · page-newsletter · page-about (process, training) · page-book or press · page-galleries (stockists and exhibitions) · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** "shop is closed, next update" notice, product card with "Sold out" left visible after a sale, product detail (dimensions, clay body, glaze, dishwasher and oven notes), kiln-opening dates block (dates, opening hours per day), "what to expect" at a kiln opening (tour the workshop, walk inside the kilns), firing-number note, newsletter signup for early notice, stockists list (galleries and shops), exhibitions list, process sequence (throwing, trimming, firing), book or video block, private appointment line.
**Content model:** Woo products plus `firing` meta (firing number, date); `sale_event` (dates, hours, location).
**Plugins:** WooCommerce, MailPoet or Jetpack Newsletter, Advanced Query Loop (next sale event).
**Signature:** a shop that sits in a visible "closed until the next update" state with every sold piece still listed as sold out, while the newsletter promises advance notice of when the shop goes live (seen on: [Florian Gadsby: Pottery Shop](https://www.floriangadsby.com/shop) and [Florian Gadsby: Newsletter](https://www.floriangadsby.com/newsletter)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Operational/seasonal: kiln-opening dates block with per-day hours that hides itself after the last day (seen on: [Mark Hewitt Pottery: Kiln Openings](https://hewittpottery.com/kiln-openings/)).
- Trust & proof: firing number stamped on each pot and shown on its product page (seen on: [Mark Hewitt Pottery: Kiln Openings](https://hewittpottery.com/kiln-openings/)).
- Care & aftercare: care card per product (food safe, dishwasher, microwave, crazing explained) downloadable as a PDF.
- Conversion helper: "notify me when this form is back" on sold-out standard pieces such as mugs and bowls.
- Local & practical: "shop by appointment year round" line with phone number for local buyers (seen on: [Mark Hewitt Pottery](https://hewittpottery.com/)).
**Real-world basis:** [Florian Gadsby: Pottery Shop](https://www.floriangadsby.com/shop) · [Florian Gadsby: Newsletter](https://www.floriangadsby.com/newsletter) · [Mark Hewitt Pottery: Kiln Openings](https://hewittpottery.com/kiln-openings/) · [Ayumi Horie Pottery](https://ayumihorie.com/)
**Style: Glaze-test catalogue**
- Type: Headings: Zodiak 700 (Fontshare) at 84px; body: General Sans 400 (Fontshare) 18px/1.6; measurements: General Sans 500 15px with tabular figures
- Palette: bg #F4F3EF (raw porcelain), text #23211E, accent #2F5E6E (celadon-teal, links and "Add to basket"), surface #E6E2DA, line #C8C1B4
- Layout: shop as a 3-column grid of square product photos with name and price below, sold items dimmed to 60% with "Sold out" text; closed state replaces the button with the next update date; 0 radius on images, 2px on buttons; nav "Shop · Kiln opening · Process · Stockists · Newsletter"
- Imagery: each pot shot on the same neutral board in daylight, one hand-held shot for scale, glaze close-ups at 1:1
- Motion: none on scroll; product image swaps to the hand-held shot on hover with a 150ms cross-fade (not a zoom)
- Why it fits now: studio potters sell out in scheduled drops and build their audience through newsletters and process videos, so the site is quiet between sales ([Florian Gadsby: Pottery Shop](https://www.floriangadsby.com/shop))
**Style variations:** Tenmoku: #3A2418 bg, #F1E9DC text · Ash: #D9D4C7 bg, #2A2724 text · Cobalt: #1D3F8C accent on white
**Refs:**
- [Florian Gadsby: Pottery Shop](https://www.floriangadsby.com/shop): closed shop with all items marked sold out, pointing people to the newsletter
- [Florian Gadsby: Newsletter](https://www.floriangadsby.com/newsletter): signup promising advance notice of when the shop goes live
- [Mark Hewitt Pottery: Kiln Openings](https://hewittpottery.com/kiln-openings/): sale dates with per-day hours, firing number and mailing list for postcards (WordPress)

<a id="007"></a>
#### 007 · Tattoo Studio (`flash`)
**For:** independent tattoo studios with a few residents and regular guest artists.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-artist · single-artist · archive-guest (guest spots) · page-booking (enquiries) · page-faq · page-aftercare · page-getting-here · page-accessibility · page-about · page-shop (optional)
**Patterns (~35):** residents grid (portrait, name, Instagram handle), artist page (portfolio grid, style line, own booking email or link), guest-spot card (name, portrait, "guesting 19–21 November", how to book), "custom tattooing by appointment" line, enquiry form (artist, idea, placement, size, reference images, preferred dates), deposit and cancellation terms, walk-ins policy ("if we have space on the day"), FAQ (cost, age, phone bookings), aftercare steps, getting-here directions from the nearest stations, parking note, accessibility details, events block.
**Content model:** `artist` (resident/guest, handle, booking email, styles, books status open/closed); `guest_spot` (artist, start, end); taxonomy `style`.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (routing to the selected artist's email), Advanced Query Loop (upcoming guest spots), Age Gate (optional).
**Signature:** a guest-artists page where each visiting artist has dates and their own booking route (email or Instagram), next to a residents page (seen on: [Parliament Tattoo: Guest artists](https://parliamenttattoo.com/blogs/guest-artists)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Operational/seasonal: per-artist "books open / closed / opening 1 March" state shown on the residents grid.
- Care & aftercare: aftercare guide page linked from every booking confirmation (seen on: [Parliament Tattoo: Aftercare](https://parliamenttattoo.com/blogs/faqs/tattoo-aftercare)).
- Accessibility & inclusion: access page with step height, doorway widths, quiet times, privacy screens and stim toys (seen on: [Parliament Tattoo: Accessibility](https://parliamenttattoo.com/pages/accessibility)).
- Local & practical: getting-here page that says "don't drive" and gives station-by-station directions (seen on: [Parliament Tattoo: Getting here](https://parliamenttattoo.com/pages/getting-here)).
- Trust & proof: deposit, walk-in and "no bookings by phone" policy stated in the FAQ (seen on: [Frith Street Tattoo: FAQ](https://frithstreettattoo.com/faq/)).
**Real-world basis:** [Parliament Tattoo: Artists](https://parliamenttattoo.com/pages/artists) · [Parliament Tattoo: Guest artists](https://parliamenttattoo.com/blogs/guest-artists) · [Frith Street Tattoo: Jake Cordal](https://frithstreettattoo.com/jake-cordal/) · [Frith Street Tattoo: FAQ](https://frithstreettattoo.com/faq/) · [Seven Doors Tattoo: Enquiries](https://www.sevendoorstattoo.com/enquiries)
**Style: Flash-sheet blackletter**
- Type: Headings: Pirata One 400 at 96px (display only, never below 40px); body: Barlow 400 18px/1.6; labels and dates: Barlow Condensed 600 16px
- Palette: bg #16130F (studio black, a trade reason for dark), text #F1E9D8 (aged flash paper), accent #C8322B (traditional red, links and booking), surface #231F1A, line #4A4238. Light variation available for daytime studios.
- Layout: residents as a 3-column grid of portrait photos with names set large underneath; artist page puts the portfolio at 8/12 and booking details at 4/12 sticky; guest spots as a dated list; 0 radius, 2px red rule under headings; nav "Artists · Guests · Book · Aftercare · Visit"
- Imagery: healed-tattoo photos in daylight, flash sheets scanned flat, no stock skulls or AI renders
- Motion: none on scroll; portfolio opens in the core lightbox
- Why it fits now: studios are moving their booking logic off Instagram DMs to their own sites, with clear policies and access info ([Parliament Tattoo: Accessibility](https://parliamenttattoo.com/pages/accessibility))
**Style variations:** Daylight: #F4EEE2 bg, #1C1A17 text · Sailor: #1E3A5F accent · Jade: #2E6B55 accent on black
**Refs:**
- [Parliament Tattoo: Guest artists](https://parliamenttattoo.com/blogs/guest-artists): dated guest spots with each artist's own booking route
- [Parliament Tattoo: Accessibility](https://parliamenttattoo.com/pages/accessibility): specific, honest access notes for a tattoo studio
- [Frith Street Tattoo: Jake Cordal](https://frithstreettattoo.com/jake-cordal/): WordPress artist page with portfolio grid and direct contact

<a id="008"></a>
#### 008 · Webcomic / Comic Artist (`panel`)
**For:** webcomic creators publishing pages on a schedule, and indie cartoonists who sell prints and books.
**Templates:** front-page (latest page) · single-comic · archive-chapter (chapter index) · taxonomy-chapter · page-archive (all pages) · page-cast · page-about · archive-blog · single-post · page-guest-art · page-store (link-out or Woo)
**Patterns (~35):** comic page with First / Previous / Archive / Random / Next / Last buttons above and below, chapter archive with a cover thumbnail per chapter, "select a page" dropdown with dates, update schedule line ("Updated Tuesdays and Fridays"), author's note under the page, "buy a print of this comic" link, tag list per strip, cast page with character cards, guest-art gallery, bonus content, hiatus notice, store row, RSS and newsletter signup, comments or Discord link.
**Content model:** `comic` CPT (page number, chapter, transcript, alt text, print link); taxonomy `chapter` (cover image, order); taxonomy `comic_tag`.
**Plugins:** none beyond core. Jetpack Newsletter optional; WooCommerce optional for a store.
**Signature:** a reader page with First / Previous / Random / Next / Last buttons that also respond to the left and right arrow keys, backed by a chapter archive with a cover per chapter and a dated page dropdown (seen on: [Sleepless Domain: Archive](https://www.sleeplessdomain.com/comic/archive), arrow keys on [Sleepless Domain](https://www.sleeplessdomain.com/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Operational/seasonal: update schedule in the site header ("Updated Tuesdays and Fridays") and a hiatus notice with return date (schedule seen on: [Strong Female Protagonist](https://strongfemaleprotagonist.com/)).
- Conversion helper: "buy a print of this comic" link on every strip, pointing to the matching product (seen on: [Wondermark: #1591](https://wondermark.com/c/1591/)).
- Accessibility & inclusion: transcript and alt text fields on every page, shown in a details block under the comic.
- Community & loyalty: cast page and guest-art gallery (seen on: [Strong Female Protagonist: Cast](https://strongfemaleprotagonist.com/cast)).
- Owner-side quality of life: "Start from the beginning" and "Read chapter 1" links that stay correct as the archive grows.
**Real-world basis:** [Sleepless Domain: Archive](https://www.sleeplessdomain.com/comic/archive) · [Octopus Pie: Comic 1](https://www.octopuspie.com/comic/1/) · [Wondermark: #1591](https://wondermark.com/c/1591/) · [Strong Female Protagonist: Issue 1, page 1](https://strongfemaleprotagonist.com/issue-1/page-1/) · [Questionable Content](https://questionablecontent.net/)
**Style: Newspaper funnies**
- Type: Headings and logo: Bagel Fat One 400 at 80px; body and author notes: Literata 400 18px/1.6; nav buttons: Literata 700 16px
- Palette: bg #FFFDF6 (newsprint, the physical reason), text #1A1A1A, accent #D7263D (button and link red), surface #F1EBDA, line #1A1A1A (2px panel borders)
- Layout: the comic is the widest element (up to 1000px), navigation buttons as a fixed row of equal boxes with 2px black borders above and below it; blog and notes at 7/12 below; 0 radius; nav "Comic · Archive · Cast · Store · About"
- Imagery: comic pages at native resolution with no cropping; chapter covers at 2:3
- Motion: none; page change is a plain load; keyboard focus shows a 3px red outline on the nav boxes
- Why it fits now: long-running webcomics are leaving platforms like Webtoon and Tapas for their own sites with archives readers can bookmark ([Octopus Pie: Comic 1](https://www.octopuspie.com/comic/1/))
**Style variations:** Night reading: #121212 bg, #EDE6D6 text · Four-colour: #FFD23F accent on newsprint · Blueline: #3A6EA5 accent, #F7F9FC bg
**Refs:**
- [Sleepless Domain: Archive](https://www.sleeplessdomain.com/comic/archive): chapter covers plus a dated page dropdown, the model for the archive template
- [Octopus Pie: Comic 1](https://www.octopuspie.com/comic/1/): WordPress comic page with first / previous / next / random, store link and comments
- [Wondermark: #1591](https://wondermark.com/c/1591/): per-strip tags and a "buy a print of this comic" link (WordPress)

<a id="009"></a>
#### 009 · Muralist / Street Artist (`wall`)
**For:** muralists, sign painters and public artists who take commercial, community and school commissions.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-mural · single-mural · page-map · taxonomy-mural-type (residential / commercial / schools / public) · page-commissions · page-shop (prints) · page-about · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** mural card (photo, title, city, year), mural facts (location, commissioner, festival, year, wall size, status completed), map of murals with pins, "archived" list for murals that are gone, type filters (residential, commercial, schools, public), commission enquiry (wall size, surface, indoor/outdoor, location, deadline), "free quote" line, process photos (wall prep, sketch, painting, finished), festival list, walking-route PDF, print shop row, press list.
**Content model:** `mural` (lat/lng, address, city, year, commissioner, festival, dimensions, status live/archived); taxonomy `mural_type`.
**Plugins:** Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap, Query Filter, Jetpack Forms.
**Signature:** a map and list of every mural where works that no longer exist move into a separate "Archived" section instead of disappearing (seen on: [Street Art Cities: Fanakapan](https://streetartcities.com/artists/fanakapan)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Content the owner gets for free: printable walking-route PDF of murals in one neighbourhood (seen on: [Mural Arts Philadelphia: Tours](https://muralarts.org/tours/)).
- Trust & proof: commissioner and status ("Completed") on every mural page (seen on: [Upfest: Malago Scholar Quarters](https://www.upfest.co.uk/project/malago-scholar-quarters/)).
- Conversion helper: separate entry points for homes, businesses and schools, each with its own photos and "free quote" form (seen on: [Gage Graphics](https://gagegraphics.co.uk/)).
- Buying confidence: wall-size guide and what the client needs to provide (access, scaffold, surface prep).
- Operational/seasonal: "Outdoor walls booked April to October, indoor all year" lead-time note.
**Real-world basis:** [Street Art Cities: Fanakapan](https://streetartcities.com/artists/fanakapan) · [Upfest: Malago Scholar Quarters](https://www.upfest.co.uk/project/malago-scholar-quarters/) · [Mural Arts Philadelphia: Tours](https://muralarts.org/tours/) · [Gage Graphics](https://gagegraphics.co.uk/) · [Walala Studio: Villa Walala](https://www.camillewalala.com/projects/villa-walala)
**Style: Sign-painter's board**
- Type: Headings: Alfa Slab One 400 at 96px; body: Barlow 400 18px/1.6; locations and years: Barlow Semi Condensed 600 16px
- Palette: bg #F5F2EA (primed wall), text #1D1D1B, accent #F2B705 (masking-tape yellow, used as a fill behind labels with black text), second accent #1F5C99 (map pins and links), line #1D1D1B
- Layout: murals as a 2-column grid of large landscape photos with city and year set big underneath; map page full-bleed with a list panel at 4/12; archived murals in a separate list below; 0 radius, 3px black rules; nav "Murals · Map · Commissions · Shop · About"
- Imagery: wide shots showing the whole wall and people for scale, then details; no mockups of murals on fake buildings
- Motion: none on scroll; clicking a list row centres the map pin with a short pan, instant under reduced motion
- Why it fits now: muralists increasingly sell to homes and schools, so sites show real walls at human scale and make quoting easy ([Gage Graphics](https://gagegraphics.co.uk/))
**Style variations:** Night wall: #1B1B1B bg, #F2B705 accent · Chalk: #E9ECEF bg, #343A40 text · Pink primer: #F4C7C3 bg, #1D1D1B text
**Refs:**
- [Street Art Cities: Fanakapan](https://streetartcities.com/artists/fanakapan): artist page with mapped artworks and a separate Archived section for lost works
- [Upfest: Malago Scholar Quarters](https://www.upfest.co.uk/project/malago-scholar-quarters/): single mural page with artist, commissioner and status (WordPress)
- [Gage Graphics](https://gagegraphics.co.uk/): one-person mural business on WordPress with residential, commercial and school work and a free-quote call

<a id="010"></a>
#### 010 · Riso & Printmaking Studio (`drum`)
**For:** risograph studios and small print co-ops that print for clients, run workshops and sell their own stationery and editions.
**Templates:** front-page · page-print-services (with quote form) · page-ink-colours · page-paper-library · page-file-setup (guides and templates) · page-print-simulator · page-workshops · page-membership (print club) · Woo: archive-product / single-product / cart / checkout · page-about · page-contact
**Patterns (~45):** services list (zines, posters, art editions, stationery), ink colour chart (colour name, swatch, notes such as "black is the cheapest"), paper library list (weight, colour, recycled), file setup guide (each layer as greyscale, colour name in filename), downloadable templates and Adobe swatch file, lead-times note, quote request form (quantity, size, colours, paper), price calculator note, workshop dates, print club membership, co-op values statement, shop categories (notebooks, cards, prints), stockists list.
**Content model:** `ink` (name, hex approximation, Pantone reference, surcharge); `paper` (name, weight, colour, recycled yes/no); `workshop` (date, places); Woo products for shop.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce, Jetpack Forms, Advanced Query Loop (upcoming workshops), Subscriptions for WooCommerce (print club, optional).
**Signature:** a print simulator where clients upload each colour layer as greyscale, pick a paper, set transparency per layer and see an approximation of the riso print before ordering (seen on: [RISOTTO: Print Simulator](https://risottostudio.com/pages/print-simulator)). Built as one companion block with canvas multiply blending and the `ink` and `paper` data.
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Buying confidence: printed ink swatch cards and paper sample packs sold in the shop (seen on: [RISOTTO: Ink Swatches](https://risottostudio.com/collections/ink-swatches)).
- Content the owner gets for free: file setup guide and downloadable templates (seen on: [Footprint Workers Co-op: Riso printing](https://www.footprinters.co.uk/colour-riso-printing/)).
- Trust & proof: "we only stock recycled paper" and co-op statement next to the quote form (seen on: [Footprint Workers Co-op](https://www.footprinters.co.uk/)).
- Operational/seasonal: current lead time line ("files in by Wednesday for Friday collection") with a holiday closure notice.
- Community & loyalty: print club membership with back issues (seen on: [RISOTTO: Riso Club membership](https://risottostudio.com/pages/riso-club-membership)).
**Real-world basis:** [RISOTTO: Print Simulator](https://risottostudio.com/pages/print-simulator) · [RISOTTO: Print services](https://risottostudio.com/pages/print-services) · [RISOTTO: Ink Swatches](https://risottostudio.com/collections/ink-swatches) · [Footprint Workers Co-op: Riso printing](https://www.footprinters.co.uk/colour-riso-printing/) · [Footprint Workers Co-op: Get a quote](https://www.footprinters.co.uk/get-a-quote/)
**Style: Riso zine**
- Type: Headings: Syne 800 at 96px; body: Manrope 400 18px/1.6; ink names and codes: Sometype Mono 500 15px uppercase only inside the ink chart
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF (paper), text #1A1A1A (riso black), accent #FF48B0 (fluorescent pink ink), second accent #0078BF (riso blue), line #1A1A1A. Two inks overprint by multiply on hero images, never as gradients.
- Layout: 12-col grid with hard 2px black rules; ink chart as a table of large square swatches with names; services as a list with one leading item; 0 radius; slight 2px mis-registration offset on the logo only; nav "Print with us · Inks · Paper · Workshops · Shop"
- Imagery: real prints photographed flat with visible grain and registration; process shots of drums and masters
- Motion: none on scroll; the simulator updates live as sliders move (the only moving thing on the site)
- Why it fits now: riso studios lean into the process itself, publishing their inks, papers and file guides openly ([RISOTTO: Print services](https://risottostudio.com/pages/print-services))
**Style variations:** Two-ink: #FF665E and #0078BF only · Kraft: #D9C4A3 bg, #1A1A1A text · Mint: #82D8D5 accent on white
**Refs:**
- [RISOTTO: Print Simulator](https://risottostudio.com/pages/print-simulator): layer upload, paper choice and transparency sliders to preview a riso print
- [RISOTTO: Ink Swatches](https://risottostudio.com/collections/ink-swatches): the full ink palette sold as swatches with a downloadable Adobe swatch file
- [Footprint Workers Co-op: Riso printing](https://www.footprinters.co.uk/colour-riso-printing/): ink list, file setup rules and co-op values on a WordPress site

<a id="011"></a>
#### 011 · Generative / Creative-Code Artist (`seed`)
**For:** artists working with code, plotters and long-form generative editions.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-work (with Digital / Physical / Spatial / Index views) · single-work (Gallery + Info) · archive-essay · single-essay (process writing) · page-prints (plotter prints and editions) · page-about · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** works grid with category tabs as links (All · Digital · Physical · Spatial · Index), work card (title, year, "[Series]" marker), outputs grid of numbered iterations (#725, #680, #529), work Info section (statement, edition size, release date, platform link), process essay with code blocks and step images, algorithm diagram, plotter print card (paper, pen, size, edition), exhibition and talks list, workshop listing with participant credits, live sketch embed with a still-image fallback, shop link.
**Content model:** `work` (year, series, category, edition size, platform link, sketch URL, still image); `output` (work, number, image); `essay` (posts with code).
**Plugins:** Code Block Pro, WooCommerce (plotter prints, optional).
**Signature:** a work page split into Gallery and Info, where the Gallery is a grid of numbered outputs from one algorithm (#725, #680…) and Info holds the statement and edition details (seen on: [Tyler Hobbs: Fidenza](https://www.tylerxhobbs.com/works/fidenza)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Content the owner gets for free: process essays with code blocks and step-by-step images, the main way these artists build an audience (seen on: [inconvergent](https://inconvergent.net/)).
- Accessibility & inclusion: every live sketch has a static still and a "stop animation" control, and never autoplays under reduced motion.
- Conversion helper: plotter prints and physical editions sold next to the digital work (seen on: [mattdesl studio shop](https://shop.mattdesl.com/)).
- Trust & proof: edition size, release date and platform link on every generative series.
- Community & loyalty: workshop pages that credit every participant by name (seen on: [Anna Carreras: Collage + code](https://www.annacarreras.com/collage-generatiu/)).
**Real-world basis:** [Tyler Hobbs: Works](https://www.tylerxhobbs.com/works) · [Tyler Hobbs: Fidenza](https://www.tylerxhobbs.com/works/fidenza) · [Art Blocks: Fidenza](https://www.artblocks.io/collection/fidenza-by-tyler-hobbs) · [inconvergent](https://inconvergent.net/) · [Anna Carreras: Collage + code](https://www.annacarreras.com/collage-generatiu/)
**Style: Plotter-sheet mono**
- Type: Headings: Departure Mono 400 at 72px (pixel mono, OFL); body: Mona Sans 400 18px/1.6; code: Departure Mono 400 16px
- Palette: bg #F6F5F1 (plotter paper), text #141414, accent #D2461E (pen-red, links only), surface #EAE8E1, line #BDB9AE
- Layout: works as a tight 4-column grid of square outputs with title and year below; single work puts the outputs grid full-width and Info at 7/12 below; essays at 68ch with code blocks breaking out to 10/12; 0 radius, 1px rules; nav "Works · Writing · Prints · About"
- Imagery: outputs shown flat and uncropped at their true ratio; plotter prints photographed on the bed with pen visible
- Motion: live sketches only run after a click on "Run sketch"; none otherwise
- Why it fits now: after the NFT wave, generative artists are rebuilding personal archives that treat outputs, prints and writing as one body of work ([Tyler Hobbs: Works](https://www.tylerxhobbs.com/works))
**Style variations:** Terminal: #101010 bg, #E8E6E1 text · Blueprint: #10357A bg, #F2F2F2 text · Graph: #FFFFFF bg, #3C7A89 lines
**Refs:**
- [Tyler Hobbs: Fidenza](https://www.tylerxhobbs.com/works/fidenza): Gallery and Info split with numbered outputs from one algorithm
- [Tyler Hobbs: Works](https://www.tylerxhobbs.com/works): works grid filtered by Digital, Spatial, Physical and a text Index
- [Anna Carreras: Collage + code](https://www.annacarreras.com/collage-generatiu/): WordPress project page for a generative workshop with tags, results grid and full credits

#### 012 · Artist-Run Space / Collective (`commons`)
**For:** volunteer-run galleries, project spaces and collectives with a small committee and a membership.
**Templates:** front-page (what's on) · archive-programme (numbered, by year) · single-programme · page-coming-up · page-membership · page-studios · page-opportunities · page-committee · page-access · page-about · page-donate · page-publications
**Patterns (~40):** "What's on" block (title, dates, opening hours, venue), coming-up list, numbered programme archive ("#183 The Prince's Seat, 06/06/2026"), archive filters by category (solo show, members show, events, residencies) and year, exhibition page (text, installation views, credits, funders), membership card (£25 a year, open to anyone, benefits list), opportunities list with deadlines, committee list with roles and tenure note, past committee members, access page, donate block, publications list, mailing list signup.
**Content model:** `programme` (number, start, end, type, artists, curator); taxonomy `programme_type`; `opportunity` (deadline, fee); `person` (role, term).
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (now / next / past by dates), Query Filter (type, year), GiveWP or Jetpack Donations, WooCommerce (membership and publications, optional).
**Signature:** a numbered programme archive where every show gets a running number, date and artist, filterable by category and year, with the current show pulled to the front page as "What's on" (seen on: [OUTPOST: Programme archive](https://www.norwichoutpost.org/programmearchive)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Community & loyalty: membership page with a flat yearly fee and the concrete things members get (members' show, residency, writing commissions) (seen on: [OUTPOST: Membership](https://www.norwichoutpost.org/membership)).
- Trust & proof: committee page with roles, a two-year tenure rule and a list of everyone who served before (seen on: [Generator Projects: Committee](https://www.generatorprojects.co.uk/committee)).
- Accessibility & inclusion: dedicated access page for the venue (seen on: [Generator Projects: Accessibility](https://www.generatorprojects.co.uk/accessibility)).
- Operational/seasonal: "Closed for install, reopens 12 June" notice driven by the gap between two programme dates.
- Content the owner gets for free: funders and credits line on each show, reusable in grant reports.
**Real-world basis:** [OUTPOST: Programme archive](https://www.norwichoutpost.org/programmearchive) · [OUTPOST: Membership](https://www.norwichoutpost.org/membership) · [Generator Projects: Committee](https://www.generatorprojects.co.uk/committee) · [Auto Italia: Projects](https://autoitaliasoutheast.org/projects/) · [Catalyst Arts: Archive](https://www.catalystarts.org.uk/archive)
**Style: Photocopied notice board**
- Type: Headings: Funnel Display 800 at 104px; body: Libre Franklin 400 18px/1.55; programme numbers and dates: Sometype Mono 500 16px
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #111111, accent #FF4F1A (fly-poster orange, used for the current show band), surface #F0F0EE, line #111111
- Layout: front page opens with the current show as a full-width orange band (number, title, dates, hours) then coming-up as a ruled list; archive as a dense table (No. / Title / Artist / Dates / Type); 0 radius, 2px rules; nav "What's on · Archive · Membership · Opportunities · Visit"
- Imagery: installation views at 3:2 shot by members, black-and-white photocopy treatment only on posters for events
- Motion: none
- Why it fits now: artist-run spaces are presenting themselves as open archives of everything they have shown, with membership as the funding model ([OUTPOST: Programme archive](https://www.norwichoutpost.org/programmearchive))
**Style variations:** Green room: #1E5631 band, white text · Carbon: #111 bg, #FFF text, orange numbers · Pastel: #F7E9A0 band, #111 text
**Refs:**
- [OUTPOST: Programme archive](https://www.norwichoutpost.org/programmearchive): numbered shows with dates and artists, filterable by category and year
- [Generator Projects: Committee](https://www.generatorprojects.co.uk/committee): volunteer committee roles, tenure limit and past members listed openly
- [Auto Italia: Projects](https://autoitaliasoutheast.org/projects/): year-grouped project archive with the current show, dates and hours up front (WordPress)

#### 013 · Independent Commercial Gallery (`vitrine`)
**For:** small independent commercial galleries with 8–20 artists, a publishing sideline and an art-fair calendar.
**Templates:** front-page (current exhibition) · archive-exhibition (Current/Future, Past) · single-exhibition (Info, Installation views, Press release) · archive-artist · single-artist · archive-viewing-room · single-viewing-room · page-fairs · page-editions · page-publications · page-news · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** current exhibition hero (artist, title, dates, private view time, address), exhibition page sections (info, installation views, press release PDF), works list with full captions (title, year, medium, dimensions), viewing room (dated, works with "Enquire" buttons, no prices), art-fair card (fair, booth, dates, artists shown), artist page (CV, selected works, exhibitions), editions list (price, "SOLD OUT", "LAST FEW REMAINING"), publications shop, "to buy several prints, email us" note, sustainability statement, address and hours.
**Content model:** `exhibition` (dates, private view, type gallery/fair/offsite, press release file); `artist` (CV file, represented yes/no); `artwork` (artist, year, medium, dimensions, availability); `viewing_room` (open, close, artworks, optional password).
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (current/future vs past), Jetpack Forms (per-work enquiry), WooCommerce (editions and publications).
**Signature:** dated online viewing rooms where each work carries full details and an "Enquire" button instead of a price, closing on a set date, optionally password-protected for collectors (seen on: [Pilar Corrias: Viewing room, Tschabalala Self](https://www.pilarcorrias.com/viewing-room/77-tschabalala-self-quotidian-figures/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Content the owner gets for free: press release PDF and installation-views section on every exhibition (seen on: [Union Pacific: Jason Thompson](https://www.unionpacific.co.uk/exhibitions/jason-thompson/)).
- Operational/seasonal: stock states on editions ("Last few remaining", "Sold out") (seen on: [Union Pacific: Editions](https://www.unionpacific.co.uk/editions/)).
- Trust & proof: sustainability page stating shipping and crating policy (seen on: [Kate MacGarry: Sustainability](https://www.katemacgarry.com/sustainability/)).
- Local & practical: private-view date and time line with address, step-free access and nearest station.
- Conversion helper: per-work enquiry form pre-filled with artist, title and dimensions.
**Real-world basis:** [Union Pacific: Jason Thompson](https://www.unionpacific.co.uk/exhibitions/jason-thompson/) · [Union Pacific: Editions](https://www.unionpacific.co.uk/editions/) · [Kate MacGarry: Exhibitions](https://www.katemacgarry.com/exhibitions/) · [Arcadia Missa: Melike Kara, HUSH](https://arcadiamissa.com/melike-kara-hush/) · [Pilar Corrias: Viewing room, Tschabalala Self](https://www.pilarcorrias.com/viewing-room/77-tschabalala-self-quotidian-figures/)
**Style: White-cube wall label**
- Type: Headings: Switzer 500 (Fontshare) at 72px; body: Switzer 400 18px/1.6; captions and wall labels: Sentient 400 italic (Fontshare) 16px for titles, Switzer 400 15px for details
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #161616, accent #161616 (links underlined, no colour), surface #F5F5F3, line #E0E0DC, one signal #B3261E for "Sold out" only
- Layout: front page is one large installation view at full width with artist, title and dates set small beneath at 6/12 left; exhibition pages as sections in sequence (Info, Installation views, Press release) rather than tabs; 0 radius; nav "Exhibitions · Artists · Fairs · Editions · Publications · Contact"
- Imagery: professional installation photography at 3:2, works photographed straight-on for viewing rooms
- Motion: none; View Transition cross-fade between exhibitions, off under reduced motion
- Why it fits now: small galleries have kept online viewing rooms since 2020 but in a quieter form, as dated, enquiry-only pages next to the physical show ([Pilar Corrias: Viewing room, Tschabalala Self](https://www.pilarcorrias.com/viewing-room/77-tschabalala-self-quotidian-figures/))
**Style variations:** Concrete floor: #E7E6E2 bg, #1A1A1A text · After hours: #151515 bg, #F2F2F2 text · Label red: #B3261E link colour
**Refs:**
- [Pilar Corrias: Viewing room, Tschabalala Self](https://www.pilarcorrias.com/viewing-room/77-tschabalala-self-quotidian-figures/): dated viewing room with full captions and "Enquire" in place of prices
- [Union Pacific: Jason Thompson](https://www.unionpacific.co.uk/exhibitions/jason-thompson/): exhibition page with info, installation views and a press release PDF
- [Union Pacific: Editions](https://www.unionpacific.co.uk/editions/): small editions shop with honest "Last few remaining" and "Sold out" states

<a id="014"></a>
#### 014 · Degree Show / Graduate Catalogue (`class-of`)
**For:** art school graduating classes, student-run shows and course teams publishing a yearly online catalogue.
**Templates:** front-page (this year's catalogue) · archive-graduate (all students, filterable) · taxonomy-programme · single-graduate (profile) · page-visit (show dates, venue, access) · page-events (talks, openings) · page-archive (previous years) · page-submit (student submission) · page-about
**Patterns (~35):** catalogue index with filters (programme, type of work, topic), Thumbnails / List view switch, student card (name, programme, one image), programme page (course statement, students), student profile (project title, statement, images, video, website, Instagram, email), show dates and opening hours block, venue map and access notes, events list, previous-years archive (web catalogues for recent years, PDFs for older ones), per-student subdomain or external link list by cohort, sponsor credits line.
**Content model:** `graduate` (programme, year, project title, statement, media, links, contact consent); taxonomies `programme`, `work_type`, `topic`, `year`.
**Plugins:** Query Filter (programme / type of work / topic), Jetpack Forms or a front-end submission form mapped to a draft `graduate` post, Advanced Query Loop.
**Signature:** a catalogue filterable by study programme, type of work and topic, switchable between Thumbnails and List views, with every past year kept as its own catalogue in an archive (seen on: [KABK Graduation Catalogue](https://graduation.kabk.nl) and [KABK: Catalogue Archive](https://graduation.kabk.nl/archive)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Accessibility & inclusion: shuffled student order on each visit so the same surnames are not always first; alphabetical available as a List option.
- Local & practical: show dates, late openings and step-free access details on a Visit page.
- Content the owner gets for free: one printable PDF catalogue generated from the profiles for the physical show.
- Community & loyalty: previous years kept online, with older years as downloadable PDFs (seen on: [KABK: Catalogue Archive](https://graduation.kabk.nl/archive)).
- Owner-side quality of life: submission form that creates a draft profile each student fills in, reviewed by one staff member before publishing.
**Real-world basis:** [KABK Graduation Catalogue](https://graduation.kabk.nl) · [KABK: Catalogue Archive](https://graduation.kabk.nl/archive) · [RCA 2025: Ceramics & Glass MA](https://2025.rca.ac.uk/school/ceramics-glass-ma/) · [RCA 2025: Mar Villegas Manzano](https://2025.rca.ac.uk/school-of-arts-humanities/ceramics-glass-ma/profile/mar-villegas-manzano/) · [Werkplaats Typografie](https://werkplaatstypografie.org/)
**Style: Year-book poster**
- Type: Headings: Unbounded 800 at 112px for the year and show title, 600 at 40px for programme names; body: Onest 400 18px/1.6; filters and labels: Onest 500 15px
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #0D0D0D, accent set per year (default #0047FF, the year's show colour, links and active filters), surface #F2F2F2, line #0D0D0D
- Layout: front page is the year set huge with show dates and venue, then the catalogue grid directly below; filters as a single row of text links with counts; profile pages at 8/12 media and 4/12 details; 0 radius; nav "Graduates · Programmes · Visit · Events · Archive"
- Imagery: student-supplied images at native ratios, cropped only in the index to 4:5; no stock campus shots
- Motion: none on scroll; filters update results in place via the Interactivity API router with no animation
- Why it fits now: schools now treat the online catalogue as a permanent yearly publication with its own archive, not a one-week microsite ([KABK: Catalogue Archive](https://graduation.kabk.nl/archive))
**Style variations:** Class colour: accent swapped per year · Newsprint: #EFECE6 bg, #111 text · Night show: #0D0D0D bg, #FFFFFF text
**Refs:**
- [KABK Graduation Catalogue](https://graduation.kabk.nl): filters by programme, type of work and topic with thumbnails and list views
- [KABK: Catalogue Archive](https://graduation.kabk.nl/archive): every past year kept, web catalogues for recent years and PDFs for older ones
- [RCA 2025: Ceramics & Glass MA](https://2025.rca.ac.uk/school/ceramics-glass-ma/): programme listing of student profiles built on WordPress

<a id="015"></a>
#### 015 · Artist Residency (`bothy`)
**For:** small rural residencies and retreat studios (5–10 residents at a time) run by a producer and a handful of staff.
**Templates:** front-page · page-residencies (about residencies) · archive-opportunity (current open calls) · single-opportunity · archive-resident (by year × programme) · single-resident · page-facilities · page-visit (location & travel) · archive-news · page-support
**Patterns (~40):** open-call card (image / title / residency dates / "Deadline 26 May"), current-opportunities list, "talk to us before you apply" producer contact block, residency types list (group / open access / partnership), what's-included list (studio, self-catering room, workshop access), facilities sections (historic studios / print studio / workshop / library / wifi), local skills network list (ceramicists, metalworkers, fabricators), residents-by-year listing grouped by programme, resident card (portrait / name / short bio / link), residency pamphlet download, rural access note (nearest station, limited buses), funders row as text credits, support/donate block.
**Content model:** `opportunity` (programme, residency start/end, deadline, fee/stipend text, status open/closed, application PDF); `resident` (year, programme taxonomy, discipline, bio, link); taxonomy `programme`.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (open vs closed by deadline meta), Jetpack Forms (enquiry), GiveWP or Jetpack Donations.
**Signature:** a residents archive grouped first by year and then by programme ("2026 · Interdisciplinary Residency · June"), so alumni can be found by when they came or which strand they joined (seen on: [Hospitalfield: Residents](https://hospitalfield.org.uk/residencies/residents/)). Open calls leave "Current opportunities" automatically once their deadline passes.
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Operational/seasonal: each open call carries residency dates and a deadline, and moves itself to "Past calls" after the deadline (seen on: [Hospitalfield: Opportunities](https://hospitalfield.org.uk/residencies/opportunities/))
- Accessibility & inclusion: an "Easy to Read" version of every open call alongside the full guidelines PDF (seen on: [Rupert: Artist Residency Open Call](https://rupert.lt/artist-residency-open-call/))
- Conversion helper: "Not sure if it's for you? Talk to our producer first" block with a named person and email, placed above the apply button (seen on: [Scottish Sculpture Workshop: Residency](https://www.ssw.org.uk/residency/))
- Local & practical: rural access paragraph (24/7 site access, limited public transport, nearest station) (seen on: [Scottish Sculpture Workshop: Residency](https://www.ssw.org.uk/residency/))
- Content the owner gets for free: facilities page with resources list (library, wifi, local skills network) reusable in funding bids (seen on: [Hospitalfield: Facilities](https://hospitalfield.org.uk/residencies/facilities/))
**Style: Field-station almanac**
- Type: Headings: Young Serif 400 at 72–96px, tracking 0; body: Public Sans 400/18px, line-height 1.6; labels and dates: IBM Plex Mono 500 15px, sentence case
- Palette: bg #EEF0EA (lichen paper), text #1E2621 (peat), accent #2F5D50 (spruce, links and deadlines), surface #DCE2D6, line #9AA597
- Layout: 12-col grid, open calls as a ruled list (date column left at 3/12, text at 9/12), 1px rules, 0 radius; top nav "Residencies · Open calls · Residents · Visit · Support"; home = current open call with photo of the studio, then this season's residents, then the facilities strip
- Imagery: plain daylight photos of studios, rooms and landscape at 3:2; no filters; resident portraits at 4:5 in natural light
- Motion: none on scroll; underline slides in on link hover (transform only) inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference
- Why it fits now: residencies are moving away from glossy arts-centre branding to calm, archival sites that read like a logbook of who came and when ([Hospitalfield: Residents](https://hospitalfield.org.uk/residencies/residents/))
**Style variations:** Moor: #E6E3DA bg, heather #6B4E5E links · Coast: #EAF0F2 bg, sea #1F5A73 accent · Winter: #1E2621 bg, frost #DDE6E0 text
**Real-world basis:** [Hospitalfield: Opportunities](https://hospitalfield.org.uk/residencies/opportunities/) · [Hospitalfield: Residents](https://hospitalfield.org.uk/residencies/residents/) · [Hospitalfield: Facilities](https://hospitalfield.org.uk/residencies/facilities/) · [Scottish Sculpture Workshop: Residency](https://www.ssw.org.uk/residency/) · [Rupert: Former residents](https://rupert.lt/category/residents/former-residents/)
**Refs:**
- [Hospitalfield: Residents](https://hospitalfield.org.uk/residencies/residents/): residents grouped by year then programme; the exact archive structure to copy (WordPress)
- [Hospitalfield: Opportunities](https://hospitalfield.org.uk/residencies/opportunities/): open-call cards that lead with residency dates and deadline, nothing else
- [Scottish Sculpture Workshop: Residency](https://www.ssw.org.uk/residency/): residency types, honest rural-access notes and a named producer to talk to before applying (WordPress)
