### II. Architecture & spatial

<a id="016"></a>
#### 016 · Architecture Studio (`plan`)
**For:** small and medium architecture offices (2–30 people).
**Templates:** front-page · archive-project (numbered index with filters) · single-project · taxonomy-type · page-about (office / people) · page-publications · archive-news · page-careers · page-contact
**Patterns (~50):** numbered project index (No. / Title / Location), filter sidebar (index range 0–99, 100–199…, type, status, location), project card with photo + drawing pair, project list row (year / title / "New!" flag), project facts block (client, location, year, status built/ongoing/unbuilt, collaborators, photographer), drawings sequence (plans / sections / models), collages page, models page, publications list, awards list, people list, job listing, office address with map.
**Content model:** `project` (project number, location, country, year or range, status built/ongoing/unbuilt, client, collaborators, photographer); taxonomies `type` (culture, education, residential, public, adaptive reuse…) and `location`.
**Plugins:** Query Filter (type / status / location filters), Advanced Query Loop (order by project number).
**Signature:** a project index keyed by the office's own project numbers, filterable by number range, type, status (built / ongoing / unbuilt) and location, each card pairing a photo with a drawing (seen on: [OFFICE KGDVS: Projects](https://officekgdvs.com/projects)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Trust & proof: status flag on each project (Built / Ongoing / Unbuilt, or "New!") so the index reads as a live record (seen on: [Assemble: Projects](https://assemblestudio.co.uk/projects))
- Community & loyalty: separate "Collages" and "Models" archives that reuse project images by medium (seen on: [OFFICE KGDVS: Collages](https://officekgdvs.com/collages))
- Content the owner gets for free: publications list with publisher and year, ready for competition submissions (seen on: [Dogma: Books](https://www.dogma.name/books/))
- Owner-side QoL: project number and year bound into the page title and OG image, so shared links carry the reference
- Local & practical: office address block with a static OpenStreetMap tile and "nearest station" line
**Style: Swiss project register**
- Type: Headings: Schibsted Grotesk 700 at 80px, tracking -0.01em; body: Schibsted Grotesk 400/18px; numbers and labels: Martian Mono 400 15px, tabular figures
- Palette: bg #F7F7F4 (tracing paper), text #111111, accent #0047AB (cobalt, links and active filters), surface #ECECE6, line #C8C8C0
- Layout: 12-col grid, filter column fixed at 2/12 on desktop, index at 10/12; hairline rules, 0 radius; nav as a single text line "Projects · Collages · Models · Publications · Office"; home = the full index with the newest project open at the top
- Imagery: photo and drawing side by side at equal height; drawings on white, never tinted; photos uncropped at 4:3 or 3:4
- Motion: filter changes swap the list with a View Transition crossfade (150ms); nothing else moves
- Why it fits now: architects are replacing slideshow homepages with the office's own project register, numbers and all ([OFFICE KGDVS: Projects](https://officekgdvs.com/projects))
**Style variations:** Blueprint: #0B2F5B bg, white text · Concrete: #D9D8D3 bg, black type · Sepia: #F2EBDD bg, #6A3B1E links
**Real-world basis:** [OFFICE KGDVS: Projects](https://officekgdvs.com/projects) · [Assemble: Projects](https://assemblestudio.co.uk/projects) · [Dogma: Projects list](https://www.dogma.name/projects-list/) · [Material Cultures: Index](https://materialcultures.org/index/)
**Refs:**
- [OFFICE KGDVS: Projects](https://officekgdvs.com/projects): numbered project cards (photo + drawing) with number-range, type, status and location filters
- [Assemble: Projects](https://assemblestudio.co.uk/projects): a plain year / title list with type, location and year filters; proof a list beats a grid
- [Material Cultures: Index](https://materialcultures.org/index/): tabular index with category, type and year columns (WordPress)

<a id="017"></a>
#### 017 · Young Practice / Research & Competitions (`section`)
**For:** 1–5-person practices that mix built work, research, teaching, competitions and publishing.
**Templates:** front-page · page-projects-list (chronological, all work) · single-project · archive-research · single-research (report / film / essay) · page-books · page-teaching · page-about · page-contact
**Patterns (~45):** chronological projects list (year / title / short description / status: competition, commission, research, study, exhibition / result: first prize, special mention, shortlisted), "in collaboration with" credit line, project page with long text and numbered image captions (ground floor, first floor, typology diagrams), team credit block, books list (cover / title / publisher, city / year), research report page with PDF download, film embed row, category index (architecture & design / learning & communities / research & policy), teaching unit card, lecture list.
**Content model:** `project` (year, status, result, collaborators, team, location); taxonomy `category` (architecture, research, learning, exhibition); `book` (publisher, city, year, cover, link).
**Plugins:** Query Filter, Advanced Query Loop.
**Signature:** a single reverse-chronological projects list where every entry carries its status and competition result ("Competition, special mention", "Commission", "Research") so built, unbuilt and research work sit side by side (seen on: [Dogma: Projects list](https://www.dogma.name/projects-list/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Trust & proof: competition result stated plainly on each entry (first prize / special mention / shortlisted) (seen on: [Dogma: Projects list](https://www.dogma.name/projects-list/))
- Content the owner gets for free: books page with cover, publisher, city and year, and a "where to buy" link (seen on: [Dogma: Books](https://www.dogma.name/books/))
- Community & loyalty: research outputs split into reports, guides and films, each with a PDF or video (seen on: [Material Cultures: Research](https://materialcultures.org/category/research/))
- Accessibility & inclusion: every drawing gets a caption that says what it shows ("First floor, housing") so the page works read aloud (seen on: [Dogma: Blue Ark](https://www.dogma.name/project/blue-ark/))
- Owner-side QoL: footnotes block enabled on research posts for citations
**Style: Academic broadsheet**
- Type: Headings: Merriweather 500 (opsz 144) at 84px; body: Newsreader Text 400/19px, line-height 1.6; labels and years: Fragment Mono 400 15px
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #1A1A1A, accent #9B1C1C (oxblood, links and results), surface #F3F1EE, line #D0CCC6
- Layout: 12-col; list rows with the year hanging in the left margin (2/12), text at 7/12, status right-aligned; long texts at 66ch with captions hanging in the margin; nav "Projects · Books · Research · Teaching · About"
- Imagery: drawings and model photos on white, black-and-white archival images allowed; 4:3 and square only
- Motion: none; print stylesheet for project pages
- Why it fits now: young practices publish as much as they build, and sites now look like a publisher's backlist rather than a portfolio ([Dogma: Books](https://www.dogma.name/books/))
**Style variations:** Collage: #EDE6D8 bg, #1F3A93 links · Axo: #F4F4F4 bg, #D1495B accent · Night: #161616 bg, #F0EDE6 text
**Real-world basis:** [Dogma: Projects list](https://www.dogma.name/projects-list/) · [Dogma: Blue Ark](https://www.dogma.name/project/blue-ark/) · [Dogma: Books](https://www.dogma.name/books/) · [Material Cultures: Research](https://materialcultures.org/category/research/) · [Material Cultures: Index](https://materialcultures.org/index/)
**Refs:**
- [Dogma: Projects list](https://www.dogma.name/projects-list/): one chronological list mixing competitions, commissions and research, each with status and result (WordPress)
- [Dogma: Blue Ark](https://www.dogma.name/project/blue-ark/): long project text, captioned drawings and a team credit block
- [Material Cultures: Research](https://materialcultures.org/category/research/): research reports, guides and films as first-class work (WordPress)

<a id="018"></a>
#### 018 · Landscape Architect / Garden Designer (`terrain`)
**For:** landscape and garden design studios, planting designers, community landscape practices.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-project · single-project (place / brief / design) · taxonomy-project-type (landscape / urbanism & research / art) · archive-photographer · page-studio · page-about · page-garden (the studio's own garden or plant library) · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** project page in three parts (The Place / The Brief / The Design), facts block (location, client, duration, status, collaborators), image gallery by photographer, project list by type (landscape / urbanism & research / art & fabrication), photographer credit and photographer archive, garden areas list (courtyard, meadows & prairies, pond…), plant library intro, visiting note ("open to groups by appointment"), awards list, books & media list, studio page.
**Content model:** `project` (location, client, duration, status, collaborators, lat/lng); taxonomies `project_type` and `photographer`.
**Plugins:** Query Filter, Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (optional project map).
**Signature:** photographer as a taxonomy: every garden credits its photographer, and each photographer has an archive page of the gardens they shot, so the site can be browsed by garden or by photographer (seen on: [Piet Oudolf: Andrew Lawson](https://oudolf.com/photographer/andrew-lawson)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Trust & proof: project status line ("Pre-construction, works start late 2026") next to the dates (seen on: [Dan Pearson Studio: Lambeth Green](https://www.danpearsonstudio.com/lambeth-green/))
- Local & practical: "Open to groups by appointment" visiting note with a booking email on the studio's own garden page (seen on: [Tom Stuart-Smith: The Barn Garden](https://www.tomstuartsmith.co.uk/the-barn-garden))
- Community & loyalty: plant library section (grid of varieties being trialled) as a living resource (seen on: [Tom Stuart-Smith: The Barn Garden](https://www.tomstuartsmith.co.uk/the-barn-garden))
- Content the owner gets for free: books & media page listing the designer's books and talks
- Accessibility & inclusion: botanical names set in italic with common names alongside, marked up with lang="la"
**Style: Botanical plate**
- Type: Headings: Hepta Slab 300 at 88px; body: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 400/18px; plant names: Victor Mono 400 italic 16px
- Palette: bg #F1F2EC (herbarium sheet), text #1F2A1F, accent #5B6B2E (moss, links), surface #E3E6D8, line #B4BAA3
- Layout: asymmetric 5/7 split on project pages (text left, images right, images break to full bleed every third image); list index by type; nav "Projects · Studio · Garden · Books · Contact"
- Imagery: long-lens garden photography, uncropped at 3:2 and 2:3, credited under each image; plans shown on white
- Motion: gallery images crossfade on click only; no scroll effects
- Why it fits now: planting-led practices present gardens as photographic essays credited to named photographers, like a book ([Piet Oudolf: Vitra](https://oudolf.com/garden/vitra))
**Style variations:** Meadow: #F5F0DC bg, #7A5C12 accent · Winter: #E9ECEE bg, #3B4A55 text · Clay: #EFE6DE bg, #6B3F2A links
**Real-world basis:** [Dan Pearson Studio: Lambeth Green](https://www.danpearsonstudio.com/lambeth-green/) · [Piet Oudolf: Vitra](https://oudolf.com/garden/vitra) · [Piet Oudolf: Andrew Lawson](https://oudolf.com/photographer/andrew-lawson) · [Tom Stuart-Smith: The Barn Garden](https://www.tomstuartsmith.co.uk/the-barn-garden) · [Hood Design Studio: Urbanism/Research](https://www.hooddesignstudio.com/urbanism-research)
**Refs:**
- [Dan Pearson Studio: Lambeth Green](https://www.danpearsonstudio.com/lambeth-green/): Place / Brief / Design structure with status and collaborators (WordPress)
- [Piet Oudolf: Andrew Lawson](https://oudolf.com/photographer/andrew-lawson): photographer archive as a second way into the gardens (WordPress)
- [Tom Stuart-Smith: The Barn Garden](https://www.tomstuartsmith.co.uk/the-barn-garden): garden areas, plant library and "groups by appointment" visiting note

<a id="019"></a>
#### 019 · Interior Designer + Shop (`room`)
**For:** interior designers and stylists who also sell their own products or antiques and pieces they source.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-project (interiors) · single-project (room-by-room story with product links) · page-how-we-work · Woo shop (archive-product, taxonomy-product_cat) · single-product · page-trade · page-contact · archive-journal
**Patterns (~50):** project story in room order (entrance → living room → bedrooms) with inline product links, pull quote from press with publication and date, project credits (photography, stylist, completed year, city), "pieces in this project" product row, design philosophy headings (personality / setting / contrast / functionality), enquiry instructions (send floor plan, photos, budget), shop categories (furniture, lighting, fabrics, wallpaper, paint), fabric by composition (linen, wool, mohair, hemp & jute), "the edit" collection tied to one project, trade account page, journal cards.
**Content model:** `project` (location, completed year, photographer, stylist, press quote); Woo products (own designs + antiques); product-to-project relationship via a shared taxonomy `project_edit`.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce, Jetpack Forms.
**Signature:** project stories written room by room with inline links to the products used in each room, so the portfolio doubles as a shop (seen on: [Beata Heuman: Historic Family Home](https://beataheuman.com/blogs/interiors/historic-family-home)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Conversion helper: a project "edit" collection page (products from one finished interior) (seen on: [Rose Uniacke](https://www.roseuniacke.com/))
- Buying confidence: enquiry instructions that say exactly what to send (floor plan, photos, budget) (seen on: [Beata Heuman: How we work](https://beataheuman.com/pages/how-we-work))
- Trust & proof: credits line (photographer, stylist, completed year, city) and one attributed press quote per project (seen on: [Studio Ashby: Hampstead Family Home](https://studioashby.com/project/hampstead-family-home/))
- Buying confidence: fabric sample request (up to five cuttings) on every fabric product
- Owner-side QoL: trade account page with a trade-discount application form
**Style: Decorator's scrapbook**
- Type: Headings: Radio Canada Big 500 at 76px, tracking -0.01em; body: Karla 400/18px; captions: Karla 500 15px
- Palette: bg #F4EFE9 (plaster), text #2B2522, accent #6E2F3A (claret, links), surface #E7DED3, line #C9BBAA
- Layout: project stories in a single 60ch column with images alternating full-width and 2-up; product links styled as underlined text with a small price after; nav "Interiors · Shop · Fabric · Journal · Contact"
- Imagery: warm natural-light room photography, 4:5 portrait for rooms, 1:1 cut-outs on plaster for products
- Motion: none on scroll; product link hover shows a small thumbnail beside the link (transform only)
- Why it fits now: designer-led shops sell through storytelling about real rooms, not catalogue grids ([Beata Heuman: Historic Family Home](https://beataheuman.com/blogs/interiors/historic-family-home))
**Style variations:** Terrazzo: #F2F0EC bg, #2E5E4E accent · Bouclé: #FAF8F5 bg, #3A3A3A text · Lacquer: #1D1B1A bg, #E4C9A8 text
**Real-world basis:** [Beata Heuman: Historic Family Home](https://beataheuman.com/blogs/interiors/historic-family-home) · [Beata Heuman: How we work](https://beataheuman.com/pages/how-we-work) · [Studio Ashby: Hampstead Family Home](https://studioashby.com/project/hampstead-family-home/) · [Studio Ashby: Sister](https://studioashby.com/sister/) · [Rose Uniacke](https://www.roseuniacke.com/)
**Refs:**
- [Beata Heuman: Historic Family Home](https://beataheuman.com/blogs/interiors/historic-family-home): room-by-room story with inline product links and a press pull quote
- [Studio Ashby: Hampstead Family Home](https://studioashby.com/project/hampstead-family-home/): project credits (photographer, stylist) and linked furniture and textiles
- [Studio Ashby: Sister](https://studioashby.com/sister/): a separate shop voice (collection / journal) beside the design practice

<a id="020"></a>
#### 020 · Exhibition & Scenography Designer (`scene`)
**For:** exhibition designers, museum and theatre designers, spatial designers working for institutions.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-project (highlights + all projects) · single-project · page-archive (full list by sector) · page-process · page-studio · page-people · page-awards · page-press · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** project facts block (client/institution, location, year, size m², services: concept / spatial design / graphic design / creative direction), collaborators and credits list (graphic design, AV, lighting, photographer), project story with named sub-sections, exhibit-by-exhibit image captions, status tag (On view / Under construction), highlights grid + all-projects list, sector tags (exhibition, theatre, architecture, graphic design), awards list per project, process page of principles illustrated with project photos (sampling, prototyping, model making), people list.
**Content model:** `project` (institution, location, year, size, services, status on view / closed / under construction, collaborators, photographer, awards); taxonomy `sector`.
**Plugins:** Query Filter, Advanced Query Loop.
**Signature:** an "On view / Under construction / Closed" status on every project, set from opening and closing dates, so the highlights grid can show what visitors can still go and see (seen on: [Kossmanndejong: Our work](https://kossmanndejong.nl/our-work/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Trust & proof: full collaborator credits (AV, graphics, lighting, photographer) on each project (seen on: [Nissen Richards Studio: The American Dream](https://www.nissenrichardsstudio.com/projects/american-dream-pop-to-the-present/))
- Content the owner gets for free: an A–Z archive of every project tagged by sector, for tender submissions (seen on: [Nissen Richards Studio: Archive](https://www.nissenrichardsstudio.com/archive-page/))
- Trust & proof: project facts including size in m² and services provided (seen on: [Kossmanndejong: Micropia](https://kossmanndejong.nl/project/micropia/))
- Local & practical: "On view until 12 Jan" line with a link to the museum's ticket page
- Community & loyalty: process page of principles illustrated with real project photos (seen on: [Nissen Richards Studio: Process](https://www.nissenrichardsstudio.com/process/))
**Style: Museum wall text**
- Type: Headings: Big Shoulders Display 800 at 96px, tracking 0.01em; body: Work Sans 400/18px; object labels: Work Sans 500 15px
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #151515, accent #C8102E (signal red, status and links), surface #F0EEEA, line #BDB8B0
- Layout: highlights as an uneven 2-up/3-up grid (spans vary), project pages with a facts panel pinned left (3/12) and story right (8/12); nav "Work · Archive · Process · Studio · Contact"
- Imagery: installation photography with visitors in frame, 3:2; exhibit close-ups at 1:1; no overlays
- Motion: none by default; project images open in the core lightbox
- Why it fits now: exhibition studios present projects like a museum label (facts first, then story), which reads as expertise to institutional clients ([Kossmanndejong: Micropia](https://kossmanndejong.nl/project/micropia/))
**Style variations:** Blackbox: #111111 bg, #F2F2F2 text · White Room: #FAFAFA bg, #151515 text · Backstage: #2B2B2B bg, #F2B138 accent
**Real-world basis:** [Nissen Richards Studio: The American Dream](https://www.nissenrichardsstudio.com/projects/american-dream-pop-to-the-present/) · [Nissen Richards Studio: Archive](https://www.nissenrichardsstudio.com/archive-page/) · [Nissen Richards Studio: Process](https://www.nissenrichardsstudio.com/process/) · [Kossmanndejong: Our work](https://kossmanndejong.nl/our-work/) · [Kossmanndejong: Micropia](https://kossmanndejong.nl/project/micropia/)
**Refs:**
- [Kossmanndejong: Our work](https://kossmanndejong.nl/our-work/): highlights with institution, city and On view / Under construction status (WordPress)
- [Kossmanndejong: Micropia](https://kossmanndejong.nl/project/micropia/): facts block (client, year, m², services) then a story in named sections
- [Nissen Richards Studio: The American Dream](https://www.nissenrichardsstudio.com/projects/american-dream-pop-to-the-present/): project page with full collaborator credits (WordPress)

<a id="021"></a>
#### 021 · Furniture & Object Maker (`joint`)
**For:** designer-makers and small furniture workshops selling collections and taking commissions.
**Templates:** front-page · Woo shop (archive-product, taxonomy by type: seating / tables & desks / cabinets / mirrors / accessories) · single-product · page-in-stock · page-materials (source book) · page-how-to-commission · page-projects (collaborations / collections) · page-workshop · page-shipping · page-aftercare · archive-news
**Patterns (~45):** product page with timber variants and price per timber, dimensions list (W / D / H / seat height in mm and inches), lead-time block (in stock 1–5 days / made to order 6–12 weeks), care & maintenance, guarantee note, "can be made to your size" line, material source book (timber species / finishes / textures / complementary materials), in-stock collection, commission process (concept / development / fabrication), workshop courses (stool-making), collaborations list, sustainability page.
**Content model:** Woo variable products (timber × finish), product meta (W/D/H mm, seat height, lead time made-to-order, in-stock flag); `material` CPT (species, finish, texture, image) linked to products.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce, Jetpack Forms.
**Signature:** a material source book (British timber species, finishes, textures and complementary materials as a swatch library) that product pages link to for each available timber (seen on: [Sebastian Cox: Material Source Book](https://www.sebastiancox.co.uk/material-source-book)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Operational/seasonal: lead-time block that switches between "In stock, ships in 1–5 days" and "Made to order, 6–12 weeks" per variant (seen on: [Jan Hendzel Studio: Peng Chair](https://www.janhendzel.com/shop/product/peng-chair/))
- Buying confidence: dimensions in mm with inches alongside (seen on: [Jan Hendzel Studio: Peng Chair](https://www.janhendzel.com/shop/product/peng-chair/))
- Care & aftercare: care notes, a 10-year guarantee and a refinishing service on every product (seen on: [Sebastian Cox: Bayleaf Floating Bedside Table](https://www.sebastiancox.co.uk/shop/p/bayleaf-floating-bedside-table))
- Community & loyalty: sell workshop experiences (stool-making courses) as bookable products (seen on: [Jan Hendzel Studio: Seating](https://www.janhendzel.com/shop/seating/))
- Conversion helper: "Visit the workshop to see and feel the timbers" appointment link from the source book
**Style: Workshop drawing sheet**
- Type: Headings: Familjen Grotesk 700 at 72px; body: Libre Caslon Text 400/18px; dimensions and labels: Red Hat Mono 400 15px
- Palette: bg #F5F1EA (planed ash), text #231F1A, accent #3E5641 (oiled green, links), surface #E8E1D5, line #BFB3A0
- Layout: product page split 7/5 (photo left, facts right: timber, dimensions, lead time, price); source book as a swatch grid with square samples and species names; nav "Shop · In stock · Materials · Commission · Workshop"
- Imagery: products on a neutral floor in daylight at 4:5; timber swatches as flat 1:1 macro shots; workshop photos in natural light
- Motion: timber variant switch crossfades the product image (200ms); no other motion
- Why it fits now: makers now lead with material provenance and lead times, which buyers of £2,000 chairs want to see ([Sebastian Cox: Material Source Book](https://www.sebastiancox.co.uk/material-source-book))
**Style variations:** Oak: #EFE7DA bg, #5A3E1B accent · Steel: #E6E8EA bg, #2A2E33 text · Ebonised: #1C1B19 bg, #E9E2D6 text
**Real-world basis:** [Jan Hendzel Studio: Peng Chair](https://www.janhendzel.com/shop/product/peng-chair/) · [Jan Hendzel Studio: Materials](https://www.janhendzel.com/materials/) · [Jan Hendzel Studio: How to commission](https://www.janhendzel.com/how-to-commission/) · [Sebastian Cox: Bayleaf Floating Bedside Table](https://www.sebastiancox.co.uk/shop/p/bayleaf-floating-bedside-table) · [Sebastian Cox: Material Source Book](https://www.sebastiancox.co.uk/material-source-book)
**Refs:**
- [Sebastian Cox: Material Source Book](https://www.sebastiancox.co.uk/material-source-book): timber species, finishes, textures and complementary materials as a browsable library
- [Jan Hendzel Studio: Peng Chair](https://www.janhendzel.com/shop/product/peng-chair/): timber variants with prices, mm/inch dimensions and in-stock vs made-to-order lead times (WordPress + WooCommerce)
- [Sebastian Cox: Bayleaf Floating Bedside Table](https://www.sebastiancox.co.uk/shop/p/bayleaf-floating-bedside-table): production window, care routine and 10-year guarantee on the product page

### III. Design & digital

<a id="022"></a>
#### 022 · UX / Product Designer Case Studies (`case`)
**For:** independent product and UX designers (freelance, fractional or job-hunting) and small UX consultancies.
**Templates:** front-page · page-work (case study list) · single-case-study · page-working-together · page-testimonials · page-about · archive-articles · page-newsletter · page-contact
**Patterns (~45):** case-study facts header (role, company, timeline, team size, platforms, tools), narrative sections with plain headings, "Outcomes" section with real figures and their source, pull quote from a client with name and role, screenshots with captions, related case studies at the end, work list (client / years / one-line summary), short NDA entry ("Details are limited due to NDA"), engagement models (design partner / advisory) with "when this fits", capacity note ("at most three engagements at a time"), testimonials page, articles list, book/newsletter block.
**Content model:** `case_study` (client, role, years, team size, platforms, tools, outcome lines, nda boolean, summary); `testimonial` (name, role, company).
**Plugins:** none required (Jetpack Newsletter optional).
**Signature:** a work list where full case studies and short NDA-limited entries sit side by side: NDA projects show client, years and a one-paragraph summary only, with a flag instead of a link (seen on: [Anton Sten: Work](https://www.antonsten.com/work/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Conversion helper: capacity note ("I take on at most three partner engagements at a time") set from a single site option (seen on: [Anton Sten: Working together](https://www.antonsten.com/working-together/))
- Trust & proof: outcomes section with specific, sourced figures and a named client quote (seen on: [Anton Sten: Summer Health](https://www.antonsten.com/case/summerhealth/))
- Content the owner gets for free: one-page CV/résumé with a print stylesheet and PDF export
- Community & loyalty: related-case links at the foot of each study (seen on: [Adham Dannaway: Creating a lean design system](https://www.adhamdannaway.com/portfolio/creating-a-lean-design-system))
- Accessibility & inclusion: every screenshot gets a caption and a text description of what changed
**Style: Plain-text product notes**
- Type: Headings: Hubot Sans 800 (condensed width 85) at 80px; body: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 400/19px; facts and labels: Commit Mono 400 15px
- Palette: bg #FBFBF8, text #16181A, accent #0A6E5C (teal, links), surface #EFF1EC, line #C9CEC6
- Layout: single 66ch reading column with the facts header as a two-column definition list; screenshots break out to 10/12; nav "Work · Working together · Writing · About"
- Imagery: product screenshots shown flat with a 1px line and no device frames; photos of workshops only if real
- Motion: none; reading-progress indicator only as a thin top rule using scroll-driven animation, off under reduced motion
- Why it fits now: senior designers are moving from dribbble-style grids to text-led case studies that read like memos ([Anton Sten: Summer Health](https://www.antonsten.com/case/summerhealth/))
**Style variations:** Memo: #FFFFFF bg, #16181A text · Blueprint: #EAF1F7 bg, #0B4A7A links · Dim: #1B1D1E bg, #E7E9E4 text
**Real-world basis:** [Anton Sten: Work](https://www.antonsten.com/work/) · [Anton Sten: Summer Health](https://www.antonsten.com/case/summerhealth/) · [Anton Sten: Working together](https://www.antonsten.com/working-together/) · [Adham Dannaway: Creating a lean design system](https://www.adhamdannaway.com/portfolio/creating-a-lean-design-system) · [Clearleft: Virgin Holidays](https://clearleft.com/work/virgin-holidays)
**Refs:**
- [Anton Sten: Summer Health](https://www.antonsten.com/case/summerhealth/): facts header, plain narrative headings and an outcomes section with real numbers
- [Anton Sten: Work](https://www.antonsten.com/work/): full case studies next to short NDA-limited entries
- [Adham Dannaway: Creating a lean design system](https://www.adhamdannaway.com/portfolio/creating-a-lean-design-system): design-system case study with intro facts and related links (WordPress)

<a id="023"></a>
#### 023 · Graphic Designer / Typographer Index (`grid`)
**For:** graphic designers, editorial designers, small design studios working for cultural clients.
**Templates:** front-page (project index) · single-project · archive-keyword · page-about · page-people · page-approach · page-careers · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** project index table (year / client / project / category / location), type-to-filter field above the table, keyword tag list (duotone, wayfinding, catalogue, binding, typeface…), project facts (year, client, location, category, collaborators, photographer), image carousel with counter (1/5), short project text, previous/next project, people list, approach text, careers note.
**Content model:** `project` (year, client, location, collaborators, photographer); taxonomies `category` (identity, exhibition, publication, wayfinding, campaign) and `keyword` (free tags).
**Plugins:** none (index filtering as a small companion Interactivity API block); Query Filter optional.
**Signature:** a project index table (year / client / project / category / location) with a "type to filter" field that narrows rows as you type (seen on: [Kellenberger–White: Project index](https://kellenberger-white.com/project-index/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Community & loyalty: a keyword page (duotone, binding, wayfinding, humour…) as a second way to browse the work (seen on: [Sara De Bondt: Filter](https://saradebondt.com/filter))
- Trust & proof: photographer and fabricator credits on each project (seen on: [Kellenberger–White: Alphabet](https://kellenberger-white.com/project/alphabet/))
- Owner-side QoL: "New" flag on recently added projects that expires after 60 days (seen on: [Sara De Bondt: Filter](https://saradebondt.com/filter))
- Content the owner gets for free: colophon page listing the site's typefaces and credits
- Accessibility & inclusion: the index is a real HTML table with sortable column headers announced to screen readers
**Style: One-size Swiss index**
- Type: everything in Host Grotesk; index and body 400/19px, project titles 700 at 88px on single pages only; no second size in the index; labels: Host Grotesk 500 15px
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #000000, accent #0000EE (default link blue), surface #F2F2F2, line #000000
- Layout: full-width table with 1px black rules, columns year 1/12, client 3/12, project 4/12, category 2/12, location 2/12; nav in one line top-left; no images on the index
- Imagery: project photography shown in a carousel with a "1/5" counter; images uncropped, flat on white
- Motion: none; filter updates the table instantly
- Why it fits now: studios for cultural clients are dropping image grids for a searchable index, which reads as confident and archival ([Kellenberger–White: Project index](https://kellenberger-white.com/project-index/))
**Style variations:** Times Mode: Tinos 19px, #FFFFFF bg · Mono Mode: Martian Mono, #F4F4F0 bg · Night: #000000 bg, #FFFFFF text
**Real-world basis:** [Kellenberger–White: Project index](https://kellenberger-white.com/project-index/) · [Kellenberger–White: Alphabet](https://kellenberger-white.com/project/alphabet/) · [Sara De Bondt: Filter](https://saradebondt.com/filter) · [Sara De Bondt: Liverpool Biennial](https://saradebondt.com/work/liverpool-biennial)
**Refs:**
- [Kellenberger–White: Project index](https://kellenberger-white.com/project-index/): year / client / project / category / location table with type-to-filter (WordPress)
- [Sara De Bondt: Filter](https://saradebondt.com/filter): keyword taxonomy as the main way to browse
- [Kellenberger–White: Alphabet](https://kellenberger-white.com/project/alphabet/): compact project facts, credits and a numbered carousel (WordPress)

<a id="024"></a>
#### 024 · Independent Type Foundry (`glyph`)
**For:** one- to three-person type foundries and open-source type collectives.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-typeface · single-typeface · page-licensing · page-trials · page-in-use · page-custom · page-about · page-help (FAQ / discounts / contact) · cart · checkout
**Patterns (~45):** type tester (editable text, size, line height, tracking, weight/slant axes for variables), styles list with per-style price, family overview ("16 styles, 8 weights"), OpenType features demo (stylistic sets with alternates), glyph set grouped by Unicode block, language support list, details block (designer, release date, version, formats OTF/TTF/WOFF2), in-use gallery, pairing suggestions, licence types (desktop + print / web / video / app + game / social / logo), company-size pricing note, trial request form, donation block for free fonts.
**Content model:** Woo variable downloadable products (licence × company size); `typeface` meta (designer, release date, version, styles count, languages, features, OFL boolean, WOFF2 file for tester).
**Plugins:** WooCommerce.
**Signature:** a typeface page that opens with a live tester and runs styles, OpenType features, glyph set, language support and designer credits in that order (seen on: [Displaay: Fellix](https://displaay.net/typeface/fellix)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Conversion helper: trial fonts via a form (choose families, get a download link by email) (seen on: [Displaay: Trials](https://displaay.net/trials))
- Buying confidence: plain licence explainer by use (desktop, web, video, app, social, logo) with company-size pricing (seen on: [Displaay: Licenses](https://displaay.net/help/licenses))
- Community & loyalty: free OFL families with a "Download" button and an optional donation (seen on: [Collletttivo: Apfel Grotezk](https://www.collletttivo.it/typefaces/apfel-grotezk))
- Trust & proof: "In use" section on each typeface page with real projects (seen on: [Production Type: Big Daily Short](https://productiontype.com/font/big-daily-short))
- Owner-side QoL: "last updated" timestamp on the trials page so buyers know files are current (seen on: [Displaay: Trials](https://displaay.net/trials))
**Style: Specimen sheet**
- Type: UI in Ronzino (Collletttivo, OFL) 400/18px, headings Ronzino 700 at 72px; numbers and prices: Azeret Mono 400 15px; the foundry's own faces shown at 160–320px in testers
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #0D0D0D, accent #E0301E (proof red, active controls), surface #F1F0EC, line #D5D3CC
- Layout: tester full-width at the top, then a strict 12-col grid; styles as ruled rows with price right-aligned; nav "Typefaces · Trials · Licensing · In use · Info"
- Imagery: in-use photographs at 3:2, uncropped; no mock-ups
- Motion: axis sliders update the tester live; no other animation
- Why it fits now: small foundries lead with the tester and a ruled price list, not a marketing hero ([Collletttivo: Apfel Grotezk](https://www.collletttivo.it/typefaces/apfel-grotezk))
**Style variations:** Proof: #F4F1E8 bg, #E0301E marks · Inverse: #0D0D0D bg, #FFFFFF text · Galley: #E9EEF2 bg, #10345C text
**Real-world basis:** [Displaay: Fellix](https://displaay.net/typeface/fellix) · [Displaay: Trials](https://displaay.net/trials) · [Displaay: Licenses](https://displaay.net/help/licenses) · [Collletttivo: Apfel Grotezk](https://www.collletttivo.it/typefaces/apfel-grotezk) · [Production Type: Big Daily Short](https://productiontype.com/font/big-daily-short)
**Refs:**
- [Displaay: Fellix](https://displaay.net/typeface/fellix): tester with weight/slant axes, stylistic sets, glyph sets and tiered family pricing
- [Collletttivo: Apfel Grotezk](https://www.collletttivo.it/typefaces/apfel-grotezk): OFL typeface page with tester, grouped glyph set and donation prompt
- [Production Type: Big Daily Short](https://productiontype.com/font/big-daily-short): styles, specimen, in-use, information and pairing in one page

#### 025 · Small Branding Studio (`studio`)
**For:** 2–15-person branding and graphic design studios.
**Templates:** front-page (selected work) · archive-work (selected / all) · single-work · taxonomy-service · taxonomy-industry · page-studio · page-people · archive-journal · page-shop (optional) · page-contact
**Patterns (~45):** selected / all toggle on the work index, filters by service (brand identity, packaging, editorial, motion, web, signage) and by industry (arts & culture, food & drink, fashion, non-profit…), work card (title + one-line tagline), case study facts (client, year, disciplines), image-led case study with short text, credits (photographer, stylist, partner), next project link, team contact list (named people and roles), new-business email, jobs email, newsletter sign-up, studio shop link.
**Content model:** `work` (client, year, tagline, selected boolean, credits); taxonomies `service` and `industry`; `person` (role, email).
**Plugins:** Query Filter, Jetpack Forms (optional contact).
**Signature:** a work index with a "Selected / All" switch plus two independent filters, Services and Industry, so a food brand can find food work and a museum can find wayfinding (seen on: [Hey Studio: Work](https://heystudio.es/work/), [StudioSmall: Selected projects](https://www.studiosmall.com/projects/selected/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Conversion helper: "Ask us for a PDF of case studies relevant to you" line on the contact page (seen on: [Form: Contact](https://form.uk.com/contact-us/))
- Trust & proof: named team list with roles on the contact page instead of a generic form (seen on: [Hey Studio: Contact](https://heystudio.es/contact/))
- Trust & proof: photographer and stylist credits on each case study (seen on: [StudioSmall: Fforme](https://www.studiosmall.com/project/fforme/))
- Community & loyalty: link to the studio's own shop of prints and objects (seen on: [Hey Studio: Contact](https://heystudio.es/contact/))
- Owner-side QoL: separate new-business and jobs email addresses bound from site options
**Style: Wide-set studio sheet**
- Type: Headings: Anybody 800 (width 120) at 96px; body: Anybody 400 (width 100)/18px; labels: Anybody 500 (width 75) 15px
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #111111, accent #FF5A1F (studio orange, links and active filters), surface #F3F3F1, line #D9D9D6
- Layout: work grid with varied spans (one 8/12 lead card per row, others 4/12), filters as two text rows above the grid; case studies image-first with a 3-line facts block; nav "Work · Studio · Journal · Contact"
- Imagery: client work photographed in use, 4:5 and 16:9; motion work as muted looping MP4 with a play/pause control
- Motion: filters swap the grid with a View Transition; hover on a card only underlines the title
- Why it fits now: studios let the work carry colour and keep the frame plain, with filtering that answers "have you done this before?" ([Hey Studio: Work](https://heystudio.es/work/))
**Style variations:** Mono: #FFFFFF bg, #111111 only · Pastel: #F3E9F0 bg, #1F4E8C links · Night: #121212 bg, #F5F5F0 text
**Real-world basis:** [Hey Studio: Work](https://heystudio.es/work/) · [Hey Studio: Contact](https://heystudio.es/contact/) · [StudioSmall: Selected projects](https://www.studiosmall.com/projects/selected/) · [StudioSmall: Fforme](https://www.studiosmall.com/project/fforme/) · [Form: Contact](https://form.uk.com/contact-us/)
**Refs:**
- [Hey Studio: Work](https://heystudio.es/work/): work filtered by Services and Industry, each card a title and one-liner (WordPress)
- [StudioSmall: Selected projects](https://www.studiosmall.com/projects/selected/): Selected / All switch plus discipline filters
- [StudioSmall: Fforme](https://www.studiosmall.com/project/fforme/): image-led case study with disciplines, credits and next project

#### 026 · Motion Designer / Animator (`frame`)
**For:** motion designers, 2D/3D animators and small animation studios.
**Templates:** front-page (reel + work) · archive-project · single-project · page-play (experiments and free files) · page-process · page-about · page-careers · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** reel hero with sound toggle, project header (client, year, type, duration 0:48), video player, credits grouped by role (creative direction / production / design / 2D animation / music & SFX), "Styleframes & process" gallery, "Style exploration" gallery, short film page with a "Why tell this story?" section, next project link, process stages (message / design / animation / audio), play page with downloadable project files, rigs and scripts, careers list, new-business contact.
**Content model:** `project` (client, agency, year, type, duration, video URL, credits as role → names repeater); `play_item` (file size, format, licence).
**Plugins:** none.
**Signature:** a project page that follows the film with role-grouped credits and then "Styleframes & process" and "Style exploration" galleries (seen on: [Ordinary Folk: Google Doodle Salsa](https://www.ordinaryfolk.co/project/google-doodle-salsa)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Community & loyalty: a "Play" page of free project files, rigs and scripts with licence (CC0) and file size shown (seen on: [Ordinary Folk: Play](https://www.ordinaryfolk.co/play))
- Buying confidence: process page in four plain stages (message, design, animation, audio) (seen on: [Ordinary Folk: Process](https://www.ordinaryfolk.co/process))
- Trust & proof: duration and year shown with every piece (seen on: [Ordinary Folk: Google Doodle Salsa](https://www.ordinaryfolk.co/project/google-doodle-salsa))
- Accessibility & inclusion: captions file (VTT) field on every video, and the reel starts muted with a visible sound toggle
- Content the owner gets for free: a short-film page template for personal films with a statement section (seen on: [Giant Ant: The Last White Rhino](https://www.giantant.ca/the-last-white-rhino))
**Style: Edit-suite timecode**
- Type: Headings: Chivo 900 at 88px; body: Chivo 400/18px; timecodes, durations and credits roles: Chivo Mono 400 15px
- Palette: bg #F2F2EF, text #121212, accent #2E6B3A (edit green, links and play states), surface #E4E4DF, line #BDBDB6
- Layout: work grid of 16:9 stills with varied spans; project page = full-width video, then a 4/8 split (credits left, text right), then galleries; nav "Work · Play · Process · About"
- Imagery: 16:9 video stills and styleframes at native aspect; no mock-ups
- Motion: stills swap to a muted preview loop on hover only where the card links to a film; all previews off under reduced motion
- Why it fits now: animation studios are giving the process (styleframes, explorations, free rigs) as much space as the finished film ([Ordinary Folk: Play](https://www.ordinaryfolk.co/play))
**Style variations:** Cel: #FFF8E7 bg, #D1495B accent · Render: #1A1A1A bg, #E8E8E2 text · Storyboard: #FFFFFF bg, #2B2B2B pencil
**Real-world basis:** [Ordinary Folk: Google Doodle Salsa](https://www.ordinaryfolk.co/project/google-doodle-salsa) · [Ordinary Folk: Play](https://www.ordinaryfolk.co/play) · [Ordinary Folk: Process](https://www.ordinaryfolk.co/process) · [Oddfellows: Material Design 3](https://oddfellows.tv/work/material-design-3) · [Giant Ant: The Last White Rhino](https://www.giantant.ca/the-last-white-rhino)
**Refs:**
- [Ordinary Folk: Google Doodle Salsa](https://www.ordinaryfolk.co/project/google-doodle-salsa): client / year / duration header, role-grouped credits, styleframes and style exploration
- [Ordinary Folk: Play](https://www.ordinaryfolk.co/play): free project files, rigs and scripts as a studio page
- [Oddfellows: Material Design 3](https://oddfellows.tv/work/material-design-3): system-level case study ending in credits and related work (WordPress)

#### 027 · 3D Artist + Asset Store (`mesh`)
**For:** 3D artists and small asset makers selling or giving away models, kits and textures.
**Templates:** front-page · Woo shop (archive-product by category: 3D / 2D / textures / audio) · single-product (asset page) · taxonomy-product_tag · page-licence · page-support (Patreon / donate) · page-about · page-faq
**Patterns (~40):** asset page with clay render and orthographic views (front / side / top), spec block (tris, real-world size, formats Blend / glTF / FBX / USD / OBJ, texture resolutions 1K–8K, texture maps), licence line (CC0) with author credit, download counter, tags and category path, pack page (number of models, included categories, preview scenes), edition tiers (free standard / pro / paid source with engine-ready files), engine support list (Unity / Unreal / Godot), asset card (name, category, series), "support on Patreon" block.
**Content model:** Woo downloadable products with variations (edition tier, texture resolution); product meta (tris, dimensions, formats, maps, engine support, licence, author).
**Plugins:** WooCommerce.
**Signature:** an asset spec sheet on every product: clay render and orthographic views, tri count and real-world size, formats and texture resolution options, licence and author credit (seen on: [Poly Haven: Wooden Display Shelves 01](https://polyhaven.com/a/wooden_display_shelves_01)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Conversion helper: free standard / pro / paid source tiers as Woo variations, with the source tier listing engine-ready files (seen on: [Quaternius: Medieval Village MegaKit](https://quaternius.com/packs/medievalvillagemegakit.html))
- Buying confidence: licence stated in one sentence on every asset ("free to use in personal, educational and commercial projects") (seen on: [Quaternius: Medieval Village MegaKit](https://quaternius.com/packs/medievalvillagemegakit.html))
- Community & loyalty: asset series tags ("City", "Modular", "Mini") to browse matching kits (seen on: [Kenney: 3D assets](https://kenney.nl/assets/category:3D))
- Trust & proof: download count on each asset page (seen on: [Poly Haven: Wooden Display Shelves 01](https://polyhaven.com/a/wooden_display_shelves_01))
- Owner-side QoL: Product and Offer schema with licence URL so assets show up properly in search
**Style: Viewport orthographic**
- Type: Headings: Geologica 700 (sharpness 50) at 80px; body: Geologica 400/18px; specs: JetBrains Mono 400 15px
- Palette: bg #E9E9E6 (clay grey), text #1B1B1B, accent #D6452B (x-axis red, links), surface #F6F6F4, line #B9B9B3
- Layout: asset page with a 7/5 split (renders left, spec block right as a two-column table); shop as a dense grid of square thumbnails with name and series only; nav "Assets · Packs · Licence · Support"
- Imagery: grey clay renders and orthographic views on a flat #E9E9E6 background, 1:1 thumbnails, 16:9 scene previews
- Motion: none; clicking a view thumbnail swaps the main image
- Why it fits now: asset makers win trust with the plain spec sheet (tris, formats, licence) that game developers check first ([Poly Haven: Wooden Display Shelves 01](https://polyhaven.com/a/wooden_display_shelves_01))
**Style variations:** Blender Dark: #232323 bg, #E87D0D accent · Wireframe: #FFFFFF bg, #1B1B1B lines · Low-poly: #EEF3F0 bg, #2F7A5B accent
**Real-world basis:** [Poly Haven: Wooden Display Shelves 01](https://polyhaven.com/a/wooden_display_shelves_01) · [Quaternius: Medieval Village MegaKit](https://quaternius.com/packs/medievalvillagemegakit.html) · [Kenney: 3D assets](https://kenney.nl/assets/category:3D)
**Refs:**
- [Poly Haven: Wooden Display Shelves 01](https://polyhaven.com/a/wooden_display_shelves_01): clay and orthographic previews, tri count, formats, texture resolutions, licence and author
- [Quaternius: Medieval Village MegaKit](https://quaternius.com/packs/medievalvillagemegakit.html): one maker's pack page with free / pro / source tiers and engine support
- [Kenney: 3D assets](https://kenney.nl/assets/category:3D): asset cards with category and series tags

#### 028 · Indie Game Studio (`pixel`)
**For:** 1–10-person game studios and small indie publishers.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-game · single-game · page-press (studio press kit) · archive-news · page-about · page-jobs · page-contact
**Patterns (~45):** game hero with trailer and screenshot carousel, store buttons (Steam wishlist / Switch / itch.io), gameplay pillars as short text sections, press quotes with outlet and score (EDGE 9/10), festival and award laurels as text, screenshot gallery, soundtrack credit, news updates on the game page, full credits list, press kit download with file size, game key request form, studio press page (founders' bios, timeline of releases, logos, awards list, press contact), newsletter sign-up.
**Content model:** `game` (release date, platforms, price, store URLs, trailer URL, press kit zip, press quotes repeater, awards, credits); studio timeline as `milestone` entries.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (key requests), Jetpack Newsletter (optional).
**Signature:** a press block on every game page: press kit zip with its file size, a key request form for press and creators, and a press@ contact (seen on: [Finji: Usual June](https://finji.co/games/usualjune/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Trust & proof: press quotes with outlet, issue and score (seen on: [inkle: A Highland Song](https://www.inklestudios.com/a-highland-song))
- Content the owner gets for free: studio press page with founder bios, a dated release timeline and logo downloads (seen on: [inkle: Press](https://www.inklestudios.com/press))
- Operational/seasonal: release date line that switches from "Wishlist on Steam" to "Buy on Steam" on launch day
- Community & loyalty: news updates listed on the game page itself (seen on: [Finji: Usual June](https://finji.co/games/usualjune/))
- Accessibility & inclusion: accessibility features list per game (subtitles, remapping, colour options)
**Style: Cartridge label**
- Type: Headings: Pixelify Sans 700 at 72px (UI and headings only); body: Lexend 400/18px; platform and date labels: Tiny5 15px
- Palette: bg #F3F0E6 (cartridge label paper), text #1C1A17, accent #D2402A (start-button red, links and store buttons), surface #E6E0CF, line #1C1A17
- Layout: game page with the trailer full-width, then alternating 5/7 text-image rows for gameplay pillars; press quotes as a two-column list, not a carousel; nav "Games · News · Press · About · Jobs"
- Imagery: native-resolution screenshots at 16:9 with pixel art scaled by integer steps (image-rendering: pixelated); key art uncropped
- Motion: none on scroll; trailer plays on click; GIF strip pauses under reduced motion
- Why it fits now: small studios keep the game art centre and build the rest like a press sheet journalists can scan ([Finji: Usual June](https://finji.co/games/usualjune/))
**Style variations:** CRT: #101410 bg, #E8F0E0 text · Game Boy: #C4CFA1 bg, #1F3B1F text · Arcade: #FFFFFF bg, #1B4DD1 links
**Real-world basis:** [Finji: Usual June](https://finji.co/games/usualjune/) · [inkle: Press](https://www.inklestudios.com/press) · [inkle: A Highland Song](https://www.inklestudios.com/a-highland-song) · [presskit()](https://dopresskit.com/)
**Refs:**
- [Finji: Usual June](https://finji.co/games/usualjune/): game page with wishlist button, credits, press quotes, press kit size and key request form
- [inkle: A Highland Song](https://www.inklestudios.com/a-highland-song): trailer, store buttons, scored press quotes, laurels and soundtrack credits
- [inkle: Press](https://www.inklestudios.com/press): studio press page with bios, dated timeline, logos and awards

#### 029 · Creative Developer / Lab (`lab`)
**For:** creative developers and web designers who code, publish side projects, and keep a personal site as a public notebook.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-project (work grid) · single-project · home (notes/blog) · single · page-now · page-uses · page-archive (past site versions) · page-about · page-colophon
**Patterns (~35):** work grid of side projects (thumbnail + title + live link), /now entry with dated header, /uses list grouped by category (Editor + Terminal / Desktop apps / Recording / Desk setup), "past versions of this site" list (v. I, v. II... with year and screenshot), notes river with tags, code snippet block, RSS subscribe line, colophon (fonts, host, build), talks list, footer with Mastodon/GitHub/CodePen links.
**Content model:** `project` (year, live_url, repo_url, stack tags). Posts for notes. `site_version` (version number, year, screenshot, case-study link) for the archive page.
**Plugins:** Code Block Pro.
**Signature:** a dated /now page where each update is a new dated section, newest first, with the latest date shown as "Updated 20 September 2026" at the top (seen on: [Maggie Appleton: Now](https://maggieappleton.com/now), [Derek Sivers: /now](https://sive.rs/now)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A "link to nownownow" line and a short "what is a now page" note under the stamp (seen on: [Derek Sivers: /now](https://sive.rs/now))
- Site-version archive with version numbers and years, a free portfolio of the owner's own redesigns (seen on: [Lynn Fisher: Archive](https://lynnandtonic.com/archive/))
- /uses page split into plain headed lists, each item with one sentence on why it is used (seen on: [Wes Bos: Uses](https://wesbos.com/uses))
- RSS link and a colophon link in the footer of every page (seen on: [Maggie Appleton: Now](https://maggieappleton.com/now))
- "Listed on uses.tech" note with a link to the directory entry (directory: [uses.tech](https://uses.tech/))
**Real-world basis:** [Maggie Appleton: Now](https://maggieappleton.com/now) · [Derek Sivers: /now](https://sive.rs/now) · [Lynn Fisher: Archive](https://lynnandtonic.com/archive/) · [Lynn Fisher: Work](https://lynnandtonic.com/work/) · [Wes Bos: Uses](https://wesbos.com/uses)
**Style: Hand-coded personal web (view-source honesty)**
- Type: headings Martian Mono 700 at 64px (tracking 0), body Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 400 at 18px/1.6, meta and dates Martian Mono 400 at 15px.
- Palette: bg #F7F7F2 (paper), text #111111, link #0047FF (hyperlink blue, underlined), visited #7A3E00 (burnt umber), line #D9D9CF, code surface #ECECE4.
- Layout: single 68ch reading column hard left with a 220px left rail for the date stamp and page title; no cards; projects as a two-column list of screenshot + one-line caption; 1px rules between entries; square corners everywhere.
- Imagery: real browser screenshots of projects at 16:10, no device frames, 1px border only.
- Motion: none by default; project thumbnails swap to a looping GIF on hover only where the owner uploads one, inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
- Why it fits now: personal sites and /now pages are having a real revival among developers leaving social platforms, and the hand-made look signals a person, not a template (example: [Lynn Fisher: Archive](https://lynnandtonic.com/archive/)).
**Style variations:** Night: #101010 bg, #F7F7F2 text, blue links · Terminal: all Martian Mono, #F2EFE6 bg · Print: black on white, footnoted links
**Refs:**
- [Maggie Appleton: Now](https://maggieappleton.com/now): dated, newest-first /now log with reading notes and an RSS line at the foot.
- [Lynn Fisher: Archive](https://lynnandtonic.com/archive/): numbered list of every past site version with year and screenshot, a strong idea for a creative developer's own history.
- [Wes Bos: Uses](https://wesbos.com/uses): plain headed /uses lists with one honest sentence per tool.

#### 030 · Web Dev Co-op / Freelancer Collective (`coop`)
**For:** worker-owned tech co-ops and freelancer collectives that build websites and tools for charities, unions and civil society.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-project · single-project (case study) · archive-member · single-member · page-services · page-about (co-op model and values) · page-handbook · page-social-value · archive (writing) · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** project index by year and sector, case study (problem / what we built / rollout / team credits / screenshots), member profile (name, role, "Life before the co-op", "When not at work"), services list in prose, "how we are owned" explainer, values statement, Living Wage employer note, writing/blog river, newsletter sign-up, footer with company registration number and link to articles of association, "book a meeting" link.
**Content model:** `project` (client, sector, year, services, team relation to `member`, funder). `member` (role, pronouns, bio sections). `handbook_page` (hierarchical pages).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms.
**Signature:** a public handbook section (hierarchical pages for how we work, pay, policies) including a published pay formula or rate table (seen on: [Hypha: Salary guide](https://handbook.hypha.coop/How-we-work/salary.html), [Hypha: Handbook](https://handbook.hypha.coop)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Team credits at the foot of every case study, linked to member profiles (seen on: [Outlandish: Nook CRM](https://outlandish.com/project/nook-crm/))
- Footer with company number, registered address and a PDF link to the articles of association (seen on: [Common Knowledge: StrikeMap](https://commonknowledge.coop/projects/strikemap/))
- Social value page with Living Wage and subsidised-work policy spelled out (seen on: [Outlandish: Social value](https://outlandish.com/social-value/))
- Member profiles written as short stories rather than skill bars, with a contact button at the end (seen on: [Agile Collective: Rae](https://agile.coop/our-people/rae/))
- "Book a 30-minute call" link beside the email address, using a Cal.com embed
**Real-world basis:** [Outlandish: About](https://outlandish.com/about/) · [Outlandish: Nook CRM case study](https://outlandish.com/project/nook-crm/) · [Common Knowledge: StrikeMap](https://commonknowledge.coop/projects/strikemap/) · [Agile Collective: Rae](https://agile.coop/our-people/rae/) · [Hypha: Handbook](https://handbook.hypha.coop)
**Style: Civic plain-text with poster headlines**
- Type: headings Gemunu Libre 800 (condensed by design), 72px, line-height 1.0; body Public Sans 400 at 18px/1.6; labels Public Sans 600 at 15px.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #0E1A12, accent #D2361E (union red, for links and one headline per page), surface #F1F4EE, line #0E1A12.
- Layout: 12-column grid with 3/9 split: section name in the left rail, content right; heavy 3px rules between sections; project index is a table (year / client / what we built); no rounded corners.
- Imagery: honest product screenshots at 16:10 on flat #F1F4EE, and group photos of members in black and white.
- Motion: none beyond underline-on-hover for links; View Transitions for page changes inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
- Why it fits now: movement-tech co-ops present themselves with plain, text-led pages that read like a manifesto, which matches clients who distrust agency gloss (example: [Common Knowledge: Projects](https://commonknowledge.coop/projects/)).
**Style variations:** Ledger: black on #F4F1E8 newsprint, no red · Strike: #D2361E bg, white type · Allotment: #1E4D2B green accent
**Refs:**
- [Outlandish: Nook CRM](https://outlandish.com/project/nook-crm/): case study that ends with named team credits and the funder, a model for co-op transparency.
- [Common Knowledge: StrikeMap](https://commonknowledge.coop/projects/strikemap/): short project page with year and services, and a footer that links the articles of association.
- [Hypha: Salary guide](https://handbook.hypha.coop/How-we-work/salary.html): a published pay formula and table, proof that open pay pages exist in the wild.

<a id="031"></a>
#### 031 · Independent Fashion Label (`seam`)
**For:** small ready-to-wear labels that shoot seasonal lookbooks and sell direct and through stockists.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-lookbook (by season) · single-lookbook · Woo shop · archive-product (by category) · single-product · page-stockists · page-journal · page-about · page-size-guide · page-care
**Patterns (~45):** season lookbook (numbered looks, photographer credit), lookbook archive list (season code + season name, e.g. "SS25 Low Tide"), "shop this look" product rail under each look, product grid with second image on hover, size guide table (UK/IT/US), fabric and mill note, stockists by country then city, journal/essay layout, coming-soon collection, newsletter sign-up.
**Content model:** `lookbook` (season, year, season_name, photographer, looks as ordered gallery with per-look product relations). Woo variable products (size × colour) with `collection` taxonomy.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce.
**Signature:** a looks page where choosing "Look 1" opens that outfit's products below with size and quick add (seen on: [Studio Nicholson: Womens Autumn 26 Looks](https://www.studionicholson.com/pages/womens-autumn-26-looks)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Stockists grouped by country then city, with online stockists listed first (seen on: [Story mfg.: Stockists](https://www.storymfg.com/pages/stockists))
- Lookbook archive back to the first season, each with its own season name (seen on: [Olderbrother: Lookbooks](https://olderbrother.us/blogs/lookbooks))
- Photographer credit line on every lookbook (seen on: [YMC: Autumn Winter 2026](https://www.youmustcreate.com/blogs/lookbooks/2026-autumn-winter))
- Size guide with garment measurements in cm/in and a "model is 178cm wearing size 2" line on product pages
- "Coming soon" collection page with a notify-me form (seen on: [Story mfg.](https://www.storymfg.com/) coming-soon collection)
**Real-world basis:** [Studio Nicholson: Womens Autumn 26 Looks](https://www.studionicholson.com/pages/womens-autumn-26-looks) · [Olderbrother: Lookbooks](https://olderbrother.us/blogs/lookbooks) · [Story mfg.: Stockists](https://www.storymfg.com/pages/stockists) · [YMC: Autumn Winter 2026](https://www.youmustcreate.com/blogs/lookbooks/2026-autumn-winter) · [Lemaire: AW26 Lookbook](https://lemaire.fr/pages/autumn-winter-2026-lookbook)
**Style: Quiet luxury mono**
- Type: headings Melodrama 500 (Fontshare) at 80px, body Hanken Grotesk 400 at 17px/1.6, labels Hanken Grotesk 500 at 15px with look numbers in tabular figures.
- Palette: bg #FAFAF8, text #1A1A1A, accent #5C4A3A (undyed wool brown, used for sale and "new" only), surface #EFEDE8, line #CFCBC3.
- Layout: full-bleed portrait images at 4:5 in a two-up spread; text sits in a narrow 4-column band; nav is wordmark centre with Shop / Lookbooks / Journal / Stockists left and Bag right; square corners.
- Imagery: location photography with natural light, no cut-outs; product shots on a single neutral wall; always credit the photographer.
- Motion: crossfade between looks (opacity only, 200ms), inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference; images never zoom on hover.
- Why it fits now: small labels sell through the look, not through banners, and a restrained serif plus calm neutrals matches the current direction of independent menswear and womenswear (example: [Studio Nicholson: Womens Autumn 26 Looks](https://www.studionicholson.com/pages/womens-autumn-26-looks)).
**Style variations:** Workwear: #2F3A2F olive text, Hanken only · Night: #141414 bg, #EDEBE6 type · Linen: #EEE8DC bg, #3B2E24 text
**Refs:**
- [Studio Nicholson: Womens Autumn 26 Looks](https://www.studionicholson.com/pages/womens-autumn-26-looks): numbered looks that expand into a product list with sizes and quick add.
- [Olderbrother: Lookbooks](https://olderbrother.us/blogs/lookbooks): a decade of named seasons in one archive page, each an image-led story.
- [Story mfg.: Stockists](https://www.storymfg.com/pages/stockists): plain country/city stockist list with links, no map needed.

<a id="032"></a>
#### 032 · Jewelry Maker (`karat`)
**For:** independent jewellers and goldsmiths who sell a small collection online and make bespoke rings by commission.
**Templates:** front-page · Woo shop · archive-product (Rings / Pendants / Earrings / One of One) · single-product · page-bespoke · page-engagement-rings · page-size-guide · page-care-sustainability · page-faq · page-about · archive (journal) · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** bespoke process steps (consultation, sketch, wax or CAD, casting, setting and finishing, hallmarking, collection), "book a free consultation" block, pricing guide in prose ("simple bands from £...", "engagement rings from £..."), deposit and payment terms, one-of-one grid with "sold" state, metal options note (platinum / 18ct / 9ct), ring size guide, care and sustainability, journal post with making photos, delivery guide.
**Content model:** Woo variable products (metal × size). `commission_story` posts (process photos per stage) for the journal.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce, Jetpack Forms (bespoke enquiry), Cal.com embed (consultations).
**Signature:** a bespoke page that walks through the real stages with photos of each one and states lead time, deposit and payment split (seen on: [Glen & Effie: Fine Jewelry Commissions](https://www.glenandeffie.com/pages/fine-jewelry-commissions), [Michael Platt: How to commission](https://michaelplatt.co.uk/how-to-commission-bespoke-jewellery/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- "Try on the wax model before casting" option explained on the bespoke page (seen on: [Glen & Effie: Commissions](https://www.glenandeffie.com/pages/fine-jewelry-commissions))
- Lead time and minimum commission stated in one line: "3–4 weeks, minimum £300" (seen on: [The Wildness Jewellery: Bespoke](https://thewildnessjewellery.com/2026/06/17/bringing-your-ideas-to-life-bespoke-jewellery/))
- Hallmarking explained as a step, with the assay office named (seen on: [Michael Platt: How to commission](https://michaelplatt.co.uk/how-to-commission-bespoke-jewellery/))
- Printable ring-size guide PDF and a "we'll send a free ring sizer" form
- "Visit the workshop to see your ring being made" note (seen on: [Alexander Davis: Commissioning process](https://www.alexanderdavisjewellery.com/blogs/diary/the-process-of-commissioning-a-bespoke-engagement-ring-in-the-uk))
**Real-world basis:** [Michael Platt: How to commission bespoke jewellery](https://michaelplatt.co.uk/how-to-commission-bespoke-jewellery/) · [Glen & Effie: Fine Jewelry Commissions](https://www.glenandeffie.com/pages/fine-jewelry-commissions) · [The Wildness Jewellery: Bespoke](https://thewildnessjewellery.com/2026/06/17/bringing-your-ideas-to-life-bespoke-jewellery/) · [Alexander Davis: Commissioning process](https://www.alexanderdavisjewellery.com/blogs/diary/the-process-of-commissioning-a-bespoke-engagement-ring-in-the-uk)
**Style: Bench specimen (macro objects on flat grounds)**
- Type: headings Italiana 400 at 76px, body Newsreader 400 at 18px/1.6, labels Newsreader 500 small caps at 15px for metal and carat.
- Palette: bg #EEF0F0 (steel bench plate), text #1D1B18, accent #8C6A2E (18ct yellow, for price and primary action), surface #E4E2DC (wax-grey), line #BDB8AE.
- Layout: asymmetric 5/7 split on product pages (details left, macro image right, image larger); process page as a vertical sequence with one photo per stage, each captioned with the stage name; square corners, 1px rules.
- Imagery: macro photography on flat single-colour grounds, one object per frame; process photos in the workshop at the bench (wax, sprue, file, setting).
- Motion: none on images; stage photos can be scrubbed left/right with keyboard support; all transitions inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
- Why it fits now: independent jewellers win bespoke work by showing the making, and a quiet specimen layout lets the object and the process carry the page (example: [Glen & Effie: Commissions](https://www.glenandeffie.com/pages/fine-jewelry-commissions)).
**Style variations:** Silver: #EDEFF1 bg, #4A5560 accent · Oxblood: #3A1418 bg, #E9DCC9 type · Wax: #D9D6CC bg, #1D1B18 text
**Refs:**
- [Glen & Effie: Fine Jewelry Commissions](https://www.glenandeffie.com/pages/fine-jewelry-commissions): four clear stages with deposit, lead time and typical prices in plain words.
- [Michael Platt: How to commission bespoke jewellery](https://michaelplatt.co.uk/how-to-commission-bespoke-jewellery/): WordPress site with a full ten-step process including hallmarking and a free-consultation call to action.
- [The Wildness Jewellery: Bringing your ideas to life](https://thewildnessjewellery.com/2026/06/17/bringing-your-ideas-to-life-bespoke-jewellery/): a solo maker explaining hand-carved wax and photo updates to the client.

#### 033 · Illustration / Artist Representation Agency (`rep`)
**For:** small agencies that represent illustrators, animators and photographers and pitch them to brands and publishers.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-artist (roster) · single-artist · archive-work · taxonomy-style (browse by style/subject/medium) · taxonomy-format (advertising, book covers, editorial, packaging) · page-animation · archive (news) · page-about · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** roster grid (image + name), discipline filter row (Illustration / Animation / Photography), browse-by-style index (Architecture, Botanical, Black & White, Maps, Characters...), works grid where every tile names its artist and client, artist page (hero, work, recent commissions, commission contact with agent name and phone), recent projects feed, agency news, podcast/interview block, about in several languages.
**Content model:** `artist` (disciplines, agent, location). `work` (artist relation, client, year, style, subject, medium, format taxonomies).
**Plugins:** Query Filter.
**Signature:** style and subject pages that pull works from the whole roster, each credited and linked to its artist (seen on: [Folio: Map illustrations](https://folioart.co.uk/illustration/style/map-illustrations/), [Folio: Illustration styles](https://folioart.co.uk/illustration-styles/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Named agent with direct email and phone on every artist page (seen on: [Handsome Frank: Jean Jullien](https://www.handsomefrank.com/illustrators/jean-jullien))
- Discipline filters on the roster (seen on: [Pocko: Artists](https://www.pocko.com/talent))
- About page available in several languages for international clients (seen on: [Folio: About](https://folioart.co.uk/about/))
- "What we need to quote" checklist: usage, territory, deadline, budget
- Separate animation roster page (seen on: [Handsome Frank: Animation](https://www.handsomefrank.com/animation))
**Real-world basis:** [Folio: Illustration styles](https://folioart.co.uk/illustration-styles/) · [Folio: Map illustrations](https://folioart.co.uk/illustration/style/map-illustrations/) · [Handsome Frank: Jean Jullien](https://www.handsomefrank.com/illustrators/jean-jullien) · [Pocko: Artists](https://www.pocko.com/talent)
**Style: Index catalogue (tight grotesk grid)**
- Type: headings Clash Grotesk 600 (Fontshare) at 88px, body Clash Grotesk 400 at 18px/1.55, captions IBM Plex Mono 400 at 15px for client and year.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #121212, accent #E24E1B (vermilion, for artist names on hover and the enquire action), surface #F2F2F0, line #121212.
- Layout: dense 6-column image grid with captions below each tile (artist, client, year); roster page as a text list of names that doubles as a filter; left-aligned; 0px radius; 1px rules between list rows.
- Imagery: each artist's own work at its native ratio, no cropping to squares on artist pages; roster thumbnails cropped 4:5.
- Motion: roster names show a small preview image beside the cursor on hover (desktop only, inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference); no image zoom.
- Why it fits now: art buyers search by style and subject first, and agencies that lead with a dense captioned index get commissioners to the right artist fastest (example: [Folio: Illustration styles](https://folioart.co.uk/illustration-styles/)).
**Style variations:** Salon: #F4F0E8 bg, #121212 text · Black book: #111111 bg, #F2F2F0 type · Primary: #1E3FD0 accent on white
**Refs:**
- [Folio: Map illustrations](https://folioart.co.uk/illustration/style/map-illustrations/): cross-roster style page with every work credited to its artist and client.
- [Handsome Frank: Jean Jullien](https://www.handsomefrank.com/illustrators/jean-jullien): artist page ending in a named agent, phone number and what to send for a commission.
- [Pocko: Artists](https://www.pocko.com/talent): roster grid with discipline filters across illustration, animation and photography.

### IV. Film & moving image

<a id="034"></a>
#### 034 · Independent Filmmaker / Film Site (`reel`)
**For:** directors, small producers and boutique distributors running a site per film or a slate of films.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-film · single-film · page-screenings · page-host-a-screening · page-press (password protected) · page-about · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** film header (title, director, year, runtime, countries), trailer embed, synopsis, press quotes with star ratings and outlet, festival laurels row, screenings list (city / venue / date / tickets), "where to watch" links, press kit download, credits block, stills gallery, host-a-screening form, newsletter.
**Content model:** `film` (director, year, runtime, countries, producers, trailer_url, press_kit file, laurels). `screening` (film relation, date, venue, city, ticket_url).
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (upcoming screenings), Jetpack Forms.
**Signature:** a screenings list on each film page: city, venue and dates with a ticket link per row, dropping past dates automatically (seen on: [Dogwoof: Hanging By A Wire](https://releasing.dogwoof.com/hanging-by-a-wire), [Grasshopper Film: Mare's Nest](https://grasshopperfilm.com/film/mares-nest/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Host-a-screening form for community and campus screenings (seen on: [Grasshopper Film: Host a Screening](https://grasshopperfilm.com/host-a-screening/))
- Press kit PDF download on the film page (seen on: [Grasshopper Film: Mare's Nest](https://grasshopperfilm.com/film/mares-nest/))
- Password-protected press area for hi-res stills and screener links (seen on: [Oscilloscope: Press area](https://oscilloscope.net/films/password-protected-area/))
- Press quotes as text with outlet and star rating, never as images
- Festival laurels set as text in a laurel-shaped block style, so the owner can add "Official Selection, Sundance 2026" without a designer
**Real-world basis:** [Grasshopper Film: Mare's Nest](https://grasshopperfilm.com/film/mares-nest/) · [Grasshopper Film: Host a Screening](https://grasshopperfilm.com/host-a-screening/) · [Dogwoof: Hanging By A Wire](https://releasing.dogwoof.com/hanging-by-a-wire) · [Oscilloscope: Press area](https://oscilloscope.net/films/password-protected-area/)
**Style: Arthouse one-sheet**
- Type: headings Bellefair 400 at 84px, body Libre Franklin 400 at 18px/1.6, credits Libre Franklin 500 at 15px uppercase with generous tracking (0.08em) only in the credit block.
- Palette: bg #F5F3EF, text #151515, accent #B3261E (festival red, for ticket links), surface #1B1B1B (trailer band), line #CFCAC1.
- Layout: film page opens with a 2.39:1 still full-bleed, title set below it left-aligned; facts in a two-column definition list; screenings as a table; credits set as a centred one-sheet block at the end (the one centred moment).
- Imagery: production stills at the film's own ratio with letterbox bars kept; poster at 2:3 beside the synopsis.
- Motion: trailer plays only on click; no autoplay; View Transitions between film pages, inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
- Why it fits now: boutique distributors keep film pages text-first with quotes, dates and a press kit, which is what programmers and press actually use (example: [Grasshopper Film: Mare's Nest](https://grasshopperfilm.com/film/mares-nest/)).
**Style variations:** Documentary: #FFFFFF bg, #0E3B5C accent · Midnight: #121212 bg, #F5F3EF type · Grindhouse: #F2D300 accent, black text
**Refs:**
- [Grasshopper Film: Mare's Nest](https://grasshopperfilm.com/film/mares-nest/): WordPress film page with facts, text press quotes, US screenings list and a press kit download.
- [Dogwoof: Hanging By A Wire](https://releasing.dogwoof.com/hanging-by-a-wire): UK cinema dates by town with a booking link per venue.
- [Grasshopper Film: Host a Screening](https://grasshopperfilm.com/host-a-screening/): short form (name, institution, film, message) that turns interest into bookings.
