#### 035 · Cinematographer / Editor / Colourist (`grade`)
**For:** DoPs, gaffers, editors and colourists who need a reel, a credits list and a kit list for producers.
**Templates:** front-page (showreel) · archive-project · single-project · taxonomy-medium (Films / Television / Commercials / Music Videos) · page-full-credits · page-stills · page-awards · page-kit · page-profile · page-contact
**Patterns (~30):** showreel hero (Vimeo embed), project list grouped by medium with "Directed by", project page (synopsis, director, production, crew, cast, video), gallery sections "Highlights / Still Frames / Behind the Scenes", full credits list (title, director, production company), kit list by category (Camera, Lenses, Rigs, Filtration, Lights), awards list, representation/agent contact.
**Content model:** `project` (medium taxonomy, director, production company, year, role, format, video_url, gallery sections).
**Plugins:** none.
**Signature:** a full-credits page grouped by medium (Films / Television / Commercials / Music Videos), each line with title, director and production company (seen on: [Lol Crawley: Full credits](https://lolcrawley.com/full-credits/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Kit list page by category so producers can see what comes with the DoP (seen on: [Matthias Djan: Kit](https://matthiasdjan.co.uk/kit/))
- Separate gaffer lighting kit page for crew who work two roles (seen on: [Matthias Djan: Lighting kit](https://matthiasdjan.co.uk/gaffer/lighting-kit/))
- Project galleries split into Highlights, Still Frames and Behind the Scenes (seen on: [Matthias Djan: Blue Snakes](https://matthiasdjan.co.uk/portfolio/blue-snakes/))
- Awards page listing festival nominations by year (seen on: [Lol Crawley: Awards](https://lolcrawley.com/awards/))
- Downloadable one-page CV PDF with agent details
**Real-world basis:** [Lol Crawley: Full credits](https://lolcrawley.com/full-credits/) · [Lol Crawley: Films](https://lolcrawley.com/films/) · [Matthias Djan: Blue Snakes](https://matthiasdjan.co.uk/portfolio/blue-snakes/) · [Matthias Djan: Kit](https://matthiasdjan.co.uk/kit/) · [Matthias Djan: Showreel](https://matthiasdjan.co.uk/showreel/)
**Style: Letterbox dark room**
- Type: headings Teko 600 at 96px, body Source Serif 4 400 at 18px/1.6, meta Red Hat Mono 400 at 15px for format and camera.
- Palette: bg #0F0F0E (grading-suite black, chosen because stills read truer on dark), text #E8E6E1, accent #C9A227 (tungsten, for links only), surface #1A1A18, line #34332F.
- Layout: stills shown at their true ratio (2.39:1, 1.85:1, 1.33:1) in a single column; project list as text lines with director on the right; credits page is plain text in four headed groups; square corners.
- Imagery: frame grabs untouched, no filters or overlays; behind-the-scenes photos kept smaller and set apart.
- Motion: reel starts only on click; project list shows a still beside the line on hover (desktop, prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference).
- Why it fits now: DoP sites that let the frames sit on dark ground with a plain credit list read as professional to producers (example: [Lol Crawley: Films](https://lolcrawley.com/films/)).
**Style variations:** Daylight: #F4F3EF bg, #111111 text · 16mm: #1C1812 bg, #E3D5B8 type · Rushes: Red Hat Mono throughout
**Refs:**
- [Lol Crawley: Full credits](https://lolcrawley.com/full-credits/): WordPress credits page grouped by medium, each with director and production company.
- [Matthias Djan: Blue Snakes](https://matthiasdjan.co.uk/portfolio/blue-snakes/): project page with full crew and cast credits and a gallery split into highlights, frames and BTS.
- [Matthias Djan: Kit](https://matthiasdjan.co.uk/kit/): kit list by category, which answers the producer's first practical question.

<a id="036"></a>
#### 036 · Micro Film Festival (`fest`)
**For:** small artist-film and short-film festivals in towns and small cities, often run by a tiny team with volunteers.
**Templates:** front-page · page-programme · archive-strand · single-event · archive-film · single-film · page-accessibility · page-creche · page-trailers · page-past-festivals · page-submissions · page-volunteer · page-press · archive (news)
**Patterns (~45):** festival dates block, programme by strand or award (e.g. "Scottish Short Film Award"), event card (date, time, venue, runtime, captions/BSL flags), film card (director, country, runtime), award winners post, trailers page, access page (step-free, captions, BSL, seat dimensions, quiet space), crèche booking, pay-what-you-can ticket note, past festivals list with PDF programmes, submissions call (FilmFreeway link), volunteer call, venue list with map.
**Content model:** `event` (datetime, venue, strand, access flags, ticket_url). `film` (director, country, year, runtime, event relation). `edition` taxonomy (year).
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop, Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap.
**Signature:** an access page that states specifics (all screenings subtitled, BSL at every Q&A, pay-what-you-can tiers, seat width and legroom, quiet room hours) (seen on: [Alchemy Film & Arts: Accessibility](https://alchemyfilmandarts.org.uk/accessibility/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Bookable festival crèche with hours (seen on: [Alchemy Film & Arts: Festival Crèche](https://alchemyfilmandarts.org.uk/festival-creche/))
- Past festivals list with each year's programme PDF (seen on: [Alchemy Film & Arts: Past Festivals](https://alchemyfilmandarts.org.uk/past-festivals/))
- Festival trailers page for press and partners to embed (seen on: [Alchemy Film & Arts: Festival Trailers](https://alchemyfilmandarts.org.uk/festival-2026-trailers/))
- Programme page that switches to "Our next programme will be announced early next year" between editions (seen on: [Glasgow Short Film Festival: Programme](https://glasgowshort.org/programme/))
- Access flags on every event card (captions, BSL, relaxed) generated from event meta
**Real-world basis:** [Alchemy Film & Arts: Accessibility](https://alchemyfilmandarts.org.uk/accessibility/) · [Alchemy Film & Arts: Past Festivals](https://alchemyfilmandarts.org.uk/past-festivals/) · [Glasgow Short Film Festival: Programme](https://glasgowshort.org/programme/) · [Open City Documentary Festival: Full programme](https://opencitylondon.com/2026-festival/programme/full-programme/)
**Style: Yearly edition identity (variable type that changes each year)**
- Type: headings Climate Crisis at 700, with the YEAR axis set per edition, 96px; body Work Sans 400 at 18px/1.6; times and runtimes Work Sans 500 tabular figures at 16px.
- Palette (Edition default): bg #FFFFFF, text #111111, accent #0B6E4F (river green, for ticket links and today's date), surface #EAF2EE, line #111111. Each edition swaps accent and surface only.
- Layout: programme as a day-by-day table (time / title / venue / access flags), strand pages as long lists; 12-column grid with the festival dates always visible in the header; square corners.
- Imagery: film stills at native ratio with director and country caption; festival photography of real audiences in town venues.
- Motion: none on scroll; the edition wordmark renders its YEAR-axis state once on load, inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
- Why it fits now: small festivals give each edition its own look while keeping one site, and practical access detail is now what audiences look for first (example: [Alchemy Film & Arts: Accessibility](https://alchemyfilmandarts.org.uk/accessibility/)).
**Style variations:** Edition A: #0B6E4F accent · Edition B: #C2410C accent, #FFF4EC surface · Edition C: #1D3F8F accent, #EEF1F8 surface
**Refs:**
- [Alchemy Film & Arts: Accessibility](https://alchemyfilmandarts.org.uk/accessibility/): WordPress access page with subtitles, BSL, PWYC tiers, crèche, quiet space and seat sizes.
- [Alchemy Film & Arts: Past Festivals](https://alchemyfilmandarts.org.uk/past-festivals/): simple year list linking each edition's programme PDF.
- [Glasgow Short Film Festival: Programme](https://glasgowshort.org/programme/): WordPress programme organised by award strand, with an honest between-editions message.

<a id="037"></a>
#### 037 · Micro-Cinema / Community Cinema (`projector`)
**For:** single-screen independent cinemas, volunteer-run cinemas and film clubs.
**Templates:** front-page (date strip + listings) · archive-screening · single-screening · archive-strand · archive-season · page-films-a-z · page-membership · page-hire · page-access · page-get-involved · page-visit
**Patterns (~40):** date strip ("Today", then each day), listing row (title, certificate, director, year, runtime, countries, times), strand and season pages, access tags (Bring Your Baby / Audio Description / Hard of Hearing / Closed captions / Pay What You Can), live-score and Q&A tags, event page with price and ticket link, membership block, volunteer and open meeting listings, café hours, programme archive, RSS feed.
**Content model:** `screening` (datetime, film relation, price, ticket_url, tags). `film` (certificate, director, year, runtime, countries). `strand` and `season` taxonomies.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop, The Events Calendar (optional for recurring café and meeting listings).
**Signature:** a date strip across the top of the homepage ("Today", "Sat 27", "Sun 28"...) that filters listings to that day, each film showing certificate, director, year and runtime (seen on: [The Garden Cinema](https://www.thegardencinema.co.uk/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Access tags as filters, including captioned, audio-described and baby-friendly screenings (seen on: [The Garden Cinema](https://www.thegardencinema.co.uk/))
- Programme views by tag with an RSS feed per view (seen on: [Star and Shadow: Closed captions view](https://www.starandshadow.org.uk/programme/view/closed-captions/))
- "Cheap night" or pay-what-you-can marker on listings (seen on: [Star and Shadow: Programme](https://www.starandshadow.org.uk/programme/view/closed-captions/))
- Open programming meetings listed alongside films so members can shape the programme (seen on: [Star and Shadow: Meetings](https://www.starandshadow.org.uk/get-involved/meetings/))
- Members' waiting list on sold-out screenings (seen on: [The Garden Cinema](https://www.thegardencinema.co.uk/))
**Real-world basis:** [The Garden Cinema](https://www.thegardencinema.co.uk/) · [Star and Shadow: Joan of Arc with live score](https://www.starandshadow.org.uk/programme/event/the-passion-of-joan-of-arc-w-live-score-performed-by-burning-pyre,9487/) · [Star and Shadow: Programme archive](https://www.starandshadow.org.uk/programme/archive/) · [Rio Cinema: Home](https://riocinema.org.uk/Rio.dll/Home)
**Style: Programme-sheet listings (condensed type, printed-leaflet feel)**
- Type: headings Antonio 700 at 88px, body Literata 400 at 18px/1.6, times and certificates Antonio 500 at 17px tabular.
- Palette: bg #FFFDF7 (listings paper stock), text #141414, accent #C8102E (box-office red, for times you can book), surface #F1ECDF, line #141414. Cream is justified here by the printed leaflet.
- Layout: date strip as a row of bordered day buttons; listings as full-width rows (poster thumbnail 2:3, title and facts, times as buttons on the right); two-column on desktop, one on mobile; square corners, 2px rules.
- Imagery: film posters or stills at native ratio; photos of the room, bar and projection booth on the Visit page.
- Motion: selected day slides its underline (transform only, 150ms) inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference; nothing else moves.
- Why it fits now: small cinemas compete with apps by being faster to read than a booking app, and the printed-leaflet listing is what regulars already know (example: [The Garden Cinema](https://www.thegardencinema.co.uk/)).
**Style variations:** Velvet: #3B0D12 bg, #F5E9D6 type · Club: #FFFFFF bg, #0A5C36 accent · Late show: #121212 bg, #FFD166 times
**Refs:**
- [The Garden Cinema](https://www.thegardencinema.co.uk/): WordPress homepage built on a date strip with certificate, director, year and runtime per film and access tags.
- [Star and Shadow: Closed captions view](https://www.starandshadow.org.uk/programme/view/closed-captions/): volunteer cinema with tag-based programme views, list/grid toggle and RSS.
- [Star and Shadow: Joan of Arc with live score](https://www.starandshadow.org.uk/programme/event/the-passion-of-joan-of-arc-w-live-score-performed-by-burning-pyre,9487/): event page with date, price, presenter and a direct ticket link.

### V. Music & sound

<a id="038"></a>
#### 038 · Band / Solo Musician (`amp`)
**For:** independent bands and solo artists who tour small venues and sell records and merch direct.
**Templates:** front-page (current release) · page-live · archive-release · single-release · Woo shop (merch) · page-watch (videos) · page-epk · page-workshops · page-mailing-list · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** current-release header with streaming and buy links, live dates list (date / venue / city / country / support / tickets), dates grouped by type (e.g. "Book readings 2026" and "Solo performances 2026"), release page (tracklist, credits, formats), video page, EPK (bio, hi-res photos with photographer credit, press quotes, press kit link), booking and management contacts by territory, mailing list sign-up, merch rail.
**Content model:** `release` (type, date, label, cat_no, links). `show` (date, venue, city, country, support, ticket_url, group).
**Plugins:** WooCommerce, Advanced Query Loop, Jetpack Newsletter.
**Signature:** a live page that lists every date with support acts and one ticket link per row, grouped by tour or type (seen on: [bdrmm: Live](https://bdrmm.co.uk/live/), [James Yorkston: Live dates](https://www.jamesyorkston.co.uk/live-dates/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Booking and management contacts split by territory (UK/EU/Rest of World, US/Canada/South America) (seen on: [Gruff Rhys: Live](https://www.gruffrhys.com/live))
- EPK page with press quotes, hi-res photos credited to the photographer and a press-kit link (seen on: [Fire Records: The Bevis Frond EPK](https://www.firerecords.com/artists/bevis-frond-epk/))
- Bilingual headings where the band works in two languages (seen on: [Gruff Rhys: Live](https://www.gruffrhys.com/live))
- Workshops or extra-events page for non-gig income (seen on: [Big Thief: Songwriting workshops](https://www.bigthief.net/songwriting-workshops))
- "Sold out" and "Low tickets" flags on dates, and past dates moving to an archive automatically
**Real-world basis:** [bdrmm: Live](https://bdrmm.co.uk/live/) · [James Yorkston: Live dates](https://www.jamesyorkston.co.uk/live-dates/) · [Gruff Rhys: Live](https://www.gruffrhys.com/live) · [Fire Records: The Bevis Frond EPK](https://www.firerecords.com/artists/bevis-frond-epk/) · [Big Thief: Tour](https://www.bigthief.net/tour)
**Style: Gig-list typography (flyer grid)**
- Type: headings Karrik (Velvetyne, OFL) at 96px, body Figtree 400 at 18px/1.6, dates Figtree 600 tabular at 17px.
- Palette: bg #EDEAE3, text #161616, accent #2E5BFF (flyer blue, for ticket links), surface #D8D3C8, line #161616.
- Layout: live dates as a full-width table with the date in a fixed first column, venue and city next, support in smaller type, tickets at the far right; release artwork large at 1:1 beside the tracklist; square corners, 2px rules.
- Imagery: band photos in black and white with visible grain; sleeve artwork always at 1:1 without a mock-up.
- Motion: none on scroll; ticket link underline on hover only.
- Why it fits now: independent bands keep sites to a release and a dates list with plain type, because fans come for the dates (example: [bdrmm: Live](https://bdrmm.co.uk/live/)).
**Style variations:** Night: #111111 bg, #EDEAE3 type · Folk: #F3EEE2 bg, #5B3A1E accent · Punk: #FFE600 bg, black type
**Refs:**
- [bdrmm: Live](https://bdrmm.co.uk/live/): WordPress live page with systematic date formatting, support acts and a ticket link per show.
- [James Yorkston: Live dates](https://www.jamesyorkston.co.uk/live-dates/): dates grouped into book readings and solo shows, each with its own ticket link.
- [Fire Records: The Bevis Frond EPK](https://www.firerecords.com/artists/bevis-frond-epk/): working EPK with bio, credited photos, press quotes and a press-kit link.

<a id="039"></a>
#### 039 · Independent Record Label (`catalog`)
**For:** small independent labels selling vinyl, CDs and digital direct, with a roster of 5–40 artists.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-release (catalogue) · single-release · archive-artist · single-artist · page-artist-epk · Woo shop · single-product · page-about · page-contact
**Patterns (~45):** catalogue grid (release date, artist, title, catalogue number, buy links), A–Z artist index, release page (cat no, release date, tracklist, press text, formats, buy links to shop and Bandcamp), artist page (releases, videos, Songkick dates, socials), artist EPK subpage, format and edition notes (marbled vinyl, numbered print, edition of 500), "SOLD OUT" states, EU customers shop note, newsletter (Substack or Jetpack).
**Content model:** `release` (cat_no, date, artist relation, tracklist, press text, linked Woo products per format). `artist`.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce, Query Filter, Jetpack Newsletter.
**Signature:** catalogue numbers shown on every release in the catalogue grid and on the release page (e.g. ZIQ479), with the catalogue sorted newest first (seen on: [Planet Mu: Releases](https://planet.mu/releases/), [Planet Mu: Body Lapse](https://planet.mu/releases/body-lapse/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Edition size and sold-out state on each format: "500 copies. SOLD OUT." (seen on: [Clay Pipe Music](https://www.claypipemusic.co.uk/))
- Note pointing EU customers to a European shop to avoid customs charges (seen on: [Clay Pipe Music](https://www.claypipemusic.co.uk/))
- Per-artist EPK pages with press quotes and photos for press and promoters (seen on: [Fire Records: The Bevis Frond EPK](https://www.firerecords.com/artists/bevis-frond-epk/))
- A–Z artist index (seen on: [Planet Mu: Artists](https://planet.mu/artists/))
- Coloured-vinyl variants with separate prices on artist pages (seen on: [Fire Records: Jane Weaver](https://www.firerecords.com/artists/jane-weaver/))
**Real-world basis:** [Planet Mu: Releases](https://planet.mu/releases/) · [Planet Mu: Body Lapse](https://planet.mu/releases/body-lapse/) · [Clay Pipe Music](https://www.claypipemusic.co.uk/) · [Fire Records: Jane Weaver](https://www.firerecords.com/artists/jane-weaver/) · [Fire Records: The Bevis Frond EPK](https://www.firerecords.com/artists/bevis-frond-epk/)
**Style: Systematic catalogue (numbered, sleeve-first)**
- Type: headings Be Vietnam Pro 900 at 80px, body Be Vietnam Pro 400 at 18px/1.55, catalogue numbers IBM Plex Mono 500 at 16px.
- Palette: bg #F4F4F1, text #0D0D0D, accent #E0301E (label red, used only on the catalogue number and buy action), surface #E6E6E1, line #0D0D0D.
- Layout: catalogue as a 4-column sleeve grid with cat no above the artwork; release page split 5/7 with sleeve left, tracklist and formats right; optional table view (cat no / artist / title / format / year); square corners.
- Imagery: sleeves flat at 1:1, no vinyl mock-ups; photos of the physical pressing (labels, inserts) on release pages.
- Motion: none; the table view sorts instantly without animation.
- Why it fits now: labels that treat the catalogue number as the organising idea have a design system that scales with every release (example: [Planet Mu: Releases](https://planet.mu/releases/)).
**Style variations:** Dub: #0F1A14 bg, #E8E3D3 type · Tape: #F2E7C9 bg, #3A2A1A text · Factory: white, black, one #E0301E rule
**Refs:**
- [Planet Mu: Releases](https://planet.mu/releases/): WordPress catalogue with date, artist, title and catalogue number on every sleeve.
- [Clay Pipe Music](https://www.claypipemusic.co.uk/): tiny label showing edition sizes, sold-out states and special editions with care.
- [Fire Records: Jane Weaver](https://www.firerecords.com/artists/jane-weaver/): WooCommerce artist page with formats and variant prices beside videos and live dates.

<a id="040"></a>
#### 040 · DJ / Electronic Producer (`bpm`)
**For:** DJs, radio hosts and producers who publish mixes and need a place for dates and booking.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-mix · single-mix · page-dates · page-releases · page-booking · page-press · page-about
**Patterns (~30):** mix page (player embed, date, location, genre tags, description, tracklist with timestamps), numbered mix series (e.g. "Mix 042"), mix archive with tag filters, today's radio schedule block with times, dates list (date, club, city), booking contacts by territory, press photos download, releases list.
**Content model:** `mix` (number, date, location, platform_url, duration, tracklist rows with timestamps, genres taxonomy). `gig` (date, venue, city, ticket_url).
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop, Query Filter.
**Signature:** a tracklist under each mix with timestamps per track (artist, title, time), with genre tags and broadcast location on the same page (seen on: [NTS: La Movida w/ Courts](https://www.nts.live/shows/dancing-2026/episodes/dancing-2026-la-movida-w-courts-26th-september-2026)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Numbered mix series so each mix has a citable ID (seen on: [RA: Podcast](https://ra.co/podcast))
- A short written intro or Q&A with each mix (seen on: [RA: Podcast](https://ra.co/podcast))
- Today's schedule with times and a stated timezone for radio residencies (seen on: [The Lot Radio](https://www.thelotradio.com/))
- Booking contacts by territory and a one-click press photo pack
- "Archive index" page listing every mix by date for crate-digging (seen on: [The Lot Radio](https://www.thelotradio.com/) index)
**Real-world basis:** [NTS: La Movida w/ Courts](https://www.nts.live/shows/dancing-2026/episodes/dancing-2026-la-movida-w-courts-26th-september-2026) · [RA: Podcast](https://ra.co/podcast) · [The Lot Radio](https://www.thelotradio.com/) · [LYL Radio](https://www.lyl.live/)
**Style: Club-night utility (dark, tabular, strobe-safe)**
- Type: headings Audiowide 400 at 88px, body Red Hat Text 400 at 18px/1.6, timestamps and BPM Red Hat Mono 500 at 16px.
- Palette: bg #121212 (club-night reason for dark), text #EDEDED, accent #FF6A13 (sodium orange, for play and ticket links), surface #1E1E1E, line #3A3A3A.
- Layout: mix page with the player pinned at the top of the column, tracklist as a three-column table (time / artist / title); archive as a dense list with number, date and tags; no cards; square corners.
- Imagery: flyer artwork and grainy club photos at 4:5; no neon glow or gradients.
- Motion: clicking a timestamp seeks the embedded player where the platform API allows; no flashing or strobe; all motion inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
- Why it fits now: radio-led DJ culture lives on tracklists and archives, and a tabular dark layout matches how NTS and similar stations present shows (example: [NTS: La Movida w/ Courts](https://www.nts.live/shows/dancing-2026/episodes/dancing-2026-la-movida-w-courts-26th-september-2026)).
**Style variations:** Daytime: #F2F2EE bg, #121212 text · Dub: #0E1B16 bg, #9FD4A3 accent · Warehouse: #1A1A1A bg, #FFFFFF only
**Refs:**
- [NTS: La Movida w/ Courts](https://www.nts.live/shows/dancing-2026/episodes/dancing-2026-la-movida-w-courts-26th-september-2026): episode page with player, timestamped tracklist, genre tags and location.
- [RA: Podcast](https://ra.co/podcast): numbered mix series (RA.####) with a one-line description per mix.
- [The Lot Radio](https://www.thelotradio.com/): today's schedule with time slots beside a live player and a full archive index.

<a id="041"></a>
#### 041 · Film & Game Composer (`score`)
**For:** media composers working across games, film, TV and concert music.
**Templates:** front-page · page-projects-games · page-projects-film-tv · single-project · page-albums · page-concert-music · page-awards · page-press · page-about · page-contact
**Patterns (~30):** featured project header with "soundtrack available now" links, credits list by year (year, title, platform, studio, publisher, role), cover-art grid of featured projects, albums split by games / film & TV / miscellaneous, works tabs (Solo / Collaboration / Film & art), concert pieces list, awards list, press quotes, Bandcamp and streaming links, store link.
**Content model:** `project` (medium, year, platform, studio, publisher, role, soundtrack links, cue audio). `album` (type, year, label, links).
**Plugins:** none.
**Signature:** a credits list by year in reverse order, each line giving title, platform, studio (linked), publisher and the composer's role (seen on: [Austin Wintory: Videogames](https://www.austinwintory.com/projects-videogames)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Albums separated from credits, grouped by games, film & TV and miscellaneous (seen on: [Austin Wintory: Albums, games](https://www.austinwintory.com/albums-games))
- Concert music section for commissions and live shows of game scores (seen on: [Austin Wintory: Concert pieces](https://www.austinwintory.com/concert-pieces))
- Works tabs splitting solo, collaboration and film/art work (seen on: [Ólafur Arnalds: Works](https://olafurarnalds.com/works/))
- Bandcamp vinyl and merch links beside each soundtrack (seen on: [Jessica Curry](https://www.jessicacurry.co.uk/))
- A playlist of short cues built on core Audio, so producers can listen without leaving the page
**Real-world basis:** [Austin Wintory: Videogames](https://www.austinwintory.com/projects-videogames) · [Ólafur Arnalds: Works](https://olafurarnalds.com/works/) · [Jessica Curry](https://www.jessicacurry.co.uk/) · [Anna Meredith](https://www.annameredith.com/)
**Style: Score-page serif (engraved titles, cue-sheet tables)**
- Type: headings Castoro Titling 400 at 84px, body Castoro 400 at 18px/1.6, credits table Source Sans 3 500 at 16px with tabular figures.
- Palette: bg #F6F5F1, text #1B1B1B, accent #1F4E79 (manuscript ink blue, for listen and links), surface #EAE8E1, line #B9B4A8.
- Layout: credits as a real table grouped by year headings; featured work as a 3/9 split with cover art left and notes right; staves are not used as decoration; square corners, 1px rules.
- Imagery: official key art for games and films at native ratio; studio photos of the composer at the desk or with players.
- Motion: none; audio only plays on click and never autoplays.
- Why it fits now: producers and game studios hire from credit lists, and a serious serif with clean tables reads as established without film-trailer clichés (example: [Anna Meredith](https://www.annameredith.com/)).
**Style variations:** Synth: #101418 bg, #7FD1C7 accent · Orchestral: #F3EFE6 bg, #6B1F1F accent · Pencil: greyscale only
**Refs:**
- [Austin Wintory: Videogames](https://www.austinwintory.com/projects-videogames): cover grid of featured games above a complete year-by-year credits list with studio and role.
- [Ólafur Arnalds: Works](https://olafurarnalds.com/works/): works split into solo, collaboration and film/art tabs with year and listen links.
- [Jessica Curry](https://www.jessicacurry.co.uk/): composer site that places games, projects, presenting and a store side by side.

<a id="042"></a>
#### 042 · Classical Ensemble / Chamber Group (`quartet`)
**For:** chamber ensembles, early-music groups and choirs that run a season, tour, record and do learning work.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-event (diary) · single-event · taxonomy-city · archive-recording (discography) · page-editions · page-musicians · page-learning · archive-learning-project · page-support · page-about · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** diary grouped by month (date, time, venue with address, city, programme), city tags (Edinburgh / Glasgow / Perth / London), concert page with programme set as composer in bold then work title, booking link to the venue, "Add to calendar" (Google, iCal, Outlook), relaxed performance and open rehearsal tags, musicians list, discography with label and catalogue number, performing editions page, learning projects (e.g. a children's Messiah), support/friends scheme, news.
**Content model:** `concert` (datetime, venue, city taxonomy, programme rows: composer + work + optional year, performers, ticket_url, tags). `recording` (label, date, cat_no, links). `musician` (instrument).
**Plugins:** The Events Calendar (iCal export and month grouping), GiveWP (friends scheme).
**Signature:** a programme block that sets each work as composer in bold followed by the work title, used on every concert page (seen on: [Hebrides Ensemble: Scotland's composers 1](https://www.hebridesensemble.com/events/event/wigmore-hall-scotlands-composers-1/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Calendar export (Google, iCal, Outlook) on the diary (seen on: [Dunedin Consort: Diary](https://www.dunedin-consort.org.uk/diary/))
- Relaxed performances and open rehearsals tagged in the diary (seen on: [Dunedin Consort: Diary](https://www.dunedin-consort.org.uk/diary/))
- City tags so audiences in each town can see only their concerts (seen on: [Dunedin Consort: Edinburgh](https://www.dunedin-consort.org.uk/diary/tag/edinburgh/))
- Learning project page with dates for schools and families (seen on: [Dunedin Consort: Children's Messiah](https://www.dunedin-consort.org.uk/learning-and-participation/childrens-messiah/))
- Discography with label and catalogue number for each album, e.g. Signum SIGCD938 (seen on: [Fretwork: Discography](https://www.fretwork.co.uk/discography))
**Real-world basis:** [Hebrides Ensemble: Events](https://www.hebridesensemble.com/events/) · [Hebrides Ensemble: Scotland's composers 1](https://www.hebridesensemble.com/events/event/wigmore-hall-scotlands-composers-1/) · [Dunedin Consort: Diary](https://www.dunedin-consort.org.uk/diary/) · [Dunedin Consort: Editions](https://www.dunedin-consort.org.uk/editions/) · [Fretwork](https://www.fretwork.co.uk/)
**Style: Concert-hall bill (display serif, strict programme columns)**
- Type: headings Libre Caslon Display 400 at 88px, body Karla 400 at 18px/1.6, composer names Karla 700 at 18px, dates Karla 500 tabular.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #1A1A1A, accent #7A1F2B (hall claret, for booking links), surface #F3F1EC, line #1A1A1A.
- Layout: diary as month headings with rows (date / venue and city / programme / book); concert page as a 5/7 split with facts left and programme right; programme rows aligned so composer names form a column; square corners, 1px rules.
- Imagery: photos of the players in rehearsal and in the venue, landscape 3:2; no instrument clip-art.
- Motion: none; month headings stay sticky while scrolling the diary, inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
- Why it fits now: ensemble audiences scan by date, town and programme, and a printed-bill layout with a strong serif carries the tradition without looking dated (example: [Dunedin Consort: Diary](https://www.dunedin-consort.org.uk/diary/)).
**Style variations:** Baroque: #F2EEE4 bg, #5A3E1B accent · Modern: #FFFFFF bg, #0F4C81 accent · Night concert: #16161A bg, #F3F1EC type
**Refs:**
- [Dunedin Consort: Diary](https://www.dunedin-consort.org.uk/diary/): WordPress diary grouped by month with city tags, calendar exports, relaxed performances and open rehearsals.
- [Hebrides Ensemble: Scotland's composers 1](https://www.hebridesensemble.com/events/event/wigmore-hall-scotlands-composers-1/): concert page with the programme set as composer then work, venue address and booking link.
- [Fretwork: Discography](https://www.fretwork.co.uk/discography): album covers with label catalogue numbers and buy/stream links.

#### 043 · Music Teacher / Lessons (`scale`)
**For:** independent instrument and voice teachers, and small community music schools with 2–20 teachers.
**Templates:** front-page · page-private-lessons (instruments, lengths, tuition) · page-faculty · archive-course (self-paced library) · single-course · page-membership · page-recitals · page-register · page-policies
**Patterns (~40):** instruments-taught index, lesson-length × tuition table (30 / 45 / 60 min, per lesson and per term), "Book a trial lesson" enquiry, term dates strip, faculty grid with instruments and styles, course cards filterable by style and level, free-lessons teaser row, membership explainer (monthly / annual), monthly recital announcement, cancellation and make-up policy, parent FAQ.
**Content model:** Sensei courses and lessons for the self-paced library (taxonomies: `style`, `level`); companion `teacher` (instruments, styles, bio, availability); term dates as a simple options page.
**Plugins:** Sensei LMS, Query Filter (style/level on the course archive), Jetpack Forms (trial-lesson enquiry), optional Cal.com embed for online slots.
**Signature:** a self-paced course library filterable by music style and level, sitting next to the live-lesson offer and a free-lessons tier (seen on: [Piano With Jonny: Courses](https://pianowithjonny.com/courses/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Tuition table showing per-lesson and per-term totals with term length stated ("35 weeks") (seen on: [Brooklyn Music School](https://www.brooklynmusicschool.org/private-lessons))
- Cancellation rule printed next to the prices ("24 hours' notice, same-day cancellations are non-refundable") (seen on: [Brooklyn Music School](https://www.brooklynmusicschool.org/private-lessons))
- "Currently taking new students: yes / waiting list" toggle per teacher
- Term-dates and half-term closure bar that switches off after the last date
- Next student recital date with a "bring a friend" note (seen on: [Brooklyn Music School](https://www.brooklynmusicschool.org/private-lessons))
**Real-world basis:** [Brooklyn Music School: Private lessons](https://www.brooklynmusicschool.org/private-lessons), [Brooklyn Music School: Faculty](https://www.brooklynmusicschool.org/faculty-and-staff), [Piano With Jonny: Courses](https://pianowithjonny.com/courses/), [Piano With Jonny: Membership](https://pianowithjonny.com/membership/), [Open Studio: Courses](https://www.openstudiojazz.com/courses/)
**Style: Conservatoire editorial serif**
- Type: Headings: Piazzolla 600 (optical size 30), tracking -0.01em; body: Source Serif 4 400/19px; labels and tuition figures: IBM Plex Mono 500, tabular numerals
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #1B1A17 / accent #1D5C3F (practice-room felt green) / surface #EEF1EC / line #C9CFC8
- Layout: 12-col grid with a wide left margin used for instrument names like marginalia; hairline 1px rules instead of cards; square corners; sticky top bar with "Book a trial" as the only button; home page = instruments index → tuition table → teachers → recital date
- Imagery: close crops of hands on instruments, natural window light, 4:5 portrait crops; no stock "happy child with violin"
- Motion: none on scroll; tuition table rows get an underline on hover; View Transitions between course cards and course pages; all disabled under prefers-reduced-motion
- Why it fits now: serif-led, quiet classical music sites have replaced glossy academy templates; see [Wigmore Hall](https://www.wigmore-hall.org.uk/)
**Style variations:** Garage: black bg, amp-orange #FF5A1F accent · Kids: cream bg, big primary crayon colours · Stave: white, five-line rules as dividers
**Refs:**
- [Brooklyn Music School: Private lessons](https://www.brooklynmusicschool.org/private-lessons): honest tuition table, trial-lesson flow, cancellation rules and recital perks on one page
- [Piano With Jonny: Courses](https://pianowithjonny.com/courses/): WordPress course archive filtered by style (blues, jazz ballads, gospel) with level badges; the model for the Sensei library
- [Open Studio: Courses](https://www.openstudiojazz.com/courses/): course cards led by the teacher's name and instrument, useful for multi-teacher schools

#### 044 · Recording Studio (`booth`)
**For:** independent recording, mixing and rehearsal studios, and freelance mastering engineers.
**Templates:** front-page · page-studios-overview · single-room (Studio A / Studio B) · page-equipment · page-booking-rates · page-engineers · page-clients (discography) · page-visit (directions, parking, load-in)
**Patterns (~40):** room page (floor plan, dimensions, console, tape machines, piano), equipment list by category (Consoles / Microphones / Recorders / Outboard / Instruments & Amps / Pedals), "shared between rooms" note, day-rate and half-day table with engineer included / not included, deposit and cancellation terms, engineer bios with credits, client discography cover grid, load-in and parking map, booking enquiry form.
**Content model:** companion `room` (dimensions, console, rate_day, rate_half); `gear` CPT with taxonomy `gear_category` and a `room` relation (or "shared").
**Plugins:** Query Filter (gear by category and room), Jetpack Forms (booking enquiry), optional Cal.com for rehearsal-room slots.
**Signature:** an equipment inventory grouped by category, split into per-room and shared items, with a plain-text version for engineers to download (seen on: [Electrical Audio: Equipment](https://www.electricalaudio.com/equipment)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- "Text-only gear list" download link for engineers planning a session (seen on: [Electrical Audio](https://www.electricalaudio.com/equipment))
- "We can source gear not on the list" note on the equipment page (seen on: [Electrical Audio](https://www.electricalaudio.com/equipment))
- Deposit and cancellation policy block next to the rates (seen on: [Electrical Audio: Booking and rates](https://www.electricalaudio.com/booking-rates))
- "Next available dates" line that the owner updates weekly
- Load-in notes: stairs, lift, parking, nearest hardware shop
**Real-world basis:** [Electrical Audio: Equipment](https://www.electricalaudio.com/equipment), [Electrical Audio: Studio A](https://www.electricalaudio.com/studio-a), [Electrical Audio: Booking and rates](https://www.electricalaudio.com/booking-rates), [The Bunker Studio: Studio A equipment](https://www.thebunkerstudio.com/studio-a-equipment), [Tarbox Road Studios: Equipment](https://tarboxroadstudios.com/equipment.html)
**Style: Utility / industrial signage**
- Type: Headings: Tektur 800 (wdth 100), uppercase; body: IBM Plex Sans 400/18px; gear model numbers and rates: JetBrains Mono 500
- Palette: bg #EDEBE6 (console grey) / text #111111 / accent #FF4F00 (record-light orange) / surface #FFFFFF / line #1A1A1A
- Layout: dense 4-col spec grid with 2px black rules, like a rack; square corners; left-hand sticky index of gear categories; home page = room photos full-bleed → rates table → gear categories as a panel of labelled buttons
- Imagery: flat-lit room photos at 3:2, console and patch-bay details in black and white, tape-box scans as texture
- Motion: category index highlights as you scroll (scroll-driven, CSS only); rate rows light up like a channel strip on hover; reduced-motion removes both
- Why it fits now: industrial product-manual design (spec tables, orange signal colour) is the current look for audio gear; see [teenage engineering](https://teenage.engineering/)
**Style variations:** Tape: cream bg, tape-box typewriter labels · Console: charcoal bg, VU-green accents · Live Room: warm wood tones, serif headings
**Refs:**
- [Electrical Audio: Equipment](https://www.electricalaudio.com/equipment): the best-organised studio gear list online: six categories, room vs shared, plus a text-only list
- [Electrical Audio: Booking and rates](https://www.electricalaudio.com/booking-rates): plain, trustworthy rate page with deposits, engineer fees and policies spelled out
- [Tarbox Road Studios: Equipment](https://tarboxroadstudios.com/equipment.html): long single-page gear inventory that shows how engineers actually scan these lists

#### 045 · DIY Music Venue / Club Night (`venue`)
**For:** small venues, members' clubs, co-op run spaces and club-night promoters.
**Templates:** front-page (listings) · archive-event (list / month / day views) · single-event · page-past-events (archive) · page-membership · page-safer-spaces · page-hire · page-access · page-visit
**Patterns (~45):** listing row (date / title / support / doors / price adv & door / ticket link), "Tonight" row, list / month / day view switch, past events archive, event page (line-up, times, price, age policy, ticket button), age policy line ("All ages, under-16s with an adult"), refund / exchange policy, access line (standing venue, chairs on request), safer spaces agreement, membership and "members and guests only" notice, venue hire with capacity and tech spec, mailing list.
**Content model:** The Events Calendar events (date, doors, venue, cost) with companion meta: `support`, `age_policy`, `status` (on sale / low tickets / sold out / cancelled), `genre` taxonomy.
**Plugins:** The Events Calendar (list, month and day views, iCal), or companion `event` CPT + Advanced Query Loop for a lighter build.
**Signature:** one listings page with List / Month / Day views and a "Previous events" archive that past gigs roll into automatically, plus iCal export (seen on: [Wharf Chambers: Events](https://wharfchambers.org/events/list/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Age policy and access notes as fields on every event (seen on: [Ramsgate Music Hall: Red Snapper](https://www.ramsgatemusichall.com/tc-events/red-snapper/))
- "No refunds, but we'll swap your ticket for another show" policy line (seen on: [Ramsgate Music Hall](https://www.ramsgatemusichall.com/tc-events/red-snapper/))
- Low tickets / sold out / cancelled stamps on listing rows
- "Members and guests only" licensing notice with a join link (seen on: [Wharf Chambers](https://wharfchambers.org/events/list/))
- Add-to-calendar / subscribe-to-listings iCal feed (seen on: [Wharf Chambers](https://wharfchambers.org/events/list/))
**Real-world basis:** [Wharf Chambers: Events list](https://wharfchambers.org/events/list/), [Wharf Chambers: Past events](https://wharfchambers.org/events/list/?eventDisplay=past), [The Windmill Brixton: event page](https://www.windmillbrixton.co.uk/events/2026-10-11-the-no-frills-folk-club-the-windmill), [Cafe OTO: Event listings](https://www.cafeoto.co.uk/events/), [Ramsgate Music Hall: event page](https://www.ramsgatemusichall.com/tc-events/red-snapper/)
**Style: Xerox punk flyer**
- Type: Headings: Anton 400 uppercase, set huge; dates: Big Shoulders Display 900; body: IBM Plex Sans Condensed 400/18px; price and door times: Martian Mono 600
- Palette: bg #F2F0EA (photocopy white) / text #0A0A0A / accent #FF2E88 (fluoro pink) / surface #FFE600 (hi-vis flyer yellow) / line #0A0A0A
- Layout: full-width listing rows split by 3px black rules; date column fixed at left in giant numerals; flyer images only on the event page and in the optional "flyer wall" view; square everything; top nav = Listings / Past / Membership / Hire / Visit
- Imagery: flyers shown as-is at their own aspect ratio; venue photos as high-contrast 1-bit halftone, square corners
- Motion: listing rows invert (black bg, white text) on hover to confirm they are links; View Transition from row to event page; no scroll effects; all inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference
- Why it fits now: DIY venues have returned to text-first listings with photocopy energy rather than slick ticketing layouts; see [The Windmill Brixton](https://www.windmillbrixton.co.uk/)
**Style variations:** Basement: black bg, acid #D4FF3A dates · Warehouse: concrete grey, stencil headings · Pub Backroom: cream, red serif chalkboard
**Refs:**
- [Wharf Chambers: Events list](https://wharfchambers.org/events/list/): WordPress + The Events Calendar used by a co-op venue: list/month/day views, past events, membership notice
- [Cafe OTO: Event listings](https://www.cafeoto.co.uk/events/): dense, typographic listings with a deep [archive](https://www.cafeoto.co.uk/events/archive/); proof that a text list beats a flyer grid
- [Ramsgate Music Hall: event page](https://www.ramsgatemusichall.com/tc-events/red-snapper/): every practical field a gig-goer needs: times, price incl. fees, age rule, seating, refund swap

#### 046 · Community / Online Radio Station (`freq`)
**For:** community, internet and freeform radio stations run by volunteers and residents.
**Templates:** front-page (live player + today) · page-schedule (week) · archive-show · single-show · archive-episode (listen back) · single-episode · archive-genre · page-support · page-submit-a-show
**Patterns (~45):** persistent live player bar (now playing / next up), "Playing this week" schedule with day tabs, timezone line ("All times Brussels CET/CEST"), show cards (name, host, genre tags, slot), episode archive with Mixcloud/SoundCloud embeds and tracklists, genre index, residents grid, guest mix series, donate / membership, submit-a-show call-out, newsletter.
**Content model:** companion `show` (weekday, start, end, hosts, genre), `episode` (show relation, air date, embed URL, tracklist), taxonomy `genre`.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (today / this week by meta), Query Filter (genre), Jetpack Donations or GiveWP.
**Signature:** a weekly schedule computed from show slots, with a stated station timezone and a "live now / up next" player bar (seen on: [Kiosk Radio: Schedule](https://www.kioskradio.com/schedule), [Resonance FM: Schedules](https://www.resonancefm.com/schedule)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Station timezone printed on the schedule, plus visitor's local time on hover (seen on: [Kiosk Radio](https://www.kioskradio.com/schedule))
- Day-by-day schedule URLs so a single day can be shared (seen on: [Resonance FM](https://www.resonancefm.com/schedule))
- "Listen back" archive grouped by show and genre (seen on: [Cashmere Radio: Listen](https://cashmereradio.com/listen/))
- Off-air / maintenance banner with a scheduled end time
- Donate link that states what it pays for (licensing, rent, streaming)
**Real-world basis:** [Kiosk Radio: Schedule](https://www.kioskradio.com/schedule), [Resonance FM: Schedules](https://www.resonancefm.com/schedule), [Noods Radio: Shows](https://www.noodsradio.com/shows), [Refuge Worldwide: Radio](https://refugeworldwide.com/radio), [Cashmere Radio: Listen](https://cashmereradio.com/listen/)
**Style: Swiss neo-grotesk index**
- Type: Headings: Radio Canada 700, tracking -0.02em at display sizes only; body: Radio Canada 400/18px; times and frequencies: DM Mono 500 tabular
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #000000 / accent #0038FF (signal blue) / surface #F2F2F2 / line #000000 / live #FF3B00
- Layout: strict 6-col grid; schedule as a table of times × shows with 1px black rules; player bar fixed to the bottom, full-width, black; home page = live player → today's schedule → latest episodes as a text index, not cards
- Imagery: show artwork in square 1:1 tiles, black-and-white until hover; no gradients
- Motion: no pulsing; the current slot is marked with a static red square and the word LIVE, driven by the real schedule; the schedule scrolls the current hour into view on load only when prefers-reduced-motion is no-preference
- Why it fits now: independent radio has settled on stark, grid-based index sites that feel like a printed programme; see [Refuge Worldwide](https://refugeworldwide.com/)
**Style variations:** Pirate: black bg, stencil type, red · FM: cream bg, dial-scale ruler graphics · Late Night: navy bg, amber monospace
**Refs:**
- [Resonance FM: Schedules](https://www.resonancefm.com/schedule): plain daily schedule with dated URLs, how a volunteer station actually publishes its week
- [Kiosk Radio: Schedule](https://www.kioskradio.com/schedule): "Playing this week" schedule with an explicit station timezone
- [Noods Radio: Shows](https://www.noodsradio.com/shows): long residents/shows index that works as the station's directory

<a id="047"></a>
#### 047 · Podcast (`episode`)
**For:** independent podcasts and small podcast networks.
**Templates:** front-page (latest episode) · archive-episode · single-episode · page-episode-index · page-transcripts · page-about · page-subscribe · page-support
**Patterns (~40):** latest-episode hero with player, "listen on" row (Apple / Spotify / Pocket Casts / RSS), numbered episode list, show notes with links, timestamped chapter list, full transcript (on page or linked), content note ("mild profanity"), guest card, word-of-the-episode box, support tiers (Patreon / membership: ad-free feed), sponsor read with codes, episode index by season, prev/next episode.
**Content model:** Seriously Simple Podcasting episodes (number, season, duration, audio) + companion meta `chapters` (time, title) and `transcript` (rich text or PDF).
**Plugins:** Seriously Simple Podcasting, Jetpack Paid Content (optional member feed).
**Signature:** timestamped chapters in the show notes that seek the player, with separate "Show notes" and "Transcript" views (seen on: [Syntax: episode 1033](https://syntax.fm/show/1033/8-new-css-js-and-html-features-you-should-know)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Content note line under the player (seen on: [The Allusionist: Hues](https://www.theallusionist.org/allusionist/hues))
- Downloadable transcript PDF per episode (seen on: [Song Exploder](https://songexploder.net/))
- Separate transcript URL per episode for search and accessibility (seen on: [99% Invisible](https://99percentinvisible.org/episode/679-the-bone-wars/transcript))
- Full episode index page, one line per episode (seen on: [Song Exploder: Episode index](https://songexploder.net/episode-index))
- "Recording break until 3 March" hiatus banner with an end date
**Real-world basis:** [Syntax: episode page](https://syntax.fm/show/1033/8-new-css-js-and-html-features-you-should-know), [The Allusionist: Hues](https://www.theallusionist.org/allusionist/hues), [Song Exploder: Episode index](https://songexploder.net/episode-index), [99% Invisible: transcript page](https://99percentinvisible.org/episode/679-the-bone-wars/transcript), [Twenty Thousand Hertz: Episodes](https://www.20k.org/episodes-archive)
**Style: Editorial serif revival**
- Type: Headings: Yeseva One 400; episode numbers: Yeseva One at 18vw; body: Newsreader 400/19px; UI and timestamps: Martian Mono 500
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #161412 / accent #D7261E (on-air lamp red) / surface #F1F1EF / line #C8C8C4
- Layout: single reading column (66ch) with running heads, bylines and captions; chapters in a sticky right rail on wide screens; episode list as a numbered typographic index; square player bar; home page = giant episode number + title + player → recent index
- Imagery: one cover art per episode at 1:1; guest portraits in duotone (text colour + paper)
- Motion: active chapter underlines as audio plays; transcript paragraph highlights at the current time; both static under prefers-reduced-motion
- Why it fits now: narrative podcasts now present like magazines, serif-led and text-rich because transcripts matter for search and access; see [The Paris Review](https://www.theparisreview.org/)
**Style variations:** Talk: white bg, black grotesk, red dot · Radio Drama: black bg, cream serif · Interview: paper bg, two-tone speaker colours
**Refs:**
- [Syntax: episode page](https://syntax.fm/show/1033/8-new-css-js-and-html-features-you-should-know): clickable timestamp chapters plus a transcript view; the exact signature feature
- [The Allusionist: Hues](https://www.theallusionist.org/allusionist/hues): a small indie show's episode page: content note, show notes, transcript link, Patreon tiers
- [Song Exploder: Episode index](https://songexploder.net/episode-index): WordPress podcast with a one-line-per-episode index and transcript PDFs

<a id="048"></a>
#### 048 · Small / DIY Music Festival (`field`)
**For:** grassroots and arts-led festivals of 500–5,000 people.
**Templates:** front-page · page-line-up (filterable) · single-artist · page-programme (stage × time grid) · page-programme-accessible (plain text) · page-tickets · page-practical-info · page-access · page-getting-here · page-volunteer · page-archive (past editions)
**Patterns (~50):** line-up list with category filters (Music / Comedy / Cinema / Literature / DJs & Late Night / Extras), artist page (bio, stage, day, time, listen embed), stage × time programme grid, plain-text accessible programme, "changes to the printed programme" list, ticket types (weekend / day / concession / under-12), practical info (camping, what to bring, re-entry), access info (viewing platforms, access tickets, quiet areas), getting there (shuttle, train, car share), volunteer call, open call for artists, past editions archive, festival zine download.
**Content model:** companion `artist` (category, day, stage, start, end, links), taxonomy `stage`, taxonomy `edition` (year).
**Plugins:** Query Filter (category, day), Advanced Query Loop (by start time), Jetpack Forms (volunteer, open call); tickets via external ticketing embed.
**Signature:** a stage × time programme grid with a separate plain-text accessible programme generated from the same data (seen on: [Supernormal: Schedule](https://www.supernormalfestival.co.uk/programme/schedule), [Supernormal: Accessible programme](https://www.supernormalfestival.co.uk/programme/accessible)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- "Changes since the printed programme" list, dated (seen on: [Supernormal](https://www.supernormalfestival.co.uk/programme/schedule))
- Printable programme image for phones without signal (seen on: [Supernormal](https://www.supernormalfestival.co.uk/programme/schedule))
- Line-up filters by strand with a reset button (seen on: [End of the Road: Line-up](https://endoftheroadfestival.com/line-up/))
- Detailed access page (access tickets, PA ticket, platforms) (seen on: [Le Guess Who?: Accessibility](https://leguesswho.com/accessibility))
- "Tier 2 tickets sold out, tier 3 on sale" status bar
**Real-world basis:** [Supernormal: Schedule](https://www.supernormalfestival.co.uk/programme/schedule), [Supernormal: Practical info](https://www.supernormalfestival.co.uk/page/practical-info), [End of the Road: Line-up](https://endoftheroadfestival.com/line-up/), [End of the Road: Accessibility](https://endoftheroadfestival.com/accessibility/), [Le Guess Who?: Line-up](https://leguesswho.com/lineup)
**Style: Kinetic variable-type maximalism**
- Type: Headings and line-up: Asap variable (wdth 75–125, wght 200–800), names sized by billing via three preset sizes; body: Hanken Grotesk 400/18px; set times: Martian Mono 400
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #14210F (hedge green-black) / accent #FF6A13 (wristband orange) / surface #DDEBC8 (field green) / line #14210F
- Layout: line-up page as a centred text poster (rows of names separated by slashes, sized by tier); programme as a horizontally scrolling grid with sticky stage names; hand-drawn site map as SVG; nav = Line-up / Programme / Tickets / Info / Access
- Imagery: crowd and site photos with visible grain at 3:2; artist images in single-colour duotone per day
- Motion: artist names tighten width on hover to confirm the link (variable wdth axis, transform-free); the programme grid scrolls to the current set time during the festival; everything static under prefers-reduced-motion
- Why it fits now: arts festivals have moved to type-only line-up posters with variable fonts and loud colour; see [Le Guess Who?](https://leguesswho.com/lineup)
**Style variations:** Forest: moss green bg, cream type · City: concrete grey, safety-yellow accent · After Dark: black bg, UV-lilac names
**Refs:**
- [Supernormal: Schedule](https://www.supernormalfestival.co.uk/programme/schedule): stage × time grid, accessible text version and programme-change notes from an artist-led festival
- [End of the Road: Line-up](https://endoftheroadfestival.com/line-up/): WordPress line-up with strand filters (Music, Comedy, Cinema, Literature) that small festivals can copy
- [Le Guess Who?: Accessibility](https://leguesswho.com/accessibility): thorough, plainly written access page to model the `page-access` template on

<a id="049"></a>
#### 049 · Sound Artist / Field Recordist (`drone`)
**For:** sound artists, field recordists, acoustic ecologists and experimental musicians.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-work · single-work (installation / composition / release) · page-sound-map · page-releases · page-workshops · page-texts (writings, scores) · page-shop (microphones, editions) · page-about
**Patterns (~35):** work page led by an audio player, recording metadata (location, date, equipment), sound map with pins that play recordings, releases / discography list, installation documentation with photos, workshops and listening walks with dates, writings and published texts list, score PDF download, small shop for editions or handmade microphones, mentoring / lectures list.
**Content model:** companion `work` (type: installation / composition / release / recording, year, location lat/lng, audio file, equipment), taxonomy `place`.
**Plugins:** Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap, optional WooCommerce for editions and microphones.
**Signature:** a sound map where each pin opens a player for the recording made at that place (seen on: [Cities and Memory: Sound map](https://citiesandmemory.com/sound-map/), [radio aporee: maps](https://aporee.org/maps/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Recording details line: date, time of day, microphone, weather
- Listening-walk and workshop dates with "places left" (seen on: [Jez riley French](https://jezrileyfrench.co.uk/))
- Headphones recommended notice on audio-heavy pages
- Score or text PDF downloads next to each work
- Small shop for handmade microphones or editions (seen on: [Jez riley French](https://jezrileyfrench.co.uk/))
**Real-world basis:** [Cities and Memory: Sound map](https://citiesandmemory.com/sound-map/), [radio aporee: maps](https://aporee.org/maps/), [Jez riley French](https://jezrileyfrench.co.uk/), [Hildegard Westerkamp: SoundWork](https://www.hildegardwesterkamp.ca/sound/), [Chris Watson](https://chriswatson.net/)
**Style: Graphic-score minimal**
- Type: Headings: Epilogue 200, lowercase, tracking +0.01em; body: EB Garamond 400/20px for texts; metadata: IBM Plex Mono 400
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #1A1A1A / accent #3A5BA0 (score blue pencil) / surface #F5F5F2 / line #BDBDBD
- Layout: asymmetric, lots of white space; works listed as a long typographic index with year in the margin; map full-bleed with minimal pins (small black dots); work pages centre the player and a waveform/spectrogram image
- Imagery: spectrograms and graphic scores as the main visuals; photos of places in muted, desaturated colour at wide 21:9
- Motion: the playing pin turns solid accent (no pulsing); waveform progress fills left to right as a transform; progress shown as a static time readout under prefers-reduced-motion
- Why it fits now: sound artists favour quiet, text-led pages that put the audio first; see [Hildegard Westerkamp: SoundWork](https://www.hildegardwesterkamp.ca/sound/)
**Style variations:** Score: white bg, Cardew-style black marks · Field: moss #5E6B3A on linen · Tape Loop: brown tape #6B3E26, cream type
**Refs:**
- [Cities and Memory: Sound map](https://citiesandmemory.com/sound-map/): WordPress-built global sound map, each point with a field recording and a reimagined piece
- [radio aporee: maps](https://aporee.org/maps/): the classic open field-recording map on OpenStreetMap; click a pin, the sound plays
- [Jez riley French](https://jezrileyfrench.co.uk/): a working field recordist's site: works, releases, workshops and a microphone shop in one plain index

### VI. Performance

<a id="050"></a>
#### 050 · Theatre Company (`stage`)
**For:** independent, touring and new-writing theatre companies.
**Templates:** front-page · page-whats-on · archive-production · single-production · page-tour-dates · page-access · page-get-involved (young company, workshops, training) · page-support-us · page-about · page-policies (touring rider, inclusivity)
**Patterns (~50):** production hero (title, writer, director, trailer), tour dates list (venue, town, dates, "Buy tickets" to the venue), past productions archive, cast and creative team credits, co-producers and funders line, press quotes, access guides downloads (visual story, screen-reader version), access line per production (BSL / captions / audio description integrated), young company and workshops, artist development call-outs, support us / donate, anti-racism touring rider and policy pages, mailing list.
**Content model:** companion `production` (writer, director, year, status: current / touring / past, access notes, visual story PDF), `performance` (production relation, venue, town, start, end, ticket URL, access type), taxonomy `access_type`.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (current vs past tour dates), GiveWP or Jetpack Donations.
**Signature:** production pages with a tour dates list that links out to each venue's box office, plus downloadable access guides (visual story and screen-reader formats) (seen on: [Paines Plough: Sapling](https://painesplough.com/productions/sapling/), [Graeae: Romeo and Juliet](https://graeae.org/event/romeo-and-juliet/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Visual story PDF and screen-reader version per production (seen on: [Graeae](https://graeae.org/event/romeo-and-juliet/))
- Tour dates that move to "past" automatically, with the production staying in the archive (seen on: [Fuel: FLIP!](https://fueltheatre.com/projects/flip/))
- Content guidance and age recommendation fields near the dates
- Touring rider and policy pages linked from the footer (seen on: [Paines Plough](https://painesplough.com/anti-racism-touring-rider/))
- Separate tour dates page across all productions (seen on: [Forced Entertainment: Tour dates](https://www.forcedentertainment.com/tour-dates/))
**Real-world basis:** [Paines Plough: Sapling](https://painesplough.com/productions/sapling/), [Graeae: What's on](https://graeae.org/whats-on/), [Graeae: Romeo and Juliet](https://graeae.org/event/romeo-and-juliet/), [Fuel: FLIP!](https://fueltheatre.com/projects/flip/), [Forced Entertainment: Tour dates](https://www.forcedentertainment.com/tour-dates/)
**Style: Playbill letterpress poster**
- Type: Headings: Rozha One 400 (heavy high-contrast display serif) at poster sizes; credit roles: Work Sans 700; body: Work Sans 400/18px
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #121212 / accent #A4161A (house-curtain red) / surface #ECEBE7 (newsprint) / line #121212
- Layout: each production page composed like a playbill: centred title stack, credits in two tight columns, tour dates as a ruled table; 12-col grid; hairline rules; square buttons; home page = current production poster full-bleed → tour dates → get involved
- Imagery: production photography in high-contrast black and white with one spot colour per production; rehearsal photos at 3:2
- Motion: tour date rows reveal venue address on hover; View Transitions from archive poster to production page; none under prefers-reduced-motion
- Why it fits now: touring companies are returning to poster-like typographic identities that work in print and on screen; see [Forced Entertainment](https://www.forcedentertainment.com/)
**Style variations:** Blackbox: black bg, white serif · Fringe: fluoro yellow, condensed grotesk · Proscenium: deep red, gold hairlines
**Refs:**
- [Paines Plough: Sapling](https://painesplough.com/productions/sapling/): WordPress production page with clean tour-dates-to-venue ticket links and creative credits
- [Graeae: Romeo and Juliet](https://graeae.org/event/romeo-and-juliet/): access guides (visual and screen-reader) built into the production page by a Deaf- and disabled-led company
- [Forced Entertainment: Tour dates](https://www.forcedentertainment.com/tour-dates/): company-wide tour dates page across a large production archive

> **Note on scope:** ideas 01–50 cover creative fields. From 51 onward the list moves deliberately toward everyday independent sites: shops, food, trades, health, education, tech, civic groups, sport, and personal sites. The brutalist flare stays and gets applied to ordinary things: a plumber's site in Swiss grid and a bakery in riso colours. That mix is how the library stands apart.

### VII. Writing, knowledge & local media

<a id="051"></a>
#### 051 · Novelist / Author (`spine`)
**For:** novelists and non-fiction authors with 1–10 books, usually with an agent and a publisher.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-book (books in order) · single-book · page-buy (all retailers, all editions) · page-book-groups · page-events · page-newsletter (with archive) · page-about · page-contact (agent, publicist, rights)
**Patterns (~40):** new-book hero with cover and one "Buy the book" action, books-in-order list (series and standalone), buy block per book (local indie via IndieBound / Bookshop.org first, then Amazon, Barnes & Noble, Apple Books, Kobo), signed copies from a named bookshop, international editions (UK/ANZ, Canada) and translations list, praise quotes with source, read an excerpt, book-group guide with discussion questions, events list, newsletter sign-up with past issues, contact routed to agent / publicist / film rights.
**Content model:** companion `book` (series, order, pub date, publisher, ISBN, formats, retailer links repeater, signed-copy shop, excerpt, guide PDF), taxonomy `edition_region`.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Newsletter, Advanced Query Loop (upcoming vs past events).
**Signature:** a per-book "Buy" block that lists the local independent bookshop and Bookshop.org before the big retailers, adds a named shop for signed copies, and separates international editions (seen on: [Celeste Ng: Buy](https://www.celesteng.com/buy)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Signed and personalised copies through one named indie bookshop (seen on: [Celeste Ng: Buy](https://www.celesteng.com/buy))
- Book-group page with downloadable discussion questions (seen on: [Celeste Ng: For book groups](https://www.celesteng.com/book-groups))
- "Books in order" list for readers who ask which to read first (seen on: [Emily St. John Mandel: Books](https://www.emilymandel.com/books))
- Newsletter archive page so the sign-up has proof behind it (seen on: [Robin Sloan: Newsletter archive](https://www.robinsloan.com/newsletters/))
- Press and rights contacts split by role (agent / publicist / film and TV) with no public email scraping
**Real-world basis:** [Celeste Ng: Buy](https://www.celesteng.com/buy), [Celeste Ng: Book groups](https://www.celesteng.com/book-groups), [Emily St. John Mandel: Books](https://www.emilymandel.com/books), [Robin Sloan: Penumbra](https://www.robinsloan.com/books/penumbra/), [Olivia Laing: Books](https://www.olivialaing.com/books)
**Style: Modernist paperback grid**
- Type: Headings: Cabin 700 (Johnston/Gill lineage, like mid-century paperbacks), tracking 0; body: Literata 400/19px; ISBNs and dates: IBM Plex Mono 400
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #1C1C1C / accent #E8641B (paperback band orange, swapped per book) / surface #F2F0EC / line #1C1C1C
- Layout: every book page built on the three-band paperback grid (colour band / white title panel / colour band); books archive as a strict 4-col shelf of flat covers, no 3D tilt; retailer buttons as a ruled list, not pills; colophon line (typefaces, printer, edition) in the footer
- Imagery: flat cover scans at 2:3; author portrait once, in black and white; no mock-up books on tables
- Motion: the band colour shifts to the book's own colour via View Transitions when moving from archive to book page; nothing else moves; off under prefers-reduced-motion
- Why it fits now: authors are moving away from template author sites toward typographic, publisher-grade pages; see [Robin Sloan](https://www.robinsloan.com/)
**Style variations:** Hardback: cloth-grey bg, foil-gold rules · Pulp: yellow bg, condensed red titles · Crime: black bands, white serif
**Refs:**
- [Celeste Ng: Buy](https://www.celesteng.com/buy): indie-first retailer order, signed copies via Porter Square Books, and international editions on one page
- [Celeste Ng: For book groups](https://www.celesteng.com/book-groups): the book-group guide pattern authors actually use
- [Emily St. John Mandel: Books](https://www.emilymandel.com/books): clear books-in-order page with buy links per title

<a id="052"></a>
#### 052 · Independent Journalist / Paid Newsletter (`dispatch`)
**For:** reporters and writers who left a newsroom or Substack and run a paid publication on their own domain.
**Templates:** front-page (latest + sign-up) · archive (posts) · single (free / members-only) · page-membership (tiers) · page-signup · page-about · page-archive-by-year · page-subscriber-goals · page-podcast (optional)
**Patterns (~35):** sign-up box with one email field, membership tiers as a plain comparison list (Free / Supporter monthly or yearly / Superfan), "what you get" list (ad-free, full archive, full-text RSS, comments, bonus podcast), members-only divider inside posts, byline and dateline, corrections note, archive by year, public subscriber-goals post (revenue and what it pays for), institutional / group subscription note, gift subscription, podcast feed for members.
**Content model:** posts + pages; Jetpack Paid Content tiers; post meta `access` (free / members), `dateline`.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Newsletter + Paid Content (or MailPoet for sending).
**Signature:** a membership page that lists each tier's price per month and per year with concrete perks (ad-free, full-text RSS, early ad-free podcast, comments), paired with an inline "members only" break in posts (seen on: [404 Media: Membership](https://www.404media.co/membership/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Public subscriber-goals post: how many paying readers the site needs and what each milestone pays for (seen on: [Aftermath: subscriber goals 2026](https://aftermath.site/aftermath-subscriber-goals-2026/))
- Group / institutional subscription offer for libraries and newsrooms (seen on: [Aftermath](https://aftermath.site/aftermath-group-institutional-subscription-deal/))
- Full-text RSS for paying members (seen on: [404 Media](https://www.404media.co/membership/))
- Gift a subscription option with a start date
- Corrections line at the foot of an edited article, dated
**Real-world basis:** [404 Media: Membership](https://www.404media.co/membership/), [404 Media: Sign up](https://www.404media.co/signup/), [Aftermath: subscriber goals](https://aftermath.site/aftermath-subscriber-goals-2026/), [Aftermath: group subscriptions](https://aftermath.site/aftermath-group-institutional-subscription-deal/), [Platformer](https://www.platformer.news/)
**Style: Wire-service broadsheet**
- Type: Headings: IBM Plex Serif 700; body: IBM Plex Serif 400/19px, 68ch; datelines, bylines and tier prices: IBM Plex Mono 500 (one superfamily with a real contrasting mono cut)
- Palette: bg #F6F6F3 (newsprint grey-white) / text #111111 / accent #0A5C8A (wire-desk blue) / surface #FFFFFF / line #111111 / highlight #FFE14D (marker)
- Layout: single strong column with a narrow left rail for dateline and time; home page = latest dispatch in full width, then a plain dated list; tiers as a ruled table; no cards; one sign-up form per page, at the end of the article
- Imagery: mostly none; documents and screenshots shown flat with a 1px rule and a caption; photos in black and white at 3:2
- Motion: none beyond focus and link underlines; View Transition from list to article
- Why it fits now: reader-owned newsrooms have gone text-first and fast, looking like wire copy rather than magazines; see [404 Media](https://www.404media.co/)
**Style variations:** Broadsheet: white, big serif headlines · Telex: yellow paper, mono throughout · Samizdat: grey paper, typewriter headings
**Refs:**
- [404 Media: Membership](https://www.404media.co/membership/): the clearest tier page in indie journalism: monthly and yearly prices, concrete perks, no fluff
- [Aftermath: subscriber goals 2026](https://aftermath.site/aftermath-subscriber-goals-2026/): publishing the business numbers as a post builds trust and converts readers
- [Platformer](https://www.platformer.news/): single-writer publication on its own domain with a calm, text-led home page

<a id="053"></a>
#### 053 · Hyperlocal News Site (`local`)
**For:** one-town or one-neighbourhood newsrooms, reader-owned co-ops and volunteer community papers.
**Templates:** front-page (news river) · category (council, housing, transport, schools) · single · archive-author · page-join (membership) · page-newsletters · page-meetings (public meetings tracker) · page-about · page-transparency (funding) · page-complaints · page-tips
**Patterns (~50):** lead story + dated river, topic sections, newsletter chooser (daily / weekly / topic), membership join form with monthly amounts, "who funds us" transparency table, complaints and corrections procedure (with press regulator), public meetings list (date / body / topic / in-person or remote / agenda / notes), "send us a tip" form, reporter profile with beat and contact, events listing, explainer series ("council funding reforms explained"), print edition and stockists.
**Content model:** posts + categories; companion `meeting` (date, body, topic, format, agenda URL, notes URL, outcome); `funder` (name, amount band, year); author profiles.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Newsletter, GiveWP or Jetpack Donations, Query Filter (meetings by topic and format), Jetpack Forms (tips). Reference architecture: Automattic's Newspack.
**Signature:** a public-meetings tracker that lists upcoming meetings by body and topic, filterable by in-person / remote, with agenda and published notes per meeting (seen on: [Documenters: Chicago meetings](https://chicago.documenters.org/meetings/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Transparency page listing funders and income sources (seen on: [The Bristol Cable: Transparency](https://thebristolcable.org/transparency/))
- Complaints procedure with the regulator named (seen on: [The Bristol Cable: Complaints](https://thebristolcable.org/complaints/))
- Newsletter chooser page with several lists (seen on: [The Oaklandside: Newsletters](https://oaklandside.org/newsletters/))
- Membership join with suggested monthly amounts and member count in a sentence (seen on: [The Bristol Cable: Join](https://thebristolcable.org/join/))
- Print edition stockist list (library, cafés, community centres)
**Real-world basis:** [Documenters: Chicago meetings](https://chicago.documenters.org/meetings/), [The Bristol Cable: Join](https://thebristolcable.org/join/), [The Bristol Cable: Transparency](https://thebristolcable.org/transparency/), [The Oaklandside: About](https://oaklandside.org/about/), [The Oaklandside: Newsletters](https://oaklandside.org/newsletters/)
**Style: Civic tabloid grid**
- Type: Headings: Francois One 400 (condensed, tabloid headline energy); body: PT Serif 400/18px; labels (topic, date, ward): Public Sans 600
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #0E0E0E / accent #00704A (civic green, from street signs) / surface #EEF3EF / line #0E0E0E / alert #D62718
- Layout: 12-col newspaper grid; lead story spans 8 cols with a 4-col "Meetings this week" rail; thick 4px top rules per section; headlines up to 9vw on the lead only; footer = address, editor, complaints, funding
- Imagery: local photography only (streets, meetings, people named in captions), 3:2 and 16:9; no stock; photo credit on every image
- Motion: none; focus states and link underlines only
- Why it fits now: reader-owned local papers are rebuilding trust with plain, dense front pages and visible accountability pages; see [The Bristol Cable](https://thebristolcable.org/)
**Style variations:** Gazette: white, serif headlines, black rules · Civic: pale green bg, condensed type · Weekly: newsprint grey, red section flags
**Refs:**
- [Documenters: Chicago meetings](https://chicago.documenters.org/meetings/): the real model for a public-meetings tracker with topic and format filters
- [The Bristol Cable: Transparency](https://thebristolcable.org/transparency/): WordPress co-op newsroom that publishes its funding in full
- [The Oaklandside: Newsletters](https://oaklandside.org/newsletters/): WordPress/Newspack local newsroom with a clear multi-newsletter sign-up page

<a id="054"></a>
#### 054 · Academic / Researcher (`cite`)
**For:** PhD students, postdocs, and professors who want a personal academic homepage.
**Templates:** front-page (bio + selected publications) · page-publications · single-publication (optional) · page-cv · page-teaching · page-talks · page-people (students, collaborators) · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** short bio with photo and affiliation, contact line (email, office, ORCID, Google Scholar, GitHub), "news" list with dates, publications grouped by year (reverse chronological), per-paper buttons (Abs / Bib / PDF / HTML / Code / Video / Slides), expandable abstract, BibTeX block, owner's name highlighted in the author list, equal-contribution and corresponding-author markers, paper thumbnail or teaser figure, CV page with PDF download, teaching list by term, talks list.
**Content model:** companion `publication` (authors, venue, year, type, doi, pdf, code, bibtex, thumbnail, selected flag), `talk`, `course`.
**Plugins:** Query Filter (year and type), Code Block Pro (BibTeX formatting).
**Signature:** a publication list where every entry has Abs / Bib / PDF buttons that expand inline, and the owner's name is automatically highlighted in the author list (seen on: [al-folio: Publications](https://alshedivat.github.io/al-folio/publications/), [Jon Barron](https://jonbarron.info/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- CV as a web page with a one-click PDF download
- "Selected publications" flag so the front page shows five, not fifty (seen on: [Jon Barron](https://jonbarron.info/))
- Equal-contribution and corresponding-author markers in author lists (seen on: [al-folio: Publications](https://alshedivat.github.io/al-folio/publications/))
- "Prospective students: read this before emailing" block with current openings
- Scholarly schema (ScholarlyArticle, Person with ORCID) for Google Scholar indexing
**Real-world basis:** [al-folio: Publications](https://alshedivat.github.io/al-folio/publications/), [al-folio: CV](https://alshedivat.github.io/al-folio/cv/), [Jon Barron](https://jonbarron.info/), [Gershman Lab: Publications](https://gershmanlab.com/pubs.html)
**Style: LaTeX paper**
- Type: Headings and body: STIX Two Text (700 for headings, 400/19px body), small caps for section heads; BibTeX and code: Source Code Pro 400
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #111111 / accent #A3182B (hyperref link red) / surface #F5F5F4 / line #D6D6D3
- Layout: one centred page at 70ch like a preprint, numbered sections (1 Research, 2 Publications) because a paper really is numbered; publications as a hanging-indent reference list with year in the margin; thumbnails 160px at left on wide screens only
- Imagery: paper teaser figures at their native ratio, no crops; one portrait
- Motion: Abs and Bib expand with a 150ms ease-out (transform/opacity only); "Copy BibTeX" confirms with text, not animation; static under prefers-reduced-motion
- Why it fits now: the plain, fast researcher homepage is the respected standard in academia, and it is widely copied; see [Jon Barron](https://jonbarron.info/)
**Style variations:** Journal: two-column, serif, running heads · Preprint: arXiv-grey header, mono metadata · Poster: A0 grid, big sans headings
**Refs:**
- [al-folio: Publications](https://alshedivat.github.io/al-folio/publications/): the de facto academic template: Abs/Bib/PDF buttons, author highlighting, year grouping
- [Jon Barron](https://jonbarron.info/): minimal homepage with teaser figures beside each paper; heavily imitated
- [Gershman Lab: Publications](https://gershmanlab.com/pubs.html): long plain publication list with PDFs, a realistic content volume to design for
