#### 117 · Independent Optician (`lens`)
**For:** single-shop independent opticians and optometrists who sell independent frame brands and run their own eye examinations.
**Templates:** front-page · page-eye-examinations · archive-brand · single-brand · page-lenses · page-contact-lenses · page-myopia-management · page-team · page-visit · archive-event (trunk shows)
**Patterns (~45):** eye examination fees (standard / with OCT / children), contact lens fitting and aftercare fees, NHS position statement ("we do / don't do NHS tests"), priced exam cards with "perfect for" and what's included, insurance/HSA explainer, brands index with a paragraph of brand history, brand page with frames on the shelf, meet-your-optometrist card (GOC no.), specialist services (myopia management, visual stress, home visits), clinic days and parking, trunk-show events, downloadable "help with eye care costs" PDF.
**Content model:** `brand` (country, maker, material, story, in-store now flag), `exam` (duration, price, inclusions, perfect-for), companion `event` (trunk shows).
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (upcoming trunk shows), Query Filter (brands by country and material). Booking via the practice's own link, or Simply Schedule Appointments.
**Signature:** a **brands index as editorial content**: each independent maker gets a heading and a paragraph of real history (where it's made, by whom, in what material), with an "in store now" flag bound to `brand` meta, so the index works as the shop window for frames that aren't sold online. (seen on: [Ra Opticians: Our brands](https://www.raopticians.com/our-brands))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Priced exam cards with "what's included" and a booking button per card, followed by a three-step insurance explainer (buying confidence). (seen on: [Ra Opticians: Eye exam](https://www.raopticians.com/eye-exam))
- A plain NHS statement ("we do not carry out NHS eye examinations, nor accept vouchers") so nobody books under a false assumption (trust & proof). (seen on: [Bromptons Opticians: Eye examinations](https://www.bromptons.com/eye-examinations))
- Clinic-day notice ("examinations Wednesdays, Fridays and Saturdays") bound to a schedule field and shown on every booking button (operational). (seen on: [Bromptons Opticians](https://www.bromptons.com/eye-examinations))
- A downloadable PDF on help with eye-care costs (content & tools). (seen on: [Keyes & McClellan: Eye examination & fees](https://www.keyeseyecare.co.uk/eye-care/eye-examinations/))
- A frame-size guide (lens width / bridge / temple, e.g. 50□20-145) with "find the numbers on your current glasses" photos (buying confidence).
**Style: Heritage optician catalogue**
- Type: headings Libre Bodoni 400 (display 5.5rem); section markers set as Snellen chart rows in Optician Sans (OFL, drawn from historic eye charts); body Commissioner 400 at 18px.
- Palette: bg #F4F4F1, text #161616, accent #8C1C13 (oxblood acetate), surface #E7E2DA (pale tortoiseshell), line #CFCAC2.
- Layout: brand index as a long two-column catalogue: brand name in Caslon, the story in a narrow column, and a single frame photo on the shelf. Exam fees sit in a ruled price list. Each page title is set like a Snellen line (large to small across two lines). Buttons 0 radius with a 1px border, images 0.
- Imagery: frames photographed flat on a neutral surface at consistent scale, plus the testing room and equipment (OCT, phoropter). No models in sunglasses on yachts.
- Motion: the Snellen-line titles gain one step of letter-spacing on hover (instant). No scroll effects.
- Why it fits now: heritage-led eyewear brands have made the optician's own history and craft vocabulary into a design language. Examples: [Keyes & McClellan: Eye examinations](https://www.keyeseyecare.co.uk/eye-care/eye-examinations/) (Baskerville Display with Gill Sans) and [Cubitts: Eye exam](https://cubitts.com/pages/eye-exam) (Caslon Doric).
**Style variations:** Chart: #F4F4F1, oxblood #8C1C13 · Tortoise: #2B2118 bg, #E7E2DA text · Clinic: white, ink #161616, no accent.
**Real-world basis:** [Bromptons: Eye examinations](https://www.bromptons.com/eye-examinations), [Ra Opticians: Eye exam](https://www.raopticians.com/eye-exam), [Ra Opticians: Our brands](https://www.raopticians.com/our-brands), [Keyes & McClellan: Eye examinations](https://www.keyeseyecare.co.uk/eye-care/eye-examinations/), [Cubitts: Eye exam](https://cubitts.com/pages/eye-exam)
**Refs:**
- [Bromptons Opticians: Eye examinations](https://www.bromptons.com/eye-examinations): a plain published fee list for exams and contact lenses, with the NHS policy.
- [Ra Opticians: Our brands](https://www.raopticians.com/our-brands): a brands index written as editorial.
- [Keyes & McClellan Eyecare: Eye examination & fees](https://www.keyeseyecare.co.uk/eye-care/eye-examinations/): tiered NHS and private fees, an OCT explainer and a downloads block.

#### 118 · Small Vet Clinic (`vet`)
**For:** independent (non-corporate) small-animal practices with one or two sites, sometimes mixed farm and equine.
**Templates:** front-page · page-prices · page-pet-health-club · page-emergencies · page-register · page-repeat-prescriptions · archive-advice · single-advice · page-why-independent · archive-team
**Patterns (~50):** price list by category and species (consultations, vaccinations course/booster, neutering, dental), out-of-hours fees, pet health plan (what's included, "you save £X a year"), emergency page (24/7 phone, out-of-hours partner, what to do on the way), register your pet form, repeat prescriptions form, "why we're independent" with director cards, symptom checker / poisons guide / factsheets, Fear Free or Cat Friendly Clinic accreditation, saying goodbye (euthanasia and cremation), payment plans, Vetstoria booking button.
**Content model:** `price_item` (category, species, price, updated date), `plan` (species, monthly price, inclusions, annual saving), `advice` (species, topic, urgency level).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (register pet, repeat prescription request), Query Filter (advice by species). Booking via the practice's Vetstoria or other link.
**Signature:** a **species-by-species price list** grouped under category headings (consultation, vaccination course and booster, neutering by species and weight, dental) with a "last updated" date, bound to `price_item` records so the receptionist updates one row, not a PDF. (seen on: [PowisVets: Prices](https://powisvets.co.uk/prices/))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- An emergency bar that switches wording by time of day: in hours "Call us now", out of hours "Call [partner] on …", driven by opening hours (operational). (seen on: [Fishguard Vets: Emergencies](https://www.fishguardvets.co.uk/emergencies/))
- Pet health plan cards per species with "you save at least £X a year" and a terms link (conversion helpers). (seen on: [Fishguard Vets: Premier Pet Care Plan](https://www.fishguardvets.co.uk/pets/premier-petcare-plan/))
- A "why we're independent" page with named directors and local bios (trust & proof). (seen on: [Fenton Vets: Why we're independent](https://www.fentonvets.co.uk/about/why-were-independent/))
- A repeat prescription request form with a "ready for collection in 48 hours" note (owner quality of life). (seen on: [PowisVets](https://powisvets.co.uk/prices/))
- A gentle "Saying goodbye" page: home euthanasia, cremation choices, paw prints (care & aftercare). (seen on: [Fenton Vets](https://www.fentonvets.co.uk/about/why-were-independent/))
**Style: Utility clinic signage**
- Type: headings Ranade 700 (Fontshare, display 5rem, tight line-height 1.0); body Ranade 400 at 18px; prices and times Spline Sans Mono 500.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #13201B, accent #1F7A4D (surgical green, primary action), emergency #C8372D (emergency bar only), surface #EAF2EC, line #C3D2C8.
- Layout: signage logic. A bold green header strip holds opening hours and the phone number, and the emergency bar sits below it. The front page is a direct list of what people come for (Book / Prices / Register / Repeat prescription / Emergency) as big text links with arrows, followed by the team and advice. The price list uses ruled rows with species subheads. Buttons 4px radius, images 0.
- Imagery: the clinic's own animals and staff, photographed in the consulting room at pet height. Species line icons drawn in a single stroke weight. No stock puppies in stethoscopes.
- Motion: none. The "open now" state updates on load from opening hours.
- Why it fits now: hospital and transport wayfinding (big type, strong colour bars) has become a favoured look for practical services, because people arrive stressed and need the phone number first. Example: [PowisVets: Prices](https://powisvets.co.uk/prices/).
**Style variations:** Surgery: white, green #1F7A4D · Farm: #F1EFE8 bg, #5B4A2E accent · Night: #13201B bg, #EAF2EC text, red bar kept.
**Real-world basis:** [PowisVets: Prices](https://powisvets.co.uk/prices/), [Fishguard Vets: Premier Pet Care Plan](https://www.fishguardvets.co.uk/pets/premier-petcare-plan/), [Fishguard Vets: Emergencies](https://www.fishguardvets.co.uk/emergencies/), [Fenton Vets: Pet club](https://www.fentonvets.co.uk/small-animals/fenton-pet-club/), [Aloha Veterinary Hospital: Privately owned](https://www.alohavethospitaloc.com/privately-owned)
**Refs:**
- [PowisVets: Prices](https://powisvets.co.uk/prices/): price-table structure: category heading, species subheading, then label and price rows.
- [Fishguard Vets: Premier Pet Care Plan](https://www.fishguardvets.co.uk/pets/premier-petcare-plan/): plan per species with benefits and the annual saving.
- [Fenton Vets: Why we're independent](https://www.fentonvets.co.uk/about/why-were-independent/): an independence story with director cards.

#### 119 · Yoga Studio (`asana`)
**For:** independent single- or two-room yoga studios (including donation-based and community studios) with 10–40 classes a week.
**Templates:** front-page · page-schedule · page-class-descriptions · page-pricing · page-new-students · archive-teacher · single-teacher · archive-workshop · single-workshop · page-teacher-training
**Patterns (~45):** weekly timetable (Mindbody / Momence / Zenoti embed, or native), class descriptions (one heading and paragraph per style, with level), new-student intro offer, pricing list (drop-in / class packs / unlimited monthly), beginner FAQ (what to bring, arrive 10 minutes early, minimum age), cancellation and waitlist policy, teacher profiles, workshops and retreats, teacher training, donation/pay-what-you-can memberships, community agreements, locations and parking.
**Content model:** `class_type` (level, duration, heat, props), `teacher` (styles, training hours, pronouns), companion `event` (workshops, retreats), optional native `session` (weekday, time, room, class_type, teacher) for studios without a booking system.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (upcoming workshops), The Events Calendar only if the studio sells workshop tickets on-site. Otherwise the booking system embed.
**Signature:** a **weekly schedule page** that embeds the studio's existing booking widget, with class descriptions bound underneath, so the timetable and "what is Yin?" are on the same page. For studios without a booking system, a native week grid built from `session` records is filtered by level with the Interactivity API. (seen on: [Happy Dog Yoga Studio: Class schedule](https://www.happydogyogastudio.com/class-schedule/))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A new-student intro offer block ("1 week unlimited for $75") with the promo code shown as copyable text (conversion helpers). (seen on: [ONEYOGAHOUSE: New students](https://oneyogahouse.com/new-students/))
- A long beginner FAQ that also covers policy (cancellation window, what to wear, water) (care & aftercare). (seen on: [The Yoga Studio Indianapolis: Beginning information](https://indyyogastudio.com/beginning-information/))
- Donation-tier memberships (sustaining / choose your own donation) for community studios (community). (seen on: [Sangha Studio: Daily schedule](https://www.sanghastudio.org/dailyschedule.html))
- A "cancelled / cover teacher" flag on individual timetable sessions, with a scheduled holiday-timetable notice (operational).
- Studio access notes: stairs, step-free entrance, props provided, changing rooms, gender-neutral toilets (accessibility & inclusion).
**Style: Soft Swiss timetable**
- Type: headings Gambarino 400 (Fontshare serif, display 5rem); body Supreme 400 at 18px (Fontshare); timetable times in Supreme 700 tabular figures.
- Palette: bg #E6E9E7 (cool stone), text #22201C, accent #3E5C4B (moss, primary action), surface #FFFFFF (timetable panel), line #C7C2B8, clay #A36A4F for "full/waitlist" labels.
- Layout: the timetable is the front page: a seven-column week with hairline rules, each class a text row (time, class, teacher), no coloured blocks. Class descriptions follow as a two-column definition list. The intro offer sits in the right margin, not in a hero. Buttons 999px radius (mat-like pills are used only for day filters), images 0.
- Imagery: the real room at different times of day, and classes photographed from the back of the room. Film grain allowed. No handstands on beaches.
- Motion: day filter switches with a short View Transition. Nothing on scroll.
- Why it fits now: community and donation-based studios are pitching themselves as neighbourhood institutions, and the timetable-first page reflects how people actually use a studio site. Example: [Sangha Studio: Daily schedule](https://www.sanghastudio.org/dailyschedule.html).
**Style variations:** Stone: #E6E9E7, moss #3E5C4B · Morning: #FFFFFF bg, clay #A36A4F · Candle: #22201C bg, #E6E9E7 text.
**Real-world basis:** [Happy Dog Yoga: Class schedule](https://www.happydogyogastudio.com/class-schedule/), [Happy Dog Yoga: Class descriptions](https://www.happydogyogastudio.com/class-descriptions/), [ONEYOGAHOUSE: New students](https://oneyogahouse.com/new-students/), [Indy Yoga Studio: Beginning information](https://indyyogastudio.com/beginning-information/), [Sangha Studio: Schedule](https://www.sanghastudio.org/dailyschedule.html)
**Refs:**
- [Happy Dog Yoga Studio: Class descriptions](https://www.happydogyogastudio.com/class-descriptions/): a list with one entry per style (WordPress).
- [ONEYOGAHOUSE: New students](https://oneyogahouse.com/new-students/): a welcome, an intro offer with promo code, and a drop-in price list in one flow.
- [The Yoga Studio Indianapolis: Beginning information](https://indyyogastudio.com/beginning-information/): a first-timer FAQ that includes policies.

#### 120 · Pilates / Reformer Studio (`reformer`)
**For:** independent reformer and apparatus studios with 6–12 machines, group classes, and 1:1 or rehab sessions.
**Templates:** front-page · page-getting-started · page-timetable · page-pricing · archive-class-type · page-private-sessions · archive-instructor · page-workshops · page-instructor-training · page-policies
**Patterns (~40):** intro/trial offer (5 classes in 2 weeks), numbered "getting started" steps (buy trial → create profile → book first class), membership table (per week / per month, with term length), credit system explainer (mat = 1 credit, reformer = 2), class packs with validity, class descriptions by format (Reformer Essentials, Jumpboard, Tower), apparatus list, 1:1 and semi-private sessions with an "ideal if you…" checklist, small class size promise, what to bring (grip socks), pause/freeze policy, booking app download.
**Content model:** `class_type` (apparatus, level, credits, duration), `instructor` (certifications, specialisms: pre/postnatal, rehab), `membership` (price, period, term, credits, pause rules).
**Plugins:** none beyond the studio's booking embed (bsport, Momence, Acuity, GymMaster). WooCommerce only if the studio sells packs on-site.
**Signature:** a **pricing page built as a matrix**: credits per month against commitment length (no term / 3 months / 6 months), with the credit cost of each class type explained alongside, so people can work out what they'll actually pay. (seen on: [Niche Pilates Studio: Pricing](https://www.nichefitstudio.com/pricing))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A numbered getting-started flow for first-timers, including which intro class to book first (care & aftercare). (seen on: [Reform Studios: Getting started](https://reformstudios.com.au/getting-started/))
- A free membership pause (2–8 weeks) stated on the pricing page (buying confidence). (seen on: [Reform Studios: Pricing](https://reformstudios.com.au/pricing/))
- An "ideal if you…" checklist on 1:1 sessions (recovering from injury, pregnant, new to Pilates) (conversion helpers). (seen on: [Spring Pilates](https://springpilates.co.uk/))
- A "never more than 8 in a class" capacity promise, plus live "2 spots left" labels where the booking system exposes them (operational). (seen on: [Spring Pilates](https://springpilates.co.uk/))
- A grip-socks and what-to-wear note with the studio's own sock stock (local & practical).
**Style: Machine-spec condensed**
- Type: headings Tanker 400 (Fontshare, heavy condensed, display 6rem); body Switzer 400 at 18px (Fontshare); specs (springs, credits, minutes) in Switzer 600 tabular figures.
- Palette: bg #F2F2F0, text #0D0D0D, accent #E4572E (upholstery vermilion, primary action), steel #8FA3AE (rules and spring diagrams), surface #FFFFFF, line #CFCFCB.
- Layout: class types are laid out like equipment spec sheets (apparatus / level / credits / minutes / what it works) in a wide table. The front page leads with a full-bleed photo of the machines in a row and the timetable link, then the intro offer as a single line of type. Pricing matrix is a real table with sticky row headers on mobile. Buttons 0 radius, images 0, inputs 0.
- Imagery: the reformers photographed straight on, in rows, with springs and straps visible; instructors cueing clients. Colour kept true to upholstery. No lens flare.
- Motion: the pricing matrix highlights the row and column of the hovered/focused cell. No scroll effects.
- Why it fits now: boutique studios are dropping soft wellness pastels for bolder, athletic, product-spec branding. Example: [Heartcore](https://weareheartcore.com/en-gb/).
**Style variations:** Spring steel: #F2F2F0, vermilion #E4572E · Studio night: #0D0D0D bg, #F2F2F0 text, steel rules · Sand: #E9E4DA bg, ink #0D0D0D.
**Real-world basis:** [Reform Studios: Pricing](https://reformstudios.com.au/pricing/), [Reform Studios: Getting started](https://reformstudios.com.au/getting-started/), [Niche Pilates Studio: Pricing](https://www.nichefitstudio.com/pricing), [Spring Pilates](https://springpilates.co.uk/)
**Refs:**
- [Reform Studios: Getting started](https://reformstudios.com.au/getting-started/): a numbered onboarding flow (WordPress).
- [Niche Pilates Studio: Pricing](https://www.nichefitstudio.com/pricing): a credits-by-commitment matrix plus the credit explainer.
- [Spring Pilates](https://springpilates.co.uk/): 1:1 and rehab positioning with an "ideal if you" checklist and a small-class promise.

<a id="121"></a>
#### 121 · Massage & Acupuncture (`needle`)
**For:** community acupuncture clinics, solo acupuncturists and small massage/bodywork practices, often running a sliding scale.
**Templates:** front-page · page-community-acupuncture · page-private-treatment · page-massage · page-prices · page-first-visit · page-faq · page-accessibility · page-cancellation-policy · archive-practitioner
**Patterns (~40):** sliding-scale price block ("$30–$75, you choose, no proof of income"), new-patient fee, private vs community room comparison, "what happens during a visit", "who community acupuncture is for", frequency of care guidance, conditions treated list, herbal consultations / cupping / gua sha add-ons, practitioner card (licence), cancellation and late policy, accessibility page (entrance, lift, cost, gender-affirming care), gift cards, Jane booking link, donation link for nonprofit clinics.
**Content model:** `service` (room type, price min/max, new-patient fee, duration), `practitioner` (licence, modalities, pronouns).
**Plugins:** GiveWP or Jetpack Donations (nonprofit clinics). Booking via Jane, or Simply Schedule Appointments for solo practitioners.
**Signature:** a **sliding-scale explainer** that states the range, the new-patient fee, what the scale covers, and "you decide what you pay each visit", with a note on how often acute problems need treatment so people can budget honestly. (seen on: [Harvard Square Community Acupuncture: Fees](https://www.hsqca.com/fees))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- An accessibility page with a photo of the accessible entrance and exact instructions ("ring the bell to the left") (accessibility & inclusion). (seen on: [Open Care Community: Accessibility](https://opencarecommunity.com/accessibility))
- A cancellation fee that is waived for illness, stated in plain words (trust & proof). (seen on: [Harvard Square Community Acupuncture: Fees](https://www.hsqca.com/fees))
- A "what to expect / what to wear" first-visit page: in a shared room, keep clothes on, roll up sleeves (care & aftercare). (seen on: [HSQCA: FAQ](https://www.hsqca.com/faq))
- Punch cards and seniors' pricing (conversion helpers). (seen on: [Wasatch Community Acupuncture](https://wasatchacupuncture.org/))
- Gift cards (conversion helpers). (seen on: [Open Care Community: Pricing](https://opencarecommunity.com/pricing))
**Style: Community clinic notice-board**
- Type: headings Tienne 700 (display 5rem); body Work Sans 400 at 18px; prices Work Sans 600 tabular.
- Palette: bg #F1F3EE (pale sage-grey), text #1E2320, accent #B03A2E (cinnabar, the red of acupuncture point charts), surface #FFFFFF, line #C7CEC4, ink-blue #274060 for links.
- Layout: the prices page is the front page's second block. The sliding scale is drawn as a simple ruler from low to high, with the text "you choose" above it, and no slider. Practitioner and service info are pinned-note blocks with a slight offset border, not cards with shadows. Point-chart line drawings are used as section dividers. Buttons 2px radius, images 0.
- Imagery: the shared treatment room with recliners and blankets, needles and moxa in close-up, practitioners at work. Muted, warm natural colour. No stones stacked on water.
- Motion: none. Accordions for FAQ open instantly under reduced motion.
- Why it fits now: community health projects are leaning into a hand-made, bulletin-board honesty that signals access over luxury. Example: [Open Care Community: Community acupuncture](https://opencarecommunity.com/community-acupuncture).
**Style variations:** Chart: #F1F3EE, cinnabar #B03A2E · Moxa: #2A2522 bg, #F1F3EE text · Paper gown: #FFFFFF, ink-blue #274060.
**Real-world basis:** [HSQCA: Fees](https://www.hsqca.com/fees), [HSQCA: FAQ](https://www.hsqca.com/faq), [Open Care Community: Pricing](https://opencarecommunity.com/pricing), [Open Care Community: Community acupuncture](https://opencarecommunity.com/community-acupuncture), [Wasatch Community Acupuncture](https://wasatchacupuncture.org/)
**Refs:**
- [Harvard Square Community Acupuncture: Fees](https://www.hsqca.com/fees): a complete sliding-scale fee page in a few honest paragraphs.
- [Open Care Community: Community acupuncture](https://opencarecommunity.com/community-acupuncture): "what happens during a visit", "who it's for" and frequency of care.
- [Open Care Community: Accessibility](https://opencarecommunity.com/accessibility): a real access page covering entrance, cost and gender-affirming care.

<a id="122"></a>
#### 122 · Barbershop (`fade`)
**For:** independent barbershops with 2–8 chairs, taking both walk-ins and bookings.
**Templates:** front-page · page-prices · archive-barber · single-barber · page-book · page-visit · page-shop (products, optional Woo) · page-gift-cards · page-careers · page-faq
**Patterns (~35):** full price menu with starting price and average length, "walk-ins welcome" status, barber cards with level (junior / barber / senior) and shop location, per-barber booking link, combo services (haircut + beard), kids and seniors prices, cash vs card price note, "arrive 5 minutes early" and lateness policy, services descriptions (skin fade, hot towel shave), products, gift cards, careers ("we're hiring"), photo gallery of cuts.
**Content model:** `barber` (level, shop, days in, specialities, booking URL, instagram), `service` (price from, average length, level surcharge).
**Plugins:** WooCommerce only for products and gift cards. Booking via the shop's own link (Booksy, Squire, Fresha), or Simply Schedule Appointments per barber.
**Signature:** a **barber directory filtered by shop and level** (senior / barber / junior), each card linking to that barber's booking, bound to `barber` meta and filtered with Query Filter. Clients book a person, not a slot. (seen on: [Fellow Barber: Barbers](https://www.fellowbarber.com/pages/barbers))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A price menu with "updated [year]" and average length per service, and the line "your barber will tell you before anything changes the number" (trust & proof). (seen on: [Eddie's: Pricing](https://eddieshaircutshave.com/pricing/))
- Cash and card prices shown side by side, plus a lateness policy (local & practical). (seen on: [Details Barbershop](https://detailsrenton.com/))
- A "walk in or book" choice, with walk-in hours bound to opening times (operational). (seen on: [Hawk & Fade: Durham](https://hawkfade.com/durham/))
- Gift cards for in-store services (conversion helpers). (seen on: [Fellow Barber](https://www.fellowbarber.com/pages/services))
- A "we're hiring" careers page with training and progression (community). (seen on: [Fellow Barber: Jobs](https://www.fellowbarber.com/jobs))
**Style: Sign-painter price board**
- Type: headings Sancreek 400 (display 7rem, a Victorian wood-type poster face); prices and menu in Courier Prime 400/700 at 19px; body Courier Prime is too dense for long text, so paragraphs use Barlow Semi Condensed 400 at 18px.
- Palette: bg #F5F5F2, text #0F0F0F, accent #C1121F (pole red, primary action), pole blue #1D3557 (links), surface #FFFFFF, line #0F0F0F (2px rules).
- Layout: the price menu is the front page, set like a board behind the chairs: service name left, dotted leader, price right, length in small type. Barber cards are a strip of portrait photos with name and level stencilled underneath. Buttons 0 radius with 2px black border, images 0.
- Imagery: black-and-white portraits of each barber at their chair, cuts photographed from the back and side against the shop wall. No stock razors on marble.
- Motion: none on scroll. Barber cards swap to a "latest cut" photo on hover (instant; static under reduced motion).
- Why it fits now: independent barbers are borrowing sign-painting and shop-front lettering to separate themselves from chain "grooming lounges". Example: [Fellow Barber: Barbers](https://www.fellowbarber.com/pages/barbers).
**Style variations:** Pole: #F5F5F2, red #C1121F, blue #1D3557 · After hours: #0F0F0F bg, #F5F5F2 text, red kept · Chalk: #1F2A24 bg, #EDEDE6 text.
**Real-world basis:** [Eddie's: Pricing](https://eddieshaircutshave.com/pricing/), [Fellow Barber: Barbers](https://www.fellowbarber.com/pages/barbers), [Details Barbershop](https://detailsrenton.com/), [Signature Barbershop NYC: Price list](https://signaturebarbershopnyc.com/price-list/), [Pall Mall Barbers: Barbers](https://www.pallmallbarbers.com/barbers/)
**Refs:**
- [Eddie's Barbershop: Pricing](https://eddieshaircutshave.com/pricing/): a published full menu with starting prices and average lengths, and a paragraph on why they publish (WordPress).
- [Fellow Barber: Barbers](https://www.fellowbarber.com/pages/barbers): a barber directory filtered by city, shop and level.
- [Details Barbershop](https://detailsrenton.com/): a small-shop menu with cash and card prices and a lateness note.

#### 123 · Hair & Beauty Salon (`salon`)
**For:** independent hair salons (with nails, brows or lashes on the side) of 3–15 stylists, with a level-based pricing system.
**Templates:** front-page · page-price-list · archive-stylist · single-stylist · archive-service · single-service · page-new-clients · page-book · page-gallery · page-careers
**Patterns (~45):** price list with columns by stylist level (1–8, or junior / senior / director), "prices from, confirmed at consultation" note, free consultation offer, colour services (single process, highlights, balayage per foil), patch test policy (48 hours before colour), stylist cards filtered by type (colourist / stylist / extensions) and price band, new client offer and refer a friend, blow-dry bar menu, bridal hair, downloadable price list PDF per salon, gallery, careers ("we're hiring").
**Content model:** `stylist` (level, type, salon, specialisms, booking URL, pronouns), `service` (category, price per level as a repeater, duration, patch test required).
**Plugins:** Query Filter (stylists by type, level and salon). Booking via the salon's system (Fresha, Phorest, Zenoti).
**Signature:** a **price list by stylist level**: every service shows one price per level in a row (e.g. $64 | 70 | 76 … 106), with a line explaining that price depends on experience and demand. It is bound to one `service` repeater, so a price rise is a single edit. (seen on: [Studio W Hair Salon: Price list](https://www.studiowsaloncv.com/castro-valley-hair-salon-price-list/))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A stylist directory filtered by type (colourist / stylist / extensions), price band and salon (conversion helpers). (seen on: [Hershesons: Meet the experts](https://www.hershesons.com/collections/meet-the-experts))
- Downloadable PDF price lists per salon and per concession (nails, brows), generated from the same data (content & tools). (seen on: [Hershesons: Belgravia](https://www.hershesons.com/pages/belgravia))
- A new client offer / refer a friend page, and a free consultation link (conversion helpers). (seen on: [Studio W: Price list](https://www.studiowsaloncv.com/castro-valley-hair-salon-price-list/))
- A patch-test notice added automatically to any service flagged `patch_test_required`, with "book your patch test 48 hours before" (care & aftercare).
- A "we're hiring" page with levels and education (community). (seen on: [Studio W](https://www.studiowsaloncv.com/castro-valley-hair-salon-price-list/))
**Style: Loud fashion poster**
- Type: headings Cabinet Grotesk 800 (Fontshare, display 8rem, all words the same weight and colour); stylist names in Boska 500 italic (Fontshare serif) as a second voice; body Cabinet Grotesk 400 at 18px.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #111111, accent #FF5FA2 (salon pink, used as whole colour fields, never on text), surface #FFE3EF, line #111111.
- Layout: the front page is poster-like: a full-bleed photo of a cut with the salon name set huge across it, then the price list link and "book". The level price list is a wide table with sticky service names. Stylists appear as a big portrait grid with uneven spans. Buttons 0 radius with 2px border, images 0.
- Imagery: the salon's own editorial shoots (hair as the subject, strong colour, flash), plus behind-the-chair portraits of stylists. No stock "model laughing with hair flip".
- Motion: hovering a stylist swaps their portrait for a recent colour or cut photo. No marquee, no scroll effects.
- Why it fits now: fashion-led independent salons use loud poster typography and flat colour fields as their identity, closer to a record label than a spa. Example: [Bleach London](https://bleachlondon.com/).
**Style variations:** Pink: white, #FF5FA2 fields · Bleach: #FFF7C2 bg, ink #111111 · Colour bar: #111111 bg, #FFE3EF text, pink kept.
**Real-world basis:** [Studio W: Price list](https://www.studiowsaloncv.com/castro-valley-hair-salon-price-list/), [Hershesons: Meet the experts](https://www.hershesons.com/collections/meet-the-experts), [Hershesons: Belgravia](https://www.hershesons.com/pages/belgravia), [Hershesons: Blow dry bar menu](https://www.hershesons.com/pages/blow-dry-bar-menu), [Bleach London](https://bleachlondon.com/)
**Refs:**
- [Studio W Hair Salon: Price list](https://www.studiowsaloncv.com/castro-valley-hair-salon-price-list/): the level-based price list with the explanation (WordPress).
- [Hershesons: Meet the experts](https://www.hershesons.com/collections/meet-the-experts): stylist filtering by type, price band and location.
- [Hershesons: Belgravia](https://www.hershesons.com/pages/belgravia): a salon page with separate downloadable price lists per service line.

<a id="124"></a>
#### 124 · Home Care Agency (`care`)
**For:** small, family-run domiciliary and live-in care agencies (CQC-registered in England, or equivalent) covering one county or a few towns.
**Templates:** front-page · page-how-care-works · archive-care-type · single-care-type · page-cost-and-funding · archive-area · single-area · page-our-carers · page-join-our-team · page-customer-charter
**Patterns (~45):** care types (personal care, dementia, respite, after hospital, companionship, live-in, couples), "how care works" steps (first chat → care consultation → carer introductions → care begins), cost and funding explainer (hourly visits vs live-in, local authority funding, direct payments, NHS continuing healthcare), areas covered, CQC rating with inspection date, "meet who'll be in your home" carer profiles, customer care charter, family carers' free guides, brochure download, testimonials from families, join our care team with apply online, 24-hour phone line.
**Content model:** `care_type` (who it's for, typical hours, related areas), `area` (towns, postcode prefixes), `carer` (first name, languages, interests, years caring, photo; opt-in only), `job` (role, hours, driving needed, pay range).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (care enquiry and job application), Query Filter (jobs by area).
**Signature:** a **cost and funding page** that explains how home care is actually charged (per visit, minimum 30 minutes, why short visits cost more, live-in vs care home) and the funding routes, so families arrive at the first call already understanding the numbers. (seen on: [GoodOaks Homecare: How much does care cost?](https://www.goodoakshomecare.co.uk/care-costs/))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A CQC rating block with the rating, inspection date and a link to the report, bound to a settings field so it is updated after each inspection (trust & proof). (seen on: [Mumby's: Cost & funding](https://mumbys.com/cost-and-funding/))
- A four-step "how care works" sequence: initial chat, care consultation, carer introductions, care begins (care & aftercare). (seen on: [Home Instead: The initial chat](https://www.homeinstead.co.uk/how/initial-call/))
- A customer care charter page and a downloadable brochure for relatives who print things out (content & tools). (seen on: [Mumby's: Customer care charter](https://mumbys.com/customer-care-charter/))
- A "how we choose our staff" page and a "join our care team" route with apply online (community). (seen on: [GoodOaks: Our staff](https://www.goodoakshomecare.co.uk/our-staff/))
- Large-text default and a "call us instead" phone number next to every form, for older readers (accessibility & inclusion).
**Style: Large-print civic utility**
- Type: headings Aleo 700 (display 4.5rem); body Hanken Grotesk 400 at 20px / 1.6; phone numbers Hanken Grotesk 700 at 28px.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #1A1A1A, accent #1D5C8C (civic blue, primary action), surface #F3F2F1, line #B1B4B6, focus #FFDD00 (yellow focus ring, GOV.UK-style).
- Layout: GOV.UK-like service pages: one question per page heading ("How much does home care cost?"), a contents list, and short paragraphs at 64ch. The phone number appears in the header on every page. Care types are a plain list with one-line descriptions. The area page is a list of towns plus a postcode checker. Buttons 0 radius with a 2px bottom border, images 0.
- Imagery: real carers and clients (with consent) in their own homes, doing ordinary things like making tea, gardening or walking. No hands-holding-old-hands stock.
- Motion: none.
- Why it fits now: plain, service-design pages built around one task each have become the benchmark for serious public-facing services, and families researching care are often stressed and older. Example: [GOV.UK](https://www.gov.uk/).
**Style variations:** Civic: white, blue #1D5C8C, yellow focus · Warm: #FAF6F0 bg, #7A4A1F accent · High contrast: #000000 on #FFFFFF, 22px body.
**Real-world basis:** [Mumby's: Cost & funding](https://mumbys.com/cost-and-funding/), [Mumby's: Join our care team](https://mumbys.com/join-our-care-team/), [GoodOaks: Care costs](https://www.goodoakshomecare.co.uk/care-costs/), [Home Instead: Initial call](https://www.homeinstead.co.uk/how/initial-call/), [Buurtzorg: Our model of care](https://www.buurtzorg.com/about-us/buurtzorgmodel/)
**Refs:**
- [GoodOaks Homecare: How much does care cost?](https://www.goodoakshomecare.co.uk/care-costs/): a plain explanation of how visits are charged (WordPress group).
- [Mumby's Live-in Care: Cost & funding](https://mumbys.com/cost-and-funding/): live-in costs compared with a care home, from a family-run, CQC Outstanding agency (WordPress).
- [Buurtzorg: Our model of care](https://www.buurtzorg.com/about-us/buurtzorgmodel/): the Dutch neighbourhood-team model; a useful framing for small agencies that want to explain self-managing local teams.

### XII. Professional services

> **Shared ground for 125–134:** regulated professions have publishing duties that the themes can make easy. SRA price transparency (UK solicitors), Form CRS / ADV (US advisers), the CMA standardised price list (UK funeral directors) and the Property Ombudsman / client money protection (UK agents) are all real pages on the sites studied. Each theme ships a ready-made page pattern for them.

<a id="125"></a>
#### 125 · Bookkeeper / Accountant for Freelancers (`ledger`)
**For:** solo bookkeepers and 2–10 person accountancy practices whose clients are freelancers, creatives and sole traders.
**Templates:** front-page · page-packages · page-instant-quote · archive-sector · single-sector (e.g. accountants for creatives) · archive-calculator · single-calculator · archive-guide · page-team · page-switching
**Patterns (~40):** fixed monthly fee packages ("from £22/mo", what each includes), instant quote form (business type, turnover band, VAT registered?, payroll?), sector page (musicians, photographers, designers: royalties, retainers, IR35), tax calculator (self-employed tax + Class 4 NI for the current tax year), tax deadlines list (31 Jan, 31 Jul, VAT quarters), switching-from-your-accountant steps, qualified-accountant row (ACCA / AAT / ICAEW with register links), software line (FreeAgent / Xero included), free consultation booking, downloadable guides (allowable expenses), glossary.
**Content model:** `package` (monthly price, inclusions, for: sole trader / Ltd), `deadline` (date, who it applies to, penalty), `guide` (PDF), `sector` (common income types, expense examples).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (quote form), Cal.com embed (free consultation), Advanced Query Loop (next deadlines by date).
**Signature:** a **self-employed tax calculator** for the current tax year (turnover, allowable expenses, pension in; income tax and Class 4 NI out, every band shown), built as an Interactivity-API block with the rates stored as editable settings, so the practice updates rates each April and gets a lead tool that works without a login. (seen on: [GoForma: Self-employed tax calculator](https://www.goforma.com/calculators/self-employed-tax-calculator))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A "next deadline" strip driven by `deadline` records, e.g. "31 January: self assessment and balancing payment", which rolls on automatically (operational).
- A sector page for creatives covering royalties, retainers and expense claims in their own words (buying confidence). (seen on: [GoForma: Accountants for creatives](https://www.goforma.com/accountants-for-creatives))
- Qualifications with links to the ACCA/AAT public registers ("real credentials, verifiable on every register") (trust & proof). (seen on: [GoForma: Packages](https://www.goforma.com/packages))
- An instant quote as a short stepped form (conversion helpers). (seen on: [Crunch: Instant quote](https://www.crunch.co.uk/instant-quote))
- A plain-English glossary (accrual, reconciliation, MTD) (content & tools). (seen on: [Steph's Books: Glossary](https://stephsbooks.com/glossary))
**Style: Ruled ledger tabular**
- Type: headings Tabular 700 (Fontshare) (display 5rem); body IBM Plex Sans 400 at 18px; all figures IBM Plex Mono 500 with tabular numerals.
- Palette: bg #FBFBF8, text #1B1F1C, accent #1E5E3A (ledger green, primary action), red ink #B3261E (negative figures and deadlines only), surface #FFFFFF, line #D9DED6 (ruled lines).
- Layout: ledger paper. Faint horizontal rules at the baseline across content areas and a double rule under section totals. Packages are columns in a single ruled table (rows = what's included, ticks as ✓ characters in mono), with no highlighted column. The calculator is a two-column form: inputs left, running result right. Buttons 2px radius, inputs 0 with bottom border only.
- Imagery: very little. Scans of real paperwork (receipts, a shoebox) in black and white, and portraits of the accountants at their desks.
- Motion: calculator totals update on input with no animation. Nothing on scroll.
- Why it fits now: finance tools for small businesses are borrowing the spreadsheet and ledger aesthetic back as a sign of plain dealing, often with monospaced figures. Example: [Pilot](https://www.pilot.com/).
**Style variations:** Ledger: #FBFBF8, green #1E5E3A · Carbon copy: #EEF1F6 bg, #23395B accent · Red pen: white, ink #1B1F1C, #B3261E accent.
**Real-world basis:** [GoForma: Packages](https://www.goforma.com/packages), [GoForma: Accountants for creatives](https://www.goforma.com/accountants-for-creatives), [GoForma: Self-employed tax calculator](https://www.goforma.com/calculators/self-employed-tax-calculator), [Crunch: Instant quote](https://www.crunch.co.uk/instant-quote), [Steph's Books: Pricing](https://stephsbooks.com/pricing)
**Refs:**
- [GoForma: Self-employed tax calculator](https://www.goforma.com/calculators/self-employed-tax-calculator): a calculator with every band broken out for the current tax year.
- [GoForma: Accountants for creatives](https://www.goforma.com/accountants-for-creatives): a sector page for creatives (royalties, retainers, IR35).
- [Steph's Books: Glossary](https://stephsbooks.com/glossary): a plain-English glossary on a small bookkeeper's site (WordPress).

#### 126 · Small Law Practice: Tenant & Immigration (`counsel`)
**For:** small solicitors' firms, law centres and legal-aid practices doing housing (possession, disrepair, homelessness) and immigration/asylum work.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-practice-area · single-practice-area · page-fees · page-legal-aid · archive-person · page-how-to-get-help · archive-news · page-policies · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** "Problems we help with" written as clients' own questions ("My landlord is going to evict me next week. Can I stop this?"), advice line hours ("Mon–Wed 10am–12pm, press 2"), "due to funding we can only help with…" scope list, legal aid explainer (means and merits test), published fees for immigration applications (SRA requirement), practice area pages, team by department, useful links (Shelter, JCWI, Refugee Council), eVisa / policy-change guidance page, complaints and SRA details, donate/support (law centres), book an appointment.
**Content model:** `practice_area` (questions we help with, legal aid available: yes/partly/no, useful links), `person` (department, SRA ID, languages), `fee_item` (application type, fee basis, estimate, disbursements).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (legal enquiry form, with a warning not to send documents), GiveWP or Jetpack Donations (law centres), Polylang (key pages in the main community languages).
**Signature:** a **published immigration fees page** meeting the SRA price-transparency rule: application types, hourly or fixed basis, typical total, what's included, and Home Office fees listed separately as disbursements. It is bound to `fee_item` records so the firm can keep it current. (seen on: [Wilsons Solicitors: Immigration fees](https://www.wilsonllp.co.uk/fees/immigration-fees))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Advice-line hours with "open now / closed" driven by those hours, and what to include if you email instead (local & practical). (seen on: [Hackney Community Law Centre: Immigration advice](https://hclc.org.uk/immigration-advice/))
- A scope notice: "due to funding restrictions we can only help with…", bound to a field and shown on each practice area (operational). (seen on: [HCLC: Immigration advice](https://hclc.org.uk/immigration-advice/))
- A legal aid page that explains the means and merits tests in plain words, with a link to the government checker (buying confidence). (seen on: [Wilsons: Legal aid](https://www.wilsonllp.co.uk/fees/legal-aid))
- A dated guidance page for policy changes (e.g. BRP to eVisa), with the date prominent (content & tools). (seen on: [HCLC: Transition to eVisa](https://hclc.org.uk/useful-information.php))
- Translated summaries of key pages and a "we can arrange an interpreter" line (accessibility & inclusion).
**Style: Protest-poster civic**
- Type: headings Special Gothic Expanded One 400 (wide by design, display 7rem); body Public Sans 400 at 19px (built for US government services); question lists in Public Sans 700.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #111111, accent #F7D117 (highlighter yellow, used as flat blocks behind black text), urgent #C4161C (deadline notices only), surface #F2F2F0, line #111111.
- Layout: the front page is a stack of big client questions, each a link to the answer ("I've been served a possession notice"). The advice line and hours are pinned at the top. Practice areas are two wide columns (Housing | Immigration), not cards. Fee tables are full-width ruled tables. Buttons 0 radius, 3px black border, images 0.
- Imagery: the community and the office (front door, reception, outreach sessions), and documentary photos of estates and streets. No gavels, scales or handshakes.
- Motion: none.
- Why it fits now: rights organisations and co-op design studios are using activist poster type and flat highlighter colour to look like the campaigns they belong to rather than corporate law. Example: [Law Centres Network](https://www.lawcentres.org.uk/) (designed by the Multitudes co-op).
**Style variations:** Highlighter: white, yellow #F7D117 · Newsprint: #EDEBE4 bg, black · Night court: #111111 bg, #F7D117 headings, white body.
**Real-world basis:** [Wilsons: Immigration fees](https://www.wilsonllp.co.uk/fees/immigration-fees), [Wilsons: Legal aid](https://www.wilsonllp.co.uk/fees/legal-aid), [HCLC: Housing advice](https://hclc.org.uk/housing-advice/), [HCLC: Immigration advice](https://hclc.org.uk/immigration-advice/), [Law Centres Network: List of law centres](https://www.lawcentres.org.uk/list-of-law-centres)
**Refs:**
- [Hackney Community Law Centre: Housing law](https://hclc.org.uk/housing-advice/): problems listed as the questions clients actually ask.
- [Wilsons Solicitors: Immigration fees](https://www.wilsonllp.co.uk/fees/immigration-fees): a fee page published to meet the SRA rule.
- [Law Centres Network: List and map of law centres](https://www.lawcentres.org.uk/list-of-law-centres): a directory with list and map views, useful for referral pages.

<a id="127"></a>
#### 127 · Mediator (`middle`)
**For:** independent family mediators (and some workplace or community mediators) working alone or in a two-person practice, often online.
**Templates:** front-page · page-how-mediation-works · page-miam · page-fees · page-voucher-scheme · page-children-in-mediation · page-about-mediator · page-client-referral · archive-guide · page-policies
**Patterns (~35):** "what you'll pay, start to finish" (MIAM per person, session fee, court form), six-step process (book MIAM → contact other party → joint sessions → parenting plan → finances → agreement), MIAM explainer and exemptions, £500 Family Mediation Voucher Scheme explainer, legal aid eligibility link, children in mediation (child-inclusive) fees, sliding-scale fees, free 15-minute chat, client referral form (for solicitors), guides (C100 form, mediation vs court), mediator accreditation (FMC / FMCA), complaints.
**Content model:** `fee_item` (service, per person / shared, price, what's included), `guide` (topic, updated date).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (client referral with both parties' details), Cal.com embed (free chat and MIAM booking).
**Signature:** a **"what you'll pay, start to finish" cost walk-through**: MIAM, sessions (typical number by case type), court certificate and the £500 voucher deduction laid out in order with a running total, so separating couples see the whole cost before the first call. (seen on: [BookMIAM: Pricing](https://www.bookmiam.co.uk/pricing/))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A voucher-scheme page with eligibility and "this may cover your first sessions" (buying confidence). (seen on: [BookMIAM: £500 voucher scheme](https://www.bookmiam.co.uk/mediation-voucher-scheme/))
- A MIAM exemptions page (domestic abuse, urgency) written carefully and plainly (accessibility & inclusion). (seen on: [BookMIAM: MIAM exemptions](https://www.bookmiam.co.uk/miam-exemptions/))
- A client referral form for solicitors (conversion helpers). (seen on: [Suzanna Stein Family Mediation: Client referral](https://www.suzannasteinfamilymediation.com/index.php/client-referral))
- Children in Mediation priced per child and shared between parents (trust & proof). (seen on: [Independent Family Mediation: Fees](https://independentfamilymediation.org/mediation-fees/))
- Separate booking links for each party, so neither has to pass on the other's contact details (owner quality of life).
**Style: Two-column dialogue editorial**
- Type: headings Gowun Batang 700 (display 4.75rem); body Karla 400 at 18px; process step numbers Gowun Batang 400 at 3rem (the process really is a sequence).
- Palette: bg #F4F6F5, text #1F2421, party A #2E6F95 (slate blue), party B #B5782A (ochre), shared #4F5E46 (moss, for agreed outcomes and primary actions), line #C5CCC7.
- Layout: a two-column device throughout. Guides and FAQs set "what one parent asks" left and "what the other asks" right, with the shared answer spanning both. The process runs as a numbered vertical sequence. The fees walk-through is a single ruled column with a running total. Buttons 6px radius, images 0.
- Imagery: rooms rather than people: two chairs and a table, a window, a video-call setup. No couples arguing, no torn paper hearts.
- Motion: none on scroll. The running total updates instantly as optional steps are ticked.
- Why it fits now: long-form editorial layouts with generous serif type are being used by professional services to signal calm and neutrality instead of the corporate-legal look. Example: [frieze](https://www.frieze.com/).
**Style variations:** Neutral: #F4F6F5, moss #4F5E46 · Paper: #FFFFFF, ink #1F2421, blue and ochre only in the diagram · Evening: #1F2421 bg, #E8ECE9 text.
**Real-world basis:** [BookMIAM: Pricing](https://www.bookmiam.co.uk/pricing/), [BookMIAM: How mediation works](https://www.bookmiam.co.uk/how-mediation-works/), [Independent Family Mediation: Fees](https://independentfamilymediation.org/mediation-fees/), [IFM: Children in mediation](https://independentfamilymediation.org/children-in-mediation-cim/), [Suzanna Stein: Standard fees](https://www.suzannasteinfamilymediation.com/index.php/standard-fees)
**Refs:**
- [BookMIAM: Family mediation costs & pricing](https://www.bookmiam.co.uk/pricing/): fixed fees, the voucher scheme and legal aid on one page (WordPress).
- [Independent Family Mediation: Mediation fees](https://independentfamilymediation.org/mediation-fees/): MIAM, session length, typical session count and Children in Mediation pricing (WordPress).
- [BookMIAM: How mediation works](https://www.bookmiam.co.uk/how-mediation-works/): the real step sequence from MIAM to court documents.

#### 128 · Fee-Only Financial Planner (`fiduciary`)
**For:** fee-only, flat-fee or advice-only planners (CFP, often solo or 2–5 people) who sell advice rather than products.
**Templates:** front-page · page-flat-fee · page-whats-included · page-services · page-who-we-serve · archive-guide · page-team · page-get-started · page-disclosures · page-faq
**Patterns (~40):** flat-fee statement ("$9,000 a year, no asset minimum"), fee-only vs fee-based explainer, "always do the math" comparison with a 1% AUM fee, what's included (tax planning, insurance review, estate, withdrawal planning, Social Security…), sample deliverables (sample tax report PDF), who is a good fit, fiduciary statement, custodian line (assets held at Schwab/Fidelity), disclosures page (Form CRS, ADV Part 2 brochure), CFP/CFA credentials, get-started steps, client login link.
**Content model:** `service_area` (what we do, sample deliverable PDF), `team_member` (designations, CRD number), `disclosure` (document, date, PDF).
**Plugins:** Cal.com embed (introductory meeting), Jetpack Newsletter (planning letters).
**Signature:** a **flat fee vs 1% comparison** ("always do the math"): visitors enter their invested assets, and an Interactivity-API block shows the yearly and 10-year cost of a 1% AUM fee next to the firm's flat fee. The numbers come from a settings field, and it is labelled as illustration only. (seen on: [Clarity Capital Advisors: Flat fees](https://www.claritycapitaladvisors.com/our-fixed-fee-pricing-simple-and-straightforward))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Sample deliverables linked as PDFs ("see a sample report") under each service (buying confidence). (seen on: [Arnold & Mote: Flat fee financial advisors](https://arnoldmotewealthmanagement.com/flat-fee-financial-advisors-planners/))
- A "What's included in the flat fee" list, one heading per area (trust & proof). (seen on: [Arnold & Mote](https://arnoldmotewealthmanagement.com/flat-fee-financial-advisors-planners/))
- A disclosures page pattern with Form CRS and ADV Part 2 slots and a "last updated" date per document (owner quality of life). (seen on: [BWFA: Form CRS](https://bwfa.com/bwfa-form-crs/))
- A "who is a good fit" / "who we're not right for" pair (conversion helpers).
- A client login link kept visually apart from marketing actions (local & practical). (seen on: [Clarity Capital Advisors](https://www.claritycapitaladvisors.com/our-fixed-fee-pricing-simple-and-straightforward))
**Style: Numbers-first annual report**
- Type: headings Domine 500 (display 5rem); body Domine 400 at 19px; figures and tables Martian Mono 400 (narrow width) with tabular numerals.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #14213D, accent #9A7B4F (brass, primary action), surface #F1EFEA, line #CFCBC2, loss/cost #8E2F2F (used only in the comparison chart).
- Layout: set out like an annual report: a large figure (the flat fee) set in mono as the first thing on the front page, with a two-line caption, then "what's included" as a ruled two-column list, then the comparison tool. Charts are simple bars in ink and brass, directly labelled with no legend. Buttons 0 radius with 1px border, images 0.
- Imagery: portraits of the planners in their office, and photos of real client-meeting materials (the plan binder, a whiteboard). No stock money, piggy banks or sunset retirees.
- Motion: the comparison bars resize instantly on input. No scroll effects.
- Why it fits now: small advice-only firms compete on transparency, and plain figure-led product pages have become the model for that. Example: [FreeAgent](https://www.freeagent.com/).
**Style variations:** Report: white, brass #9A7B4F · Statement: #F1EFEA bg, navy #14213D accent · Ink: #14213D bg, #F1EFEA text, brass kept.
**Real-world basis:** [Clarity Capital Advisors: Flat fees](https://www.claritycapitaladvisors.com/our-fixed-fee-pricing-simple-and-straightforward), [Clarity: Firm disclosures](https://www.claritycapitaladvisors.com/firm-disclosures), [Arnold & Mote: Flat fee advisors](https://arnoldmotewealthmanagement.com/flat-fee-financial-advisors-planners/), [BWFA: ADV brochure](https://bwfa.com/adv-brochure/), [Advice-Only Network](https://adviceonlynetwork.com/)
**Refs:**
- [Clarity Capital Advisors: Flat fee pricing](https://www.claritycapitaladvisors.com/our-fixed-fee-pricing-simple-and-straightforward): the "do the math" argument with a stated flat fee and no minimum.
- [Arnold & Mote Wealth Management: Flat fee financial advisors](https://arnoldmotewealthmanagement.com/flat-fee-financial-advisors-planners/): what's included with sample reports (WordPress).
- [BWFA: Form CRS](https://bwfa.com/bwfa-form-crs/): a disclosure page pattern (WordPress).

#### 129 · Independent Estate / Letting Agent (`listing`)
**For:** independent neighbourhood or design-led estate and letting agents with 20–150 live listings, selling and letting in a few postcodes.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-property (sale / rent) · single-property · taxonomy-collection · page-past-sales · page-book-a-valuation · page-sell-your-home · page-landlords · page-property-alerts · archive-journal (area guides)
**Patterns (~50):** property card (price / per week, area + postcode, beds, sq ft, status: available / under offer / let agreed / sold), listing filters (buy or rent, type, neighbourhood, beds, price), map view, themed collections ("Homes with a view", "Neighbourhood gems", "First homes"), single property (gallery, floor plan, EPC, council tax band, tenure, key facts, viewing request), past sales with days on market, book a valuation, property alerts sign-up (buy/rent, type, area, beds), landlord services (fully managed / let only), area guides, redress scheme and client money protection badges, tenant fees page.
**Content model:** `property` (sale/rent, price, price qualifier, beds, baths, sq ft, EPC rating, council tax band, tenure, status, days on market, lat/lng, floor plan, gallery), `collection` taxonomy, `area` taxonomy.
**Plugins:** Query Filter (sale/rent, type, area, beds, price), Advanced Query Loop (status and price ordering), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (map view), Jetpack Forms (viewing request, valuation, alerts).
**Signature:** a **past sales archive with "sold in X days on the market"** on each card, pulled from the same `property` records when status changes to sold, so the agent's track record builds itself and sellers see proof on the valuation page. (seen on: [Idyll: Past sales](https://www.theidyll.co.uk/sell-your-home/past-sales))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Themed collections alongside ordinary filters ("Homes with a view", "Neighbourhood gems"), each with a filter by type and neighbourhood (conversion helpers). (seen on: [Idyll: Homes with a view](https://www.theidyll.co.uk/properties-for-sale-in-london/homes-with-a-view))
- A property alerts form (buy or rent, type, neighbourhood, bedrooms) that emails new matches (conversion helpers). (seen on: [Idyll: Register for property alerts](https://www.theidyll.co.uk/register-for-property-alerts))
- Status stamps (under offer / let agreed / sold) set in the card as a typographic stamp, never removed silently (trust & proof).
- A required-information block on each listing (EPC, council tax band, tenure, material information), printed on a one-page A4 brochure view (content & tools).
- Redress scheme and client money protection badges with membership numbers in the footer (trust & proof). (seen on: [Storeys](https://storeys.co/landlord-services/))
**Style: Architectural listing index**
- Type: headings Panchang 800 (Fontshare, wide by design, display 6rem); body Karla 400 at 18px; key facts Karla 500 with tabular figures.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #151515, accent #D2382B (stamp red, used for status stamps and the primary action), surface #EDEDEA, line #BDBDB8, map ink #3C3C3C.
- Layout: listings are an index: large photo, then one line of key facts (£ / beds / sq ft / area / status) in condensed type, with a switch between index, grid and map. The single property page is editorial: full-bleed lead photo, a key-facts table, floor plan given the same weight as photos, then prose. Buttons 0 radius, images 0, inputs 0.
- Imagery: architectural photography of the homes (straight verticals, daylight, no fisheye), floor plans as clean line drawings, and street photos for area guides.
- Motion: View Transitions between the listing card and property page (the photo expands). Map pins highlight their card on hover. Nothing on scroll.
- Why it fits now: design-led agents have made property pages look like architecture magazines, and buyers now expect floor plans and sq ft up front. Example: [The Modern House](https://www.themodernhouse.com/).
**Style variations:** Index: white, stamp red #D2382B · Brick: #F0E7DF bg, #6E2B1E accent · Concrete: #DADAD6 bg, ink #151515.
**Real-world basis:** [Idyll: Homes with a view](https://www.theidyll.co.uk/properties-for-sale-in-london/homes-with-a-view), [Idyll: Past sales](https://www.theidyll.co.uk/sell-your-home/past-sales), [Storeys: Available properties](https://storeys.co/available-properties/), [Storeys: Landlord services](https://storeys.co/landlord-services/), [The Modern House: Homes for sale](https://www.themodernhouse.com/sales-list/homes/all/)
**Refs:**
- [Idyll: Past sales](https://www.theidyll.co.uk/sell-your-home/past-sales): sold homes with price, sq ft and days on market.
- [Idyll: Homes with a view](https://www.theidyll.co.uk/properties-for-sale-in-london/homes-with-a-view): a themed collection with type and neighbourhood filters.
- [Storeys: Available properties](https://storeys.co/available-properties/): an independent Hackney agent's lettings archive (WordPress).

#### 130 · Business & Life Coach (`coach`)
**For:** independent coaches (leadership, founder, career, life) working 1:1 and with small teams, who publish writing or a podcast.
**Templates:** front-page · page-approach · page-coaching · page-teams · archive-coach (for small collectives) · archive-case-study · single-case-study · archive-podcast · page-faq · page-inquire
**Patterns (~35):** approach statement (how the coaching works and what it doesn't do), coaching offer (length of engagement, session frequency, format), who it's for / who it isn't, coach profiles (training, accreditation, background), case studies (client situation → work done → what changed, anonymised), downloadable fact sheet PDF, inquiry form (role, company size, what's going on), FAQ (confidentiality, cancellation, company-paid coaching), podcast episodes, book, newsletter, workshops and events.
**Content model:** `case_study` (client type, engagement length, themes), `episode` (audio URL, guests, date), `coach` (accreditation, specialisms).
**Plugins:** Seriously Simple Podcasting (if the coach runs a podcast), Jetpack Newsletter, Jetpack Forms (inquiry), Cal.com embed (chemistry call).
**Signature:** a **downloadable one-page fact sheet** alongside the inquiry form (format, length, cost range, how matching works), because many coaching clients need something to forward to the person who approves the budget. (seen on: [Joan Garry Consulting: Executive coaching](https://joangarry.com/work-with-joan-executive-coaching/))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- An FAQ on confidentiality and what gets shared with the employer who pays (trust & proof). (seen on: [Joan Garry Consulting](https://joangarry.com/work-with-joan-executive-coaching/))
- Anonymised case studies as situation, work and outcome (trust & proof). (seen on: [Reboot: Case studies](https://www.reboot.io/case-studies/))
- A podcast archive with episodes and transcripts (community). (seen on: [Reboot: Podcast](https://www.reboot.io/podcast/))
- A "taking new clients from [month]" availability line on the inquiry page (operational).
- A reading list or "leadership library" page (content & tools). (seen on: [Reboot](https://www.reboot.io/about/coaches/))
**Style: Letterpress essay**
- Type: headings Hedvig Letters Serif 400 (display 5rem); body Hedvig Letters Sans 400 at 19px / 1.65; pull quotes Hedvig Letters Serif at 2.5rem.
- Palette: bg #F7F7F4, text #1C1B19, accent #3B5BA5 (ink blue, links and primary action), surface #ECEBE6, line #C9C7BF.
- Layout: essay-first. The front page is a short piece of writing (the approach) set at 62ch with running heads and footnotes, then the offer, then the latest writing or episode. Case studies are long-form with a margin column for the facts (engagement length, themes). Buttons 0 radius with underline hover, images 0.
- Imagery: one honest portrait of the coach, and photographs of the places where the work happens (a walk, a room). No mountain summits or "breakthrough" stock.
- Motion: none on scroll. Footnotes open inline.
- Why it fits now: coaches with a following are presenting themselves as writers and thinkers, with serif essay sites rather than landing pages. Example: [Reboot](https://www.reboot.io/) (Tiempos serif, essay-led).
**Style variations:** Paper: #F7F7F4, ink blue #3B5BA5 · Notebook: #FFFFFF, ruled lines #D6E0EE · Late: #1C1B19 bg, #ECEBE6 text.
**Real-world basis:** [Reboot: Coaches](https://www.reboot.io/about/coaches/), [Reboot: Case studies](https://www.reboot.io/case-studies/), [Reboot: Podcast](https://www.reboot.io/podcast/), [Joan Garry Consulting: Executive coaching](https://joangarry.com/work-with-joan-executive-coaching/)
**Refs:**
- [Joan Garry Consulting: Executive coach & strategic advisor](https://joangarry.com/work-with-joan-executive-coaching/): an inquiry form, FAQ and downloadable fact sheet on one page (WordPress).
- [Reboot: Case studies](https://www.reboot.io/case-studies/): case studies written about the people as well as the outcomes (WordPress).
- [Reboot: Coaches](https://www.reboot.io/about/coaches/): a small collective's coach profiles, framed by a shared approach.

<a id="131"></a>
#### 131 · Virtual Assistant (`va`)
**For:** solo VAs and two-person admin/marketing support businesses serving small business owners.
**Templates:** front-page · page-services · single-service · page-pricing · page-examples · page-about · page-how-we-work · page-faq · page-contact
**Patterns (~30):** services list (inbox and calendar, email marketing, social scheduling, bookkeeping admin, website updates), hourly rate + monthly retainer hours (10 / 20 / 30 hours), retainer terms (hours don't roll over, response times), examples/portfolio (emails written and built), tools I use (Klaviyo, Mailchimp, Asana, Xero), how we work (onboarding call → access set-up → weekly check-in), working hours and time zone, "who we are: two people, one business" about, contact/coffee call.
**Content model:** `service` (tasks included, tools), `example` (type, client sector, image), `retainer` (hours/month, price, response time).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms, Cal.com embed (intro call).
**Signature:** an **examples page** showing actual work (email campaigns designed and built, with the goal of each: sale, abandoned cart, re-engagement), which proves the service better than a list of tasks. (seen on: [Astraea VA: Examples](https://astraeava.com/portfolio/))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A retainer table showing hours, price and "hours don't roll over", written as a plain table with no highlighted tier (buying confidence).
- A "tools I use" row as a plain text list of tool names, no logo cloud (trust & proof). (seen on: [Astraea VA: Examples](https://astraeava.com/portfolio/))
- Working hours with the VA's local time shown live and converted to the visitor's time zone (local & practical).
- A capacity line ("2 retainer spots open for November") bound to a setting (operational).
- An onboarding checklist PDF for new clients (access, logins, preferences) (care & aftercare).
**Style: Index-card utility**
- Type: headings Istok Web 700 (display 5rem); body Istok Web 400 at 18px; task lists and times Fragment Mono 400.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #111111, accent #FFE45C (highlighter, flat fields behind text), link #1F4E8C, surface #F2F2EF, line #111111.
- Layout: organised like a to-do list. Services are checklists of real tasks, with headings as index-card tabs. The front page runs top to bottom: what I take off your plate (a checklist), how it works (three real steps), hours and price, examples. Buttons 4px radius, 2px border, images 0.
- Imagery: screenshots of real work (an email, a tidy calendar) in simple frames, plus one portrait. No laptop-and-latte flatlays.
- Motion: checklist items tick off on hover (a stroke draws instantly). Nothing on scroll.
- Why it fits now: plain, list-driven sites have become the credible look for small service businesses tired of template landing pages. Example: [Are.na](https://www.are.na/).
**Style variations:** Highlighter: white, #FFE45C · Manila: #F3E7C9 bg, ink #111111 · Inbox zero: #111111 bg, #F2F2EF text, yellow kept.
**Real-world basis:** [Astraea VA: Examples](https://astraeava.com/portfolio/), [Astraea VA: Services](https://astraeava.com/services/), [We Are Neidín](https://weareneidin.com/)
**Refs:**
- [Astraea VA: Email marketing examples](https://astraeava.com/portfolio/): a solo VA's work shown as examples, with the tools listed (WordPress).
- [We Are Neidín](https://weareneidin.com/): a two-person support business with a voice of its own ("the boring bits. sorted.") (WordPress).

<a id="132"></a>
#### 132 · Translator / Interpreter (`lingua`)
**For:** freelance translators and interpreters (literary, academic, legal, technical, games) working in one or two language pairs.
**Templates:** front-page (bilingual) · page-services · single-service (per field) · page-translations (published work) · page-examples · page-writing · page-faq · page-contact · page-credentials
**Patterns (~30):** language pairs and direction ("French > English only, into my native language"), fields (social sciences, psychoanalysis, software, games), services (translation, proofreading, MTPE, revision), published translations list (title, author, publisher, year), examples (side-by-side source and target excerpt), professional memberships and code of conduct (SFT, ITI, ATA, CIOL), clients list, ORCID / ProZ / academic profiles, "why not machine translation" note, contact/quote form (word count, deadline, file type).
**Content model:** `translation` (title, author, publisher, year, source language, cover), `example` (source text, target text, field).
**Plugins:** Polylang (full mirror of the site in both languages), Jetpack Forms (quote request with word count and deadline).
**Signature:** a **fully bilingual site** with a language switch on every page and a published-translations list. The site is written in both languages, so the translator's own writing is the sample. (seen on: [John Holland Translations: Translations](https://jhollandtranslations.com/en/translations.html))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A side-by-side source/target example block on service pages (buying confidence). (seen on: [John Holland: Examples](https://jhollandtranslations.com/en/examples.html))
- Membership of a professional body linked to its code of conduct (trust & proof). (seen on: [John Holland Translations](https://jhollandtranslations.com/en/services.html))
- A field page per specialism (software, games, websites), each with its own terms and examples (conversion helpers). (seen on: [Anthony Teixeira: Video game translation](https://www.at-it-translator.com/english-to-french-video-games-translation-services/))
- A quote form that asks for word count, deadline and file type, plus a "rush" note (operational).
- The translator's local time and "currently booked until [date]" (local & practical).
**Style: Multiscript specimen**
- Type: headings Noto Serif Display 600 (display 5rem, chosen for script coverage across Latin, Cyrillic, Greek and more); body Noto Serif 400 at 18px; language codes and metadata Noto Sans Mono 500 (FR > EN).
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #111111, accent #B5121B (proofreader's red, links and primary action), surface #F0EEE9, line #CFCBC3.
- Layout: two parallel columns as the core device: source language left, target right, aligned by paragraph, used for examples and for the front-page statement shown in both languages. Published translations are a bibliography list with cover thumbnails. Buttons 0 radius, images 0.
- Imagery: book covers of published translations, the translator's desk with dictionaries, and an honest portrait. No flags, no globes.
- Motion: hovering a paragraph highlights its counterpart in the other column. Nothing on scroll.
- Why it fits now: type foundries are showing multiscript families in parallel columns, and that specimen look suits someone whose work is the move between languages. Example: [Typotheque](https://www.typotheque.com/).
**Style variations:** Specimen: white, red #B5121B · Galley proof: #F0EEE9 bg, ink #111111 · Night desk: #1A1A1A bg, #F0EEE9 text.
**Real-world basis:** [John Holland: Translations](https://jhollandtranslations.com/en/translations.html), [John Holland: Services](https://jhollandtranslations.com/en/services.html), [John Holland: Examples](https://jhollandtranslations.com/en/examples.html), [Anthony Teixeira: Games translation](https://www.at-it-translator.com/english-to-french-video-games-translation-services/), [Anthony Teixeira: Proofreading](https://www.at-it-translator.com/french-proofreader-editing-and-revision-services/)
**Refs:**
- [John Holland Translations: Translations](https://jhollandtranslations.com/en/translations.html): a bilingual site with a published-work list.
- [Anthony Teixeira: Video game translation](https://www.at-it-translator.com/english-to-french-video-games-translation-services/): a per-field service page for a solo translator (WordPress).

<a id="133"></a>
#### 133 · Sustainability Consultancy (`impact`)
**For:** small sustainability consultancies (1–10 people) helping SMEs with B Corp certification, carbon footprints and supply-chain requirements.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-solution · single-solution · page-b-corp · archive-case-study · single-case-study · page-sectors · archive-resource · page-about · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** productised solutions with fixed scope (PPN 006 carbon reduction plan, SECR reporting, B Corp climate action plan, SBTi targets), "what does it include" list per solution, B Corp standards explainer (V2, what changed, baseline requirements), case studies with a real outcome (contract won, target hit, days to compliance), sectors served, resources and guides, fractional sustainability lead offer, book a call, partners (B Corp, carbon accounting tools), "our own footprint" page.
**Content model:** `solution` (who needs it, requirement/regulation, deliverables, turnaround), `case_study` (client, sector, requirement, outcome, time taken), `resource` (topic, updated date).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms, Cal.com embed, Query Filter (case studies by sector and solution).
**Signature:** **productised compliance pages**, one per requirement (e.g. PPN 006 Carbon Reduction Plan): who needs it, what the plan contains, how the consultancy gets you there, turnaround, and linked case studies. Each page answers a tender or a buyer's question directly. (seen on: [Green Business: PPN 006 Carbon Reduction Plans](https://green.business/products/ppn-006-carbon-reduction-plan))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A dated "what changed" explainer for standards updates (B Corp V2), with a "last reviewed" date bound to the post (content & tools). (seen on: [Footprint Sustainability: B Corp](https://footprintsustainability.co/b-corp))
- Case studies filtered by sector, each leading with the concrete outcome (trust & proof). (seen on: [Green Business: Case studies](https://green.business/blogs/case-studies))
- A "this website's footprint" note: page weight, hosting, and a low-data mode that swaps photos for dithered versions (owner quality of life).
- Deadline notices tied to regulations (e.g. reporting year ends), shown on the relevant solution page (operational).
- Sector pages in the client's vocabulary (construction, food, professional services) (conversion helpers). (seen on: [Green Business: Sectors](https://green.business/pages/sectors))
**Style: Dither / low-carbon 1-bit**
- Type: headings Silkscreen 400 (OFL pixel face, display 4.5rem); body Libre Franklin 400 at 18px; data labels Silkscreen at 14px.
- Palette: bg #F2F0E6 (recycled-paper stock, a physical reason for the off-white), text #1A1A1A, accent #2F6B2F (leaf, primary action), surface #FFFFFF, line #1A1A1A, warning #A34A1F (regulatory deadlines only).
- Layout: a dense, useful grid. Solution pages start with a fact block (who needs it / deadline / deliverables / turnaround) in mono, then prose. Case-study outcomes are stated as one sentence set large, never as a stat row. Charts are 1-bit bar charts. Buttons 0 radius, 1px border, images 0.
- Imagery: dithered 1-bit photographs of clients' real sites (factories, farms, offices), served as small PNGs (a real weight saving), with full-colour versions on click.
- Motion: none. No autoplay video.
- Why it fits now: low-carbon web design (dithered images, small pages, solar hosting) has become a visible stance, and it fits a consultancy that measures footprints. Example: [Low-tech Magazine (solar)](https://solar.lowtechmagazine.com/).
**Style variations:** Recycled: #F2F0E6, leaf #2F6B2F · Solar: #FFD84D bg, ink #1A1A1A · Night grid: #1A1A1A bg, #F2F0E6 text, leaf kept.
**Real-world basis:** [Green Business: PPN 006](https://green.business/products/ppn-006-carbon-reduction-plan), [Green Business: Case studies](https://green.business/blogs/case-studies), [Green Business: Sectors](https://green.business/pages/sectors), [Footprint Sustainability: B Corp](https://footprintsustainability.co/b-corp), [Footprint Sustainability: Services](https://footprintsustainability.co/services)
**Refs:**
- [Green Business: PPN 006 Carbon Reduction Plans](https://green.business/products/ppn-006-carbon-reduction-plan): a productised compliance page for SMEs.
- [Footprint Sustainability: B Corp](https://footprintsustainability.co/b-corp): a dated explainer of the new B Corp standards from a boutique consultancy.
- [Green Business: Case studies](https://green.business/blogs/case-studies): case studies that lead with concrete outcomes.
