<a id="134"></a>
#### 134 · Funeral Director / Celebrant (`rites`)
**For:** independent funeral directors with one to four branches, and independent celebrants who work alongside them.
**Templates:** front-page · page-when-someone-dies · page-funeral-costs · archive-service · single-service (cremation, burial, direct cremation, child funerals) · page-plan-your-own-funeral · archive-branch · single-branch · page-bereavement-support · archive-team
**Patterns (~40):** 24/7 phone line, "what to do when someone dies" checklist (medical certificate, registering, green form), published prices (unattended cremation £X all inclusive, simple service, full support) and CMA standardised price list PDF, instant estimate by email, service types (cremation, burial, religious, non-religious, natural burial, baby and child), coffins and urns, funeral cars, flowers, reception, repatriation, branches with addresses, meet the team, funeral wishes consultation (free, 45 minutes), bereavement support group (monthly, free), funeral notices.
**Content model:** `service` (price from, inclusions, what's not included), `branch` (address, phone, hours), `notice` (name, dates, service time and place, donations link, family-approved), companion `event` (bereavement group).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (estimate request, wishes consultation), Advanced Query Loop (upcoming funerals and group dates), GiveWP or Jetpack Donations (in-memory donations on notices, where offered), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (branches).
**Signature:** a **transparent prices page** with each option's full inclusions listed in plain words (collection and care, coffin, documentation, crematorium, date chosen by us or you), plus the downloadable CMA price list and an estimate sent by email, so families can compare without phoning round. (seen on: [Exit Here: Funeral prices](https://www.exithere.com/funeral-prices))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A step-by-step "what to do when someone dies" guide with the 24/7 number repeated at each step (care & aftercare). (seen on: [Exit Here: What to do when someone dies](https://www.exithere.com/what-to-do-when-someone-dies))
- An estimate form that emails an indicative quote, clearly labelled "not a fixed total" (buying confidence). (seen on: [Poppy's Funerals: Funeral costs](https://www.poppysfunerals.co.uk/funeral-costs/))
- A free funeral wishes consultation for people planning their own (conversion helpers). (seen on: [Poppy's: Funeral wishes consultation](https://www.poppysfunerals.co.uk/funeral-wishes-consultation/))
- A monthly bereavement support group listed as upcoming dates (community). (seen on: [Exit Here: Bereavement support](https://www.exithere.com/bereavement-support-group))
- The CMA standardised price list PDF linked in the footer of every page (trust & proof). (seen on: [Exit Here: Service pricing PDF](https://www.exithere.com/s/Exit-Here-Service-Pricing.pdf))
**Style: Quiet memorial serif**
- Type: headings Trirong 400 (display 4.5rem, with a real italic used for names on notices); body Jost 400 at 19px / 1.65 (a Futura-like geometric with humanist warmth); phone numbers Jost 500 at 26px.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #1E1E1E, accent #1F2C44 (hearse navy, primary action), surface #EEEDEA, line #C9C6C0, stone #6B6E70 for dates.
- Layout: quiet and orderly. The phone number and "someone has died" link sit at the top of every page. The front page leads with the prices and the guide, not with sympathy copy. Funeral notices are set like newspaper notices: name in italic, dates, service details. There is generous white space but a firm grid. Buttons 2px radius, images 0.
- Imagery: the funeral home's own rooms, cars and staff; flowers from actual services; natural burial grounds. Desaturated slightly. No doves, sunsets or candle stock.
- Motion: none.
- Why it fits now: a new generation of independent funeral directors is replacing religious and sentimental imagery with calm, modern, price-transparent design. Example: [Exit Here](https://www.exithere.com/) (Gill Sans with Baskerville, navy).
**Style variations:** Navy: white, #1F2C44 · Stone: #EEEDEA bg, #3F4A3C accent · Woodland: #F3F1EA bg, #2F4A33 accent (natural burial).
**Real-world basis:** [Exit Here: Funeral prices](https://www.exithere.com/funeral-prices), [Exit Here: What to do when someone dies](https://www.exithere.com/what-to-do-when-someone-dies), [Poppy's: Funeral costs](https://www.poppysfunerals.co.uk/funeral-costs/), [Poppy's: When someone dies](https://www.poppysfunerals.co.uk/plan-a-funeral/when-someone-dies/), [Poppy's: Approach to death care](https://www.poppysfunerals.co.uk/about/poppys-approach-to-death-care/)
**Refs:**
- [Exit Here: Funeral prices](https://www.exithere.com/funeral-prices): all-inclusive packages with every inclusion listed.
- [Poppy's Funerals: Funeral costs](https://www.poppysfunerals.co.uk/funeral-costs/): three price tiers with an email estimator.
- [Exit Here: What to do when someone dies](https://www.exithere.com/what-to-do-when-someone-dies): a practical step-by-step checklist with a 24/7 line.

### XIII. Mobility & transport

<a id="135"></a>
#### 135 · Independent Garage / Mechanic (`garage`)
**For:** one- to five-bay independent garages doing MOTs, servicing and repairs, often family-run for decades.
**Templates:** front-page · page-mot · page-servicing · page-repairs · page-diagnostics · page-book · archive-vehicle · single-vehicle · page-about · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** MOT test centre block with vehicle classes (1, 2, 4), "what the MOT checks" list, service tier table (interim / full / major), online MOT booking form with registration number first, opening hours table (Mon–Fri 8–5:30, Sat 8–12, Sun closed), accreditation row (DVSA test centre, Trust My Garage, RMI), vehicles for sale grid (mileage, MOT expiry, price), family history strip ("established 1980, now run by the son"), collect-and-return radius note, postcode coverage list, mechanic / MOT tester vacancy notice
**Content model:** `vehicle` (make, model, year, mileage, MOT expiry, price, sold flag); `service` (tier, price from, interval). Opening hours and scheme membership numbers as site options, bound into footer and schema.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms.
**Signature:** a dedicated MOT booking page with one fixed online price and a short form that asks for the registration number first (seen on: [Archdeacon Motors](https://www.archdeaconmotors.co.uk/Cambridge-MOT-Booking-Online.html)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Collect-and-return note with a stated radius, "within 10 miles" (seen on: [Exminster Garage](https://exminstergarage.co.uk/exeter-mot-test-centre/))
- Opening hours block with a scheduled bank-holiday closure bar that switches itself off after the end date (hours seen on: [Hadlow Stair Garage](https://hadlowstairgarage.co.uk/car-servicing-in-tonbridge/))
- Trust My Garage and RMI badges linking to the scheme's customer charter (seen on: [Hadlow Stair Garage](https://hadlowstairgarage.co.uk/car-servicing-in-tonbridge/))
- Complaints policy PDF linked from the footer (seen on: [Clerkenwell Motors](https://www.clerkenwellmotors.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/CMComplaintsPolicy.pdf))
- AutoRepair schema with opening hours and the MOT price, so the garage shows properly in local search
**Style: Utility/industrial signage**
- Type: headings Russo One 400, uppercase only on the MOT price and reg plate, tracking 0; body Atkinson Hyperlegible 400/18px; labels and prices Martian Mono 500
- Palette: bg #F4F4F2 (workshop white), text #151515, accent #FFC20E (signal yellow), surface #2B2E33 (ramp grey), line #151515
- Layout: 12-column grid with thick 3px rules like floor markings; square buttons, 2px radius on inputs only; top bar carries phone number and today's hours; home opens with a yellow MOT price panel beside a photo of the actual workshop, then a services table (not cards)
- Imagery: straight documentary photos of the bays, lifts and staff at work, cropped 3:2; no stock cars; the reg field styled like a UK number plate (yellow rear plate)
- Motion: none on scroll; buttons invert colour on hover; reg field shakes once on an invalid plate, disabled under prefers-reduced-motion
- Why it fits now: wayfinding-style sites read as trustworthy and quick on a phone in a car park, the same reason transport signage works (example: [Transport for London](https://www.tfl.gov.uk/))
**Style variations:** Night shift: #151515 bg, yellow #FFC20E text · Tyre black: #0E0E0E rules, white panels · Oil blue: #0B3D91 accent, white ground
**Real-world basis:** [Hadlow Stair Garage: MOTs](https://hadlowstairgarage.co.uk/mot-testing-in-tonbridge/), [Hadlow Stair Garage: vehicles for sale](https://hadlowstairgarage.co.uk/vehicles-for-sale/), [Exminster Garage: MOT](https://exminstergarage.co.uk/exeter-mot-test-centre/), [Clerkenwell Motors: MOT](https://www.clerkenwellmotors.co.uk/m-o-t/), [Archdeacon Motors: MOT booking](https://www.archdeaconmotors.co.uk/Cambridge-MOT-Booking-Online.html)
**Refs:**
- [Archdeacon Motors: MOT online booking](https://www.archdeaconmotors.co.uk/Cambridge-MOT-Booking-Online.html): one price, one form, no detours
- [Clerkenwell Motors: MOT](https://www.clerkenwellmotors.co.uk/m-o-t/): vehicle classes and the postcodes they serve, listed plainly
- [Hadlow Stair Garage: vehicles for sale](https://hadlowstairgarage.co.uk/vehicles-for-sale/): a small used-car list living on a service garage's site

<a id="136"></a>
#### 136 · Classic Car & Motorbike Restorer (`chrome`)
**For:** small restoration and custom shops building one-off cars and motorbikes to commission, plus the odd finished build for sale.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-build · single-build · page-commission · archive-for-sale · page-workshop · page-press · page-events · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** build index grouped by status (commission / for sale / sold), build bio with long-form story, spec list grouped by system (engine / chassis / wheels and tyres / electrical / controls), embedded build video, commission steps (questionnaire, design meeting, donor vehicle, teardown, fabrication, inspection, delivery), build questionnaire PDF download, two-workshop contact block, motorcycles for sale grid, press list with magazine links, show and event dates
**Content model:** `build` (donor make/model/year, engine, chassis, wheels, electrical, controls, status, price, video URL), taxonomy `marque`. `update` child posts for the client build log.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms.
**Signature:** per-build spec sheet grouped by system and bound from meta, set under the story of the build (seen on: [Revival Cycles: The Revival Six](https://www.revivalcycles.com/blogs/revival-build-bio/the-revival-six)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Downloadable build questionnaire that clients fill in and email back (seen on: [Untitled Motorcycles](https://www.untitledmotorcycles.com/commission-a-build))
- Password-protected client build log with dated photos per stage, from teardown to inspection (seen on: [ECD Auto Design](https://ecdautodesign.com/build-journey-defender/))
- "Sold" state that keeps finished builds in the archive as portfolio instead of deleting them (seen on: [Revival Cycles](https://www.revivalcycles.com/collections/custom-motorcycles-for-sale))
- Press page listing features by publication and date (seen on: [Singer](https://www.singervehicledesign.com/press/))
- "Booking commissions for spring 2027" lead-time line set once in site options
**Style: Workshop-manual editorial**
- Type: headings Khand 700 at 9vw; body Newsreader 400/19px with 68ch measure; spec labels IBM Plex Mono 500
- Palette: bg #E9E7E3 (manual paper), text #121212, accent #004225 (racing green), surface #FFFFFF, line #121212
- Layout: asymmetric 7/5 split on build pages (story left, sticky spec sheet right, like an exploded-diagram caption); build index as a numbered ledger with thumbnails, not cards; hairline rules between spec rows
- Imagery: full-bleed workshop photography with honest grease, detail crops of welds and machined parts at 4:5, one wide profile shot per build on a plain backdrop
- Motion: spec sheet stays pinned while the story scrolls; image galleries use View Transitions between thumbnail and full view; static under reduced motion
- Why it fits now: long-form build stories are how this trade sells and the magazines it reads use the same spec-box convention (example: [Hagerty UK](https://www.hagerty.co.uk/))
**Style variations:** Garage floor: #2A2A2A bg, paper text · Concours: white ground, #004225 rules · Scrambler: #C2A878 khaki, black type
**Real-world basis:** [Revival Cycles: build bio](https://www.revivalcycles.com/blogs/revival-build-bio/the-revival-six), [Untitled Motorcycles: bikes](https://www.untitledmotorcycles.com/untitled-motorcycles-bikes), [Purpose Built Moto: Speedway commission](https://www.purposebuiltmoto.com/blogs/gallery/the-speedway-commission), [ECD Auto Design: build stages](https://ecdautodesign.com/build-journey-defender/), [ECD Auto Design: available stock](https://ecdautodesign.com/available-stock/)
**Refs:**
- [Revival Cycles: The Revival Six](https://www.revivalcycles.com/blogs/revival-build-bio/the-revival-six): story first, then a spec list split by system
- [ECD Auto Design: build stages](https://ecdautodesign.com/build-journey-defender/): the commission explained stage by stage, including client photo updates
- [Untitled Motorcycles: commission a build](https://www.untitledmotorcycles.com/commission-a-build): a short page that just hands over the questionnaire

#### 137 · Driving School (`learner`)
**For:** independent driving instructors and small schools of 2–10 instructors teaching manual and automatic.
**Templates:** front-page · page-prices · page-manual · page-automatic · page-intensive · page-instructors · page-pass-club · page-test-centres · page-first-lesson · page-faq · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** price table (manual / automatic × weekday / evening and weekend), 10-hour block booking row, test day package (2.5 hours), intensive course with deposit terms, instructor cards (car, gearbox, areas, languages), area list by postcode, pass wall grouped by month, "your first lesson" checklist (provisional licence, glasses, shoes), local test centre list, special needs lessons page, "become an instructor" block, DVSA news posts
**Content model:** `instructor` (car, transmission, areas, languages); `pass` (pupil first name, area, test date, instructor, first-time flag, photo).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms, Advanced Query Loop.
**Signature:** a pass club wall grouped by month, each entry naming the pupil, their area, the instructor and whether it was a first-time pass (seen on: [Bubble Driving School](https://www.bubbledrivingschool.co.uk/bubble-pass-club)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Availability post pinned to the front page when new slots open (seen on: [Bubble Driving School](https://www.bubbledrivingschool.co.uk/updated-availability-from-this-week-lots-of-manual-and-automatic-lessons-available-now))
- Admin fee and intensive-course deposit stated beside the prices (seen on: [Bubble Driving School](https://www.bubbledrivingschool.co.uk/driving-lesson-prices-bristol-south-gloucestershire-and-north-somerset))
- Local test centres page with addresses and routes (seen on: [A-Class Driving School](https://www.aclassdrivingschoolbristol.co.uk/driving-test-centres))
- Lessons for learners with additional needs on their own page (seen on: [Bubble Driving School](https://www.bubbledrivingschool.co.uk/special-needs-driving-lessons-bristol-north-somerset))
- "What to bring to your first lesson" printable checklist (seen on: [Bubble Driving School](https://www.bubbledrivingschool.co.uk/first-driving-lesson-with-bubble-driving-school))
**Style: Road-sign plain utility**
- Type: headings Overpass 900 (a Highway Gothic descendant), sentence case; body Overpass 400/18px; prices and times Overpass Mono 600
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #0B0C0C, accent #D7191C (L-plate red), surface #F3F2F1, line #1D5AAB (sign blue)
- Layout: one wide column with a price table that stays readable at 360px; a red square "L" as the only logo device; instructor list as a two-column table with car photo; pass wall as a tight month-by-month list with small photos
- Imagery: real pupils holding their pass certificate beside the car (with consent), square crops; instructor photos next to their actual car
- Motion: none apart from focus states; the price table's weekday/weekend columns swap order on mobile via container queries, not animation
- Why it fits now: parents and 17-year-olds both trust the plain public-service look, and it loads fast on bad mobile signal (example: [GOV.UK](https://www.gov.uk/))
**Style variations:** Green P: #00843D accent for Pass Plus · Motorway: #1D5AAB ground, white type · Night drive: #0B0C0C bg, #FFD100 text
**Real-world basis:** [Bubble Driving School: prices](https://www.bubbledrivingschool.co.uk/driving-lesson-prices-bristol-south-gloucestershire-and-north-somerset), [Bubble Driving School: pass club](https://www.bubbledrivingschool.co.uk/bubble-pass-club), [POM Driving School: prices](https://www.pomdrivingschool.co.uk/prices), [POM Driving School: instructors](https://www.pomdrivingschool.co.uk/instructors), [A-Class Driving School: prices](https://www.aclassdrivingschoolbristol.co.uk/driving-lesson-prices)
**Refs:**
- [Bubble Driving School: pass club](https://www.bubbledrivingschool.co.uk/bubble-pass-club): proof by volume, one line per pass, grouped by month
- [Bubble Driving School: prices](https://www.bubbledrivingschool.co.uk/driving-lesson-prices-bristol-south-gloucestershire-and-north-somerset): every price the pupil will meet, including test day and admin fee
- [A-Class Driving School: new changes to test booking](https://www.aclassdrivingschoolbristol.co.uk/new-changes-to-driving-test-booking): news posts that answer the question pupils are already asking

#### 138 · Cycle Courier Co-op (`courier`)
**For:** worker-owned cargo-bike courier co-ops and small bike logistics firms in one city.
**Templates:** front-page · page-services · page-how-it-works · page-coverage · page-book · page-business-accounts · page-become-a-rider · page-sustainability · page-about-the-co-op · archive-news
**Patterns (~40):** load class table (micro 6kg / small 12kg / cargo 150kg / trailer 300kg) with example items, service list (same-day, next-day, collections and returns, ship-from-store), operating hours table (weekdays 6:30–21:00, weekends 7:00–19:00), coverage map with service radius, sectors served (food, flowers, medical, retail), rider recruitment with pay and bike training, co-op statement (who owns it, how decisions get made), business account and API note, accreditation row (FORS, City & Guilds cargo bike training), news
**Content model:** `service` (max weight, max size, lead time, example items); `zone` (name, postcodes, GeoJSON).
**Plugins:** Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap, Jetpack Forms.
**Signature:** a "what can we carry" table by weight class, from documents up to 300kg trailer loads, with an example item per row (seen on: [Pedal Me](https://pedalme.co.uk/services)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Out-of-hours jobs routed through a separate contact form (seen on: [Pedal Me](https://pedalme.co.uk/services))
- Rider recruitment page with pay and what training is given (seen on: [Pedal Me](https://pedalme.co.uk/become-a-rider))
- Sustainability page with the emissions saved per delivery, written plainly (seen on: [Zedify](https://zedify.co.uk/sustainability/))
- Same-day cut-off time in the header that turns into "next-day only" after the cut-off, driven by the site timezone
- Coverage checker: postcode field that answers yes or no against the zone list
**Style: Agitprop hand-set poster**
- Type: headings Fjalla One 400 (condensed), set big and stacked; body Public Sans 400/18px; labels Red Hat Mono 500
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #111111, accent #FF5F1F (courier-bag orange), surface #EDEDED, line #111111
- Layout: poster-scale front page with the load table directly under the headline; blocky black rules; coverage map full width with orange zone fill; rider stories as a plain list with photos, no carousels
- Imagery: riders and bikes shot on real streets in flat daylight, high contrast black-and-white with orange left in (spot colour), 4:5 crops
- Motion: none on scroll; the load table row under the pointer turns orange; map pans only on user input
- Why it fits now: loud, hand-made brand type is back for co-ops and challenger brands that want to sound like people (example: [Oatly](https://www.oatly.com/))
**Style variations:** Night run: #111 bg, #FF5F1F type · Blueprint: #0047AB ground, white rules · Riso: #FF48B0 pink with #0078BF blue
**Real-world basis:** [Pedal Me: services](https://pedalme.co.uk/services), [Pedal Me: become a rider](https://pedalme.co.uk/become-a-rider), [Zedify: locations](https://zedify.co.uk/locations/), [Zedify: how it works](https://zedify.co.uk/how-it-works/), [CoopCycle: cooperatives](https://coopcycle.org/en/cooperatives/)
**Refs:**
- [Pedal Me: services](https://pedalme.co.uk/services): weight classes and hours stated as facts, not slogans
- [Zedify: how it works](https://zedify.co.uk/how-it-works/): a booking flow explained for shops that have never used a courier
- [CoopCycle: the couriers' house](https://coopcycle.org/en/the-couriers-house/): how a courier co-op talks about ownership and mutual support

#### 139 · E-Bike Rental & Tours (`ride`)
**For:** small e-bike hire shops that also run guided tours in a town, park or wine region.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-tour · single-tour · page-rentals · page-private-tours · page-group-bookings · page-safe-cycling · page-faq · page-about · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** tour card (duration, distance, difficulty, price, season), rider requirements strip (minimum age 16, minimum height 4'11", maximum combined weight), start times and meeting point, tour languages, what's included (helmet, lock, trunk bag, map), rental price table (half day / full day), add-ons (kids' trailer, dog trailer, cargo bike), private tour prices, weather and cancellation policy, what to bring, route map, FareHarbor booking button
**Content model:** `tour` (duration, distance, difficulty, price, min age, min height, max weight, season start/end month, start times, meeting point, languages, booking URL, GPX).
**Plugins:** Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap. Booking through a FareHarbor embed (external).
**Signature:** each tour card carries a rider requirements strip and its season window next to the book button, so people check they qualify before paying (seen on: [Sol Rides](https://www.solrides.com/tours-and-rentals)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Tours hide themselves outside their season months (April–October) using the season meta (seen on: [Sol Rides](https://www.solrides.com/tours-and-rentals))
- Cancellation terms in one paragraph: full refund over 48 hours, 50% inside, reschedule for smoke or heat (seen on: [Sol Rides](https://www.solrides.com/faq))
- Early-morning tour at a lower price (seen on: [Amp'd Adventures](https://ampdadventures.com/tours/))
- Safe cycling page with local traffic rules for visitors (seen on: [MacBike](https://www.macbike.nl/en/safe-cycling/))
- Downloadable GPX and a printable route card for self-guided rentals
**Style: Topographic trail map**
- Type: headings Titillium Web 700; body Source Serif 4 400/18px; distances, gradients and times Fragment Mono 400
- Palette: bg #F4F6F1 (map paper), text #1E2A22, accent #E07A1F (contour orange), surface #FFFFFF, line #3C7DC4 (water blue)
- Layout: tour pages lead with a large route map and an elevation strip, details in a two-column fact table below; tour archive as a list sorted by distance; requirements strip styled like a map legend
- Imagery: riders small in big landscapes, shot from the roadside at eye level, 16:9 for routes and 1:1 for bikes; no drone clichés
- Motion: the elevation strip draws its line on load (static under reduced motion); map zoom only on click
- Why it fits now: cycling brands have moved to editorial, route-first pages that read like a ride report (example: [Rapha](https://www.rapha.cc/gb/en))
**Style variations:** Vineyard: #6B1F3A accent on white · Glacier: #DCEAF2 ground, navy type · Night ride: #1E2A22 bg, orange lines
**Real-world basis:** [Sol Rides: tours and rentals](https://www.solrides.com/tours-and-rentals), [Sol Rides: FAQ](https://www.solrides.com/faq), [Amp'd Adventures: tours](https://ampdadventures.com/tours/), [MacBike: bike tours](https://www.macbike.nl/en/bike-tours/), [MacBike: safe cycling](https://www.macbike.nl/en/safe-cycling/)
**Refs:**
- [Sol Rides: tours and rentals](https://www.solrides.com/tours-and-rentals): distance, difficulty, season and rider limits on every route
- [MacBike: bike tours](https://www.macbike.nl/en/bike-tours/): daily start times, meeting points and languages listed per tour
- [Sol Rides: FAQ](https://www.solrides.com/faq): honest weather and cancellation rules in the owner's voice

#### 140 · Boat Charter / Skipper (`charter`)
**For:** owner-skippers and tiny charter outfits running day sails, evening trips and short skippered voyages.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-trip · single-trip · page-schedule · page-our-boats · single-boat · page-rya-courses · page-faq · page-booking-terms · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** trip type list (half day, full day, evening), per-boat price (private yacht, 7 hours), departure point with postcode and parking, sample routes that depend on wind and tide, voyage schedule cards (date, duration, vessel, departure port / return port, board), berth status labels (berths available / limited berths / private charter), £/€ price display, boat spec cards (length, berths, guests, year), RYA course list, what's included (coffee and pastries, paddleboards), booking terms, FAQ
**Content model:** `trip` (duration, price per boat or per berth, max guests, departure, inclusions); `sailing` (date, vessel, berths status, departure port, return port, price); `boat` (length, berths, max guests, year).
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (upcoming sailings only), Jetpack Forms.
**Signature:** a sailing schedule where each date shows vessel, ports and a berth status label (berths available / limited berths / private charter) (seen on: [VentureSail Holidays](https://venturesailholidays.com/destination/sailing-holidays-cornwall/schedule/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Prices shown in £ and € from one stored value (seen on: [VentureSail Holidays](https://venturesailholidays.com/destination/sailing-holidays-cornwall/schedule/))
- Sample routes with a plain note that the day is "guided by the weather on the day" (seen on: [Take a Turn Yachting](https://takeaturnyachting.co.uk/full-day-sailing-trips/))
- Boat pages with length, berths and photos below deck (seen on: [Take a Turn Yachting](https://takeaturnyachting.co.uk/about-our-boats/))
- Gift vouchers for a day sail, sold as a simple form plus bank payment or Woo if already installed
- What to bring list (soft bag, non-marking shoes, layers) printable from the trip page
**Style: Nautical chart and tide table**
- Type: headings Fjord One 400 at large sizes; body Hanken Grotesk 400/18px; times, tides and coordinates JetBrains Mono 500
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #0B1F3A (chart navy), accent #C8102E (port-hand red), surface #DCE9F2 (shallow-water blue), line #0B1F3A
- Layout: schedule as a tide-table style list with rules and columns; trip pages with a chart-like route figure and a fact column; boat pages as a spec sheet with a deck plan drawing
- Imagery: wide sea horizons at low sun, deck details, the skipper at the helm; 3:2 crops; no drone shots of turquoise water
- Motion: berth status label changes are instant; route figure uses View Transitions between trips; nothing on scroll
- Why it fits now: travel and lifestyle titles use calm serif-led editorial layouts that suit small premium trips (example: [Monocle](https://www.monocle.com/))
**Style variations:** Night passage: #0B1F3A bg, white type · Starboard: #00843D accent · Estuary: #E8E4D8 sand-grey ground
**Real-world basis:** [Take a Turn Yachting: sailing trips](https://takeaturnyachting.co.uk/sailing-trips/), [Take a Turn Yachting: full day](https://takeaturnyachting.co.uk/full-day-sailing-trips/), [Take a Turn Yachting: evening trips](https://takeaturnyachting.co.uk/evening-sailing-trips/), [VentureSail Holidays: Cornwall schedule](https://venturesailholidays.com/destination/sailing-holidays-cornwall/schedule/), [Freewinds: Cornish day sailing](http://www.freewinds.co.uk/cornish_day_sailing.html)
**Refs:**
- [VentureSail Holidays: Cornwall schedule](https://venturesailholidays.com/destination/sailing-holidays-cornwall/schedule/): berth status and ports on every sailing date
- [Take a Turn Yachting: full day sailing](https://takeaturnyachting.co.uk/full-day-sailing-trips/): one price per boat and real sample routes
- [Take a Turn Yachting: about our boats](https://takeaturnyachting.co.uk/about-our-boats/): boat pages that answer "how many of us fit"

### XIV. Education & childcare

<a id="141"></a>
#### 141 · Forest School (`woodland`)
**For:** forest school nurseries, outdoor kindergartens and holiday camps running on one or more woodland sites.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-site · single-site · page-fees · page-term-dates · page-kit-list · page-safeguarding · page-ofsted · page-waiting-list · page-holiday-camps · page-open-days · page-noticeboard
**Patterns (~45):** seasonal kit list (summer / spring and autumn / winter), term dates table (autumn, spring, summer, INSET days, bank holidays), fees with funded hours explained, site locations grid, holiday camp dates, open days list, safeguarding contacts per site, Ofsted registration per site, "why outdoors" evidence page, food page, team list, waiting list form, parent app page
**Content model:** `site` (address, days open, ages, Ofsted URN, evacuation policy PDF, safeguarding contact); `term` (name, start, end, INSET days).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms, Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap.
**Signature:** a seasonal kit list, split by summer, spring and autumn, and winter, naming the items and brands parents should buy and the "label everything" rule (seen on: [Little Forest Folk](https://www.littleforestfolk.com/kit-list)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Virtual noticeboard with per-site evacuation policy, safeguarding contacts, Ofsted certificate and insurance (seen on: [Little Forest Folk](https://www.littleforestfolk.com/virtual-noticeboard))
- Plain explanation of how funded hours are stretched across 51 weeks (seen on: [Outdoor Owls](https://www.outdoorowls.com/fees))
- Open days list with dates per site (seen on: [Outdoor Owls](https://www.outdoorowls.com/open-days))
- Supplier discount codes on the kit list (seen on: [Little Forest Folk](https://www.littleforestfolk.com/kit-list))
- "Site closed today" weather notice with start and end time, set by staff from the editor
**Style: Field-guide nature notebook**
- Type: headings Kreon 600; body Figtree 400/18px; labels and dates Recursive Mono (casual axis 1) 500
- Palette: bg #F1F3EC (lichen grey), text #1F2A1C, accent #4E6B2F (moss), surface #FFFFFF, line #6B4E2E (bark)
- Layout: kit list laid out like a field-guide plate, three season columns with small drawings of each item; term dates as a plain table; site pages lead with a map and the practical box (address, hours, ages, Ofsted URN)
- Imagery: children from behind or at a distance in real woods (no faces without consent), close-ups of hands, mud and tools; pencil drawings for kit items
- Motion: none on scroll; season columns reorder to put the current season first on load
- Why it fits now: parents respond to warm, slow editorial layouts over bright nursery clip-art (example: [Kinfolk](https://www.kinfolk.com/))
**Style variations:** Winter: #E8EDF0 frost ground, navy type · Bracken: #8A4B2A accent · Canopy: #1F2A1C bg, lichen text
**Real-world basis:** [Little Forest Folk: kit list](https://www.littleforestfolk.com/kit-list), [Little Forest Folk: term dates](https://www.littleforestfolk.com/term-dates), [Little Forest Folk: safeguarding](https://www.littleforestfolk.com/safeguarding), [Outdoor Owls: fees](https://www.outdoorowls.com/fees), [Outdoor Owls: clothing](https://www.outdoorowls.com/clothing)
**Refs:**
- [Little Forest Folk: kit list](https://www.littleforestfolk.com/kit-list): season-by-season clothing, specific enough to shop from
- [Little Forest Folk: term dates](https://www.littleforestfolk.com/term-dates): three terms, INSET days and what full-day families get in half term
- [Outdoor Owls: fees](https://www.outdoorowls.com/fees): funding and tax-free childcare explained without jargon

<a id="142"></a>
#### 142 · Small Independent School (`school`)
**For:** small independent, democratic, Steiner and alternative schools with 50–300 pupils.
**Templates:** front-page · page-ethos · page-approach-to-learning · page-admissions · page-fees · page-term-dates · page-timetable · page-inspection · page-policies · page-safeguarding · page-exam-results · page-parents
**Patterns (~50):** inspection report list (inspecting body, date, outcome, short quote, PDF), policies list with PDFs and review dates, fees list (termly fee, VAT note, bus and lunch extras, deposit, bursaries), term dates table, weekly timetable, safeguarding hub (DSL and deputies with photos and emails), exam results table by year, open days and visiting, "a typical day", school bus routes, newsletters archive, vacancies
**Content model:** `document` (type: policy / inspection / statutory; issued date; review date; PDF; inspecting body; outcome); `term` (start, end, half term).
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop, Jetpack Forms.
**Signature:** an inspection page that lists each report with the inspecting body, date, outcome, a short quote and the PDF, newest first (seen on: [Sands School](https://www.sands-school.co.uk/about-sands/inspection/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Fees page listing extras (bus, lunches, camp), the returnable deposit and how bursaries work (seen on: [Sands School](https://www.sands-school.co.uk/about-sands/fees/))
- Safeguarding hub naming the DSL and deputies with photos and direct emails (seen on: [Michael Hall](https://www.michaelhall.co.uk/parents/the-safeguarding-hub))
- School bus routes and pick-up points (seen on: [Michael Hall](https://www.michaelhall.co.uk/parents/school-buses))
- Password-protected parents' page for letters and forms, using core post passwords
- Policy "review due" date shown next to each PDF so governors see what is out of date
**Style: Swiss school notice board**
- Type: headings Golos Text 800 at 8vw, sentence case; body Literata 400/18px; labels Golos Text 600 small caps via font-feature-settings
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #101010, accent #E4002B (school red), surface #1F4D3A (chalkboard green), line #101010
- Layout: 12-column grid, strong left alignment, documents as numbered tables with file size and date; parent information gathered under one "Parents" section; home page leads with a real sentence about the school and the next open day
- Imagery: documentary photos of lessons, workshops and outdoor work, often mid-activity; 3:2 crops; pupils' own artwork used as section openers
- Motion: none; document rows get a red underline on hover and focus
- Why it fits now: public institutions have gone back to typographic, grid-led sites that put information first (example: [Serpentine](https://www.serpentinegalleries.org/))
**Style variations:** Chalk: #1F4D3A bg, white type · Ink: #101010 bg, red accents · Exercise book: #F2F7FB with blue rules
**Real-world basis:** [Sands School: inspection](https://www.sands-school.co.uk/about-sands/inspection/), [Sands School: term dates](https://www.sands-school.co.uk/information-for-parents/term-dates/), [Summerhill: statutory documents](https://www.summerhillschool.co.uk/statutory-documents/), [Brockwood Park: inspections](https://brockwood.org.uk/inspections), [Michael Hall: term dates](https://www.michaelhall.co.uk/parents/term-dates)
**Refs:**
- [Sands School: inspection](https://www.sands-school.co.uk/about-sands/inspection/): each report dated, quoted and linked
- [Summerhill: statutory documents and inspection reports](https://www.summerhillschool.co.uk/statutory-documents/): all the required documents in one place
- [Michael Hall: safeguarding hub](https://www.michaelhall.co.uk/parents/the-safeguarding-hub): names and faces for the people parents should contact

<a id="143"></a>
#### 143 · Nursery / Childminder (`nursery`)
**For:** single-site day nurseries, pre-schools and registered childminders.
**Templates:** front-page · page-our-nursery · single-room · page-typical-day · page-fees-and-funding · page-meals · page-ofsted · page-policies · page-safeguarding · page-parent-portal · page-careers · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** room cards (baby suite, toddler suite, preschool suite) with ages and ratios, typical day timetable (7am open, 8am breakfast, noon lunch, 4pm tea), "what's included" fee list (meals, nappies, wipes, formula), funded childcare explainer (15 and 30 hours, tax-free childcare), sibling discount and refer-a-friend credit, Ofsted block, meals and nutrition, policies list, safeguarding, parent app login link, food hygiene rating, vacancies
**Content model:** `room` (ages, ratio, capacity, photos); `document` (policy, date, PDF).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms.
**Signature:** an Ofsted block showing the grade, inspection date, a PDF of the report and a direct link to the provider's page on the Ofsted site by URN (seen on: [Orchard Day Nursery](https://www.orcharddaynursery.com/ofsted-inspection)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Parent portal page that links out to the nursery app login (Famly or similar) (seen on: [Orchard Day Nursery](https://www.orcharddaynursery.com/famly-portal))
- Fees page that lists exactly what is included and the sibling discount (seen on: [Teepee Day Nursery](https://teepeedaynursery.co.uk/fees/))
- Typical day timetable as a printable A4 for the fridge (seen on: [Teepee Day Nursery](https://teepeedaynursery.co.uk/our-nursery/our-typical-day/))
- Food hygiene rating linked from the footer (seen on: [Orchard Day Nursery](https://www.orcharddaynursery.com/))
- "Spaces available from January: toddler room" state per room, set in room meta
**Style: Soft neo-brutalism (hard shadows, pastel fills)**
- Type: headings Fredoka 700; body Andika 400/18px for early readers' parents; labels Andika 700
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #1B1B1B, accent #FFD8E4 (pink fill), surface #CDEBD9 (mint), line #1B1B1B
- Layout: 3px black borders and a 4px offset shadow on room cards and buttons only; inputs 8px radius, images square; typical day as a vertical timetable with times in the left column
- Imagery: real rooms and garden, shot at child eye height; children's paintings scanned and used as backgrounds for the fee and funding boxes
- Motion: buttons press down into their shadow on click; no scroll effects
- Why it fits now: flat pastel fills with hard outlines look friendly without clip-art and are easy to keep accessible (example: [Gumroad](https://gumroad.com/))
**Style variations:** Sunshine: #FFE58F fills · Sky: #CFE6FF fills, navy lines · Crayon: black ground, pastel type
**Real-world basis:** [Teepee Day Nursery: typical day](https://teepeedaynursery.co.uk/our-nursery/our-typical-day/), [Teepee Day Nursery: fees](https://teepeedaynursery.co.uk/fees/), [Teepee Day Nursery: funded childcare](https://teepeedaynursery.co.uk/helpful-info/funded-childcare/), [Orchard Day Nursery: Ofsted](https://www.orcharddaynursery.com/ofsted-inspection), [Orchard Day Nursery: fees and funding](https://www.orcharddaynursery.com/fees-and-funding)
**Refs:**
- [Orchard Day Nursery: Ofsted](https://www.orcharddaynursery.com/ofsted-inspection): grade, PDF and the official Ofsted link together
- [Teepee Day Nursery: our typical day](https://teepeedaynursery.co.uk/our-nursery/our-typical-day/): the day as a timetable parents can picture
- [Teepee Day Nursery: baby suite](https://teepeedaynursery.co.uk/our-nursery/environment/baby-suite/): one page per room

<a id="144"></a>
#### 144 · Private Tutor (`tutor`)
**For:** self-employed tutors teaching one to three subjects at GCSE, A-level and university level, in person and online.
**Templates:** front-page · page-subjects · single-subject · page-fees · page-success-stories · page-resources · page-safeguarding · page-online-tutoring · page-about · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** subjects and levels list, fees table (pay-as-you-go / termly membership × tutor's premises / online / your home), downloadable price schedule with term dates, success stories (predicted grade to achieved grade), parent and student quotes attributed by role ("dad", "Year 13 student"), exam resources list, safeguarding and DBS statement, online lesson setup (whiteboard, camera, headset), in-school tuition services, booking or enquiry form
**Content model:** `story` (student alias, subject, level, predicted grade, achieved grade, year, quote, attribution role); `subject` (levels, exam boards).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms; Cal.com embed for booking a first call (external).
**Signature:** success stories that show the predicted grade and the achieved grade side by side, with anonymised names (seen on: [Private Maths Tuition](https://privatemathstuition.co.uk/success-stories/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Downloadable pricing schedule with the term dates the membership follows (seen on: [Private Maths Tuition](https://privatemathstuition.co.uk/the-difference-mr-coach-makes/fees/))
- Safeguarding and DBS page (seen on: [Private Maths Tuition](https://privatemathstuition.co.uk/the-difference-mr-coach-makes/safeguarding/))
- Free exam resources page (seen on: [Private Maths Tuition](https://privatemathstuition.co.uk/essential-resources-gcse-a-level-maths-physics/))
- "Taking new Year 11 students from January: yes / no" toggle in the header
- The Tutors' Association membership badge with number (scheme: [The Tutors' Association](https://www.thetutorsassociation.org.uk/))
**Style: Exam paper and graph paper**
- Type: headings Noticia Text 700; body Source Sans 3 400/18px; grades and working Courier Prime 700
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #111111, accent #D62828 (marking red), surface #EAF3FA (graph paper), line #CFE3F2
- Layout: pages framed with the margin line of an exam paper; success stories as marked scripts, predicted grade struck through in red with the achieved grade written beside it; fees as a two-by-three table
- Imagery: hands, pencils and worked solutions on real paper; no smiling-teen stock; tutor portrait in natural light
- Motion: the red strike-through draws on hover and focus; static under reduced motion
- Why it fits now: plain, book-like typography signals expertise to parents better than ed-tech gloss (example: [Practical Typography](https://practicaltypography.com/))
**Style variations:** Blackboard: #1E2B24 bg, chalk white text · Squared: full graph-paper ground · Answer key: #0B57D0 blue pen accent
**Real-world basis:** [Private Maths Tuition: fees](https://privatemathstuition.co.uk/the-difference-mr-coach-makes/fees/), [Private Maths Tuition: success stories](https://privatemathstuition.co.uk/success-stories/), [Private Maths Tuition: online tutoring](https://privatemathstuition.co.uk/tutoring-services/online-tutoring/), [Bristol Maths Tutor: GCSE maths](https://bristolmathstutor.co.uk/gcse-maths/), [Bristol Maths Tutor: book tuition](https://bristolmathstutor.co.uk/book-tuition/)
**Refs:**
- [Private Maths Tuition: success stories](https://privatemathstuition.co.uk/success-stories/): grade movement as proof, with names changed
- [Private Maths Tuition: fees](https://privatemathstuition.co.uk/the-difference-mr-coach-makes/fees/): two payment models and three locations, laid out honestly
- [Bristol Maths Tutor: GCSE maths](https://bristolmathstutor.co.uk/gcse-maths/): a one-tutor site that stays small and direct

#### 145 · Language School (`lingo`)
**For:** small independent language schools running evening group classes, private lessons and short intensives.
**Templates:** front-page · page-schedule · archive-course · single-course · page-placement-test · page-prices-and-policies · page-private-lessons · page-accommodation · page-exam-preparation · page-faq · page-contact
**Patterns (~45):** term schedule table (level, days, time with timezone, dates, in-person / online, teacher, seats), level ladder (Beginner I–V, Intermediate I–V, mapped to CEFR A1–C2), placement test, prices and policies (registration fee, refunds, missed classes), private lessons, evening courses, intensive courses, price calculator (course × weeks + accommodation), accommodation options, exam preparation (DELE, CCSE), student of the month, newsletter archive
**Content model:** `class` (level, CEFR, days, time, start date, end date, format, teacher, seat status); taxonomy `level`.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce (registration and payment), Advanced Query Loop.
**Signature:** a term schedule with a seat status column (YES / NEAR FULL / FULL / CLOSED) and a line stating which timezone the times are in (seen on: [Tierra Educational Center](https://tierracenter.com/spanish-class-schedule-upcoming)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Free online placement test that emails the result (seen on: [Inhispania](https://inhispania.com/level-test-spanish/))
- Price calculator for course, weeks and accommodation, with the one-off registration fee shown (seen on: [Inhispania](https://inhispania.com/price-calculator/))
- Newsletter archive page (seen on: [Tierra Educational Center](https://tierracenter.com/content/newsletter-archive))
- Student visa course page for long stays (seen on: [Inhispania](https://inhispania.com/courses/long-term-courses-student-visa/))
- Class times shown in the visitor's local time for online classes, with the school's time kept as the source
**Style: Kinetic variable-type poster**
- Type: headings Anek Latin variable (width 75–125), level names set wide and course titles set condensed; body Commissioner 400/18px; schedule figures Commissioner 600 tabular numerals
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #0E0E0E, accent #FF4F00, surface #F2F2F2, line #1438A6 (cobalt)
- Layout: the schedule is the home page's main object, a full-width table grouped by level; level ladder as a horizontal scale; course pages keep the practical box (dates, time, price, seats) top right
- Imagery: small classroom photos and street photography from the language's cities, black and white with one colour; no flags
- Motion: headline width axis eases from condensed to wide once on load (off under reduced motion); seat status updates without animation
- Why it fits now: arts venues use big, flexible poster type to turn listings into the design (example: [Barbican](https://www.barbican.org.uk/))
**Style variations:** Cobalt: #1438A6 ground, white type · Terraza: #F6D7B0 sand, black type · Metro: #0E0E0E bg, orange figures
**Real-world basis:** [Tierra Educational Center: schedule](https://tierracenter.com/spanish-class-schedule-upcoming), [Tierra Educational Center: placement tests](https://tierracenter.com/spanish_placement_tests), [Tierra Educational Center: prices and policies](https://tierracenter.com/prices-policies), [Inhispania: evening courses](https://inhispania.com/courses/evening-spanish-courses/), [ILI: Spanish classes](https://ilidc.com/flp/spanishclass/)
**Refs:**
- [Tierra Educational Center: class schedule](https://tierracenter.com/spanish-class-schedule-upcoming): levels, times, format, teacher and seats in one table
- [Inhispania: placement test](https://inhispania.com/level-test-spanish/): a level test that stops whenever the learner wants
- [Inhispania: price calculator](https://inhispania.com/price-calculator/): course plus housing priced before enquiry

<a id="146"></a>
#### 146 · Kids Coding Club (`code-club`)
**For:** volunteer-run coding clubs and dojos for 7–17 year olds meeting in libraries, schools and science centres.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-session · single-session · page-projects · page-mentors · page-parents · page-safeguarding · page-code-of-conduct · page-venue · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** next session card (date, venue, age range 12–17, booking link), term session list, what to bring (laptop, charger), project path cards (Scratch, Python, HTML and CSS), mentor call-out with DBS requirement, safeguarding page (lead contact, reporting steps, adult-to-child ratio), code of conduct, venue and partners, club news, parent information (drop-off and pick-up rules)
**Content model:** `session` (date, time, venue, age range, capacity, booking URL); project paths as Sensei LMS courses and lessons.
**Plugins:** Sensei LMS, Advanced Query Loop, Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap.
**Signature:** project paths, each a short run of six projects a child works through and ticks off, built as Sensei courses (seen on: [Code Club](https://codeclub.org/en/learn-to-code)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Session pages that link to Eventbrite and say the age range and venue up front (seen on: [CoderDojo Scotland](https://coderdojoscotland.com/clubs/glasgow))
- Safeguarding page with reporting steps and a named contact (seen on: [Hack Club](https://hackclub.com/safeguarding/))
- Code of conduct page linked from every session (seen on: [Hack Club](https://hackclub.com/conduct/))
- "Loan laptops available: 4" line on each session, so families without one still come
- Printable parent consent and photo permission form
**Style: Web 1.0 revival**
- Type: headings Press Start 2P 400 (set smaller, it runs wide); body Atkinson Hyperlegible 400/18px; code and project numbers JetBrains Mono 500
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #111111, accent #FFE500 (highlighter), surface #F0F0F0, line #0047FF (hyperlink blue)
- Layout: visible underlined links, bevel-free boxes with 2px black borders, a sticky "next session" box; project paths as a numbered checklist, not cards
- Imagery: kids' own Scratch sprites and screenshots of their projects (with permission), photos of hands on keyboards; pixel icons drawn for the theme, not Lucide
- Motion: completed projects get a checkbox tick; cursor-follow sprite only on the 404 page, off under reduced motion
- Why it fits now: teen maker communities have made early-web looks their own again, and kids read it as "made by people like us" (example: [Hack Club](https://hackclub.com/))
**Style variations:** Terminal: #111 bg, #00FF66 text · Scratch: #FFAB19 accent · Library: #F7F2E8 ground, blue links
**Real-world basis:** [Code Club: learn to code](https://codeclub.org/en/learn-to-code), [Code Club: run a club](https://codeclub.org/en/run-a-club), [CoderDojo Scotland: clubs](https://coderdojoscotland.com/clubs), [CoderDojo Scotland: Glasgow](https://coderdojoscotland.com/clubs/glasgow), [Hack Club: clubs](https://hackclub.com/clubs/)
**Refs:**
- [CoderDojo Scotland: Glasgow club](https://coderdojoscotland.com/clubs/glasgow): venue, frequency, age range and booking on one page
- [Code Club: learn to code](https://codeclub.org/en/learn-to-code): project paths organised by tool
- [Hack Club: safeguarding](https://hackclub.com/safeguarding/): clear reporting steps for volunteers

<a id="147"></a>
#### 147 · Online Course Creator (`course`)
**For:** individual teachers selling one or two in-depth online courses in a craft or technical subject.
**Templates:** front-page · page-curriculum · single-course · single-lesson · page-sample-lesson · page-pricing · page-teams · page-faq · page-login · page-code-of-conduct
**Patterns (~45):** full syllabus listing every unit and lesson with durations, free sample lesson, instructor bio with past work, what's included (lifetime access, free updates, community), pricing as a plain comparison table of editions, team licences with seat discounts, regional pricing note, student discount, 30-day refund promise, letter to your manager, certificate of completion, community code of conduct, FAQ
**Content model:** Sensei LMS courses, modules and lessons (duration meta per lesson); `edition` (name, price, what's included) for the pricing table.
**Plugins:** Sensei LMS for delivery and progress; Jetpack Paid Content to gate paid lessons (Sensei's own selling needs the paid Pro add-on).
**Signature:** a curriculum page that lists every unit and lesson with lesson counts and running times, so buyers see the whole course before paying (seen on: [Learn UI Design](https://www.learnui.design/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- "Letter to your manager" page to get the course expensed (seen on: [Josh W Comeau](https://courses.joshwcomeau.com/letter-to-your-manager))
- Regional pricing and a student discount stated on the pricing page (seen on: [CSS for JavaScript Developers](https://css-for-js.dev/))
- Team seat discounts by number of seats (seen on: [Learn UI Design](https://www.learnui.design/))
- Free sample lesson open without login (seen on: [Learn UI Design](https://www.learnui.design/))
- Certificate of completion PDF generated from Sensei on course completion
**Style: Book-like syllabus, serif revival**
- Type: headings Cardo 400 at very large sizes; body Libre Caslon Text 400/19px; UI and lesson times Hanken Grotesk 500
- Palette: bg #FBFBF8, text #1C1C1C, accent #1F4E9C (ink blue), surface #FFFFFF, line #D9D6CE
- Layout: the curriculum page is a table of contents with dotted leaders to running times; lesson pages use a narrow 64ch column with a progress rail; editions compared in one table with ticks, no highlighted middle column
- Imagery: real screenshots of lessons and exercises at 1:1 scale, framed with a thin rule, never inside a fake browser
- Motion: progress rail fills as lessons complete; View Transitions between lessons; nothing on scroll
- Why it fits now: independent publishers use book typography online to signal depth and permanence (example: [Stripe Press](https://press.stripe.com/))
**Style variations:** Night class: #1C1C1C bg, paper text · Margin notes: #FFF6D6 note fills · Blueprint: #1F4E9C ground, white type
**Real-world basis:** [CSS for JavaScript Developers](https://css-for-js.dev/), [Josh W Comeau: courses](https://www.joshwcomeau.com/courses/), [Learn UI Design](https://www.learnui.design/), [Epic React](https://www.epicreact.dev/), [Testing JavaScript](https://testingjavascript.com/)
**Refs:**
- [Learn UI Design](https://www.learnui.design/): the full syllabus with running times and a free lesson
- [CSS for JavaScript Developers](https://css-for-js.dev/): refunds, regional pricing, team licences and the student discount, all stated
- [Josh W Comeau: letter to your manager](https://courses.joshwcomeau.com/letter-to-your-manager): a ready-made expense request

<a id="148"></a>
#### 148 · Homeschool Co-op (`homeschool`)
**For:** parent-run homeschool co-ops and learning groups meeting one or two days a week.
**Templates:** front-page · page-classes · page-monday · page-tuesday · page-calendar · page-teachers · page-faqs · page-application · page-members · page-other-co-ops · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** class grid by hour block (Hour A, B, C) and grade band (PK–2, 3–5, 6–8, 9–12 and adult), one page per co-op day, course catalogue PDF, semester calendar (16 weeks, holiday breaks), teacher list, parent service credits explained (9 per semester), drop-off rules by age, fees (supply fees plus monthly tuition set by each teacher), application with background check, code of conduct download, other local co-ops list
**Content model:** `class` (day, hour block, grade band, teacher, supply fee, monthly tuition, capacity, room); `teacher`.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms, Advanced Query Loop.
**Signature:** a class grid by hour block and grade band that the public can browse, with teacher names and fees shown only to members (seen on: [homeschool-life.com public schedule](https://www.homeschool-life.com/671/custom/73821)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Members-only page for fees, rosters and forms using core password protection (seen as "details are available only to members" on: [homeschool-life.com](https://www.homeschool-life.com/671/custom/73821))
- Service credits explained with examples of jobs that earn them (seen on: [FACET](https://facethomeschool.org/faqs/))
- Course catalogue PDF per day (seen on: [FACET](https://facethomeschool.org/tuesday/))
- Other local co-ops page for families who don't fit this one (seen on: [TLC](https://www.mytlcnj.com/co-ops))
- Class "full" flag with a waitlist form
**Style: Warm Scandi minimal**
- Type: headings Nunito 700; body Lora 400/18px; hour blocks and grade bands Nunito 600 tabular numerals
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #222222, accent #2E6B5E (pine), surface #F3EFE8 (birch), line #CFC8BC
- Layout: generous white space, a strict 6-column grid, the class grid as a real table with sticky header row on mobile; one page per day keeps printing simple
- Imagery: children's work on tables, parents teaching in borrowed halls; soft daylight, 4:3 crops
- Motion: none; table rows highlight on hover and focus
- Why it fits now: calm, uncluttered Scandinavian layouts suit parent volunteers who update the site between classes (example: [HAY](https://www.hay.dk/))
**Style variations:** Linen: #EFE9DF ground · Fjord: #2B4C7E accent · Lamp: #222 bg, birch type
**Real-world basis:** [FACET: classes](https://facethomeschool.org/classes/), [FACET: FAQs](https://facethomeschool.org/faqs/), [FACET: calendar](https://facethomeschool.org/calendar/), [homeschool-life.com: public class schedule](https://www.homeschool-life.com/671/custom/73821), [TLC: other local co-ops](https://www.mytlcnj.com/co-ops)
**Refs:**
- [homeschool-life.com: public class schedule](https://www.homeschool-life.com/671/custom/73821): hour blocks against grade bands
- [FACET: FAQs](https://facethomeschool.org/faqs/): the parent commitment spelled out in numbers
- [FACET: teachers](https://facethomeschool.org/teachers/): who teaches what

#### 149 · Adult Evening Classes (`evening`)
**For:** small adult education centres, craft studios and community colleges running evening and weekend courses.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-course · single-course · taxonomy-subject · page-evening · page-fees-and-concessions · page-venues · page-tutors · page-refunds · page-gift-cards · page-accessibility
**Patterns (~45):** course page (course code, day, time, start and end dates, number of sessions, fee tiers, what you'll learn, what to bring, next course), course list with filters (day, daytime / evening, online / in-person, level), "last few places" flag, subject index, tutor profiles, venues with access information, refund and credit policy, bursary fund, gift cards, accessibility statement
**Content model:** `course` (code, day, start time, end time, start date, sessions, venue, full fee, senior fee, concession fee, materials, book, next course); taxonomies `subject`, `level`.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce (booking and gift cards), Query Filter (day, time of day, format, level), Advanced Query Loop.
**Signature:** a course page with the course code, number of sessions, three fee tiers (full, senior, concession) and a link to the next course in the sequence (seen on: [City Lit](https://www.citylit.ac.uk/courses/italian-beginners-module-3)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- "Last few places" flag on listings when stock is low (seen on: [City Lit](https://www.citylit.ac.uk/courses))
- Bursary fund page with who can apply (seen on: [Oxford Lifelong Learning](https://lifelong-learning.ox.ac.uk/about/bursary-fund/))
- Tutor profiles (seen on: [WEA](https://www.wea.org.uk/about-us/our-tutors))
- Accessibility statement and venue access notes (seen on: [Morley College](https://morleycollege.ac.uk/about/our-policies/website-accessibility-statement/))
- "What to bring" and required book listed on each course, printable as a joining sheet
**Style: Newsprint listings**
- Type: headings Plein 700 (Fontshare, newspaper grotesk); body Newsreader 400/18px; codes, dates and fees IBM Plex Mono 500 tabular numerals
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #111111, accent #FFE600 (listings yellow), surface #F4F4F4, line #111111
- Layout: dense, column-based listings like a weekly guide, grouped by evening (Monday to Thursday); course pages with a fact column on the left and prose on the right; filters as plain checkboxes above the list
- Imagery: real classes in progress, hands at wheels, easels and keyboards; black and white with the yellow used for callouts only
- Motion: filter results update in place with View Transitions; nothing else moves
- Why it fits now: news and listings sites have made dense, text-first layouts feel current again (example: [The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/))
**Style variations:** Late: #111 bg, yellow type · Pottery: #B5651D clay accent on white · Library: #EDF1F4 ground, navy type
**Real-world basis:** [City Lit: courses](https://www.citylit.ac.uk/courses), [City Lit: Italian Beginners Module 3](https://www.citylit.ac.uk/courses/italian-beginners-module-3), [Morley College: ceramics](https://morleycollege.ac.uk/subject-areas/ceramics), [WEA: arts courses](https://www.wea.org.uk/courses/arts-crafts/arts/), [Oxford Lifelong Learning: bursary fund](https://lifelong-learning.ox.ac.uk/about/bursary-fund/)
**Refs:**
- [City Lit: Italian Beginners Module 3](https://www.citylit.ac.uk/courses/italian-beginners-module-3): codes, sessions, three fee tiers and the next course
- [City Lit: courses](https://www.citylit.ac.uk/courses): filters by day, evening, format and level
- [Morley College: ceramics](https://morleycollege.ac.uk/subject-areas/ceramics): a subject page that gathers every course in one place

#### 150 · University Student Society (`society`)
**For:** student-run clubs and societies (hillwalking, theatre, computing, debating) that want their own site beyond the union page.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-event · single-event · page-join · page-committee · page-constitution · page-minutes · page-kit-lists · page-sponsors · page-training-fund · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** trip and event list (dates, destination, type, "sign-ups open in X days"), membership prices (student / non-student, 12 months, what it includes), how to join in steps, committee list by role and year, constitution, AGM and EGM minutes list, kit lists, training fund, sponsor benefits, show listings, newsletter sign-up
**Content model:** `event` (start, end, type, destination, sign-up opens, sign-up URL); `officer` (role, name, year); `minutes` (date, meeting type, PDF).
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop, Jetpack Forms.
**Signature:** a trip list where each trip shows "Sign-ups open in X days" or "Sign-ups closed", worked out from a stored sign-up date (seen on: [CUHWC](https://www.cuhwc.org.uk/trips/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Minutes archive grouped by AGM, EGM and ordinary meetings, going back years (seen on: [SRCF](https://www.srcf.net/minutes))
- Kit lists for trips (seen on: [CUHWC](https://www.cuhwc.org.uk/trips/safety-equipment/kit-lists/))
- Sponsor benefits page (seen on: [SRCF](https://www.srcf.net/sponsors/benefits))
- Training fund page for members (seen on: [CUHWC](https://www.cuhwc.org.uk/about/andy-gibson-training-fund/))
- Committee handover checklist page, password protected, so next year's officers inherit the logins and suppliers
**Style: Photocopied DIY flyer**
- Type: headings Terminal Grotesque (Velvetyne) at 10vw; body Public Sans 400/18px; dates and prices Martian Mono 500
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #0A0A0A, accent #FF3EA5 (highlighter pink), surface #EFEFEF, line #0A0A0A
- Layout: poster-like home page with the next three events stacked big; committee as a plain list with roles; minutes as a table; everything left-aligned, rules drawn slightly thick
- Imagery: members' own trip and rehearsal photos, pushed to high-contrast black and white with a halftone filter applied in CSS
- Motion: none on scroll; countdown text updates daily on page load, not live
- Why it fits now: small groups use hand-made, self-published web pages to feel like a club, not a brand (example: [mmm.page](https://mmm.page/))
**Style variations:** Toner: #0A0A0A bg, pink type · Union: #003C71 navy accent · Summit: #E2F0D9 green ground
**Real-world basis:** [CUHWC: trips](https://www.cuhwc.org.uk/trips/), [CUHWC: join us](https://www.cuhwc.org.uk/join-us/), [SRCF: committee](https://www.srcf.net/committee), [SRCF: minutes](https://www.srcf.net/minutes), [Durham Student Theatre: what's on](https://www.durhamstudenttheatre.org/whats-on)
**Refs:**
- [CUHWC: trips](https://www.cuhwc.org.uk/trips/): sign-up status on each trip
- [SRCF: minutes](https://www.srcf.net/minutes): decades of minutes kept in the open
- [Durham Student Theatre: membership](https://www.durhamstudenttheatre.org/membership): membership explained for an umbrella of societies

### XV. Tech & indie software

<a id="151"></a>
#### 151 · Indie SaaS Product (`saas`)
**For:** one- to five-person software companies selling a single web product by subscription.
**Templates:** front-page · page-features · page-pricing · page-compare · single-comparison · page-when-not-to-use · archive-release · page-about · page-migration · page-responsibility
**Patterns (~40):** one-paragraph product explanation in the founder's voice, live demo link, pricing by volume (subscriber or pageview slider with a table fallback), add-ons list with prices, nonprofit discount note, comparison page against a named competitor, "when not to use us" list naming alternatives, changelog entries (date, title, body, docs link), status page link, about page with named people, free migration offer, climate commitment, customer quotes page with full names and links
**Content model:** `release` (date, title, type, docs link); `comparison` (competitor, rows of feature / us / them).
**Plugins:** none.
**Signature:** a "when not to use us" page that lists the jobs the product does not do and names the tools that do them (seen on: [Plausible](https://plausible.io/when-not-to-use-plausible)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Free migration from a named competitor, done by a person (seen on: [Buttondown](https://buttondown.com/features/concierge-migration))
- Nonprofit discount stated with what proof is needed (seen on: [Buttondown](https://buttondown.com/pricing))
- Status page link in the footer (seen on: [Buttondown](https://status.buttondown.com))
- Public live demo using the company's own account (seen on: [Plausible](https://plausible.io/plausible.io))
- Climate or responsibility commitment page (seen on: [Buttondown](https://buttondown.com/climate))
**Style: README-first plain page**
- Type: headings Anonymous Pro 700; body PT Serif 400/18px; code, prices and numbers IBM Plex Mono 500
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #161616, accent #0B6E4F (deep green), surface #F4F4F4, line #161616
- Layout: single 70ch column for the front page, starting with what the product does in two sentences and a real screenshot at 1:1; pricing as a table with a volume slider above it; comparison pages as two-column tables; no feature card grid
- Imagery: honest product screenshots and short screen recordings, no illustrations; founder photos on About
- Motion: slider updates the price instantly; changelog items expand in place; nothing on scroll
- Why it fits now: indie software with a clear point of view is winning trust by talking plainly (example: [Buttondown](https://buttondown.com/))
**Style variations:** Terminal: #161616 bg, #E8E8E8 text · Graph: #F0F7F4 ground · Receipt: #FFFFFF with dotted rules
**Real-world basis:** [Plausible: when not to use Plausible](https://plausible.io/when-not-to-use-plausible), [Plausible: vs Matomo](https://plausible.io/vs-matomo), [Buttondown: pricing](https://buttondown.com/pricing), [Fathom: changelog](https://usefathom.com/changelog), [Fathom: vs Jetpack Stats](https://usefathom.com/features/vs-jetpack-stats)
**Refs:**
- [Plausible: when not to use Plausible](https://plausible.io/when-not-to-use-plausible): turning limits into trust
- [Buttondown: pricing](https://buttondown.com/pricing): volume pricing, à la carte add-ons and the nonprofit rule
- [Fathom: vs Jetpack Stats](https://usefathom.com/features/vs-jetpack-stats): a comparison page aimed at WordPress users

<a id="152"></a>
#### 152 · Mobile App Landing Site (`app`)
**For:** indie developers and two-person studios with one paid or freemium iOS, Android or Mac app.
**Templates:** front-page · page-features · page-pricing · page-download · archive-release · page-trust · page-press · page-support · page-privacy · page-about
**Patterns (~35):** platform download buttons (Mac, iPhone, iPad, Watch), feature pages per platform, pricing note (price set in USD, store converts it), release notes (version, date, New / Improved / Fixed), trust page (what data stays on device, what the app can access, audits), press kit download (icon, screenshots, one-paragraph description), press quotes with links, support guide, privacy summary, status of sync services, jobs
**Content model:** `release` (version, date, minimum OS, new, improved, fixed); `platform` (store URL, minimum OS).
**Plugins:** none.
**Signature:** a trust page that says in plain words where the user's data lives, which permissions the app asks for and which audits it has passed (seen on: [Mimestream](https://mimestream.com/trust)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Press kit ZIP with a date on it (seen on: [Things](https://culturedcode.com/press/))
- Release notes grouped by New, Improved and Fixed with the minimum OS noted (seen on: [Mimestream](https://mimestream.com/releases))
- Pricing page that explains store currency conversion instead of guessing local prices (seen on: [Things](https://culturedcode.com/things/pricing/))
- Status page for sync and account services (seen on: [Things](https://culturedcode.com/status/))
- Smart App Banner meta and App Store badge per platform, kept in one pattern
**Style: Tactile skeuo 2.0**
- Type: headings Baloo 2 800; body Red Hat Text 400/18px; version numbers Red Hat Mono 500
- Palette: bg #ECEAE6 (brushed aluminium), text #1A1A1A, accent #F2542D (placeholder for the app icon colour), surface #FFFFFF, line #BDB9B2
- Layout: the app icon large and alone at the top, then real device screenshots at native size in a row that scrolls sideways on mobile; buttons with a 1px inner highlight and a crisp 1px shadow like hardware keys (buttons only)
- Imagery: the app icon as the hero; product screenshots without device frames or with the one frame Apple provides; no hands holding phones
- Motion: buttons depress on click; screenshot row snaps with CSS scroll-snap; no scroll-triggered effects
- Why it fits now: camera and utility apps have brought back physical, material detail as a sign of craft (example: [Halide](https://www.halide.cam/))
**Style variations:** Graphite: #2B2B2B bg, silver type · Paper: #FFFFFF, black keys · Signal: app accent as full ground
**Real-world basis:** [Mimestream: trust center](https://mimestream.com/trust), [Mimestream: releases](https://mimestream.com/releases), [Things: pricing](https://culturedcode.com/things/pricing/), [Things: press](https://culturedcode.com/press/), [Halide: changelog](https://www.lux.camera/halide-changelog/)
**Refs:**
- [Mimestream: trust center](https://mimestream.com/trust): the data answer people want before installing
- [Mimestream: release notes](https://mimestream.com/releases): versions, dates and grouped changes
- [Things: status](https://culturedcode.com/status/): release and service status on the product's own domain

<a id="153"></a>
#### 153 · WordPress Plugin Business (`plugin`)
**For:** solo developers and small teams selling a premium WordPress plugin next to a free one on wordpress.org.
**Templates:** front-page · page-features · page-pricing · archive-release · page-docs · single-doc · page-known-conflicts · page-feature-requests · page-try · page-brand-assets · page-account
**Patterns (~45):** licence table by number of sites (1 / 3 / unlimited) with renewal discount, free vs premium comparison, try-in-a-sandbox block, release notes (version, date, added / fixed), known conflicts list (does not work / limited / has issues, with workarounds), feature requests list by status with vote counts, knowledge base, example set-ups (real estate list, WooCommerce products), refund policy, affiliate programme, brand assets
**Content model:** `release` (version, date, type, notes); `doc` (hierarchical, product area); `conflict` (plugin name, severity, symptom, workaround); `request` (status, votes, date, reason).
**Plugins:** Code Block Pro. Sales through the business's existing licence store (external), linked from the pricing table.
**Signature:** a known conflicts page grouping other plugins by severity (doesn't work / limited / has issues) with the workaround for each (seen on: [Relevanssi](https://www.relevanssi.com/known-conflicts/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Free sandbox site for 7 days, no card needed (seen on: [WPCodeBox](https://wpcodebox.com/try))
- Feature requests grouped by status, including "not planning to implement" with reasons (seen on: [Perfmatters](https://perfmatters.io/docs/feature-requests/))
- Renewal discount and 30-day refund stated under the licence table (seen on: [Perfmatters](https://perfmatters.io/pricing/))
- Brand assets page for reviewers (seen on: [Admin Columns](https://www.admincolumns.com/brand-assets-presskit/))
- Example set-ups for specific trades (seen on: [Admin Columns](https://www.admincolumns.com/example-of-a-real-estate-website))
**Style: Dither / 1-bit bitmap**
- Type: headings Workbench (OFL, scanline bitmap) at large sizes; body Public Sans 400/18px; code JetBrains Mono 400
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #000000, accent #3858E9 (WordPress blue, used for links only), surface #F2F2F2, line #000000
- Layout: two-column docs with a plain tree nav; pricing as a four-row table; conflicts as a severity-grouped list with monospace plugin slugs; front page is one screenshot of the wp-admin screen the plugin changes, dithered, with a paragraph beside it
- Imagery: wp-admin screenshots converted to 1-bit dither for marketing pages, full-colour and crisp in docs
- Motion: none; copy buttons on code blocks confirm with a text change
- Why it fits now: 1-bit graphics signal "made by a developer" and keep pages light (example: [Playdate](https://play.date/))
**Style variations:** Admin grey: #F0F0F1 ground · Inverse: #000 bg, white bitmap · Changelog green: #008A20 accents
**Real-world basis:** [Relevanssi: known conflicts](https://www.relevanssi.com/known-conflicts/), [Relevanssi: release notes](https://www.relevanssi.com/release-notes/), [WPCodeBox: pricing](https://wpcodebox.com/pricing), [Perfmatters: changelog](https://perfmatters.io/docs/changelog/), [Admin Columns: pricing](https://www.admincolumns.com/pricing-purchase/)
**Refs:**
- [Relevanssi: known conflicts](https://www.relevanssi.com/known-conflicts/): saving support time by publishing what breaks
- [WPCodeBox: try](https://wpcodebox.com/try): a sandbox instead of a demo video
- [Perfmatters: feature requests](https://perfmatters.io/docs/feature-requests/): saying no in public, with reasons

<a id="154"></a>
#### 154 · Browser Extension (`extension`)
**For:** independent developers of a free or donation-funded browser extension across Chrome, Firefox, Edge and Safari.
**Templates:** front-page · page-install · page-help · page-privacy · page-permissions · page-changelog · page-support-us · page-stats · page-faq
**Patterns (~30):** install matrix (browser, store link, manifest version, stable / beta), one-paragraph explanation with a before/after screenshot, help page, privacy policy in plain words, permissions explained one by one, changelog, donate / support us, public usage stats, comparison of full and lite versions, FAQ, translations list
**Content model:** `browser` (name, store URL, channel, manifest version, notes); `release` (version, date, notes).
**Plugins:** none.
**Signature:** an install page listing every browser with its store link, stable and beta channels and any caveats (seen on: [Violentmonkey](https://violentmonkey.github.io/get-it/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Privacy policy that says what is not collected and when it was last updated (seen on: [Dark Reader](https://darkreader.org/privacy/))
- Page explaining full vs lite versions and which browsers get which (seen on: [uBlock Origin](https://ublockorigin.com/lite/))
- Public stats page (seen on: [SponsorBlock](https://sponsor.ajay.app/stats/))
- Support us page with several payment routes (seen on: [Dark Reader](https://darkreader.org/support-us/))
- Browser detection that puts the visitor's own browser first in the install list
**Style: Browser-chrome literalism**
- Type: headings Fira Sans 900; body Fira Sans 400/18px; permissions and version strings Fira Mono 500
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #121212, accent #00875A, surface #E8E8E8 (toolbar grey), line #C4C4C4
- Layout: the front page frames a before/after pair of the same website with and without the extension; install matrix as a table; permissions as a definition list
- Imagery: real before/after screenshots of well-known sites, cropped tight; extension icon at 128px
- Motion: before/after uses a draggable divider (keyboard accessible); otherwise static
- Why it fits now: tool sites that look like plain web pages, not ads, get installed by cautious users (example: [Are.na](https://www.are.na/))
**Style variations:** Dark toolbar: #202124 bg, light text · Firefox: #FF7139 accent · Safari: #0A84FF accent
**Real-world basis:** [Violentmonkey: get it](https://violentmonkey.github.io/get-it/), [Dark Reader: help](https://darkreader.org/help/), [uBlock Origin: Firefox](https://ublockorigin.com/firefox/), [SponsorBlock: stats](https://sponsor.ajay.app/stats/), [Tampermonkey: changes](https://www.tampermonkey.net/changelog.php)
**Refs:**
- [Violentmonkey: get it](https://violentmonkey.github.io/get-it/): every browser and channel in one list
- [uBlock Origin: Lite](https://ublockorigin.com/lite/): an honest comparison of two versions
- [Dark Reader: privacy](https://darkreader.org/privacy/): short, dated and specific
