<a id="155"></a>
#### 155 · Developer Tool / API Docs (`api`)
**For:** small teams and solo maintainers documenting an API, SDK or library.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-doc · single-doc · page-reference · single-endpoint · page-examples · page-essays · archive-release · page-going-to-production · page-community
**Patterns (~40):** reference page of tables (attributes, events, headers, config) linking to detail pages, endpoint page (method and path, SDK examples, path / query / body parameter tables, responses per status code with example JSON), examples gallery, essays, getting started, "going to production" checklist, release notes, credits and sponsors, community links
**Content model:** hierarchical `doc`; `endpoint` (method, path, auth, parameters as structured meta, response examples); `release`.
**Plugins:** Code Block Pro.
**Signature:** endpoint pages that show method and path, parameter tables and an example response for each status code (seen on: [PocketBase](https://pocketbase.io/docs/api-records)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- One-page reference of every attribute, event and header with one-line descriptions (seen on: [htmx](https://htmx.org/reference/))
- "Going to production" checklist page (seen on: [PocketBase](https://pocketbase.io/docs/going-to-production))
- Credits page for contributors and sponsors (seen on: [Eleventy](https://www.11ty.dev/docs/credits/))
- Status page link and a link to the changelog in the docs header (seen on: [Buttondown docs](https://docs.buttondown.com/api-introduction))
- Copy button on every code block and a "last updated" date on every doc page
**Style: Man-page plain docs**
- Type: headings JetBrains Mono 800; body Source Serif 4 400/18px at 70ch; code JetBrains Mono 400
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #1B1B1B, accent #0645AD (classic link blue), surface #F4F4F4, line #1B1B1B
- Layout: left tree nav, content, right "on this page" list; parameter tables with monospace names; method labels as plain uppercase text in a bordered box (GET, POST), no coloured pills
- Imagery: none except diagrams drawn as ASCII or simple SVG line art
- Motion: none; anchor links scroll instantly
- Why it fits now: developers trust documentation that looks like documentation and loads instantly (example: [htmx](https://htmx.org/))
**Style variations:** Dark terminal: #111 bg, #E6E6E6 text · Paper: #FBFAF6 ground · Blueprint: #0B3D91 headings
**Real-world basis:** [htmx: reference](https://htmx.org/reference/), [htmx: hx-swap](https://htmx.org/attributes/hx-swap/), [PocketBase: API records](https://pocketbase.io/docs/api-records), [Buttondown docs: API introduction](https://docs.buttondown.com/api-introduction), [Eleventy: data cascade](https://www.11ty.dev/docs/data-cascade/)
**Refs:**
- [PocketBase: API records](https://pocketbase.io/docs/api-records): parameter tables and per-status responses
- [htmx: reference](https://htmx.org/reference/): the whole surface area in one page of tables
- [htmx: essays](https://htmx.org/essays/): docs with an argument behind them

<a id="156"></a>
#### 156 · DIY Hardware Kits: keyboards, synths (`kit`)
**For:** small makers selling DIY kits and assembled versions of synth modules, split keyboards and similar hardware.
**Templates:** front-page · Woo shop · single-product · archive-product (by size) · page-build-guides · single-guide · page-legacy · page-shipping · page-us-customers · page-about
**Patterns (~45):** product spec block (HP width, depth, current draw +12V / -12V), DIY kit vs assembled variant, downloads (assembly instructions, schematic, BOM spreadsheet), difficulty note ("not a first build"), browse by HP size, beginner kits and no-soldering categories, build guides index, soldering how-to, legacy / retired products with old docs, open-source licence and GitHub links, "where to buy" list of stockists, shipping policy, US customers page
**Content model:** Woo products with spec meta (HP, depth, +12V mA, -12V mA, difficulty, kit/assembled); `guide` (product, steps, PDF); product status (current / legacy).
**Plugins:** WooCommerce, Query Filter (HP size, difficulty, kit or assembled).
**Signature:** a product page with the spec block (HP, depth, current draw) and a downloads list of assembly instructions, schematic and BOM, with kit and assembled as two variants (seen on: [Befaco](https://www.befaco.org/even-vco/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Browse by HP size so people can fill a gap in their case (seen on: [Thonk](https://www.thonk.co.uk/find-by-hp-size/))
- "How to solder if you've never soldered before" guide (seen on: [Music Thing Modular](https://www.musicthing.co.uk/extras/soldering.html))
- Legacy page keeping docs for discontinued products (seen on: [Befaco](https://www.befaco.org/legacy/))
- Difficulty warning on dense builds: "not recommended as a first DIY build" (seen on: [Music Thing Modular](https://www.musicthing.co.uk/Turing-Machine/))
- Build guides separated from the shop and linked from each product (seen on: [splitkb.com](https://docs.splitkb.com/hc/en-us/categories/360002241559-Build-Guides))
**Style: Industrial product spec**
- Type: headings Chakra Petch 700; body Manrope 400/18px; specs and part numbers Martian Mono 500
- Palette: bg #E6E6E6 (panel aluminium), text #111111, accent #FF5A00 (knob orange), surface #FFFFFF, line #0C6B3A (PCB green)
- Layout: product pages as a spec sheet: front panel photo at true proportion, specs in a two-column table, downloads as a file list with sizes; shop grid sorted by HP width with the width drawn to scale
- Imagery: flat, evenly lit front-panel shots on grey, PCB close-ups, build-in-progress photos from above
- Motion: none; hovering a product shows the PCB side via a plain image swap
- Why it fits now: instrument makers use exact, catalogue-like product pages that respect the buyer's knowledge (example: [teenage engineering](https://teenage.engineering/))
**Style variations:** Black panel: #111 bg, white legends · Solder mask: #0C6B3A ground · Cream panel: #EDE6D6 with brown legends
**Real-world basis:** [Befaco: Even VCO](https://www.befaco.org/even-vco/), [Befaco: JumpSkiff DIY kit](https://www.befaco.org/jumpskiff-diy-kit/), [Thonk: find by HP size](https://www.thonk.co.uk/find-by-hp-size/), [Music Thing Modular: Turing Machine](https://www.musicthing.co.uk/Turing-Machine/), [splitkb.com: keyboard kits](https://splitkb.com/collections/keyboard-kits)
**Refs:**
- [Befaco: Even VCO](https://www.befaco.org/even-vco/): specs and every build file on the product page
- [Music Thing Modular: Turing Machine](https://www.musicthing.co.uk/Turing-Machine/): open-source project page with honest difficulty advice
- [splitkb.com: build guides](https://docs.splitkb.com/hc/en-us/categories/360002241559-Build-Guides): guides organised per product

<a id="157"></a>
#### 157 · Build-in-Public Solo Founder (`founder`)
**For:** solo founders who run several small products and write openly about building them.
**Templates:** front-page · page-projects · page-now · page-stack · page-costs · archive (posts) · single · page-newsletter · page-about
**Patterns (~35):** projects index grouped by status (current / exits / shut down), project line (name, one-liner, link), /now page with a date, stack page (tools and costs), "startup costs" breakdown, challenge posts (12 startups in 12 months) with a running list, public stats link, newsletter sign-up, post archive by month and year, about
**Content model:** `project` (one-liner, URL, status, year started, year ended, revenue optional); posts.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Newsletter.
**Signature:** a projects page grouped by status (current, exits, shut down) so failures stay on the record (seen on: [Marc Köhlbrugge](https://marc.io/projects)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- /now page with a last-updated date (seen on: [Derek Sivers](https://sive.rs/now); format from [nownownow.com](https://www.nownownow.com/about))
- Stack page listing tools used (seen on: [Marc Köhlbrugge](https://marc.io/stack))
- Honest costs breakdown (seen on: [Justin Jackson](https://justinjackson.ca/costs))
- Link to a public analytics dashboard (seen on: [Plausible live demo](https://plausible.io/plausible.io))
- "Last updated" stamp on the projects page, bound from post modified date
**Style: Hand-kept ledger**
- Type: headings News Cycle 700; body Libre Franklin 400/18px with a serif second voice for posts, Libre Caslon Text 400; figures Courier Prime 700
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #1A1A1A, accent #B00020 (ledger red for shut-down projects), surface #F5F5F2, line #1A1A1A
- Layout: one column; projects as ledger rows with status in the margin; /now as a dated entry; archive grouped by year with post counts
- Imagery: almost none; founder photo on About; product screenshots only inside posts
- Motion: none
- Why it fits now: founder blogs that look personal, fast and unpolished are read as more honest than product-style sites (example: [@levelsio](https://levels.io/))
**Style variations:** Night ledger: #1A1A1A bg, paper text · Green ink: #0B6E4F accent · Carbon copy: #E9EEF5 ground, blue type
**Real-world basis:** [Marc Köhlbrugge: projects](https://marc.io/projects), [Marc Köhlbrugge: #buildinpublic](https://marc.io/buildinpublic), [@levelsio: 12 startups in 12 months](https://levels.io/12-startups-12-months), [Justin Jackson: startup costs](https://justinjackson.ca/costs), [Derek Sivers: /now](https://sive.rs/now)
**Refs:**
- [Marc Köhlbrugge: projects](https://marc.io/projects): current, sold and shut down in one list
- [@levelsio: 12 startups in 12 months](https://levels.io/12-startups-12-months): a public challenge tracked in one post
- [Derek Sivers: /now](https://sive.rs/now): the original /now page

#### 158 · AI Tool Landing + Waitlist (`waitlist`)
**For:** small teams launching a software tool (often AI-assisted) that is live on one platform and waitlisted on others.
**Templates:** front-page · page-download · page-waitlist · page-early-access · page-transparency · page-students · page-nonprofits · archive-release · page-faq · page-privacy
**Patterns (~30):** per-platform availability (download for Mac / join the Windows waitlist), waitlist form with what happens next, early access programme page, release notes, data and model transparency page (what is stored, for how long, whether it trains models), student and nonprofit offers, status link, FAQ, privacy policy, founders note
**Content model:** `platform` (name, status: available / waitlist / planned, download URL, waitlist form); `release`.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (waitlist), Jetpack Newsletter (launch emails).
**Signature:** per-platform download buttons where unreleased platforms turn into "join the waitlist" with their own form (seen on: [Dia](https://www.diabrowser.com/windows)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Transparency page on data retention and model training (seen on: [Granola](https://www.granola.ai/transparency))
- Student offer page (seen on: [Granola](https://www.granola.ai/students))
- Early access programme page (seen on: [Dia](https://www.diabrowser.com/earlybirds))
- "Latest release notes" permalink (seen on: [Dia](https://www.diabrowser.com/release-notes/latest))
- Confirmation page that tells people what happens after they join the waitlist and roughly when, instead of a bare "thanks"
**Style: Quiet e-paper minimal**
- Type: headings Rowan (Fontshare) 500 at large sizes; body General Sans (Fontshare) 400/18px; version and dates Fragment Mono 400
- Palette: bg #EFEDE8 (e-paper grey), text #1D1B18, accent #1D1B18 (ink only; the product screenshot carries the colour), surface #FFFFFF, line #CFCBC2
- Layout: short front page: one sentence on what the tool does, a real screenshot or 20-second screen recording, then the platform list; long text lives on the transparency and FAQ pages
- Imagery: real product captures only; no sparkles, orbs or robot art
- Motion: the screen recording plays muted with controls, paused under reduced motion; nothing else animates
- Why it fits now: calmer, paper-like sites have become the counter-signal to loud AI launches (example: [Daylight Computer](https://daylightcomputer.com/))
**Style variations:** Ink: #1D1B18 bg, paper text · Graphite: #D9D7D2 ground · Signal: one brand colour for the download button only
**Real-world basis:** [Dia: Windows](https://www.diabrowser.com/windows), [Dia: early birds](https://www.diabrowser.com/earlybirds), [Granola: transparency](https://www.granola.ai/transparency), [Granola: nonprofits](https://www.granola.ai/nonprofits), [Daylight Computer: FAQ](https://daylightcomputer.com/faq)
**Refs:**
- [Dia: Windows](https://www.diabrowser.com/windows): one platform live, one waitlisted, both clear
- [Granola: transparency](https://www.granola.ai/transparency): the data questions answered before sign-up
- [Zed: compare](https://zed.dev/compare): comparisons written for a technical audience

#### 159 · Freelance Developer / Consultant (`consult`)
**For:** independent developers, accessibility consultants and technical writers who sell their time, talks and workshops.
**Templates:** front-page · page-hire · page-projects · page-speaking · page-press-kit · page-endorsements · archive (posts) · page-uses · page-colophon · page-newsletter · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** hire page (services, who they won't work with, contact), projects list, speaking list (events, dates, slides, video), press kit (short and long bio, pronunciation, headshots to download, handles), endorsements split into client stories and workshop quotes, uses page, colophon, newsletter, writing archive, /now or availability line
**Content model:** `project` (client, year, role, link); `talk` (event, date, city, slides URL, video URL); `endorsement` (name, role, company, type: client / workshop).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Newsletter.
**Signature:** a press kit page with short and long bios, a pronunciation guide, social handles and downloadable headshots (seen on: [Sara Soueidan](https://www.sarasoueidan.com/press-kit/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Hire page that states who the consultant does not work with (seen on: [HeydonWorks](https://heydonworks.com/hire))
- Endorsements separated into long client stories and short workshop quotes (seen on: [Sara Soueidan](https://www.sarasoueidan.com/endorsements/))
- Speaking page with past events and slides (seen on: [hidde.blog](https://hidde.blog/speaking/))
- Uses page listing tools (seen on: [Zach Leatherman](https://www.zachleat.com/uses/))
- "Booking work from February" availability line in the header, set in one place
**Style: Kinetic variable-type homepage**
- Type: Sono variable for everything, 800 for headings, proportional (MONO 0) and 400 for body at 18px, MONO 1 for code and dates
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #111111, accent #FFE14D (highlighter), surface #F4F4F4, line #0B57D0 (link blue)
- Layout: personal, asymmetric page with a large name set in the casual cut and a plain list of what they do; projects and talks as dated lists; press kit as a download grid with file sizes
- Imagery: honest portraits, conference photos, and screenshots of their own work; no stock desks
- Motion: the casual axis eases between 0 and 1 on hover over the name only; off under reduced motion
- Why it fits now: independent web people have kept personal, hand-built homepages as their main calling card (example: [Miriam Eric Suzanne](https://www.miriamsuzanne.com/))
**Style variations:** Midnight: #111 bg, yellow links · Marker: #FF6FAE highlighter · Plain: black on white, blue links only
**Real-world basis:** [HeydonWorks: hire](https://heydonworks.com/hire), [Sara Soueidan: press kit](https://www.sarasoueidan.com/press-kit/), [Sara Soueidan: endorsements](https://www.sarasoueidan.com/endorsements/), [Zach Leatherman: projects](https://www.zachleat.com/projects/), [hidde.blog: speaking](https://hidde.blog/speaking/)
**Refs:**
- [Sara Soueidan: press kit](https://www.sarasoueidan.com/press-kit/): everything an event organiser needs on one page
- [HeydonWorks: hire](https://heydonworks.com/hire): services and ethics stated plainly
- [Miriam Eric Suzanne: colophon](https://www.miriamsuzanne.com/colophon/): a personal site that explains how it is made

<a id="160"></a>
#### 160 · Product Changelog & Public Roadmap Hub (`roadmap`)
**For:** small software teams that want a changelog, public roadmap and feature request list on their own domain instead of a hosted board.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-release · single-release · page-roadmap · archive-request · single-request · page-submit-request · page-subscribe · page-changelog-rss
**Patterns (~35):** changelog entry (date, title, image or video, fixes list, improvements list), change types (added / changed / deprecated / removed / fixed / security), roadmap in three sections (now / next / community requests), request list by status (pending / added / fixed / not possible / not planning) with vote counts and dates, reasons shown for declined requests, subscribe by email and RSS, version anchors, link to docs from each entry
**Content model:** `release` (version, date, type, change groups); `request` (status, votes, submitted date, decision reason, linked release).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Newsletter (email on new release), Jetpack Forms (request submission).
**Signature:** a feature request list grouped by status that keeps "not planning to implement" items visible with the reason, plus vote counts and dates (seen on: [Perfmatters](https://perfmatters.io/docs/feature-requests/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Roadmap split into "currently working on", "coming up next" and community items with votes (seen on: [Zed](https://zed.dev/roadmap))
- Change groups that follow Keep a Changelog, with linkable versions and dates (seen on: [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/))
- Fixes and improvements as lists under each feature announcement (seen on: [Linear](https://linear.app/changelog))
- Request marked "shipped" links to the release that shipped it, via the linked release meta
- RSS feed per product area for customers who only care about one part
**Style: Departure board status list**
- Type: headings Jersey 10 400; body Onest 400/18px; versions, dates and vote counts JetBrains Mono 500
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #111111, accent #F2A900 (in progress), surface #F3F3F3, line #0A7F3F (shipped); #9B1C1C used only for "not planning"
- Layout: roadmap as a departures-style table (item, status, updated), statuses as text with a coloured square, never a pulsing dot; changelog as a dated column with version anchors in the margin
- Imagery: product screenshots in changelog entries only, at native size
- Motion: none; status changes are instant
- Why it fits now: teams are moving roadmaps back onto their own sites as plain, linkable lists (example: [Zed roadmap](https://zed.dev/roadmap))
**Style variations:** Night board: #111 bg, amber text · Paper log: #FBFAF6 ground · Mono: black and white, status as words only
**Real-world basis:** [Perfmatters: feature requests](https://perfmatters.io/docs/feature-requests/), [Zed: roadmap](https://zed.dev/roadmap), [Linear: changelog](https://linear.app/changelog), [Plausible: changelog](https://plausible.io/changelog), [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/)
**Refs:**
- [Perfmatters: feature requests](https://perfmatters.io/docs/feature-requests/): statuses, votes and reasons for declining
- [Zed: roadmap](https://zed.dev/roadmap): now, next and community-voted items
- [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/): the change types this theme's release blocks should follow

### XVI. Civic, political & nonprofit

<a id="161"></a>
#### 161 · Local Election Candidate (`ballot`)
**For:** first-time and independent candidates for council, mayor, school board or a by-election, and small local parties running a slate of ward candidates.
**Templates:** front-page (donate takeover) · page-meet-the-candidate · archive-priority · single-priority · page-endorsements · page-record · page-events · page-volunteer · page-how-to-vote · page-privacy
**Patterns (~40):** donate takeover with preset amounts ($10 / $25 / $100 / $250 / other), sign-up strip (name, email, postcode, mobile + SMS consent), priorities grid (one tile per issue linking to its own page), "Meet [name]" biography, endorsements list (people and organisations), accomplishments / record timeline, candidates-by-ward list with postcode search, events list (canvassing, hustings, "Day of Action"), how-to-vote box (registration deadline, postal/proxy vote, polling day), imprint footer ("Promoted by … on behalf of …").
**Content model:** `priority` (short title, one-line pledge, order), `endorsement` (name, role, type: person/org/union), `candidate` (ward, bio, photo) for slates; `event` (date, place, type). Ward taxonomy.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (sign-up, volunteer), GiveWP or Jetpack Donations (or a link out to ActBlue/CrowdPac where law requires), Advanced Query Loop (upcoming events only), Polylang where the ward is multilingual.
**Signature:** a homepage donate takeover with preset-amount buttons that deep-link into the donation form, switched off after polling day (seen on: [Zohran for NYC](https://www.zohranfornyc.com/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Imprint line in the footer ("Promoted by [agent] on behalf of [candidate], both at [address]"), required for UK election material, bound to site settings (seen on: [Hackney Greens: Candidates](https://www.hackneygreens.org.uk/candidates)).
- "Away on polling day? Apply for a postal or proxy vote" box with the deadline date, which hides itself after the deadline (seen on: [Sheffield Green Party: Elections](https://sheffieldgreenparty.org.uk/elections/)).
- Postcode-to-ward lookup that shows "your candidate" on multi-ward slates (seen on: [Hackney Greens: Candidates](https://www.hackneygreens.org.uk/candidates)).
- Accomplishments record for incumbents, as a dated list (seen on: [Alexis for Seattle: Accomplishments](https://www.alexisforseattle.com/accomplishments)).
- Local public-funding explainer where it exists, e.g. Seattle's Democracy Vouchers (seen on: [Alexis for Seattle: Vouchers](https://www.alexisforseattle.com/vouchers)).
- Printable A5 leaflet version of the priorities page for canvassers.
**Style: Campaign poster takeover**
- Type: headings Passion One 900, set huge (12–16vw on the takeover) with normal tracking; body Public Sans 400/18px; small print and imprint IBM Plex Mono 400.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, ink #111111, campaign colour #F5C400 (hi-vis yellow, swappable per party), second colour #1D3FBF (ballot-paper blue), line #111111.
- Layout: full-bleed poster block on the front page with one slogan and the donate buttons as fat rectangular slabs (0 radius); below that a strict 4-column priorities grid with black 2px rules. Sticky slim top bar with only "Donate" and "Volunteer". No hero image carousel.
- Imagery: candidate photographed on real local streets in daylight, cut square and printed as a one-colour duotone (ink on the campaign colour); no studio headshots against grey.
- Motion: the takeover collapses to a bar after first dismissal (remembered in localStorage); View Transitions between priority tiles and their pages; nothing animates under prefers-reduced-motion.
- Why it fits now: the 2025 New York mayoral campaign made fly-poster type and one loud colour the grammar of insurgent local campaigns ([zohranfornyc.com](https://www.zohranfornyc.com/)).
**Style variations:** Fly-post: yellow bg, black type · Ballot: white, ballot-blue slabs · Night canvass: #111 bg, yellow type
**Real-world basis:** [Zohran for NYC](https://www.zohranfornyc.com/) · [Alexis for Seattle: Priorities](https://www.alexisforseattle.com/priorities) · [Hackney Greens: Candidates 2026](https://www.hackneygreens.org.uk/candidates) · [Sheffield Green Party: Walkley ward priorities](https://sheffieldgreenparty.org.uk/2026/09/14/water-litter-and-public-libraries-sebs-priorities-for-walkley-ward/) · [Run for Something: Local office guide](https://runforsomethingcivics.net/local-guide/)
**Refs:**
- [Zohran for NYC: home](https://www.zohranfornyc.com/): poster-scale slogan, preset donate amounts, SMS sign-up and a treasurer line in the footer; the takeover pattern to copy.
- [Alexis for Seattle: Priorities](https://www.alexisforseattle.com/priorities): eight priorities as a grid, each with its own page; a clean model for `priority` posts.
- [Hackney Greens: Candidates](https://www.hackneygreens.org.uk/candidates): one page per ward with a postcode search; how a small party runs a slate.

<a id="162"></a>
#### 162 · Local Councillor (`ward`)
**For:** sitting ward and parish councillors (and small council groups) who report back to residents between elections.
**Templates:** front-page · archive (ward reports) · single · taxonomy-issue · page-about-me · page-surgeries · page-report-a-problem · page-useful-links · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** monthly ward-report card (month, headline issues, tags), issue tags (fly-tipping, rats, ASB, greening, licensing, planning), councillor profile (ward, committee roles, council email/phone), "Report it" link panel (council service, FixMyStreet, WriteToThem), surgery dates list (date / venue / time), casework-update post, "introducing my ward colleague" card, useful-websites directory, planning and licensing application notices, imprint line.
**Content model:** posts (ward reports) with an `issue` taxonomy; `surgery` (date, venue, start/end, booking needed y/n); `councillor` (ward, party, committees, contact) for group sites.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (casework contact with consent tick), Advanced Query Loop (next surgery only), Polylang where needed.
**Signature:** a monthly ward-report series with every post tagged by local issue, so residents can open "everything on fly-tipping" (seen on: [Forest Gate North: Ward report](https://forestgatenorth.com/2020/09/24/ward-report-september-2020/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- "Useful websites" page that points residents to the right council service before they email (seen on: [Forest Gate North: Useful websites](https://forestgatenorth.com/useful-websites/)).
- Report-it panel with deep links to FixMyStreet and the council's own forms (seen on: [FixMyStreet](https://www.fixmystreet.com/)).
- Committee roles and council contact details on the profile, bound from `councillor` meta (seen on: [Bristol Green Party: Cllr Ed Plowden](https://bristolgreenparty.org.uk/councillor/ed-plowden/)).
- "Promoted by and on behalf of" line, plus an automatic pre-election-period notice that pauses campaign posts during purdah (seen on: [Bristol Green Party: Cllr Ed Plowden](https://bristolgreenparty.org.uk/councillor/ed-plowden/)).
- Casework form with a clear "What I can and can't help with" note and a response-time promise.
- Printable surgery poster (A4) for the library noticeboard, generated from the next `surgery` post.
**Style: Civic utility (public-service design lineage)**
- Type: headings B612 700 at large sizes (drawn for cockpit-screen legibility); body Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 400/19px; dates and ward names Newsreader 500 italic for a second, human voice.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #0B0C0C, ward green #00703C, focus/highlight #FFDD00, line #B1B4B6, surface #F3F2F1.
- Layout: single 66ch reading column with a left index of issues; wide black 5px top border on the header like a council notice; "Report it" as full-width link rows, not cards. Mobile-first; no carousels.
- Imagery: real photos of the ward (bins, parks, the estate), taken by the councillor, shown at 3:2 with captions and dates; no stock handshake images.
- Motion: none beyond focus states and underline thickening on hover; View Transitions between report archive and single.
- Why it fits now: plain public-service design is the trusted register for civic information in 2025–26 and is what residents already know from [GOV.UK](https://www.gov.uk/).
**Style variations:** Town hall: green rule, white page · Parish: warm #F3F2F1 surface, serif dates · Night: #0B0C0C bg, yellow focus
**Real-world basis:** [Forest Gate North: Ward report](https://forestgatenorth.com/2020/09/24/ward-report-september-2020/) · [Forest Gate North: Betting shop licence post](https://forestgatenorth.com/2025/07/31/betting-shop-licence-application/) · [Bristol Green Party: Cllr Ed Plowden](https://bristolgreenparty.org.uk/councillor/ed-plowden/) · [WriteToThem](https://www.writetothem.com/) · [TheyWorkForYou](https://www.theyworkforyou.com/)
**Refs:**
- [Forest Gate North: Ward report](https://forestgatenorth.com/2020/09/24/ward-report-september-2020/): a councillor's own WordPress blog with monthly reports tagged by issue; the core content habit.
- [Bristol Green Party: Cllr Ed Plowden](https://bristolgreenparty.org.uk/councillor/ed-plowden/): councillor profile built from a custom post type (ward, role, contacts, latest news); the `councillor` model.
- [WriteToThem](https://www.writetothem.com/): postcode-first civic utility; the plain, trustworthy register to aim for.

<a id="163"></a>
#### 163 · Tenants' Union (`tenants`)
**For:** renters' unions, tenant associations and estate residents' groups that organise members, defend evictions and run rights clinics.
**Templates:** front-page · page-join · page-know-your-rights · single-right (one topic per page) · page-member-defence · archive-campaign · single-campaign · page-calendar · page-branches · page-donate
**Patterns (~45):** join form with dues calculated from hourly pay, "Know your rights" topic index (evictions / Section 21, rent increases, repairs, deposits, discrimination, pets), member-defence request form, campaign pages ("Rent control now"), branch list with meeting nights, calendar (branch meetings, trainings, actions), demands list, walk-in clinic hours + hotline box, union elections notice, shop (badges, tote), press releases.
**Content model:** `right` (topic, jurisdiction, last reviewed date, summary), `campaign` (status: live/won/closed), `branch` (area, meeting night, venue), `event`. Language taxonomy via Polylang.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (join, member defence), GiveWP (donations and dues via recurring), The Events Calendar or companion `event` + Advanced Query Loop, Polylang.
**Signature:** a join page where dues are set by your hourly wage, with fixed special rates for unemployed and retired members (seen on: [ACORN: Join](https://acorntheunion.org.uk/join/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Walk-in clinic hours and hotline times at the top of the rights pages ("Tuesdays, arrive by 6:30pm") (seen on: [Met Council on Housing: Walk-in clinic](https://www.metcouncilonhousing.org/tenants--rights-mutual-walk-in-clinic)).
- "Up your dues" page for existing members after a pay rise (seen on: [ACORN: Update your dues](https://acorntheunion.org.uk/join/update-your-membership-dues/)).
- Member-defence request form for bailiffs and illegal evictions, with an "if it's happening now, call…" line (seen on: [ACORN: Member defence](https://acorntheunion.org.uk/contact/bailiff-member-defence/)).
- "Last reviewed" date and a "this is not legal advice" note on every rights page, bound from `right` meta.
- Translated rights pages, with the language list shown as words not flags.
- Union elections and AGM notices with nomination deadlines (seen on: [London Renters Union: Elections 2026](https://londonrentersunion.org/2026/lru-elections-2026/)).
**Style: Protest-poster black and white**
- Type: headings Protest Strike 400 in capitals, set tight but not crushed (0 tracking), used at poster scale; body Public Sans 400/18px; labels Public Sans 600.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, ink #000000, action red #D7261E, newsprint grey #E9E9E4 (surface), line #000000.
- Layout: two-column poster grid; the demands list as numbered full-width bands; rights pages as a long single column with a sticky topic index. Buttons are hard black rectangles; forms have 2px black borders.
- Imagery: black-and-white photos of real actions and door-knocking, high contrast, cropped tight on placards and faces with consent; hand-lettered placards used as found type.
- Motion: none on content; red underline swipe on link hover (transform only); fully static under prefers-reduced-motion.
- Why it fits now: renters' unions have grown fast since 2020 and the black-and-white poster look signals "movement, not charity" ([London Renters Union](https://londonrentersunion.org/)).
**Style variations:** Placard: red bg, black type · Newsprint: grey paper, black ink · Nightshift: black bg, white type
**Real-world basis:** [ACORN: Join](https://acorntheunion.org.uk/join/) · [ACORN: Renters' rights](https://acorntheunion.org.uk/renters-rights/) · [London Renters Union: Calendar](https://londonrentersunion.org/calendar/) · [London Renters Union: Demands](https://londonrentersunion.org/demands/) · [Met Council on Housing: Walk-in clinic](https://www.metcouncilonhousing.org/tenants--rights-mutual-walk-in-clinic)
**Refs:**
- [ACORN: Join](https://acorntheunion.org.uk/join/): wage-linked dues with special rates; the fairest join flow in the sector.
- [ACORN: Renters' rights](https://acorntheunion.org.uk/renters-rights/): rights split by topic in plain language; the template for `right` posts.
- [London Renters Union: Demands](https://londonrentersunion.org/demands/): short, numbered demands in poster type; the visual register for this theme.

<a id="164"></a>
#### 164 · Trade Union Branch (`branch`)
**For:** workplace and local union branches (university UCU branches, IWW and independent unions, hospital and council branches) run by volunteer officers.
**Templates:** front-page · page-join · page-reps · archive-motion · single-motion · page-minutes · page-ballot · page-know-your-rights · page-hardship-fund · archive-campaign · page-events
**Patterns (~45):** subscription band table (salary band → monthly dues), reps table (department / rep / email / "vacancy"), current ballot box (opening and closing dates, turnout threshold, "request a replacement ballot"), motions archive (passed / fell / date), minutes list, know-your-rights pages (missing wages, sick pay, annual leave), hardship / support fund application, "how to stand" for officer roles, campaign pages, events (branch meeting, picket rota), language switcher.
**Content model:** `motion` (date, meeting, outcome), `minutes` (meeting date, PDF), `rep` (department, role, vacancy flag), `ballot` (open, close, threshold, status), `right` (topic, last reviewed). Language via Polylang.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (join enquiry, hardship fund, update details), Advanced Query Loop (current ballot, next meeting), Query Filter (motions by year/outcome), Polylang.
**Signature:** a ballot information page with voting dates, the 50% turnout rule, replacement-ballot instructions and an FAQ, surfaced site-wide while the ballot is open (seen on: [Goldsmiths UCU: Upcoming ballot](https://goldsmithsucu.org/2026/03/10/information-on-gucu-upcoming-ballot-march-16-to-april-10-2026/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Reps table with "Vacancy" flags that double as a recruitment ask (seen on: [Goldsmiths UCU: Departmental reps](https://goldsmithsucu.org/departmental-reps/)).
- Subscription table by salary band so people can see their dues before joining (seen on: [Cambridge UCU: Join](https://www.ucu.cam.ac.uk/join/)).
- Hardship / support fund page with a short confidential form (seen on: [Goldsmiths UCU: Support fund](https://goldsmithsucu.org/support-fund/)).
- Translated know-your-rights pages for migrant workers (seen on: [UVW: Know your rights](https://www.uvwunion.org.uk/en/know-your-rights)).
- "Update your details" form for members who change job or address (seen on: [Cambridge UCU: Update your details](https://www.ucu.cam.ac.uk/contact/update-your-details/)).
- Searchable motions and minutes archive, so a branch's decisions are on the record.
**Style: Banner heritage meets plain bulletin**
- Type: headings Vidaloka 400 (a fat high-contrast serif that recalls painted union banners) at 4–6× body size; body IBM Plex Sans 400/18px; tables, dates and motion numbers IBM Plex Mono 500.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #1A1A1A, banner crimson #9E1B32, banner gold #C9A227, deep navy #14213D (header band), line #D8D4CC.
- Layout: navy header band with the branch name set like a banner; content below in a plain two-column bulletin (main + "Current ballot / Next meeting" sidebar). Tables use full rules, no zebra striping. Motions read like minutes, numbered.
- Imagery: photos of the branch's own banner, picket lines and meetings; archive scans of old leaflets; no stock handshakes.
- Motion: none; the only state change is the ballot box switching from "open" to "result" by date.
- Why it fits now: union membership among younger workers is rising and branches are reclaiming banner heritage in print and online; the reference collection is the [People's History Museum](https://phm.org.uk/).
**Style variations:** Banner: navy band, gold serif · Bulletin: white, black tables · Picket: crimson bg, white type
**Real-world basis:** [Goldsmiths UCU: Departmental reps](https://goldsmithsucu.org/departmental-reps/) · [Goldsmiths UCU: Ballot info](https://goldsmithsucu.org/2026/03/10/information-on-gucu-upcoming-ballot-march-16-to-april-10-2026/) · [Cambridge UCU: Join](https://www.ucu.cam.ac.uk/join/) · [IWW London branch](https://iww.org.uk/london/) · [UVW: Know your rights](https://www.uvwunion.org.uk/en/know-your-rights)
**Refs:**
- [Goldsmiths UCU: Upcoming ballot](https://goldsmithsucu.org/2026/03/10/information-on-gucu-upcoming-ballot-march-16-to-april-10-2026/): dates, threshold and FAQ on one page; the model for the `ballot` pattern.
- [Cambridge UCU: Join](https://www.ucu.cam.ac.uk/join/): salary-band dues table on a WordPress branch site.
- [UVW: Know your rights](https://www.uvwunion.org.uk/en/know-your-rights): multilingual rights pages (EN/ES) for low-paid migrant workers.

<a id="165"></a>
#### 165 · Mutual Aid Network (`mutual`)
**For:** neighbourhood mutual aid groups, solidarity networks and free stores run by volunteers with little money and less time.
**Templates:** front-page (two doors: need / offer) · page-request-help · page-offer-help · page-donate-items · page-calendar · archive-resource · single-resource · page-faq · page-about
**Patterns (~30):** two-door front page ("I need help" / "I can help"), request form with a phone-line alternative, offer / volunteer form with skills checkboxes, items wishlist ("We need: nappies size 4, tinned fish"), capacity notice ("Deliveries currently take 3–5 days"), confidentiality statement, anonymised requests map by postcode area, calendar (free store, distribution days), resource library by topic (food, bail funds, childcare), seasonal projects (heatwave buddies, fruit gleaning), FAQ.
**Content model:** `resource` (topic, link, last checked), `need` (item, quantity, urgency), `event`. No personal data stored in posts.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (request, offer), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (anonymised map), Polylang, Jetpack Donations.
**Signature:** separate "Request help" and "Offer help" pathways from the front page, each a short form, with a phone number for people without internet (seen on: [Berkeley Mutual Aid: Need assistance](https://www.berkeleymutualaid.org/need-assistance) and [Offering assistance](https://www.berkeleymutualaid.org/offering-assistance)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Capacity notice set by an admin toggle, e.g. "Deliveries currently take 3–5 days" (seen on: [ROC Mutual Aid: Request aid](https://rocmutualaid.com/requests)).
- Anonymised fulfilled-requests map by postcode area, which proves the work without exposing anyone (seen on: [ROC Mutual Aid: Requests map](https://rocmutualaid.com/resources/requests-map)).
- Items wishlist that volunteers can update without editing the page (seen on: [ROC Mutual Aid: Donate items](https://rocmutualaid.com/donate/items)).
- Seasonal buddy schemes switched on by date (heatwave, wildfire smoke, cold snap) (seen on: [Berkeley Mutual Aid: Wildfire buddies](https://www.berkeleymutualaid.org/wildfire-buddies)).
- Printable A4 "we're here" poster with a tear-off phone number strip, for lamp posts and launderettes.
- Plain-language and translated versions of the request page.
**Style: Web 1.0 text-first revival**
- Type: headings Mukta 800 at large sizes, normal tracking; body Atkinson Hyperlegible 400/19px; links underlined always.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #111111, link blue #0033CC, visited #333399, highlight #FFF2A8 (marker yellow), line #111111.
- Layout: one column, 70ch, no cards; the two doors are two huge text links stacked on mobile and side by side on desktop. Lists everywhere. Page weight under 200 KB so it loads on a prepaid phone.
- Imagery: almost none; a hand-drawn map or photocopied flyer scans at most. Photos only of real distribution days, with consent.
- Motion: none. Pages must work with JS off.
- Why it fits now: low-bandwidth, text-first sites are back in favour with organisers and link-sharing communities, as on [Are.na](https://www.are.na/), and they load for the people who most need them.
**Style variations:** Photocopy: grey #EDEDED paper, black type · Marker: yellow highlight headings · Night line: black bg, white type
**Real-world basis:** [ROC Mutual Aid: Request aid](https://rocmutualaid.com/requests) · [ROC Mutual Aid: Requests map](https://rocmutualaid.com/resources/requests-map) · [Berkeley Mutual Aid: Need assistance](https://www.berkeleymutualaid.org/need-assistance) · [MANA: Free store offer](https://www.wearemana.org/free-store-offer-services-or-goods) · [Big Door Brigade: Mutual aid toolbox](https://bigdoorbrigade.com/mutual-aid-toolbox/)
**Refs:**
- [ROC Mutual Aid: Request aid](https://rocmutualaid.com/requests): honest capacity notice, confidentiality note and a bilingual phone line on the request page.
- [Berkeley Mutual Aid: Offering assistance](https://www.berkeleymutualaid.org/offering-assistance): the "offer" door; short and specific about what help is needed.
- [Big Door Brigade: Mutual aid toolbox](https://bigdoorbrigade.com/mutual-aid-toolbox/): a WordPress, text-first resource library by topic; the model for `resource`.

<a id="166"></a>
#### 166 · Housing Co-op / Community Land Trust (`landtrust`)
**For:** community land trusts, housing co-ops and cohousing groups that build or hold homes, allocate them to local people and raise community shares.
**Templates:** front-page · page-what-is-a-clt · archive-project · single-project · archive-home (homes available) · single-home · page-apply · page-invest · page-residents · page-governance · page-publications
**Patterns (~40):** "What is a CLT / co-op" explainer, project page with timeline (site found → planning → build → move-in), homes-for-sale list with price breakdown (market value / trust subsidy / your price), prices-by-bedroom table, allocation criteria and application steps, community share offer box, residents' stories, governance (board, one-member-one-vote, rules PDF), annual reports, developments in progress, interpretation / translated guides.
**Content model:** `project` (stage, homes, tenure mix, completion), `home` (bedrooms, sq ft/m², market value, subsidy, buyer price, status: available/under offer/sold), `publication` (year, PDF).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (register interest), GiveWP (donations; share offers usually link to Ethex or the co-op's own form), Query Filter (homes by bedrooms/status), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (project map), Polylang.
**Signature:** a homes-for-sale listing that shows market value, the trust's investment and the buyer's price side by side for every home (seen on: [Champlain Housing Trust: Find a home](https://www.getahome.org/find-a-home/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Project timeline strip from 2009 to move-in, with applicant numbers and "% of open market value" (seen on: [London CLT: St Clements](https://www.londonclt.org/st-clements)).
- Homeowner guides in many languages plus an "interpretation services available" note (seen on: [Champlain Housing Trust: Learn about your home (Somali)](https://www.getahome.org/learn-about-your-home-somali/)).
- Annual reports and publications archive, as PDF plus an HTML summary (seen on: [Champlain Housing Trust: Publications](https://www.getahome.org/cht-publications/)).
- "Become an investor" page for community shares with the risk statement up front (seen on: [Radical Routes: Become an investor](https://www.radicalroutes.org.uk/become-an-investor/)).
- Plain explainer of the tenure model (mutual home ownership, shared equity) (seen on: [LILAC: Affordable](https://www.lilac.coop/affordable/)).
- "Sold" / "Under offer" states on homes, driven by one select field.
**Style: Housing-plan civic modernism**
- Type: headings Didact Gothic 400 at large sizes; body Literata 400/18px for long explainers; plan labels and prices IBM Plex Mono 500.
- Palette: bg #FBFBF8, text #10231F, trust green #006A51, deep green #02362F (footer), brick #B32E16 (accent), line #C9D3CF.
- Layout: project pages use a site-plan grid: a large axonometric or plan drawing, then a table of homes. Explainers are single-column with margin notes. Home cards are flat rectangles with a thin rule, square corners, price table inside.
- Imagery: architects' plans and elevations, construction photos with dates, residents photographed in their own homes; no CGI families.
- Motion: timeline scrolls horizontally with scroll-snap on mobile; plan drawings open in the core lightbox; static under reduced motion.
- Why it fits now: community-led housing is growing again in the UK and US, and the most trusted trusts present homes like public architecture, not estate-agent listings ([Champlain Housing Trust](https://www.getahome.org/)).
**Style variations:** Blueprint: #10231F bg, pale lines · Brick: brick red headers, white page · Allotment: sage #DDE5DF surface
**Real-world basis:** [Champlain Housing Trust: Find a home](https://www.getahome.org/find-a-home/) · [Champlain Housing Trust: Shared equity FAQ](https://www.getahome.org/faq-shared-equity/) · [London CLT: St Clements](https://www.londonclt.org/st-clements) · [LILAC: Affordable](https://www.lilac.coop/affordable/) · [Radical Routes: How to set up a co-op](https://www.radicalroutes.org.uk/how-to-set-up-a-co-op/)
**Refs:**
- [Champlain Housing Trust: Find a home](https://www.getahome.org/find-a-home/): the price breakdown per home; the core `home` binding.
- [London CLT: St Clements](https://www.londonclt.org/st-clements): one project told as a timeline with prices by bedroom.
- [LILAC: Affordable](https://www.lilac.coop/affordable/): a WordPress co-op explaining its tenure model in plain words.

#### 167 · Community Energy Co-op (`gridcoop`)
**For:** community benefit societies and energy co-ops that put solar on schools, estates and village halls and fund them with community shares.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-project · single-project · page-invest (share offer) · page-how-it-works · page-community-fund · page-get-involved · page-open-meetings · page-members · page-agm · page-faq · archive (news)
**Patterns (~40):** project card (site, kWp, went live, CO₂ saved, investors), share-offer box (minimum £50 / target / closing date / expected interest), "How community energy works" diagram, community fund explainer (surplus spent locally), open project meetings list, AGM notices and accounts, investor login link, volunteer sign-up (energy champions), fuel-poverty / warm-homes advice, FAQ (risk, withdrawal, one member one vote), partners list.
**Content model:** `project` (site, kWp, go-live date, annual generation, CO₂, investors, share offer raised), `share_offer` (min, target, raised, opens, closes, status), `event` (open meeting, AGM).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (pledge, volunteer), Advanced Query Loop (open share offer, next meeting), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (map of rooftops), GiveWP for the community fund.
**Signature:** per-project pages with installed capacity (kWp), go-live date and the amount raised by the share offer, grouped on one projects archive (seen on: [Repowering London: Lambeth Community Solar](https://www.repowering.org.uk/lambeth-community-solar/) and [Brixton Energy Solar 3](https://brixtonenergy.co.uk/projects/brixton-energy-solar-3/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Share-offer state box: "Pledge to invest from £50", open/closed by date, with the risk warning next to the button (seen on: [Energy Garden: Community energy](https://www.energygarden.org.uk/community-energy)).
- Open project meetings page so neighbours can come before the panels go up (seen on: [Brixton Energy: Open meetings](https://brixtonenergy.co.uk/get-involved/open-meetings/)).
- AGM papers and accounts archive for members (seen on: [Brixton Energy: Projects FAQ](https://brixtonenergy.co.uk/projects/faq/)).
- "How to invest" explainer that covers withdrawal, interest and tax relief in plain words (seen on: [Repowering London: How to invest](https://www.repowering.org.uk/how-to-invest/)).
- Printable one-page share-offer summary for door-to-door and school newsletters.
- Directory link to other open offers nationally (seen on: [Community Energy England: Share offers](https://communityenergyengland.org/share-offers/)).
**Style: Data-journal editorial**
- Type: headings Reddit Sans 800 at large sizes; body Source Serif 4 400/18px; numbers (kWp, £, tCO₂) Chivo Mono 500 with tabular figures.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #1B1F1D, solar yellow #F2B705, grid blue #1F5FAD, surface #F2F4F1, line #D5DAD6.
- Layout: numbers-led front page: one big live figure ("1,284 kWp owned by 900 neighbours", real data only) set in mono, then a map of rooftops, then projects as a table/list with small photos. Project pages read like a short report: figures table, then story.
- Imagery: aerial and rooftop photos of the actual installations, school kids with the inverter, drawn single-line diagrams; no generic solar-farm stock.
- Motion: generation chart draws once when in view, only if motion is allowed; hover on a map pin highlights the project row.
- Why it fits now: clear, chart-first explainers of energy data are what the public now trusts on climate topics ([Our World in Data](https://ourworldindata.org/)).
**Style variations:** Midday: yellow accents on white · Grid: blue header, white · Dusk: #1B1F1D bg, yellow figures
**Real-world basis:** [Brixton Energy: Projects](https://brixtonenergy.co.uk/projects/) · [Repowering London: Lambeth Community Solar](https://www.repowering.org.uk/lambeth-community-solar/) · [Energy Garden: Community energy](https://www.energygarden.org.uk/community-energy) · [BHESCo: Invest](https://bhesco.co.uk/invest-community-energy) · [Sharenergy: Projects](https://www.sharenergy.coop/projects/)
**Refs:**
- [Repowering London: Lambeth Community Solar](https://www.repowering.org.uk/lambeth-community-solar/): project page with money raised, kWp per school and a community fund; the `project` fields.
- [Brixton Energy: Open meetings](https://brixtonenergy.co.uk/get-involved/open-meetings/): a WordPress co-op site that keeps meetings, projects and AGMs simple.
- [BHESCo: Invest](https://bhesco.co.uk/invest-community-energy): a 2026 share offer page with target return and minimum investment.

#### 168 · Food Bank / Community Pantry (`pantry-share`)
**For:** independent food banks, Trussell-network food banks, community pantries and social supermarkets run by volunteers and a coordinator.
**Templates:** front-page · page-get-help · page-how-to-get-a-voucher · page-locations · page-at-the-food-bank · page-give-food · page-volunteer · page-join-a-pantry · page-donate · page-faqs · archive (news, real stories)
**Patterns (~40):** "Get help" first block (how to get a voucher or referral, what happens on the day), distribution centres list (venue / day / hours), "most-needed items" shopping list, online giving store link, membership explainer for pantries ("£5 a week, food worth more"), order-ahead / online ordering info, volunteer roles, referral agency sign-up, additional support (debt, benefits, cookery courses), real stories, legacy giving, supermarket collection points.
**Content model:** `location` (venue, address, day, open/close, step-free y/n, what3words optional), `need` (item, status: urgent/normal/not needed), `story`.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (volunteer, referral agency), GiveWP or Jetpack Donations, Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (locations), Polylang.
**Signature:** a live "most-needed items" list that volunteers update from one screen, shown on the front page and the give-food page (seen on: [Hackney Foodbank: Give food](https://www.hackney.foodbank.org.uk/give-food)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Locations list where each centre shows its own day and hours, with "open today" highlighted (seen on: [Hackney Foodbank: Locations](https://www.hackney.foodbank.org.uk/locations)).
- Order-ahead explainer for clients who can't queue ("counts as your monthly visit") (seen on: [Common Pantry: Online ordering](https://www.commonpantry.org/online-ordering/)).
- Pantry membership explainer with the weekly price and the value members get (seen on: [Church Action on Poverty pantry network: Join a pantry](https://www.yourlocalpantry.co.uk/join-a-pantry/)).
- "No items today" / "Not needed this month" states on the shopping list, so donors stop bringing pasta.
- Christmas and bank-holiday opening changes as a dated notice.
- Plain-language and translated "What happens when you visit" page, with step-free access notes per venue.
**Style: Shelf-label utility, dignity first**
- Type: headings Livvic 700 at large sizes; body Atkinson Hyperlegible 400/19px (made for low-vision readers); item lists in Livvic 600 with tabular figures.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #1C1C1C, shelf-label yellow #FFD83D, pantry green #1F7A4D, surface #F4F4F0, line #1C1C1C.
- Layout: the first screen answers "I need food" in one sentence with three steps; donors come second. The shopping list is styled as shelf labels (yellow tag, bold item name, status). Hours and venues are tables, not cards.
- Imagery: volunteers and shelves photographed at the real warehouse; no photos of clients' faces unless they tell their own story; no sad-hands-holding-bowl stock.
- Motion: none beyond focus; the "open today" row is highlighted by date on the server, not animated.
- Why it fits now: the pantry movement has moved language from charity to membership and choice, and its sites use accessible, friendly type like FS Me ([Church Action on Poverty pantry network](https://www.yourlocalpantry.co.uk/)).
**Style variations:** Shelf: yellow labels on white · Market: green header, white · Large print: 22px body, black on white
**Real-world basis:** [Hackney Foodbank: Get support](https://www.hackney.foodbank.org.uk/get-support) · [Hackney Foodbank: Locations](https://www.hackney.foodbank.org.uk/locations) · [Common Pantry: Emergency food](https://www.commonpantry.org/emergency-food/) · [Church Action on Poverty pantry network: Deal Pantry](https://www.yourlocalpantry.co.uk/pantry-listings/deal-pantry/) · [Trussell: Find a food bank](https://www.trussell.org.uk/emergency-food/find-a-foodbank)
**Refs:**
- [Hackney Foodbank: Give food](https://www.hackney.foodbank.org.uk/give-food): most-needed items with an online giving store delivered to the warehouse.
- [Common Pantry: Online ordering](https://www.commonpantry.org/online-ordering/): a WordPress pantry explaining order-ahead pickup with dignity and clear rules.
- [Church Action on Poverty pantry network: Join a pantry](https://www.yourlocalpantry.co.uk/join-a-pantry/): the membership model and pantry finder.

#### 169 · Repair Café (`repair`)
**For:** volunteer repair cafés, restart parties and fixing groups that meet monthly in libraries, church halls and community centres.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-event · single-event · page-what-we-fix · page-house-rules · page-before-you-come · page-volunteer · page-impact · page-faq · page-find-a-repair-shop · page-donate
**Patterns (~35):** next repair café box (date, time, venue, last item accepted at), what-we-fix list (electricals, textiles, bikes, jewellery, toys, sharpening) with "what we can't fix", house rules / liability disclaimer, pre-arrival instructions (bring the charger, describe the fault), volunteer fixer sign-up by skill, impact numbers from logged repairs, local repair-business directory, event list with venues across the area, FAQ, donation jar note.
**Content model:** `event` (date, start, last-entry, venue, skills present), `repair_log` (category, outcome: fixed/repairable/end of life, weight) for the impact page, `venue`.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (upcoming sessions), Jetpack Forms (volunteer, pre-registration), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap.
**Signature:** an impact page fed by a simple repair log (items brought, fixed, kg saved), in the style of the Restart Project's open repair data (seen on: [The Restart Project: The Fixometer](https://therestartproject.org/fixometer-2/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- House rules and liability statement that visitors read before the event (seen on: [Tucson Repair Cafe: House rules](https://www.tucsonrepaircafe.com/house-rules)).
- Pre-arrival instructions: bring chargers and parts, one item per visit, arrive before last entry (seen on: [Tucson Repair Cafe: Pre-arrival instructions](https://www.tucsonrepaircafe.com/pre-arrival-instructions)).
- Upcoming sessions across several venues in one list (seen on: [Repair Café Silicon Valley](https://repaircafesv.org/)).
- "Can't wait for the next café?" link to local repair businesses (seen on: [London Repairs](https://londonrepairs.org/)).
- Volunteer fixer roles by skill (electrical, sewing, bikes, greeter) (seen on: [Repair Café Silicon Valley: Volunteer opportunities](https://repaircafesv.org/volunteer-opportunities/)).
- Printable A4 event poster generated from the next `event`.
**Style: Service-manual technical drawing**
- Type: headings Michroma 400 (wide technical lettering) at large sizes; body IBM Plex Sans 400/18px; part numbers and dates JetBrains Mono 500.
- Palette: bg #F7F7F4, text #1D1D1B, safety orange #FF6A13, schematic blue #2457A6, line #1D1D1B.
- Layout: pages set like a service manual: numbered sections (they are real sequences here: arrive, register, wait, fix), exploded-view line drawings as section heads, parts-list tables for "what we fix". Square corners, 1.5px black rules.
- Imagery: close-up photos of hands and tools at real sessions, opened-up toasters and sewing machines on a neutral table, plus simple black line drawings of common items.
- Motion: none; hover on a "what we fix" row reveals its line drawing (static fallback shows all).
- Why it fits now: the right-to-repair movement has made repair guides and exploded diagrams part of mainstream culture ([iFixit guides](https://www.ifixit.com/Guide)).
**Style variations:** Workbench: orange tags, grey paper · Blueprint: blue bg, white lines · Library: white, black rules only
**Real-world basis:** [Repair Café International: Visit](https://www.repaircafe.org/en/visit/) · [The Restart Project: Upcoming parties](https://therestartproject.org/parties/) · [Tucson Repair Cafe: Events](https://www.tucsonrepaircafe.com/event-list) · [Repair Café Silicon Valley: FAQ](https://repaircafesv.org/faq/) · [Portsmouth: Repair](https://shareportsmouth.org.uk/repair/)
**Refs:**
- [The Restart Project: The Fixometer](https://therestartproject.org/fixometer-2/): how logged repairs become impact stats; the basis for the impact page.
- [Tucson Repair Cafe: House rules](https://www.tucsonrepaircafe.com/house-rules): plain house rules and liability terms every café needs.
- [Repair Café Silicon Valley](https://repaircafesv.org/): a WordPress site listing sessions across many venues.

<a id="170"></a>
#### 170 · Library of Things (`borrow`)
**For:** tool libraries, libraries of things and share shops lending drills, carpet cleaners, tents and sewing machines to members.
**Templates:** front-page · page-how-borrowing-works · page-join · page-catalogue (embed or link) · page-locations · single-location · page-donate-things · page-volunteer · page-workshops · page-faqs · page-policies
**Patterns (~35):** how-borrowing-works steps (join, reserve, collect, return), membership tiers and concessions (free for social housing, £1/year, £50 standard), catalogue categories grid (DIY, garden, cleaning, camping, kitchen, parties, kids), popular items list with weekly fee, locations with opening hours and click-and-collect, ID and proof-of-address note, borrowing terms / late fees, donate-things wishlist, repair and workshop events, FAQs.
**Content model:** `location` (address, hours, collection type: staffed/locker), `thing_category` taxonomy; the live catalogue stays in Lend Engine / myTurn and is linked or embedded, with a companion `thing` CPT (fee per week, deposit, category) for small libraries without one.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (donate things, volunteer), Query Filter (things by category), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (locations).
**Signature:** a "how borrowing works" page in four steps with the price per item per week shown in the catalogue (seen on: [Library of Things: How borrowing works](https://www.libraryofthings.co.uk/how-borrowing-works) and [Portsmouth Library of Things: Borrow](https://shareportsmouth.org.uk/borrow/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Concession and free membership rules stated up front (free in social housing or on benefits) (seen on: [Borrow It!: Joining](https://borrowit.org.uk/joining/)).
- Late-fee and maintenance-fee rules explained per item (seen on: [Toronto Tool Library: Membership](https://torontotoollibrary.com/search_tools/)).
- "Coming soon" state for new branches, with a crowdfunder link (seen on: [Share Bristol: Easton](https://sharebristol.org.uk/locations/easton/)).
- "Donate things" page listing what they want and what they can't take (seen on: [Share Bristol: Donate things](https://sharebristol.org.uk/support-us/donate-things/)).
- Printable care card per item (how to clean the carpet cleaner before return).
- Gift memberships.
**Style: Catalogue card index**
- Type: headings Hoover 700 (Fontshare slab) at large sizes; body Figtree 400/18px; catalogue numbers and fees Martian Mono 400.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #1A1A1A, index-card buff #F1E6C8 (surface for cards only), library red #C8102E, tool green #2E6B3F, line #1A1A1A.
- Layout: things shown as index cards in a tight grid (buff card, red top rule, catalogue number, name, "£3/week"), square corners; category nav as a Dewey-style list with numbers. Locations as a table. Plenty of white page around the cards.
- Imagery: every item photographed the same way on a plain white sweep, top-down, same scale bar, like a museum catalogue; members photographed using things in real homes.
- Motion: card hover lifts nothing; it flips the card to show the care note (CSS 3D flip, static list under reduced motion).
- Why it fits now: borrowing instead of buying is going mainstream in UK cities, and the leading library presents its catalogue with friendly, clear type ([Library of Things](https://www.libraryofthings.co.uk/)).
**Style variations:** Card: buff cards, red rule · Shed: tool green header · Locker: black bg, yellow numbers
**Real-world basis:** [Library of Things: How borrowing works](https://www.libraryofthings.co.uk/how-borrowing-works) · [Share Bristol: FAQs](https://sharebristol.org.uk/about/faqs/) · [Borrow It!: Joining](https://borrowit.org.uk/joining/) · [Portsmouth Library of Things: Borrow](https://shareportsmouth.org.uk/borrow/) · [Toronto Tool Library: Membership](https://torontotoollibrary.com/search_tools/)
**Refs:**
- [Portsmouth Library of Things: Borrow](https://shareportsmouth.org.uk/borrow/): a WordPress library with £1 membership, weekly fees and click-and-collect.
- [Borrow It!: Joining](https://borrowit.org.uk/joining/): honest membership copy that covers ID, free tiers and the monthly price.
- [Toronto Tool Library: Membership](https://torontotoollibrary.com/search_tools/): one simple membership with clear maintenance and late fees.

<a id="171"></a>
#### 171 · Animal Rescue & Adoption (`rescue`)
**For:** small independent dog and cat rescues, home-carer networks (animals live with volunteers) and local shelters with one to three rehoming sites.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-animal · single-animal · page-adoption-process · page-adoption-fees · page-fostering · page-surrender · archive-happy-tails · page-volunteer · page-donate · page-shop · page-faqs
**Patterns (~45):** animals-looking-for-homes grid (photo, name, age, sex, good with kids/dogs/cats, location), single animal profile (story, needs, fee, "apply to adopt"), adoption process steps (apply, review, vet reference, home visit, meet), adoption fees and what's included, foster carers appeal, "surrender your pet" page, happy tails / rehomed stories, retirees or long-stayers section, sponsor-a-kennel, donate in memory, vet clinic treatment prices (where the rescue runs a clinic), shop.
**Content model:** `animal` (species, breed, age, sex, size, good with, location, status: available/reserved/adopted, fee, intake date), `species` and `location` taxonomies, `story`.
**Plugins:** Query Filter (by species, size, location), Jetpack Forms (adoption and foster carer applications), GiveWP (donate, in memory, sponsor), WooCommerce only if they sell merch.
**Signature:** animal listings filterable by species and location, with each profile moving to a "Happy tails" archive when its status changes to adopted (seen on: [Compact Canine Rescue: Ready for adoption](https://compactcaninerescue.org/available-dogs/) and [Rejoice! alumni](https://compactcaninerescue.org/happy-tails-dogs/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Adoption fees range with "what's included" (vaccinations, microchip, neutering) (seen on: [Compact Canine Rescue: Adoption fees](https://compactcaninerescue.org/adoption-fees/)).
- "Surrender / rehome your pet" guidance for owners who can't cope (seen on: [The Little Red Dog: How to rehome your pet](https://thelittlereddog.org/how-to-rehome-your-pet)).
- Transparent treatment price list for the rescue's low-cost vet clinic (seen on: [Celia Hammond Animal Trust: Treatment prices](https://www.celiahammond.org/treatment-prices)).
- Matching process explainer: "register interest rather than apply for one dog" (seen on: [Battersea: How to rehome a dog](https://www.battersea.org.uk/rehome/dogs)).
- "Reserved" ribbon on profiles and a "long-stayer" flag after 90 days in care, computed from the intake date.
- Donate-in-memory page for pets that have died (seen on: [Celia Hammond Animal Trust: Donate in memory](https://www.celiahammond.org/donate-in-memory/)).
**Style: Portrait-led warm editorial**
- Type: headings Bree Serif 400 at large sizes; body Hanken Grotesk 400/18px; animal facts in Hanken Grotesk 600 small caps.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #222222, collar red #C23B22, kennel blue #2F5D8A, straw #F3E3B5 (tags), line #E2DED6.
- Layout: animal portraits first: a big 4:5 portrait grid (two across on mobile), name set large under each photo; profiles open with the portrait full height beside the story and a facts table. Round corners only on the "good with" tags.
- Imagery: animals photographed at eye level in daylight against plain walls or grass, no cages visible, same crop for every portrait; volunteer carers' homes shown as they are.
- Motion: View Transitions from grid photo into the profile portrait; nothing else moves.
- Why it fits now: rehoming sites that treat each animal as a portrait with a name and a story perform best on adoption, as the largest UK rescue does ([Battersea](https://www.battersea.org.uk/)).
**Style variations:** Kennel: blue header, white page · Straw: warm straw tags, red links · Night: #222 bg, white portraits
**Real-world basis:** [Compact Canine Rescue: Adoption process](https://compactcaninerescue.org/adoption-process/) · [Celia Hammond Animal Trust: Adopt a cat](https://www.celiahammond.org/adopt-a-cat/) · [The Little Red Dog: Dogs to adopt](https://thelittlereddog.org/dogs-to-adopt) · [Little Dog Rescue: Adopt](https://www.littledogrescue.org/adopt) · [Battersea: How to rehome a dog](https://www.battersea.org.uk/rehome/dogs)
**Refs:**
- [Compact Canine Rescue: Ready for adoption](https://compactcaninerescue.org/available-dogs/): a WordPress rescue with available, retiree and alumni archives; the `animal` status model.
- [Compact Canine Rescue: Adoption process](https://compactcaninerescue.org/adoption-process/): the numbered steps from application to home.
- [Celia Hammond Animal Trust: Adopt a cat](https://www.celiahammond.org/adopt-a-cat/): a small UK trust on WordPress with rehoming by centre, a shop and clinic prices.

#### 172 · Environmental Action Group (`wild`)
**For:** local climate action groups, Transition towns, tree-planting groups and river and park friends' groups.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-event · single-event · archive-project · single-project · page-get-involved · page-green-plan · page-resources · page-donate · archive (news) · page-about
**Patterns (~40):** upcoming events list (tree planting, stream clean-up, seed swap, apple pressing, monthly meeting), event page with RSVP and "what to wear / bring", project groups (energy, food, nature, flood resilience, transport), local green plan (numbered actions, which are a real list here), home energy case studies, "get a tree" / request form, volunteering map, local suppliers directory, monthly update newsletter, leaflets download, annual report.
**Content model:** `event` (date, meeting point, RSVP link, kit list, accessibility), `project` (theme, contact, status), `resource` (type: leaflet/guide/case study, PDF).
**Plugins:** The Events Calendar (or companion `event` + Advanced Query Loop), Jetpack Forms (RSVP, tree requests), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (planting sites, volunteering map), Jetpack Newsletter, GiveWP.
**Signature:** a planting-season event calendar where each event needs an RSVP and says what to wear and where to meet (seen on: [Friends of Trees: Event calendar](https://friendsoftrees.org/event-calendar/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Numbered local green plan that the group can report progress against (seen on: [Climate Action Stokesley and Villages: 10 point green plan](https://climateactionstokesleyandvillages.org/10-point-green-plan/)).
- Home energy case studies from local households (seen on: [Climate Action Stokesley: Home energy case studies](https://climateactionstokesleyandvillages.org/energy/home-energy-case-studies/)).
- Volunteering map of all local projects (seen on: [Transition Town Totnes: Volunteering map](https://www.transitiontowntotnes.org/blog-article/volunteering-map)).
- "Get a tree" request form for residents' front gardens and streets (seen on: [Friends of Trees: Get a tree](https://friendsoftrees.org/get-a-tree/)).
- Rescheduled / weather-cancelled flag on events, set by one field (seen on: [EcoAction Arlington: Fall stream cleanup](https://www.ecoactionarlington.org/fall-stream-cleanup-2026/)).
- Printable leaflets page for stalls and letterboxes (seen on: [Climate Action Stokesley: Leaflets](https://climateactionstokesleyandvillages.org/casav-leaflets/)).
**Style: Field-guide naturalist print**
- Type: headings Manuale 700 at large sizes; body Newsreader 400/18px; Latin names, dates and grid refs Recursive Mono 400.
- Palette: bg #FAFAF5, text #1F2A1F, moss #3E6B35, river blue #2C6E8F, rosehip #B8412B (small accents only), line #CBD3C3.
- Layout: field-guide pages: two-column spreads with a plate (photo or drawing) and a caption column; events as a dated list with the kit list inline; projects as numbered plates. Thin double rules between sections.
- Imagery: members' own photos of planting days and species, plus scanned botanical drawings from out-of-copyright field guides; muddy boots over drone shots.
- Motion: none by default; a seasonal colour swap of the accent (spring green, autumn rust) set by date in PHP, not animated.
- Why it fits now: nature-led, editorial design has replaced "save the planet" stock imagery for UK rewilding and local climate groups ([Rewilding Britain](https://www.rewildingbritain.org.uk/)).
**Style variations:** Spring: moss accent, pale page · Autumn: rust accent, oat page · Estuary: river blue header
**Real-world basis:** [Friends of Trees: Event calendar](https://friendsoftrees.org/event-calendar/) · [Transition Town Totnes: Events](https://www.transitiontowntotnes.org/events) · [Climate Action Stokesley and Villages: Planting and keeping trees](https://climateactionstokesleyandvillages.org/nature/planting-and-keeping-trees/) · [EcoAction Arlington: Get involved](https://www.ecoactionarlington.org/get-involved/) · [Energy Garden: Events](https://www.energygarden.org.uk/events)
**Refs:**
- [Friends of Trees: Event calendar](https://friendsoftrees.org/event-calendar/): RSVP-required planting events with clear rules; the core event pattern.
- [Climate Action Stokesley and Villages: 10 point green plan](https://climateactionstokesleyandvillages.org/10-point-green-plan/): a small WordPress group with a green plan, events and themed project pages.
- [Transition Town Totnes: Events](https://www.transitiontowntotnes.org/events): the long-running Transition model: project groups, events and volunteering.

### XVII. Sport & fitness

<a id="173"></a>
#### 173 · Amateur Football Club (`fc`)
**For:** non-league, grassroots and fan-owned football clubs with several teams (men's, women's, reserves, veterans, youth) run by volunteers.
**Templates:** front-page · archive (news by team) · single (match report, preview) · page-fixtures-and-results (per team) · page-league-table · page-squad · page-coaching-staff · page-admission-prices · page-directions · page-membership · page-safeguarding · page-sponsorship · Woo shop
**Patterns (~50):** next match box (opponent, kick-off, ground, competition), fixtures and results table (date / match / kick-off or result / competition / ground / scorers / attendance), league table, squad list by position, coaching staff per team, match preview and match report templates, admission prices with concessions, directions and ground regulations, matchday FAQ for away fans, sponsorship packages (player, match, ball) with brochure, club shop, accountability / transparency page, community work (food bank collections).
**Content model:** `team` (name, league, season), `match` (date, kick-off, opponent, home/away, competition, ground, score, scorers, attendance, report link), `player` (position, squad number, team, season), `sponsor_package`.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (upcoming vs past matches per team, ordered by date meta), Query Filter (by team and season), WooCommerce (shirts, season tickets), Jetpack Forms (volunteer, sponsorship enquiry).
**Signature:** one fixtures-and-results table per team per season, with scorers and attendance filled in after each match and links back to earlier seasons (seen on: [Clapton CFC: Men's first team fixtures and results](https://www.claptoncfc.co.uk/calendar/clapton-cfc-mens-first-team-2026-2027-fixtures-and-results/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Admission prices with concessions and pay-what-you-can rules (seen on: [Clapton CFC: Admission prices](https://www.claptoncfc.co.uk/admission-prices-for-clapton-cfc-womens-and-mens-first-team-games/)).
- Fixture-change notice posts that also update the fixture table (seen on: [Clapton CFC: Two fixture changes for October](https://www.claptoncfc.co.uk/2026/09/26/two-fixture-changes-for-october-at-the-old-spotted-dog-ground/)).
- Matchday FAQ for first-time and away fans: kick-off, prices, parking, directions (seen on: [Dulwich Hamlet: Matchday FAQ](https://dulwichhamletfc.co.uk/club-info/matchday/matchday-faq)).
- Fan sponsorship tiers with a downloadable brochure (seen on: [Dulwich Hamlet: Fan sponsorship](https://dulwichhamletfc.co.uk/commercial/fan-sponsorship)).
- Named safeguarding officer page (seen on: [Dulwich Hamlet: Safeguarding](https://dulwichhamletfc.co.uk/club-info/club/safeguarding)).
- Accountability page for fan-owned clubs (seen on: [Clapton CFC: Accountability](https://www.claptoncfc.co.uk/accountability/)).
**Style: Matchday programme print**
- Type: headings Jockey One 400 (condensed) at large sizes; body Libre Franklin 400/18px; scores, kick-offs and squad numbers Big Shoulders Text 800 with tabular figures.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #111111, club colour 1 #C8102E (swappable), club colour 2 #0B2A5B, programme paper #F2EFE6 (surface for tables only), line #111111.
- Layout: the front page reads like a matchday programme cover: next match set huge (team names stacked, kick-off in numerals), then the last result, then news. Tables are full-width with heavy header rules; squad list as numbered rows, not player cards.
- Imagery: grainy terrace and pitch-side photos from the club's own photographers, fans and flags included; crest used flat; no stadium stock.
- Motion: none on scroll; the next-match box flips to "Full time" with the score on the day by date, not by animation.
- Why it fits now: fan-owned and non-league clubs have built their identity on print, flags and programme design, and their sites carry that dense, political look ([Clapton CFC](https://www.claptoncfc.co.uk/)).
**Style variations:** Home: club colour header · Away: second colour header · Floodlight: #111111 bg, white type
**Real-world basis:** [Clapton CFC: League table](https://www.claptoncfc.co.uk/2026-2027-essex-senior-football-league-table/) · [Clapton CFC: Men's first team squad](https://www.claptoncfc.co.uk/list/clapton-cfc-mens-first-team-squad-2026-27/) · [Clapton CFC: Fixtures and results](https://www.claptoncfc.co.uk/calendar/clapton-cfc-mens-first-team-2026-2027-fixtures-and-results/) · [Dulwich Hamlet: Matchday FAQ](https://dulwichhamletfc.co.uk/club-info/matchday/matchday-faq)
**Refs:**
- [Clapton CFC: Fixtures and results](https://www.claptoncfc.co.uk/calendar/clapton-cfc-mens-first-team-2026-2027-fixtures-and-results/): per-team season table with scorers and attendance; the core `match` model.
- [Clapton CFC: League table](https://www.claptoncfc.co.uk/2026-2027-essex-senior-football-league-table/): the league table as its own page, linked from every match.
- [Dulwich Hamlet: Fan sponsorship](https://dulwichhamletfc.co.uk/commercial/fan-sponsorship): small sponsorship packages that fund a non-league club.
