#### 192 · Overland Journey / Bikepacking Blog (`route`)
**For:** one rider or a couple documenting long bike or overland journeys and publishing the routes they ride for others to follow.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-journey · single-journey · single (dispatch post) · archive-route · single-route · page-planning · page-bike · page-kit · page-about · page-support
**Patterns (~40):** journey list in reverse chronological order (dates, countries, distance, one-paragraph summary), dispatch post header (day number, place, date), photo essay with section headings, route facts (distance / elevation gain / % unpaved / days / difficulty x/10) as a definition list, embedded route map with "Download GPX" button, route sections (Highlights / Must know / Camping / Food and water / Trail notes), bike specification list grouped by system (frame, drivetrain, brakes, wheels), kit list, planning guide index, newsletter and support links.
**Content model:** `journey` (start_date, end_date, countries, distance), posts linked to a journey, `route` (distance_km, elevation_m, unpaved_pct, days, difficulty_technical, difficulty_physical, gpx file, rwgps_url, best_months), taxonomy `country`.
**Plugins:** Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (start/finish and overnight markers); GPX stored in the Media Library with a bound Download button; optional Ride with GPS or Komoot iframe for the full track; Jetpack Newsletter.
**Signature:** a route page with a fixed facts bar (distance, elevation, percentage unpaved, difficulty out of 10), an embedded route map with a "Download GPX" button beneath, and Highlights / Must know / Camping / Food and water sections (seen on: [BIKEPACKING.com: Olney Overnighter](https://bikepacking.com/routes/olney-overnighter/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Difficulty split into technical and physical scores, with a one-line reason for each (seen on: [BIKEPACKING.com: Olney Overnighter](https://bikepacking.com/routes/olney-overnighter/)).
- Distances and climbing in both km/m and miles/ft, plus a "best months" and seasonal temperature note (seen on: [BIKEPACKING.com: Olney Overnighter](https://bikepacking.com/routes/olney-overnighter/)).
- A "how to use our routes" help page: downloading GPX, sending to a device, choosing map layers (seen on: [BIKEPACKING.com: using routes](https://bikepacking.com/plan/using-routes/)).
- Planning guide split into The basics / On the road / Bikes and gear / Reader questions (seen on: [Tom's Bike Trip: planning a bike tour](https://tomsbiketrip.com/planning-a-bike-tour/)).
- Affiliate-link disclosure pattern and ready-made privacy page for kit posts.
**Style: Documentary photo essay**
- Type: Headings: Brawler 700, 72–96px, sentence case; body: Brawler 400/19px at 66ch for long dispatches; facts and captions: JetBrains Mono 500 16px.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #141414 / accent #A16207 (dust ochre, only for facts and the GPX link) / surface #F1EEE8 / line #D9D4CB.
- Layout: single reading column with photos breaking out to full bleed; route pages switch to two columns (facts and sections left, map right, map sticky); the journey index is a plain ruled list, one line per trip with dates and km. Radii: 0 on photos and map, 4px on the GPX button.
- Imagery: 35mm-style colour photos at 3:2, sequences of 3–4 in a row like contact sheets; no filters, no text over images; the rider small in the landscape.
- Motion: photo sequences open in the core lightbox; the facts bar sticks under the nav; nothing animates on scroll; reduced-motion makes the lightbox instant.
- Why it fits now: the best cycling publications have moved to long, photo-led reportage with almost no interface chrome, e.g. [The Radavist: Korean Coasts Part II](https://theradavist.com/korean-coasts-part-ii).
**Style variations:** Desert: #EFE3CF bg, rust #9A3412 · Tundra: #0D1B1E bg, ice #CFE8EF text · Gravel: grey #E5E5E0, black mono
**Real-world basis:** [BIKEPACKING.com: Olney Overnighter](https://bikepacking.com/routes/olney-overnighter/), [BIKEPACKING.com: using our routes](https://bikepacking.com/plan/using-routes/), [Tom's Bike Trip: adventures](https://tomsbiketrip.com/adventures/), [Tom's Bike Trip: expedition bike specs](https://tomsbiketrip.com/toms-expedition-bike-specifications-gallery/), [The Radavist: Korean Coasts Part II](https://theradavist.com/korean-coasts-part-ii)
**Refs:**
- [BIKEPACKING.com: Olney Overnighter](https://bikepacking.com/routes/olney-overnighter/): the reference route page: facts, difficulty breakdown, map, GPX and practical sections.
- [Tom's Bike Trip: adventures](https://tomsbiketrip.com/adventures/): a full chronological list of journeys, each with a short summary linking into the blog (WordPress).
- [Tom's Bike Trip: expedition bike specifications](https://tomsbiketrip.com/toms-expedition-bike-specifications-gallery/): parts list grouped by system plus gallery, a page every touring blog needs.

#### 193 · Trail Guide / Hiking Routes (`trail`)
**For:** a local walking-guide author, footpath group or national park volunteer team publishing a library of walks or one long-distance path in stages.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-walk · single-walk · taxonomy-area · page-long-distance-path · single-stage · page-trail-status · page-safety-and-access · page-maps-and-books
**Patterns (~40):** walk facts header (start point, distance in miles and km, ascent, time, grade Easy / Moderate / Hard), map with route line and start pin, "Download GPX / KMZ" buttons, OS Explorer map reference, numbered photo sequence with captions along the route, stage list for a long-distance path (Chipping Campden to Broadway, 6 miles / 9.6 km, ascent and descent), "Continue to part 2" stage navigation, current diversions and closures list with dates, parking and public transport to the start, countryside code and access notes, walks-by-area index.
**Content model:** `walk` (start, grid_ref, distance, ascent, time, grade, gpx, kmz, os_map, lat/lng, parking), `stage` (path, order, from, to, distance, ascent, descent), `notice` (type diversion/closure, location, start_date, end_date), taxonomies `area` and `grade`.
**Plugins:** Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (start points and area map), Advanced Query Loop (active notices only, stages ordered by number), Query Filter (area / grade / distance band).
**Signature:** a trail status list of current diversions and closures, each with location and date range ("Temporary diversion from 29 May for at least 6 months near Birdlip"), shown on the path page and dropped automatically once the end date passes (seen on: [National Trails: Cotswold Way trail information](https://www.nationaltrail.co.uk/en_GB/trails/cotswold-way/trail-information/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- OS Explorer sheet number and scale on every walk, for people who still carry paper (seen on: [Walking Englishman: Dales Way part 1](https://www.walkingenglishman.com/dalesway1.htm)).
- Named start car park on each walk, with a "by bus or train" line under it (seen on: [Dartmoor Walks](https://www.dartmoorwalks.org.uk/walks.php)).
- Printable A4 walk card (facts, map, numbered directions) via a print stylesheet.
- Personalised A4 completion certificate for finishing a long-distance path, sold through WooCommerce (seen on: [The Trails Shop: Coast to Coast certificate](https://thetrailsshop.co.uk/collections/coast-to-coast/products/coast-to-coast-walk-completion-certificate)).
- Countryside and swimmer's code block (leave no trace, park considerately, know your limits) linked from every walk (seen on: [Outdoor Swimming Society: swimmer's code](https://www.outdoorswimmingsociety.com/outdoor-swimmers-code/)).
**Style: Japanese outdoor utility (waymark minimal)**
- Type: Headings: M PLUS 1 800 (a Japanese-designed sans for waymark clarity), 80–96px; body: M PLUS 1 400/18px; grid references and distances: M PLUS 1 Code 600 17px.
- Palette: bg #F5F3EE / text #1F2421 / waymark yellow #F2C230 (footpath) / bridleway blue #2B6CB0 / moss #4A6B3A / line #1F2421.
- Layout: walk pages lead with a boxed facts panel styled like a waymark post (arrow, colour, distance); full-width map beneath; the long-distance path page is a vertical numbered stage list like a route card; generous whitespace. Radii: 0 on panels and map, 2px on buttons, 50% on waymark arrows.
- Imagery: honest walker's-eye photos at 3:2 in numbered sequence, no drone shots; OS-style contour lines as a light SVG on section headers only.
- Motion: stages expand inline with the Details block; the map pans to the selected stage; no parallax; reduced-motion turns the map pan into a jump.
- Why it fits now: outdoor makers use restrained Japanese minimalism with signage cues instead of adrenaline imagery, e.g. [and wander](https://www.andwander.com/).
**Style variations:** Moorland: #3B3A2E bg, heather #B58DB6 accent · Chalk: white bg, flint grey type · Winter Hills: #E9EEF2 bg, navy text
**Real-world basis:** [National Trails: Cotswold Way route](https://www.nationaltrail.co.uk/en_GB/trails/cotswold-way/route/), [National Trails: Cotswold Way trail information](https://www.nationaltrail.co.uk/en_GB/trails/cotswold-way/trail-information/), [Walking Englishman: Dales Way part 1](https://www.walkingenglishman.com/dalesway1.htm), [Dartmoor Walks: walks](https://www.dartmoorwalks.org.uk/walks.php)
**Refs:**
- [National Trails: Cotswold Way trail information](https://www.nationaltrail.co.uk/en_GB/trails/cotswold-way/trail-information/): a live list of temporary and permanent diversions; the feature to make date-driven.
- [National Trails: Cotswold Way route](https://www.nationaltrail.co.uk/en_GB/trails/cotswold-way/route/): 15 numbered stages with distances in miles and km plus ascent and descent.
- [Walking Englishman: Dales Way part 1](https://www.walkingenglishman.com/dalesway1.htm): facts header, GPX and KMZ downloads, OS map reference and 20 numbered, captioned photos.

#### 194 · Wild Swimming & Sauna Community (`sauna`)
**For:** a community sauna CIC, mobile sauna club or lake/sea swim group with one to five sites and a membership scheme.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-location · single-location · page-book · page-first-time · page-memberships · page-concessions · page-private-hire · archive-event · page-gift-vouchers
**Patterns (~40):** location page (address with what3words, opening hours per day, last session time), weekly session timetable (standard, quiet, women-only, 50+, trans sauna, NHS slots), price table (off-peak / peak / weekend by duration), first-timer guide (what to bring, arrive 10 minutes early, hot / cold / rinse / rest / repeat, 2–3 rounds), sauna etiquette list, membership tiers with monthly and annual prices, concessions note, cancellation terms, capacity per sauna, medical note (check with your GP if pregnant or with a heart condition), swimmer's code, gift vouchers and multi-session packages, private hire enquiry.
**Content model:** `location` (address, what3words, hours per day, facilities, capacity, booking_url), `session` (location, weekday, start, end, type, audience), taxonomy `session_type`.
**Plugins:** Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (site locations), Jetpack Forms (private hire), optional WooCommerce (gift vouchers and packages) or an external booking embed.
**Signature:** a per-location weekly timetable that marks community sessions by audience (Trans Sauna, Mamma Swim, 50+ Women's Sauna, NHS timeslots) alongside standard sessions, with opening hours and last entry per day (seen on: [Community Sauna Baths: Hackney Wick](https://www.community-sauna.co.uk/locations/hackneywick)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- what3words address and "final session starts 20:00" on each location page (seen on: [Community Sauna Baths: Hackney Wick](https://www.community-sauna.co.uk/locations/hackneywick)).
- What-to-bring list with towel hire prices and a "no comments on bodies or tattoos" etiquette line (seen on: [Community Sauna Baths: first time](https://www.community-sauna.co.uk/first-time)).
- Weather policy: sessions run in most conditions, rescheduled for high wind or lightning, with the 24-hour cancellation fee spelled out (seen on: [Wild Sauna Club: how it works](https://www.wildsaunaclub.co.uk/howitworks)).
- Gift vouchers valid for a year plus shareable multi-session packages (seen on: [Wild Sauna Club: gift vouchers](https://www.wildsaunaclub.co.uk/gift-vouchers)).
- Concessions from £5 and a free guided look round before joining (seen on: [Saunas By The Sea: membership](https://www.saunasbythesea.co.uk/membership/)).
**Style: Warm Scandi minimal**
- Type: Headings: Afacad 700, 80–104px, sentence case; body: Karla 400/18px; timetable and prices: Karla 600 with tabular numerals.
- Palette: bg #F1F2EE (birch-grey) / text #1E2426 / fjord #2F5D6B (primary, cold plunge and swim) / ember #A8321C (hot sessions only) / surface #E2E5DF / line #B9BFB8.
- Layout: calm single column with a large today's-hours line under the logo ("Open today 7:00–21:30, last session 20:00") and a Book button fixed top right; timetable as a week grid with sessions as coloured bars; location pages as a two-column split (facts left, photos right). Radii: 6px on buttons, 0 on photos and timetable cells.
- Imagery: steam, timber and water photographed in low winter light with natural grain, 4:5 crops; people from behind or wrapped in towels, never posed; no stock spa imagery.
- Motion: the timetable day switcher uses the Interactivity API with a short crossfade; a slow steam-texture loop on the front-page photo that stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
- Why it fits now: the sauna revival has settled on warm, understated Nordic design with hours and booking up front, e.g. [Löyly Helsinki](https://www.loylyhelsinki.fi/).
**Style variations:** Polar Night: #11181C bg, ember accent · Salt: white bg, fjord blue type · Cedar: #6B4A2F bg, pale birch type
**Real-world basis:** [Community Sauna Baths: Hackney Wick](https://www.community-sauna.co.uk/locations/hackneywick), [Community Sauna Baths: first time](https://www.community-sauna.co.uk/first-time), [Wild Sauna Club: how it works](https://www.wildsaunaclub.co.uk/howitworks), [Saunas By The Sea: membership](https://www.saunasbythesea.co.uk/membership/), [Outdoor Swimming Society: swimmer's code](https://www.outdoorswimmingsociety.com/outdoor-swimmers-code/)
**Refs:**
- [Community Sauna Baths: Hackney Wick](https://www.community-sauna.co.uk/locations/hackneywick): hours, community sessions by audience, prices by duration and what3words on one location page.
- [Community Sauna Baths: first time](https://www.community-sauna.co.uk/first-time): the best first-timer page: what to bring, etiquette, hot/cold rounds, medical note.
- [Wild Sauna Club: how it works](https://www.wildsaunaclub.co.uk/howitworks): a mobile club explaining the Hot / Cold / Rinse / Rest cycle, capacity per site and cancellation terms.

### XX. Hobbies, clubs & fandom

<a id="195"></a>
#### 195 · Chess Club (`gambit`)
**For:** volunteer-run local chess clubs with a weekly club night, several league teams and a junior section.
**Templates:** front-page · page-joining · archive-tribe_events (club calendar) · single-tribe_events · archive-post (club news and match reports) · page-juniors · page-adult-beginners · page-tournaments · page-honours · page-fair-play
**Patterns (~40):** club night times block (day / time / room / what to bring), venue with bus and tube lines, membership fees table (standard / concession / junior / titled), "free taster night" note, team list by league (London League, Middlesex League), match report with score line and board results, tournament table (date / rounds / time control / sections / entry fee / byes), past champions roll by year, junior and girls' hour sessions, fair play and safeguarding notice
**Content model:** posts (match reports, club news) + The Events Calendar events with categories (club night, league match, junior hour, lecture). Companion `team` taxonomy on events and posts. `honour` meta table (year, name, title) for the champions roll.
**Plugins:** The Events Calendar.
**Signature:** a single club calendar with every club night, league fixture, junior hour and lecture, and "subscribe" links for Google Calendar, iCal and Outlook so members get fixtures in their own diary (seen on: [Hammersmith Chess Club: Events](https://hammerchess.co.uk/events/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Fees table with concession, women and girls, and titled-player rates, plus bank details for paying subs (seen on: [Hammersmith Chess Club: Joining](https://hammerchess.co.uk/joining/))
- "Come to a free Monday taster first" line on the joining page (seen on: [Hammersmith Chess Club: Joining](https://hammerchess.co.uk/joining/))
- Tournament listing that states time control, bye policy and member/non-member entry fee in the same row (seen on: [Marshall Chess Club: Upcoming tournaments](https://www.marshallchessclub.org/tournaments/upcoming))
- Sortable club champions roll going back to the club's founding (seen on: [Marshall Chess Club: Champions](https://www.marshallchessclub.org/club/champions))
- schema.org `Event` on fixtures and `SportsClub` on the home page, so "chess club near me" searches show the club night
**Style: Tournament-bulletin Swiss**
- Type: Headings: PT Sans Narrow 700, set tight to the face's own spacing; body: Source Serif 4 400 at 18px; data (time controls, scores, ratings): IBM Plex Mono 500 with tabular figures. Display 80px against 18px body.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF (paper) / text #111111 (ink) / accent #1F6B45 (tournament-hall baize green, used for links and the next fixture only) / surface #F1F1EE (light square) / line #111111 (1px hard rules) / muted #5B5B57
- Layout: 12-column grid with hard 1px rules between rows, like a printed pairing sheet. Home page leads with "Next club night" as a large dated line, then a two-column split of the fixtures list and the latest match report. Tables are the main component. No cards. Buttons get 0 radius; the fixture date block gets 2px. Nav is a plain text row: Club nights · Teams · Juniors · Tournaments · Join.
- Imagery: black-and-white reportage from real club nights: hands, clocks, scoresheets, cropped tight at 3:2. Board diagrams are drawn as flat 8×8 SVG grids in ink and baize green.
- Motion: none on scroll. Calendar month changes use a View Transition cross-fade of 150ms. Hovering a fixture row fills it with the light-square colour. All of it is off under prefers-reduced-motion.
- Why it fits now: club chess has boomed since 2020 and new members come from online play; a sharp, tabular Swiss look reads as "organised and serious" without the dated look of a 2008 club site. Style reference: [Swissted](https://www.swissted.com).
**Style variations:** Night Match: #121212 bg, baize #3F9C6B links · Scoresheet: carbon-copy blue #2B4C9B ink · Congress: bold red #B3261E fixture dates
**Real-world basis:** [Hammersmith Chess Club: Events](https://hammerchess.co.uk/events/) · [Hammersmith Chess Club: Joining](https://hammerchess.co.uk/joining/) · [Marshall Chess Club: Upcoming tournaments](https://www.marshallchessclub.org/tournaments/upcoming) · [Guildford Chess Club: Match reports](https://www.guildfordchessclub.com/?category=match-reports)
**Refs:**
- [Hammersmith Chess Club: Events](https://hammerchess.co.uk/events/): one calendar for club nights, league fixtures, junior and girls' hours, with month/list views and iCal/Google/Outlook export; this is The Events Calendar on WordPress
- [Marshall Chess Club: Upcoming tournaments](https://www.marshallchessclub.org/tournaments/upcoming): the dense tournament table: rounds, time control, sections, fees, byes, prize fund
- [Marshall Chess Club: Champions](https://www.marshallchessclub.org/club/champions): a century-long honours roll as a plain sortable table

<a id="196"></a>
#### 196 · TTRPG Campaign Site (`campaign`)
**For:** game masters running a long home or streamed campaign who want a public (or players-only) record of sessions, characters and the world.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-session · single-session · archive-character · single-character · page-world (setting primer) · page-house-rules · page-schedule · page-players-only (password-protected)
**Patterns (~35):** campaign index (sessions numbered, with sub-parts A/B/C), session recap with date, in-game date and "previously on" link, cast list (character / class / played by), party roster with retired and fallen characters, stream or play schedule block ("Sundays 7:30 pm"), campaign status line (ongoing / complete, level range), world primer with map image and gazetteer, house rules list, one-shots archive, GM essays linked from the sessions that inspired them
**Content model:** `session` (number, part, real date, in-game date, level range, video URL), `character` (class, ancestry, player, status: active / retired / dead), `campaign` taxonomy (so one site can hold several campaigns). Characters linked to sessions through a companion relation field.
**Plugins:** none. Players-only secrets use core password-protected posts.
**Signature:** a campaign index that lists every session in order with numbered sub-parts, the cast list of player characters with who plays them, and links to essays that grew out of specific sessions (seen on: [The Alexandrian: In the Shadow of the Spire](https://thealexandrian.net/in-the-shadow-of-the-spire)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Play schedule with the local time of the next session shown in the reader's own timezone (stream schedule stated on: [RogueWatson: Session recaps](https://roguewatson.com/tabletoproleplaying/))
- Campaign status and level range on each campaign ("levels 3–9, ongoing"), plus a "completed campaigns" shelf (seen on: [RogueWatson: Session recaps](https://roguewatson.com/tabletoproleplaying/))
- GM-only and players-only notes kept hidden until the reveal, using password-protected posts (the need is shown by permissioned secrets on: [Kanka](https://kanka.io/))
- "Previously on…" link at the top of each recap to the session before, and a printable one-page session sheet for the table
- Safety tools page (lines and veils, X-card) linked from the house rules
**Style: Antiquarian gazetteer**
- Type: Headings: IM Fell English SC 400 at up to 88px; body: Alegreya 400 at 19px with real italics for in-world quotes; data (session numbers, dates, levels): Alegreya Sans SC 500.
- Palette: bg #F7F4EC (laid paper, chosen because the site imitates a printed gazetteer) / text #1E1B16 (iron-gall ink) / accent #7A2E1F (rubrication red for session numbers and links) / surface #ECE6D6 / line #8C8272 / map ink #2E4A3F
- Layout: a book-like single column at 66ch with a wide left margin that holds session numbers and in-game dates as marginalia. The home page is a table of contents: current arc, then the numbered session list, then the cast. Character pages use a two-column "dramatis personae" layout. No cards. Rules are thin double lines, like a printed book. Map images break out to full width.
- Imagery: public-domain engravings and the GM's own scanned hand-drawn maps at full resolution, uncropped. Character portraits as small square woodcut-style crops. No AI art.
- Motion: none by default. Hovering a character name in a recap shows a small inline preview card (Interactivity API), and this is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
- Why it fits now: actual-play and "campaign journal" culture keeps growing, and readers now expect the look of a real book, not a fantasy video-game UI. Style reference: [The Public Domain Review](https://publicdomainreview.org).
**Style variations:** Grimoire: #14110D bg, candle #E2B45A accent · Sci-fi Log: slate #1D2530, amber #F2A23A · Pulp: newsprint #EFE8D8, red #C4271B
**Real-world basis:** [The Alexandrian: In the Shadow of the Spire](https://thealexandrian.net/in-the-shadow-of-the-spire) · [RogueWatson: Session recaps](https://roguewatson.com/tabletoproleplaying/) · [Kanka: campaign manager](https://kanka.io/)
**Refs:**
- [The Alexandrian: In the Shadow of the Spire](https://thealexandrian.net/in-the-shadow-of-the-spire): the model campaign index: 48+ numbered sessions with sub-parts, PC cast list with players, GM essays tied to sessions
- [RogueWatson: Session recaps](https://roguewatson.com/tabletoproleplaying/): several campaigns on one page, each with status, level range and session titles with video links
- [Kanka: home](https://kanka.io/): shows which entity types players actually track (characters, locations, organisations, timelines, maps) and hidden-until-revealed secrets

<a id="197"></a>
#### 197 · Fan Site / Fan Wiki (`fandom`)
**For:** an individual fan or small fan community keeping a long-running site about one author, series or show.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-post (news) · archive-by-date (month/year archive) · single-post · archive-work (books/episodes) · single-work · archive-entry (characters, places) · single-entry · page-annotations · page-contribute
**Patterns (~40):** news river with date, author and category, month-by-month archive going back years, bibliography / episode guide in publication order, character entry with infobox (race, occupation, first appearance, appears in), places index, annotations by book (page reference + note), fan creators and fan-site listings, spoiler notice block, "how to contribute / corrections" block, licence note (CC BY-NC-SA)
**Content model:** posts (news) + `work` (type: book/episode/film, order, year), `entry` (type: character/place/thing, infobox meta), `annotation` (linked work, page or timestamp, note, contributor). Companion relation field links entries to the works they appear in.
**Plugins:** Query Filter (filter entries by work and type).
**Signature:** annotations organised per book, each a numbered list of page references with the note and who contributed it (seen on: [L-Space Web: The Annotated Pratchett File](https://www.lspace.org/books/apf/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Character infobox that lists every work the character appears in, auto-built from the relation field (seen on: [Discworld & Terry Pratchett Wiki: Rincewind](https://wiki.lspace.org/Rincewind))
- Complete month-by-month archive plus a subject index, so twenty years of posts stay findable (seen on: [The Leaky Cauldron: Archives](https://www.the-leaky-cauldron.org/archives))
- Community directory of societies, podcasts and other fan sites (seen on: [Sherlockian.net](https://www.sherlockian.net))
- Spoiler notice block that states which book or episode the page spoils up to
- Visible licence and "how to send a correction" line on every entry (licence stated on: [Discworld & Terry Pratchett Wiki](https://wiki.lspace.org/Main_Page))
**Style: Web 1.0 revival, done carefully**
- Type: Headings: Righteous 400 at up to 96px; body: Atkinson Hyperlegible 400 at 18px; badges and navigation: Silkscreen 400 at 15px (pixel face, used only for small interface labels).
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #101010 / link #0033CC (classic hypertext blue, underlined) / visited #551A8B / surface #FFF4B8 (sticky-note yellow for spoiler and notice blocks) / line #101010
- Layout: a left-hand sidebar of links like an old homepage, with the main column at 68ch. The home page is a "what's new" log with dates, then a big index of works. Entries use a right-floated infobox table with 1px borders. 88×31 "button" badges for linked fan sites. Underlined links everywhere. Radius 0 everywhere except badges.
- Imagery: book covers and screen grabs at their real proportions with plain 1px borders. The owner's own photos of convention visits. No stock photos.
- Motion: none. Only a visited-link colour change and an underline-thickness change on hover.
- Why it fits now: personal, hand-made fan sites are back (Neocities, IndieWeb, the move away from ad-heavy wiki farms), and fans value the look of a site run by one person. Style reference: [Cameron's World](https://www.cameronsworld.net).
**Style variations:** Geocities Night: #000033 bg, #FFFF66 links · Library Card: #F2EEE3 bg, stamp red #B22222 · Zine: photocopy grey #E6E6E6, black
**Real-world basis:** [L-Space Web: The Annotated Pratchett File](https://www.lspace.org/books/apf/) · [Discworld & Terry Pratchett Wiki: Rincewind](https://wiki.lspace.org/Rincewind) · [The Leaky Cauldron: Archives](https://www.the-leaky-cauldron.org/archives) · [Sherlockian.net](https://www.sherlockian.net)
**Refs:**
- [L-Space Web: The Annotated Pratchett File](https://www.lspace.org/books/apf/): annotations organised by book, a community-maintained reference running for decades
- [Discworld & Terry Pratchett Wiki: Rincewind](https://wiki.lspace.org/Rincewind): the character entry format: infobox, sections, list of book appearances
- [The Leaky Cauldron: Archives](https://www.the-leaky-cauldron.org/archives): a WordPress fan site with a month-by-month archive back to 2000 plus a subject index

#### 198 · Collector's Catalogue (`collection`)
**For:** a private collector (typewriters, cameras, calculators, radios, pens) who documents each object properly and wants others to find it.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-object · single-object · taxonomy-maker · taxonomy-decade · page-serial-numbers · page-wanted · page-about-the-collection · page-articles
**Patterns (~35):** object record header (maker / model / year / serial number), specification table, condition and restoration notes, provenance ("found at…, acquired…"), photo set (front, back, detail, serial plate), sample or specimen image (e.g. typeface specimen), serial-number dating table by maker, index by maker and decade, wanted list, "last edited" line, related objects
**Content model:** `object` (maker, model, year, serial, condition, acquired date, source, status: in collection / sold / on loan), `maker` and `decade` taxonomies, `serial_range` table meta on maker terms for dating.
**Plugins:** Query Filter (maker, decade, type, status).
**Signature:** a full object record per item: serial number, year, typeface specimen, colour, condition notes, acquisition story, photos, owner and "last edited" date (seen on: [Typewriter Database: 1959 Olympia SM3](https://typewriterdatabase.com/1959-olympia-sm3.28698.typewriter)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Wanted list, with the exact era and models the collector is still looking for (seen on: [Old Calculator Web Museum](https://www.oldcalculatormuseum.com/))
- Serial-number lookup page that dates a machine from its serial range (seen on: [Lockhart's List](https://lockhartslist.com/))
- "Status" flag on each object: in collection, sold, on loan, for trade
- Printable object label (A6) with maker, model, year and a short URL for fairs and shelves
- schema.org `Product`/`CreativeWork` markup and alt text written as condition descriptions, for accessibility and search
**Style: Museum register**
- Type: Headings: Instrument Sans 600 at up to 84px; body: Newsreader 400 at 18px; catalogue data (serials, accession numbers, years): Martian Mono 400 with tabular figures.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #141414 / accent #0E5A8A (archive-folder blue for links and accession numbers) / surface #F3F3F1 / line #CFCFCB / status red #A12B2B (sold / wanted only)
- Layout: the index is a dense table-first grid: small square photos in a strict 6-column contact sheet, or a list view with maker / model / year / serial columns. Object pages put the spec table on the left and a large photo sequence on the right. Numbering follows the collection's real accession numbers. Photos get 0 radius; filter chips get 3px.
- Imagery: studio photos on a plain grey sweep, same angle for every object, square 1:1 for the index and 4:3 for records. Detail shots of serial plates and specimens at 100% crop.
- Motion: a View Transition morph from the index thumbnail to the object's lead photo. Nothing else, and none under prefers-reduced-motion.
- Why it fits now: museums and collectors are publishing collections as open, searchable records, and the calm catalogue look signals care and accuracy. Style reference: [Are.na](https://www.are.na).
**Style variations:** Workshop: #1A1A18 bg, brass #C9A227 data · Specimen: white, black, one red #D2231E · Ledger: pale green #EEF3EA, ink #1C2A1F
**Real-world basis:** [Typewriter Database: 1959 Olympia SM3](https://typewriterdatabase.com/1959-olympia-sm3.28698.typewriter) · [Lockhart's List](https://lockhartslist.com/) · [Old Calculator Web Museum](https://www.oldcalculatormuseum.com/) · [Old Calculator Web Museum: Friden EC-130](https://www.oldcalculatormuseum.com/friden130.html)
**Refs:**
- [Typewriter Database: 1959 Olympia SM3](https://typewriterdatabase.com/1959-olympia-sm3.28698.typewriter): the object record: serial, year, typeface specimen, condition, acquisition story, owner
- [Old Calculator Web Museum: Friden EC-130](https://www.oldcalculatormuseum.com/friden130.html): a long single-object page with serial, history, specifications and 20+ photos
- [Lockhart's List: home](https://lockhartslist.com/): serial-number lookup, models, variants and a timeline for one maker

#### 199 · Naturalists' Society / Birding Group (`fieldnotes`)
**For:** county bird clubs and local natural history societies with field meetings, indoor talks, recording and a journal.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-sighting · single-sighting · page-submit-sighting · archive-event (field meetings and talks) · single-event · page-sections (botany / birds / insects / geology) · page-recording · page-membership · page-publications
**Patterns (~40):** recent sightings list (date / species / location / observer), "submit a sighting" form, field meeting card (date, leader, meeting point, grid reference, what3words, what to bring), indoor talk listing, sections index (botany, ornithology, invertebrates, geology), recording guidelines (species, date, grid reference, count, breeding code), rare species description form link, guided walks for non-members, journal and annual report archive, membership rates, surveys needing volunteers
**Content model:** `sighting` (species, count, date, site, grid ref, observer, sensitive flag), `event` (type: field meeting / talk / survey; leader, meeting point, grid ref, w3w, what to bring, booking), `section` taxonomy, `publication` (year, PDF).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (sighting submissions and bookings), Advanced Query Loop (upcoming vs past meetings), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (meeting points).
**Signature:** a moderated "recent sightings" log where members submit date, species, location and notes, shown newest first on the home page with "view all sightings" (seen on: [Sussex Ornithological Society: Recent sightings](https://sos.org.uk/recent-sightings/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Field meeting pages with leader, meeting point, OS grid reference, what3words and "bring a hand lens" kit list (seen on: [Bristol Naturalists' Society: Woodland Bryophytes](https://bristolnats.org.uk/events/woodland-bryophytes/))
- Sensitive-species rule on the submission form: no Schedule 1 breeding birds, with sightings held back or site blurred (seen on: [Sussex Ornithological Society: Recent sightings](https://sos.org.uk/recent-sightings/))
- Guided walks for non-members with duration, terrain and public transport notes (seen on: [Sussex Ornithological Society: Join a walk](https://sos.org.uk/about/our-work-with-people/join-a-walk/))
- Recording guidelines page that tells members how to send records on to BirdTrack or the county recorder (seen on: [Sussex Ornithological Society: Reporting guidelines](https://sos.org.uk/about/our-work-with-birds/general-bird-records-reporting-guidelines/))
- Journal back-issues as downloadable PDFs by year, and a plain-language "new to birding" page
**Style: Field-guide editorial**
- Type: Headings: Faustina 600 at up to 88px; body: Literata 400 at 18px; Latin binomials in Literata italic as the naming convention requires; data (grid refs, dates, counts): Recursive Mono 400.
- Palette: bg #FBFAF5 (field-notebook paper, chosen because the look is a naturalist's notebook) / text #1B2118 / accent #3E6B35 (lichen green for links and "new" sightings) / surface #EEF0E6 / line #B9BFAE / plate ochre #B8862B (used only on illustration plates)
- Layout: two columns on the home page: a narrow, dated sightings log on the left like a notebook margin, and the next field meeting as a large block on the right with a map. Section pages (botany, birds, insects) open with a full-width plate illustration. Events are rows, not cards. Inputs get 2px radius; images 0.
- Imagery: members' own record photos, credited, at natural aspect ratios. Public-domain natural history plates (e.g. from the Biodiversity Heritage Library) as section headers. No stock wildlife.
- Motion: the map on an event page only loads its tiles when scrolled into view. No other animation. prefers-reduced-motion respected.
- Why it fits now: nature writing and citizen science are growing, and a restrained editorial look is what current nature publishing uses. Style reference: [Emergence Magazine](https://emergencemagazine.org).
**Style variations:** Dawn Chorus: pale sky #EAF0F4, heron grey #4A5A63 · Heathland: #F6F1E9, heather #6E3F6B · Estuary: mud #3A342C bg, reed #D9C98F text accents
**Real-world basis:** [Sussex Ornithological Society: Recent sightings](https://sos.org.uk/recent-sightings/) · [Bristol Naturalists' Society: Events](https://bristolnats.org.uk/events/) · [Bristol Naturalists' Society: Woodland Bryophytes](https://bristolnats.org.uk/events/woodland-bryophytes/) · [London Natural History Society](https://www.lnhs.org.uk)
**Refs:**
- [Sussex Ornithological Society: Recent sightings](https://sos.org.uk/recent-sightings/): moderated sightings log with submit button and sensitive-species guidance, on WordPress
- [Bristol Naturalists' Society: Woodland Bryophytes](https://bristolnats.org.uk/events/woodland-bryophytes/): the ideal field meeting page: leader, meeting point, grid ref, what3words, kit, booking form
- [Sussex Ornithological Society: Join a walk](https://sos.org.uk/about/our-work-with-people/join-a-walk/): walks listed with site, leader contact, meeting point, duration and terrain

#### 200 · Model Railway Club (`gauge`)
**For:** model railway clubs with clubrooms, a few club layouts that travel to exhibitions, and an annual show of their own.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-layout · single-layout · page-exhibition · page-previous-exhibitions · archive-tribe_events (club nights, running nights, lectures) · page-membership · page-library · page-visit-us
**Patterns (~40):** club nights block (Tuesdays 7–10 pm, visitors welcome), layouts roster (name / scale and gauge / era / region), layout page (what it models, size, how it travels, builders, exhibitions attended), annual exhibition block (date, venue, hours, admission, free parking, refreshments), layouts attending list (name / scale / owner or club), traders attending list, previous exhibitions archive by year, junior section, library additions list, "work in progress" build log posts
**Content model:** `layout` (scale, gauge, era, region modelled, size, transport, status: operational / under construction / retired, exhibitions attended), `exhibition` (year, date, venue, admission, layouts attending as relation, traders list), posts for build logs. Events via The Events Calendar.
**Plugins:** The Events Calendar, Advanced Query Loop (upcoming exhibition vs previous years).
**Signature:** a layouts roster where each layout carries scale, era and region, linking to a full page with what it models, how big it is, its history and the shows it has attended (seen on: [The Model Railway Club: Layouts](https://themodelrailwayclub.org/layouts/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Exhibition block with admission prices, under-16s free, opening hours, free parking and "refreshments for sale" (seen on: [Letchworth Model Railway Society: Annual exhibition](https://www.letchworthmrs.org.uk/index.php/annual-exhibition/))
- "Layouts attending" and "traders attending" lists per show year, with "more to be confirmed" state (seen on: [Letchworth MRS: 2019 layouts attending](https://www.letchworthmrs.org.uk/index.php/home/2019-annual-exhibition/2019-layouts-attending/))
- "Visitors welcome, come along and introduce yourself" note on running nights (seen on: [The Model Railway Club: Track running nights](https://themodelrailwayclub.org/events/category/track-running-nights/))
- Exhibition-manager info on each layout (size, crew needed, fits in a transit van) so other shows can book it (seen on: [The Model Railway Club: Copenhagen Fields](https://themodelrailwayclub.org/layouts/copenhagen-fields/))
- Step-free access and quiet-hour note on the exhibition page, and schema.org `Event` for the show
**Style: Railway signage and timetable**
- Type: Headings: Mada 800 at up to 96px (a signage-clear sans); body: Public Sans 400 at 18px; times, scales and layout codes: Overpass Mono 600.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #0F1A2A / accent #1D4F91 (rail blue for links and headers) / surface #EEF2F7 / line #0F1A2A / warning #F2B705 (only for "this weekend" and "cancelled")
- Layout: timetable logic. The home page opens with a departure-board style block: next club night, next exhibition, next running night, each as one row with time and place. Layout roster below as a two-column list with a photo and a data strip (scale · era · region). Station-sign headers: white type on a solid rail-blue band with square ends. Buttons 0 radius; photos 0.
- Imagery: honest, well-lit photos of the layouts at eye level (the "rail-level" view), wide 16:9 panoramas for layout pages, plus scanned exhibition flyers.
- Motion: none on scroll. Rows on the departure-board block change background on hover. prefers-reduced-motion respected.
- Why it fits now: transit identity (Vignelli's NYCTA manual, British Rail's Double Arrow) is widely reprinted and loved, and it is the visual language this audience already knows. Style reference: [Standards Manual](https://standardsmanual.com).
**Style variations:** GWR: chocolate #5A3A22 and cream #EFE3C8 (carriage livery) · Night Mail: #0F1A2A bg, signal yellow #F2B705 · Narrow Gauge: sage #6F8A6A, black
**Real-world basis:** [The Model Railway Club: Layouts](https://themodelrailwayclub.org/layouts/) · [The Model Railway Club: Copenhagen Fields](https://themodelrailwayclub.org/layouts/copenhagen-fields/) · [Letchworth Model Railway Society: Annual exhibition](https://www.letchworthmrs.org.uk/index.php/annual-exhibition/) · [Wyre Forest MRC: The club](http://wyreforestmrc.com/index-a.htm)
**Refs:**
- [The Model Railway Club: Layouts](https://themodelrailwayclub.org/layouts/): layout roster with scale, era and region per layout, on WordPress
- [The Model Railway Club: Copenhagen Fields](https://themodelrailwayclub.org/layouts/copenhagen-fields/): the layout page: what it models, size, 40-year history, techniques, exhibitions
- [Letchworth Model Railway Society: Annual exhibition](https://www.letchworthmrs.org.uk/index.php/annual-exhibition/): show page with date, venue, prices, layouts and traders attending

#### 201 · Amateur Astronomy Society (`orbit`)
**For:** local astronomical societies with a small observatory, monthly talks and weather-dependent public stargazing nights.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-event (talks, stargazing, telescope clinics) · single-event · page-observatory · page-observing (what's up, observing sites) · page-membership · page-schools-and-groups · page-faq · page-publications
**Patterns (~35):** next stargazing night with its go/no-go status, formal talk listing (speaker, title, venue), observatory page (telescopes, season, opening times), "what's up this month" sky notes, observing sites list with directions, telescope clinic ("bring your telescope"), what to bring (warm clothes, torch, binoculars), visiting rules (red light only, no flash), group and school visits, newsletter/journal archive
**Content model:** `event` (type: stargazing / talk / members' observing / clinic; weather status: scheduled / decision on the day / on / cancelled; ticket URL; age limit; access notes), `site` (observing locations with coordinates), posts for sky notes.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (upcoming events), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (observatory and dark-sky sites). Tickets link out to Eventbrite.
**Signature:** a weather status on each public stargazing night, "decision at 10:00 on the day", then On or Cancelled (cloud), with tickets only released if the forecast is good (seen on: [Bristol Astronomical Society: Come Stargazing](https://bristolastrosoc.org.uk/events/come-stargazing-48/)). Implemented as a companion status field bound to a badge on the event and on the home page.
**Nice-to-haves:**
- "Not suitable for under-8s", step-free access and "park at X, not at the observatory" notes on each public night (seen on: [Bristol Astronomical Society: Come Stargazing](https://bristolastrosoc.org.uk/events/come-stargazing-48/))
- Visiting rules: red light only, no flash photography, leave light-up shoes at home (seen on: [ASGH: Public observing](https://asgh.org/public-observing/))
- Observatory season and hours ("October to April, Fri and Sat 8–10 pm, clear skies only") with the telescopes described (seen on: [Hampstead Observatory](https://www.hampsteadscience.ac.uk/observatory.html))
- Telescope-buying advice page for beginners and a group/school visit request form (seen on: [Bristol Astronomical Society: Observing](https://bristolastrosoc.org.uk/observing/))
- A "red light" reading mode for the observing pages, for use at the eyepiece
**Style: Star-atlas cartographic with dithered photos**
- Type: Headings: Tomorrow 600 at up to 90px; body: IBM Plex Sans 400 at 18px; coordinates, times and magnitudes: IBM Plex Mono 400.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #10151F / accent #2A4B8D (chart-blue for links and constellation lines) / surface #EEF1F7 / line #C9D2E3 / status red #C8102E (cancelled only, always with a text label)
- Layout: star-chart grid: thin coordinate lines on headers only, events as a vertical timeline of dated rows with the status label at the right edge. The observatory page leads with a large dithered photo of the dome and the telescope specs as a table. The home page order: next public night and its status, then talks, then this month's sky notes. Buttons 0 radius; status labels 2px.
- Imagery: members' astrophotography shown full-size and uncropped with capture data (scope, exposure) in the caption. Decorative photos (dome, members at the eyepiece) are 1-bit dithered to keep pages light.
- Motion: none on scroll. The red-light mode switches colours instantly. prefers-reduced-motion respected.
- Why it fits now: dithered, low-energy images have become a recognised web look, and they suit a society that cares about dark skies and low light. Style reference: [Low-tech Magazine (solar)](https://solar.lowtechmagazine.com).
**Style variations:** Red Light: #0B0B0B bg, #C8102E text (a real observing need, not decoration) · Blueprint: #13294B bg, #E8EEF7 lines · Almanac: #F4F1E8 paper, black ink
**Real-world basis:** [Bristol Astronomical Society: Come Stargazing](https://bristolastrosoc.org.uk/events/come-stargazing-48/) · [Bristol Astronomical Society: Observing](https://bristolastrosoc.org.uk/observing/) · [Hampstead Observatory](https://www.hampsteadscience.ac.uk/observatory.html) · [ASGH: Public observing](https://asgh.org/public-observing/)
**Refs:**
- [Bristol Astronomical Society: Come Stargazing](https://bristolastrosoc.org.uk/events/come-stargazing-48/): weather-dependent public night: tickets released on the morning, what to bring, age and access notes
- [Hampstead Observatory: observatory page](https://www.hampsteadscience.ac.uk/observatory.html): season, hours, clear-sky rule, telescopes and booking in one page
- [ASGH: Public observing](https://asgh.org/public-observing/): cancellation notice by 6 pm, red-light etiquette and access notes

#### 202 · Beekeeping Association (`hive`)
**For:** local and county beekeeping associations with a training apiary, beginner courses, a swarm service and members selling local honey.
**Templates:** front-page · page-swarms (is it a swarm? + collectors) · page-what-bee-is-this · page-courses · archive-event (apiary meetings, winter talks) · single-event · page-local-honey · page-asian-hornet · page-membership · page-newsletters
**Patterns (~40):** "Found a swarm?" help block with identification triage, what bee is this (honey bee / bumblebee / solitary / wasp / hornet / hoverfly with photos), swarm collectors list by area, beginners' course dates and fees, apiary meeting listing, "this month in the apiary" and "this month in flower" notes, local honey directory (beekeeper, area, jar sizes and prices), Asian hornet reporting block, membership rates, newsletter archive
**Content model:** `collector` (name, areas covered, phone, availability), `honey_seller` (beekeeper, postcode area, how to buy, jar sizes, prices), `event` (type: apiary meeting / talk / course), posts for monthly notes.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (course enquiries, swarm reports), Advanced Query Loop (upcoming meetings).
**Signature:** a swarm help page that first helps the public check it really is a honey bee swarm (with a photo guide to lookalikes), then lists local volunteer collectors by area (seen on: [BBKA: Swarm collection](https://www.bbka.org.uk/swarm-collection) and [Michigan Beekeepers Association: Swarm list](https://michiganbees.org/Swarm-List)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Local honey directory by postcode area with jar sizes, prices and where to collect (seen on: [London Beekeepers' Association: Honey](https://www.lbka.org.uk/honey.html))
- "Courses for this year are full, next run April/May" state with an enquiry email (seen on: [London Beekeepers' Association: Courses](https://www.lbka.org.uk/courses.html))
- "It is not customary to pay for swarm removal" note and a disclaimer about collectors (seen on: [Michigan Beekeepers Association: Swarm list](https://michiganbees.org/Swarm-List))
- Photo ID guide with labelled species and sex so the public can tell bees from wasps and hoverflies (seen on: [BBKA: What bee is this?](https://www.bbka.org.uk/what-bee-is-this))
- Printable swarm-season poster (A4) for noticeboards, and a seasonal "swarm season" notice that runs May to July
**Style: Hand-drawn allotment noticeboard**
- Type: Headings: Shantell Sans 700 at up to 84px; body: Karla 400 at 18px; handwritten annotations on diagrams: Kalam 400 (small, used only on labels in illustrations).
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #2A1C0B (propolis brown) / accent #D99A00 (honey amber for links and "swarm" action) / surface #FFF6DB (wax) / line #2A1C0B / leaf #4F7A3A (seasonal "in flower" notes)
- Layout: asymmetric: the swarm help block always sits top-left as a big bordered panel with a phone number. Monthly notes run as a two-column almanac ("in the apiary" / "in flower"). Honey directory as a plain table grouped by area. Hand-drawn hexagon rules divide sections, but never as a background pattern. Buttons 4px; photo 0; panels 0 with a 2px ink border.
- Imagery: close, sharp photos of real frames, swarms on branches and members in suits, cropped square or 4:5. Simple hand-drawn line illustrations of hive parts and bee anatomy with Kalam labels.
- Motion: none. Hovering a species in the ID guide swaps in a second photo (Interactivity API), off under prefers-reduced-motion.
- Why it fits now: hand-drawn, friendly brand illustration has become a mainstream way to look human and not corporate, and it suits a volunteer association that speaks to the public. Style reference: [Oatly](https://www.oatly.com).
**Style variations:** Heather Honey: #3B2440 bg, amber #E3A21A · Beeswax: #FFF2C6 bg, brown ink · Winter Cluster: grey #E9E7E2, black, amber accents
**Real-world basis:** [BBKA: Swarm collection](https://www.bbka.org.uk/swarm-collection) · [BBKA: What bee is this?](https://www.bbka.org.uk/what-bee-is-this) · [Michigan Beekeepers Association: Swarm list](https://michiganbees.org/Swarm-List) · [London Beekeepers' Association: Honey](https://www.lbka.org.uk/honey.html)
**Refs:**
- [BBKA: Swarm collection](https://www.bbka.org.uk/swarm-collection): honey bee vs other bees triage, then a postcode finder for a local collector
- [Michigan Beekeepers Association: Swarm list](https://michiganbees.org/Swarm-List): collectors listed by county with city and phone, self-managed by members
- [London Beekeepers' Association: Honey](https://www.lbka.org.uk/honey.html): members' honey directory by area with jar prices and how to buy

#### 203 · Ham Radio Club (`callsign`)
**For:** local amateur radio clubs and societies with a club callsign, weekly on-air nets, field days and licence training.
**Templates:** front-page · page-nets · archive-report (field days, special events) · single-report · archive-event · page-training · page-logbook-and-qsl · page-special-event-stations · page-membership · page-web-sdrs
**Patterns (~40):** nets table (day / net name / time / frequency / mode / net control callsign), club callsign header with QRZ link, special event stations list (callsign / award number / operator), field day report (location, stations, antennas, bands, contacts), "on the air" events (Mills on the Air, Churches on the Air), licence training (Foundation / Intermediate / Full) with exam info, QSL policy (bureau, direct, eQSL, LoTW), members' ads (equipment for sale), web SDR links, repeater info, membership form PDF
**Content model:** `net` (day, time UTC, frequency, mode, net control), `report` (event type, date, callsign used, bands, QSO count), `station` (callsign, award ref, operator). Events via companion Event CPT.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (upcoming events and recent reports).
**Signature:** the weekly nets schedule as a table: day, net name, time, frequency (with "± QRM"), mode and net control callsign (seen on: [RSARS: Radio nets](https://rsars.org.uk/radio-nets/)). The theme adds a UTC/local time toggle using the Interactivity API.
**Nice-to-haves:**
- QSL card policy in plain words: no paper cards collected, cards via bureau on request, logs uploaded to QRZ, LoTW and eQSL (seen on: [CDARC: Logbook](https://www.cdarc.org.uk/logbook/) (unverified))
- Special event stations list with callsign, award number and who operates it (seen on: [RSARS: Special event stations](https://rsars.org.uk/special-event-stations/))
- Link to the national society's club finder and affiliation status in the footer (seen on: [RSGB: Clubs](https://rsgb.org/main/clubs/))
- Downloadable membership form PDF and constitution, and a members' ads page for used equipment
- A "new to radio" page in plain language: what the Foundation licence lets you do and when the next course runs
**Style: Terminal log and QSL card**
- Type: Headings: VT323 400 at up to 88px (a terminal-bitmap monospace); body: Mona Sans 400 at 18px; frequencies, callsigns and times: VT323 at text size.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #111111 / accent #D2481F (QSL-card orange for links and the club callsign) / surface #F2F2EF / line #111111 / band green #2F6B3A (used only in the nets table for "on air now")
- Layout: log-book structure. The home page is a single wide table of "this week on air" (nets and events), then the latest report, then training. Callsigns set large like on a QSL card. Report pages open with a data strip (date · callsign · bands · QSOs). Photos in a strict 3-column grid. Everything 0 radius except inputs (2px).
- Imagery: real field day photos (masts, antennas, portable stations) in natural colour, and scans of the club's own QSL cards, front and back, at card proportions (140×90).
- Motion: none on scroll. "On air now" is a static text label driven by the nets schedule, not a pulsing dot. prefers-reduced-motion respected.
- Why it fits now: monospace, text-first sites have become a sign of craft among technical hobbyists, and they suit a hobby built on logs and callsigns. Style reference: [Hundred Rabbits](https://100r.co).
**Style variations:** Shack Night: #141414 bg, #F2E7C9 text, orange callsigns · Field Day: khaki #D8D2B8, black · Morse: white, black, no colour
**Real-world basis:** [RSARS: Radio nets](https://rsars.org.uk/radio-nets/) · [RSARS: Special event stations](https://rsars.org.uk/special-event-stations/) · [RSGB: Clubs](https://rsgb.org/main/clubs/) · [CDARC: Logbook](https://www.cdarc.org.uk/logbook/) (unverified)
**Refs:**
- [RSARS: Radio nets](https://rsars.org.uk/radio-nets/): the nets table: day, net name, time, frequency and net control callsign, on WordPress.com
- [RSARS: Special event stations](https://rsars.org.uk/special-event-stations/): callsigns, award numbers and operators in a scannable list
- [RSGB: Clubs](https://rsgb.org/main/clubs/): what a club site should link to: club finder, affiliation, club of the year, events pack

<a id="204"></a>
#### 204 · Cosplay / Prop Maker (`prop`)
**For:** a cosplayer or prop and armour maker who shows builds, sells patterns and templates, and appears at conventions.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-build (portfolio) · single-build · page-free-templates · Woo archive-product (patterns shop) · Woo single-product · Woo cart · Woo checkout · page-events (convention appearances) · page-commissions · page-faq
**Patterns (~40):** portfolio grid filtered by franchise, build log post (character, source game/film, materials list, process by stage, tools, collaborators, time taken), free templates library (prop name / franchise / format PDF-STL-SVG / tutorial link), pattern product card (digital PDF, price, what's included), pattern bundles, convention appearances (event / city / dates / role: guest, judge, workshop), commissions open/closed notice, usage terms for templates, tutorial books, tools and materials list
**Content model:** `build` (character, franchise, materials, tools, hours, collaborators, pattern link), `franchise` taxonomy, `appearance` (convention, city, dates, role), WooCommerce downloadable products for patterns.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce (downloadable products), Query Filter (portfolio by franchise).
**Signature:** a templates library where each prop or armour piece has a free download (PDF, SVG or STL), a link to its tutorial, and clear usage terms, alongside paid PDF patterns and bundles (seen on: [Punished Props: Free blueprint files](https://www.punishedprops.com/free-blueprint-files/) and [Kamui Cosplay: Pauldron patterns](https://www.kamuicosplay.com/product-category/patterns/pauldron-patterns/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Convention appearances with the role at each show ("invited guest", "armour workshop", "judge") (seen on: [Kamui Cosplay: Events](https://www.kamuicosplay.com/events/))
- Build logs that list every material and tool used, plus credits for wig and prop collaborators (seen on: [Kamui Cosplay: Yelan build](https://www.kamuicosplay.com/2025/10/18/yelan-from-genshin-impact/))
- Plain usage terms on templates: personal use only for patterns, sell your prints with credit for 3D files (seen on: [Punished Props: Free blueprint files](https://www.punishedprops.com/free-blueprint-files/))
- Commissions open/closed state with separate enquiry types (custom, trophies/awards), and a shipping crate note for large props (seen on: [Volpin Props](https://www.volpinprops.com))
- Scale guide on each pattern (the pattern printed next to an A4 sheet and a hand) and a printable "test square" page to check the printer scale
**Style: Soft neo-brutalism (hard shadows, flat fills)**
- Type: Headings: Titan One 400 (a fat rounded display face) at up to 104px; body: Figtree 400 at 18px; product data (formats, sizes, prices): Azeret Mono 500.
- Palette: bg #FFFDF7 / text #111111 / accent #FF5A1F (foam-orange for "download" and "add to basket") / surface #FFE45C (EVA-foam yellow) / line #111111 (2px) / second fill #9ED8DB (worbla teal, used on pattern cards only)
- Layout: portfolio is a loose masonry of build photos with thick 2px black borders and a 6px solid offset shadow (no blur). Build pages run a stage-by-stage strip (pattern → foam → seal → paint) with a materials table in the margin. Products show price and format in a hard-edged label. Buttons 6px radius; product cards 0; labels 999px only on format chips.
- Imagery: finished costume shots against plain seamless backdrops, full-length 4:5, plus messy real workshop process photos (foam offcuts, heat gun) at 1:1. Characters' names credited to the franchise.
- Motion: buttons shift 2px down-right onto their shadow when pressed. No hover zoom. Nothing on scroll. prefers-reduced-motion respected.
- Why it fits now: flat colour with thick outlines and hard shadows is the current look for indie creator shops selling digital files, and it matches foam, paint and cut-out craft. Style reference: [Gumroad](https://gumroad.com).
**Style variations:** Workshop: kraft #C9A676 bg, black · Villain: #151515 bg, blood #C1121F buttons · Pastel Magical: #F7D6E0 fill, mint #BDE7D0 borders
**Real-world basis:** [Punished Props: Free blueprint files](https://www.punishedprops.com/free-blueprint-files/) · [Punished Props: Portfolio](https://www.punishedprops.com/portfolio/) · [Kamui Cosplay: Pauldron patterns](https://www.kamuicosplay.com/product-category/patterns/pauldron-patterns/) · [Kamui Cosplay: Events](https://www.kamuicosplay.com/events/) · [Volpin Props](https://www.volpinprops.com)
**Refs:**
- [Punished Props: Free blueprint files](https://www.punishedprops.com/free-blueprint-files/): 200+ free templates by franchise and format with tutorials and usage terms, on WordPress
- [Kamui Cosplay: Pauldron patterns](https://www.kamuicosplay.com/product-category/patterns/pauldron-patterns/): WooCommerce shop of digital PDF patterns with single patterns and bundles
- [Kamui Cosplay: Yelan build](https://www.kamuicosplay.com/2025/10/18/yelan-from-genshin-impact/): the build-log format: materials, stage-by-stage process, tools, collaborators, timeline

### XXI. Events & occasions

<a id="205"></a>
#### 205 · Wedding: the couple's site (`vows`)
**For:** couples who want their own domain instead of a Joy/Zola/The Knot subpage, and a friend who "does websites" setting it up for them.
**Templates:** front-page (names, date, place) · page-schedule · page-travel · page-rsvp · page-wedding-party · page-our-story · page-faq · page-registry · page-photos (password-protected, after the day)
**Patterns (~30):** names-and-date masthead, ceremony and reception details (venue, address, time, map link), weekend schedule list (welcome drinks / ceremony / breakfast / Sunday brunch, each with dress code), parking and shuttle note, hotel room-block card with booking code and "book by" date, RSVP form with deadline, wedding party grid with one-line bios, how-we-met story, Q&A (dress code, children, plus-ones, dietary needs), registry/gift-list note, things to do nearby, livestream link block, post-wedding photo gallery.
**Content model:** posts + pages only. Schedule items are a synced pattern with pattern overrides (time, title, place, dress code). RSVP answers are stored as Jetpack Forms feedback entries.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (RSVP with attending / meal choice / dietary needs / song request fields). Optional Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap for the venue map.
**Signature:** a clear section per guest question (Story · Schedule · Travel · Q&A · Wedding Party · Registry) so guests never have to message the couple, with a gift note in the couple's own words ("Your presence at the wedding is present enough for us…") (seen on: [Amy & Dave on Joy](https://withjoy.com/amyplusdave)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- An "RSVP by 1 May" line that the RSVP pattern reads from one date setting. After that date the form swaps itself for "RSVPs are closed, message us directly" (operational). (seen on: [Joy checklist: RSVP form with deadline](https://withjoy.com/blog/what-to-put-on-your-wedding-website-the-complete-checklist/))
- A hotel room-block card with the booking code and a "block released on" date (local & practical). (seen on: [Joy checklist](https://withjoy.com/blog/what-to-put-on-your-wedding-website-the-complete-checklist/))
- Password protection with core's post password, so the address and the Sunday brunch aren't public (owner QoL). (seen on: [Joy checklist: privacy/password settings](https://withjoy.com/blog/what-to-put-on-your-wedding-website-the-complete-checklist/))
- Printable A5 "day card" with schedule, address and taxi numbers for older guests, generated from the same schedule items with a print stylesheet (content & tools).
- Step-free access and quiet-room notes for each venue on the schedule (accessibility).
**Style: Stationery-suite editorial** (the website is set like the couple's paper suite, so invitation, menu and site match)
- Type: Headings: Kaisei Decol 500 at clamp(3.5rem, 11vw, 9rem); body: Karla 400/18px, 1.6 line-height; small print (times, dress codes): Karla 500 with tabular figures.
- Palette: paper #FFFFFF bg · ink #1D2A24 text · bottle green #2F5D46 accent · blush #F1D9D3 surface for the RSVP block · line #CAD3CD.
- Layout: a single narrow column (60ch) for prose with the schedule set as a two-column table (time | event) that breaks out to full width. Hairline rules instead of cards; buttons are 2px squares, images unrounded. Nav is a single line of section names under the names. The home page is: names at poster size, date and town, then the schedule table immediately. No hero photo is required.
- Imagery: 1–3 film-grain engagement photos in 4:5, uncropped. The venue shown by a line drawing or a real photo, never stock florals.
- Motion: none apart from a View Transition cross-fade between sections. The RSVP success state swaps in place. Honours prefers-reduced-motion by removing the transition.
- Why it fits now: couples are choosing matching suites across invitations, menus, place cards and order of service; the site should be the digital piece of that suite (example: [Papier wedding stationery](https://www.papier.com/gb/wedding)).
**Style variations:** Garden: green #2F5D46, blush RSVP panel · Town Hall: black ink, one red #B3261E rule · Seaside: navy #1B3557 on white, sand #E9E1D3
**Real-world basis:** [Amy & Dave (Joy): sections](https://withjoy.com/amyplusdave) · [Joy: what to put on your wedding website](https://withjoy.com/blog/what-to-put-on-your-wedding-website-the-complete-checklist/) · [Papier: wedding suite (invitations, orders of service, place cards)](https://www.papier.com/gb/wedding)
**Refs:**
- [Amy & Dave on Joy: home](https://withjoy.com/amyplusdave): the minimum set of sections (Story, Schedule, Travel, Q&A, Wedding Party, Registry) and a warm, plain-spoken gift note.
- [Joy: wedding website checklist](https://withjoy.com/blog/what-to-put-on-your-wedding-website-the-complete-checklist/): what guests actually need: parking, RSVP deadline, room block, dress code, children policy, livestream.
- [Papier: wedding](https://www.papier.com/gb/wedding): one design carried across save-the-dates, menus, table plans and order of service; the site should behave the same way.

<a id="206"></a>
#### 206 · Wedding Planner (`dayof`)
**For:** independent planners and on-the-day coordinators (one or two people, maybe a small team of assistants) working a region.
**Templates:** front-page · page-services (packages) · archive-wedding (portfolio) · single-wedding · page-about (my story) · page-kind-words · archive-post (blog/wedding news) · page-faq · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** package ladder (On the Day / Partial / Full) with "from" prices and what's included, "what happens when" timeline (booking meeting → six-week planning session → the day), coverage-hours note, supplier-liaison list, portfolio grid of weddings named by venue, single-wedding story with supplier credits, kind-words quotes from named couples, "about me" with photo, areas covered, extra services (waiting and bar staff), free intro call booking, FAQ.
**Content model:** `wedding` CPT (venue, location, date, season, guest count, supplier credits, photographer credit). Taxonomy `venue-type` (country house / barn / city / destination).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (enquiry with date, venue, guest numbers, package interest); Cal.com embed for the free intro call.
**Signature:** a package ladder with honest "from" prices and a plain list of what each includes, ending in a line that the full-planning tier needs a stated minimum budget (seen on: [Holly & Rebecca Weddings: Packages](https://hollyandrebeccaweddings.co.uk/packages)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A "Now booking 2027 · 2026 Saturdays full" availability line that the owner changes in one place (operational). (seen on: [On The Day Ltd: services, packages by guest count and hours](https://www.onthedaywcs.co.uk/services))
- "Book a complimentary 20-minute call" button tied to Cal.com (conversion helper). (seen on: [On The Day Ltd: services](https://www.onthedaywcs.co.uk/services))
- A "what's in my emergency kit" list (buying confidence). (seen on: [Holly & Rebecca: Packages](https://hollyandrebeccaweddings.co.uk/packages))
- A downloadable PDF price list and a sample on-the-day running order, both printable from the site (content & tools).
- Supplier credits on each wedding story, which venues and photographers share (trust & proof). Adds schema.org `Event` + `LocalBusiness` markup (owner QoL).
**Style: Run-sheet utility** (the planner's actual tool, a timed running order, used as the design language)
- Type: Headings: Yanone Kaffeesatz 700 at clamp(3rem, 9vw, 7.5rem); body: IBM Plex Sans 400/18px; times and prices: IBM Plex Mono 500.
- Palette: white #FFFFFF bg · graphite #1E1E1E text · highlighter yellow #FFE14D for "now booking" and key times · ruled blue #2B59C3 for links · line #D9D9D9.
- Layout: a 12-column grid with a fixed left time column (like a run sheet: 13:00 · 13:30 · 14:15) running down the home page. Services, portfolio and kind words each sit at a time slot. Packages are set as a three-row table (not three cards), with hard 1px rules, square buttons and 4px-radius inputs.
- Imagery: real wedding photography credited to the photographer, full-bleed 3:2, plus behind-the-scenes phone photos of set-up (chairs, signage, the kit bag).
- Motion: a highlighter sweep animation under the current "Now booking" line on load only; nothing on scroll. Reduced-motion shows the highlight static.
- Why it fits now: couples compare planners on clarity and price transparency, and utilitarian, tool-like interfaces with honest rules and plain type read as organised (example: [Are.na](https://www.are.na)).
**Style variations:** Clipboard: white, yellow #FFE14D highlights · Evening: ink #14213D bg, paper text, yellow kept · Garden Party: canvas #F3EFE6, black, green #3C6E47 links
**Real-world basis:** [Holly & Rebecca: Packages](https://hollyandrebeccaweddings.co.uk/packages) · [The Wedding Day Planner: Services](https://weddingdayplanner.co.uk/services-1) · [On The Day Ltd: Services](https://www.onthedaywcs.co.uk/services) · [The Bijou Studio: Portfolio](https://www.thebijoustudio.com/portfolio)
**Refs:**
- [Holly & Rebecca Weddings: Packages](https://hollyandrebeccaweddings.co.uk/packages): three named tiers with "from" prices, a six-week planning session and an emergency kit bag listed as inclusions.
- [On The Day Ltd: Services](https://www.onthedaywcs.co.uk/services): packages set by guest count and coverage hours, and a free 20-minute call as the first step.
- [The Bijou Studio: Portfolio](https://www.thebijoustudio.com/portfolio): weddings listed by venue name (Babington House, Kew Gardens), which is how couples search.

<a id="207"></a>
#### 207 · Small Conference (`conf`)
**For:** single-track, 100–600-person community conferences run by one organiser or a small crew (web, design, Ruby, indie).
**Templates:** front-page (this year) · archive-speaker · single-speaker · archive-talk (all years) · single-talk (video + slides) · page-schedule · page-tickets · page-venue · page-cfp · page-accessibility · page-code-of-conduct · page-scholarship · archive-year
**Patterns (~45):** this-year masthead (date, city, venue), speaker grid (portrait, name, talk title when announced), schedule table (time, speaker, talk), ticket block (price, what's included, sold-out state), venue and getting-there, CFP page (what we pay speakers), scholarship/diversity tickets explainer, accessibility provisions list, code of conduct with reporting contact, past years index, talk page (video embed, abstract, slides link), photo gallery link, partners credited in text, newsletter signup.
**Content model:** `speaker` (bio, links, pronouns), `talk` (speaker relation, year, video URL, slides URL, topics taxonomy), `edition` taxonomy for the year.
**Plugins:** Query Filter (talk archive filtered by topic and year); WooCommerce or an external ticketing embed (Tito); Advanced Query Loop (current edition vs past).
**Signature:** a permanent talk archive across every year, with speaker, title and year per talk and a topic filter (accessibility, CSS, JavaScript…) (seen on: [FFConf: Talks](https://ffconf.org/talks)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- An accessibility page with specifics: live captioning, step counts to the balcony, free companion tickets, large-print agendas, photo opt-out lanyards (accessibility). (seen on: [FFConf: Accessibility](https://ffconf.org/accessibility))
- A CFP page stating exactly what speakers get (travel, hotel, honorarium, talk length) and the open/closed state (trust & proof, operational). (seen on: [FFConf: CFP](https://ffconf.org/articles/cfp))
- Scholarship tickets that attendees can buy for others, with an optional public credit (community). (seen on: [FFConf: Scholarship](https://ffconf.org/scholarship))
- An attendee guide with childcare, food, wifi, transport and local tips (local & practical). (seen on: [XOXO: Guide](https://xoxofest.com/guide/))
- A "Convince your boss" page with a printable justification letter (content & tools). Adds schema.org `Event` with `performer` per speaker (owner QoL).
**Style: Kinetic poster type** (the conference as a typographic poster that changes each year)
- Type: Display: Pathway Extreme variable (wdth 75–100, wght 900) set huge and condensed for the city and date; body: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 400/18px; schedule times: Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono 500.
- Palette: white #FFFFFF bg · black #0D0D0D text · cobalt #1F3FFF accent (per-edition colour changes yearly) · signal yellow #FFD400 for "sold out" · line #0D0D0D at 2px.
- Layout: the home page opens with the date and city filling the viewport width (the width axis adjusts so it exactly fits). Below that is a hard-ruled 4-column speaker index (name large, talk small), then the schedule as a real table. Past years run as a list of years along the bottom. No card shadows; images are square-cornered, buttons have a 2px radius.
- Imagery: speaker portraits shot by the event photographer, converted to 1-colour duotone in the edition colour. Venue photos are full-colour.
- Motion: the display word's width axis responds to scroll position on the home page only (a CSS scroll-driven animation). Reduced motion locks it to a fixed width.
- Why it fits now: independent design conferences keep a strong typographic identity with speaker-led pages and a year-by-year archive (example: [beyond tellerrand Düsseldorf 2027](https://beyondtellerrand.com/events/dusseldorf-2027)).
**Style variations:** Edition Blue: cobalt #1F3FFF · Edition Orange: #FF5F1F on white · Night Session: black bg, white text, yellow #FFD400
**Real-world basis:** [FFConf: Talks](https://ffconf.org/talks) · [FFConf: CFP](https://ffconf.org/articles/cfp) · [beyond tellerrand: Düsseldorf 2027](https://beyondtellerrand.com/events/dusseldorf-2027) · [Brighton Ruby 2025](https://brightonruby.com/2025) · [XOXO: Guide](https://xoxofest.com/guide/)
**Refs:**
- [FFConf: Talks](https://ffconf.org/talks): 118 talks from 2009 on, each with speaker, title and year, plus topic filters; the archive is the conference's long-term value.
- [Brighton Ruby: 2025](https://brightonruby.com/2025): each edition keeps its own page with speakers and talk videos, linked from a row of years back to 2014.
- [FFConf: Accessibility](https://ffconf.org/accessibility): concrete provisions (captioning, companion tickets, steps counted) instead of a generic statement.
