<a id="208"></a>
#### 208 · Hackathon / Meetup Group (`meetup`)
**For:** volunteer-run monthly tech or maker meetups (JS nights, CSS evenings, Homebrew Website Club chapters, small hack days) that want to own their archive rather than rent it from Meetup.com.
**Templates:** front-page (next event) · archive-event · single-event · archive-talk · single-talk · archive-person (speakers/organisers) · page-about · page-code-of-conduct · page-speak (submit a talk) · page-host (for venue sponsors)
**Patterns (~30):** next-event block (full date and time, talk titles, speaker bio, venue address with map), past events list by year, talk card (title, speaker, video, slides), speaker profile with links, "submit a talk" form, "host us" note for venues, code of conduct with contacts, community chat link (Slack/Discord/Matrix), sponsor thank-you line, coach/mentor list with pronouns (for teaching meetups), RSVP via external link or native RSVP.
**Content model:** `event` (date, venue, RSVP URL, number), `talk` (event relation, speaker relation, video, slides), `person` (role: organiser / speaker / coach, pronouns, links).
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (next event vs past); Event Tickets (free RSVP with capacity) or a link to Meetup/Luma; Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap for the venue.
**Signature:** a "Next event" block at the top with the full date ("Thursday, 1st October 2026 7:00pm"), speaker bio, venue address and map, and underneath it every past event in one reverse-chronological archive going back to 2010 (seen on: [Async: Events](https://asyncjs.com/events/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- An RSVP capacity state ("32 of 60 places left" → "Waitlist") from Event Tickets (operational, conversion).
- A talk archive that keeps working when videos disappear, with an honest note for lost recordings (community). (seen on: [LNUG: Talks](https://lnug.org/talks))
- Coach and speaker lists with pronouns (accessibility & inclusion). (seen on: [codebar: upcoming events](https://codebar.io/events/upcoming))
- A "host us" page for venues with capacity, AV and pizza needs spelled out (content & tools).
- Events also exported as iCal and marked up with schema.org `Event`, so they show up in indie event aggregators (owner QoL). (seen on: [IndieWeb: Homebrew Website Club, events on events.indieweb.org](https://indieweb.org/Homebrew_Website_Club))
**Style: Departure-board mono** (event listings set like a station departure board: date, time, platform/venue)
- Type: Display: Sixtyfour 400 at clamp(3rem, 10vw, 8rem) for the next event's date; body: Source Serif 4 400/18px for talk abstracts; metadata: Sixtyfour 400/15px.
- Palette: board black #111111 surface for the next-event strip only · page white #FAFAFA bg · text #111111 · amber #FFB000 for times on the board · link blue #0033CC · line #CCCCCC.
- Layout: the top of the home page is a full-width black "board" strip with the date, time, venue and talk titles in amber mono. Below, the archive is a dense, ruled list (one line per event: No. 142 · 01.10.2026 · two talks · venue), grouped by year with year numbers in the margin. No cards. Buttons are rectangles with 0 radius, inputs 3px.
- Imagery: group photos from the actual nights and speaker photos, kept small (1:1 at 96px) in the list and 4:3 on talk pages. No stock "people at laptops".
- Motion: board characters flip once on load for the next event only (skipped entirely under reduced motion). No scroll effects.
- Why it fits now: community tech groups are moving archives back to their own simple sites with dense, dated event lists (example: [Async: Events](https://asyncjs.com/events/)).
**Style variations:** Platform: black board, amber #FFB000 · Daylight: white board, black text, red #D7263D times · Terminal Green: #0B3D2E board, mint #9FE3C1 text
**Real-world basis:** [Async: Events](https://asyncjs.com/events/) · [LNUG: Talks](https://lnug.org/talks) · [London CSS: Events](https://www.londoncss.dev/events) · [codebar: Upcoming](https://codebar.io/events/upcoming) · [IndieWeb: Homebrew Website Club](https://indieweb.org/Homebrew_Website_Club)
**Refs:**
- [Async: Events](https://asyncjs.com/events/): next event with full date, speaker bio, address and map, then an unbroken archive to 2010.
- [LNUG: Talks](https://lnug.org/talks): talk-first archive with video thumbnail, abstract and speaker bio per talk.
- [codebar: Upcoming events](https://codebar.io/events/upcoming): multi-chapter workshop listings with host venue and coaches (with pronouns) per event.

<a id="209"></a>
#### 209 · Charity Run / Fundraiser (`fundraise`)
**For:** small charities, schools, hospices and community groups running an annual fun run, walk or swim with sponsorship.
**Templates:** front-page (this year's event) · single-event (per city/date) · page-routes · page-enter · page-fundraising (where your money goes) · page-volunteer · page-faq · archive-news · page-results · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** event masthead (date, start location), distance tiers (e.g. 3–5 miles family / 10–15 / 20+) with entry fees by age, route map per distance with start and finish, "choose your charity" or "fundraise for us" explainer, fundraising total with target, where-your-money-goes explanation (who covers costs, Gift Aid), start-time slots, bus/transport to start, volunteer sign-up, kit and T-shirt note, results table by distance, FAQ.
**Content model:** `event` (date, city, start/finish, distance tiers, fees, status). `route` meta holds the GPX file for the map. Results are a table block or CSV import into a `result` CPT (bib, name, distance, time).
**Plugins:** GiveWP (donation form with goal bar, Gift Aid add-on optional); Event Tickets + WooCommerce for paid entries by tier; Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (route lines from GPX/GeoJSON); Advanced Query Loop.
**Signature:** distance tiers with plain names and per-tier, per-age entry fees on one event page (e.g. "Wee Wander 3–5 miles: £13 adults, £7 children"), with fundraising done per walker for the charity of their choice (seen on: [Kiltwalk: Glasgow](https://www.thekiltwalk.co.uk/events/glasgow)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A "where your money goes" page explaining who pays for the event and how much reaches the charity (trust & proof). (seen on: [Kiltwalk: Where your money goes](https://www.thekiltwalk.co.uk/charity/fundraising/where-your-money-goes))
- A "Route details to be confirmed" state on the route block that switches to the map when the GPX is uploaded (operational). (seen on: [Kiltwalk: Glasgow FAQ](https://www.thekiltwalk.co.uk/events/glasgow))
- Start-time slots with "some slots sell out quicker" flags (operational, conversion). (seen on: [Kiltwalk: Glasgow](https://www.thekiltwalk.co.uk/events/glasgow))
- A volunteer sign-up page (marshals, water stations) (community). (seen on: [Race for Life: home, volunteer link](https://raceforlife.cancerresearchuk.org/))
- Bus-to-the-start booking info, a downloadable fundraising pack PDF, and step-free/buggy-friendly notes per route (local & practical, content & tools, accessibility). (seen on: [Kiltwalk: Buses](https://www.thekiltwalk.co.uk/events/buses))
**Style: Race-bib signage** (numbers, distances and start times set like a paper race bib and roadside marshal signs)
- Type: Display: Squada One 400 at clamp(4rem, 14vw, 12rem) for distances and dates; body: Public Sans 400/18px; numbers (fees, times, totals): Big Shoulders Text 700 with tabular figures.
- Palette: bib white #FFFFFF bg · black #0E0E0E text · charity colour #E4002B (set per site) for tier labels and the donate button · hi-vis yellow #F4FF3A used only as the marshal-sign panel with black text · route blue #1565C0 on maps.
- Layout: the home page is a stack of distance tiers, each a full-width band with the distance set huge on the left and fee/age/start-slot data on the right in a ruled table. The fundraising total sits as one line of large figures with the target beside it (no stat row). Buttons are 0-radius with a 3px black border, like bib safety-pin corners. Map blocks run full-bleed.
- Imagery: real photos of last year's walkers and runners (finish lines, families, fancy dress), shot at 3:2 with no overlay; route maps from real GPX data.
- Motion: none on scroll. The goal bar animates to the current total once, on load; reduced motion shows it static.
- Why it fits now: mass-participation charity events lead with named distance tiers and plain fees rather than campaign slogans (example: [Kiltwalk: Glasgow](https://www.thekiltwalk.co.uk/events/glasgow)).
**Style variations:** Hospice: charity green #00754A · Winter Dip: navy #0B2545 with ice #DDEFFB panels · School Fun Run: black on hi-vis yellow #F4FF3A signs
**Real-world basis:** [Kiltwalk: Glasgow](https://www.thekiltwalk.co.uk/events/glasgow) · [Kiltwalk: Where your money goes](https://www.thekiltwalk.co.uk/charity/fundraising/where-your-money-goes) · [Kiltwalk: Buses](https://www.thekiltwalk.co.uk/events/buses) · [Race for Life: home](https://raceforlife.cancerresearchuk.org/) · [Race for Life: Find an event](https://raceforlife.cancerresearchuk.org/find-an-event)
**Refs:**
- [Kiltwalk: Glasgow](https://www.thekiltwalk.co.uk/events/glasgow): three named distances with per-age fees, time slots and an FAQ that admits when routes aren't confirmed yet.
- [Kiltwalk: Where your money goes](https://www.thekiltwalk.co.uk/charity/fundraising/where-your-money-goes): explains who covers event costs and where fundraising and Gift Aid go.
- [Race for Life: home](https://raceforlife.cancerresearchuk.org/): distances (3k, 5k, 10k, Pretty Muddy) explained in one line each, with volunteering as an equal way in.

<a id="210"></a>
#### 210 · Reunion / Private Party (`rsvp`)
**For:** whoever got lumbered with organising the 20-year school reunion, a family reunion, a big birthday or a leaving do.
**Templates:** front-page (the invitation) · page-schedule · page-rsvp · page-whos-coming · page-in-memoriam · page-travel-stay · page-photos (password-protected) · page-faq · page-contact
**Patterns (~25):** invitation masthead (what, when, where), weekend schedule (Friday drinks / Saturday dinner / Sunday picnic), RSVP form (attending, plus-one, dietary needs, "what have you been up to" bio), "who's coming" list, "help us find" missing-people list, in memoriam list, tickets/contribution block, where-to-stay list, class photo then/now, shared photo album, FAQ (dress code, kids, parking), organiser contacts.
**Content model:** posts + pages only, plus Event Tickets attendees for RSVPs. A `person` CPT (name then/now, class/family branch, found/not found, in memoriam flag) powers the "who's coming", "help us find" and "in memoriam" lists.
**Plugins:** Event Tickets (free RSVP with attendee list, or paid tickets via WooCommerce for dinner contributions); Jetpack Forms ("I know where X is" tip form).
**Signature:** a "who's coming" list built from real RSVPs, next to an in memoriam page, so people see friends are going and nobody is forgotten (seen on: [MyEvent: class reunion platform](https://myevent.com/class-reunions/class-reunion-platform)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A "help us find" list of missing classmates with a one-field tip form (community).
- Schedule by day with the "anniversary year" in the title (5th, 10th, 20th) and an organiser contact block (local & practical). (seen on: [West Point AOG: Class reunions](https://www.westpointaog.org/events/reunion/))
- RSVP closes on a set date and the form swaps to "Late? Email Jo"; ticket sales show "12 places left" (operational).
- Guests add photos to a shared album after the party (community). (seen on: [Partiful](https://partiful.com))
- A password on the photos and guest list pages, plus a privacy note on what is shown publicly (owner QoL, trust).
**Style: Riso party flyer** (two-colour risograph flyer, overprinted and slightly off-register, like a photocopied invite)
- Type: Display: Shrikhand 400 at clamp(4rem, 13vw, 11rem); body: Figtree 400/18px; small print: Figtree 600.
- Palette: paper #FFFFFF bg · riso fluorescent pink #FF48B0 · riso yellow #FFE800 · ink #1A1A1A text · overprint (pink × yellow) #FF6A3D for the RSVP button.
- Layout: the home page reads like a folded flyer: huge WHAT / WHEN / WHERE blocks, each rotated 0–2° with a 2px offset second-colour layer (CSS mix-blend-mode: multiply), then the RSVP form sitting straight on a yellow panel. "Who's coming" is a plain comma-separated run of names in large type, not avatar tiles. Radius 0 on everything except the RSVP button (full stadium shape, the only rounded element).
- Imagery: old class or family photos run through a two-tone riso halftone (pink + ink); new photos stay full colour in the album.
- Motion: the off-register layer shifts 2px on hover of the main CTA only. No scroll motion; reduced motion removes the shift.
- Why it fits now: party invitations have moved from paper to link-shared pages with playful poster-style design and live RSVP lists (example: [Partiful](https://partiful.com)).
**Style variations:** Class of '06: pink #FF48B0 + yellow · Family Picnic: green #00A95C + orange #FF6C2F · Leaving Do: blue #0078BF + red #FF4C65
**Real-world basis:** [MyEvent: class reunion platform](https://myevent.com/class-reunions/class-reunion-platform) · [West Point AOG: Class reunions](https://www.westpointaog.org/events/reunion/) · [Partiful](https://partiful.com)
**Refs:**
- [MyEvent: class reunion platform](https://myevent.com/class-reunions/class-reunion-platform): the reunion-specific features: who's coming, ticketing, directory, in memoriam, visitor photo uploads.
- [West Point AOG: Class reunions](https://www.westpointaog.org/events/reunion/): reunions organised by anniversary year with dates and named contacts.
- [Partiful: home](https://partiful.com): guest list, comments and a shared photo album on the invitation itself.

### XXII. Personal

<a id="211"></a>
#### 211 · Link-in-Bio (`links`)
**For:** musicians, makers, podcasters and small shops who want their own-domain replacement for Linktree, linked from an Instagram/TikTok/Bluesky bio.
**Templates:** front-page (the link page) · page-privacy · 404 · (optional) page-shop · page-press
**Patterns (~20):** avatar + name + one-line bio header, platform-branded link buttons (icon + label, each in its service's colour), featured link block (new release / new drop, with cover image), embedded player (Bandcamp/Spotify/YouTube), mini shop row (3 products with prices), newsletter signup, social icon row, "latest post" auto-link, contact email button, footer credit.
**Content model:** posts + pages only. Each link is a Button block with a registered block style per platform (Bluesky, Instagram, Spotify, GitHub, Bandcamp, Substack…), so colour and icon come from one click.
**Plugins:** none. Optional WooCommerce for the shop row, optional Jetpack Newsletter.
**Signature:** a library of platform-branded buttons (icon plus brand colour per service) the owner picks from a style menu instead of uploading logos (seen on: [Seth Cottle (LittleLink)](https://seth.social)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A "featured" slot with start/end dates, so "New single out Friday" becomes "Listen now" on release day and drops back to normal a month later (operational). (seen on: [Selena Gomez on Linktree: release-led featured links](https://linktr.ee/selenagomez))
- A shop row pulling three live products (conversion helper). (seen on: [Selena Gomez on Linktree: merch section](https://linktr.ee/selenagomez))
- Its own privacy page and no third-party trackers by default (owner QoL, trust). (seen on: [LittleLink sample: privacy policy link](https://littlelink.io/sample.html))
- A high-contrast mode where branded buttons fall back to black and white with text labels, never icon-only (accessibility).
- An auto-generated OG share image with the avatar and name (owner QoL).
**Style: Sticker-sheet tactile** (buttons feel like a sheet of printed vinyl stickers: thick outlines, flat colour, a hard offset shadow)
- Type: Name: Sniglet 800 at clamp(2.75rem, 12vw, 5.5rem); bio and labels: Rethink Sans 500/18px.
- Palette: page #F2F0EB bg (paper grey, not cream) · ink #111111 · owner accent #0057FF · sticker shadow #111111 (3px hard offset, no blur) · platform colours only inside their buttons.
- Layout: a single 440px column, left-aligned on desktop with the avatar hanging in the left margin. Buttons are 56px tall with a 2px ink border, a 10px radius and a hard 3px offset shadow that collapses on press. Images have 0 radius and the avatar is a circle. No cards around groups; spacing does the grouping.
- Imagery: one real portrait or logo; the featured release uses the actual cover art at 1:1.
- Motion: button press moves 3px down-right into its shadow (transform only). Nothing else moves; reduced motion keeps the colour change and skips the shift.
- Why it fits now: people are moving their bio links from rented Linktree pages to self-hosted open-source pages with proper per-platform buttons (example: [Seth Cottle](https://seth.social)).
**Style variations:** Default: paper grey, blue #0057FF · Merch Night: black bg, white stickers with ink outline · Pastel Pack: #FFD6E0 page, ink outlines kept
**Real-world basis:** [Seth Cottle](https://seth.social) · [LittleLink: sample](https://littlelink.io/sample.html) · [Selena Gomez on Linktree](https://linktr.ee/selenagomez)
**Refs:**
- [Seth Cottle: link page](https://seth.social): around 18 links, each with its own platform colour and icon, readable in one scroll.
- [LittleLink: sample](https://littlelink.io/sample.html): the open-source baseline: avatar, name, role and branded buttons, with nothing else.
- [Linktree: Selena Gomez](https://linktr.ee/selenagomez): how a release-led page groups music, video and merch.

<a id="212"></a>
#### 212 · CV / Résumé (`resume`)
**For:** job seekers, freelancers and academics outside the lab (designers, developers, nurses, teachers) who need one URL that also prints as a clean PDF.
**Templates:** front-page (the CV) · page-projects · single-project · page-writing · page-contact · page-print (A4/Letter print view)
**Patterns (~25):** header with name, role, location and contact links; summary paragraph; experience list (date range column, title and company, two-line description, skill tags); projects with links; education; awards; volunteer work; languages and skills grouped by category; references ("available on request" or named); "View full résumé (PDF)" link; writing/talks list; availability line.
**Content model:** `role` CPT (company, title, start, end, location, tags) and `project` CPT (year, link, stack), rendered with Query Loops. Or pages only for a single-page CV.
**Plugins:** none.
**Signature:** an experience list with a date-range column on the left, the role and company linked, a short description and skill tags per role, followed by a "View Full Résumé" link (seen on: [Brittany Chiang](https://www.brittanychiang.com)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A print stylesheet so the same page prints as a two-page A4 or US Letter CV (switch in the footer), with links written out as URLs (content & tools).
- "Available from March 2027 · open to contract" availability line with an on/off toggle (operational, conversion).
- The CV structured the JSON Resume way (work, projects, education, awards, volunteer, skills by category) and exported as JSON (owner QoL). (seen on: [Thomas Davis on JSON Resume](https://registry.jsonresume.org/thomasdavis))
- schema.org `Person` markup with `sameAs` links (owner QoL, trust).
- A plain-language summary at the top and a date format setting (Mar 2024 vs 2024-03) (accessibility, local & practical).
**Style: Swiss CV** (a typeset document, not a portfolio: grid, hierarchy and nothing extra)
- Type: Name: Wix Madefor Display 800 at clamp(3.5rem, 9vw, 7rem); body: Wix Madefor Text 400/18px, 1.55; dates and tags: IBM Plex Mono 400/15px.
- Palette: white #FFFFFF bg · ink #141414 text · one accent #C8102E (hyperlinks and the name's underline only) · rule #D6D6D6 · print uses black only.
- Layout: a 12-column grid. Dates sit in columns 1–3, content in 4–10, and the name block breaks the grid at full width. Section headings are sentence-case at 1.5× body, not eyebrow labels. Ruled lines between roles, tags as plain mono text separated by middots (not pills). A4 print view uses the same grid in mm.
- Imagery: none by default. Optional small square portrait in grayscale, top right.
- Motion: none. Link underlines thicken on hover.
- Why it fits now: recruiters skim in seconds and ATS parsers read clean HTML; the dated-column CV with tags is the pattern that stuck on respected developer and designer sites (example: [Brittany Chiang](https://www.brittanychiang.com)).
**Style variations:** Red Line: #C8102E accent · Blueprint: #0B3D91 accent, Plex Mono headings · Plain Paper: black only, print-first
**Real-world basis:** [Brittany Chiang](https://www.brittanychiang.com) · [Thomas Davis on JSON Resume](https://registry.jsonresume.org/thomasdavis) · [JSON Resume: Themes](https://jsonresume.org/themes/)
**Refs:**
- [Brittany Chiang: home and résumé](https://www.brittanychiang.com): dated experience list with skill tags and a full-résumé link; the best-known developer CV pattern.
- [JSON Resume registry: Thomas Davis](https://registry.jsonresume.org/thomasdavis): the complete section set (summary, work, projects, education, awards, volunteer, skills, references).
- [JSON Resume: Themes](https://jsonresume.org/themes/): one data source rendered in many layouts; this theme's style variations should work the same way.

<a id="213"></a>
#### 213 · IndieWeb Personal Homepage (`home`)
**For:** people who want a personal site that is the canonical home for everything they post (notes, articles, links, photos), syndicated out to Mastodon/Bluesky.
**Templates:** front-page (stream) · single (note / article / link / photo formats) · archive (by year and month) · taxonomy-tag · page-about · page-now · page-colophon · page-blogroll · page-contact · search · 404
**Patterns (~30):** h-card header (photo, name, pronouns, one-line bio), mixed stream (notes, articles, links, books) with post-type filter, note card with timestamp permalink, link post (quoted source + comment), "also on" syndication links, webmention replies/likes list, year/month archive, tag list, /now page with last-updated date, colophon (CMS, hosting, fonts), blogroll, contact options, RSS/JSON Feed links, 88x31 button row.
**Content model:** posts with core post formats (aside/status for notes, link, image) and tags. Syndication URLs stored as post meta and shown via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** Webmention and ActivityPub (both on wordpress.org, maintained by the IndieWeb/Automattic folks) for replies and fediverse following.
**Signature:** a /now page with a "last updated" date, listed on nownownow.com, saying what the person is focused on this month (seen on: [Derek Sivers: /now](https://sive.rs/now)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A "last updated" date that the /now pattern reads from the page's modified date, plus a gentle "this is 6 months old" note when it goes stale (operational).
- A post-type filter on the home stream (all / articles / notes / links / books) (local & practical). (seen on: [Kev Quirk: book posts filter](https://kevquirk.com/?type=book))
- A colophon listing CMS, hosting, CDN and font (trust & proof). (seen on: [Kev Quirk: Colophon](https://kevquirk.com/colophon))
- POSSE "also on" links under each post and incoming webmentions shown as replies (community). (seen on: [Tantek Çelik](https://tantek.com))
- A year → month archive with a "hand-picked highlights" page (content & tools). (seen on: [Adactio: Journal archive](https://adactio.com/journal/archive))
**Style: Personal almanac** (a well-set book of days: serif text, mono timestamps, generous margins, visible links)
- Type: Headings: Andada Pro 600 at clamp(3rem, 8vw, 6rem); body: Andada Pro 400/19px, 1.6, 66ch measure; timestamps and meta: Victor Mono 400/15px.
- Palette: page #FDFDFB bg · ink #1B1B1B text · link #0645AD underlined, visited #0B0080 (classic hypertext colours kept on purpose) · margin notes #6B5B3E (7:1 on bg) · rule #E4E2DC.
- Layout: a single text column with a wide right margin used for timestamps, reply counts and syndication links (sidenote-style). The stream mixes formats by typography, not boxes: notes in body size, articles with a large title, links with the quoted source indented. No cards, no avatars in the stream.
- Imagery: photo posts at their native ratio, max 66ch wide, with alt text shown as a caption on request.
- Motion: none. Focus rings are a 3px ink outline offset by 2px.
- Why it fits now: the fediverse has made owning your own posts practical again, and long-running personal sites are the model (example: [Adactio](https://adactio.com/journal/archive)).
**Style variations:** Almanac: link blue #0645AD · Marginalia: sepia ink #3B2F2F, red #A61B1B links · Night Reading: #15171A bg, #E8E6E1 text, link #8AB4F8
**Real-world basis:** [Tantek Çelik](https://tantek.com) · [Kev Quirk: About](https://kevquirk.com/about) · [Kev Quirk: Colophon](https://kevquirk.com/colophon) · [Derek Sivers: /now](https://sive.rs/now) · [nownownow.com](https://nownownow.com)
**Refs:**
- [Derek Sivers: /now](https://sive.rs/now): the original /now page: a dated, plain list of current focus, linked to the nownownow directory.
- [Tantek Çelik: home stream](https://tantek.com): h-card, a timestamped note stream with short permalinks, and syndication to Mastodon/Bluesky from one home.
- [Adactio: Journal archive](https://adactio.com/journal/archive): 25 years browsable by year and month, plus tags and hand-picked highlights.

<a id="214"></a>
#### 214 · Memorial / Tribute (`remember`)
**For:** families making an online memorial for someone who has died: to share funeral details, collect memories and raise money for a chosen charity.
**Templates:** front-page (tribute) · page-life-story · page-funeral (service details) · page-memories (thoughts and stories) · page-gallery · page-candles · page-donate · page-contact-family
**Patterns (~25):** name and dates masthead with portrait, short family message, life story, funeral notice (date, time, venue, map, livestream link with password), donation block for the chosen charity with running total, "light a candle" with a message, memories/stories list, photo gallery with contributor names, video tributes, music (favourite songs), "help grow the tribute" invitation, anniversary and birthday candle prompts.
**Content model:** core comments on the tribute page are the "memories" and "candles" (a comment type stored as comment meta and shown with separate Comment Query Loops). Photos are contributed via a Jetpack Forms upload and approved before publishing.
**Plugins:** GiveWP (in-memory donations to one charity, with a goal and total); Jetpack Forms (photo and story submissions with file upload).
**Signature:** visitors "light a candle" with a short message, alongside written memories and a fundraising total for the family's chosen charity, all on one tribute (seen on: [Linda Nolan's tribute on MuchLoved](https://linda-nolan.muchloved.com)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A funeral notice block with date, time, venue, map and a password-protected livestream link, which moves under "The service" after the day (operational, local & practical). (seen on: [Linda Nolan's tribute: funeral details](https://linda-nolan.muchloved.com))
- Contribution approval so the family checks every memory and photo before it appears (trust & proof, owner QoL). (seen on: [MuchLoved: tribute features, access control](https://www.muchloved.com/gateway/tribute-features))
- Birthday and anniversary candle types, and a printable order-of-service PDF (community, content & tools). (seen on: [MuchLoved: tribute features, thought and birthday candles](https://www.muchloved.com/gateway/tribute-features))
- Gift Aid shown on donations for UK charities (trust & proof). (seen on: [Linda Nolan's tribute: fundraising](https://linda-nolan.muchloved.com))
- Public / invited-only / private switch using core visibility and post passwords (owner QoL).
**Style: Book of remembrance** (a hand-set memorial book: calm serif, wide margins, one quiet colour)
- Type: Name: Forum 400 at clamp(3.5rem, 10vw, 8rem); body: EB Garamond 400/20px, 1.6; dates and small labels: EB Garamond small caps (font-variant: small-caps) at body size, not tracked capitals.
- Palette: white #FFFFFF bg · ink #232323 text · moss #4A5A3C accent (links, candle flame outline) · stone #EDEBE7 surface for the funeral notice panel · rule #CFCBC3.
- Layout: a centred book page (62ch) for the life story; memories run as a single column with the writer's name in small caps under each. Candles are listed as a quiet text list (name, message, date) with a small line-drawn flame, not animated tiles. The funeral notice sits in a stone panel with square corners. Buttons are 2px-radius outlines.
- Imagery: the family's real photos, left in original colour or black-and-white as supplied, shown at native ratio with dates. No stock lilies or sunsets.
- Motion: none. A lit candle adds itself to the top of the list with no animation.
- Why it fits now: families want something calmer and less commercial than funeral-directory pages, closer to the restraint of long-form literary publishing (example: [London Review of Books](https://www.lrb.co.uk)).
**Style variations:** Moss: #4A5A3C · Slate: #3E4C59 accent, stone panels · Garden: white, leaf #5B7F3A, pale green #EEF3E8 panels
**Real-world basis:** [Linda Nolan's tribute on MuchLoved](https://linda-nolan.muchloved.com) · [MuchLoved: tribute features](https://www.muchloved.com/gateway/tribute-features) · [MyEvent: in memoriam page feature](https://myevent.com/class-reunions/class-reunion-platform)
**Refs:**
- [MuchLoved: Linda Nolan tribute](https://linda-nolan.muchloved.com): funeral details with livestream, candles, memories and a hospice fundraising total with Gift Aid on one page.
- [MuchLoved: tribute features](https://www.muchloved.com/gateway/tribute-features): full feature set: thought and birthday candles, stories, funeral notice with printable maps, and access control.

<a id="215"></a>
#### 215 · Family Recipe Archive (`grandma`)
**For:** a family (often one grandchild) digitising handwritten recipe cards and the stories that go with them, to share with relatives and print as a book.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-recipe · single-recipe · archive-cook (per family member) · single-cook · taxonomy-occasion (Christmas, Sukkot, Sunday lunch) · page-story (essays) · page-print-book
**Patterns (~30):** recipe card (ingredients grouped by component, method, serves, time, difficulty), scan of the original handwritten card beside the transcription, "whose recipe" byline linking to a family member, story block (where the dish came from, the migration route, who taught whom), archival family photo with caption and year, occasion collections, substitutions and "Mum's notes" margin annotations, cook profile (dates, places lived), recipe index by person, printable card view.
**Content model:** `recipe` CPT (cook relation, serves, prep/cook time, difficulty, occasion taxonomy, original-card image). `cook` CPT (name, birth/death years, places). Recipe schema.org output.
**Plugins:** none. A companion recipe block handles ingredients and servings (shared with the library's recipe themes).
**Signature:** every recipe is attached to a named family member and paired with the story of where it came from, including an old family photo (seen on: [Jewish Food Society: a great-grandmother's stuffed cabbage](https://www.jewishfoodsociety.org/stories/on-sukkot-a-great-grandmothers-stuffed-cabbage-helps)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Recipes titled by the cook's name ("Vicky's Broad Bean Tagliatelle") with time, difficulty and serves on the index card (local & practical). (seen on: [Pasta Grannies: All recipes](https://www.pastagrannies.com/all-recipes/))
- Occasion collections (holiday menus) that surface automatically in the weeks before each holiday (operational, community). (seen on: [Jewish Food Society: Sukkot collection](https://www.jewishfoodsociety.org/collections/sukkot-recipes))
- Long lead times called out at the top of a recipe ("plus 48 hours to freeze and thaw the cabbage") (care & preparation). (seen on: [Jewish Food Society: stuffed cabbage story](https://www.jewishfoodsociety.org/stories/on-sukkot-a-great-grandmothers-stuffed-cabbage-helps))
- A "print the family cookbook" view: A5 pages, one recipe per page, index by cook (content & tools).
- Transcriptions alongside every handwritten scan, so screen readers and younger relatives can read them (accessibility).
**Style: Recipe-card archive** (index cards, ruled lines and original handwriting treated as museum objects)
- Type: Headings: Rosarivo 400 at clamp(3rem, 9vw, 7rem); body: Hanken Grotesk 400/18px; quantities: Hanken Grotesk 600 with tabular figures; handwritten notes are shown as the real scans, not a script font.
- Palette: card white #FFFFFF bg · ink #2A2522 text · ruled-line blue #7FA7D9 (card lines, 1px) · margin red #C0392B (the single vertical margin rule, and links) · kitchen-table surface #E9E6E1 behind cards.
- Layout: each recipe is laid out as a large index card with the horizontal blue rules and a red margin line on a table-grey page. The scan of the original card is pinned top-right at 4:3. The home page is a card index: recipes filed under each cook's name like tabbed dividers. Cards have 2px corners, buttons 0.
- Imagery: flat-scanned original cards and family photos at their true colour (no sepia filter added); new dish photos shot overhead on the family's own table, 4:5.
- Motion: none on scroll. The card index opens a cook's section with a View Transition.
- Why it fits now: families and food archives are preserving heritage recipes together with the person who cooked them and the story behind the dish (example: [Jewish Food Society](https://www.jewishfoodsociety.org)).
**Style variations:** Index Card: blue rules, red margin · Oilcloth: #E03C31 gingham header band, white cards · Pantry Shelf: kraft #CDB594 surface, black ink
**Real-world basis:** [Jewish Food Society: stuffed cabbage story](https://www.jewishfoodsociety.org/stories/on-sukkot-a-great-grandmothers-stuffed-cabbage-helps) · [Jewish Food Society: home and collections](https://www.jewishfoodsociety.org) · [Pasta Grannies: All recipes](https://www.pastagrannies.com/all-recipes/)
**Refs:**
- [Jewish Food Society: a great-grandmother's stuffed cabbage](https://www.jewishfoodsociety.org/stories/on-sukkot-a-great-grandmothers-stuffed-cabbage-helps): recipe, migration story (Poland → New York → St. Louis → Jerusalem) and a 1940s family photo together.
- [Pasta Grannies: All recipes](https://www.pastagrannies.com/all-recipes/): recipes named after the person who cooks them, with time, difficulty and serves on each card.

<a id="216"></a>
#### 216 · Genealogy / Family History (`lineage`)
**For:** family historians and one-name-study researchers who want to publish their tree and sources without running GEDCOM software.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-person (surname index) · single-person · archive-family · archive-place · single-place · archive-source · page-anniversaries (this month's births/marriages/deaths) · page-about-the-study · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** person page (vital events: birth/baptism, marriage, death/burial with date, place and source), parents link, spouse(s) and children list, siblings, life notes/biography with footnoted sources, media (census images, certificates, headstones, photos), pedigree chart (4 generations), descendants list, surname index A–Z, places index with map, sources list, "this month in the family" anniversaries, living-person privacy notice, "is this your ancestor? contact us" form.
**Content model:** `person` CPT with companion relation meta: `father`, `mother`, `spouses[]` (with marriage date/place), plus events (type, date, date-qualifier "abt/bef/aft", place relation, source relation). `place` CPT (lat/long). `source` CPT (repository, citation). Children and siblings are derived by querying persons whose `father`/`mother` match. No GEDCOM import required; a CSV import is optional.
**Plugins:** Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (places); Jetpack Forms (contact/corrections).
**Signature:** a person page linking straight to parents, spouse's family and children, with details of living or recent people withheld automatically ("Details withheld") (seen on: [Hardcastle One-Name Study: person page](https://hardcastle.one-name.net/getperson.php?personID=I1&tree=1)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Automatic privacy: anyone without a death date and born under 100 years ago shows only their name, because of the living-person rule (trust & proof, owner QoL). (seen on: [Hardcastle: M.J. Bayliss-Hardcastle](https://hardcastle.one-name.net/getperson.php?personID=I30432&tree=1))
- Media browsable by type (census, baptisms, headstones, military, wills) (local & practical). (seen on: [Hardcastle One-Name Study: home](https://hardcastle.one-name.net/index.php))
- An "anniversaries this month" page generated from event dates (community). (seen on: [Hardcastle One-Name Study: home, anniversaries link](https://hardcastle.one-name.net/index.php))
- Date qualifiers (abt., bef., aft.) and "last modified" on every person (trust & proof).
- A printable family group sheet per couple (content & tools), and schema.org `Person` with `parent`/`spouse`/`children` (owner QoL).
**Style: Parish register** (the ledger of a record office: ruled columns, reference numbers, restrained serif)
- Type: Names: Caudex 700 at clamp(2.75rem, 8vw, 6rem); body: PT Serif 400/18px; dates, IDs (I30432, F1) and citations: IBM Plex Mono 400/15px.
- Palette: register paper #FBFBF8 bg · iron-gall ink #1F2430 text · archive red #9E2B25 for reference numbers and links · ledger rule #C9C4B8 · withheld grey panel #EEEDE8 with ink text (not grey text).
- Layout: the person page is a ruled ledger: a left column of event types, then date, place and source columns, with family relations beneath as an indented tree of links (father / mother, then spouse → children). Surname index as a dense A–Z register. Pedigree chart drawn with SVG hairlines, not boxes with shadows. Square corners throughout; inputs 2px.
- Imagery: scans of real documents and headstones at their true proportions, with a mono citation line under each; portrait photos in original tone.
- Motion: none. Hovering a relation link highlights that person's row in the pedigree chart (colour only).
- Why it fits now: serious amateur history sites are moving away from dated TNG/PHP layouts towards clean, source-first pages, and the register look carries archival trust (example: [Hardcastle One-Name Study](https://hardcastle.one-name.net/index.php), the content model to modernise).
**Style variations:** Register: red #9E2B25 references · Census: blue-black #1B2A4A, form-green #E7EFE6 panels · Chapel: black and white only, rules at 2px
**Real-world basis:** [Hardcastle One-Name Study: person I1](https://hardcastle.one-name.net/getperson.php?personID=I1&tree=1) · [Hardcastle: person I30432](https://hardcastle.one-name.net/getperson.php?personID=I30432&tree=1) · [Hardcastle: home (media types, anniversaries)](https://hardcastle.one-name.net/index.php) · [Guild of One-Name Studies: members' websites](https://one-name.org/about-members-websites/)
**Refs:**
- [Hardcastle One-Name Study: person page](https://hardcastle.one-name.net/getperson.php?personID=I1&tree=1): parents, children with birth place and date, family group links, and living-person details withheld.
- [Guild of One-Name Studies: members' websites](https://one-name.org/about-members-websites/): who publishes these sites and why a hosted, low-maintenance option matters to them.

<a id="217"></a>
#### 217 · Reading Log (`reading`)
**For:** readers who keep a list of every book they finish, with notes, and want it on their own site instead of Goodreads.
**Templates:** front-page (currently reading + recent) · archive-book · single-book (notes) · taxonomy-year · taxonomy-shelf (to-read / read / abandoned) · page-recommended · page-about
**Patterns (~22):** currently-reading block, reverse-chronological read list (title, author, date finished), book notes page (ISBN, date read, recommendation score, summary, highlights), "how strongly I recommend it" score, top picks list, year index with count per year, shelf filter, bookshelf list with marks for great/above-average, buy link (Bookshop.org / library search), quotes list.
**Content model:** `book` CPT (author, ISBN, date_finished, rating 1–10, shelf taxonomy, format, cover). Year is derived from date_finished for archives.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (order by date_finished, filter by year); Query Filter (shelf, rating).
**Signature:** each book gets a notes page headed with ISBN, date read and "how strongly I recommend it: 8/10", and the index can be sorted by that score (seen on: [Derek Sivers: Four Thousand Weeks](https://sive.rs/book/4000Weeks)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Bold for "particularly great" and italic for "above average" in a plain list, which works without stars (local & practical). (seen on: [Patrick Collison: Bookshelf](https://patrickcollison.com/bookshelf))
- A simple title / author / date list going back decades, each linking to its review (content & tools). (seen on: [Tom MacWright: Reading](https://macwright.com/reading))
- A "library first" link (the reader's local library catalogue search by ISBN) next to the Bookshop.org link (community, conversion).
- A books-per-year count as a sentence at the top of each year archive ("41 books in 2026"), not a stat row (content & tools).
- schema.org `Book` + `Review` with the rating (owner QoL).
**Style: Library catalogue card** (typewritten catalogue cards, call numbers and date stamps)
- Type: Headings: Quattrocento 700 at clamp(3rem, 8vw, 6.5rem); body: Quattrocento 400/19px; ISBNs, dates and scores: Courier Prime 400/16px.
- Palette: catalogue card #FFFFFF bg · ink #1E1E1E text · date-stamp purple-red #8C1D40 for scores and dates (a stamp colour, not violet) · drawer oak #C9B38A for the year tabs · rule #D8D4CB.
- Layout: the index is a long ruled list set like a card drawer: year tabs down the left edge, entries as single lines (date · title · author · score). A book page is one large catalogue card with call-number style metadata at the top and notes below at 66ch. Covers are optional thumbnails at 2:3, 0 radius.
- Imagery: real cover scans or photos of the physical copy; no mock 3D books.
- Motion: none. The year tab of the current section stays sticky while scrolling (position: sticky only).
- Why it fits now: people are leaving Goodreads for self-hosted reading lists with their own notes and scoring (example: [Derek Sivers: Books](https://sive.rs/book)).
**Style variations:** Stamp: #8C1D40 dates · Paperback: orange spine #E8641B tabs, black ink · Reading Room: green-shade #2E5E4E header, brass #B08D57 rules
**Real-world basis:** [Derek Sivers: Books](https://sive.rs/book) · [Derek Sivers: Four Thousand Weeks](https://sive.rs/book/4000Weeks) · [Patrick Collison: Bookshelf](https://patrickcollison.com/bookshelf) · [Tom MacWright: Reading](https://macwright.com/reading)
**Refs:**
- [Derek Sivers: Four Thousand Weeks](https://sive.rs/book/4000Weeks): ISBN, date read, a 1–10 recommendation score and dense notes; the model for single-book.
- [Tom MacWright: Reading](https://macwright.com/reading): two decades of books as a plain title/author/date list linking to reviews.
- [Patrick Collison: Bookshelf](https://patrickcollison.com/bookshelf): typographic marks (bold/italic) instead of stars.

<a id="218"></a>
#### 218 · Photo-a-Day Journal (`daily`)
**For:** people doing a 365 project or a years-long daily photo habit who want their journal on their own site (Blipfoto and Flickr group refugees).
**Templates:** front-page (today + recent days) · single-day · archive-year (calendar grid) · archive-month · taxonomy-place · page-about-the-project · page-rules
**Patterns (~20):** today's entry (date, title, photo, short text), calendar month grid with a thumbnail per day, previous/next day navigation, "one year ago today" link, EXIF line (camera, shutter, aperture, focal length, ISO), place tags, entry count and start date, streak/missed-day marker, favourites, comments, project rules page.
**Content model:** `day` CPT whose slug is the date (2026-09-18). One entry per date is enforced by the companion plugin. EXIF is read from the attachment into meta and shown via Block Bindings. Place taxonomy.
**Plugins:** none (EXIF comes from core's attachment metadata). Optional Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap for a map of places.
**Signature:** a single-day page with the camera's EXIF line under the photo, previous/next-day arrows and a jump to the same day one year earlier (seen on: [Blipfoto: "Closing down", 18 September 2026](https://www.blipfoto.com/entry/3547620153132844668)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- One photo per calendar day, enforced, with the EXIF capture date checked against the entry date (trust & proof). (seen on: [Flickr: 365 Days group rules](https://www.flickr.com/groups/365days/))
- A running total ("4,613 entries since 2013") in the header as a sentence (community). (seen on: [Blipfoto: Cheeryoscuro](https://www.blipfoto.com/Cheeryoscuro))
- A catch-up rule: missed days can be backfilled with the real capture date (limit per day) and are marked as late (operational). (seen on: [Flickr: 365 Days group rules](https://www.flickr.com/groups/365days/))
- Alt text required before publishing, shown as a caption toggle (accessibility).
- A year-in-review contact sheet page that prints as an A3 poster (content & tools).
**Style: Contact sheet** (a photographer's proof sheet: frame numbers, grease-pencil marks, strict grid)
- Type: Headings/dates: RX100 400 (Fontshare, signage monospace like film-edge numbers) at clamp(3rem, 12vw, 9rem); body: Figtree 400/18px; EXIF and frame numbers: JetBrains Mono 400/14px (captions only; body stays 18px).
- Palette: light-table white #F6F6F4 bg · film-rebate black #121212 for the calendar grid gutters and text · grease-pencil red #D1261F for today's circle and favourites · frame-number amber #C98A1B · rule #CFCFCB.
- Layout: the home page shows today's photo big (up to 85vh, native ratio), with the date set huge beside it. Below is the month as a contact-sheet grid: 7 columns, black rebate gutters and mono day numbers printed in the gutter like frame numbers. Missed days are empty frames. Today is ringed in red. 0 radius on everything, since photos are never rounded.
- Imagery: the owner's own photos, uncropped and at their original aspect ratio; grid thumbnails are cropped square only in the calendar view.
- Motion: View Transitions between a calendar thumbnail and the single-day page (the image morphs into place). Reduced motion falls back to an instant swap. No hover zoom.
- Why it fits now: long-running daily photo communities like Blipfoto still thrive, and people want their own archive with the calendar-and-EXIF habits intact (example: [Blipfoto: Cheeryoscuro](https://www.blipfoto.com/Cheeryoscuro)).
**Style variations:** Light Table: white, red #D1261F marks · Darkroom: #1A1A1A bg with #F2F2F2 text and amber #C98A1B marks · Polaroid: white frames with thick bottom border on #ECE9E4
**Real-world basis:** [Blipfoto: Cheeryoscuro journal](https://www.blipfoto.com/Cheeryoscuro) · [Blipfoto: single entry](https://www.blipfoto.com/entry/3547620153132844668) · [Flickr: 365 Days group](https://www.flickr.com/groups/365days/)
**Refs:**
- [Blipfoto: single entry](https://www.blipfoto.com/entry/3547620153132844668): title, photo, short text, EXIF (camera, shutter, aperture, focal length, ISO), place tags, previous/next day and "one year ago".
- [Flickr: 365 Days group](https://www.flickr.com/groups/365days/): community rules that make a daily project credible: one photo per day, EXIF-dated, limited catch-up.

### XXIII. Heritage, museums & archives

<a id="219"></a>
#### 219 · Small Museum (`museum`)
**For:** single-building museums, historic houses and collection trusts with a small staff, free or low-cost entry and a volunteer front desk.
**Templates:** front-page · page-visit · archive-exhibition · single-exhibition · archive-event · single-event · archive-object · single-object · page-support · page-venue-hire
**Patterns (~45):** "Open today" header strip (hours pulled from the weekly schedule), visit block (days, last admission, free entry or price, "no need to pre-book"), free tours timetable (tour name, days, time, max group size, "first come, first served"), group bookings note (8+ must book), house rules list (bags, touching, flash, tripods), getting here (address, nearest station, buses, bike docks), exhibition hero with run dates, object feature (image, caption, accession number, "see in the collection" link), related events list, membership/friends box, admission price sidebar (with/without Gift Aid donation), venue hire and filming enquiry.
**Content model:** `exhibition` (start, end, floor, access note), `object` (accession no., date, maker, material, dimensions, credit line), `event` (date, time, price, capacity), companion "opening hours" option set (weekly hours + exception dates), all shown via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (current / upcoming / past exhibitions), Jetpack Forms (group and venue-hire enquiries), Jetpack Donations or GiveWP.
**Signature:** a site-wide "Open today 10am–3pm" / "Closed today" strip computed from the opening-hours set and exception dates, so bank holidays and install weeks update themselves (seen on: [Garden Museum](https://www.gardenmuseum.org.uk/visit/), and as "Open today, Saturday 26 September" on [Museum of the Home](https://museumofthehome.org.uk/plan-your-visit/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- House-rules block for bags, cloakroom, touching and photography, written in plain sentences (seen on: [Sir John Soane's Museum: your visit](https://www.soane.org/your-visit))
- Free-tour timetable with daily times and maximum group sizes (seen on: [Sir John Soane's Museum: your visit](https://www.soane.org/your-visit))
- Admission shown "with donation / without donation" so Gift Aid is explained at the point of paying (seen on: [Freud Museum: 40 Objects, 40 Years](https://www.freud.org.uk/exhibitions/40-objects-40-years/))
- Access note on each exhibition ("first floor, lift available") bound from exhibition meta (seen on: [Freud Museum: 40 Objects, 40 Years](https://www.freud.org.uk/exhibitions/40-objects-40-years/))
- Virtual tour link for people who can't visit in person (seen on: [Freud Museum: virtual tour](https://www.freud.org.uk/visit/virtual-tour/))
**Style: Editorial serif revival (museum label and printed catalogue)**
- Type: Headings Yrsa 600 at 5–7rem with normal tracking; body Yrsa 400 at 19px; accession numbers, dates and dimensions in IBM Plex Mono 500 at 14px, set like a wall label.
- Palette: bg #F2F0EB (gallery wall), text #1B1B1A, accent oxblood #7A1F2B for links and the open/closed strip, surface #E4E0D6 for label cards, line #1B1B1A at 1px.
- Layout: 12-column grid with a wide left margin for captions; object images sit off-centre with the label block hanging beside them, never centred. Nav is a plain top row (Visit, What's on, Collection, Support); home leads with today's hours, then the current exhibition at full width, then two object features in an asymmetric pair.
- Imagery: straight, evenly lit object photography on neutral backgrounds, 4:5 and 1:1 crops, no overlays; exterior shots in overcast light.
- Motion: none on scroll. Object images use a View Transition from archive card to single page; link underlines thicken on hover. Reduced motion disables the transition.
- Why it fits now: museums are moving away from glossy campaign sites back to catalogue typography that reads like the printed labels in the room, e.g. [The Public Domain Review](https://publicdomainreview.org/).
**Style variations:** Night opening: #151515 bg, #E8E2D0 serif text · Label card: white bg, oxblood rule lines · Guidebook: two-column text, pale green #DDE5D8.
**Real-world basis:** [Sir John Soane's Museum: your visit](https://www.soane.org/your-visit), [Freud Museum: 40 Objects, 40 Years](https://www.freud.org.uk/exhibitions/40-objects-40-years/), [Garden Museum: visit](https://www.gardenmuseum.org.uk/visit/), [Museum of the Home: plan your visit](https://museumofthehome.org.uk/plan-your-visit/), [Pollock's Toy Museum: visit](https://www.pollockstoymuseum.co.uk/visit-pollocks-toy-museum/)
**Refs:**
- [Sir John Soane's Museum: your visit](https://www.soane.org/your-visit): the best single visit page in the set: hours, free entry, tour times, group rules and cloakroom all on one scroll.
- [Garden Museum: visit](https://www.gardenmuseum.org.uk/visit/): the "Open Today" strip in the header and a visit page split into museum, gardens and café.
- [Freud Museum: 40 Objects, 40 Years](https://www.freud.org.uk/exhibitions/40-objects-40-years/): exhibition page with run dates, access note, related talks and the admission-with-donation sidebar.

<a id="220"></a>
#### 220 · Local Historical Society (`archive`)
**For:** volunteer-run local history and civic societies with a talks programme, a membership list, a journal and a shelf of self-published books.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-event · single-event · page-publications · single-publication · archive-journal · page-membership · page-walks · page-plaques · page-research-enquiries · archive (news)
**Patterns (~40):** talks programme list (date, speaker, title, "illustrated Zoom talk" or venue), journal back-issue list (issue number, year, price, article titles, "Sold out" / "PDF available"), publications shelf (title, price, format, "Read more"), membership rates and join form, walking guides with route maps, plaques scheme (person, address, date unveiled, nomination link), buildings-at-risk list, AGM notice and minutes, research enquiry form, volunteer call-out.
**Content model:** `talk` (date, speaker, venue or online link, recording URL), `publication` (price, ISBN, format, stock status, PDF), `journal_issue` (number, year, contents list), `plaque` (person, address, lat/lng, unveiled), bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce (books and back issues), Advanced Query Loop (upcoming/past talks), Jetpack Forms (membership, research enquiries), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (plaques and walks).
**Signature:** a journal back-issue index where every issue lists its article titles, price and stock state ("Sold out", "available as PDF"), going back decades on one page (seen on: [Camden History Society: publications](https://www.camdenhistorysociety.org/publications)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Talk entries flagged "illustrated Zoom talk" or "in person" with the joining link sent to members (seen on: [Camden History Society: events](https://www.camdenhistorysociety.org/events))
- Printable walking-guide PDFs sold alongside the books (seen on: [Hackney Society: walking guides](https://www.hackneysociety.org/walking-guides/))
- Plaque nomination form and the story of each plaque, including who made it (seen on: [Hackney Society: plaques scheme](https://www.hackneysociety.org/planning/plaques-scheme/))
- Buildings-at-risk list members can add to (seen on: [Hackney Society: buildings at risk](https://www.hackneysociety.org/campaigns/buildings-at-risk-group/))
- Out-of-print titles as free PDF downloads, so the archive keeps working after stock runs out (seen on: [Camden History Society: publications](https://www.camdenhistorysociety.org/publications))
**Style: Card-catalogue archival**
- Type: Headings Lusitana 700; body Source Serif 4 at 18px; index-card fields (issue, year, price) in Courier Prime 400, like a typed catalogue card.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, card manila #EFE3C2, text #231F1A, library green #2F4A3A for nav and buttons, rubber-stamp red #B3261E for "Sold out", line #9C8B63.
- Layout: journal issues and books appear as ruled index cards in a tight grid with square corners and a punched-hole detail; talks are a dated ledger (date column left, title and speaker right). Home: next talk in large type, then the new publication, then the ledger.
- Imagery: archive photographs shown at their original proportions with a thin white border and a typed caption card; no cropping to 16:9.
- Motion: cards slide 4px when hovered like a card in a drawer (transform only); reduced motion removes it.
- Why it fits now: archival, card-and-block interfaces are back in fashion as a counter to feed layouts, e.g. [Are.na](https://www.are.na/).
**Style variations:** Minute book: ruled lines, black ink on white · Blue plaque: #1F4E8C with white Caslon · Lantern slide: #1A1A1A bg, sepia #C9B38A type.
**Real-world basis:** [Camden History Society: publications](https://www.camdenhistorysociety.org/publications), [Camden History Society: events](https://www.camdenhistorysociety.org/events), [Hackney Society: plaques scheme](https://www.hackneysociety.org/planning/plaques-scheme/), [Hackney Society: walking guides](https://www.hackneysociety.org/walking-guides/), [Hackney Society: buildings at risk](https://www.hackneysociety.org/campaigns/buildings-at-risk-group/)
**Refs:**
- [Camden History Society: publications](https://www.camdenhistorysociety.org/publications): journal issues back to 1973 with contents lists, prices and stock states.
- [Hackney Society: plaques scheme](https://www.hackneysociety.org/planning/plaques-scheme/): a society running its own plaques, with a custom typeface and a nomination route.
- [Camden History Society: events](https://www.camdenhistorysociety.org/events): a talks programme that mixes Zoom and in-person dates cleanly.

#### 221 · Oral History Project (`voices`)
**For:** community groups, unions, museums and campaign archives recording and publishing interviews with a defined group of people.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-interview · single-interview · taxonomy-subject · page-about-the-project · page-participate · page-teach · page-terms-of-use
**Patterns (~35):** numbered interview index (number, name, life dates, interview date), browse by number range (001–020, 021–040), browse by subject with interview counts, interview page (video or audio, full transcript, subject tags, interviewer, location), narrator list A–Z, "share your story" call-out, education/lesson plans block, terminology note, terms of use and credit line, funders.
**Content model:** `interview` (number, narrator, birth/death years, date, interviewer, place, duration, media URL, transcript PDF, rights), taxonomy `subject`, taxonomy `collection`, bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** Query Filter (subject and collection), companion transcript block (plain HTML transcript with speaker labels under the core Audio/Video block). No podcast plugin needed.
**Signature:** a numbered interview index that can be browsed by number range, alphabetically or by subject, so a 180-interview archive stays navigable without search (seen on: [ACT UP Oral History Project: numerical interviews](https://actuporalhistory.org/numerical-interviews) and [ACT UP: interview index](https://actuporalhistory.org/interview-index)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Full transcript on the page and as a PDF, with the interview number in the file name (seen on: [ACT UP: 002 Robert Vazquez-Pacheco](https://actuporalhistory.org/numerical-interviews/002-robert-vazquez-pacheco))
- Narrator index page listing every person interviewed (seen on: [Densho Digital Repository: narrators](https://ddr.densho.org/narrators/))
- Terminology page explaining the words the archive chooses to use and why (seen on: [Densho: terminology](https://densho.org/terminology/))
- "Share your collection" route for families holding their own recordings (seen on: [Densho: share your collections](https://densho.org/share-your-collections/))
- Lesson-plan downloads for teachers (seen on: [Densho: lesson plans](https://densho.org/teach/lesson-plans/))
**Style: Transcript-led typographic**
- Type: Transcript body in Literata 400 at 20px with 1.6 line height; speaker labels (Q:, name initials) and timecodes in Martian Mono 500; headings Spline Sans 700 at normal tracking.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #111111, cobalt #0047AB for links and the playhead, highlighter yellow #FFE45C behind the passage matching the current timecode, line #D0D0D0.
- Layout: single 68ch transcript column with a sticky media player above it; the interview number sits huge (12rem) in the left gutter. Index pages are dense tables: number, name, years, date. Home opens with a randomly chosen quote from a transcript and its interview number.
- Imagery: stills from the interview video in black and white at 16:9, archival photos labelled with their source; no stock portraits.
- Motion: clicking a timecode scrolls the player and moves the highlight; no autoplay. Reduced motion jumps without smooth scrolling.
- Why it fits now: publishers are putting full transcripts next to audio for access and search, and the transcript itself has become the design, e.g. [This American Life: episode 1 transcript](https://www.thisamericanlife.org/1/transcript).
**Style variations:** Tape: #F3EFE6 bg, brown #5B3A1E labels · Broadcast: black bg, white Literata, yellow highlight · Archive box: kraft #CBB38F header band.
**Real-world basis:** [ACT UP Oral History Project: numerical interviews](https://actuporalhistory.org/numerical-interviews), [ACT UP: interview index](https://actuporalhistory.org/interview-index), [Densho: oral history collection](https://densho.org/collections/oral-history/), [Densho Digital Repository: narrators](https://ddr.densho.org/narrators/), [StoryCorps: stories](https://storycorps.org/stories/)
**Refs:**
- [ACT UP: interview index](https://actuporalhistory.org/interview-index): subject index with interview numbers, names and dates under each campaign.
- [Densho Digital Repository: narrators](https://ddr.densho.org/narrators/): a narrator directory as the front door to a large archive.
- [StoryCorps: stories](https://storycorps.org/stories/): short, titled story pages that pull one moment out of a long interview.

#### 222 · Heritage Railway (`steam`)
**For:** volunteer-run preserved railways and tramways selling day tickets, experiences and memberships.
**Templates:** front-page · page-timetable · archive-event · single-event · page-fares · archive-experience · single-experience · page-locomotives · page-plan-your-visit · page-accessibility · page-support · archive (news)
**Patterns (~50):** running-day calendar (click a date to see the timetable, events and engines), fares table (adult, child, family, rover, donation/basic price), weekly locomotive roster (date, loco number and class, event), special-event trains (Santa, gin train, scare train), experience cards (footplate, brake van, driver for a fiver), rolling-stock pages, station facilities per stop, dogs on trains page, railway accessibility (wheelchair space in which coach), webcams, 200 Club / membership, adopt-a-loco appeal, vacancies and volunteering.
**Content model:** `running_day` (date, timetable code, loco IDs, event IDs), `timetable` (code, departures per station), `locomotive` (number, class, builder, year, status: in service / overhaul), `experience` (price, duration, age limits), bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce (experiences, gift vouchers, merchandise; day tickets can stay on the railway's existing ticketing), Advanced Query Loop (upcoming events), companion running-day calendar block (Interactivity API).
**Signature:** a date-picker calendar where each running day opens its timetable, special events and the engines rostered for that day (seen on: [Talyllyn Railway: timetable](https://www.talyllyn.co.uk/plan/timetable)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Weekly roster of which locomotive is running, for enthusiasts who plan around a specific engine (seen on: [Keighley & Worth Valley Railway: weekly roster](https://kwvr.co.uk/about-the-railway/weekly-roster/))
- Fares table showing the basic price and the Gift Aid donation price side by side (seen on: [Talyllyn Railway: timetable and fares](https://www.talyllyn.co.uk/plan/timetable))
- Dogs page: dogs welcome in 3rd class for £5, one dog-free carriage on every train (seen on: [Talyllyn Railway: dog friendly](https://www.talyllyn.co.uk/dogs))
- Station webcams page (seen on: [Keighley & Worth Valley Railway: webcams](https://kwvr.co.uk/about-the-railway/webcams/))
- Footplate and other experiences sold as gift vouchers from the main menu (seen on: [KWVR: footplate experience](https://kwvr.co.uk/experiences/footplate-experience/))
**Style: Utility/industrial signage (railway timetable)**
- Type: Headings Josefin Sans 700 at 6rem; body Barlow 400 at 18px; departure times in Overpass Mono 600 with tabular figures.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #0E0E0E, railway blue #003F7D for header and running-day cells, signal yellow #F2C200 for "special event" days, line #0E0E0E at 2px.
- Layout: timetable-first. Home shows today's (or the next) running day as a departure board with columns per station, then the calendar, then events. Hard 2px rules, no radius anywhere except the round loco number discs. Nav is a station-sign bar.
- Imagery: documentary photos of engines in steam and volunteers at work, 3:2 crops, some black-and-white archive shots with dates.
- Motion: calendar cells swap content with a quick crossfade; departure board has no flip animation. Reduced motion shows static content.
- Why it fits now: public-signage typography (Kinneir and Calvert's road and rail systems) is being reissued and studied, and suits an organisation whose whole product is a timetable, e.g. [Jock Kinneir Library](https://jockkinneirlibrary.org/).
**Style variations:** Maroon coach: #5E1B24 bg, cream-white #F4F1E8 type · Diesel: #1F5C3A green, yellow warning panel · Night mail: #0B1B2B bg, #F2C200 times.
**Real-world basis:** [Talyllyn Railway: timetable](https://www.talyllyn.co.uk/plan/timetable), [Talyllyn Railway: dog friendly](https://www.talyllyn.co.uk/dogs), [KWVR: weekly roster](https://kwvr.co.uk/about-the-railway/weekly-roster/), [KWVR: footplate experience](https://kwvr.co.uk/experiences/footplate-experience/), [Ffestiniog & Welsh Highland Railways: locomotives](https://www.festrail.co.uk/locomotives/)
**Refs:**
- [Talyllyn Railway: timetable](https://www.talyllyn.co.uk/plan/timetable): the click-a-date calendar tying timetable, events and engines together.
- [KWVR: weekly roster](https://kwvr.co.uk/about-the-railway/weekly-roster/): a plain table of date, locomotive and event that enthusiasts rely on.
- [KWVR: 200 Club](https://kwvr.co.uk/support/200-club/): a small recurring-support scheme presented simply.

#### 223 · "Friends of" a Park or Cemetery (`friends`)
**For:** volunteer "Friends of" groups that look after a public park, nature reserve or historic cemetery with the council.
**Templates:** front-page · page-visit · archive-event · single-event · page-grave-research · page-nature · archive-habitat · page-volunteer · page-membership · page-donate · archive (news) · page-constitution
**Patterns (~40):** visit block (gates, opening times, rules, map PDF), events calendar (guided walks, fungi foray, open day, bat walk), grave enquiry / search service (what to find first, fee, booking), burial-records guidance (where registers are held), monumental inscriptions volunteer sessions, biodiversity and habitat pages, species highlights, volunteering days, corporate volunteering, membership and donate, newsletter archive, AGM minutes and constitution.
**Content model:** `event` (date, meeting point, booking link, capacity), `habitat` (name, species list, season), `notable_grave` (name, dates, square/grave number, lat/lng), bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** The Events Calendar (walks and work parties, with iCal export), Jetpack Forms (grave enquiries, volunteer sign-up), GiveWP or Jetpack Donations, Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap.
**Signature:** a grave search service page that tells people what to gather first (name, burial date, grave and square number), what is included and the fee, then books an accompanied visit (seen on: [Highgate Cemetery: grave searches](https://highgatecemetery.org/graves/searches) and [Friends of Tower Hamlets Cemetery Park: grave enquiries](https://fothcp.org/grave-enquiries-research/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Seasonal capacity note ("we can help less in summer; visit September–April") on the research page (seen on: [FoTHCP: grave enquiries](https://fothcp.org/grave-enquiries-research/))
- Monumental inscriptions volunteer sessions with fixed monthly dates and a named contact (seen on: [Nunhead Cemetery: monumental inscriptions](https://www.nunheadcemetery.org.uk/join-us/monumental-inscriptions))
- Explore pages split by architecture, ecology, history and remembrance (seen on: [Nunhead Cemetery: ecology](https://www.nunheadcemetery.org.uk/explore/category/ecology))
- Biodiversity page listing habitats and species, useful for grant applications (seen on: [FoTHCP: our biodiversity](https://fothcp.org/our-biodiversity/))
- Visitor rules and a downloadable location map PDF (seen on: [Highgate Cemetery: visitor information](https://highgatecemetery.org/visit))
**Style: Botanical field-guide riso**
- Type: Headings Averia Serif Libre 700; body Alegreya 400 at 18px; species labels and Latin names in Alegreya Sans SC 500.
- Palette: bg #F2F5F2 (leaf-litter paper, faintly green), ink #1D2B24, riso green #00A95C for nav and dates, fluorescent pink #FF48B0 used once per page as an overprint on illustrations, line #1D2B24.
- Layout: field-guide spreads: a species or monument on the left in a narrow column, a large two-colour illustration on the right. Events in a dated list with month dividers. Home: next walk, then "in season now" (three species), then how to help.
- Imagery: two-colour riso-style drawings of leaves, lichens and headstones, plus real photos of volunteers at work sessions in natural light.
- Motion: illustrations shift their pink layer 2px on hover to show misregistration; reduced motion keeps them aligned and still.
- Why it fits now: rewilding and nature-recovery projects present land with field-notes restraint rather than glossy tourism layouts, e.g. [Knepp](https://knepp.co.uk/).
**Style variations:** Winter: #E9EEF0 bg, slate #2E3A40 ink · Bluebell: riso blue #0078BF overprint · Dusk walk: #13201A bg, #F2F5F2 type.
**Real-world basis:** [Highgate Cemetery: grave searches](https://highgatecemetery.org/graves/searches), [FoTHCP: grave enquiries](https://fothcp.org/grave-enquiries-research/), [FoTHCP: events](https://fothcp.org/events/), [Nunhead Cemetery: monumental inscriptions](https://www.nunheadcemetery.org.uk/join-us/monumental-inscriptions), [Highgate Cemetery: visitor information](https://highgatecemetery.org/visit)
**Refs:**
- [Highgate Cemetery: grave searches](https://highgatecemetery.org/graves/searches): a paid research service described in one short, clear page.
- [Nunhead Cemetery: ecology](https://www.nunheadcemetery.org.uk/explore/category/ecology): the "explore" taxonomy that treats a cemetery as a nature reserve too.
- [FoTHCP: our biodiversity](https://fothcp.org/our-biodiversity/): a volunteer group documenting its own land.

<a id="224"></a>
#### 224 · Community Digitised Collection (`digitise`)
**For:** community archives, camera clubs, local libraries and volunteer projects publishing scanned photographs, maps and documents.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-item · single-item · taxonomy-keyword · page-keywords-a-z · archive-collection · single-collection · page-map · page-album · page-contribute · page-takedown · page-about
**Patterns (~40):** item record (image, catalogue number, title, date, description, keywords, copyright line, "add to album"), keyword A–Z index, advanced search form, themed collections grid, map view of items, story/essay pages linking items, contributors list, credits and funders, contribute-your-photos form, takedown policy, help page, new additions list.
**Content model:** `item` (catalogue no., date or date range, creator, source collection, rights statement, lat/lng, IIIF/image URL), taxonomies `keyword`, `place`, `collection`, bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** Query Filter (keyword, place, decade), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap, Jetpack Forms (contributions with the File Upload field, takedown requests).
**Signature:** an item record built around the catalogue number, with every keyword linking to a keyword page and an "add to my album" button that keeps a personal selection (seen on: [TheGlasgowStory: image TGSE01403](https://www.theglasgowstory.com/image/?inum=TGSE01403) and [TheGlasgowStory: keywords](https://www.theglasgowstory.com/keywords/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Keyword A–Z page as a complete public index (seen on: [TheGlasgowStory: keywords](https://www.theglasgowstory.com/keywords/))
- Takedown policy page for rights holders and families (seen on: [Layers of London: takedown policy](https://www.layersoflondon.org/takedown-policy))
- Themed collections contributed by different organisations (seen on: [Historypin: LGBTQ America collection](https://www.historypin.org/collections/1357/))
- Map as a first-class way in (seen on: [Layers of London: map](https://www.layersoflondon.org/map))
- Copyright and credit line printed on every record so reuse is clear (seen on: [TheGlasgowStory: image TGSE01403](https://www.theglasgowstory.com/image/?inum=TGSE01403))
**Style: Swiss neo-grotesk dense index**
- Type: Headings and body in Synonym (Fontshare) 500/400, headings at 4.5rem; catalogue numbers and dates in IBM Plex Mono 400 at 14px.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #000000, signal red #E30613 for catalogue numbers and the active filter, surface #F0F0F0, line #BDBDBD.
- Layout: a strict 12-column grid; the archive is a dense table-and-thumbnail list (thumb, number, title, date, place) with sortable headers, switchable to a contact-sheet grid. Item pages: image at 8 columns, metadata as a definition list in 4. Home: newest additions, a keyword cloud set as a plain comma list, then collections.
- Imagery: scans shown whole with their borders, film rebates and handwriting; never cropped or colour-graded.
- Motion: table rows highlight on hover; a View Transition carries the thumbnail into the item page. Reduced motion removes it.
- Why it fits now: publishers and archives favour data-dense, grid-true catalogues over card carousels, e.g. [Lars Müller Publishers](https://www.lars-mueller-publishers.com/).
**Style variations:** Contact sheet: black bg, white numbers · Glass plate: #EAE7DF bg, sepia ink · Ordnance: #F4F7F2 bg, OS green #2E6B3F.
**Real-world basis:** [TheGlasgowStory: image record](https://www.theglasgowstory.com/image/?inum=TGSE01403), [TheGlasgowStory: keywords](https://www.theglasgowstory.com/keywords/), [Layers of London: map](https://www.layersoflondon.org/map), [Historypin: collections](https://www.historypin.org/collections/), [The Public Domain Review: collections](https://publicdomainreview.org/collections/)
**Refs:**
- [TheGlasgowStory: image TGSE01403](https://www.theglasgowstory.com/image/?inum=TGSE01403): a complete, honest item record with catalogue number, keywords and copyright line.
- [Layers of London: takedown policy](https://www.layersoflondon.org/takedown-policy): the legal page every community archive needs.
- [The Public Domain Review: collections](https://publicdomainreview.org/collections/): how to write short, readable context around scanned material.
