### XXIV. Making, manufacturing & small B2B

<a id="225"></a>
#### 225 · Laser / CNC Cutting Service (`cut`)
**For:** small laser and CNC bureaux cutting acrylic, plywood, card and sheet metal for designers, architects' model makers, shopfitters and hobbyists.
**Templates:** front-page · page-get-a-quote · archive-material · single-material · page-services · page-getting-started · page-drawing-resources · archive-case-study · single-case-study · page-faq · page-contact
**Patterns (~45):** quote form with file upload (accepted formats, max size), "what to tell us" checklist (material, thickness, quantity, deadline, delivery or collection), materials library (material, thicknesses, colours, sheet size, notes on edge finish), per-material page with laser settings notes, drawing guidelines (line colours for cut vs engrave, minimum feature size, kerf), downloadable templates, services list (cutting, engraving, drawing service, finishing), case studies, FAQ (tolerances, "what if I don't have a CAD file"), turnaround note, referral page.
**Content model:** `material` (thicknesses, sheet sizes, colours, price per sheet or per cm² band, min feature size), `case_study` (client, material, process, photos), bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (quote form with the File Upload field for AI/DXF/SVG/PDF), WooCommerce (sample packs and stock sizes), companion sheet-cost estimator block (Interactivity API).
**Signature:** a two-step quote form that takes the cutting file (AI, PDF, SVG, DXF, DWG, ZIP up to 256 MB) with a checklist of what to include and a same-day reply promise, next to a live sheet-cost estimator (material × thickness × sheet count) for a ballpark before uploading (form seen on: [CutLaserCut: get a quote](https://cutlasercut.com/get-a-quote/); calculator approach seen on: [SendCutSend: bending calculator](https://sendcutsend.com/bending-calculator/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Reply-time note that is honest about Friday afternoons ("after 5pm Friday we reply Monday") (seen on: [CutLaserCut: get a quote](https://cutlasercut.com/get-a-quote/))
- Drawing resources page with templates and line-colour rules (seen on: [CutLaserCut: drawing resources](https://cutlasercut.com/drawing-resources/))
- Free material sample offer (seen on: [Ponoko: materials](https://www.ponoko.com/materials))
- Per-material pages with thicknesses and what each is good for (seen on: [RazorLAB: acrylic](https://razorlab.online/laser-cutting-and-engraving-materials-overview/acrylic/))
- Tolerance and "no CAD file?" FAQ answers linked from the form (seen on: [SendCutSend: FAQ](https://sendcutsend.com/faq/what-is-your-cut-tolerance/))
**Style: Technical-drawing / CAD utility**
- Type: Headings Bai Jamjuree 600 at 5rem; body IBM Plex Sans 400 at 17px; dimensions, thicknesses and prices in IBM Plex Mono 500.
- Palette: bg #FAFBFC, ink #0B1F33, cut-line red #E4002B (the colour laser files use for cut paths), engrave blue #1F5FBF, construction grey #9FB3C8 for gridlines on product shots only.
- Layout: pages framed like a drawing sheet with a title block in the footer (company, scale, date, sheet no.). Materials as a spec table with thickness columns. Home: quote form at the top right beside a photo of the machine bed, then materials table, then recent jobs.
- Imagery: top-down photos of cut parts on the honeycomb bed, macro shots of edges, dimensioned line drawings in red and blue hairlines.
- Motion: estimator figures update in place without animation; hairline outlines draw on hover over case-study thumbnails (stroke-dashoffset). Reduced motion shows the finished line.
- Why it fits now: makers trust sites that show the file rules and tolerances plainly, like a drawing sheet, e.g. [CutLaserCut: drawing resources](https://cutlasercut.com/drawing-resources/).
**Style variations:** Blueprint: #0B3D91 bg, white linework · Plywood: #E8D3B0 surface, black ink · Night shift: #111418 bg, red #FF3B30 cut lines.
**Real-world basis:** [CutLaserCut: get a quote](https://cutlasercut.com/get-a-quote/), [CutLaserCut: materials](https://cutlasercut.com/materials/), [RazorLAB: materials overview](https://razorlab.online/laser-cutting-and-engraving-materials-overview/acrylic/), [SendCutSend: materials](https://sendcutsend.com/materials/), [Ponoko: laser cutting](https://www.ponoko.com/laser-cutting)
**Refs:**
- [CutLaserCut: get a quote](https://cutlasercut.com/get-a-quote/): the upload form, file types and what-to-include checklist.
- [SendCutSend: bending calculator](https://sendcutsend.com/bending-calculator/): a small calculator page that answers a technical question before the customer orders.
- [SendCutSend: sheet cutting guidelines](https://sendcutsend.com/guidelines/sheet-cutting/): minimum features and file rules laid out as a reference.

<a id="226"></a>
#### 226 · 3D Printing Service (`layer`)
**For:** small 3D print bureaux (FDM, SLS, MJF, resin) doing prototypes, batch parts and design help.
**Templates:** front-page · page-upload-for-quote · archive-material · single-material · page-materials-comparison · page-finishes · archive-case-study · single-case-study · page-design-service · page-guides · page-quality-control
**Patterns (~40):** upload-for-quote form (STL/STEP/3MF/OBJ), materials comparison chart (strength, detail, flexibility, heat, rated 0–5), finishes table (natural, vibro polished, shot peened, vapour smoothed, with added cost and minimum wall), colour options table, order-type availability (express, economy, trade, scheduled), design rules guide (wall thickness, escape holes, tolerances), case studies by industry, CAD design service, quality control statement, prototype vs batch production pages.
**Content model:** `material` (process, properties 0–5, min wall, max build size, colours, lead time), `finish` (cost modifier, min thickness, compatible materials), `case_study` (industry, material, quantity), bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (upload with the File Upload field), companion price estimator block (volume × material rate × finish, with a quantity break table), Query Filter (case studies by industry).
**Signature:** a materials comparison chart where visitors toggle materials on and off and compare rated properties, with finish and colour cost tables underneath (seen on: [3DPRINTUK: materials comparison](https://www.3dprint-uk.co.uk/3d-printed-materials-comparison)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Post-processing finishes comparison page with photos of each finish (seen on: [3DPRINTUK: finishes comparison](https://www.3dprint-uk.co.uk/3d-printed-post-processing-finishes-comparison/))
- Upload-first quote page that accepts common 3D file formats (seen on: [Craftcloud: upload](https://craftcloud3d.com/en/upload))
- Material guide written for non-engineers (seen on: [Craftcloud: material guide](https://craftcloud3d.com/en/material-guide))
- Design guides library (wall thickness, tolerances) linked from each material (seen on: [3DPRINTUK: 3D printing guides](https://www.3dprint-uk.co.uk/3d-printing-guides/))
- Quality control page stating how parts are checked before dispatch (seen on: [3DPRINTUK: quality control](https://www.3dprint-uk.co.uk/3d-printing-quality-control/))
**Style: Dither / 1-bit bitmap**
- Type: Headings Exo 2 800 at 6rem; body IBM Plex Sans 400 at 17px; specs and property scores in Spline Sans Mono 400.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #000000, filament orange #FF6A13 as the only colour (buttons, active toggles), surface #EDEDED, line #000000.
- Layout: a tight 8-column grid with 1px black rules; property charts drawn as stepped bar blocks rather than smooth lines. Home: upload box first, then the comparison chart, then a strip of part photos.
- Imagery: part photos processed to 1-bit ordered dither in the hero and case-study thumbnails, with the full-colour photo on the single page; layer lines shown in macro shots.
- Motion: toggling a material redraws its bars in steps (CSS steps() timing); reduced motion swaps instantly.
- Why it fits now: dithered, low-bandwidth imagery has become a design stance for technical and sustainability-minded sites, e.g. [Low-tech Magazine](https://solar.lowtechmagazine.com/).
**Style variations:** Resin: #F4F4F4 bg, amber #FFB000 accent · Nylon: white bg, grey #5A5A5A dither · Print farm: #000000 bg, orange type.
**Real-world basis:** [3DPRINTUK: materials comparison](https://www.3dprint-uk.co.uk/3d-printed-materials-comparison), [3DPRINTUK: finishes comparison](https://www.3dprint-uk.co.uk/3d-printed-post-processing-finishes-comparison/), [3DPRINTUK: services](https://www.3dprint-uk.co.uk/3d-printing-services/), [Craftcloud: upload](https://craftcloud3d.com/en/upload), [Craftcloud: material guide](https://craftcloud3d.com/en/material-guide)
**Refs:**
- [3DPRINTUK: materials comparison](https://www.3dprint-uk.co.uk/3d-printed-materials-comparison): comparison chart plus finish and colour cost tables on one page.
- [Craftcloud: upload](https://craftcloud3d.com/en/upload): an upload-first quote flow.
- [3DPRINTUK: finishes comparison](https://www.3dprint-uk.co.uk/3d-printed-post-processing-finishes-comparison/): finishes explained with cost and minimum wall.

<a id="227"></a>
#### 227 · Sign Maker (`sign`)
**For:** hand-painted sign writers, gilders and small sign workshops doing shopfronts, murals, pub signs and lettering.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-project · single-project · page-services · page-wordmarks · page-process · page-shop · page-about · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** project case study (client, location, technique: gold leaf, enamel, reverse glass), before/after shopfront pair, process strip (drawing, pounce pattern, painting, gilding), services list (shopfronts, glass gilding, murals, vehicles, interiors), wordmarks / lettering gallery, field notes blog, shop for prints and caps, enquiry form with site photos, press list, careers (apprentice painters).
**Content model:** `project` (client, location, year, technique, surface, size), taxonomy `technique`, bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (enquiry with File Upload for shopfront photos and measurements), WooCommerce (prints and merch), Query Filter (by technique).
**Signature:** project pages that show the job as a process sequence, from sketch to finished shopfront, with client, place and technique on one line (seen on: [Ged Palmer: Darby's Oyster Bar](https://www.gedpalmer.com/projects/darbys-oyster-bar) and [Colossal Media: work](https://www.colossalmedia.com/work)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Enquiry form that asks for a photo of the wall or fascia and rough measurements
- Field-notes journal from jobs in progress (seen on: [Colossal Media: field notes](https://www.colossalmedia.com/field-notes))
- Lettering/wordmark gallery as a separate page from signage jobs (seen on: [Ged Palmer: wordmarks](https://www.gedpalmer.com/wordmarks))
- Small shop for prints, caps and tees made from the lettering (seen on: [Ornamental Conifer: shop](https://www.ornamentalconifer.com/collections/all))
- Printable care note for gilded glass (cleaning, no abrasive pads) handed over with the job
**Style: Sign-painter vernacular**
- Type: Headings Mr Dafoe 400 (a sign-painter's brush script, used only for headings); body Work Sans 400 at 18px; captions Work Sans 600 small caps.
- Palette: bg #F5F1E6 (primed board), text #111111, gold leaf #C9A227 (flat, never gradient), enamel red #C1121F, line #111111.
- Layout: full-bleed photos of finished signs; project titles set in Mr Dafoe like a fascia board across the full width. Home: one big recent shopfront, then a grid of close-ups, then the process strip.
- Imagery: close-ups of brush strokes and gold leaf texture, wide street shots of shopfronts, the painter's hands; no mock-ups.
- Motion: none beyond underline and colour changes on links. Reduced motion is the default.
- Why it fits now: independent shops are commissioning hand lettering again and the painters' own sites lead with the work at full size, e.g. [Ged Palmer](https://www.gedpalmer.com/).
**Style variations:** Glass gilding: black bg, gold #C9A227 type · Pub sign: bottle green #1F4D2B, cream lettering · Circus: red #C1121F bg, white Mr Dafoe.
**Real-world basis:** [Ged Palmer: projects](https://www.gedpalmer.com/projects), [Ged Palmer: Darby's Oyster Bar](https://www.gedpalmer.com/projects/darbys-oyster-bar), [Colossal Media: work](https://www.colossalmedia.com/work), [Colossal Media: field notes](https://www.colossalmedia.com/field-notes), [Ornamental Conifer: shop](https://www.ornamentalconifer.com/collections/all)
**Refs:**
- [Ged Palmer: Darby's Oyster Bar](https://www.gedpalmer.com/projects/darbys-oyster-bar): a case study told through process photos.
- [Colossal Media: work](https://www.colossalmedia.com/work): a large hand-painted portfolio indexed by project.
- [Ged Palmer: wordmarks](https://www.gedpalmer.com/wordmarks): lettering presented separately from site work.

<a id="228"></a>
#### 228 · Local Print Shop (`press`)
**For:** risograph studios, print co-ops and small litho/digital printers serving artists, charities, zines and local businesses.
**Templates:** front-page · page-get-a-quote · page-riso-printing · page-digital-printing · page-paper-and-card · page-finishing · page-lead-times · page-environment · page-workshops · archive-portfolio · Woo shop · single-product
**Patterns (~45):** quote form with artwork upload, riso ink colour chart (named inks with swatches), paper and card stock list (weight, colour, recycled content), lead-times table by job type and colour count, finishing options (folding, stapling, binding, trimming), artwork setup guide (separations, bleed, greyscale per layer), portfolio of printed jobs, workshops, environmental statement, co-op/"why we're a workers' co-op" page, shop (ink swatch cards, blank paper, notebooks).
**Content model:** `ink` (name, hex approximation, riso code), `stock` (weight, finish, sizes, recycled %), `job` portfolio (client, process, colours, pages), bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (quote with File Upload), WooCommerce (swatch packs, stationery), companion print-price estimator (size × quantity × colours × sides, with setup fee).
**Signature:** a lead-times table by product and colour count ("single-sided riso, 1–5 colours: 2–5 working days"), with finishing and binding add-ons listed as extra days (seen on: [Footprint Workers Co-op: lead times](https://www.footprinters.co.uk/lead-times/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Ink swatch cards sold in the shop so clients can see real colours on paper (seen on: [RISOTTO: ink swatches](https://risottostudio.com/collections/ink-swatches))
- Paper and card page listing stocks the shop actually carries (seen on: [Footprint: paper and card](https://www.footprinters.co.uk/paper-and-card/))
- Honest note that rushing leads to mistakes and rushed jobs can't be reprinted free (seen on: [Footprint: lead times](https://www.footprinters.co.uk/lead-times/))
- Environmental considerations page (inks, paper, waste) (seen on: [Footprint: environmental considerations](https://www.footprinters.co.uk/environmental-considerations/))
- Workshops for people who want to print themselves (seen on: [Calverts: workshops](https://www.calverts.coop/workshops/))
**Style: Riso overprint spot colour**
- Type: Headings Mazius Display (Collletttivo) at 7rem; body Rethink Sans 400 at 18px; job specs in Red Hat Mono 400.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF (uncoated paper), riso fluorescent pink #FF48B0, riso blue #0078BF, riso yellow #FFE800, ink #1A1A1A. Overlaps use CSS mix-blend-mode: multiply to show true overprints.
- Layout: poster-like home with the shop name split across two ink layers slightly out of register; content in a 3-column print-sheet grid with crop marks at section corners. Lead times and prices as plain tables.
- Imagery: photos of stacks, drum changes and printed sheets, plus scanned riso prints with visible grain; no mock-up frames.
- Motion: headline layers drift 1–2px apart on pointer move; reduced motion locks them.
- Why it fits now: riso studios have kept the overprint look current through ink-led branding, e.g. [RISOTTO: ink swatches](https://risottostudio.com/collections/ink-swatches).
**Style variations:** Two-colour: pink and blue only · Teal and orange: #00838A with #FF6C2F · Mono drum: black ink on #F3F1EA.
**Real-world basis:** [Footprint Workers Co-op: lead times](https://www.footprinters.co.uk/lead-times/), [Footprint: get a quote](https://www.footprinters.co.uk/get-a-quote/), [Footprint: colour riso printing](https://www.footprinters.co.uk/colour-riso-printing/), [RISOTTO: ink swatches](https://risottostudio.com/collections/ink-swatches), [Calverts: risograph](https://www.calverts.coop/portfolio/risograph/)
**Refs:**
- [Footprint Workers Co-op: lead times](https://www.footprinters.co.uk/lead-times/): working-day lead times by job type, colours and finishing.
- [RISOTTO: ink swatches](https://risottostudio.com/collections/ink-swatches): selling the colour chart as a product.
- [Calverts: risograph](https://www.calverts.coop/portfolio/risograph/): portfolio of riso jobs from a long-running co-op.

<a id="229"></a>
#### 229 · Contract Workshop / Small Manufacturer (`workshop`)
**For:** small furniture workshops, metal and joinery shops and batch manufacturers making to order for designers, brands and fit-out contractors.
**Templates:** front-page · page-capabilities · archive-product · single-product · archive-project · single-project · page-trade · page-request-a-quote · page-about-the-workshop · page-environment · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** capability sheet (processes, materials, minimum order, lead time, sectors), machine list, product catalogue with made-to-order lead times, trade and contract enquiry form with drawing upload, project case studies (client, quantity, materials), workshop tour photos, timber sourcing / environment page, sample and finish swatches, sale and ex-display stock, delivery and installation note.
**Content model:** `capability` (process, materials, max size, tolerance), `product` (lead time, finishes, dimensions), `project` (client, sector, quantity), company-level meta for minimum order and standard lead time, bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (quote with File Upload for drawings and specs), WooCommerce (catalogue and ex-display sale), companion batch-cost estimator (unit price by quantity break).
**Signature:** a one-screen capability sheet listing processes, materials, minimum order (e.g. "£2,500–£5,000") and lead time (e.g. "8–12 weeks") so buyers can qualify the workshop before calling (seen on: [Make Works: Alex Begg & Co profile](https://make.works/companies/AlexBeggandCo)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Downloadable capability PDF generated from the same fields, for procurement files
- Sale / ex-display page for seconds and samples (seen on: [Benchmark: sale](https://www.benchmarkfurniture.com/sale/))
- Product categories with made-to-order notes (seen on: [Benchmark: tables](https://benchmarkfurniture.com/product-category/tables/))
- Fit-out service page for offices wanting several pieces at once (seen on: [Opendesk: workspaces](https://opendesk.cc/workspaces))
- "Currently booking for [month]" lead-time line updated by the owner
**Style: Swiss industrial catalogue**
- Type: Headings Gothic A1 800 at 6rem; body Gothic A1 400 at 18px; spec tables in Red Hat Mono 400.
- Palette: bg #EDEDEA (workshop concrete), text #121212, safety orange #FF5A1F for "request a quote" and lead-time flags, surface #FFFFFF, line #121212.
- Layout: product catalogue as a numbered spec list (code, name, material, lead time) with a photo column; capability sheet as a two-column table. Home: workshop photo at full width, the capability sheet, then projects. Square corners throughout; buttons are solid rectangles.
- Imagery: honest workshop photography: machines, offcuts, jigs, people at benches; products shot on a plain grey sweep.
- Motion: table rows gain an orange left marker on hover; reduced motion keeps colour change only.
- Why it fits now: makers selling to trade are adopting the calm systematic catalogue style of long-lived furniture brands, e.g. [Vitsœ](https://www.vitsoe.com/).
**Style variations:** Oak: #E6D5B8 surface, black type · Steel: #2B2F33 bg, white specs · Blueprint: #F4F7FA bg, #1F4E8C lines.
**Real-world basis:** [Make Works: Alex Begg & Co](https://make.works/companies/AlexBeggandCo), [Benchmark: tables](https://benchmarkfurniture.com/product-category/tables/), [Benchmark: sale](https://www.benchmarkfurniture.com/sale/), [Opendesk: workspaces](https://opendesk.cc/workspaces), [Make Works: glossary](https://make.works/glossary)
**Refs:**
- [Make Works: Alex Begg & Co](https://make.works/companies/AlexBeggandCo): the profile format (processes, materials, minimum order, lead time, contact) a workshop should publish about itself.
- [Benchmark: tables](https://benchmarkfurniture.com/product-category/tables/): a small workshop's catalogue on WordPress.
- [Make Works: glossary](https://make.works/glossary): plain definitions of manufacturing terms for non-specialist buyers.

#### 230 · Custom Packaging Maker (`box`)
**For:** small packaging makers and print-on-box suppliers selling mailer boxes, tubes and bags to independent brands in low minimums.
**Templates:** front-page · Woo shop · single-product · page-boxes-by-size · page-dieline-request · page-free-sample · page-artwork-guidelines · page-custom-order · page-sustainability · page-faq · archive-case-study
**Patterns (~45):** boxes-by-size grid (internal L × W × H), product page with quantity price breaks, dieline request form (box type, dimensions, email, returned as AI file), free sample pack, artwork guidelines per product (bleed, safe zone, ink limits), custom quote form with artwork upload, material and certification notes (FSC, recycled content, compostable), case studies of brands, packaging 101 guide, bill of materials page.
**Content model:** Woo product meta (internal dimensions, board grade, print sides, MOQ, price breaks), `case_study` (brand, box type, quantity), bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce, Jetpack Forms (dieline request and custom quote with File Upload), companion quantity-break calculator (unit price × quantity, with setup fee and lead time).
**Signature:** a dieline request form where the customer picks a box style and enters dimensions and gets the flat Adobe Illustrator dieline back within 1–2 business days, with a note sending undersized boxes to a custom quote (seen on: [Arka: dieline request](https://www.arka.com/pages/dieline-request)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Free sample page (seen on: [Arka: free sample](https://www.arka.com/pages/free-sample))
- Browse boxes by size rather than by name (seen on: [Arka: boxes by sizes](https://www.arka.com/collections/boxes-by-sizes))
- Artwork guidelines per product with downloadable templates (seen on: [EcoEnclose: artwork guidelines](https://www.ecoenclose.com/artwork))
- Bill of materials page explaining what each pack is made of (seen on: [EcoEnclose: bill of materials](https://www.ecoenclose.com/bill-of-materials/))
- Size check against common products ("fits an A4 print", "fits a 250g coffee bag") on each box
**Style: Tactile die-line cardboard**
- Type: Headings Boxing 400 (Fontshare) at 6rem; body Karla 400 at 17px; dimensions and die labels in Azeret Mono 500.
- Palette: kraft #C8A27A, board white #FFFFFF, dieline magenta #E6007E for cut lines, crease cyan #00A3E0 for dashed fold lines, ink #1E1A16.
- Layout: product pages show the flat dieline drawing beside the folded-box photo; section dividers are dashed crease lines; cards are flat rectangles with a single "tab" notch. Home: size finder first, then best sellers, then the sample-pack offer.
- Imagery: real boxes on a plain kraft table, flat-lays of unfolded boxes, hands packing orders; no floating 3D renders.
- Motion: on hover a dieline outline animates its dash offset as if being cut; reduced motion shows the static drawing.
- Why it fits now: stationery and packaging shops are using real material photography and office-supply graphics instead of 3D mock-ups, e.g. [Present & Correct](https://www.presentandcorrect.com/).
**Style variations:** White board: #FFFFFF bg, magenta cut lines · Black mailer: #151515 bg, kraft type · Tissue: #F6D7E0 surface, black ink.
**Real-world basis:** [Arka: dieline request](https://www.arka.com/pages/dieline-request), [Arka: boxes by sizes](https://www.arka.com/collections/boxes-by-sizes), [Arka: free sample](https://www.arka.com/pages/free-sample), [EcoEnclose: artwork guidelines](https://www.ecoenclose.com/artwork), [noissue: home](https://noissue.co/)
**Refs:**
- [Arka: dieline request](https://www.arka.com/pages/dieline-request): turning a technical file into a lead-generating form.
- [EcoEnclose: artwork guidelines](https://www.ecoenclose.com/artwork): per-product artwork rules and templates.
- [Arka: boxes by sizes](https://www.arka.com/collections/boxes-by-sizes): navigation by dimension.

#### 231 · Small-Run Garment Manufacturer (CMT) (`cmt`)
**For:** cut-make-trim units and small clothing factories producing samples and low-minimum runs for emerging fashion brands.
**Templates:** front-page · page-services · page-get-a-quote · page-moq-and-pricing · page-sampling · page-product-types · page-how-it-works · archive-case-study · page-tech-pack-guide · page-about-the-factory · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** MOQ panel (per style, per colourway, per order), services list (pattern cutting, grading, sampling, CMT, full package), product types (jersey, wovens, outerwear, babywear, plus size), how-it-works steps from tech pack to bulk, quote form with tech pack upload, tech pack checklist, sampling costs and timelines, factory floor photos and machine list, ethical audit / accreditation note, case studies of brands, consultancy offer for start-ups.
**Content model:** `service` (stage, price from, lead time), `product_type` (MOQ, sample lead time), `case_study` (brand, garment, quantity), bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (quote with File Upload for tech packs and patterns), companion MOQ/price calculator (units × styles × colourways, flags when an order falls below the minimum).
**Signature:** an MOQ panel that spells out minimums per style, per colourway and per order (e.g. "50 units per style, split into 2 colourways and up to 5 sizes; 250 units per order") before the quote form (seen on: [Clothing Manufacturers UK: home](https://www.clothingmanufacturersuk.com/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Tech-pack guide page linked from the quote form (seen on: [Sewport: tech pack](https://sewport.com/tech-pack))
- Garment labelling requirements explained for new brands (seen on: [Sewport: garment labeling](https://sewport.com/learn/garment-labeling-and-requirements))
- Factory journal with production stories (seen on: [Blackhorse Lane Ateliers: journal](https://blackhorselane.com/blogs/journal))
- "Taking bulk orders for [season]" capacity line on the home page
- Profile on a regional maker directory linked from the footer (seen on: [Make Works: companies](https://make.works/companies))
**Style: Quiet luxury mono fashion editorial**
- Type: Headings Tenor Sans 400 (a flared, fashion-house sans) at 8rem; body Hanken Grotesk 400 at 17px; spec labels Hanken Grotesk 600 at 13px with 0.02em tracking.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #0A0A0A, tailor's chalk blue #3D5A80 for links and buttons, pattern-paper #EFE9DD for form panels, line #0A0A0A at 1px.
- Layout: large white margins, a 6-column grid with images breaking out to the edge; MOQ and pricing set as a clean price list, not cards. Home: one factory-floor photograph at full width, the MOQ panel, then product types as a text index.
- Imagery: black-and-white factory photography (machinists, cutting tables, pattern hooks) and colour close-ups of seams and fabric.
- Motion: images reveal their colour version on hover (opacity crossfade, no zoom); reduced motion keeps black and white.
- Why it fits now: fashion brands have moved to austere, typographic stores; a CMT that looks like that speaks to them, e.g. [LEMAIRE](https://www.lemaire.fr/).
**Style variations:** Toile: #F2EDE3 bg, black type · Denim: #1E2F4A bg, white Bodoni · Chalk: white bg, blue #3D5A80 rules.
**Real-world basis:** [Clothing Manufacturers UK: home](https://www.clothingmanufacturersuk.com/), [Sewport: tech pack](https://sewport.com/tech-pack), [Sewport: how it works for manufacturers](https://sewport.com/how-it-works-manufacturers), [Fashion Enter: home](https://fashion-enter.com/), [Blackhorse Lane Ateliers: journal](https://blackhorselane.com/blogs/journal)
**Refs:**
- [Clothing Manufacturers UK: home](https://www.clothingmanufacturersuk.com/): minimums stated in full, early on the page.
- [Sewport: tech pack](https://sewport.com/tech-pack): what a brand needs to send before a factory can quote.
- [Blackhorse Lane Ateliers: journal](https://blackhorselane.com/blogs/journal): a factory telling its own production story.

#### 232 · Architectural Salvage Yard (`salvage`)
**For:** reclamation yards and salvage dealers selling one-off doors, fireplaces, panelling, flooring and lighting to homeowners and designers.
**Templates:** front-page · Woo shop · product-category · single-product (one-off lot) · page-new-arrivals · page-we-buy · page-designer-trade · page-locations · page-guides · archive (inspiration) · page-faqs · page-contact
**Patterns (~45):** lot card (stock number, photo, dimensions, price, "Reserved" / "Sold" state), category tree (chimneypieces, doors, flooring, lighting, radiators, panelling), new arrivals list, "we buy" form with photo upload, designer and trade programme, locations with yard hours, re-use guides (salvaged panelling, reclaimed brick), delivery and collection note, provenance line where known, inspiration projects.
**Content model:** Woo product meta (stock no., dimensions H/W/D in mm, condition, provenance, weight, reserved flag), taxonomy for category and period, bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce (stock of 1, reserved status via a custom stock status), Query Filter (category, period, material), Jetpack Forms ("we buy" with File Upload).
**Signature:** one-off lot pages with a stock number in the title, exact dimensions in millimetres, condition in one line and a visible "Reserved" state that keeps the item online (seen on: [Retrouvius: bobbin corner chair #2257](https://www.retrouvius.com/product/bobbin-corner-chair-2257/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Guide to re-using a material type, written from experience (seen on: [Retrouvius: guide to re-using salvaged panelling](https://www.retrouvius.com/guide-to-re-using-salvaged-panelling/))
- Designer and wholesale programme page (seen on: [Olde Good Things: designer & wholesale](https://ogtstore.com/designer-wholesale/))
- Several yard locations with hours on one page (seen on: [Olde Good Things: locations](https://ogtstore.com/locations/))
- Deep category tree for fireplaces and hardware (seen on: [LASSCO: chimneypieces & firegrates](https://www.lassco.co.uk/category/chimneypieces-firegrates/))
- cm/in toggle on dimensions for overseas buyers
**Style: Auction-lot catalogue**
- Type: Headings Sorts Mill Goudy 400 at 5rem; body Source Serif 4 at 18px; lot numbers and dimensions in Courier Prime 400.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #1C1C1C, patina green #3C6E5B for links and "Reserved" labels, brass #B08D57 for price, line #D9D4CA.
- Layout: category pages as a printed sale catalogue: lot number, photo, one-line description, dimensions, price, in a two-column list; single lot pages with several large photos and a condition report block. Home: new arrivals as a numbered list, then categories as text links.
- Imagery: honest yard photography with the item against a brick wall or on pallets, scale objects in shot, detail photos of wear.
- Motion: thumbnails swap to a second photo on hover; reduced motion disables the swap.
- Why it fits now: salvage dealers now sell through the catalogue look of their own stock numbers rather than lifestyle imagery, e.g. [Retrouvius](https://www.retrouvius.com/).
**Style variations:** Yard: #2E2B27 bg, brass type · Sale day: white bg, red #B3261E "Sold" stamps · Oak panel: #E7DCC8 bg, dark green ink.
**Real-world basis:** [Retrouvius: bobbin corner chair #2257](https://www.retrouvius.com/product/bobbin-corner-chair-2257/), [Retrouvius: FAQs](https://www.retrouvius.com/faqs/), [LASSCO: all categories](https://www.lassco.co.uk/categories/), [Olde Good Things: locations](https://ogtstore.com/locations/), [Reclaimed Brick Company: home](https://reclaimedbrickcompany.co.uk/)
**Refs:**
- [Retrouvius: bobbin corner chair #2257](https://www.retrouvius.com/product/bobbin-corner-chair-2257/): a one-off lot page on WooCommerce with stock number, dimensions and "Reserved".
- [LASSCO: chimneypieces & firegrates](https://www.lassco.co.uk/category/chimneypieces-firegrates/): a salvage category tree that goes several levels deep.
- [Retrouvius: guide to re-using salvaged panelling](https://www.retrouvius.com/guide-to-re-using-salvaged-panelling/): content that helps a buyer commit to a used material.

### XXV. Directories, boards & marketplaces

<a id="233"></a>
#### 233 · Niche Job Board (`jobs`)
**For:** a single-sector job board (arts, design, architecture, a local trade) run by one person or a membership body.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-job · single-job · page-post-a-job · page-pricing · page-guarantee · archive-company · single-company · page-events · page-resources · page-faq
**Patterns (~40):** job listing row (title, organisation, location, salary, contract type, closing date, posted date), job page (salary, hours, contract, closing date and time, how to apply, contact name), filters (full-time, freelance, remote, location), company profile (founded, size, location, current roles), post-a-job form, pricing (standard vs featured, monthly), satisfaction guarantee, salary guide for employers, closing-soon list, events and resources for candidates.
**Content model:** `job` (organisation, salary min/max or day rate, contract type, hours, location, remote flag, closing date, apply URL/email, featured), `company` (founded, size, location), bound via Block Bindings. Expired jobs drop off by closing date.
**Plugins:** Two honest routes. (a) WP Job Manager (Automattic, v2.4.7, updated Sept 2026): solid engine for the `job_listing` CPT, expiry and front-end submission, but its readme says it is shortcode-based, not block-native; use it only as the back end, render jobs with Query Loop and Block Bindings, and place the single `[submit_job_form]` in a Shortcode block. (b) Lighter: companion `job` CPT + Jetpack Forms (moderated submission) + WooCommerce for the listing fee. Either way add Advanced Query Loop (order by closing date, hide expired) and Query Filter.
**Signature:** every listing shows salary, contract type, closing date and posted date in the row itself, and the single page gives the exact closing time and a named contact for applications (seen on: [Arts Jobs: Rambert listing](https://www.artsjobs.org.uk/jobs/85123)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- "Satisfaction guarantee: free repost or refund within 30 days" page for employers (seen on: [Authentic Jobs: guarantee](https://authenticjobs.com/guarantee/))
- Salary calculator/guide for employers so listings include real pay (seen on: [Authentic Jobs: salary calculator](https://authenticjobs.com/salary-calculator-for-employers/))
- Company profiles with size, founding year and open roles (seen on: [Creative Lives in Progress: company directory](https://creativelivesinprogress.com/company-directory/dixonbaxi))
- "Closing this week" list on the home page, driven by the closing-date meta
- Discounted rate note for charities and education (seen on: [Authentic Jobs: pricing](https://authenticjobs.com/pricing/))
**Style: Broadsheet classifieds**
- Type: Headings Old Standard TT 700 at 5rem; body PT Serif 400 at 18px; category heads and salary figures in Oswald 600 (condensed).
- Palette: bg #F1EFE9 (newsprint), ink #111111, classified red #D0021B for "closing soon" and featured rules, surface #FFFFFF, line #111111.
- Layout: a multi-column classifieds page: jobs as dense text blocks in three columns on desktop, divided by hairline rules, grouped by category heads; featured jobs boxed with a double rule. Home: today's new jobs, then closing this week, then categories.
- Imagery: none in listings; company logos only on company pages, shown in black on white.
- Motion: none. Filters update the list with no animation.
- Why it fits now: text-first classifieds pages load fast and are easy to scan, and literary magazines still run them this way, e.g. [The New York Review of Books: classifieds](https://www.nybooks.com/classifieds/).
**Style variations:** Evening edition: #111 bg, newsprint text · Trade paper: #FFF3C4 bg, black · Union notice: white bg, red #D0021B headers.
**Real-world basis:** [Arts Jobs: job listing](https://www.artsjobs.org.uk/jobs/85123), [Arts Jobs: jobs](https://www.artsjobs.org.uk/jobs), [Authentic Jobs: pricing](https://authenticjobs.com/pricing/), [Arts Jobs: events](https://www.artsjobs.org.uk/events), [Creative Lives in Progress: opportunities](https://creativelivesinprogress.com/opportunities)
**Refs:**
- [Arts Jobs: Rambert listing](https://www.artsjobs.org.uk/jobs/85123): the fields a sector board should require (salary, closing date and time, contract, contact).
- [Authentic Jobs: pricing](https://authenticjobs.com/pricing/): a small WordPress-based board with a simple standard/featured model.
- [Creative Lives in Progress: company directory](https://creativelivesinprogress.com/company-directory): employer profiles (size, founded, open roles) that keep candidates coming back.

#### 234 · Local Business Directory (`directory`)
**For:** a town, region or sector directory run by a volunteer group, a BID or a maker network listing independent businesses and workshops.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-listing · single-listing · taxonomy-category · taxonomy-area · page-map · page-get-listed · page-suggest-a-listing · page-glossary · page-about · archive (stories)
**Patterns (~40):** listing card (name, category, area, one-line description), listing page (processes or services, materials, minimum order, lead time, contact person, phone, email, address, photos), filter by region, process and material, "random listing" button, map view, get-listed criteria page, suggest-a-listing form, glossary of terms, stories/interviews with listed businesses, region landing pages.
**Content model:** `listing` (category, area, contact name, phone, email, address, lat/lng, opening hours, minimum order, lead time, photos, verified date), taxonomies `category`, `area`, `process`, `material`, bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** companion `listing` CPT + Query Filter + Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap + Jetpack Forms (moderated "suggest a listing" with photo upload; the owner publishes after checking). Directorist (16 blocks, freemium) and GeoDirectory (blocks, Bootstrap-based) exist but add weight and upsells; Business Directory Plugin is shortcode-based, so avoid it.
**Signature:** filter listings by region, process and material at once, then open profiles that carry the practical facts (minimum order, lead time, named contact) instead of marketing copy (seen on: [Make Works: manufacturers](https://make.works/companies) and [Make Works: Alex Begg & Co](https://make.works/companies/AlexBeggandCo)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- "Random listing" link for browsing and discovery (seen on: [Make Works: random](https://make.works/random))
- Getting-listed page with the criteria and who it is for (seen on: [Make Works: getting listed](https://make.works/getting_listed))
- Glossary of trade terms (seen on: [Make Works: glossary](https://make.works/glossary))
- "Last checked [date]" on each listing so stale entries are visible
- Printable A4 area map of listings for shop windows and events
**Style: Yellow-pages utility**
- Type: Headings Pragati Narrow 700 at 6rem; body Public Sans 400 at 18px; phone numbers and postcodes in Overpass Mono 600.
- Palette: directory yellow #FFD400 for the header and category tabs, black #000000 text, white #FFFFFF listing surface, pale yellow #FFF6BF for search panel, line #000000.
- Layout: A–Z category tabs across the top; listings as a two-column phone-book list with bold names and hairline rules; single listings as a fact sheet. Home: search and filters first, then "new this month", then the map.
- Imagery: photos taken by the directory team in each workshop or shop, same crop (4:3) and daylight treatment for consistency.
- Motion: none beyond focus and hover colour. Map pins get a thicker outline on focus.
- Why it fits now: useful local directories are winning back attention from platforms by being plainly useful, e.g. [Make Works: manufacturers](https://make.works/companies).
**Style variations:** Night directory: #111 bg, yellow type · Green pages: #2E7D32 header, white · Paper book: #F3EAD3 bg, black.
**Real-world basis:** [Make Works: manufacturers](https://make.works/companies), [Make Works: Scotland](https://make.works/regions/scotland), [Make Works: getting listed](https://make.works/getting_listed), [Creative Lives in Progress: company directory](https://creativelivesinprogress.com/company-directory), [Totally Locally: home](https://www.totallylocally.org/)
**Refs:**
- [Make Works: manufacturers](https://make.works/companies): multi-facet filtering (region, process, material) over a volunteer-built directory.
- [Make Works: Alex Begg & Co](https://make.works/companies/AlexBeggandCo): the listing detail page to copy.
- [Make Works: getting listed](https://make.works/getting_listed): how to explain who qualifies.

<a id="235"></a>
#### 235 · Swap / Classifieds Board (`swap`)
**For:** neighbourhood give-and-take groups, tool libraries, school uniform swaps and small community classifieds.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-advert · single-advert · page-post-an-item · page-my-items · page-guidelines · page-find-your-area · page-events · page-about · page-donate
**Patterns (~35):** item card (photo, title, area, "Offer" / "Wanted" / "Taken", time since posted), browse with distance and type filters, list / photo list / card layout switch, post-an-item form, manage my items, guidelines (what can't be posted, pickup etiquette, one person at a time), area/group finder, swap events list, volunteer moderators, donate to keep it running, "free stuff guides" by town.
**Content model:** WPAdverts `advert` post type with custom fields for type (offer/wanted), area and status (available/taken), plus companion `event`; bound via Block Bindings where the template is core.
**Plugins:** WPAdverts (free core; v2.3.4, updated Sept 2026; ships real blocks: Classifieds List, Search, Publish/Manage and Single Contact, rebuilt in Aug 2026), Jetpack Forms (report a post), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (area map).
**Signature:** an Offer / Wanted / Taken status on every item, filterable by distance and age of post, with a choice of list, photo list or card layout (seen on: [Trash Nothing: browse](https://trashnothing.com/browse)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Plain-language guidelines with pickup etiquette ("arrange with one person; be punctual") (seen on: [Freecycle: guidelines](https://freecycle.org/pages/guidelines))
- Area finder listing each local group (seen on: [Freecycle: find a town](https://freecycle.org/find-towns))
- Auto-expire posts after N days with a "still available?" email to the poster
- Free-stuff guides for common items (furniture, baby kit) (seen on: [Trash Nothing: free stuff guides](https://trashnothing.com/free-stuff-guides))
- Donate page explaining what hosting costs (seen on: [Freecycle: donate](https://freecycle.org/pages/donate))
**Style: Soft neo-brutalism (hard shadows, pastel fills)**
- Type: Headings Mochiy Pop One 400 at 4.5rem; body Figtree 400 at 18px; status tags in Figtree 700.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, ink #111111, mint #B8F2D0 for "Offer", butter #FFE79A for "Wanted", pink #FFC4E1 for "Taken", hard shadow #111111 offset 4px.
- Layout: item cards with a 2px black border, 4px solid offset shadow and 6px radius (buttons 0px, images 0px, so radii differ by element). Grid of 2–4 columns; the post-an-item button is a big fixed block bottom-right on mobile. Home: "just posted" grid, then area finder, then guidelines.
- Imagery: members' own phone photos, square-cropped, no filters; placeholder is a drawn outline of the item type, not a stock photo.
- Motion: cards press down 2px on click (shadow shrinks); reduced motion removes the offset change.
- Why it fits now: neo-brutalist UI with flat pastels and hard shadows is the friendly, legible look of creator and community tools, e.g. [Gumroad](https://gumroad.com/).
**Style variations:** Tool library: #F5F5F5 bg, yellow #FFD400 tags · School swap: navy #1D3557 borders, mint fills · Night market: #111 bg, pastel cards.
**Real-world basis:** [Trash Nothing: browse](https://trashnothing.com/browse), [Trash Nothing: groups](https://trashnothing.com/groups/), [Freecycle: guidelines](https://freecycle.org/pages/guidelines), [Freecycle: find a town](https://freecycle.org/find-towns), [Freecycle: Amsterdam group](https://freecycle.org/town/AmsterdamNL)
**Refs:**
- [Trash Nothing: browse](https://trashnothing.com/browse): distance filter, offer/request types and three layout modes.
- [Freecycle: guidelines](https://freecycle.org/pages/guidelines): the rules page any swap board needs, in plain words.
- [Freecycle: find a town](https://freecycle.org/find-towns): one site hosting many local groups.

<a id="236"></a>
#### 236 · Freelancer Directory (`talent`)
**For:** member networks and collectives listing freelance illustrators, photographers, designers or technicians for hire in one field or region.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-person · single-person · page-a-z · taxonomy-discipline · page-rates-of-pay · page-commissioning-guide · page-join · page-resources · archive (magazine) · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** A–Z portfolio index with a count ("154 illustrators found"), portfolio card (square image, name), profile page (images, disciplines, location, availability, contact, website), filter by discipline and location, rates-of-pay guide, commissioning guide for clients, join/membership page, member resources, magazine archive, meet-ups and events, code of conduct.
**Content model:** `person` (disciplines, location, availability status, website, email, pronouns, member since), taxonomy `discipline`, bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** Query Filter (discipline, location), Jetpack Forms (join application and client briefs with File Upload), companion availability toggle block.
**Signature:** an A–Z portfolio index with a running count and one representative image per person, so clients can browse faces of work rather than profiles of text (seen on: [Illustrators Australia: portfolios](https://www.illustratorsaustralia.com/portfolios/all)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Rates-of-pay page for members and clients (seen on: [Illustrators Australia: rates of pay](https://www.illustratorsaustralia.com/rates-of-pay/))
- Commissioning guide explaining how to brief and license work (seen on: [IllustrationX: commissioning](https://www.illustrationx.com/commissioning))
- "Available from [month]" status on each profile, set by the member
- Pronouns field on profiles
- Magazine archive of past member publications (seen on: [Illustrators Australia: magazine archive](https://www.illustratorsaustralia.com/magazine-archive/))
**Style: Kinetic variable-type**
- Type: Names set in Readex Pro (variable: weight 160–700, HEXP 0–100) at 5rem; body Readex Pro 400 at 18px; tags in Sometype Mono 500.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #0D0D0D, signal orange #FF3B00 for availability "open", surface #F2F2F2, line #0D0D0D.
- Layout: the A–Z index is a long typographic list of names; hovering a name reveals that person's image in a fixed panel on the right. Profiles: images in a tight masonry, facts in a narrow sidebar. Home: this month's new members as names in huge type.
- Imagery: the members' own work only, shown uncropped; no headshots required.
- Motion: names shift from weight 400 to 800 and casual 0 to 1 on hover (font-variation-settings); reduced motion swaps weight instantly.
- Why it fits now: type foundries and studios use variable-axis motion as their interface, e.g. [Dinamo Typefaces](https://abcdinamo.com/).
**Style variations:** Mono list: black on white, no images · Night index: #0D0D0D bg, orange names · Paper: #F4F1EA bg, blue #1F4FFF names.
**Real-world basis:** [Illustrators Australia: portfolios](https://www.illustratorsaustralia.com/portfolios/all), [Illustrators Australia: rates of pay](https://www.illustratorsaustralia.com/rates-of-pay/), [IllustrationX: illustrators](https://www.illustrationx.com/illustrators), [Association of Illustrators: about](https://theaoi.com/about/), [Women Who Draw](https://womenwhodraw.com/)
**Refs:**
- [Illustrators Australia: portfolios](https://www.illustratorsaustralia.com/portfolios/all): the A–Z index with counts.
- [Illustrators Australia: rates of pay](https://www.illustratorsaustralia.com/rates-of-pay/): a members' pricing guide published in public.
- [IllustrationX: commissioning](https://www.illustrationx.com/commissioning): client-side guide to hiring.

<a id="237"></a>
#### 237 · City "What's On" Events Aggregator (`whatson`)
**For:** one-person or small-team listings sites for a city's gigs, clubs, theatre and free events.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-event (tonight / this weekend / by date) · single-event · archive-venue · single-venue · taxonomy-genre · page-submit-an-event · page-newsletter · page-about · page-ticket-shop
**Patterns (~40):** tonight list, this weekend list, date strip, genre filters (gigs, club, comedy, theatre, free), event row (date, venue, title, price, "Free entry", "Sold out"), venue guide (address, capacity, access notes, upcoming events), submit-an-event form with lead-time rule ("at least 7 days away"), weekly email picks, featured/editor's picks, festival and carnival specials.
**Content model:** The Events Calendar `tribe_events` and venues, with extra meta for price band, genre, age limit and ticket status; bound via Block Bindings in single templates.
**Plugins:** The Events Calendar (events, venues, iCal), Jetpack Forms (submit an event; TEC's Community Events add-on is paid, so avoid), Jetpack Newsletter (weekly picks).
**Signature:** "tonight" and "this weekend" entry points on every page, backed by a venues guide where each venue page lists what's coming up there (seen on: [Headfirst Bristol: gigs and live music](https://www.headfirstbristol.co.uk/gigs-and-live-music) and [Headfirst Bristol: venues](https://www.headfirstbristol.co.uk/venues)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Submission rule stated clearly ("events must be at least 7 days away") (seen on: [The List: submit](https://www.list.co.uk/submit))
- Free listing for promoters explained in one line (seen on: [Headfirst Bristol: event manager](https://www.headfirstbristol.co.uk/event-manager))
- Weekly email as the main product, with the website as the archive (seen on: [Nonsense NYC](https://nonsensenyc.com/))
- "Sold out" and "few left" flags set by the editor on each event
- Step-free access note on venue pages
**Style: Fly-poster gig wall**
- Type: Headings Six Caps 400 at 9rem, stacked; body Karla 400 at 18px; dates and prices in IBM Plex Mono 600.
- Palette: bg #E8E4DA (wheatpaste), ink #0F0F0F, fluoro orange #FF6B00 for "tonight", magenta #E4007C for "free", white #FFFFFF paper panels.
- Layout: the event list is a wall of overlapping paper rectangles at slight rotations (±1°) on desktop, a straight list on mobile; dates in huge numerals on the left. Home: tonight's list first, then weekend, then genres.
- Imagery: promoters' own posters and artist photos, shown whole; black-and-white photos of crowds and venues.
- Motion: posters straighten to 0° on hover and focus; reduced motion shows them straight.
- Why it fits now: listings sites that feel like the street they cover stand out from ticketing apps, e.g. [Headfirst Bristol: gigs](https://www.headfirstbristol.co.uk/gigs-and-live-music).
**Style variations:** Club night: #0F0F0F bg, orange type · Theatre: #7A0019 bg, cream-white #F4F1E8 · Daytime: white bg, magenta dates.
**Real-world basis:** [Headfirst Bristol: gigs and live music](https://www.headfirstbristol.co.uk/gigs-and-live-music), [Headfirst Bristol: venues](https://www.headfirstbristol.co.uk/venues), [Headfirst Bristol: event manager](https://www.headfirstbristol.co.uk/event-manager), [The List: what's on](https://list.co.uk/whats-on), [Nonsense NYC](https://nonsensenyc.com/)
**Refs:**
- [Headfirst Bristol: venues](https://www.headfirstbristol.co.uk/venues): a complete venue guide feeding the listings.
- [The List: submit](https://www.list.co.uk/submit): submission rules and lead time.
- [Nonsense NYC](https://nonsensenyc.com/): a one-person weekly list with a loyal readership.

#### 238 · Independent City / Food Guide (`cityguide`)
**For:** independent writers and small publishers producing opinionated guides to one city (food, shops, walks), often with a printed map.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-place · single-place · taxonomy-neighbourhood · taxonomy-theme · page-map · archive-guide · Woo shop (printed guides) · page-delivery · page-about · page-client-work
**Patterns (~40):** place entry (name, neighbourhood, one-paragraph review, address, hours, price band, "last visited"), themed lists (literary, music, late-night, cheap eats), neighbourhood pages, map with numbered pins matching the list, printed guide shop (folded maps by city), delivery page, events and accommodation sections for cheap-travel guides, newsletter, client work/commissions, corrections note.
**Content model:** `place` (neighbourhood, address, lat/lng, hours, price band, last visited, closed flag), `guide` (city, theme, printed product link), taxonomies `neighbourhood`, `theme`, bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap, Query Filter (neighbourhood, theme, price), WooCommerce (printed guides), Jetpack Newsletter.
**Signature:** themed, illustrated guides where each numbered entry on the map matches a numbered entry in the list, sold as folded print maps and mirrored on the site (seen on: [Herb Lester Associates: all guides](https://www.herblester.com/collections/all-guides)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- "Last visited [month year]" and a "Closed" flag on every place, so the guide stays honest
- Delivery page with times by country for the printed guides (seen on: [Herb Lester: delivery](https://www.herblester.com/pages/delivery))
- Accommodation sections by type (capsule hotel, ryokan, hostel) for visitors (seen on: [Tokyo Cheapo: accommodation](https://tokyocheapo.com/accommodation/all/))
- Printable one-page PDF per neighbourhood list
- Client-work page for commissioned guides (seen on: [Herb Lester: client work](https://www.herblester.com/pages/client-work))
**Style: Pocket-map editorial illustration**
- Type: Headings Recia 500 (Fontshare) at 6rem; body Commissioner 400 at 18px; map numbers and addresses in Commissioner 700 tabular.
- Palette: map paper #F6F1E3, ink navy #1D2A44, park green #5E8C61, route red #C8102E for numbers and the active pin, line #1D2A44.
- Layout: split view: numbered list on the left, sticky illustrated map on the right; on mobile the map folds into a panel above the list. Entries set like a printed guide: number, name, one paragraph, address line.
- Imagery: commissioned line illustrations of shopfronts and dishes in two colours; photographs only on single place pages, taken by the writer.
- Motion: hovering a list item highlights its pin and vice versa; no fly-to animation. Reduced motion keeps highlight only.
- Why it fits now: printed, illustrated city guides have a following among people tired of rating apps, e.g. [Herb Lester Associates: our guides](https://www.herblester.com/pages/our-guides).
**Style variations:** Night map: #1D2A44 bg, paper-coloured type · Seaside: #E3F1F4 bg, red numbers · Market day: #FFF4D6 bg, green ink.
**Real-world basis:** [Herb Lester: all guides](https://www.herblester.com/collections/all-guides), [Herb Lester: our guides](https://www.herblester.com/pages/our-guides), [Tokyo Cheapo: accommodation](https://tokyocheapo.com/accommodation/all/), [The List: eat and drink](https://www.list.co.uk/eat-drink), [Herb Lester: delivery](https://www.herblester.com/pages/delivery)
**Refs:**
- [Herb Lester: all guides](https://www.herblester.com/collections/all-guides): themed guides as products, each with a clear subject.
- [Tokyo Cheapo: accommodation](https://tokyocheapo.com/accommodation/all/): an independent guide organised by practical traveller needs.
- [The List: eat and drink](https://www.list.co.uk/eat-drink): a regional listings brand handling food alongside events.

### XXVI. Farms & land

<a id="239"></a>
#### 239 · Small Vineyard / Winery (`vine`)
**For:** small vineyards and wineries selling bottles direct, running a cellar door, tours and sometimes rooms or a restaurant.
**Templates:** front-page · Woo shop · single-product (wine) · product-category (still, sparkling, mixed cases, archive wines) · page-visit · archive-event · page-wine-club · page-tours · page-gifting · archive (journal) · page-contact
**Patterns (~45):** wine card (vintage, grapes, style, bottle size, price, "sold out"), tasting notes and vineyard notes per wine, mixed cases, gifting by price band (under £50, £50–£100, £100+), gift cards, wine club with tiers and founding-member waitlist, tours and tastings booking, visit block (address, opening hours, rooms, restaurant), harvest journal, awards line, events (harvest dinners), age gate.
**Content model:** Woo product meta (vintage, grapes, ABV, vineyard block, style, bottles produced, food notes), `event`, bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce, Age Gate, Subscriptions for WooCommerce (wine club), Simply Schedule Appointments or Event Tickets (tours), MotoPress Hotel Booking Lite only if there are rooms.
**Signature:** gifting shop filtered by price band (under £50 / £50–£100 / over £100), with mixed cases and gift cards in the same place (seen on: [Westwell Wines: gifting](https://www.westwellwines.com/collections/gifting)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Wine club waitlist for founding members before launch (seen on: [Tillingham: wine club](https://tillingham.com/wine-club/))
- Archive wines collection for older vintages still in stock (seen on: [Westwell Wines: archive wines](https://www.westwellwines.com/collections/archive-wines))
- Harvest updates in the journal, written by the grower (seen on: [Westwell Wines: gearing up to harvest 2026](https://www.westwellwines.com/blogs/journal/gearing-up-to-harvest-2026))
- Visit page combining opening hours, rooms, restaurant and wine tours (seen on: [Tillingham: visit](https://tillingham.com/visit/))
- "Christmas delivery: order by [date]" banner with an end date that removes itself
**Style: Natural-wine label art**
- Type: Headings Aktura (Fontshare, blackletter-cut display) 400 at 6rem; body General Sans (Fontshare) 400 at 18px; vintage and ABV in General Sans 600 tabular.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, text #1A1A1A, pét-nat pink #F4A6B8, vine green #3F5E3A, lees #6B2737 for buttons and prices.
- Layout: each wine page is built around its label artwork shown large and flat, with facts in a short column. Shop grid is two columns of bottles on plain white. Home: the current release label full-screen, then visit info, then the journal.
- Imagery: flat label artwork, bottles on white, the vineyard through the seasons shot on film-like colour; people picking at harvest.
- Motion: bottle images switch to the back label on hover; reduced motion shows a "back label" link instead.
- Why it fits now: small English and European producers sell through their label art and plain shop layouts, e.g. [Westwell Wines: still wines](https://www.westwellwines.com/collections/still-wines).
**Style variations:** Orange wine: #F2A541 surface, black · Sparkling: white bg, gold #B89B4A rules · Cellar: #2A1F1D bg, pink type.
**Real-world basis:** [Westwell Wines: gifting](https://www.westwellwines.com/collections/gifting), [Westwell Wines: mixed cases](https://www.westwellwines.com/collections/mixed-cases), [Westwell Wines: best cellar door](https://www.westwellwines.com/blogs/journal/best-cellar-door-small), [Tillingham: visit](https://tillingham.com/visit/), [Tillingham: wine club](https://tillingham.com/wine-club/)
**Refs:**
- [Westwell Wines: gifting](https://www.westwellwines.com/collections/gifting): gifting by price band with cases and cards.
- [Tillingham: visit](https://tillingham.com/visit/): a WordPress vineyard combining rooms, restaurant, pizza and tours.
- [Tillingham: wine club](https://tillingham.com/wine-club/): pre-launch waitlist for founding members.

#### 240 · Pick-Your-Own Orchard (`orchard`)
**For:** family farms running pick-your-own fruit, pumpkins and Christmas trees with a farm shop and seasonal events.
**Templates:** front-page · page-pyo · page-whats-picking · page-farm-tickets · page-your-visit · page-faq · archive-event · single-event · page-farm-shop · page-cafe · page-jobs
**Patterns (~40):** "What's picking today?" crop list (crop, field, status: good / limited / finished), season calendar by crop and month, farm ticket booking (sessions, "entry only, crops paid separately"), late-season capacity note, your-visit guide (containers, wellies, toilets, dogs, buggies), FAQ, pumpkin festival and maze events, farm shop hours, café, awards line, seasonal jobs.
**Content model:** `crop` (season start/end, status, field, price per kg), `session` (date, time, capacity), `event`, bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** Event Tickets (timed farm tickets with capacity), WooCommerce (ticket checkout and gift cards), companion "what's picking" block (status per crop, set by the farmer on a phone).
**Signature:** a "What's picking today?" crop status list updated daily, next to timed farm tickets whose numbers are cut when crop volumes fall (seen on: [Garson Farm: PYO](https://www.garsons.co.uk/pyo-farm)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Clear ticket rule: "Tickets permit entry only; crops picked are sold separately" (seen on: [Garson Farm: PYO](https://www.garsons.co.uk/pyo-farm))
- FAQ that answers the awkward questions (no toilets in the fields, passes non-refundable, daily limits) (seen on: [Crockford Bridge Farm: FAQ](https://www.crockfordbridgefarm.co.uk/FAQ))
- Harvest calendar by crop and month (seen on: [PickYourOwn.org: harvest calendars](https://www.pickyourown.org/USharvestcalendar.htm))
- Weather closure notice with a start and end time
- Gift cards for the farm shop (seen on: [Garsons: gift cards](https://www.garsons.co.uk/garden-centre-departments/gift-cards))
**Style: Grainy organic warm**
- Type: Headings Neco (Fontshare) 700 at 6rem; body Karla 400 at 18px; crop status labels in Karla 700.
- Palette: bg #FBF3E4, apple red #C1272D for "picking now", leaf #2E5E3E for nav and buttons, straw #F2C14E for "limited", ink #2B1D14.
- Layout: home is the crop board: a big list of crops with status and field, then ticket sessions, then your visit. Sections separated by generous but varied spacing; photo bands at full bleed between them.
- Imagery: warm, grain-textured photos of hands, crates and rows of fruit (grain applied to photos only, never to empty backgrounds); kids and dogs in wellies.
- Motion: none on scroll; crop status changes appear on reload. Buttons darken on hover.
- Why it fits now: food and farm brands have moved to warm, tactile photography and plain type after years of flat lifestyle stock, e.g. [Daylesford](https://www.daylesford.com/).
**Style variations:** Pumpkin: #E86A17 accent, black type · Christmas trees: #1E3B2F bg, white · Strawberry: #F7D6D0 surface, red #C1272D.
**Real-world basis:** [Garson Farm: PYO](https://www.garsons.co.uk/pyo-farm), [Crockford Bridge Farm: FAQ](https://www.crockfordbridgefarm.co.uk/FAQ), [Crockford Bridge Farm: pumpkin picking](https://www.crockfordbridgefarm.co.uk/pick-your-own-pumpkins), [PickYourOwn.org: harvest calendars](https://www.pickyourown.org/USharvestcalendar.htm), [Garsons: pumpkin parade](https://www.garsons.co.uk/pyo-farm/pumpkin-parade)
**Refs:**
- [Garson Farm: PYO](https://www.garsons.co.uk/pyo-farm): the crop board plus capacity-limited tickets.
- [Crockford Bridge Farm: FAQ](https://www.crockfordbridgefarm.co.uk/FAQ): a practical FAQ that heads off complaints.
- [PickYourOwn.org: harvest calendars](https://www.pickyourown.org/USharvestcalendar.htm): crop timing data to seed the season calendar.

<a id="241"></a>
#### 241 · Honey Producer (`honey`)
**For:** small beekeepers and urban apiaries selling raw single-origin honey, running tastings and supplying restaurants.
**Templates:** front-page · Woo shop · single-product (honey) · page-wholesale · page-tastings-and-workshops · page-bee-tours · page-our-apiaries · archive (journal/recipes) · page-faq · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** honey card (origin/apiary, harvest season, floral source, set or runny, jar size), monofloral range, jar size filter (227g, 340g, tubs), bundles and gift sets, "real honey is seasonal" explainer (why stock changes), crystallisation note, wholesale for hospitality (buckets, comb, comb stands), honey sommelier tastings, bee garden tours, pollinator planting / biodiversity services, recipes.
**Content model:** Woo product meta (apiary, harvest date, floral source, texture, batch no., jar size), `apiary` (location, forage), bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce, Jetpack Forms (wholesale and tasting enquiries), Simply Schedule Appointments (tours and tastings), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (apiary locations, approximate).
**Signature:** honey sold by origin and harvest, never blended, with each release's floral source and apiary on the jar page and a note that some honeys are seasonal releases (seen on: [Bermondsey Street Bees: raw honey wholesale](https://bermondseystreetbees.co.uk/raw-honey-wholesale-for-hospitality/) and [Savannah Bee Company: monofloral honey](https://savannahbee.com/collections/monofloral-honeys)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- "Real honey is seasonal" explainer for when a favourite sells out (seen on: [Savannah Bee: real honey is seasonal](https://savannahbee.com/blogs/the-latest-buzz/real-honey-is-seasonal))
- Tutored tasting and honey sommelier sessions for groups and businesses (seen on: [Bermondsey Street Bees: honey sommelier](https://bermondseystreetbees.co.uk/honey-sommelier-workshops-services/))
- Bee garden tours bookable online (seen on: [Savannah Bee: bee garden tours](https://savannahbee.com/pages/bee-garden-tours))
- Filter by jar size and bundle deals (seen on: [Taunton Honey: Somerset honey](https://www.wildflowerhoney.co.uk/shop/catalog/honey))
- "Why has my honey set?" care card on every product
**Style: Warm Scandi minimal**
- Type: Headings Hahmlet 500 at 5.5rem; body Figtree 400 at 18px; batch and harvest data in Figtree 600 tabular.
- Palette: bg #FAF8F3, text #2A241D, honey #E0A526 for buttons and the jar colour band, comb wax #F3E3B5 surface, line #D8CFBF.
- Layout: calm, wide margins; products in a two-column grid with jars photographed against the same light wall. Each honey page opens with a colour band matching that honey's actual colour. Home: current releases, then the apiary map, then tastings.
- Imagery: jars in daylight on linen and wood, frames and comb close-ups, the beekeeper at the hives; consistent warm white balance.
- Motion: none on scroll. Colour band fades in with the page (View Transition); reduced motion removes the fade.
- Why it fits now: warm, quiet Scandinavian-style layouts suit single-origin food products and slow editorial brands, e.g. [Kinfolk](https://www.kinfolk.com/).
**Style variations:** Heather: #6E4B6B band, cream type · Clover: #F6EBC2 bg, dark text · Dark honey: #3A2412 bg, honey type.
**Real-world basis:** [Bermondsey Street Bees: raw honey wholesale](https://bermondseystreetbees.co.uk/raw-honey-wholesale-for-hospitality/), [Bermondsey Street Bees: honey sommelier](https://bermondseystreetbees.co.uk/honey-sommelier-workshops-services/), [Savannah Bee: monofloral honey](https://savannahbee.com/collections/monofloral-honeys), [Savannah Bee: bee garden tours](https://savannahbee.com/pages/bee-garden-tours), [Taunton Honey: Somerset honey](https://www.wildflowerhoney.co.uk/shop/catalog/honey)
**Refs:**
- [Bermondsey Street Bees: raw honey wholesale](https://bermondseystreetbees.co.uk/raw-honey-wholesale-for-hospitality/): a WordPress site selling single-origin honey to restaurants.
- [Savannah Bee: real honey is seasonal](https://savannahbee.com/blogs/the-latest-buzz/real-honey-is-seasonal): explaining stock changes as part of the product.
- [Taunton Honey: Somerset honey](https://www.wildflowerhoney.co.uk/shop/catalog/honey): a small producer's shop filtered by jar size.

#### 242 · Sheep / Alpaca Farm & Wool (`fleece`)
**For:** small flocks and fibre farms selling breed-specific yarn, fleece, patterns and kits, often with workshops and farm visits.
**Templates:** front-page · Woo shop · product-category (by breed, by weight) · single-product (yarn) · page-our-breeds · page-caring-for-your-wool · page-patterns · archive-event · page-stockists · page-wholesale · page-story
**Patterns (~40):** yarn card (breed, weight, yardage, colourway, dye lot), shop by breed (Gotland, Hampshire, Bluefaced Leicester), shop by weight (4ply, DK, aran, lace), breed guide (origin, handle, staple length, micron, where sourced), pattern shop and pattern books, kits, care guide, stockists list and map, become-a-stockist (wholesale login), events and workshops, farm story, testimonials and reviews submission.
**Content model:** Woo product meta (breed, weight, yardage per 100g, micron, dye lot, flock), `breed` (origin, handle, staple length, micron, source), `stockist` (address, lat/lng), bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce, Event Tickets (workshops and farm days), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (stockists).
**Signature:** a breed guide listing each breed's origin, handle, staple length, micron count and where the fleece is sourced, linked to the yarns made from it (seen on: [baa ram ewe: our wool breeds](https://baaramewe.co.uk/pages/our-wool-breeds)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Care page for washing and storing wool (seen on: [baa ram ewe: caring for your wool](https://baaramewe.co.uk/pages/caring-for-your-wool))
- Stockists list and a wholesale route (seen on: [baa ram ewe: our stockists](https://baaramewe.co.uk/pages/our-stockists) and [become a stockist](https://baaramewe.co.uk/pages/become-a-stockist))
- Shop by breed, then by weight (seen on: [The Grey Sheep Co: Gotland](https://www.thegreysheep.co.uk/collections/gotland))
- Dye-lot note on each colourway ("buy enough for your project from one lot")
- Printable catalogue PDF for yarn shops (seen on: [baa ram ewe: catalogue](https://baaramewe.co.uk/pages/catalogue))
**Style: Tactile textile craft**
- Type: Headings Solway 700 at 5.5rem; body Work Sans 400 at 18px; yarn specs (micron, yardage) in Azeret Mono 500.
- Palette: undyed fleece #EEE9DF bg, moss #6B7F3A for buttons, heather #8E6C8A accent, ink #2C2A26, line #BDB4A2.
- Layout: product grid of skeins photographed on the same neutral cloth; breed guide as a specimen table with a fibre photo per row. Home: the flock (photo), then breeds, then new colourways, then stockists map.
- Imagery: macro shots of fibre and stitch, sheep in their fields, hands knitting; yarn colour photographed in daylight with a grey card for accuracy.
- Motion: skein images switch to a knitted swatch on hover; reduced motion shows a "swatch" link.
- Why it fits now: British wool brands are telling the breed and farm story in detail as buyers ask where fibre comes from, e.g. [baa ram ewe: our wool breeds](https://baaramewe.co.uk/pages/our-wool-breeds).
**Style variations:** Natural: undyed greys only · Hedgerow: #A23B4F berry accent · Winter flock: #2C2A26 bg, fleece type.
**Real-world basis:** [baa ram ewe: our wool breeds](https://baaramewe.co.uk/pages/our-wool-breeds), [baa ram ewe: caring for your wool](https://baaramewe.co.uk/pages/caring-for-your-wool), [baa ram ewe: become a stockist](https://baaramewe.co.uk/pages/become-a-stockist), [The Grey Sheep Co: Gotland](https://www.thegreysheep.co.uk/collections/gotland), [The Grey Sheep Co: story](https://www.thegreysheep.co.uk/blogs/story)
**Refs:**
- [baa ram ewe: our wool breeds](https://baaramewe.co.uk/pages/our-wool-breeds): breed guide with handle, staple length and micron.
- [The Grey Sheep Co: Gotland](https://www.thegreysheep.co.uk/collections/gotland): shopping by breed and then weight.
- [baa ram ewe: our stockists](https://baaramewe.co.uk/pages/our-stockists): stockist list for a brand sold in shops.

#### 243 · Market Garden (`market`)
**For:** small market gardens, community farms and CSAs selling veg boxes, market stalls and restaurant supply.
**Templates:** front-page · Woo shop · single-product (veg box) · page-veg-boxes · page-pickup-points · page-markets · page-our-growers · archive (news from the field) · page-recipes · page-volunteer · page-open-days · page-faqs
**Patterns (~45):** veg box sizes with "this week's box contents", pickup points list and map (host venue, collection days), delivery days, pause and holiday dates, markets list (where to find us), CSA share explained (5–7 items weekly, pickup day), growers/producers list with food-zone distances, monthly "news from the field", recipes using this week's veg, volunteering sessions, open days, discounts (pensioners, Healthy Start), wholesale for restaurants.
**Content model:** Woo subscription product meta (size, contents this week, delivery day), `pickup_point` (host, address, lat/lng, days, hours), `producer` (farm, distance, zone), bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce, Subscriptions for WooCommerce (weekly/fortnightly boxes with pause), Order Delivery Date for WooCommerce (delivery day), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (pickup points).
**Signature:** "Box contents" listed on the veg box product and updated weekly, so buyers see exactly what's in this week's bag (seen on: [Sutton Community Farm: small veg box](https://www.suttoncommunityfarm.org.uk/c/organic-vegboxes/small-veg-box-1)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Pause and holiday-date booking explained up front (seen on: [Growing Communities: veg schemes](https://growingcommunities.org/vegschemes))
- 30 pickup points hosted by local businesses, with self-service over 2–3 days (seen on: [Growing Communities: veg schemes](https://growingcommunities.org/vegschemes))
- Food-zones map showing how far each producer is from the city (seen on: [Growing Communities: food zones](https://growingcommunities.org/food-zones))
- Monthly "news from the field" diary (seen on: [Sutton Community Farm: news from the field, September](https://www.suttoncommunityfarm.org.uk/news/news-from-the-field-september))
- Healthy Start vouchers and pensioner discount stated clearly (seen on: [Growing Communities: veg schemes](https://growingcommunities.org/vegschemes))
**Style: Riso seed-packet**
- Type: Headings Gluten 700 at 6rem; body Atkinson Hyperlegible 400 at 18px; weights and days in Atkinson Hyperlegible 700.
- Palette: paper #FFFFFF, riso yellow #FFE800, riso teal #00838A for nav and buttons, fluorescent pink #FF48B0 for "this week", ink #222222.
- Layout: box sizes shown as seed-packet rectangles with a big illustration of the week's star veg; pickup points as a numbered list beside the map. Home: this week's box contents, then box sizes, then pickup map, then news from the field.
- Imagery: two-colour illustrations of vegetables in the style of old seed packets, plus real photos of harvest crates and growers in the field.
- Motion: none on scroll; illustrations have a slight overprint offset that resets on hover. Reduced motion keeps them aligned.
- Why it fits now: seed companies and small growers use art-packet illustration to sell the season, e.g. [Hudson Valley Seed Company](https://hudsonvalleyseed.com/).
**Style variations:** Brassica: #3E6B48 bg, yellow type · Beetroot: #8C1D40 accent, white · Frost: #E6F0F2 bg, teal ink.
**Real-world basis:** [Sutton Community Farm: small veg box](https://www.suttoncommunityfarm.org.uk/c/organic-vegboxes/small-veg-box-1), [Growing Communities: veg schemes](https://growingcommunities.org/vegschemes), [Growing Communities: our producers](https://growingcommunities.org/our-producers), [Singing Frogs Farm: CSA](https://www.singingfrogsfarm.com/csa), [Singing Frogs Farm: markets](https://www.singingfrogsfarm.com/markets)
**Refs:**
- [Sutton Community Farm: small veg box](https://www.suttoncommunityfarm.org.uk/c/organic-vegboxes/small-veg-box-1): weekly box contents on the product page.
- [Growing Communities: veg schemes](https://growingcommunities.org/vegschemes): pickup network, pausing and discounts in one page.
- [Singing Frogs Farm: CSA](https://www.singingfrogsfarm.com/csa): CSA share size, pickup day and pickup sites explained plainly.
