#### 244 · Riding Stables (`stable`)
**For:** riding schools and livery yards offering lessons, hacks, children's riding, intensive courses and livery.
**Templates:** front-page · page-prices · page-book-a-ride · page-lessons · page-childrens-riding · page-intensive-courses · page-horses · page-livery · page-membership · page-faqs · archive-event · page-gift-vouchers · page-local-area
**Patterns (~40):** price list (private lesson, group lesson, hack, 30/60 min, members vs non-members), booking/enquiry form, rider requirements (weight limit, minimum age, clothing), equipment provided (boots, hats, waterproofs), meet the horses (name, breed, height, character, suitable riders), team and instructor qualifications, children's riding and pony days, intensive courses, livery options, membership and members' FAQ, open afternoons, events (quiz night, horse walk), gift vouchers, cancellation policy.
**Content model:** `horse` (breed, height in hands, age, temperament, rider level), `lesson_type` (duration, price member/non-member, min age), `event`, bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** Simply Schedule Appointments (lessons and hacks), WooCommerce (gift vouchers), Jetpack Forms (livery and membership enquiries), Advanced Query Loop (events).
**Signature:** a riding FAQ that states the rider weight limit, minimum age, what kit is provided and the cancellation policy before anyone books (seen on: [Hyde Park Stables: riding FAQs](https://www.hydeparkstables.com/riding-faqs)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Meet-the-horses page with each horse matched to rider levels (seen on: [Wimbledon Village Stables: horses](https://www.wvstables.com/horses/))
- Gift vouchers for rides (seen on: [Hyde Park Stables: gift voucher](https://www.hydeparkstables.com/buy-a-horse-riding-gift-voucher-london))
- Monthly open afternoon for families thinking about lessons (seen on: [WVS: open afternoons](https://www.wvstables.com/open-afternoons/))
- Separate FAQs for members and non-members (seen on: [WVS: non-member FAQs](https://www.wvstables.com/non-member-faqs/))
- Livery page with options and what's included (seen on: [WVS: livery](https://www.wvstables.com/livery/))
**Style: Heritage equestrian serif**
- Type: Headings Oranienbaum 400 at 6rem; body Lora 400 at 18px; prices and times in Lora 600 with tabular figures.
- Palette: bone #F3EFE6 bg, racing green #0F3B2E for header and buttons, saddle brown #5A3825, brass #B8913A for rules and prices, ink #16130F.
- Layout: price list set like a printed tariff card with dotted leaders; horses as a two-column register (photo, name, height, "suits"). Home: next open afternoon, the tariff, then the horses.
- Imagery: documentary photos of lessons and hacks in real weather, portraits of each horse in the yard, tack details; no stock show-jumping.
- Motion: none on scroll; horse cards show a second photo on hover. Reduced motion disables the swap.
- Why it fits now: heritage leather and equestrian goods makers use restrained serif layouts that fit a traditional sport without looking dated, e.g. [Ettinger](https://ettingerlondon.com/).
**Style variations:** Hunting pink: #9E1B32 accent · Gymkhana: white bg, rosette blue #1F4E8C · Winter yard: #1B2420 bg, brass type.
**Real-world basis:** [Hyde Park Stables: prices](https://www.hydeparkstables.com/london-hyde-park-horse-riding-prices), [Hyde Park Stables: riding FAQs](https://www.hydeparkstables.com/riding-faqs), [Wimbledon Village Stables: horses](https://www.wvstables.com/horses/), [WVS: book a ride](https://www.wvstables.com/book-a-ride/), [WVS: livery](https://www.wvstables.com/livery/)
**Refs:**
- [Hyde Park Stables: riding FAQs](https://www.hydeparkstables.com/riding-faqs): weight limit, age, kit and cancellations answered directly.
- [Wimbledon Village Stables: horses](https://www.wvstables.com/horses/): a WordPress stables introducing its horses and how riders are matched.
- [Hyde Park Stables: prices](https://www.hydeparkstables.com/london-hyde-park-horse-riding-prices): a single clear price page.

### XXVII. Pets & animals

<a id="245"></a>
#### 245 · Dog Walker (`walkies`)
**For:** solo dog walkers and small walking teams covering a few postcodes, offering group walks, solo walks, puppy visits and house sitting.
**Templates:** front-page · page-dog-walking · page-puppy-visits · page-house-sitting · page-small-pet-visits · page-charges · page-meet-the-team · page-faq · page-gallery · page-area (one per village/postcode) · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** services list, charges table (weekday vs weekend, per dog, additional dog from same household), group size promise ("max 6 dogs per walker"), free meet-and-greet booking, meet the team (walker, dogs of their own, first-aid training), areas covered list and map, FAQ (insurance incl. key cover, keys, bad weather, first meeting), gallery of walks, per-area landing pages, contact with phone number in the header.
**Content model:** `service` (duration, weekday price, weekend price, additional dog price), `area` (name, postcodes), `team_member` (role, qualifications, pronouns), bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (new client form with dog details and vet), Cal.com embed or Simply Schedule Appointments (meet-and-greet slots), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (areas covered).
**Signature:** a charges table with weekday and weekend prices per service and an "additional dog from the same household" rate, next to a free face-to-face meet-and-greet booking (seen on: [Muddy Paws Dog Walking: charges](https://www.muddypawsdogwalking.co.uk/charges/) and [Muddy Paws: FAQ](https://www.muddypawsdogwalking.co.uk/faq/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Insurance answer that mentions key cover and offers to show the certificate (seen on: [Muddy Paws: FAQ](https://www.muddypawsdogwalking.co.uk/faq/))
- How keys are stored ("kept separate from your address") (seen on: [Muddy Paws: FAQ](https://www.muddypawsdogwalking.co.uk/faq/))
- Per-area pages for each village covered (seen on: [Muddy Paws: dog walking Locks Heath](https://www.muddypawsdogwalking.co.uk/dog-walking-locks-heath/))
- "Currently full on Mondays and Fridays" availability line the walker updates
- Bad-weather policy ("we get wet; leave a towel") (seen on: [Muddy Paws: FAQ](https://www.muddypawsdogwalking.co.uk/faq/))
**Style: Playful sticker / hand-drawn doodle**
- Type: Headings Rammetto One 400 at 5rem; body Lexend 400 at 18px; doodle annotations in Gochi Hand at 1.4rem used sparingly next to photos.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, ink #1F1F1F, grass #3FA34D for buttons, sky #9AD1F5 surface, ball yellow #FFD23F for prices.
- Layout: photos of the actual dogs as die-cut stickers (white outline) scattered at small angles over a clean grid; the charges table stays straight and readable. Home: phone number and areas first, then prices, then team.
- Imagery: the walker's own phone photos of dogs on walks, cut out as stickers; hand-drawn arrows and paw marks drawn by the owner, not clip art.
- Motion: stickers rotate back to 0° on hover; no bouncing. Reduced motion keeps them still.
- Why it fits now: pet brands use bright, sticker-and-doodle identities that feel human rather than corporate, e.g. [Wild One](https://wildone.com/).
**Style variations:** Muddy: #6B4F2C bg, yellow type · Beach walk: #F4E7C5 bg, sea blue #1F6F8B · Night reflective: #111 bg, hi-vis #D7FF00 labels only on buttons.
**Real-world basis:** [Muddy Paws: charges](https://www.muddypawsdogwalking.co.uk/charges/), [Muddy Paws: FAQ](https://www.muddypawsdogwalking.co.uk/faq/), [Muddy Paws: meet the team](https://www.muddypawsdogwalking.co.uk/meet-the-team/), [Muddy Paws: dog walking Locks Heath](https://www.muddypawsdogwalking.co.uk/dog-walking-locks-heath/), [The Dog Stop: home](https://thedogstop.com/)
**Refs:**
- [Muddy Paws: charges](https://www.muddypawsdogwalking.co.uk/charges/): weekday/weekend and additional-dog pricing.
- [Muddy Paws: FAQ](https://www.muddypawsdogwalking.co.uk/faq/): the trust questions every walker gets, answered.
- [Muddy Paws: meet the team](https://www.muddypawsdogwalking.co.uk/meet-the-team/): introducing who will actually have your keys.

#### 246 · Dog Groomer (`groom`)
**For:** home-based and small-salon dog groomers, some also grooming cats or offering self-service wash bays.
**Templates:** front-page · page-dog-grooming · page-cat-grooming · page-puppy-introduction · page-groom-your-own-dog · page-prices · page-booking · page-gallery · page-reviews · page-terms · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** services price board (bath and towel dry, bath and tidy, full groom, de-shed, hand strip, teeth, pawdicure; "from £" prices), puppy introduction course (3–4 visits under 6 months), cat grooming, self-service "groom your own dog" bay, deposit and payment terms, matted-coat and nervous-dog policy, before/after gallery, reviews page, booking with deposit, location note (e.g. inside a garden centre, parking), phone and email in the header.
**Content model:** `service` (price from, duration, coat types, size band), bound via Block Bindings; `gallery` uses core Gallery.
**Plugins:** Simply Schedule Appointments (booking by service length), WooCommerce (deposits and gift vouchers), Jetpack Forms (new-dog form: breed, age, coat condition, vaccination date).
**Signature:** a price board of services with "from" prices plus a staged puppy introduction package spread over several short visits (seen on: [Scruffs Dog Grooming: dog grooming services](https://www.scruffsgrooming.co.uk/dog-grooming%20services)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Deposit taken at booking, balance on collection, stated in the terms (seen on: [Bark and Blossom: services](https://www.barkandblossom.co.uk/services))
- Self-service "groom your own dog" option listed alongside full grooms (seen on: [Scruffs Dog Grooming: home](https://www.scruffsgrooming.co.uk/))
- Cat grooming page for groomers who take cats (seen on: [Scruffs: cat grooming services](https://scruffsgrooming.co.uk/cat-grooming-services/))
- Matted-coat policy in plain words (shave-down for welfare, extra charge)
- "What to expect at your dog's first groom" page for nervous owners
**Style: Pastel salon price board**
- Type: Headings Chillax (Fontshare) 600 at 5rem; body Hanken Grotesk 400 at 18px; prices in Red Hat Mono 500 aligned right.
- Palette: blush #FDE8EC bg, mint #CDEFE3 surface for price panels, butter #FFF1B8 highlight for offers, ink #2B2B2B, chrome grey #BFC5CC for rules.
- Layout: the price board is the hero: a salon-style menu with services left and prices right, dotted leaders, grouped by coat type. Buttons are 999px pills (the only pill in the theme); panels square. Home: price board, then before/after pairs, then booking.
- Imagery: before/after photo pairs of real clients shot in the same spot and light; close-ups of tools; no stock "dog in bathrobe" images.
- Motion: before/after pairs use a draggable divider (keyboard accessible); reduced motion shows the two photos side by side.
- Why it fits now: pastel, clean salon branding borrowed from beauty retail reads as calm and hygienic to owners, e.g. [Glossier](https://www.glossier.com/).
**Style variations:** Mint parlour: #CDEFE3 bg, black type · Candy stripe: pink and white stripes on header only · Barber: #1C1C1C bg, chrome text.
**Real-world basis:** [Scruffs: dog grooming services](https://www.scruffsgrooming.co.uk/dog-grooming%20services), [Scruffs: cat grooming](https://scruffsgrooming.co.uk/cat-grooming-services/), [Bark and Blossom: services](https://www.barkandblossom.co.uk/services), [Pooch Parlour: home](https://pooch-parlour.co.uk/), [The Cat Spa: home](https://www.thecatspa.co.uk/)
**Refs:**
- [Scruffs: dog grooming services](https://www.scruffsgrooming.co.uk/dog-grooming%20services): a full "from £" price list and the staged puppy introduction.
- [Bark and Blossom: services](https://www.barkandblossom.co.uk/services): deposit and payment terms beside the services.
- [The Cat Spa: home](https://www.thecatspa.co.uk/): a groomer that specialises in cats.

#### 247 · Dog Trainer (`heel`)
**For:** independent dog trainers and behaviourists running puppy classes, 1:1 training and online courses, often under a network or accreditation.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-class · single-class · page-find-a-class · page-1-2-1-training · page-behaviour · page-puppy-advice · page-our-tutors · page-testimonials · page-online-courses · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** class course page (weeks, class size, age range, what's covered, price, venue), find-a-class by postcode, class dates and places left, curriculum list (recall, sit/down/stand, loose-lead walking, handling and vet-exam prep, settle), homework note, members' video area, tutors list with qualifications and accreditation, puppy advice articles, 1:1 and behaviour consult booking, testimonials, accreditation badge (APDT, ABTC).
**Content model:** `class` (course type, start date, weeks, venue, max dogs, places left, price, age limit), `tutor` (area, qualifications, accreditation no.), bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** Event Tickets (class places with capacity) or WooCommerce, Simply Schedule Appointments (1:1 sessions), Sensei LMS (optional online course), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (class venues).
**Signature:** a six-week course page that states class size ("maximum of eight puppies"), age limit and a week-by-week curriculum, with a find-a-class search by location (seen on: [Puppy School: puppy school class](https://www.puppyschool.co.uk/our-classes/puppy-school) and [Puppy School: find a class](https://www.puppyschool.co.uk/find-a-class)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- "Places left" counter on each class date, turning to "waiting list" when full
- Accreditation badge with a membership number that links to the association's find-a-trainer page (seen on: [APDT UK: find a trainer](https://www.apdt.co.uk/))
- Puppy advice library for owners before and after class (seen on: [Puppy School: puppy advice](https://www.puppyschool.co.uk/puppy-advice))
- Tutor pages with qualifications and areas covered (seen on: [Puppy School: our tutors](https://www.puppyschool.co.uk/our-tutors))
- Printable homework sheet per week of the course
**Style: Utility training-manual diagrams**
- Type: Headings Varta 700 at 5.5rem; body Varta 400 at 18px; step numbers and cue words in IBM Plex Mono 600 (the steps are a real sequence).
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF, ink #111111, signal blue #0055A4 for buttons and cue words, lead red #D7263D for "places left" and warnings, surface #F1F1EE.
- Layout: course pages read like a manual: numbered weeks down the left, each with a small line diagram (dog position, handler position, lead) and a short instruction. Class dates in a table with places left. Home: next courses, find a class, then advice.
- Imagery: simple two-colour line diagrams drawn for the theme (sit, down, loose lead, recall), plus real class photos in village halls and fields.
- Motion: none. Diagrams are static SVG; a "show step" toggle reveals the next frame for multi-step cues.
- Why it fits now: instruction-manual clarity is being used by product brands as a visual identity, and suits a service that is teaching step by step, e.g. [teenage engineering: guides](https://teenage.engineering/guides).
**Style variations:** Field: #E6EFE3 bg, green #2F6B3A cues · Night class: #111111 bg, white diagrams · Clicker: yellow #FFD23F surface, black.
**Real-world basis:** [Puppy School: puppy school class](https://www.puppyschool.co.uk/our-classes/puppy-school), [Puppy School: find a class](https://www.puppyschool.co.uk/find-a-class), [Puppy School: our tutors](https://www.puppyschool.co.uk/our-tutors), [APDT UK](https://www.apdt.co.uk/), [The Dog Spa: training](https://www.thedogspa.co.uk/training)
**Refs:**
- [Puppy School: puppy school class](https://www.puppyschool.co.uk/our-classes/puppy-school): class size, ages and curriculum laid out before booking.
- [Puppy School: find a class](https://www.puppyschool.co.uk/find-a-class): location search across many independent tutors.
- [APDT UK](https://www.apdt.co.uk/): the accreditation body's find-a-trainer route a badge should point to.

#### 248 · Cattery / Pet Boarding (`boarding`)
**For:** licensed catteries and small boarding kennels with a fixed number of pens, drop-off windows and peak-season deposits.
**Templates:** front-page · page-our-pens · page-pricing · page-availability-enquiry · page-booking-request · page-boarding-conditions · page-what-to-bring · page-gallery · page-about · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** licence panel (council, licence number, star rating, "licensed for up to 18 cats"), pens/suites description (heated, UPVC, private, outdoor run), pricing table (one cat, pair sharing, three or more POA; half-day charge note), availability enquiry form (dates, AM/PM arrival and collection, cats, breed, size), boarding conditions (vaccination certificate, flea treatment, deposits, cancellation, vet consent), what to bring checklist, drop-off and collection time slots (and Christmas closures), updates by text and photo during the stay, pet taxi, gallery of the pens.
**Content model:** MotoPress accommodation types for pen sizes (single, double, family), plus meta for heating, run size and outlook; site-wide licence meta (authority, number, star rating, capacity), bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** MotoPress Hotel Booking Lite (pens as accommodation types with availability calendar), Jetpack Forms (availability enquiry and new-cat form with the File Upload field for the vaccination certificate).
**Signature:** a boarding conditions page that sets out vaccination and flea-treatment rules, peak-period 50% deposits with cancellation cut-offs, vet consent and a what-to-bring list, linked from every booking form (seen on: [Charlesberry Cattery: boarding conditions](https://thecattery.com/boarding-conditions/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Licence number and council shown in the footer on every page (seen on: [Cosy Cats Cattery: home](https://www.cosycats.co.uk/) and [Purr-fect Place Cattery: home](https://www.purrfectcattery.co.uk/))
- Half-day charging for arrival and departure days, explained on the price page (seen on: [Charlesberry Cattery: pricing](https://thecattery.com/pricing/))
- Drop-off and collection by time slot, with Christmas Day and Boxing Day closures listed (seen on: [Charlesberry Cattery: home](https://thecattery.com/))
- Vaccination certificate uploaded with the booking so it isn't forgotten on the day
- "Updates by text and email during the stay, just ask" line (seen on: [Cosy Cats Cattery: home](https://www.cosycats.co.uk/))
**Style: Warm boutique-hotel editorial**
- Type: Headings Alike 400 at 5.5rem; body Karla 400 at 18px; prices and times in Karla 700 tabular.
- Palette: linen #F4EFE7 bg, wall green #2F4F46 for header and buttons, blanket ochre #D9A441 accent, stripe pink #E7B7B0 for surface panels, ink #1E1E1C.
- Layout: pens presented like hotel rooms: a large photo, a short description, a facts line (heated, run, shelf, window), then price. Conditions and what-to-bring as clear checklists. Home: licence panel and star rating, the pens, pricing, then the availability form.
- Imagery: photos of the real pens with blankets and shelves, cats settled in them, staff with cats; warm but accurate colour.
- Motion: pen photos cross-fade between two shots on hover; reduced motion shows the first only.
- Why it fits now: owners choose boarding the way they choose a hotel, and small boutique hotels set the tone for "calm and cared for", e.g. [Firmdale Hotels](https://www.firmdalehotels.com/).
**Style variations:** Country kennel: #3E5A3C bg, cream-white type · Seaside: #E8F1F2 bg, navy #1D3557 · Night quiet: #1E1E1C bg, ochre type.
**Real-world basis:** [Charlesberry Cattery: boarding conditions](https://thecattery.com/boarding-conditions/), [Charlesberry Cattery: pricing](https://thecattery.com/pricing/), [Charlesberry Cattery: availability enquiry](https://thecattery.com/availability-enquiry/), [Cosy Cats Cattery: boarding fees](https://www.cosycats.co.uk/menu), [The Dog Spa: kennels](https://www.thedogspa.co.uk/kennels)
**Refs:**
- [Charlesberry Cattery: boarding conditions](https://thecattery.com/boarding-conditions/): a WordPress cattery's full conditions: vaccinations, deposits, cancellation, what to bring.
- [Charlesberry Cattery: availability enquiry](https://thecattery.com/availability-enquiry/): the fields a boarding enquiry actually needs.

### XXVIII. Spaces, hire & unusual services

> **Rental stack (applies to 253–256, and to hireable rooms and kit elsewhere in this batch).** Checked on wordpress.org in September 2026: **Booking and Rental Manager for WooCommerce** (MagePeople, sold as "WpRently", free tier, updated September 2026, 1,000+ installs) handles single-day and multi-day hire with hourly, daily and weekly pricing, per-item inventory, availability-aware date pickers, extra services and add-ons, and WooCommerce block checkout. It ships five blocks: Rental Items List, Search Form, Filter, Add to Cart and Search Results. Its "Security Deposit Management" and admin booking calendar are **Pro-only**, so the themes do this instead. The **refundable deposit** is a required extra-service line on each item, refunded through the normal Woo refund screen. The **damage waiver** is an optional add-on priced as a percentage of the hire. The public availability view is a companion Interactivity-API block that reads booked dates from Woo orders. Rejected: Easy Booking (free, but per-date stock is a paid add-on), WPS Bookings (slot-based, suits appointments rather than kit), YITH Request a Quote (free tier works but is rated 3.3/5 with slow support). Where hire is quote-led (marquees, entertainers, bands), the themes use a **request-to-book** flow: a companion "quote list" block that pre-fills a Jetpack Form with items, date, venue and postcode, as real hire firms do.

<a id="249"></a>
#### 249 · Makerspace / Hackerspace (`solder`)
**For:** volunteer-run, member-funded hackspaces and community makerspaces (30–300 members, one unit, a laser cutter and a wiki) where the board are unpaid and the website has to answer "is anyone in tonight?"
**Real-world basis:** [Leeds Hackspace: home with live open/closed status](https://leedshackspace.org.uk/), [Leeds Hackspace: membership](https://leedshackspace.org.uk/membership/), [Hackspace Manchester: visit us](https://www.hacman.org.uk/visit-us/), [Hackspace Manchester docs: laser cutter](https://docs.hacman.org.uk/equipment/visual_arts/equipment/laser_cutter/), [Maker Nexus: facilities and tools](https://makernexus.org/facilities-and-tools), [LVL1: about the space](https://www.lvl1.org/about-the-space/)
**Templates:** front-page (status line, open nights, what's in the space) · page-what-is-a-hackspace · page-visit (getting here, open evening tour) · page-membership (how to join, rates, probationary vs 24/7) · archive-tool (equipment grouped by area) · single-tool (spec, materials, induction) · archive-event (calendar) · page-donations · page-about (board, bylaws, constitution) · page-contact
**Patterns (~42):** space status line ("The space is currently open / closed"), open-hours block ("Tuesdays 7pm–9pm, 2nd Saturday 12pm–4pm"), open evening tour notice ("most Wednesdays, no booking required, 30–45 minutes"), equipment-by-area index (Woodshop, Metal Shop, Visual Arts, Electronics, Textiles, 3D Printing, Laser), tool spec sheet (make/model, bed size, power, "usable by members who have had an induction"), allowed / banned / higher-risk materials table, membership rates (Standard, Concessionary for students and unwaged), "how to join" steps (visit, sign up, standing order, induction, tool inductions, sponsorship to full member), probationary vs 24/7 member explainer, lone-working rules, "Be excellent to each other" house policy, how-to-find-the-door photo directions, access notes, donations and "we need" kit list, bylaws and minutes list (PDF), wiki / forum / mailing-list links row
**Content model:** companion `tool` CPT (taxonomy `area`; meta: make_model, bed_size, power, induction_required, materials_allowed, materials_banned, status working/out of order, docs_url), companion `event` for open nights and inductions, one site option `space_status` (open/closed, open_until, opened_by) exposed through a Block Bindings source.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (upcoming events, tools filtered by area), Jetpack Forms (visit / induction requests), optional Subscriptions for WooCommerce if the space takes card dues instead of standing orders.
**Signature:** a live **space status line** on every page: "The space is currently Open, someone is in until about 9pm". A keyholder flips it from a two-button companion block on their phone (logged-in only, Interactivity API writing the `space_status` option); the value is bound site-wide via Block Bindings, and each change is also logged as a short post in a `status` category so members can follow the core RSS feed, the way Leeds' OpenBot posts open/closed messages. (seen on: [Leeds Hackspace](https://leedshackspace.org.uk/social/openbot))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- "How to find the door" block with a photo and one plain sentence per landmark ("pacman symbol painted on it and HACMAN above it, large green doorbell") plus buses, tram stops, cycle parking and on-street parking hours. (seen on: [Hackspace Manchester](https://www.hacman.org.uk/visit-us/))
- Honest access note: "one small doorstep to get in, mostly on one level, floor can be uneven, no employed cleaners so walkways aren't guaranteed clear". (seen on: [Hackspace Manchester](https://www.hacman.org.uk/visit-us/))
- Printable materials card per machine (allowed / banned / higher-risk) generated from `tool` meta, for pinning next to the laser. (seen on: [Hackspace Manchester docs](https://docs.hacman.org.uk/equipment/visual_arts/equipment/laser_cutter/))
- Concessionary rate shown in the same table as the standard rate, with the 18+ rule stated once in plain words. (seen on: [Leeds Hackspace](https://leedshackspace.org.uk/membership/))
- Dated notice block for schedule changes ("Wednesday open evening tour time has changed for 2026") with start/end dates so it switches itself off. (seen on: [Hackspace Manchester](https://hacman.org.uk/))
**Style: Utility/industrial signage**
- Type: Headings: Stick No Bills 800 (OFL, a stencil-cut signage face from Sri Lanka), uppercase, 72–128px, tracking +0.01em, line-height 0.95; tool codes and area labels: Stick No Bills 600; body: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 400/18px, line-height 1.6; spec tables and timestamps: Martian Mono 500/15px.
- Palette: #EDEDE8 bg (painted blockwork grey) · #141414 text and header band · #F2C200 safety yellow (warnings, induction-required flag) · #1F7A3A go green (only for "Open" and "Working") · #C8102E stop red (only for "Closed", "Banned material", "Out of order") · #B9B9B2 line
- Layout: black header band with a thin white rule across the top, like a transit sign; the status line sits directly under it, full width, with a text label next to its colour so state never relies on colour alone. 12-column grid, 0 radius, 2px black rules instead of cards. Front page is status, this week's open nights, then the equipment index as a long ruled table (code, machine, area, induction, status) that links to each tool sheet. Top nav is five words; wiki and forum are external links in the footer row.
- Imagery: flash-lit documentary photos of the actual machines and benches at 4:3, square corners, each captioned with its tool code (LZ-01, WS-03); no people-at-laptops stock. Area pages open on a full-bleed photo of the wall of tools.
- Motion: status change cross-fades (opacity only, 180ms); View Transitions between the equipment index and a tool sheet; nothing on scroll. All of it wrapped in prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
- Why it fits now: the 1970 NYC subway manual reissue made plain civic signage a live design reference again, and it suits spaces that are literally full of warning labels: [Standards Manual: NYCTA Graphics Standards Manual](https://standardsmanual.com/products/nyctacompactedition)
**Style variations:** Night Shift (#141414 bg, #F2C200 type) · Workshop Floor (#D9D4C7 bg, black stencil codes) · Electronics Bench (#E9EEF0 bg, #0F5E8C solder-mask blue)
**Refs:**
- [Leeds Hackspace: OpenBot status feed](https://leedshackspace.org.uk/social/openbot): open/closed status driven by a device in the space and published as a feed; the model for the status line and its RSS log
- [Hackspace Manchester docs: laser cutter](https://docs.hacman.org.uk/equipment/visual_arts/equipment/laser_cutter/): what a real tool sheet holds: bed size, power, allowed/banned/higher-risk materials, induction rule
- [Leeds Hackspace: membership](https://leedshackspace.org.uk/membership/): rates, probationary vs 24/7 members, and the step-by-step joining route in the space's own words

<a id="250"></a>
#### 250 · Coworking Space (`desk`)
**For:** single-building independent coworkings (20–80 desks, often freelancer-only) that sell part-time plans, day passes and a community, not private office floors.
**Real-world basis:** [The Skiff (Brighton): pricing](https://www.theskiff.org/pricing), [The Skiff: home with named zones](https://www.theskiff.org/), [Indy Hall (Philadelphia): pricing](https://indyhall.org/pricing/), [Indy Hall: Clubhouse Card](https://indyhall.org/card/), [Indy Hall: monthly clubs](https://indyhall.org/monthlies/), [Cornerstone Coworking: memberships](https://cancollab.com/services/coworking-memberships/)
**Templates:** front-page · page-pricing (plans and add-ons) · page-day-pass (guest pass) · page-trial-card · page-tour (book a tour and trial day) · page-meeting-rooms · single-room · page-members (member directory) · page-clubs (recurring events) · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** plan table by days per month (Occasional / Regular / Key, with hours and "up to 5 days (40 hours)"), evening-and-weekend plan row, day pass block (price, what's included, "one hour of call room, pending availability"), 5-day trial card offer, "month-to-month, no lock-in" terms line, annual prepay discount line, add-ons price list (business address and mailbox, printing, extra members, guest passes), zone guide with rules per room (main room, quiet room "no phone calls", kitchen, phone booths), meeting room sheet (seats, screen, whiteboard, casting, hourly/daily rate), book-a-tour embed with fallback link, member directory (name, trade, link), recurring clubs list ("1st Friday", "2nd & 4th Wednesday", RSVP), host-an-event enquiry, hours and front-desk times, sponsored membership note
**Content model:** companion `room` CPT (seats, kit, hourly_rate, daily_rate), `member` CPT (name, trade, url, opt_in), companion `event` for clubs with a recurrence text field; plans are WooCommerce subscription products.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce + Subscriptions for WooCommerce (monthly plans, day pass, trial card), Booking and Rental Manager for WooCommerce (hourly/daily meeting-room hire, per the rental stack), Jetpack Forms (event hosting enquiries, sponsored membership applications), Cal.com embed for tours (the real sites use SavvyCal and Calendly embeds).
**Signature:** a **5-day trial card**: one Woo product sold as "5 full days, use them in a row or across 12 months", shown next to the day pass with the saving worked out in plain words ("$149 for 5 days, 40% less than 5 day passes"), valid 9am–6pm weekdays, 30 minutes of call room per visit, extra call time priced per hour. Days are ticked off at the front desk, so no check-in system is needed. (seen on: [Indy Hall](https://indyhall.org/card/))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Free sponsored membership for people under-represented in tech, funded by members and sponsors and reviewed quarterly, with an application form. (seen on: [The Skiff](https://www.theskiff.org/pricing))
- Zone rules printed where they apply: the quiet room says "no phone calls", the kitchen says when the shared lunch is. (seen on: [The Skiff](https://www.theskiff.org/))
- Add-ons as a plain price list: business address with mailbox $40/month, printing $5/month, extra guests $10. (seen on: [Cornerstone Coworking](https://cancollab.com/services/coworking-memberships/))
- Tour embed with a text fallback ("If the calendar does not appear, use this link") and a choice of video call or in-person visit. (seen on: [Indy Hall](https://indyhall.org/tour/))
- Open clubs list for non-members ("All are welcome with an RSVP, no membership required unless noted"), including a pay-what-you-wish coworking day. (seen on: [Indy Hall](https://indyhall.org/monthlies/))
**Style: Warm Scandi minimal**
- Type: Headings: Ysabeau Office 600 (OFL, a humanist sans with a calligraphic warmth), 76–104px, tracking -0.01em, line-height 1.02; body: Newsreader 400/18px, line-height 1.65, 66ch measure; prices and times: Ysabeau Office 500 with tabular figures at 17px.
- Palette: #F6F6F2 bg (limewashed wall) · #23221F text · #3F6B4F linoleum green (links, primary action) · #E4DED2 birch-ply surface (plan table, zone guide) · #A7794B oak (dividers under headings, one use per section) · #CDC6B8 line
- Layout: asymmetric 5/7 grid with generous, uneven section spacing. Front page opens with one wide daylight photo of the main room and a left-aligned sentence ("A coworking room for freelancers, two minutes from the station"), then the plan table as ruled rows, the zone guide as photo + short rules per room, then this month's clubs. 2px radius on buttons only, images square. Nav: Pricing, Visit, Rooms, Members, Clubs, and one "Book a tour" text link.
- Imagery: natural-light photos at 3:2 of the real rooms at working hours: desks, plants, plywood, lino, the kettle; members photographed at their own desks with permission. No laptop-and-latte flatlays.
- Motion: View Transitions between room list and room page; a 150ms colour shift on links; nothing on scroll; reduced motion removes transitions entirely.
- Why it fits now: soft, daylight-led Scandinavian minimalism is what independent workspaces use to look calm rather than corporate, and it is carried by material photography, not decoration: [Norm Architects](https://normcph.com/)
**Style variations:** Winter Light (#EEF1F2 bg, #2F4F5F slate accent) · Oak (#E9E0D1 bg, #6B4A2B type) · After Hours (#1E1F1C bg, #D9CBB2 text)
**Refs:**
- [Indy Hall: Clubhouse Card](https://indyhall.org/card/): the trial-card offer, its terms and how it is sold against the day pass
- [The Skiff: pricing](https://www.theskiff.org/pricing): plans by days per month, evening/weekend plan, and a free sponsored membership line in the same table
- [Indy Hall: monthly clubs](https://indyhall.org/monthlies/): recurring community events listed by ordinal day with RSVP, open to non-members

<a id="251"></a>
#### 251 · Escape Room (`locked`)
**For:** independent escape-room venues with 2–6 themed rooms, private bookings only, selling birthdays, hen and stag dos and team building on the side.
**Real-world basis:** [The Quandary (Chicago): room quiz](https://quandaryescape.com/quiz), [The Quandary: walk-ins](https://quandaryescape.com/walkins), [The Quandary: Lab of the Lost](https://quandaryescape.com/lab-of-the-lost), [clueQuest (London): Revenge of the Sheep](https://www.cluequest.co.uk/escape-room-missions/revenge-of-the-sheep), [clueQuest: FAQ](https://www.cluequest.co.uk/faq), [Bewilder Box (Brighton): home](https://www.bewilderbox.co.uk/)
**Templates:** front-page · archive-room (Our Rooms / Missions) · single-room · page-quiz (find your room) · page-booking · page-walk-ins · page-birthdays · page-hen-and-stag · page-corporate (team building) · page-vouchers · page-faq · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** room poster card (title, one-line story, players "2–7", 60 minutes, difficulty "4/5", age "14+"), story block ("You have 60 minutes to..."), room spec line, per-room booking button into the booking embed, "private bookings only, whatever your group size" note, per-person price with weekday offer code, seasonal edition banner with dates, birthday package, hen and stag package, team-building page with group capacity, gift voucher block (valid 1 year, printable), walk-ins status, arrival and late-arrival policy, cancellation policy, accessibility notes per room (wheelchair lift copies, flashing lights, sound and colour puzzles, doors can stay open), under-16 supervision rule, team photo note, address with parking and nearest station
**Content model:** companion `room` CPT (players_min, players_max, duration, difficulty 1–5, min_age, story, access_notes, flashing_lights, wheelchair_copy, edition_start, edition_end, booking_url), one site option `walkins` (available / not today) bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** Resova or Bookeo embed for bookings and gift vouchers (both real sites run bookings and vouchers through a hosted booking system; Simply Schedule Appointments is the self-hosted fallback with one calendar per room), Jetpack Forms (corporate and party enquiries).
**Signature:** a **"find your room" quiz**: eight quick questions (group size, ages, first time or seasoned, scary or not, how competitive) answered one screen at a time with Back and Start over, ending in a recommended room with a "Why this one" paragraph, an "Also a great fit" second choice and a Book button. Built as an Interactivity API block that scores answers against `room` meta; no email capture. (seen on: [The Quandary](https://quandaryescape.com/quiz))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Walk-ins page with a single state the manager flips ("Walk-ins available") and the door instruction ("Dial 1-0-0 on the call box for entry"). (seen on: [The Quandary](https://quandaryescape.com/walkins))
- Access notes on every room: which copies have wheelchair lift access, "flashing light elements", puzzles that rely on sound or colour, doors can stay open for claustrophobic players. (seen on: [clueQuest](https://www.cluequest.co.uk/faq))
- Arrival and cancellation terms in plain words: arrive 10 minutes early, over 15 minutes late shortens the game, no refunds but a voucher with 14 days' notice. (seen on: [clueQuest](https://www.cluequest.co.uk/faq))
- Seasonal edition that swaps itself in and out by date ("Spooky Edition, Sept 16 to Nov 9") using the room's edition dates. (seen on: [The Quandary](https://quandaryescape.com/))
- "Team photos sent next business day by email" line, with an optional gallery of opted-in team photos. (seen on: [clueQuest](https://www.cluequest.co.uk/faq))
**Style: Cinematic film-title poster (dark)**
- Type: Titles: Smooch Sans 700 (OFL), uppercase, up to 20vw on room pages, tracking +0.02em, line-height 0.9; billing block and body: Source Serif 4 400/19px, line-height 1.6; specs and clock figures: Share Tech Mono 400/16px.
- Palette: #0F0E0C bg (blackout) · #ECE6DA text (projector white) · #E0A33B tungsten amber (links, Book buttons) · #1D1B18 surface (spec rows, quiz panel) · #3B362F line · #2E8B57 exit-sign green (only for "Walk-ins available")
- Layout: every room page is a one-sheet: a letterboxed still at 2.39:1 across the full width, the title set huge below it, then a billing block that reads like poster credits (PLAYERS 2–7 · 60 MIN · DIFFICULTY 4/5 · AGE 14+ · WHEELCHAIR ACCESS: ONE COPY). The rooms archive is a stack of these one-sheets, not a card grid. Front page: this season's featured room, then the quiz entry, then the other rooms as titles only. 0 radius, 1px rules. Dark is justified by the trade (the rooms are dark sets).
- Imagery: real set photographs lit by the practicals in the room (desk lamps, emergency lights), film grain allowed, letterboxed 2.39:1; no stock padlocks, no fake smoke, no overlays above 40%.
- Motion: one orchestrated moment: on a room page the title card fades in over 600ms after the still, like a title sequence; quiz steps slide 24px with opacity; no scroll-reveal. All inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, otherwise everything is simply shown.
- Why it fits now: title design is having a moment as an online genre of its own, and it gives each room the weight of a film rather than a game-room listing: [Art of the Title](https://www.artofthetitle.com/)
**Style variations:** House Lights (#ECE6DA bg, #0F0E0C type) · Red Room (#1A0D0C bg, #D9B37A accent) · Lab Report (#E9EEEA bg, #1F5C4A accent)
**Refs:**
- [The Quandary: room quiz](https://quandaryescape.com/quiz): eight-question picker with Back / Start over, "Why this one" and "Also a great fit" results
- [clueQuest: Revenge of the Sheep](https://www.cluequest.co.uk/escape-room-missions/revenge-of-the-sheep): a full room page: story, players per unit, difficulty, age, access warnings, gallery and reviews
- [clueQuest: FAQ](https://www.cluequest.co.uk/faq): arrival, late, cancellation, wheelchair, claustrophobia and team-photo answers written as policy

#### 252 · Social Games Bar: darts, karaoke, shuffleboard (`oche`)
**For:** independent "competitive socialising" bars with a few darts lanes, two to four karaoke booths and shuffleboard tables, selling hourly lanes, group packages and a weekly league.
**Real-world basis:** [The All Out (Amsterdam): interactive darts](https://theallout.com/activities/interactive-darts), [The All Out: karaoke](https://theallout.com/activities/karaoke), [The All Out: Let The Games Begin package](https://theallout.com/packages/let-the-games-begin), [Two Social (Dayton): bar sports league](https://2socialdayton.com/events/bar-sports-league), [Two Social: FAQ](https://2socialdayton.com/faq), [Lucky Voice: song catalogue](https://luckyvoice.com/songs)
**Templates:** front-page · archive-activity (Activities) · single-activity (darts, karaoke, shuffleboard, table games) · page-packages · single-package · page-songs (songbook) · page-food-and-drinks · page-groups (birthday, hen and stag) · page-corporate (team events) · page-league · archive-event (agenda) · page-faq · page-maps-parking
**Patterns (~42):** activity sheet (duration "55 min", players per lane "up to 8", "from €27.50 per lane", Book now), darts game-modes list (501, Killer, Shanghai, Halve It), karaoke booth list by name and theme with capacity and 50/110-minute prices, "order from your booth" menu note, package table (activities included, minutes each, per-person price, "custom quote over 10 people"), weekly programme (Friday karaoke from 10pm, Wednesday league 7pm), league sign-up (team fee vs free-agent fee, six-week season, weekly game lineup, week-6 tournament), opening hours table ("Monday closed"), house rules (21+ or 18+ at all times, closed-toe shoes, digital waiver), cancellation terms, walk-ins vs bookings note ("online bookings always get priority"), food and drink menu, song request form, maps and parking
**Content model:** companion `activity` CPT (duration, players_per_lane, price_from, booking_url, modes), `song` CPT (title, artist, duration, language) imported from the karaoke supplier's CSV, `league` season as a WooCommerce product with team / free-agent variations and a `week` repeater (game per week), companion `event` for weekly nights.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce (league fees, gift vouchers), Simply Schedule Appointments or the venue's hosted booking embed (both real sites book lanes through an external platform), Jetpack Forms (party enquiries, song requests), Advanced Query Loop (this week's agenda).
**Signature:** a **searchable songbook**: every song in the venue's catalogue listed as title / artist / duration, with instant search and an Artists filter (Interactivity API over the `song` CPT, server-rendered first so it works without JS), a "Top songs" list, and a "Not finding your song? Submit a song request" form at the bottom. (seen on: [Lucky Voice](https://luckyvoice.com/songs))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- League page that sells both team entries and free-agent places with "guaranteed placement", a six-week game lineup and a week-6 tournament where the top two pick the games. (seen on: [Two Social](https://2socialdayton.com/events/bar-sports-league))
- Cancellation terms as two lines: 24 hours' notice gets a credit, a week's notice gets a refund. (seen on: [Two Social](https://2socialdayton.com/faq))
- House rules block (21+ at all times, closed-toe shoes, waiver done online at booking) shown on the booking page as well as the FAQ. (seen on: [Two Social](https://2socialdayton.com/faq))
- "Bring your own food" note that names the neighbours worth ordering from. (seen on: [Two Social](https://2socialdayton.com/faq))
- Game-modes list on each lane page so groups know what they're booking (501, Killer, Shanghai, Halve It; automatic scoring). (seen on: [The All Out](https://theallout.com/activities/interactive-darts))
**Style: Kinetic variable-type maximalism**
- Type: Display: Science Gothic (OFL, variable width 50–200, weight 100–900) at 900 weight, width set per line so lane and game names fill the measure, 96–240px, line-height 0.88; body: Figtree 400/18px, line-height 1.55; scores, prices and times: Doto 700 (OFL dot-matrix) at 20–48px like a scoreboard.
- Palette: #FAFAF6 bg (chalk white) · #111111 text and rules · #0B7A3E board green (primary action, "Book") · #D2232A board red (sold-out and rule warnings only) · #C9A26B cork surface (league table, package table) · #111111 2px line
- Layout: big and loud but on a strict 12-column grid: each activity is a full-width band with the name stretched edge to edge, then a dense two-column spec (price, minutes, players, modes) and one photo at 4:5 offset to the right. Front page: tonight's programme as a scoreboard strip in Doto, then the activities as stacked bands, then packages as a real table, then hours and address. Square corners everywhere, 2px black rules, no cards.
- Imagery: flash photography from inside the venue at night, hard shadows, people mid-throw and mid-chorus, cropped tight at 4:5 and 1:1; no stock "friends laughing" shots.
- Motion: on hover or focus, an activity name eases from wdth 100 to wdth 120 over 200ms; the front-page headline tightens its width axis with a scroll-driven animation once, then stops; songbook results update without animation. All inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference; reduced motion keeps widths static.
- Why it fits now: variable width axes let independent brands be loud with type alone instead of effects, and foundries like this one are the reference point for playful maximal type: [OH no Type Co](https://ohnotype.co/)
**Style variations:** Chalkboard (#1F2A24 bg, #F4F1E8 chalk type) · Treble Ring (#FAFAF6 bg, #D2232A headings) · Booth Night (#16110F bg, #E7B53C scores)
**Refs:**
- [Lucky Voice: song catalogue](https://luckyvoice.com/songs): searchable title/artist/duration table with an Artists filter, Top songs and a song request form
- [The All Out: interactive darts](https://theallout.com/activities/interactive-darts): a lane page done properly: price per lane, 55 minutes, players, game modes, automatic scoring
- [Two Social: bar sports league](https://2socialdayton.com/events/bar-sports-league): six-week league with team and free-agent entry, weekly game lineup and final tournament

#### 253 · Camera & Film Gear Rental House (`rental`)
**For:** small rental houses (one counter, one tech, a few hundred serialised items) serving indie film crews, students and photographers.
**Real-world basis:** [Hireacamera: How it works](https://www.hireacamera.com/how-it-works/), [Hireacamera: Sony FX6 product page](https://www.hireacamera.com/products/HAC00-06989-sony-fx6/), [CineMechanics: How to rent](https://cinemechanics.com/how-to-rent), [CineMechanics: Rental FAQ](https://cinemechanics.com/rental-faq), [Boston Photo Rental: Lens rental](https://www.bostonphotorental.com/boston-lens-rental/)
**Templates:** front-page · Woo shop (by category: cameras / lenses / lighting / audio / grip / monitoring) · single-product (kit) · taxonomy-mount · page-how-to-rent · page-forms-and-insurance · page-rental-faq · page-request-a-quote · page-studio · page-contact
**Patterns (~50):** category index by mount (Canon RF / Sony E / Nikon Z / PL), kit card ("From £130 per day", Hire Now or "not currently available" + waitlist), "Check live availability" date bar (start / end), kit contents table ("25+ items": body cap, batteries, charger, cards, flight case), compatible accessories rail ("you'll also need"), six-step "How it works" (account → order → send ID → verification call → delivery or click & collect → return), deposit explainer, damage waiver explainer with value threshold, insurance / certificate-of-insurance requirements with sample COI download, pick-up and return times ("pick up 3pm the day before, return by 10am the day after"), 3-day-week billing note, new rental account application form, click & collect stockists list.
**Content model:** Woo attributes (mount, format, sensor, power, replacement value band); `kit_contents` repeater meta bound to a table; rental pricing and stock units from Booking and Rental Manager for WooCommerce; `stockist` CPT for collection points.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce, Booking and Rental Manager for WooCommerce (free tier: day/week pricing, per-unit inventory, extra-service lines for deposit and waiver), Product Filters, Jetpack Forms (account application and ID upload).
**Signature:** **live availability on every kit page with deposit and damage waiver shown before checkout.** The visitor picks hire dates once in a "Check live availability" bar. Each kit shows whether a unit is free and the day rate × days. The cart then adds a refundable deposit based on kit value, plus an optional accidental damage waiver that is only offered below a value threshold, with "bring your own insurance" above it. (seen on: [Hireacamera: Sony FX6](https://www.hireacamera.com/products/HAC00-06989-sony-fx6/) and [Hireacamera: insurance FAQ](https://www.hireacamera.com/faqs-insurance/))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- "Not currently available: join the waitlist" state on sold-out kit that emails when a unit comes back (seen on: [Hireacamera: cinema cameras](https://www.hireacamera.com/cameras/video/digital-cinema/full-range/))
- Printable check-out sheet generated from the kit contents table, so the counter and the customer tick the same list at pick-up and return (seen on: [Hireacamera: Sony FX6 kit table](https://www.hireacamera.com/products/HAC00-06989-sony-fx6/))
- Downloadable sample certificate of insurance and the rental T&Cs as PDFs on a "Forms & insurance" page (seen on: [CineMechanics: How to rent](https://cinemechanics.com/how-to-rent))
- Deposit timeline in plain words: "taken 7 days before dispatch, released on inspection, 1–5 working days back to your card" (seen on: [Hireacamera: deposit FAQ](https://www.hireacamera.com/faqs-deposit/))
- Schema.org Product + Offer markup per kit, and a used-kit-for-sale list for ex-rental stock (seen on: [CineMechanics](https://cinemechanics.com/), linked "Used Equipment Sale")
**Style: Swiss neo-grotesk index (rental catalogue)**
- Type: headings Zalando Sans 800 at 72–120px, tracking set per size (−0.01em at display, 0 below 32px); body Zalando Sans 400/18px; item codes, mounts and day rates in IBM Plex Mono 500 (the "HAC00-06989" style SKU is shown, not hidden).
- Palette: paper #F6F6F4 (bg), ink #111214 (text), gaffer-tape orange #E8591A (accent, only for "Hire" actions and availability gaps), steel #D9DBDD (lines/surfaces), cool grey #5B6066 (secondary text, 7:1 on paper), available green #1E7A45 (used only with a text label "Available").
- Layout: 12-column index with hairline rules instead of cards; the shop is a dense table-like list (image thumb · name · mount · day rate · status) that switches to a 4-up grid; kit page is 5/7 split with the contents table running full width below; sticky date bar under the header; 0px radius on everything except inputs (2px).
- Imagery: studio product shots on a plain grey paper backdrop at 1:1, kit laid out flat top-down in the open flight case at 3:2; no lifestyle shots on the shop grid.
- Motion: none by default; the date bar uses a View Transition when dates change so availability states swap without a reload; all motion inside `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`.
- Why it fits now: crews read rental sites like spec sheets, and the sober Swiss catalogue look (modular list, one accent, mono codes) is what the best product-system brands use today, e.g. [Vitsoe: 606 Universal Shelving System](https://www.vitsoe.com/gb/606).
**Style variations:** Flight Case (black #151515 bg, orange rates) · Slate (white, clapperboard black-white stripe rules) · Studio Grey (#E4E4E1 bg, Plex Mono headings)
**Refs:**
- [Hireacamera: Sony FX6 product page](https://www.hireacamera.com/products/HAC00-06989-sony-fx6/): the model kit page: live availability search, full "what's in the case" table and accessory upsells in one place.
- [Hireacamera: insurance FAQ](https://www.hireacamera.com/faqs-insurance/): honest waiver rules with a value threshold; copy this structure for the deposit and waiver explainer pattern.
- [CineMechanics: How to rent](https://cinemechanics.com/how-to-rent): day-before pick-up, 3-day-week billing and COI requirements set out as a short procedure.

#### 254 · Tool Hire (`hire`)
**For:** independent local tool and plant hire yards (one to a few depots) serving trades and DIYers, plus membership tool libraries.
**Real-world basis:** [Local Tool Hire: General information](https://www.localtoolhire.co.uk/general-information), [Local Tool Hire: Breaking & drilling](https://www.localtoolhire.co.uk/home/Breaking-&-Drilling-c132507539), [South West Hire and Sales: Delivery & collection](https://www.southwesthireandsales.co.uk/delivery-collection-service/), [South West Hire and Sales: Drilling, breaking & fixing](https://www.southwesthireandsales.co.uk/product-category/drilling-breaking-fixing/), [Library of Things: Terms of borrowing](https://www.libraryofthings.co.uk/terms-of-borrowing)
**Templates:** front-page · Woo shop · taxonomy-product_cat (Access & Support / Breaking & Drilling / Concreting & Compaction / Gardening & Landscaping / Heating / Plumbing & Pumping …) · single-product · page-general-information · page-delivery-collection · page-open-an-account · page-branches · page-downloads · page-terms-of-hire · page-power-tool-repairs
**Patterns (~45):** 16–22 category tiles in the trade's own names (Breaking & Drilling, Lift & Shift, Sanding & Surface Preparation), subcategory list with item counts ("Combi Hammer Drills (3)"), product card with hire periods (Day / 2 Days / Week, "prices subject to VAT"), "illustration only, make and model may vary" note, damage waiver options table (10% damage waiver / 15% loss & damage waiver), deposit rule for non-account customers, hire period definitions ("day hire covers 24 hours…"), branch list with phone per depot, delivery & collection rules (two-hour window, someone must sign), open-a-credit-account form, downloads (credit application, T&Cs, safety sheets), SafeHire certified badge, power tool repairs & PAT testing service.
**Content model:** Woo attributes (power: 110V / 240V / petrol / battery, weight, PPE required); `branch` CPT (address, phone, hours, email); rental pricing periods and stock per branch from Booking and Rental Manager for WooCommerce.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce, Booking and Rental Manager for WooCommerce (free tier; waiver options as extra services), Jetpack Forms (credit account and reservation requests), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (branches).
**Signature:** **a two-tier waiver choice on every hire.** Each reservation offers a basic damage waiver at 10% of the hire charge or a loss & damage waiver at 15% (covering theft and malicious damage), or neither with a deposit based on equipment value for non-account customers. The choice is shown per item in the cart with the hire periods defined underneath. (seen on: [Local Tool Hire: General information](https://www.localtoolhire.co.uk/general-information))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Hire-period glossary under every price ("Day hire covers 24 hours, usable over two days; a week covers any 7 days including weekends") (seen on: [Local Tool Hire: General information](https://www.localtoolhire.co.uk/general-information))
- Per-branch contact cards with the depot's own email and phone, so trades call the nearest yard (seen on: [South West Hire and Sales](https://www.southwesthireandsales.co.uk/))
- Downloads page with the credit account application, terms of hire and safety data as PDFs (seen on: [South West Hire and Sales: Downloads](https://www.southwesthireandsales.co.uk/downloads/))
- Late-return and cleaning rules in one line each ("late fee of 1.5× the daily cost per day"; cleaning fee if returned dirty) (seen on: [Library of Things: Terms of borrowing](https://www.libraryofthings.co.uk/terms-of-borrowing))
- Saturday-morning hours notice ("8am to 1pm every Saturday") driven by the branch hours meta with an "open now" label (seen on: [Local Tool Hire: General information](https://www.localtoolhire.co.uk/general-information))
**Style: Hi-vis trade catalogue**
- Type: headings Sofia Sans Extra Condensed 900 at 80–140px, uppercase for category names only; body Archivo 400/18px; prices and SKUs in Martian Mono 500.
- Palette: hi-vis yellow #FFD400 (header band and price flags), black #141414 (text and rules), white #FFFFFF (bg), concrete #E6E4DF (surfaces), safety red #C8102E (used only for "PPE required" and late-fee notes).
- Layout: catalogue grid with thick 3px black rules between rows; category index is a tall two-column list with item counts at the right edge; product page puts the three hire-period prices in a boxed price table at the top; phone number and branch selector in a fixed top bar; 0px radius, buttons are hard rectangles.
- Imagery: cut-out tool photos on white at consistent scale (a breaker next to a drill shows real size), one photo of the yard per branch; no stock builders in hard hats.
- Motion: none beyond a colour swap on hover for clickable rows; all transitions inside `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`.
- Why it fits now: tradespeople shop by category and price, and the yellow-and-black power-tool catalogue language is the most recognised visual code on site today, e.g. [DeWalt UK](https://www.dewalt.co.uk/).
**Style variations:** Site Yard (concrete #E6E4DF bg, black rules) · Night Shift (black bg, yellow type) · Tool Library (white, forest #1F5130 accent, friendlier copy)
**Refs:**
- [Local Tool Hire: General information](https://www.localtoolhire.co.uk/general-information): hire periods, deposits and the 10% / 15% waiver options stated in plain words on one page.
- [South West Hire and Sales: Delivery & collection](https://www.southwesthireandsales.co.uk/delivery-collection-service/): WordPress/Woo hire site with branch-based delivery rules and a clear two-hour window.
- [Library of Things: Terms of borrowing](https://www.libraryofthings.co.uk/terms-of-borrowing): friendly but firm damage, late-fee and cleaning clauses for community-scale lending.

#### 255 · Party & Event Hire: marquees, furniture (`marquee`)
**For:** family-run marquee, tipi and event-furniture hire firms doing weddings, parties, schools and corporate events in one region.
**Real-world basis:** [WA Carr & Son: Tableware hire](https://wacarrandson.co.uk/product-category/tableware-hire/), [WA Carr & Son: FAQs](https://wacarrandson.co.uk/contact-us/faqs/), [PapaKåta: Tipi tents](https://www.papakata.co.uk/our-tents/tipi-tents/), [The Marquee and Furniture Company: Weddings](https://www.marqueeandfurniturecompany.co.uk/weddings), [Pinnacle Marquees: Marquees](https://www.pinnaclemarquees.co.uk/Marquees)
**Templates:** front-page · archive-structure (marquees / tipis / stretch tents) · single-structure · Woo shop (furniture, linen, tableware, dancefloors, bar) · single-product · page-quote-request · page-faqs · page-delivery · page-coverage-area · page-gallery (real weddings / parties & corporate) · page-health-safety-legal
**Patterns (~45):** event-type entry points (weddings / parties / corporate / schools / film & TV), structure sizes list ("clear span widths 3, 6, 9, 12, 15m, lengths in 3m multiples"), capacity table (1 tipi: up to 70 dining / 100 party … 4+ tipis: 170+), "prices from £2,500 incl. flooring and lighting" line, furnishings grouped by job (take a seat / raise a glass / added sparkle / technical), "build your quote" six-step strip (add items → event details → submit → official quote → confirm → delivery), quote form (name, phone, event location, type, date, message), damage hold explainer (pre-authorised card hold), cleaning charge note for crockery and glassware, delivery rules (ground floor, Mon–Fri 8am–8pm), cancellation terms, coverage-area map, real-event gallery by venue, trade memberships (MUTA / NOEA).
**Content model:** `structure` (type, width × length, dining and standing capacity, from-price); `venue` for gallery grouping; Woo products for loose items with a "quote only" flag (price hidden, "Add to quote").
**Plugins:** WooCommerce, Booking and Rental Manager for WooCommerce (only where a firm hires small kit at fixed prices, e.g. bell tents or fire pits), Jetpack Forms (quote request), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (coverage area).
**Signature:** **a "build your quote" basket instead of a checkout.** Customers add chairs, linen, tableware and dancefloor to a quote list, enter event details, and submit. Nothing is paid online. The firm replies with an official quote, and a pre-authorised card hold covers damage. The theme builds this as a companion "quote list" block that pre-fills a Jetpack Form with the items and quantities. (seen on: [WA Carr & Son: Tableware hire](https://wacarrandson.co.uk/product-category/tableware-hire/))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Downloadable floor-plan kit with scale cut-outs of tables and dancefloors so couples can plan the layout at home (seen on: [PapaKåta: Tipi tents](https://www.papakata.co.uk/our-tents/tipi-tents/), "Papa Kutouts")
- Capacity table by number of structures, visible before the quote form (seen on: [PapaKåta: Tipi tents](https://www.papakata.co.uk/our-tents/tipi-tents/))
- "Do I need to wash the plates?" answer with a cleaning-service option and the charge, set as a visible FAQ (seen on: [WA Carr & Son: FAQs](https://wacarrandson.co.uk/contact-us/faqs/))
- Coverage-area page listing the counties served, plus a separate festivals/large-events line (seen on: [WA Carr & Son: Marquee hire coverage](https://wacarrandson.co.uk/marquee-hire-coverage/))
- Health, safety & legal page (method statements, insurance, trade association links) for venues and schools that ask for paperwork (seen on: [WA Carr & Son: Health, safety & legal](https://wacarrandson.co.uk/health-safety-legal/))
**Style: Editorial serif revival (wedding-magazine layout)**
- Type: headings Rosaline 400 (Fontshare display script, headings only) at 88–128px, set tight at 1.0 line-height; body Newsreader 400/19px with real italics for captions; quantities and sizes in Newsreader tabular figures.
- Palette: canvas white #F4F3EE (bg, justified by marquee canvas), ink #1B1D1A (text), hedge green #2F4A36 (accent: links, "Add to quote"), rope #BFB8A6 (lines), deep shade #4A4F47 (secondary text).
- Layout: magazine spreads: a full-bleed venue photo, then a two-column text + caption layout with hanging captions in the margin; structures shown as a size table rather than cards; the furniture shop is a 3-column catalogue with quantities, no prices unless set; footer is address, phone and coverage area on one row.
- Imagery: real events shot at dusk from outside the structure, 16:9 and 4:5 alternating; furniture on a plain grass or floor ground, 1:1; no drone clichés.
- Motion: a single View Transition from a gallery thumbnail to the venue page; nothing on scroll; `prefers-reduced-motion` honoured.
- Why it fits now: couples plan weddings from slow editorial magazines, and the quiet serif spread (big photo, captions, generous margins) is how the best independent titles look today, e.g. [Kinfolk](https://www.kinfolk.com/).
**Style variations:** Village Fete (white, bunting-red #B2302B rules) · Candlelit (ink #1B1D1A bg, canvas type) · Hedgerow (sage #DDE3D6 bg, green headings)
**Refs:**
- [WA Carr & Son: Tableware hire](https://wacarrandson.co.uk/product-category/tableware-hire/): WooCommerce used as a quote basket with the six booking steps stated up front.
- [PapaKåta: Tipi tents](https://www.papakata.co.uk/our-tents/tipi-tents/): capacity table, a "from" price and a downloadable planning kit on one page.
- [WA Carr & Son: FAQs](https://wacarrandson.co.uk/contact-us/faqs/): damage card hold, cleaning charges, delivery and cancellation terms written as clear answers.

#### 256 · Photo-Booth Rental (`photobooth`)
**For:** one- to three-booth operators (vintage chemical or digital) hiring to weddings, parties and brand events within a set travel radius.
**Real-world basis:** [MN Booth: Templates](https://mnbooth.com/templates), [MN Booth: FAQ](https://mnbooth.com/faq), [Time Into Pixels: Reserve](https://tipbooth.com/reserve/), [Classic Photo Booth: Photo booth comparison](https://www.classicphotobooth.net/photo-booth-comparison/), [Photomatica: Photo booth rental](https://www.photomatica.com/photo-booth-rental)
**Templates:** front-page · archive-booth (vintage / open-air / glam / 360 / audio guest book) · single-booth · page-packages · page-templates · page-backdrops · page-gallery (by booth type) · page-faq · page-reviews · page-check-your-date
**Patterns (~35):** booth type pages with sample galleries per type, package list with hours and what's included (unlimited strips, on-site attendant, digital copies), "Check your date" form with package pre-selected from the link, print template gallery by event type and format (2×6 strip / 4×6 print), backdrop swatches, props, vintage vs digital comparison table (process, strips per hour, finish, copies, colour), space & power requirements ("10ft × 10ft, 9ft ceiling, outlet within 10–15ft"), setup time note, travel area ("free within 25 miles"), non-refundable deposit to hold the date, private online gallery link, audio guest book add-on.
**Content model:** `booth` (type, footprint, ceiling height, power, print format, strips per hour); `print_template` (number, event type, format, image); `package` (hours, inclusions, price from).
**Plugins:** WooCommerce (date-holding deposit as a simple product), Booking and Rental Manager for WooCommerce (one unit per booth, day-wise, blocks double-booking), Jetpack Forms (check your date, logo upload).
**Signature:** **a numbered print-template library the customer books from.** Templates are filed by event type and format (2×6 or 4×6). The couple quotes "template 37" in the booking form, or uploads a logo and colours, and the operator's designer returns a mock-up for approval before the event. (seen on: [MN Booth: Templates](https://mnbooth.com/templates) and [Time Into Pixels: Reserve](https://tipbooth.com/reserve/))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Package links that pre-fill the enquiry ("/contact?package=gold"), so the form already knows what they picked (seen on: [MN Booth](https://mnbooth.com/))
- Space-and-power checklist for the venue coordinator as a printable card (seen on: [MN Booth: FAQ](https://mnbooth.com/faq))
- Deposit and cancellation in two sentences: "$100 non-refundable deposit secures your date; cancel any time, no further fee" (seen on: [MN Booth: FAQ](https://mnbooth.com/faq))
- Vintage vs digital comparison table (strips per hour, finish, copies, colour choice) (seen on: [Classic Photo Booth: comparison](https://www.classicphotobooth.net/photo-booth-comparison/))
- Service-area notice ("rentals in California only") set site-wide from one setting (seen on: [Photomatica: Photo booth rental](https://www.photomatica.com/photo-booth-rental))
**Style: Riso zine / photo-strip**
- Type: headings Bowlby One 400 at 96–160px, set in stacked lines like a strip; body Work Sans 400/18px; template numbers and sizes in Azeret Mono 500.
- Palette: paper white #FFFFFF (bg), riso black #1A1A1A (text), fluorescent pink #FF48B0 (accent: "Check your date"), riso blue #0078BF (links and rules), yellow #FFE800 (template numbers only), newsprint grey #EDEBE6 (surfaces).
- Layout: the page is cut into four-frame vertical strips on desktop (4 narrow columns) that collapse to one strip on mobile; the template library is a tight grid of real strips at true 2×6 proportions with the template number printed under each; packages as a plain rate list, no tiers highlighted.
- Imagery: scans of real printed strips (paper edge visible), overprint two-colour duotones (pink + blue) for hero photos, backdrops shown as flat swatches.
- Motion: one moment: a white flash on the hero when the page first loads (150ms), skipped under `prefers-reduced-motion`; nothing on scroll.
- Why it fits now: riso printing is the living print culture of the photo-booth crowd, and two-colour overprint looks honest next to real strips, e.g. [RISOTTO Studio](https://www.risottostudio.com/).
**Style variations:** Chemical (black-and-white only, matte grey #D8D6D0 bg) · Glam (black #121212 bg, silver type) · Summer Fete (yellow #FFE800 bg, blue type)
**Refs:**
- [MN Booth: Templates](https://mnbooth.com/templates): numbered template library by event type and print format; the core of this theme.
- [MN Booth: FAQ](https://mnbooth.com/faq): deposit, space, power, travel and gallery answers every booth site needs.
- [Classic Photo Booth: Photo booth comparison](https://www.classicphotobooth.net/photo-booth-comparison/): a clear side-by-side of vintage and digital booths that helps customers choose.

<a id="257"></a>
#### 257 · Kids' Party Entertainer (`party`)
**For:** solo children's entertainers (magic, games, balloon modelling, kids' discos, toddler play sessions) who also do schools, libraries and holiday shows within a 30–50 mile patch.
**Real-world basis:** [The Children's Magician: About](https://www.thechildrensmagician.com/about-us-magician-for-hire-near-me/), [The Children's Magician: Parties](https://www.thechildrensmagician.com/childrens-magician-and-entertainer-for-magic-parties-games-and-balloons/), [Magic Fred: Birthday party packages](https://magicfredshow.com/birthday-parties), [Magic Fred: Availability](https://magicfredshow.com/availability), [Magic Mike: Kids Disco](https://www.magicmikeparties.co.uk/kids-disco/)
**Templates:** front-page · page-parties (package overview) · single-package (Magic Party / Wizard Party / Kids Disco / Toddlers Package / Balloon Twisting) · page-schools-and-libraries · page-holiday-shows · page-availability · page-reviews · page-gallery · page-faq · page-areas (town list) · single-area · page-contact
**Patterns (~34):** package block with running length and price ("Package 1: 1 hour, magic show and balloons for every child" / "Package 2: 2 hours, games, show and balloons"), themed-party row (Wizard, Circus, Dinosaur, Superhero, Halloween, Christmas), disco tier table (Silver 1 hr / Gold 1.5 hr / Platinum 2 hr), add-ons price list (bubble machine, glow sticks, glitter tattoos, extra time, magic wand goodie bags), "birthday child is the star" section, credentials line (Enhanced DBS, public liability insurance with Equity, local magic society membership), "all I need from you" space card (cleared area, size, setup and pack-down times), school assembly and library show offer, areas covered town list, parent reviews in the parents' own words, enquiry form (town, date, type of event, approximate number of children), poster and flyer request for libraries and schools.
**Content model:** `package` (duration, price, age guidance, included items, add-ons allowed), `booking` (date, start time, town, public or private; private entries publish only as a greyed date), `area` (town, travel note), taxonomy `party_theme`.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (enquiry and hold requests), Advanced Query Loop (upcoming public library and holiday shows).
**Signature:** an availability calendar with two views (month grid and list). Dates with a booking are greyed with the note "Event listed: I may still have availability depending on timing and travel", and each booking reserves a 3-hour block for setup, show, pack-down and buffer, so a parent can see a 4pm party blocks 3–6pm before they enquire. Built as a companion Interactivity-API block reading `booking` dates; clicking a free date opens the enquiry form with the date filled in. (seen on: [Magic Fred: Availability](https://magicfredshow.com/availability))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Operational: a 48-hour date hold ("I can hold a date for 48 hours, longer if you need") as a checkbox on the enquiry form, plus a "Weekends book up fast" flag the owner switches on per month. (seen on: [Magic Fred: FAQ](https://magicfredshow.com/faq), [Magic Mike: Kids Disco](https://www.magicmikeparties.co.uk/kids-disco/))
- Trust & proof: a credentials line under every package with Enhanced DBS, Equity public liability insurance and local magic circle membership, each with its reference number field. (seen on: [The Children's Magician: About](https://www.thechildrensmagician.com/about-us-magician-for-hire-near-me/))
- Local & practical: a printable "what I need from you" card: a cleared space about 10 ft wide by 7 ft deep, arrival 60 minutes before, 30 minutes to pack away. (seen on: [Magic Fred: Birthday party packages](https://magicfredshow.com/birthday-parties))
- Accessibility & inclusion: a note on non-elimination games so no child goes out upset, and shows adapted for children and adults with additional needs, with a field on the form to tell the entertainer what helps. (seen on: [The Children's Magician: Parties](https://www.thechildrensmagician.com/childrens-magician-and-entertainer-for-magic-parties-games-and-balloons/))
- Owner content: a poster and flyer page where libraries, schools and hosts pick one of three designs, send their event details and file format (JPG, PNG or print PDF), and get a ready-to-print poster back. (seen on: [Magic Fred: Poster/flyers](https://magicfredshow.com/poster/flyers))
**Style: Soft neo-brutalism (hard shadows, pastel fills)**
- Type: display Grandstander 900 at 84–96px, tracking 0, line-height 1.0; body Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 400/18px, line-height 1.6 (parents read this on a phone at the school gate); prices and times in Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono 500/16px.
- Palette: bg #FFF4D6 (butter paper), ink #141414, fill #FFC6D3 (party pink, used only for package blocks), state-free #BFE8CB (mint, free date), state-booked #D9D4CC (grey, booked date), action #E0431B (tomato, buttons and links).
- Layout: 12-column grid, 3px ink borders and a hard 6px 6px 0 #141414 shadow on package blocks and buttons only; buttons radius 10px, package blocks radius 0, inputs radius 4px. Home page opens with a big photo of a real party mid-trick on the left and the next free Saturday on the right, then packages as a stacked list where Package 2 spans wider, then the availability calendar, then credentials and areas. Top nav with a persistent "Check a date" button.
- Imagery: real party photos from the child's eye level, cropped 4:5, square corners with a 3px ink border; balloon models shot on plain paper as cut-outs for package headers.
- Motion: buttons press into their shadow on :active (translate 3px, 80ms); calendar month change uses a View Transition slide of 120ms; everything static under prefers-reduced-motion. No bounce, no confetti.
- Why it fits now: neo-brutalist hard-shadow blocks moved from indie tools into friendly consumer brands and read as playful without looking like a children's TV template. [Gumroad](https://gumroad.com/)
**Style variations:** Sherbet (mint #BFE8CB fields, tomato buttons) · Blackboard (chalk #2B3A2F ground, butter type) · Big Top (red #C8102E stripes, cream ground)
**Refs:**
- [Magic Fred: Availability](https://magicfredshow.com/availability): calendar and list views, greyed booked dates with the "may still have availability" note, 3-hour reservation rule.
- [Magic Fred: Birthday party packages](https://magicfredshow.com/birthday-parties): three priced packages, extra-child pricing, space size and setup times in plain words.
- [Magic Mike: Kids Disco](https://www.magicmikeparties.co.uk/kids-disco/): tier table by duration and a priced add-ons list parents can build from.
