#### 258 · Magician (`trick`)
**For:** working close-up and cabaret magicians (and mentalists or pickpockets) who do weddings, corporate events and private parties.
**Real-world basis:** [Close-Up Chris: Wedding Magician](https://www.closeupchris.co.uk/wedding-magician/), [Close-Up Chris: Booking Process](https://www.closeupchris.co.uk/booking-process/), [Close-Up Chris: Magicians for Hire](https://www.closeupchris.co.uk/magicians-for-hire/), [Jeff Black Magic: Weddings](https://jeffblackmagic.com/weddings), [Richard Pinner: Performer](https://richardpinner.com/performer)
**Templates:** front-page · page-weddings · page-corporate · page-private-parties · single-format (Mix & Mingle, The Room of Mystery, The Close-Up Corner, stage show) · page-magicians-for-hire (team) · page-booking-process · page-reviews · page-media · page-faq · page-contact ("Check your date") · page-area (city pages) · page-terms
**Patterns (~32):** wedding day in three moments (drinks reception / wedding breakfast between courses / evening reception), package ladder with "from" prices (The Party Starter, The Cosmopolitan, The Showman), formats list (strolling close-up, cabaret, stage show 15–45 min, hosting and auctioneering), Room of Mystery running order (spare room, groups of 4–8, 10–15 minutes each, sworn to secrecy), booth spec card (width, height, depth, lighting, reaction camera), four-step booking process, "Check your date" form, insurance line, reviews with source and date, media page (photos, videos, socials), FAQ, city coverage list.
**Content model:** `format` (duration, group size, space needed, from-price), `moment` taxonomy (drinks, meal, evening, stage), `review` (source, date, event type), `area` (city, region).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (check-your-date enquiry).
**Signature:** a "Plan the magic" picker on the weddings and corporate pages: the visitor ticks the moments they want covered (drinks reception, between courses, evening) and enters a guest count; the block recommends the matching package and, above 80–100 guests per performer, how many magicians to book, then carries that into the "Check your date" form. Interactivity API over `format` and `moment` terms, no backend. (seen on: [Close-Up Chris: Wedding Magician](https://www.closeupchris.co.uk/wedding-magician/) for the three moments and three packages, and [Close-Up Chris: Magicians for Hire](https://www.closeupchris.co.uk/magicians-for-hire/) for the one-per-80–100-guests rule)
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Buying confidence: a four-step booking page (choose package, complete form, pay deposit, final payment before the event) with accepted payment methods. (seen on: [Close-Up Chris: Booking Process](https://www.closeupchris.co.uk/booking-process/))
- Local & practical: a footprint card for anything that takes floor space, e.g. a booth at 3 m wide, 2.3 m tall, 2.5 m deep with its own lighting. (seen on: [Close-Up Chris: The Close-Up Corner](https://www.closeupchris.co.uk/the-closeup-corner/))
- Operational: a lead-time line the owner edits ("Weekend dates usually book 4–8 weeks ahead") near every enquiry button. (seen on: [Close-Up Chris: Party Magician](https://www.closeupchris.co.uk/party-magician/))
- Trust & proof: the public liability figure stated beside prices ("All fees include £5m public liability insurance") and the magic society membership in the footer. (seen on: [Close-Up Chris: Party Magician](https://www.closeupchris.co.uk/party-magician/), [Richard Pinner: Performer](https://richardpinner.com/performer))
- Owner content: a media page split into photos, videos and socials that planners can pull from. (seen on: [Jeff Black Magic: Media](https://jeffblackmagic.com/media))
**Style: Victorian playbill wood-type revival**
- Type: display Ultra 400 (fat-face wood type) at 96–128px, line-height 0.95, tracking +0.01em; secondary display lines in Rye 400 at 40px, used once per page; body Old Standard TT 400/19px, line-height 1.6; small caps via Old Standard TT for running heads.
- Palette: bg #EFE6CF (poster newsprint, a physical reason for the warm paper), ink #1B1512, red #A8231B (letterpress red, headings and links), gold #B8902F (rules and ornaments only), velvet #2A1E1C (footer band).
- Layout: the home page is set like a bill: a centred stack of lines at different sizes (justified here because a playbill is centred), then the site drops into a strict 12-column grid for moments, formats and reviews. Double rules (2px + 1px) between sections, square corners everywhere except form inputs (2px). Nav is a single line of small caps across the top with "Check your date" set in red.
- Imagery: black-and-white performance photos with heavy grain, cropped tight on hands and faces at 3:2; one full-bleed photo per page; ornaments are printers' fleurons drawn as SVG, never clip art.
- Motion: none on scroll. Links get a 2px red underline that draws left to right in 150ms; the picker's recommendation swaps with a View Transition crossfade; both off under prefers-reduced-motion.
- Why it fits now: wood-type and letterpress revival is back in event and cultural branding as a reaction to flat sans sites, and a playbill is what magic actually looked like. [Hamilton Wood Type & Printing Museum](https://woodtype.org/)
**Style variations:** Velvet (dark #2A1E1C ground, gold rules) · Handbill (white #FAFAF7 paper, black only) · Mentalist (slate #2F3B3A ground, bone type)
**Refs:**
- [Close-Up Chris: Wedding Magician](https://www.closeupchris.co.uk/wedding-magician/): the wedding day told as three moments, each mapped to a named package with a "from" price.
- [Close-Up Chris: The Room of Mystery](https://www.closeupchris.co.uk/room-of-mystery/): a format page that explains the running order step by step and sells the secrecy.
- [Richard Pinner: Performer](https://richardpinner.com/performer): formats (cabaret, hosting, mix-and-mingle) on one page with a repeated "Check Your Date" action.

#### 259 · Wedding DJ / Function Band (`firstdance`)
**For:** owner-run wedding DJs and small function bands (4–8 piece) booked directly by couples.
**Real-world basis:** [The Other Wedding DJ: home](https://theotherweddingdj.com/), [Brighton Wedding DJ: Pricing](https://brightonweddingdj.co.uk/pricing/), [Brighton Wedding DJ: FAQs](https://brightonweddingdj.co.uk/faqs/), [Manchester Wedding DJ: Pricing](https://manchesterweddingdj.co.uk/pricing/), [The Function Band: Live Wedding Music](https://www.thefunction.band/live-wedding-music/)
**Templates:** front-page · page-pricing · single-package · page-kit · page-music-planner · page-weddings (the day, from ceremony to last song) · page-reviews · page-faq · page-booking-form · page-terms · page-contact · archive-song (bands only, setlist)
**Patterns (~36):** philosophy intro in the DJ's own voice ("I won't play the Electric Slide"), package table with hours and what's in each (DJ only / DJ with PA and lighting / The Works with mic for speeches), evening vs all-day package split, extras list (uplighting, LED dance floor, MC, background music for the meal), kit list with a photo of the real setup, day running order (ceremony, drinks, dinner sets, two hours of party sets, DJ to close), deposit and balance terms, backup DJ promise, reviews pulled from Google and Yelp with dates, enquiry form (event type, date, venue), setlist by genre for bands, first dance note.
**Content model:** `package` (hours, price, inclusions, day part), `song` (artist, decade, genre; bands only), `kit_item` (name, photo, notes).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (enquiry and music planner submission), Query Filter (band setlist by genre and decade).
**Signature:** a music planner organised by part of the day (ceremony, cocktail hour, dinner, dance floor): the couple adds songs to each section and marks each one "must play" or "do not play", then sends it with their booking form; the DJ gets a printable sheet per section. Interactivity-API block that writes into a hidden field of a Jetpack Form, with a local draft saved in the browser. (seen on: [The Other Wedding DJ](https://theotherweddingdj.com/), who plans music "by each section of the wedding" with must-play and do-not-play lists)
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Trust & proof: prices in the open, three packages with the same 4-hour set so the only difference is the kit. (seen on: [Brighton Wedding DJ: Pricing](https://brightonweddingdj.co.uk/pricing/))
- Buying confidence: a kit page listing every piece of equipment with one photo of the full rig and the room size it suits ("small to medium sized rooms"). (seen on: [Brighton Wedding DJ: Kit](https://brightonweddingdj.co.uk/kit/))
- Operational: deposit and balance terms in one sentence (10% retainer to reserve, balance 14 days before, bank transfer) and a backup promise if the DJ is ill. (seen on: [Brighton Wedding DJ: FAQs](https://brightonweddingdj.co.uk/faqs/))
- Conversion helper: evening-only and all-day packages side by side, the all-day one adding MC, meal music and wireless mics for speeches. (seen on: [Manchester Wedding DJ: Pricing](https://manchesterweddingdj.co.uk/pricing/))
- Care & aftercare: a "requests on the night" rule (guests can ask, nothing on the do-not-play list gets through). (seen on: [Brighton Wedding DJ: FAQs](https://brightonweddingdj.co.uk/faqs/))
**Style: Quiet luxury mono**
- Type: display Aboreto 400 at 88px, line-height 1.02, tracking 0; body Figtree 400/18px, line-height 1.6; prices, times and song durations in IBM Plex Mono 400/15px.
- Palette: bg #F4F2EE (off-white), ink #161514, secondary #56524D (7.4:1 on bg), line #D8D4CD, accent #6D1F27 (oxblood, links and the planner's "must play" mark only).
- Layout: wide margins, 12-column grid with prose held to 64ch; hairline 1px rules instead of boxes, no cards, buttons square with a 1px ink border. Home page: one full-bleed photo of a real dance floor, a two-line statement set left, then the day running order as a timeline down the left column with packages to its right, then reviews as quoted paragraphs. Nav right-aligned, small, with "Check your date" last.
- Imagery: documentary wedding photos by the couple's photographers (credited), black-and-white or low-saturation colour, 3:2 and 4:5 crops, square corners.
- Motion: planner rows reorder with a 120ms View Transition; hover on links is an underline offset change only; nothing moves under prefers-reduced-motion.
- Why it fits now: couples who hire an "alternative" DJ are furnishing their day from fashion and interiors brands that sell with restraint, not disco graphics. [Lemaire](https://www.lemaire.fr/)
**Style variations:** Ivory Tux (#FAF8F3 ground, #111 type) · Late Set (charcoal #1E1D1B ground, bone type) · Brass (#8A6A2E accent on off-white)
**Refs:**
- [The Other Wedding DJ](https://theotherweddingdj.com/): a one-page site where the DJ's voice leads, with music planned per section and must-play and do-not-play lists.
- [Brighton Wedding DJ: Pricing](https://brightonweddingdj.co.uk/pricing/): a clear three-row price table that couples can compare in seconds.
- [Manchester Wedding DJ: Pricing](https://manchesterweddingdj.co.uk/pricing/): evening vs all-day packages and what each adds.

#### 260 · Piano Tuner & Technician (`tune`)
**For:** independent piano tuners and technicians who tune in homes, schools and venues, and sometimes restore or sell pianos from a small workshop.
**Real-world basis:** [Philatuner: FAQ](https://philatuner.com/faq/), [Philatuner: Restoration](https://philatuner.com/restoration/), [Sheffield Piano Tuner: Tuning Reminder](https://www.sheffieldpianotuner.co.uk/tuning-reminder/), [Cambridge Piano Tuner: Services](https://www.cambridgepianotuner.co.uk/services), [Russell Kassman: Piano Sales](https://www.russellkassman.com/piano-sales/)
**Templates:** front-page · page-piano-tuning · page-piano-repairs · page-restoration · archive-piano (for sale) · single-piano · page-tuning-reminder · page-clients · page-gallery · page-faq · page-about · page-contact
**Patterns (~30):** tuning price by condition (fine tuning if tuned within the last 12–18 months / pitch raise or pitch adjustment if further off), repairs at an hourly rate with a list of typical jobs (sticking keys, strings, hammers, levelling), restoration tiers (reconditioning / restoration / rebuilding) with what each covers (action, case, belly), seven-step restoration process, areas covered list, "how often to tune" note (twice a year for seasonal humidity), instruments tuned (grand, upright, square, harpsichord, clavichord), piano-for-sale listing (maker, model, size, finish, photo), alphabetical client list, workshop visit by appointment, contact with "texts preferred".
**Content model:** `piano` (maker, model, size, finish, year, price, status: available / reserved / sold), `service` (price, typical duration, when it applies), `client` (name, type: venue / school / artist).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (booking request and tuning reminder).
**Signature:** a tuning reminder form: the customer picks the month of the last tuning and how often they tune (1–24 months), the block shows the month the next tuning is due and offers an .ics file for their own calendar, and the entry lands in Jetpack Forms responses so the tuner can export "due in March" and send reminders. Interactivity API, no backend. (seen on: [Sheffield Piano Tuner: Tuning Reminder](https://www.sheffieldpianotuner.co.uk/tuning-reminder/))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Buying confidence: tuning prices tied to when the piano was last tuned (for example a lower rate if tuned in the last year, a higher one if not), so nobody is surprised by a pitch raise. (seen on: [Philatuner: FAQ](https://philatuner.com/faq/), [Cambridge Piano Tuner: Services](https://www.cambridgepianotuner.co.uk/services))
- Operational: current lead time ("usually 1–3 weeks") and the cancellation rule (less than 24 hours' notice is charged at 50%) printed beside the booking form. (seen on: [Philatuner: FAQ](https://philatuner.com/faq/))
- Care & aftercare: a restoration process page with the seven steps from consultation and moving to final inspection, delivery and a settling-in tuning. (seen on: [Philatuner: Restoration](https://philatuner.com/restoration/))
- Trust & proof: an alphabetical client list covering halls, schools and players. (seen on: [Russell Kassman: Clients List](https://www.russellkassman.com/clients-list/))
- Local & practical: pitch standard in plain words (tuned to A440, pitch raise if the piano sits below A430) and a "texts preferred" note on the phone number. (seen on: [Sheffield Piano Tuner: Piano Tuning](https://www.sheffieldpianotuner.co.uk/piano-tuning/))
**Style: Classical music-engraving editorial**
- Type: display Besley 400 at 80–104px, line-height 1.05, tracking +0.005em; body Crimson Pro 400/19px, line-height 1.6, oldstyle figures in prose and lining tabular figures in price tables; musical marks (staves, clefs, the A above middle C) set in Bravura (SIL OFL, from SMuFL) as small inline illustrations.
- Palette: bg #F8F7F2 (engraved-score paper), ink #121212, secondary #4A4843, rule #BDB8AE (staff lines, rules only), accent #8E1B1F (felt-hammer red, links and prices).
- Layout: a page laid out like an Urtext edition: generous outer margins, a running head with the page title and area in small caps, five thin horizontal rules as section dividers (a stave), prose at 62ch. Home page leads with a photo of the tuner at work inside an open grand, then prices as a two-column table, then the reminder form, then areas and clients. Square corners; buttons are text with a 1px red underline; inputs 2px radius.
- Imagery: close photographs of actions, hammers, pins and soundboards, natural light, 3:2, square corners; restoration before and after set side by side at the same crop.
- Motion: none on scroll. The reminder result appears with a 100ms View Transition; link underlines thicken on hover; nothing moves under prefers-reduced-motion.
- Why it fits now: classical publishers and venues are going back to quiet, paper-like pages that let engraving and photography carry the weight, which suits a trade that lives on precision. [G. Henle Verlag](https://www.henle.de/en/)
**Style variations:** Ebony (#141414 ground, ivory type, red prices) · Manuscript (#FBFAF5 paper, sepia #5B4630 rules) · Concert (#1F3B2F green-baize accent on white)
**Refs:**
- [Sheffield Piano Tuner: Tuning Reminder](https://www.sheffieldpianotuner.co.uk/tuning-reminder/): a simple form with month of last tuning and tuning interval, the basis for the signature.
- [Philatuner: FAQ](https://philatuner.com/faq/): honest price tiers by condition, tuning frequency, lead time and cancellation terms on one page.
- [Philatuner: Restoration](https://philatuner.com/restoration/): restoration sold as a step-by-step process with three tiers of work.

#### 261 · Watch & Clock Repair (`tick`)
**For:** one- to three-person watch and clock repair shops (often family-run for decades) that service wristwatches, pocket watches and antique clocks, sell restored pieces and make house calls for longcase clocks.
**Real-world basis:** [Watch and Clock Shop: services](https://www.watchclockshop.com/services), [Bowers Watch and Clock Repair: repairs](https://www.bowerswatchandclockrepair.com/clockandwatchrepair.htm), [Bowers: shipping instructions](https://www.bowerswatchandclockrepair.com/shippinginstructions.htm), [About Time: clock repairs](https://www.thewatchfixer.co.uk/clock-repairs), [Timepiece Repairs: repairs](https://www.timepiecerepairs.co.uk/repairs/)
**Templates:** front-page · page-watch-repairs · page-clock-repairs · page-house-calls · page-send-in (shipping instructions) · archive-timepiece (for sale, split by longcase / bracket and mantel / carriage / wall / watches) · single-timepiece · page-glossary · page-about (founded year, generations) · page-directions
**Patterns (~34):** clock repair price list by type (quartz movement replacement / 8-day mantel strip-down / longcase full strip-down, with "bushes included, handmade parts extra"), watch service list (battery, strap and link sizing, crystal, full overhaul, dial refinishing), "while you wait" battery and band-sizing notice with today's hours, house-call panel for grandfather and large wall clocks (with the "after 20 to 25 years a service call may not be enough" note), packing guide for clocks (remove pendulum and key, keep weights at home, two boxes with 3–4 in of packing), packing guide for watches, free-estimate-before-work statement, timepiece-for-sale card (maker, case wood, approx. date, height, features such as moonphase or bell strike, price), warranty line under every service, A–Z clock glossary entry, "since 1943" family history strip set as a sentence, trade-body membership line (BHI / AWCI / NAWCC), directions with parking.
**Content model:** companion `timepiece` CPT (maker, place, case material, approx. date, height, movement, strike, features, price, status for sale / reserved / sold) with taxonomy `timepiece_type`; `glossary_term` CPT (term, definition, see-also); site options for hours, warranty months, watch-repair intake open/closed and waiting-list text, bound via Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (send-in slip, house-call request, estimate request). WooCommerce only if the shop wants to take payment for restored clocks online; most list them with "call to view".
**Signature:** a **send-in slip with packing instructions**: the customer picks what they are sending (wristwatch, pocket watch, mantel clock, wall clock with pendulum, longcase movement) and the page shows only the packing steps for that item (Interactivity API), then a Jetpack Form collects name, address, phone, email, estimated value and a description of the fault. On submit the page prints an A4 slip to put in the box, with the shop's "no work without your authorisation, return postage is due even if you decline" terms at the foot. (seen on: [Bowers Watch and Clock Repair](https://www.bowerswatchandclockrepair.com/shippinginstructions.htm))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Warranty stated in months under each service, filled from one site option so it never disagrees across pages (trust & proof) (seen on: [Bowers: repairs](https://www.bowerswatchandclockrepair.com/clockandwatchrepair.htm))
- Downloadable house-call questionnaire for longcase and wall clocks, so the visit is quoted before the drive (content & tools) (seen on: [Bowers: repairs](https://www.bowerswatchandclockrepair.com/clockandwatchrepair.htm))
- Intake toggle: "We are not taking new watch repairs. Waiting list about three years. Clocks still accepted." shown on the watch page and the send-in page (operational) (seen on: [Timepiece Repairs](https://www.timepiecerepairs.co.uk/repairs/))
- A–Z glossary (escapement, suspension spring, grande sonnerie) linked from price-list terms, so customers understand the quote (care & aftercare) (seen on: [Bowers: glossary](https://www.bowerswatchandclockrepair.com/glossaryclocks.htm))
- "Battery while you wait" line that only shows during opening hours, including the "every other Saturday, call first" exception (local & practical) (seen on: [Watch and Clock Shop](https://www.watchclockshop.com/))
**Style: Technical drawing / tactile skeuo 2.0**
- Type: display Azeret Mono 300 at 88px, tracking 0 (its drafting-lettering feel carries the headings); body Source Serif 4 400 at 18px / 1.6; captions and price-list columns Azeret Mono 500 at 15px with tabular figures.
- Palette: #F2F3EF drafting film (bg), #1B2430 graphite ink (text), #A57A2C brass (accent: rules, buttons with ink text, active item in the packing picker), #E3E5DF plate grey (surface), #8E989E hairline (line), #7A1F1F case-oxblood (sold flags only).
- Layout: 12-column grid with visible 1px hairline column guides on the front page only; price lists as ruled tables with dimension-line style leaders between service and price; 0 radius everywhere except the round "dial" status marker on timepiece cards; top nav as a single ruled strip (Watches · Clocks · House calls · Send in · For sale · Directions). Home opens with a left-aligned repair-type chooser and today's hours, then the for-sale clocks.
- Imagery: macro photos of movements shot square on a neutral plate; line drawings (exploded movement, pendulum and key) in graphite for the packing steps; timepiece-for-sale photos full height at 2:3, never cropped round.
- Motion: packing steps swap with a 150 ms crossfade; a thin seconds-hand SVG in the header ticks once per second only when prefers-reduced-motion is not set, otherwise it is static.
- Why it fits now: engineering-drawing product pages with tactile hardware photography are the current look for precision goods, as on [teenage engineering: OP–1](https://teenage.engineering/products/op-1), and they suit a trade whose work is measured in tenths of a millimetre.
**Style variations:** Enamel Dial (#FBFAF6 bg, #14213D numerals) · Longcase (#2E2118 oak, #D8C7A1 text) · Bench Lamp (#FFFDF7 bg, #A57A2C brass rules)
**Refs:**
- [Bowers Watch and Clock Repair: shipping instructions](https://www.bowerswatchandclockrepair.com/shippinginstructions.htm): separate clock and watch packing steps, what details to enclose, free estimate and authorisation terms.
- [About Time: clock repairs](https://www.thewatchfixer.co.uk/clock-repairs): a plain price list by clock type with what each price includes.
- [Timepiece Repairs: longcase clocks](https://www.timepiecerepairs.co.uk/longcase-clocks/): for-sale card fields (maker, woods, date, height, features, price).

<a id="262"></a>
#### 262 · Bookbinder / Book Restoration (`bind`)
**For:** one- or two-person binderies doing conservation of old books, custom bindings and clamshell boxes, thesis and script binding, and the odd private-press edition.
**Real-world basis:** [Gibbs Bookbinding: conservation](https://www.gibbsbookbinding.com/repair), [Gibbs Bookbinding: project specifications](https://www.gibbsbookbinding.com/book-specifications), [Gibbs Bookbinding: scripts](https://www.gibbsbookbinding.com/script-thesis), [Ars Obscura Bookbinding: services](https://www.arsobscurabookbinding.com/?page_id=8), [J. S. Wilson & Son: thesis binding](https://www.jswilsonandson.co.uk/thesis-binding/)
**Templates:** front-page · page-conservation · page-bookbinding (custom bindings) · page-boxes (clamshells and slipcases) · page-thesis-scripts · page-specifications · page-swatches · page-order-process · archive-work (gallery) · single-work · archive-notes (studio news) · page-classes · page-about
**Patterns (~32):** conservation service list (re-hinging, red rot consolidation, page repair with toned Japanese tissue, map and document repair), before/after pair (two images, same crop, side by side), estimate request with photos, thesis binding options table (wire / channel / soft buckram / thermal / hard case, with "max 7 cm per volume" and "title, initials and surname in gold on the spine"), script binding price table (cloth hardcover / leather hardcover / stamping die / printing per page), "rush not available" turnaround line, materials section (bookcloth lines, goatskin colours, marbled and Japanese endpapers), clamshell box spec card, publishing trade terms table, classes panel with "temporarily unavailable" state, conservator credentials line (degree and institution), order-process steps (send deadline, PDF, dimensions, page count, quantity; mockup and itemised estimate follow).
**Content model:** companion `work` CPT (structure, covering material, endpapers, tooling, dimensions, year, before/after image pair) with taxonomy `service` (conservation / binding / boxes / scripts); `swatch` CPT (code, name, line such as "Library buckram" or "Asahi", material cloth / leather / paper, stock note, image) with taxonomy `swatch_line`.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (estimate request with photo upload, thesis/script order form), WooCommerce (optional: blank journals and fixed-price script bindings), Query Filter (swatch lines).
**Signature:** a **swatch library that feeds the order form**: every in-stock bookcloth and leather colour as a square photo with its maker's code and line, stock notes such as "limited stock, mill closed 2022", filterable by line. "Use this cloth" writes the code into the order form's material field (Interactivity API), and a fixed note says screen colours are indicative. (seen on: [Gibbs Bookbinding: in-stock bookcloth](https://www.gibbsbookbinding.com/studionotes/2024/8/20/fabric-samples), [J. S. Wilson & Son: colour swatches](https://www.jswilsonandson.co.uk/colour-swatches/))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- "Colours are indicative only and subject to availability" set under every swatch grid, plus an offer to post a physical sample (buying confidence) (seen on: [J. S. Wilson & Son: colour swatches](https://www.jswilsonandson.co.uk/colour-swatches/))
- Turnaround line on the scripts page, "2–3 weeks, rush not currently available", driven by one option so it can change at thesis season (operational) (seen on: [Gibbs Bookbinding: scripts](https://www.gibbsbookbinding.com/script-thesis))
- "By appointment only, no walk-ins" with the booking email and text number in the header of the visit page (local & practical) (seen on: [Ars Obscura: services](https://www.arsobscurabookbinding.com/?page_id=8))
- Small-edition trade terms table (trade cloth 40% off, minimum 3 copies) for authors and small presses (conversion helpers) (seen on: [Ars Obscura: services](https://www.arsobscurabookbinding.com/?page_id=8))
- Stamping-die and custom artwork specs page (die price from $175, file requirements, foil colours) so customers send usable files (content & tools) (seen on: [Gibbs Bookbinding: project specifications](https://www.gibbsbookbinding.com/book-specifications))
**Style: Editorial book typography (private press)**
- Type: display Goudy Bookletter 1911 400 at 84px, line-height 1.05 (drawn from Goudy's Kennerley, a private-press staple that reads as metal type); body Crimson Pro 400 at 19px / 1.6; running heads and swatch codes in Courier Prime 400 at 15px, letterspaced 0.04em.
- Palette: #F5F0E6 laid paper (bg; the brief's physical reason is paper stock), #1E1B18 ink (text), #1F4D3A bottle-green buckram (accent: links, "use this cloth"), #B08D3C gold-foil (hairline rules and folio numbers only), #E7DFCF board (surface), #CFC4AF line.
- Layout: a real book grid with classical margins (inner 1, top 1.2, outer 2, foot 2.4); single text column of 62ch with side-notes in the outer margin for dimensions and materials; running head across the top of each page, folio-style page numbers in the footer; the colophon (typefaces, paper, printer) as the site footer. Home: a large before/after pair from a recent conservation job, then the service list as a contents page with dot leaders.
- Imagery: raking-light photos of spines and tooling at 4:5; swatches as flat, colour-checked squares with the code set underneath; before/after pairs always the same size and crop.
- Motion: none on scroll. Swatch filter uses a View Transition to reorder; hover on a swatch raises the code line to full ink. Reduced motion disables the transition.
- Why it fits now: independent publishers are leaning into book-page typography on the web, with running heads and generous margins, as on [Fitzcarraldo Editions](https://fitzcarraldoeditions.com/); it is the obvious language for a bindery.
**Style variations:** Buckram (#1F4D3A green, #F5F0E6 paper) · Goatskin (#3B1F18 bg, #EADFC8 text) · Vellum (#FBF8F1 bg, #6B5A3A ink)
**Refs:**
- [Gibbs Bookbinding: in-stock bookcloth](https://www.gibbsbookbinding.com/studionotes/2024/8/20/fabric-samples): swatch grid with maker codes, lines and stock notes.
- [Gibbs Bookbinding: scripts](https://www.gibbsbookbinding.com/script-thesis): honest per-copy prices, die cost, turnaround and no-rush statement.
- [J. S. Wilson & Son: thesis binding](https://www.jswilsonandson.co.uk/thesis-binding/): binding options written as a spec list students can match to university rules.

<a id="263"></a>
#### 263 · Luthier / Guitar Builder (`fret`)
**For:** solo luthiers and workshops of two to four who build acoustic or electric guitars to order, sell finished instruments from stock and take a few repairs.
**Real-world basis:** [Ruokangas: Guitar Creator](https://ruokangas.com/guitar-creator/), [Ruokangas: in stock](https://ruokangas.com/in-stock/), [Fylde Guitars: custom building](https://www.fyldeguitars.com/custom-build.html), [Northwood Guitars: recent builds](https://www.northwoodguitars.com/recent-builds), [Erlewine: order guitar](https://danerlewine.com/order-guitar/)
**Templates:** front-page · archive-model · single-model · page-features-options (tops, back and sides, trim, headstocks) · page-tonewoods · page-custom-building · archive-instrument (in stock) · single-instrument · archive-build (recent builds) · page-price-list · page-repairs · page-care · page-guarantee · page-dealers
**Patterns (~36):** model page header (body size, scale length, nut width, top, back and sides, price inc. VAT), price list table grouped by family (standard / signature / mandolins) with a dated heading ("Price list July 2025"), custom-build steps (discuss, quote, 25% deposit and estimated completion date, final payment, collect or ship), options page sections (headstock shapes, back and sides tropical/domestic, soundboards, inlays), in-stock grid with AVAILABLE / SOLD and serial, recent-build entry (one title line such as "Cocobolo 12-fret 00 with redwood top", hero photo and angle thumbnails), "personal selection" note for maker's-choice instruments, repair list (neck resets, refrets, bracing, refinishing in nitro), care guide, guarantee statement, dealer list by country, order request form with pickup or ship.
**Content model:** companion `model` CPT (body size, scale, nut width, standard woods, base price); `instrument` CPT (model, serial, top, back and sides, neck, fingerboard, finish, weight, price, status available / reserved / sold, audio/video URL); `wood_set` CPT (species, origin, grade, photos of the actual set, status in stock / reserved); `build` posts linked to an instrument.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce (in-stock instruments and a "commission deposit" product), Jetpack Forms (custom-build enquiry, repair request), Query Filter (in-stock by model and wood).
**Signature:** a **pick-your-actual-wood-set chooser**: the tonewoods page lists every top and back-and-sides set currently in the workshop, photographed as the real boards with their set number. The customer picks a model, then a top and a back set, and the Interactivity API block shows the model's base price, the set upcharges and the 25% deposit. "Reserve these woods" adds the deposit product to the Woo cart with the set numbers as order meta and marks the sets reserved. (seen on: [Ruokangas: Guitar Creator](https://ruokangas.com/guitar-creator/))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Humidity and temperature care page (40–55% RH, 18–25°C, no lemon oil) linked from every instrument page and the order confirmation email (care & aftercare) (seen on: [Fylde Guitars: care](https://www.fyldeguitars.com/care.html))
- Export price note on the price list: "outside the UK divide by 1.2 to remove VAT; import duty is payable by the buyer" (local & practical) (seen on: [Fylde Guitars: price list](https://www.fyldeguitars.com/price_list.html))
- Guarantee written in full, including exclusions (humidity damage, electronics, shipping), as its own page (trust & proof) (seen on: [Fylde Guitars: guarantee](https://www.fyldeguitars.com/guarantee.html))
- AVAILABLE / SOLD state on each in-stock instrument, with sold ones kept as a record of past work (operational) (seen on: [Ruokangas: in stock](https://ruokangas.com/in-stock/))
- Delivery preference (collect from the workshop or ship) asked in the order form, with the collection address pre-filled (conversion helpers) (seen on: [Erlewine: order guitar](https://danerlewine.com/order-guitar/))
**Style: Warm craft catalogue grotesk**
- Type: display Belanosima 700 at 80px, line-height 1.0, tracking -0.01em; body Literata 400 at 18px / 1.6 for model descriptions; spec tables in IBM Plex Mono 400 at 15px with tabular figures.
- Palette: #FAF8F3 spruce white (bg), #231A12 rosewood (text), #9A5A1E nitro amber (accent: links, "reserve" action), #ECE3D2 maple (surface), #CDBFA6 line, #3E4A3A cedar green (reserved/sold labels).
- Layout: catalogue grid of 4 columns on desktop, 2 on phones; instruments shown as tall 2:3 photos with the spec table directly below, ruled, no card borders; model pages use a left spec column and a right image column that scrolls; 0 radius; nav: Models · In stock · Custom · Tonewoods · Repairs · Prices. Home opens with what is in stock now, then the current lead time sentence, then the models.
- Imagery: full-length instrument photos on a warm grey backdrop, same angle for every model; wood sets shot flat under daylight at 1:2 with the set number chalked on; build photos in the workshop without filters.
- Motion: wood set choice updates price figures in place (no layout shift); View Transition from in-stock grid to instrument page; nothing animates on scroll; reduced motion removes the transition.
- Why it fits now: craft retailers have moved to plain catalogue grids with a confident grotesk and honest product photography, as on [Labour and Wait](https://www.labourandwait.co.uk/), which suits builders who want the wood to do the talking.
**Style variations:** Spruce (#FAF8F3 bg, #9A5A1E amber) · Rosewood (#2B1B14 bg, #EFE3CF text) · Sunburst (#F4E9D4 bg, #6B2E12 edges)
**Refs:**
- [Ruokangas: Guitar Creator](https://ruokangas.com/guitar-creator/): choosing tops from the maker's actual board inventory.
- [Fylde Guitars: price list](https://www.fyldeguitars.com/price_list.html): dated, VAT-inclusive list grouped by family with an export note.
- [Fylde Guitars: custom building](https://www.fyldeguitars.com/custom-build.html): the commission process in plain steps with the 25% deposit.

<a id="264"></a>
#### 264 · Synth & Guitar-Pedal Maker (`patchbay`)
**For:** small pedal builders and Eurorack module makers (one to ten people) selling assembled units and DIY kits direct and through dealers.
**Real-world basis:** [Old Blood Noise Endeavors: manuals](https://www.oldbloodnoise.com/manuals), [Old Blood Noise Endeavors: dealers](https://www.oldbloodnoise.com/dealers), [Befaco: Even VCO](https://www.befaco.org/even-vco/), [Aion FX: Luna optical tremolo](https://aionfx.com/project/luna-optical-tremolo/), [ZVEX Effects: repairs](https://www.zvex.com/repairs)
**Templates:** front-page · archive-product (Woo, with categories: delay and reverb / drive and fuzz / modulation / utility / modules / kits) · single-product · archive-product-retired · page-manuals · page-firmware · page-dealers · page-repairs · page-custom (artwork commissions) · page-custom-gallery · archive-news · page-contact
**Patterns (~38):** product spec block (HP, depth assembled and kit, +12V/-12V mA, or for pedals 9V centre-negative and mA), assembled vs DIY kit choice with separate prices, docs list (assembly manual, schematic, BOM, parts spreadsheet) with version numbers, build difficulty line (beginner / intermediate), parts substitution note, demo video embed, controls list, manuals grid (pedal face image links to the PDF, retired pedals included), firmware download table, dealer directory by state and country, repair steps (troubleshoot first, request an RMA, ship with the number), troubleshooting table (symptom / likely cause / fix), warranty terms per range (lifetime on hand-painted, 1 year on printed, extendable by registration), custom artwork request panel with lead time, limited colourway note.
**Content model:** WooCommerce products with attributes `format` (pedal / eurorack / kit / pcb), `hp`, `depth_mm`, `plus12_ma`, `minus12_ma`, `power` and `difficulty`; companion `doc` CPT (linked product, doc type, version, date, file); `dealer` CPT (name, address, region, URL to their search for the brand); `trouble` CPT (symptom, cause, fix, product family).
**Plugins:** WooCommerce (variable products for assembled / kit / PCB only), Jetpack Forms (RMA request, custom artwork request), Jetpack Newsletter (release and restock emails), Query Filter (category and format filters).
**Signature:** a **docs and power panel on every product**: the product page reads its attributes into a spec block (width in HP, depth assembled vs kit, +12V and -12V current), switches between assembled and DIY kit with the price, and lists the versioned documents (assembly manual, schematic, BOM file) plus a ModularGrid link. The same `doc` records feed the site-wide manuals page, so a new PDF version appears in both places. (seen on: [Befaco: Even VCO](https://www.befaco.org/even-vco/))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Troubleshooting table on the repairs page (dead battery, crackling pots, no LED) that customers work through before the RMA form appears (care & aftercare) (seen on: [ZVEX Effects: repairs](https://www.zvex.com/repairs))
- Manuals for retired products stay online, with the release date in the filename and link text (content & tools) (seen on: [Old Blood Noise Endeavors: manuals](https://www.oldbloodnoise.com/manuals))
- Dealer directory grouped by state and country, each dealer linking to a search of their own shop for the brand (local & practical) (seen on: [Old Blood Noise Endeavors: dealers](https://www.oldbloodnoise.com/dealers))
- Parts-substitution note on a kit when a component is discontinued, with a link to the substitutes sheet (buying confidence) (seen on: [Aion FX: Luna](https://aionfx.com/project/luna-optical-tremolo/))
- Custom artwork lead time ("expect 8–12 weeks, payment upfront") on the custom page, set from one option (operational) (seen on: [ZVEX Effects: custom artwork](https://www.zvex.com/design-a-custom))
**Style: Dither / 1-bit bitmap**
- Type: display Doto 900 at 96px (a dot-matrix face that reads like an LED display or silkscreened panel legend), tracking 0.02em; body Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 400 at 18px / 1.55; specs, mA figures and version numbers in Departure Mono 400 at 15px.
- Palette: #EFEDE6 panel white (bg), #111111 ink (text and 1-bit imagery), #1F6F5C solder-mask green (accent: links, add to cart), #D8D5CB surface, #9C998F line, #C8102E LED red (sold out and "retired" only).
- Layout: a strict 8px baseline and a 12-column grid that echoes rack units; product pages set like a front panel, with the spec block as a boxed legend in the top right; 1px black rules, 0 radius; nav in Departure Mono (Pedals · Modules · Kits · Manuals · Dealers · Repairs). Home leads with the newest release as a large dithered photo and its spec block, then the category list as plain text links.
- Imagery: product photos processed to 1-bit Atkinson dither for listings and heroes (files are small), with the full-colour photo on the product gallery; schematics and panel drawings as black line art.
- Motion: a product image switches from dithered to full colour on hover or focus with a 120 ms step change; no scroll effects; reduced motion shows the colour image without the swap.
- Why it fits now: 1-bit dithering has returned as a deliberate, low-weight image style for technical and DIY communities, as on [Low-Tech Magazine (solar)](https://solar.lowtechmagazine.com/), and it matches the schematic-and-silkscreen world of small hardware makers.
**Style variations:** Stompbox (#F2C230 enclosure yellow, #111 legends) · Eurorack (#D9DCDF aluminium, #111 panel type) · Schematic (#F7F7F2 bg, #1B3A6B trace blue)
**Refs:**
- [Befaco: Even VCO](https://www.befaco.org/even-vco/): HP, depth and current specs next to assembled and DIY kit links and versioned build files.
- [Aion FX: Luna optical tremolo](https://aionfx.com/project/luna-optical-tremolo/): kit vs PCB-only options, difficulty, build PDFs and a substitution note.
- [ZVEX Effects: repairs](https://www.zvex.com/repairs): warranty by range, troubleshoot-first table and RMA process.

### XXIX. Land, food craft & self-sufficiency

<a id="265"></a>
#### 265 · Tiny House Builder (`tiny`)
**For:** one-workshop builders of tiny houses on wheels (a crew of 3–10, a few dozen homes a year) who sell built-to-order models, shells and the odd consignment home, and spend half their week answering "how much, how long, where can I park it?"
**Real-world basis:** [Indigo River Tiny Homes: planning tool](https://www.indigorivertinyhomes.com/planning-tool), [Indigo River Tiny Homes: events and farm tours](https://www.indigorivertinyhomes.com/events), [Rocky Mountain Tiny Houses: pricing](https://rockymountaintinyhouses.com/pricing/), [Rocky Mountain Tiny Houses: how to get started](https://rockymountaintinyhouses.com/about/how-to-get-started/), [Rocky Mountain Tiny Houses: delivery](https://rockymountaintinyhouses.com/about/tiny-house-delivery/), [Tru Form Tiny: models](https://truformtiny.com/models/), [Tru Form Tiny: homes for sale](https://truformtiny.com/tiny-homes-for-sale/)
**Templates:** front-page (current lead time, models, homes available now) · archive-model (Our Homes) · single-model · page-planning-tool (pricing) · page-get-started · page-financing · archive-inventory (available now and consignment) · page-delivery · page-events (tours and open houses) · page-faq · archive (build journal)
**Patterns (~40):** current lead time line ("Lead time: 4–18 months, summer is our busiest season"), model row (name, length, width, loft or main-floor bedroom, "starting at" price), shell vs complete price table by trailer length (12–14 ft, 16–20 ft, 22–26 ft, 28–34 ft, 40 ft, gooseneck), what's standard list (trailer, framing, insulation, RV hook-up, off-grid options), "Design your own" call-out per model, available-now card (year, model, price, "Learn more"), consignment note, contract types explained (commitment letter, design agreement, construction agreement), getting-started steps (email, call, design rounds, estimate, draws), delivery rate table by distance, recommended transport companies, "Where can I put a tiny home?" explainer, certification note (NOAH, not RVIA, and why), financing lenders row with example monthly payment, tour dates at the workshop, press row with real article links, build journal post card
**Content model:** companion `model` CPT (length_ft, width, layout, sleeps, base_price_complete, base_price_shell, options_json for the planning tool), companion `inventory` CPT (year, model, price, status available/pending/sold, consignment yes/no), companion `event` for tours; one site option `lead_time` bound site-wide through Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (planning-tool submission, tour and design-appointment requests), Advanced Query Loop (available-now homes first, sold last; upcoming tours), optional WooCommerce for a paid design appointment and downloadable plan sets.
**Signature:** a **planning tool** that prices a build as you choose: pick a length (20, 24, 28, 32 or 36 ft, each with a starting price), a width (8 ft 6 in standard or 10 ft upgrade), a floor plan, then structural options (gooseneck bonus room, SIPs, loft storage) and finishes (roof, siding, windows, solar), each showing "+$" beside it and a running total pinned to the side. A short "not included" line (sales tax, registration, delivery, financing) sits under the total. On submit, a Jetpack Form carries the chosen options and total to the builder, and the visitor is offered a design appointment. Built as a companion Interactivity-API block reading `options_json` from the model, so there is no custom backend. (seen on: [Indigo River Tiny Homes](https://www.indigorivertinyhomes.com/planning-tool))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A current lead-time line in the header area, set once in site options, with the plain note that summer is the busiest season and winter the slowest. (seen on: [Rocky Mountain Tiny Houses](https://rockymountaintinyhouses.com/faq/))
- Delivery rate table by distance (100 miles $270, 200 miles $540, and so on) plus the names of the transport firms they trust for longer moves. (seen on: [Rocky Mountain Tiny Houses](https://rockymountaintinyhouses.com/about/tiny-house-delivery/))
- A paid design appointment whose fee is credited against the build, stated right under the booking button. (seen on: [Indigo River Tiny Homes](https://www.indigorivertinyhomes.com/planning-tool))
- Open-book pricing page for time-and-materials builds: materials at cost plus a small consumables fee, crew rates and the builder fee by trailer length. (seen on: [Rocky Mountain Tiny Houses](https://rockymountaintinyhouses.com/pricing/contract-pricing-details/))
- Tour listings with a date range ("now through Christmas 2026"), the farm address and a map, so seasonal open days retire themselves. (seen on: [Indigo River Tiny Homes](https://www.indigorivertinyhomes.com/events))
**Style: Warm Scandi minimal (timber)**
- Type: Headings: Plus Jakarta Sans 600 (OFL) at 76–112px, tracking 0 at display and +0.01em below 32px, line-height 1.02; body: Literata 400/18px, line-height 1.65, 64ch measure; lengths, weights and prices: Red Hat Mono 500/16px with tabular figures.
- Palette: #F4F1EA bg (planed spruce) · #1E1C19 text · #A8703C oiled larch (links, running total) · #34503F pine green (available-now status, focus ring) · #E3DDD0 surface (plan panels) · #C9C1B1 line
- Layout: 12-column grid with wide gutters; 0 radius on images, 4px on buttons and inputs. Front page opens with one full-bleed photo of a finished house on site, the lead-time line directly underneath, then models as a ruled list (name, length, "starting at") rather than cards. Model pages put the floor plan drawing at full width, the spec table beside a single photo column, and the planning tool on its own page with the total docked in a sticky right column on desktop and a bottom bar on phones.
- Imagery: daylight photos of the real houses at 3:2, shot level from standing height, interior shots showing the loft ladder and kitchen run; floor plans as single-weight line drawings in #1E1C19 on #E3DDD0 with dimensions in Red Hat Mono.
- Motion: running total ticks with a 120ms opacity change when an option is added; View Transitions from model list to model page; nothing moves on scroll. All wrapped in prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
- Why it fits now: small cabin and tiny-home makers now sell on calm, timber-toned sites built around daylight photos rather than lifestyle stock, as on [Koto: cabins](https://koto.co.uk/cabins)
**Style variations:** Birch (#F7F5F0 bg, #1E1C19 ink, pale larch) · Tar Paper (#1F1E1B bg, #E9E2D3 type) · Cedar Shingle (#EFE6D8 bg, #7A4A2A rules)
**Refs:**
- [Indigo River Tiny Homes: planning tool](https://www.indigorivertinyhomes.com/planning-tool): the full option list with "+$" prices by length, width and floor plan, the "not included" line and the emailed estimate at the end
- [Rocky Mountain Tiny Houses: pricing](https://rockymountaintinyhouses.com/pricing/): shell vs complete price ranges by trailer length in one plain table
- [Rocky Mountain Tiny Houses: how to get started](https://rockymountaintinyhouses.com/about/how-to-get-started/): contract types, deposits and design rounds explained in the builder's own blunt voice

#### 266 · Camper-Van Conversion Builder (`vanlife`)
**For:** small conversion shops (one bay to a dozen staff) that build out Sprinters, Transits and ProMasters to order, sell a fixed line-up of layouts plus full customs, and move a few used or consigned vans on the side.
**Real-world basis:** [Ready. Set. Van.: home with model line-up](https://www.readysetvan.com/), [Ready. Set. Van.: Joyride](https://www.readysetvan.com/joyride), [Ready. Set. Van.: FAQ](https://www.readysetvan.com/faq), [Vanlife Customs: estimate your build](https://vanlifecustoms.com/estimateyourbuild), [Vanlife Customs: vans for sale](https://vanlifecustoms.com/vans-for-sale), [Vanlife Customs: FAQ](https://vanlifecustoms.com/faq), [Camplife Customs: process](https://camplifecustoms.com/process/)
**Templates:** front-page (line-up, build slots, vans for sale) · archive-model (by chassis: Sprinter, Transit, ProMaster) · single-model · page-custom-builds · page-process · archive-van-for-sale · single-van-for-sale · page-service-and-upgrades · archive-gallery (past builds) · page-faq · page-book-a-call
**Patterns (~40):** model line-up chart (model, base cost, seats, sleeps, shower interior/outdoor, chassis), model spec sheet (battery Ah, inverter W, solar W and "expandable to", fresh and grey water gallons, fridge litres, heater BTU, fan), standard vs optional upgrades list, "conversion only, vehicle not included" price note, chassis sourcing explainer (bring your own or we source through dealers), build slot line ("Now booking limited build slots"), retainer block, process steps (consultation, chassis, systems, interior, exterior, quote, build, orientation), handover orientation note, warranty statement, vans for sale grid (name, year and chassis, features, price, status), consignment offer, service menu (heaters, electrical, suspension), heater FAQ, build gallery by chassis, financing terms line, press and reviews links, book-a-call block
**Content model:** companion `model` CPT (chassis, wheelbase, base_price, seats, sleeps, shower, battery_ah, inverter_w, solar_w, solar_max_w, fresh_gal, grey_gal, fridge_l, heater), taxonomy `chassis`; companion `van_for_sale` CPT (year, chassis, features, price, status available/pending/sold, consigned yes/no); site option `build_slots` (text plus next start month) bound through Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce (build-date retainer as a simple product, service parts), Jetpack Forms (custom build questionnaire, consignment enquiries), Advanced Query Loop (vans for sale with sold last, models filtered by chassis), Cal.com embed for intro calls.
**Signature:** a **model line-up chart** on the front page and model archive: one row per layout with base cost, seats, sleeps, shower (interior or outdoor) and which chassis it fits, plus a final "Custom builds" row with a price range. Each row links to the model's spec sheet, where every system line is marked standard or optional and upgrades are listed underneath. Built from `model` meta with a Query Loop inside a companion table block, so a new layout appears in the chart the day it is published. (seen on: [Ready. Set. Van.](https://www.readysetvan.com/))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Build-slot line with the next production start ("start dates currently 2–3 months out") and the build length once the van arrives ("8–12 weeks"), edited in one site option. (seen on: [Vanlife Customs](https://vanlifecustoms.com/faq))
- A retainer product that holds the next available build date ("$10,000 retainer"), sold through Woo checkout with the terms printed beside the button. (seen on: [Ready. Set. Van.](https://www.readysetvan.com/faq))
- Warranty in one sentence on every model page ("1 year / 24,000 miles on craftsmanship and materials"), with component warranties handed to the maker. (seen on: [Vanlife Customs](https://vanlifecustoms.com/faq))
- Vans for sale with Pending and Sold flags, sold vans kept at the bottom as proof, and a "sell your van with us" consignment note. (seen on: [Vanlife Customs](https://vanlifecustoms.com/vans-for-sale))
- A handover step called out in the process: a personal orientation session and road test before the keys change hands. (seen on: [Camplife Customs](https://camplifecustoms.com/process/))
**Style: 70s outdoor supergraphics revival**
- Type: Headings: Sansita 800 (OFL, a heavy 70s-flavoured display with a real italic) at 84–136px, tracking -0.005em, line-height 1.0; body: Barlow 400/18px (drawn from California highway signs), line-height 1.6; spec labels and table heads: Barlow Condensed 600/16px, uppercase only inside the spec table.
- Palette: #F6F4EE bg (primer white) · #20231F text · #E86A1C stripe orange (primary buttons, "Now booking") · #F4B41A marigold stripe · #6B3A1F brown stripe and footer · #2E6B5A pine teal (links, focus ring)
- Layout: three stacked livery stripes (orange, marigold, brown, each 10px) run along the top edge and break diagonally at the right, like van side graphics; they reappear once as the footer band and nowhere else. 12-column grid, 0 radius on photos, 6px on buttons. Front page: one wide side-on photo of a finished van, the build-slot line, the line-up chart, then vans for sale. The spec sheet is a two-column ruled table with standard items in text colour and options in brown.
- Imagery: side-on and rear-door-open photos of real builds at 16:9 and 4:5, shot in daylight at trailheads rather than studio renders; one top-down layout drawing per model in single-weight line.
- Motion: stripes do not move; the line-up chart row highlights on hover with a background change only; View Transitions between a chart row and its spec sheet. All motion gated by prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
- Why it fits now: camper hire and van brands are going back to bold, bright livery and friendly heavy type, as in the 2023 Vanzzz identity: [Fonts In Use: Vanzzz visual identity](https://fontsinuse.com/uses/56701/vanzzz-visual-identity)
**Style variations:** Westfalia (#F2E8D5 bg, #2E6B5A teal stripes) · Desert Night (#1D1F1A bg, #F4B41A type) · Trailhead (#EEF1EA bg, #3F6B2F green stripes)
**Refs:**
- [Ready. Set. Van.: home with model line-up](https://www.readysetvan.com/): one table comparing layouts by base cost, seats, sleeps, shower and chassis, ending in a custom-build price range
- [Ready. Set. Van.: Joyride](https://www.readysetvan.com/joyride): a real model spec sheet with battery, inverter, solar, water, fridge and heater, plus the optional upgrades list
- [Vanlife Customs: vans for sale](https://vanlifecustoms.com/vans-for-sale): used and consigned vans with Pending and Sold states and the limited-guarantee note

#### 267 · Off-Grid Homestead Blog + Courses (`homestead`)
**For:** homesteading couples and families who write, film and teach from their own land, earning from a membership or a few courses, printables, books and a podcast.
**Real-world basis:** [An Off Grid Life: seasonal homestead checklists](https://www.anoffgridlife.com/seasonal-homestead-checklists/), [An Off Grid Life: garden planner](https://www.anoffgridlife.com/garden-planner/), [Homestead and Chill: start here](https://homesteadandchill.com/start-here-top-posts/), [The Prairie Homestead: courses](https://www.theprairiehomestead.com/courses), [The Ready Life Academy (Sustainable Preparedness)](https://www.thereadylife.com/academy/)
**Templates:** front-page · page-start-here · archive (category: Garden, Preserving, Chickens, Off-Grid Power, Water, Self-Reliance) · single (post with printable) · page-seasonal-checklists · archive-course (Sensei) · single-course · page-academy (membership) · page-free-library · page-shop (printables, books, DVDs) · archive-podcast · page-about
**Patterns (~42):** "Start here" grouped reading list (Garden 101, preserving recipes, chickens 101, off-grid power basics), category landing with sub-topics (seed starting, raised beds, composting, pest control, irrigation), seasonal checklist (Winter, Spring, Summer, Fall with garden, animals, buildings, preserving), printable download block (page count, format, "print a master copy"), free library row (coop checklist, quick-start garden guide), newsletter sign-up with the free toolkit it sends, course card (title, what's inside: videos, ebooks, printables, recipes), membership plan block (monthly and annual with guarantee days), course module list, preserving recipe card (method: water bath, pressure, freezer, fridge), build project with materials list and cut list, "about us" land story with years off grid, podcast episode row, books row, shop category list (DVDs, downloads, books)
**Content model:** posts with taxonomies `topic` and `season`; companion `checklist_item` CPT (season, area garden/animals/buildings/preserving, linked post); recipe fields (method, yield, jar size, processing time) as post meta bound into a recipe card; Sensei courses and lessons.
**Plugins:** Sensei LMS (courses and lessons), Jetpack Newsletter (weekly letter and opt-in delivery of the free toolkit), WooCommerce (printables as downloadable products, books and DVDs), Subscriptions for WooCommerce (monthly and annual academy plans), Seriously Simple Podcasting.
**Signature:** a **seasonal homestead checklist**: tasks grouped into Winter, Spring, Summer and Fall, and within each season by area (garden, animals, buildings, preserving). The block opens on the current season from the visitor's date, lets them switch seasons, tick tasks off (kept in localStorage), and each task links to the post or lesson that explains it ("Clean out chicken coops and change the bedding"). A print button outputs the season as a single A4 page. Companion Interactivity-API block over the `checklist_item` CPT. (seen on: [An Off Grid Life](https://www.anoffgridlife.com/seasonal-homestead-checklists/))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Newsletter opt-in that delivers a free printable garden-planning toolkit with seed-starting and planting calendars for every growing zone. (seen on: [Homestead and Chill](https://homesteadandchill.com/start-here-top-posts/))
- Membership plans with the guarantee stated next to each price: monthly with a 7-day money-back guarantee, annual with 30 days and the saving shown in dollars. (seen on: [The Ready Life Academy](https://www.thereadylife.com/academy/))
- A dated "free this week" window on a printable (free 19–25 February, then in the shop) that flips itself to a normal product after the end date. (seen on: [An Off Grid Life](https://www.anoffgridlife.com/garden-planner/))
- Printable pack page listing every sheet inside (seed inventory, seed-starting tracker, monthly watering chart, harvest record) with the note to print a master and copy it each year. (seen on: [An Off Grid Life](https://www.anoffgridlife.com/garden-planner/))
- Monthly group coaching call and private forum listed as part of the membership, with the call schedule shown on the academy page. (seen on: [The Ready Life Academy](https://www.thereadylife.com/academy/))
**Style: Almanac letterpress**
- Type: Headings: Coustard 900 (OFL, a heavy slab cut like old wood type) at 80–128px, tracking +0.005em, line-height 1.02; body: Crimson Pro 400/19px (an old-style book face), line-height 1.6, 66ch measure; season names, dates and checklist areas: Crimson Pro italic at 17px, small caps via font-variant only on running heads.
- Palette: #F1EBDD bg (uncoated almanac stock) · #1D1B16 text · #2F5D3A seed-packet green (links, ticked tasks, focus ring) · #C9962B harvest mustard (current-season marker, printable badge) · #E4DCC8 surface (recipe and checklist panels) · #8F8676 line
- Layout: a running head across every page like an almanac ("Fall · Preserving"), double hairline rules between sections, a strict two-column text grid on posts with the recipe card or materials list in the outer column. Front page reads like a contents page: this season's checklist first, then Start Here, then the latest posts as a numbered list with dates. 0 radius everywhere except checkboxes (2px).
- Imagery: real photos from the land (jars on the shelf, the woodpile, the coop) at 4:5, lightly desaturated and printed with a subtle paper grain overlay; section openers use public-domain 19th-century seed-catalogue and farm engravings, credited in captions.
- Motion: ticking a task draws a short line through it (150ms); season switch swaps content without animation; no scroll effects. Respect prefers-reduced-motion: reduce by removing the strike-through animation.
- Why it fits now: seed and garden sellers are leaning into print-era catalogue art and heavy type to stand apart from glossy lifestyle blogs, as on [Hudson Valley Seed Company: art packs](https://hudsonvalleyseed.com/collections/art-packs)
**Style variations:** Root Cellar (#2A241C bg, #F1EBDD type, mustard rules) · Seed Packet (#F4EFE2 bg, #2F5D3A headings) · Frost Date (#E9EEEA bg, #1F3A4A ink)
**Refs:**
- [An Off Grid Life: seasonal homestead checklists](https://www.anoffgridlife.com/seasonal-homestead-checklists/): tasks by season across garden, animals, buildings and preserving, the base for the checklist block
- [Homestead and Chill: start here](https://homesteadandchill.com/start-here-top-posts/): a Start Here page grouped by topic, with the free zone-by-zone planting toolkit as the newsletter hook
- [The Ready Life Academy: membership](https://www.thereadylife.com/academy/): monthly vs annual plans, guarantees, coaching calls and forum laid out on one page

#### 268 · Permaculture Design & Courses (`swale`)
**For:** small permaculture teaching farms and design practices (two to five people) that run a PDC, hands-on weekends and online courses, and sell property designs priced by the size of the land.
**Real-world basis:** [Midwest Permaculture: design services](https://midwestpermaculture.com/permaculture-design-services/), [Midwest Permaculture: hands-on extended weekend](https://midwestpermaculture.com/hands-on-permaculture-extended-weekend-training/), [Midwest Permaculture: office hours](https://midwestpermaculture.com/office-hours/), [The Permaculture Lab: Permaculture Design Course](https://thepermaculturelab.com/Permaculture_Design_Course), [Verge Permaculture: scholarship fund](https://vergepermaculture.ca/bonnie-ann-scholarship-fund/), [Verge Permaculture: virtual tour](https://vergepermaculture.ca/virtual-tour/)
**Templates:** front-page · page-design-services · page-pdc (in-person) · page-online-pdc · archive-course (catalogue) · single-course · archive-event (hands-on weekends, tours) · single-event · page-scholarships · page-virtual-tour · page-office-hours · page-free-resources · archive (blog)
**Patterns (~40):** property scale switch (Residence up to 1 acre, Homestead 1–10 acres, Farm 10+ acres), design service ladder (site assessment by Zoom, walkabout, framework design, full design, management oversight), "what's included" per service (base map, water layer, plant layer, hardscape layer, plant lists with suppliers), quote fee note, hourly consulting line with minimum session, PDC weekend schedule (six weekends listed by date, 9am–4:30pm), early-bird and payment-plan block, work-trade note, lodging options table (tent camping, community rooms, private bath, earth-shelter cabin), meals note (all meals, vegan options), what to bring list, cancellation refund ladder, class size line, registration open/closed state, office hours block (second Monday, noon to 1pm Central), scholarship block (amount, who qualifies, deadline), virtual tour with site features (food forest, passive solar greenhouse, swales, cob oven), free resources list, graduates page
**Content model:** companion `service` CPT with meta per scale (price_residence, price_homestead, price_farm, quote_fee_*), companion `event` via The Events Calendar for weekends and in-person PDCs, Sensei courses for online PDC and mini-courses, companion `site_feature` CPT for the tour (name, photo, x/y position on the site plan, description).
**Plugins:** The Events Calendar + Event Tickets (weekend and PDC places, with lodging as separate ticket types and a capacity cap), Sensei LMS (online PDC, mini-courses), Jetpack Forms (site assessment intake with address and sketch upload, scholarship applications), Jetpack Donations block (scholarship fund), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (how to reach the farm).
**Signature:** a **property scale switch** on the design services page: three buttons (Residence, Homestead, Farm, each with its acreage) change every price on the page at once, from the Zoom site assessment and walkabout to the framework and full design ranges and their quote fees, so visitors only ever read prices for land like theirs. Built as a companion Interactivity-API block reading per-scale meta through Block Bindings; the chosen scale is remembered in the URL so it can be shared. (seen on: [Midwest Permaculture](https://midwestpermaculture.com/permaculture-design-services/))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Lodging and meals table on each event (free tent camping, community-centre room, private bath, earth-shelter cabin for three nights) with prices, sold as Event Tickets types so rooms cannot be overbooked. (seen on: [Midwest Permaculture](https://midwestpermaculture.com/hands-on-permaculture-extended-weekend-training/))
- Plain cancellation ladder: full refund less $25 more than 60 days out, less $100 at 30–60 days, less $150 inside 30 days, none once training starts. (seen on: [Midwest Permaculture](https://midwestpermaculture.com/hands-on-permaculture-extended-weekend-training/))
- Scholarship page with the award amount, who qualifies, the rule that forms are due 4 weeks before the course, and the list of donors who fund it. (seen on: [Verge Permaculture](https://vergepermaculture.ca/bonnie-ann-scholarship-fund/))
- Work-trade places mentioned on the course page ("a couple of partial and sometimes full work trade positions per class"). (seen on: [The Permaculture Lab](https://thepermaculturelab.com/Permaculture_Design_Course))
- Monthly drop-in office hours for students and graduates, with the fixed slot and time zone stated. (seen on: [Midwest Permaculture](https://midwestpermaculture.com/office-hours/))
**Style: Hand-drawn field map, earth tones**
- Type: Headings: Inknut Antiqua 600 (OFL, a chunky, slightly hand-cut serif) at 76–120px, tracking 0, line-height 1.04; map labels and annotations: Kalam 400 (OFL, Indian Type Foundry handwriting) at 17–20px, used only on plans and diagrams; body: Alegreya Sans 400/18px, line-height 1.6, 66ch measure; prices and acreages: Alegreya Sans tabular figures.
- Palette: #E6E8DA bg (survey paper) · #22261C text · #4F7A2E leaf green (links, selected scale, focus ring) · #2E6E8E water blue (swales, water layer, rainfall notes) · #8A6A3B contour brown (rules, map lines) · #D4D7C3 surface
- Layout: every section sits on a faint contour-line background drawn in #8A6A3B at 12% opacity; content is held in a strict 12-column grid with hand-lettered map labels only on drawings. Front page: one aerial or site-plan drawing across the full width with the next course dates under it, then the three services by scale, then the tour. Hairline brown rules, 0 radius on images, 3px on buttons.
- Imagery: the practice's own base maps and site plans (water layer in blue, plant layer in green), hand-inked and scanned at 3:2; photos of students digging swales and of mature food forests, natural colour, no filters.
- Motion: scale switch cross-fades prices over 150ms; tour points on the site plan open a caption on focus or click, not hover-only; nothing moves on scroll. All gated by prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
- Why it fits now: illustrated, hand-drawn maps are back as a sign of first-hand local knowledge, as in the fold-out guides of [Herb Lester: Into the Fog map](https://www.herblester.com/products/into-the-fog-sherlock-holmes-london)
**Style variations:** Dry Season (#EDE3CF bg, #8A6A3B rules) · Keyline (#E3EBE6 bg, #2E6E8E contours) · Canopy (#1E2A1C bg, #D9E0C6 type)
**Refs:**
- [Midwest Permaculture: design services](https://midwestpermaculture.com/permaculture-design-services/): every service priced three ways by property scale, with quote fees and what each design layer includes
- [Midwest Permaculture: hands-on extended weekend](https://midwestpermaculture.com/hands-on-permaculture-extended-weekend-training/): lodging options, meals, what to bring, class size and the tiered refund policy on one event page
- [Verge Permaculture: scholarship fund](https://vergepermaculture.ca/bonnie-ann-scholarship-fund/): a donor-funded PDC scholarship with amount, eligibility and deadline rules

#### 269 · Foraging Walks (`forage`)
**For:** a one- or two-person foraging business running seasonal walks and courses (plants, fungi, seaweed), private group sessions and a long-running wild food guide.
**Real-world basis:** [Wild Walks Southwest: Calendar](https://wildwalks-southwest.co.uk/calendar/), [Wild Walks Southwest: FAQs](https://wildwalks-southwest.co.uk/faqs/), [Galloway Wild Foods: Accessible/Scooter Friendly Events](https://gallowaywildfoods.com/product-category/accessiblescooter-friendly-events/), [Galloway Wild Foods: Visiting Galloway](https://gallowaywildfoods.com/visiting-galloway-for-galloway-wild-foods-events/), [Wild Food UK: Mushroom Guide](https://www.wildfooduk.com/mushroom-guide/)
**Templates:** front-page · page-course-calendar · single-tribe_events (one course date) · page-courses (course types) · archive-species (wild food guide) · single-species · category-season (spring, summer, autumn, winter) · page-private-experiences · page-gift-vouchers · page-faqs · page-visiting · single (blog and recipes)
**Patterns (~34):** course calendar row (date, course, meeting place, "8 places left" / "1 place left" / "Sold out", Book now), course category filter (Seaweed, Fungi, Plant, Cordage, Accessible/scooter friendly), course type summary ("A 4hr experience to sustainably forage and taste local seaweeds"), species record (common name, scientific name, other names, season start, season end, cap, gills, stem, habitat, spore print, frequency), possible confusion panel linking to the lookalike's record, poisonous species list, in season now strip, foraging code (numbered rules), what to bring and wear, weather policy, private experiences enquiry, gift voucher (valid 12 months), where to stay near events, press and articles, testimonials (named, real), foraging alerts sign-up, wild recipe (wild booze, seaweed, mushroom).
**Content model:** companion `species` CPT (scientific name, other names, `species_type` taxonomy: mushroom / plant / seaweed; `season_start` and `season_end` as month numbers; edibility: edible / inedible / poisonous / deadly; habitat; spore print; frequency; `confused_with` relationship to other species), `season` taxonomy on posts; course dates are The Events Calendar events with the venue used as the meeting point.
**Plugins:** The Events Calendar + Event Tickets (paid tickets through WooCommerce, capacity per date), WooCommerce (gift vouchers sold as a product and redeemed as coupons; books), Query Filter (species type), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (meeting points map), Jetpack Forms (private experiences), MailPoet (foraging alerts).
**Signature:** a season-filtered wild food guide. The species index is a table (photo, common name, scientific name, type, season start, season end) with two selects: type and month. Choosing "October" keeps only species whose season range includes October, including ranges that wrap the year (Nov–Feb). Deadly and poisonous species stay in the list and carry a red edibility label, because knowing what not to pick is the point. A companion Interactivity API block does the month logic on `season_start`/`season_end` meta; Query Filter handles type. (seen on: [Wild Food UK: Mushroom Guide](https://www.wildfooduk.com/mushroom-guide/))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Low-capacity states on every date ("8 places left", "Last few tickets", "Sold out") pulled from Event Tickets stock, with sold-out dates kept visible so people can see how fast they go (seen on: [Wild Walks Southwest](https://wildwalks-southwest.co.uk/calendar/))
- Booking policy block: goes ahead in rain unless torrential, date changes allowed up to 2 weeks before, places transferable, vouchers valid 12 months (seen on: [Wild Walks Southwest](https://wildwalks-southwest.co.uk/faqs/))
- An "Accessible/scooter friendly" event category with its own archive link in the main nav (seen on: [Galloway Wild Foods](https://gallowaywildfoods.com/product-category/accessiblescooter-friendly-events/))
- A visiting page for people travelling in: getting there, B&Bs, hostels, camp sites near the meeting points (seen on: [Galloway Wild Foods](https://gallowaywildfoods.com/visiting-galloway-for-galloway-wild-foods-events/))
- After-course email template listing the species covered, with links to their guide records (seen on: [Wild Walks Southwest](https://wildwalks-southwest.co.uk/faqs/))
**Style: Herbarium editorial**
- Type: Display: Brygada 1918 600, 84px/1.02, tracking -0.01em; scientific names in Brygada 1918 Italic 500. Body: Literata 400, 18px/1.6. Collector-label data (date, habitat, grid ref, season): Courier Prime 400, 15px. Display to body ratio 4.7x.
- Palette: mounting sheet #F1F2EC (bg), green-black ink #1C2419 (text), sorrel green #45602A (links, actions), fly agaric red #A3191F (poisonous and deadly labels only), label white #FFFFFF (surface), pencil grey #BFC3B4 (rules).
- Layout: 12-column grid, left-aligned, hairline rules instead of boxes. Each species page is laid out as a herbarium sheet: one tall 3:4 specimen photo "mounted" with two paper-tape strips (CSS pseudo-elements), and a boxed collector's label bottom right in Courier. The calendar is a ruled list, one row per date. Nav is plain text: Courses, Wild Food Guide, Private, Vouchers, About. Home opens with the next three dates, then "In season now" as a row of three sheets, then the latest article.
- Imagery: specimens shot on plain paper from above, square crops for the index, habitat shots at 3:2 with a caption and location; no rounded corners, no filters.
- Motion: changing the month in the guide swaps rows with a 150ms View Transitions cross-fade; the tape strips darken on hover. Everything is static under prefers-reduced-motion.
- Why it fits now: nature-education and museum sites are moving to catalogue layouts where the object record is the design, which suits a trade built on identification. [Garden Museum: Collection](https://www.gardenmuseum.org.uk/collection/)
**Style variations:** Pressed (#F1F2EC sheet, #1C2419 ink) · Kelp (#E6ECE8 bg, #1F4A45 links) · Spore Print (#EDE7DC bg, #5A3A22 brown)
**Refs:**
- [Wild Food UK: Mushroom Guide](https://www.wildfooduk.com/mushroom-guide/): type and season filters over a table with season start and end columns; each record has a "Possible Confusion" section.
- [Wild Walks Southwest: Calendar](https://wildwalks-southwest.co.uk/calendar/): one-row-per-date course list with category filter, meeting place and live places-left counts.
- [Galloway Wild Foods: Accessible/Scooter Friendly Events](https://gallowaywildfoods.com/product-category/accessiblescooter-friendly-events/): accessibility treated as a browsable event category, alongside fungi, plant and coastal.
