<a id="270"></a>
#### 270 · Mushroom Grower / Grow Kits (`spore`)
**For:** a small gourmet mushroom farm selling fresh mushrooms to restaurants and a neighbourhood share, plus grow kits, plug spawn and classes online.
**Real-world basis:** [Mycopolitan: Farm Share](https://www.mycopolitan.com/share), [Mycopolitan: Our Mushrooms](https://www.mycopolitan.com/our-mushrooms), [Cascadia Mushrooms: Growing Mushrooms at Home](https://cascadiamushrooms.com/pages/growing-mushrooms-at-home), [Far West Fungi: Shiitake Mini-Farm Grow Kit](https://farwestfungi.com/products/shiitake-mushroom-grow-kit), [Fungi Ally: Mushroom Cultivation Classes](https://www.fungially.com/pages/mushroom-cultivation-classes)
**Templates:** front-page · archive-product (grow kits, plugs, dried) · single-product (grow kit) · page-farm-share · page-our-mushrooms (varieties for cooks and chefs) · page-growing-at-home (instructions per variety) · page-find-our-mushrooms (restaurants, retail, markets) · page-wholesale · archive-tribe_events (classes, farm tours) · page-faq
**Patterns (~32):** grow kit summary (price, difficulty: Beginner, "first flush within two weeks of activation"), what you need to succeed checklist (non-chlorinated water, mister, forks, loose plastic bag), grow guide jump list (Shiitake, Lion's Mane, Oyster, Reishi, Wine Cap, Plugs), temperature and light panel ("55–70°F, north-facing window"), first crop guarantee panel, variety entry for cooks (flavour, how to cook it, shelf-life), farm share tiers with pickup neighbourhoods, find our mushrooms (restaurants, retail, farmers' market days), wholesale enquiry, classes list (home growers, commercial growers), outdoor plug spawn and wine cap garden section, grower photo reviews, free shipping threshold bar.
**Content model:** WooCommerce products with attributes (variety, format: kit / plugs / dried, difficulty); companion `variety` CPT (scientific name, temperature range, light, days to first flush, shelf-life, flavour, cooking notes) linked to products; companion `stockist` CPT (type: restaurant / retail / market, neighbourhood, day); classes and farm tours as The Events Calendar events.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce (Local Pickup locations for share sites), Subscriptions for WooCommerce (bi-weekly share), The Events Calendar + Event Tickets (classes, farm tours), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (stockists and markets), Jetpack Forms (wholesale).
**Signature:** a sliding-scale farm share. One bi-weekly subscription with three prices (Sustainer $32, Supporter $38, Supported $23) and a pickup neighbourhood chosen at checkout. The rule from the real share is shown as plain text and enforced: for every 1 Supporter and every 10 Sustainer shares, one Supported share opens up. A companion Interactivity API block counts active subscriptions per variation and shows "Supported shares open: 2"; when the count is zero the Supported option is disabled with a short explanation instead of disappearing. Pickup sites are Woo Local Pickup locations, so no custom checkout. (seen on: [Mycopolitan: Farm Share](https://www.mycopolitan.com/share))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Kit storage note on every grow kit: can't start within a week? Refrigerate at 34–39°F for up to four weeks (seen on: [Cascadia Mushrooms](https://cascadiamushrooms.com/pages/growing-mushrooms-at-home))
- First crop guarantee with a "send us photos of your block" troubleshooting form (Jetpack Forms with file upload) (seen on: [Far West Fungi](https://farwestfungi.com/products/shiitake-mushroom-grow-kit))
- Shelf-life line on each variety for chefs ("Excellent shelf-life" for trumpet, "Fair shelf-life" for lion's mane) (seen on: [Mycopolitan](https://www.mycopolitan.com/our-mushrooms))
- Free shipping threshold in the header bar, set from the Woo free-shipping rule so it never goes stale (seen on: [Cascadia Mushrooms](https://cascadiamushrooms.com/pages/growing-mushrooms-at-home))
- Farmers' market list with a store locator map (seen on: [Far West Fungi](https://farwestfungi.com/pages/our-farmers-markets-1))
**Style: Riso zine**
- Type: Display: Gasoek One 400, 96px/0.95, tracking 0.005em. Body: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 400, 18px/1.6. Labels, prices and grow data: Martian Mono 500, 15px. Display to body ratio 5.3x.
- Palette: uncoated paper #F7F5EE (bg; the stock the farm's printed kit instructions are on), riso black #1D1D1B (text), fluorescent pink #FF48B0 (fills and highlights only, never text), riso teal #00666B (links and actions), yellow #FFE800 (sold-out and notice fills), ink overlap #7A3A6B (the multiply of pink over teal, image duotone shadow).
- Layout: pages composed as zine spreads: an asymmetric 7/5 split, 3px black rules, headings set big and flush left over the gutter. The grow guide runs as a real numbered sequence down the page with a fixed jump list on wide screens. Nav is a single text row plus a numeric cart count. Home: "Grown this week" spread with a big two-ink photo, then grow kits in a plain three-up row with prices in mono, then the farm share block with its live count.
- Imagery: mushroom clusters and grow rooms as two-colour duotones (core duotone filter, pink over teal) with a 2px misregistration offset on the second layer; raw product shots on paper for the shop; square corners throughout.
- Motion: on hover the second ink layer shifts 2px back into register; add-to-cart counter ticks without animation. No motion under prefers-reduced-motion.
- Why it fits now: two-ink fluorescent print has become the look of small makers who do their own packaging and inserts, and it reads as hands-on rather than wellness-brand. [RISOTTO Studio](https://risottostudio.com/)
**Style variations:** Pink Teal (#FF48B0 on #F7F5EE paper) · Riso Blue (#0078BF ink, #1D1D1B text) · Sunflower (#FFE800 fills, #1D1D1B ink)
**Refs:**
- [Mycopolitan: Farm Share](https://www.mycopolitan.com/share): sliding-scale share with the 1-per-1 and 1-per-10 rule written out, pickup neighbourhoods listed on the page.
- [Cascadia Mushrooms: Growing Mushrooms at Home](https://cascadiamushrooms.com/pages/growing-mushrooms-at-home): one long instruction page with a jump link per variety, a "what you need" list and a water note.
- [Far West Fungi: Shiitake Mini-Farm Grow Kit](https://farwestfungi.com/products/shiitake-mushroom-grow-kit): product page built around the first-crop guarantee and photo-based troubleshooting.

#### 271 · Cheesemaker (`curd`)
**For:** a farmstead or small creamery making cheese from its own herd's milk, selling at markets, through a farm store, weekly drop sites and mail order.
**Real-world basis:** [Clover Creek Cheese Cellar: Drop Site Order](https://clovercreekcheese.com/drop-site-order/), [Clover Creek Cheese Cellar: The Farm Store](https://clovercreekcheese.com/online-store/the-farm-store/), [Chaseholm Farm Creamery: Cheeses](https://www.cfcreamery.com/cheeses), [Lincolnshire Poacher Cheese: Lincolnshire Poacher](https://lincolnshirepoachercheese.com/our-produce/lincolnshire-poacher/), [Holden Farm Dairy: Hafod Cheese](https://holdenfarmdairy.co.uk/hafod-cheese)
**Templates:** front-page · page-cheeses (range by style) · archive-product · single-product · page-drop-site-order · page-farm-store (visit, directions, honesty payment) · page-cheesemaking (how we make it) · page-markets (month and agenda views) · single-tribe_events (cheese experience) · page-wholesale · page-weddings (cheese wedding cakes)
**Patterns (~32):** range list by style (Fresh, Soft ripened, Washed rind, Alpine, Cheddar) with milk, rind and age ("cave aged 6–8 weeks") plus one pairing line, maturity grades (Poacher 14–16 months, Vintage 18–22 months, tasted at 12 months to decide), make-day facts ("2000 litres every other day, 18–20 cheeses of 10kg"), herd and land panel, drop-site timetable (place, time), order deadline line, farm store hours and honesty payment steps, market month calendar, cheese experience (date, length, price, 16 places), ship-to states or regions list, holiday collection box, wedding cheese cake enquiry, raw milk note, gift cards, recipes.
**Content model:** WooCommerce attributes: milk (cow / goat / sheep), treatment (raw / pasteurised), rennet (animal / vegetarian), `cheese_style` taxonomy, age in months (min and max meta); drop sites are Woo Local Pickup locations with a time in the description; markets and the cheese experience are The Events Calendar events.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce (Local Pickup locations; the core Cash on Delivery gateway relabelled "Pay at pickup"), Order Delivery Date (Lite) (mail-order dispatch days), The Events Calendar + Event Tickets (markets, cheese experience), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (drop sites and farm store), Jetpack Forms (wholesale, wedding cakes).
**Signature:** a weekly drop-site order. The page states the rule once ("Order by Thursday 3 p.m. for Friday delivery"), lists the Friday route in order (Bellwood 1:00 p.m., Altoona 1:30 p.m., Newry 2:15 p.m.), then shows a quick-order table of every product with quantity fields and add-to-cart. A companion block reads the cut-off day and time from settings and prints the live line "Orders for Friday 2 October close Thursday 3 p.m."; after the cut-off it rolls to the next Friday. At checkout the drop sites are the only pickup options and payment can be card or pay at pickup. (seen on: [Clover Creek Cheese Cellar: Drop Site Order](https://clovercreekcheese.com/drop-site-order/))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A plain list of the states or regions the creamery ships chilled cheese to, shown on the shop page and at checkout (seen on: [Chaseholm Farm Creamery](https://www.cfcreamery.com/cheese-shop))
- Delivery window honesty: "Orders may arrive +/- 2 days from your preferred delivery date" next to the date picker (seen on: [Neal's Yard Dairy](https://www.nealsyarddairy.co.uk/))
- Farm store visit page: self-serve during daylight, staffed Saturdays 10 a.m.–12 p.m., step-by-step driveway directions, how to pay at the honesty box, pre-order for a whole wheel (seen on: [Clover Creek Cheese Cellar](https://clovercreekcheese.com/online-store/the-farm-store/))
- Cheese experience capped at 16 people, with the reason given in one sentence and a places-left count (seen on: [Clover Creek Cheese Cellar](https://clovercreekcheese.com/events-calendar/experience/))
- Cheese wedding cake enquiry page with a phone number and a short form (seen on: [Lincolnshire Poacher Cheese](https://lincolnshirepoachercheese.com/cheese-wedding-cakes/))
**Style: Farmhouse editorial serif**
- Type: Display: Linden Hill 400 (The League, OFL), 80px/1.05, tracking 0; pairing lines in Linden Hill Italic. Body: Newsreader 400 (text optical size), 18px/1.6. Data lines (milk, age, rennet, drop-site times): Sometype Mono 400, 15px. Display to body ratio 4.4x.
- Palette: bloom white #FAFAF6 (bg, the colour of a bloomy rind), wax black #1F1E1B (text), rind ochre #8A5E10 (links and actions), pasture green #3D5634 (full-width bands with white text), whey grey #D9D6CC (rules), ash #55574F (captions).
- Layout: a magazine column of 64ch with full-bleed photo breaks. The range is a printed list, not cards: cheese name at 44px, one mono data line, two sentences, a pairing line, price and add-to-cart on the right. Running heads on long pages ("The Range", "Visiting"). Nav: wordmark left, five text links, cart as a word. Home: the drop-site deadline line sits above the masthead, then a make-room photo, then the range by style, then the farm store and markets.
- Imagery: natural-light make-room and ageing-room photos, wheels on wooden shelves at 4:5, cut faces shot straight on at 1:1, black-and-white archive photos for the farm history; no rounded corners, no overlays.
- Motion: View Transitions morph the product photo from the range list into the product page; link underlines thicken on hover. Nothing moves under prefers-reduced-motion.
- Why it fits now: cheese sellers are writing long, specific making stories and presenting ranges like a printed catalogue, which rewards a serif with character over a generic shop grid. [Neal's Yard Dairy](https://www.nealsyarddairy.co.uk/)
**Style variations:** Bloom (#FAFAF6 bg, #8A5E10 ochre) · Ash Rind (#2B2C28 bg, #EDEBE4 text) · Pasture (#3D5634 bands, #F4F4EE text)
**Refs:**
- [Clover Creek Cheese Cellar: Drop Site Order](https://clovercreekcheese.com/drop-site-order/): cut-off rule, timed drop route and a quick-order product table on one WooCommerce page.
- [Lincolnshire Poacher Cheese: Lincolnshire Poacher](https://lincolnshirepoachercheese.com/our-produce/lincolnshire-poacher/): one cheese sold at three maturity grades, each explained in months and taste.
- [Chaseholm Farm Creamery: Cheeses](https://www.cfcreamery.com/cheeses): the range grouped by style (fresh, soft ripened, washed) with ageing time and a pairing per cheese.

<a id="272"></a>
#### 272 · Whole-Animal Butcher (`cleaver`)
**For:** an independent nose-to-tail butcher shop buying whole animals from a few named farms, selling over the counter, by weekly order and through a monthly basket.
**Real-world basis:** [Left Bank Butchery: Menu, Cuts & Cooking](https://leftbankbutchery.com/menu-cuts-cooking), [Left Bank Butchery: Our Farms](https://leftbankbutchery.com/our-farms), [The Local Butcher Shop: Butcher Baskets](https://thelocalbutchershop.com/pages/butcher-baskets), [The Meat Hook: Holiday Reservations](https://www.themeathook.com/holiday-reservations), [Turner & George: Delivery & Storage](https://www.turnerandgeorge.co.uk/pages/delivery-storage)
**Templates:** front-page · page-menu-cuts-cooking · archive-product (by animal) · single-product · page-weekly-order · page-butcher-basket · page-our-farms · page-classes · page-holiday-reservations · page-visit (locations and hours) · page-delivery-storage
**Patterns (~32):** cut menu by animal (Pork, Beef, Lamb, Sausage, Charcuterie, Poultry) with a one-line note per cut ("Coppa chop: boneless, from the tender part of the Boston butt"), cut groups within an animal (Chops, Larger roasts, Smaller cuts), farm profile (farm, town, farmer, breeds, how they're raised), hang time panel ("hung 14 to 30 days"), dry-aged in house panel, butcher basket explainer (what's in it, pickup window, order cut-off), class listing (date, time, price, "Sold out"), holiday centrepiece reservation, location card (address, phone, open daily hours), delivery slots and weight tolerance, rendered fats, bones and stock shelf, pet grind, sandwich of the day, gift card.
**Content model:** companion `farm` CPT (location, farmer, animals, breeds, practices) linked to products; Woo products with `animal` taxonomy, `cut_group` taxonomy, and meta for weight, feeds, bone-in, hang days; `location` via the companion Stockist CPT reused for the shop's own branches (address, hours, phone).
**Plugins:** WooCommerce (Local Pickup locations per branch), Subscriptions for WooCommerce (monthly butcher basket), Order Delivery Date (Lite) (holiday pickup days, weekly order days), The Events Calendar + Event Tickets (butchery and cooking classes).
**Signature:** holiday centrepiece reservations. A seasonal page (Thanksgiving, Christmas, Easter and Passover) where customers pick the centrepiece (heritage turkey, standing rib, porchetta, lamb leg), choose the pickup branch, then choose a pickup day limited to the two or three days before the holiday. Reservations close on a set date, after which the page swaps to a "reservations closed, walk-ins from the counter" notice. Built as a Woo product category with pickup days from Order Delivery Date (Lite), branches as Local Pickup locations, and a companion date-switch block for the close. (seen on: [The Meat Hook: Holiday Reservations](https://www.themeathook.com/holiday-reservations))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Basket calendar rule shown on the basket page: pickups run the first full week of each month, orders placed after the 27th start the following month (seen on: [The Local Butcher Shop](https://thelocalbutchershop.com/pages/butcher-baskets))
- Weight tolerance and slot capacity notes: single cuts may be +/- 5% of the listed weight; if a delivery slot can't be picked it is full; next-day cut-off at 12 p.m. (seen on: [Turner & George](https://www.turnerandgeorge.co.uk/pages/delivery-storage))
- Class cards with the practical line people ask about: "$90 per person + 10% off all purchases. Coolers encouraged." and a sold-out state per date (seen on: [Left Bank Butchery](https://leftbankbutchery.com/class))
- Class gift certificates emailed to the recipient with a code (seen on: [The Local Butcher Shop](https://thelocalbutchershop.com/pages/classes))
- Per-branch opening hours on one visit page, each with address and phone as tappable links (seen on: [The Meat Hook](https://www.themeathook.com/visit))
**Style: Enamel-sign utility**
- Type: Display: Pathway Gothic One 400, uppercase, 88px/1.0, tracking 0.01em (condensed like pressed-steel shop signs). Body: Public Sans 400, 18px/1.6. Weights, prices and hang days: Overpass Mono 500, 15px. Display to body ratio 4.9x.
- Palette: enamel white #F5F6F3 (bg), black #141414 (text), enamel red #B3202A (primary actions and "Sold out" plates), enamel blue #0F4C81 (section plates with white text), tile grey #D5D8D2 (rules and table lines).
- Layout: section headings are enamel plates: a solid blue or red block with a 2px white inset keyline and a 6px radius (the only radius in the theme, taken from pressed-steel signs). The cut menu runs in two columns per animal with the cut name in caps and a one-line note beneath, like a counter board. Nav is a single plate-coloured bar with five text links. Home: "On the block this week" plate (which animals came in, from which farm), then weekly order, butcher basket, classes and the visit block.
- Imagery: counter, cutting block and cold-room photos in hard daylight at 3:2; farm portraits in black and white at 4:5; cuts shot flat on butcher paper at 1:1. No rounded images, no raw close-ups on the home page.
- Motion: plates press down 1px on active; nothing else. No motion under prefers-reduced-motion.
- Why it fits now: independent food shops are dropping stock photography for flat two-ink sign colours and big condensed type that matches their shopfronts. [The Meat Hook](https://www.themeathook.com/visit) (flat red #B22129 and blue #2E3A87 throughout)
**Style variations:** Counter (#F5F6F3 bg, #B3202A red plates) · Tiled (#FFFFFF bg, #0F4C81 plates, grey tile lines) · Stockroom (#1E3A2B green plates, #F5F6F3 text)
**Refs:**
- [Left Bank Butchery: Menu, Cuts & Cooking](https://leftbankbutchery.com/menu-cuts-cooking): full cut menu by animal and cut group with a plain one-line explanation of each cut.
- [The Local Butcher Shop: Butcher Baskets](https://thelocalbutchershop.com/pages/butcher-baskets): monthly basket with a stated pickup window, order cut-off and member discount.
- [The Meat Hook: Holiday Reservations](https://www.themeathook.com/holiday-reservations): seasonal centrepiece reservations starting with the choice of pickup location.

#### 273 · Kombucha & Ferments Brewer (`scoby`)
**For:** a one-site kombucha, kraut and kimchi producer with a taproom or fill counter, farmers-market stalls, a short list of local stockists, and hands-on fermentation classes.
**Real-world basis:** [IndieFerm: Kombucha](https://independentfermentations.com/kombucha/), [IndieFerm: Taproom](https://independentfermentations.com/brewery-taproom/), [Fermensch: Flavors](https://fermensch.com/flavors), [Fermensch: Local Home Delivery](https://fermensch.com/local-home-delivery), [Firefly Kitchens: Classes](https://fireflykitchens.com/classes-1)
**Templates:** front-page · page-flavors · page-on-tap · page-taproom · page-where-to-find-us (stockists + farmers markets) · page-local-delivery · page-wholesale · page-what-is-kombucha · archive-class · Woo shop · single-product · page-supplies (SCOBYs, kits)
**Patterns (~34):** flavor entry (name, one-line taste tag, paragraph, organic ingredient list, format flag), "The Classics" and "Seasonal & Experimental" flavor groups, past flavors list, on-tap board (six kombucha taps beside the kraut and kvass jars), growler fill sizes (32 oz / 64 oz), bottle-return discount note ("$1 off every bottle you bring back"), farmers-market days table, stockists list with map link, class card (Kraut 101, price, seats, private-group minimum), SCOBY and starter-kit shelf, wholesale enquiry form, "keep refrigerated, it is alive" care line, how we brew (tea, sugar, SCOBY, 1–3 weeks) process strip.
**Content model:** Woo products with attributes `format` (can / bottle / growler / keg only), `status` (classic / seasonal / past), `base tea`; companion `stockist` (name, town, type: shop / café / market, day and time); companion `event` for classes.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce (Local Pickup), Order Delivery Date (Lite) (local delivery days), Event Tickets (class seats), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap.
**Signature:** a **flavor board with format and lifecycle flags**: flavors sit under The Classics, Seasonal & Experimental, and Past Flavors, and each one carries its format line, such as "only available in growlers and kegs", driven by Woo attributes. Moving a flavor to "past" drops it from the shop but keeps it in the archive list, so regulars can still see what used to pour. (seen on: [Fermensch: Flavors](https://fermensch.com/flavors))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Bottle-return credit note on every product and at checkout: bring back a clean bottle and save $1 on a refill (seen on: [IndieFerm: Kombucha](https://independentfermentations.com/kombucha/))
- Taproom house rules block with dog policy by area ("dog-friendly for friendly dogs" outside, none where food is served) and flight tastings (seen on: [IndieFerm: Taproom](https://independentfermentations.com/brewery-taproom/))
- Private class terms: minimum 8, maximum 14 people, refundable deposit, shown beside the class dates (seen on: [Firefly Kitchens: Classes](https://fireflykitchens.com/classes-1))
- "Keep refrigerated, unpasteurised" care card on every ferment, plus a plain-language "What is kombucha" page (seen on: [Firefly Kitchens](https://fireflykitchens.com/), [Fermensch: What is Kombucha](https://fermensch.com/what-is-kombucha))
- Supply-shop hours block that differs from taproom hours, with a named staff member who answers brewing questions (seen on: [IndieFerm: Supplies](https://independentfermentations.com/supplies/))
**Style: Soft neo-brutalism bright**
- Type: display DynaPuff 700 at 84–104px, tracking 0, line-height 1.0; body Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 400 at 18px, line-height 1.6; labels and format flags Martian Mono 500 at 14px uppercase, +0.04em.
- Palette: #FFF4C7 bg (pale lemon, like unbleached label stock) · #161310 text and all rules · #E8457A accent (hibiscus, links and the add-to-cart button only) · #BDE7C9 surface for flavor entries (SCOBY mint) · #FFC9A8 surface for class entries (peach) · hard shadow 4px 4px 0 #161310.
- Layout: 12-column grid; flavor entries are flat pastel blocks with a 2px ink border and hard offset shadow, radius 6px on blocks and 0 on images; one entry per row on mobile, 7/5 split on desktop with the ingredient list in the narrow column. Home leads with the on-tap board, then this week's market stalls, then the shop. Nav is a single bordered bar with the taproom hours inside it.
- Imagery: straight-on photos of growlers and jars on the fill counter, square crops, no rounding; ingredient close-ups (dried hibiscus, ginger) at 4:5.
- Motion: buttons press down 3px into their shadow on :active (transform only, 120ms ease-out); no scroll effects; all motion inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
- Why it fits now: the hard-shadow, flat-pastel neo-brutal look is the current language of small, friendly direct sellers and reads as hand-made rather than corporate. [Gumroad](https://gumroad.com/)
**Style variations:** Hibiscus (pink #E8457A on lemon ground) · Ginger (warm #F2A93B fills, ink borders) · Green Tea (mint #BDE7C9 ground, black type)
**Refs:**
- [Fermensch: Flavors](https://fermensch.com/flavors): classic, seasonal and past flavor grouping, with format-only notes like growlers and kegs.
- [IndieFerm: Brewery Taproom](https://independentfermentations.com/brewery-taproom/): tap count, growler sizes, dog rules and food partner written as plain operational copy.
- [Firefly Kitchens: Classes](https://fireflykitchens.com/classes-1): short class list at one flat price with private-group minimum and maximum.

#### 274 · Cidery / Meadery (`cider`)
**For:** a small orchard cidery or meadery with a barn shop or tasting room, a few seasonal open days, and a short list of dry-to-sweet bottlings sold direct and through local shops.
**Real-world basis:** [Farnum Hill Ciders: Ciders](https://farnumhillciders.com/ciders), [Farnum Hill Ciders: Growler Days](https://farnumhillciders.com/growler-days), [Albemarle CiderWorks: Harrison](https://www.albemarleciderworks.com/our-cider/cider-varieties/harrison), [Eve's Cidery: Visit & Taste](https://www.evescidery.com/tastings-eves-cidery/), [Beach Bee Meadery: Loyalty Clubs](https://www.beachbeemeadery.com/loyalty-clubs/)
**Templates:** front-page · archive-cider (Our Ciders) · single-cider (product) · page-orchard (Poverty Lane-style orchard history) · page-our-apples · page-seasonal-hours · page-growler-days · page-visit · page-where-to-buy · page-awards · Woo shop · page-private-events
**Patterns (~38):** cider spec block (ABV, dryness in words: "totally dry", "barely off-dry", apple varieties, still or sparkling), sold-out line on a bottling, apple variety note (history, first recorded, tannin and acid), orchard history timeline, seasonal hours table (Sept–Nov / Dec–Aug), growler day notice, self-serve barn shop note (21+, cash, card, check), shop-open header line ("Shop open Saturdays 11–1, other times by appointment"), directions paragraph with landmarks, large-group guidelines (8+), awards list in running text, loyalty tier table, stockists list.
**Content model:** Woo products with attributes `abv`, `dryness` (totally dry / off-dry / semi-sweet / sweet), `style` (sparkling / still / perry / mead), `varieties`; companion `variety` (name, history, first recorded, tannin, acidity, linked ciders); companion `event` with type `growler-day` / `open-day`.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce, Age Gate, Advanced Query Loop (next growler day, upcoming open days), Jetpack Newsletter (the date list), Jetpack Forms (private events and large groups).
**Signature:** a **Growler Day block**: the orchard opens on one Thursday or Saturday a month outside harvest, and the block shows the next date from the `event` CPT, the refill price per half-gallon, the price of a new glass growler, "bring your own half-gallon jug", dogs-on-leash note and payment methods, then a sign-up for the date emails. Past dates drop off by themselves through Advanced Query Loop. (seen on: [Farnum Hill Ciders: Growler Days](https://farnumhillciders.com/growler-days))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Variety pages that tell the apple's story (the Harrison apple, first praised in 1817, once thought lost) and link to every cider that uses it (seen on: [Albemarle CiderWorks: Harrison](https://www.albemarleciderworks.com/our-cider/cider-varieties/harrison))
- Seasonal hours that switch by date range: harvest-season days and the rest of the year, set once in the editor (seen on: [Albemarle CiderWorks](https://www.albemarleciderworks.com/))
- Honest "how to find us" copy for a barn with no sign: "after the bridge over Cayuta Creek, next on the left", with a photo of the gambrel roof (seen on: [Eve's Cidery: Visit & Taste](https://www.evescidery.com/tastings-eves-cidery/))
- Email-only loyalty tiers with plain rules: spend thresholds, points per dollar, tier held for this year and next (seen on: [Beach Bee Meadery: Loyalty Clubs](https://www.beachbeemeadery.com/loyalty-clubs/))
- Nursery or tree catalogue state: "closed, reopens in November", shown on the page and in the shop (seen on: [Albemarle CiderWorks](https://www.albemarleciderworks.com/))
**Style: Heritage label serif**
- Type: display Rufina 700 at 76–96px, tracking -0.01em, line-height 1.05; body Literata 400 at 18px (optical size on), line-height 1.6; labels Alegreya Sans SC 500 at 15px, +0.06em, used for ABV and dryness lines.
- Palette: #F5F1E6 bg (uncoated label paper, the physical reason for the warm ground) · #1E1A14 text · #2F4A2B accent (orchard green, links and buttons) · #B8862B secondary (perry gold, rules and the dryness scale marker) · #E7DFCB surface for the visit and hours blocks · #CFC4A8 line.
- Layout: centred label-style masthead only for the wordmark; everything below sits on a left-aligned 5/7 grid. Each cider is a flat "label" panel with a double rule border (1px + 3px gold) and square corners; the dryness line is a four-step printed scale with a gold tick, not a slider. Home order: next growler day or open day, current ciders, orchard story, where to buy. Footer holds address, seasonal hours and the 21+ line.
- Imagery: bottles shot straight on against barn boards; orchard rows at 3:2 in winter and at harvest; engraved-style apple cross-sections for variety pages, one hand-drawn set per site.
- Motion: none on load; the dryness tick slides to its place once when a cider page opens (transform, 200ms ease-out), inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
- Why it fits now: craft drinks are moving back to printed-label heritage cues (small caps, double rules, engraved fruit) as a sign of orchard provenance. [Oliver's Cider and Perry](https://oliversciderandperry.co.uk/)
**Style variations:** Kingston Black (deep #3B1F1A ground, paper type) · Perry Pear (pale #E9EBD2 ground, gold rules) · Apiary (honey #D9A441 labels, ink text)
**Refs:**
- [Farnum Hill Ciders: Growler Days](https://farnumhillciders.com/growler-days): monthly refill day with clear price, container and dog rules, and an email list for dates.
- [Farnum Hill Ciders: Ciders](https://farnumhillciders.com/ciders): dryness described in words, apple varieties, ABV and a sold-out reserve bottling.
- [Albemarle CiderWorks: Harrison](https://www.albemarleciderworks.com/our-cider/cider-varieties/harrison): a cider page built around one heirloom apple's history.

<a id="275"></a>
#### 275 · Seed Library / Seed Swap (`seedlib`)
**For:** a volunteer seed lending library housed in a public library or rec centre (one glass cabinet or several branches), running spring seed swaps and seed-saving classes, often bilingual.
**Real-world basis:** [Richmond Grows: Borrow Seeds](https://www.richmondgrowsseeds.org/borrow-seeds.html), [Richmond Grows: Donate Seeds](https://www.richmondgrowsseeds.org/donate-seeds.html), [Seed Library Network: Check Out](https://www.seedlibrarynetwork.org/check-out.html), [Garden Organic: How the Heritage Seed Library works](https://www.gardenorganic.org.uk/what-we-do/hsl/how-the-seed-library-works), [Toronto Seed Library](https://torontoseedlibrary.org/)
**Templates:** front-page · page-borrow-seeds · page-save-seeds · page-donate-seeds (return seeds) · archive-seed (seed list) · single-seed · page-library-finder (branches) · archive-event (classes & events, seed swaps) · page-new-gardeners · page-create-a-library · page-volunteer · page-espanol
**Patterns (~32):** "What's a seed lending library?" intro with the no-fines line, borrow / grow / return cycle (a real sequence, so numbered), seed drawer entry (crop, variety, year grown, saver, difficulty: super easy / easy / advanced), "start with super easy" beginner note (peas, beans, tomatoes, lettuce, arugula), return checklist (dry, clean, properly saved, label), "Crossed?" warning for brassicas, cucurbits, corn and sunflowers, printable envelope label, planting-times-by-month table, branch listing (location, contact, hours, how this branch works), seed swap event row, grow-a-row appeal, recommended books list.
**Content model:** companion `seed` (crop, variety, year grown, saved by, difficulty, pollination, drawer/branch, stock: plenty / low / out); taxonomies `crop family` and `difficulty`; companion `branch` (address, host, hours, notes); companion `event` for swaps and classes.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (checkout and return logs), Query Filter (by crop family, difficulty, branch), Advanced Query Loop (upcoming swaps), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (branches), Polylang (English and Spanish).
**Signature:** **phone checkout by QR code**: each drawer or jar gets a printable label with a QR code (generated by a small companion block) that opens a short Jetpack Form on the phone, already filled with that variety, so borrowers log what they took without a volunteer at the desk. The same form in "return" mode logs donated seed. Volunteers see borrow counts per variety in the form responses and set the stock flag by hand. (seen on: [Seed Library Network: Check Out](https://www.seedlibrarynetwork.org/check-out.html))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Printable envelope label PDF (common name, variety, year grown, where grown, saver) and a note to put spare labels in with returned seed (seen on: [Richmond Grows: Donate Seeds](https://www.richmondgrowsseeds.org/donate-seeds.html))
- "Seed list open until end of February, up to six packets" style season window, with a late-joiner note "while stocks last" (seen on: [Garden Organic: How the Heritage Seed Library works](https://www.gardenorganic.org.uk/what-we-do/hsl/how-the-seed-library-works))
- Branch list with an "updated" date and a per-branch note, because each branch runs slightly differently; also offered as a downloadable PDF (seen on: [Toronto Seed Library](https://torontoseedlibrary.org/))
- Plain-language Spanish pages that mirror every English page rather than one summary page (seen on: [Richmond Grows](https://www.richmondgrowsseeds.org/))
- Quantity guidance sign: take 2–3 seeds per plant you intend to grow, or a pinch of small seed (seen on: [Seed Library Network: Check Out](https://www.seedlibrarynetwork.org/check-out.html))
**Style: Card-catalogue Web 1.0 revival**
- Type: display Xanh Mono 400 at 72–88px, tracking 0, line-height 1.05; body Public Sans 400 at 18px, line-height 1.65; card fields and stamps Courier Prime 400/700 at 16px.
- Palette: #FFFFFF bg · #1B1B1B text · #F2E8C9 surface (manila catalogue card, the physical reason for the tint) · #0B6B3A accent (seed green, all links, underlined) · #C8102E date-stamp red (only for "out of stock" and closing dates) · #9FB4CF ruled line (the blue rule on an index card).
- Layout: a narrow single column (68ch) like a 1998 library page, with a left "drawer" index of crop families as a plain text list; each seed is a 3:5 index card with a red top rule, typed fields and a stamp area; cards sit in a two-column grid on desktop, one on mobile. No hero image: the home page opens with the borrow / grow / return steps and today's branch hours. Horizontal rules between sections, underlined links, visited links in a darker green.
- Imagery: scans of real seed packets and hand-written envelopes at 1:1 on white; black-and-white photos of the cabinet and drawers; botanical line drawings only if the library has them.
- Motion: none, apart from a 150ms colour change on link hover; the page works fully with JS off.
- Why it fits now: small community groups are turning to plain, fast, archival-looking pages that load on old phones and read like a well-kept index. [Cabinet: All issues](https://www.cabinetmagazine.org/issues/allissuesbycover.php)
**Style variations:** Manila (#F2E8C9 cards, green links) · Date Stamp (white ground, #C8102E stamps) · Drawer (oak #6B4A2B index, cream cards)
**Refs:**
- [Richmond Grows: Donate Seeds](https://www.richmondgrowsseeds.org/donate-seeds.html): return rules, printable envelope label and the "Crossed?" note, written for first-time savers.
- [Seed Library Network: Check Out](https://www.seedlibrarynetwork.org/check-out.html): self-serve versus staffed checkout, QR phone forms and per-household limits.
- [Garden Organic: How the Heritage Seed Library works](https://www.gardenorganic.org.uk/what-we-do/hsl/how-the-seed-library-works): a dated seed list with a choosing window and volunteer Seed Guardians.

<a id="276"></a>
#### 276 · Community Fridge (`fridge`)
**For:** a volunteer mutual-aid group running one to six outdoor fridges and pantries, open 24/7, with cleaning shifts, partner shops and small online donations.
**Real-world basis:** [ATX Free Fridge: Home](https://www.atxfreefridge.com/), [ATX Free Fridge: Cleaning](https://www.atxfreefridge.com/cleaning), [ATX Free Fridge: Support](https://www.atxfreefridge.com/support-atxff), [Germantown Community Fridges: FAQ](https://www.germantowncommunityfridge.com/faq), [Freedge: Freedge Yourself](https://freedge.org/freedge-yourself/)
**Templates:** front-page · archive-fridge (locations map) · single-fridge · page-access (how to use the fridges) · page-donate-food (guidelines) · page-cleaning · page-volunteer (get involved) · page-faq · page-other-resources · page-partners · page-start-a-fridge · page-espanol
**Patterns (~30):** "give what you can, take what you need" opening statement, fridge location entry (address, fridge + pantry, 24/7, photo of the actual fridge), access rules (no sign-up, take what you need today, close the door), YES list and NO list (all produce, dairy, labelled home-cooked meals / no raw meat except the freezer, no alcohol, no opened or unlabelled food), home-cooked label rule (dish name, ingredients and allergens, date made), eight-step cleaning checklist, hot-season cleaning note, partner businesses in running text, Open Collective donation line with "we will never ask for Venmo, PayPal or Zelle", wishlist links, other local resources list (211, food bank, pet food pantry), printable fridge-door poster.
**Content model:** companion `fridge` (address, host, has pantry, has freezer, shift sign-up URL, last cleaned date, photo); companion `resource` (name, type, link).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (cleaning log, volunteer and partner sign-up), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap, Polylang (English and Spanish). Donations go to the group's existing Open Collective page; no donation plugin.
**Signature:** a **per-fridge cleaning board**: every fridge on the map links straight to its own shift sign-up, and after a shift the volunteer ticks the eight-step checklist on a short phone form (discard unsafe items, wipe shelves, check the temperature, flatten boxes, and so on). The companion plugin writes the submission time to that fridge's "last cleaned" field, so the locations page shows "cleaned 2 days ago" beside each fridge and organisers can see which one needs help. (seen on: [ATX Free Fridge: Cleaning](https://www.atxfreefridge.com/cleaning))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Printable A4 fridge-door poster with the YES / NO lists and the label rule, in English and Spanish, generated from the same content as the web page (seen on: [Germantown Community Fridges: FAQ](https://www.germantowncommunityfridge.com/faq))
- Seasonal notice for May to September: clean in the early morning or evening, and bring your own bag if the site has no dumpster (seen on: [ATX Free Fridge: Cleaning](https://www.atxfreefridge.com/cleaning))
- Scam warning next to every donate link: the only channel is Open Collective, never Venmo, PayPal or Zelle (seen on: [ATX Free Fridge: Support](https://www.atxfreefridge.com/support-atxff))
- Other-resources page for when the fridge is empty: 211 helpline, local mutual aid, food programme, pet food pantry (seen on: [Germantown Community Fridges: FAQ](https://www.germantowncommunityfridge.com/faq))
- "Start a fridge" toolkit page linking food-safety protocol, liability notes and host flyers (seen on: [Freedge: Freedge Yourself](https://freedge.org/freedge-yourself/))
**Style: Protest poster Swiss**
- Type: display Days One 400 at 96–140px uppercase, tracking 0, line-height 0.95, used only for page titles and YES / NO; body Hanken Grotesk 400 at 19px, line-height 1.55; addresses and times Red Hat Mono 500 at 16px.
- Palette: #FFFFFF bg (appliance enamel) · #0F0F0F text · #FFD400 accent field (safety yellow, the donate and sign-up bands, black type on it) · #1E7B47 YES green · #C4231C NO red (both only on the rules lists, always with the word) · #E6E6E1 line.
- Layout: strict 6-column Swiss grid, flush-left, 0 radius everywhere, heavy 4px black rules between sections. The home page is a poster: the rule line in huge type, then the fridge list as a typeset table (name, street, fridge / pantry / freezer, last cleaned) beside the map on desktop and above it on mobile. YES and NO lists run as two full-height columns. Footer: email, Instagram, Open Collective, language switch.
- Imagery: plain phone photos of each actual fridge, painted and stickered, cropped 4:5 and set in black-and-white halftone; no stock food photography.
- Motion: none by default; the language switch uses a View Transition cross-fade of 150ms inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
- Why it fits now: campaign and mutual-aid groups have moved to flat, loud, poster-grid sites built from big statements and real photos, which print well as door posters too. [Extinction Rebellion UK](https://extinctionrebellion.uk/)
**Style variations:** Enamel (white ground, #FFD400 bands) · Fridge Magnet (#1E7B47 ground, white type) · Night Shift (#0F0F0F ground, #FFD400 type)
**Refs:**
- [ATX Free Fridge: Cleaning](https://www.atxfreefridge.com/cleaning): per-fridge shift sign-up, eight-step cleaning checklist and the summer timing note.
- [ATX Free Fridge: Support](https://www.atxfreefridge.com/support-atxff): yes / no donation rules, label requirements and the payment scam warning.
- [Germantown Community Fridges: FAQ](https://www.germantowncommunityfridge.com/faq): plain answers on what can go in, 24/7 access and where else to find food.

<a id="277"></a>
#### 277 · Darkroom / Print Co-op (`darkroom`)
**For:** community darkrooms and photo co-ops that rent enlarger time by the hour, run memberships and classes, and process film over the counter.
**Real-world basis:** [Gowanus Darkroom: Reserve](https://www.gowanusdarkroom.com/reserve), [Gowanus Darkroom: Prices](https://www.gowanusdarkroom.com/prices), [Gowanus Darkroom: Membership](https://www.gowanusdarkroom.com/membership), [Photofusion: Become a member](https://shop.photofusion.org/pages/become-a-member), [Darkroom Co-op Austin: Join](https://www.darkroomcoop.net/join.html)
**Templates:** front-page · page-prices · page-reserve · page-membership · page-partial-membership · archive-class (basics workshops, alternative processes, private lessons) · page-drop-off · page-mail-in · page-artist-in-residence · page-faq · page-gift-cards · page-teachers
**Patterns (~40):** price list by service (B&W darkroom $15/hour, colour $18/hour, 8×10 enlarger $20/hour, 35mm processing $10/roll, 4×5 $5/sheet with 4-sheet minimum), hourly reservation with deposit, "one person per slot" and "washing and drying counts as your time" rules, membership terms (monthly fee, minimum commitment, one-hour orientation with fee), membership application form, discount membership line for students and unwaged, class list with dates and places left, teacher bios, drop-off steps (fill in the form, put it in the box, invoice by email, pick up when notified), turnaround notice ("up to one week"), mail-in processing, artist residency call, gift cards and bundles, opening hours.
**Content model:** `equipment` (enlarger, format, colour/B&W, hourly rate); `class` via Event Tickets; `teacher` (bio, processes taught); `residency_call` (deadline, brief).
**Plugins:** Simply Schedule Appointments (hourly darkroom slots with a deposit via its Woo/Stripe payment option) or Cal.com embed, WooCommerce + Subscriptions for WooCommerce (memberships, gift cards, chemistry and paper), The Events Calendar + Event Tickets (classes), Jetpack Forms (membership application, drop-off form).
**Signature:** **hourly darkroom booking with a deposit that counts towards the session.** Customers book a timed slot per room (B&W, colour, large format). A deposit is taken at booking and deducted from the hourly total. The page states the house rules next to the calendar: one person per slot, and washing and drying time is part of your booking. (seen on: [Gowanus Darkroom: Reserve](https://www.gowanusdarkroom.com/reserve))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- "Membership closed until October" state that swaps the join form for a waitlist form (seen on: [Gowanus Darkroom: Membership](https://www.gowanusdarkroom.com/membership))
- Cancellation rule in one line ("a $10 fee for cancellations within 3 hours of the start") printed on the confirmation email (seen on: [Gowanus Darkroom: Reserve](https://www.gowanusdarkroom.com/reserve))
- Printable A4 price list for the door, generated from the same price table as the site (seen on: [Gowanus Darkroom: Drop-off](https://www.gowanusdarkroom.com/drop-off), which points to "the price list at our door")
- Concession membership priced per day ("£85 a year, 23p a day; £40 for students, pensioners and unwaged") (seen on: [Photofusion: Become a member](https://shop.photofusion.org/pages/become-a-member))
- Member board: each member's photo and name on a "who's in the co-op" page, from the join requirement for a 4×6 portrait (seen on: [Darkroom Co-op Austin: Join](https://www.darkroomcoop.net/join.html))
**Style: Contact-sheet mono (1-bit photographic)**
- Type: headings Kode Mono 700 at 72–112px, set like frame numbers on a film edge; body Karla 400/18px; prices, formats and times in Kode Mono 400.
- Palette: fixer white #FAFAF8 (bg), silver-gelatin black #0E0E0E (text), safelight red #B3261E (accent: "Reserve" and the one open-slot marker), grey card #8C8C8C (rules; 18% grey, the photographer's reference), selenium grey #D6D4D0 (surfaces).
- Layout: pages set as contact sheets: a strict grid of 3:2 frames with frame numbers and a grease-pencil circle (SVG) marking the chosen image; the price list is a plain two-column table; the reservation calendar sits on a black band like the inside of the darkroom; radius 0 everywhere.
- Imagery: members' own black-and-white prints, scanned with the paper border; film-rebate edges kept on photos; no colour photography except on the colour darkroom page.
- Motion: none. A "safelight" style variation swaps to red-on-black for use inside the darkroom; there are no animations to disable.
- Why it fits now: analogue photography is growing with younger members, and the contact sheet is the format they know from the archive, e.g. [Magnum Photos](https://www.magnumphotos.com/).
**Style variations:** Safelight (black #0E0E0E bg, red #B3261E type) · Cyanotype (Prussian blue #1D3F73 bg, white type) · Fibre Print (warm white #F4F2EC, deep black headings)
**Refs:**
- [Gowanus Darkroom: Prices](https://www.gowanusdarkroom.com/prices): a darkroom price list done right, with rooms, formats and processing in one plain table.
- [Gowanus Darkroom: Reserve](https://www.gowanusdarkroom.com/reserve): deposit, slot rules and cancellation fee next to the booking calendar.
- [Photofusion: Become a member](https://shop.photofusion.org/pages/become-a-member): two honest membership tiers with a concession rate and the member discounts listed.

#### 278 · Dark-Sky Park / Observatory Visits (`darksky`)
**For:** public observatories, dark-sky parks and astronomy societies that sell tickets to evening observing sessions.
**Real-world basis:** [Kielder Observatory: Which event?](https://www.kielderobservatory.org/our-events/which-event), [Kielder Observatory: Event FAQs](https://www.kielderobservatory.org/events/faqs), [Kielder Observatory: What's up September 2026](https://www.kielderobservatory.org/news/latest-news/507-what-s-up-september-2026), [Appalachian State Dark Sky Observatory: Public access](https://dso.appstate.edu/public-access/), [Mayland Earth to Sky Park](https://www.mayland.edu/foundation/foundation-projects/earth-to-sky-park/)
**Templates:** front-page · archive-event (main / weekend late night / family / specialist) · single-event · page-which-event · page-when-you-arrive · page-faqs · page-private-events · page-places-to-stay · archive-post (monthly sky guide, news) · page-equipment · page-gift-vouchers · page-donate · page-education
**Patterns (~40):** event list with category, age guidance and seats left, "which event?" guide by category, event page with the 45-minute talk topic (Aurora Night, Origins of the Universe), cloudy-night policy ("sessions go ahead in most weather; if cloudy, talks and a tour instead"), what to wear (layers, low-heeled shoes, domes are not heated), arrival instructions (arrive 15 minutes early, 15mph access track, wait in your car), grounds vs telescopes (car park open 24 hours; telescopes only at ticketed events), accessibility details (level access, two accessible telescope rooms, one turret has six steps, car park 80m on an unsealed surface), monthly sky guide (constellations, planets and Moon, deep-sky objects), equipment page (telescope apertures), private events enquiry, places to stay nearby, gift vouchers, donate, podcast.
**Content model:** companion `event` (category, age guidance, talk topic, start time, moon phase); `telescope` (aperture, type, dome/turret, accessible yes/no); `sky_guide` posts with image descriptions required.
**Plugins:** The Events Calendar + Event Tickets (ticketed sessions, family tickets), WooCommerce (gift vouchers, shop), Jetpack Forms (private events, school visits).
**Signature:** **a "which event?" chooser.** Sessions are filed under four colour-coded categories (main, weekend late night, family, specialist), each with age guidance and what makes it different (the subject of the 45-minute talk). The chooser leads straight to the matching dates. (seen on: [Kielder Observatory: Which event?](https://www.kielderobservatory.org/our-events/which-event))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Cloudy-night policy shown on every event page, with the refund or rebook voucher rule and "self-cancel for a voucher up to 7 days before" (seen on: [Kielder Observatory: Event FAQs](https://www.kielderobservatory.org/events/faqs))
- "When you arrive" page with night-driving directions, car park photos and the arrival window (seen on: [Kielder Observatory: Event FAQs](https://www.kielderobservatory.org/events/faqs) and [DSO: Public access](https://dso.appstate.edu/public-access/))
- Access facts in numbers (steps, distances, surfaces, drop-off by arrangement) rather than a wheelchair icon (seen on: [Kielder Observatory: Event FAQs](https://www.kielderobservatory.org/events/faqs))
- Monthly "What's up" sky guide with star charts and image descriptions, which doubles as the newsletter (seen on: [Kielder Observatory: What's up September 2026](https://www.kielderobservatory.org/news/latest-news/507-what-s-up-september-2026))
- Will-call list for visitors who cannot print tickets (seen on: [DSO: Public access](https://dso.appstate.edu/public-access/))
**Style: Scientific dark index**
- Type: headings Jura 700 at 80–128px; body Source Serif 4 400/18px for the sky guides; coordinates, times and apertures in Red Hat Mono 500 (RA 18h 36m, Dec +38° 47′).
- Palette: night #0B0F14 (bg; justified because pages are read outdoors at night), star white #E9ECEF (text, 15:1), red-light #C8372D (accent: "Book", and the red night-mode variation), slate #2A323C (surfaces), chart line #56606B (rules, used only for chart grids with real data).
- Layout: the event list is a dated table (date · category · talk · age · seats) with the category as a coloured text label, not a dot; sky guide articles use a 7/5 split with charts in the wide column and notes in the margin; practical info (arrival, clothing, access) as one long visible page with h3 questions, no accordions.
- Imagery: members' astrophotos at native crop with exposure data captions, Stellarium charts exported in the site palette, one daytime photo of the building for finding it.
- Motion: none on scroll; a "red light mode" toggle (Interactivity API) switches the palette to red on black for use at the telescope, respecting `prefers-reduced-motion` for the switch.
- Why it fits now: observatories and space agencies now publish image-first dark sites where the photograph carries the page, e.g. [ESO: public site](https://www.eso.org/public/).
**Style variations:** Red Light (black bg, #C8372D type only) · Daylight Planetarium (white #FFFFFF bg, night-blue #0B2A4A headings) · Star Chart (paper #F2F1EC, fine black chart lines)
**Refs:**
- [Kielder Observatory: Which event?](https://www.kielderobservatory.org/our-events/which-event): a guided choice between event types with ages and talk subjects.
- [Kielder Observatory: Event FAQs](https://www.kielderobservatory.org/events/faqs): cloudy nights, clothing, arrival and access written for people who have never been to an observatory.
- [Appalachian State Dark Sky Observatory: Public access](https://dso.appstate.edu/public-access/): a short, practical visitor page with the indoor plan for cloudy nights.

<a id="279"></a>
#### 279 · Citizen Science Project (`observe`)
**For:** small volunteer-led monitoring projects (river invertebrates, bees, ladybirds, rain gauges, amphibian crossings) run by a researcher, a trust or a local group.
**Real-world basis:** [Lost Ladybug Project: Participate](http://www.lostladybug.org/participate.php), [Riverfly Partnership: Data (Cartographer)](https://www.riverflies.org/cartographer), [Riverfly Partnership: Get involved](https://www.riverflies.org/get-involved), [BeeWalk: Resources](https://www.beewalk.org.uk/resources), [Green Valleys Watershed Association: Volunteer monitoring](https://greenvalleys.org/volunteer-monitoring-programs/)
**Templates:** front-page · page-participate (how to take part) · page-how-to · page-identification-tools · page-upload (submission form) · page-data (map and downloads) · page-resources · archive-post (news and monthly newsletters) · page-annual-summary · page-kids · page-faqs · page-about
**Patterns (~40):** "why we need you" statement, three-step participation (find, photograph, send), submission form (photos, date, time, location, habitat), quick tips ("zeros are useful data"), identification tools and A4 ID guides (PDF), printable recording forms (monthly form, site details form), photography guide for identifiable photos, health and safety guidance, recent submissions map colour-coded by area, open data link and download, monthly and annual reports, programme cards for each volunteer track (rain gauge, water stewards, amphibian patrol, nest boxes) with time commitment and training, find a local group or coordinator, kids' page, English/Spanish switch.
**Content model:** `observation` (date, time, lat/long, habitat, species or reading, photos, observer, status: submitted / verified), `programme` (training, time commitment, kit, where the data goes), `resource` (PDF, type: ID guide / form / manual).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (submissions with photo upload into pending `observation` posts), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (sites and recent records), Query Filter (records by species, area, month), Polylang (second language).
**Signature:** **a map of the last month's verified records, colour-coded by area, with an open data link.** Every verified submission appears on a public map for 30 days, grouped by catchment or county, and the full dataset is downloadable as CSV with a licence note. (seen on: [Riverfly Partnership: Data (Cartographer)](https://www.riverflies.org/cartographer))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- "Zeros are useful data" tip plus a "found nothing" option on the form, so empty surveys get recorded (seen on: [Lost Ladybug Project: Participate](http://www.lostladybug.org/participate.php))
- Resources page with printable A4 ID guides, recording forms and a photography guide (seen on: [BeeWalk: Resources](https://www.beewalk.org.uk/resources))
- Programme cards that state the time commitment honestly ("an hour or two of amphibian patrol on migration nights") (seen on: [Green Valleys: Volunteer monitoring](https://greenvalleys.org/volunteer-monitoring-programs/))
- "No experience necessary, full training provided" with a find-your-coordinator form (seen on: [Riverfly Partnership: Get involved](https://www.riverflies.org/get-involved))
- English/Spanish language switch on participation pages (seen on: [Lost Ladybug Project: Participate](http://www.lostladybug.org/participate.php))
**Style: Data-journalism monospace**
- Type: headings Hind 700 at 72–104px; body Literata 400/18px for explanations; data labels, counts and coordinates in JetBrains Mono 500.
- Palette: survey white #FFFFFF (bg), ink #15191C (text), river teal #0F6E6E (accent: "Submit a record", map points), field khaki #CFC8B0 (surfaces for forms), rule grey #9AA3A8 (chart axes), alert amber #B86E00 (only for "unverified" labels).
- Layout: long single-column explainers at 68ch with full-bleed maps and charts breaking out; the data page leads with the map, then a plain table of recent records; resources as a document list (title · type · size · PDF), no card grid.
- Imagery: volunteers' own field photos with date and place in the caption; specimen photos on a plain white card with a scale bar; no stock nature imagery.
- Motion: charts and maps are static SVG/tiles; filter changes use a short View Transition; everything visible with JS off.
- Why it fits now: people now trust data they can see and download, and the explanatory data-story style is how that is presented today, e.g. [The Pudding](https://pudding.cool/).
**Style variations:** Field Notebook (khaki #E9E4D2 bg, pencil-grey type) · River (teal #0F6E6E header band, white type) · Lab Sheet (white, black-only with amber flags)
**Refs:**
- [Riverfly Partnership: Data (Cartographer)](https://www.riverflies.org/cartographer): recent records mapped by catchment plus open access to the full dataset.
- [BeeWalk: Resources](https://www.beewalk.org.uk/resources): the resource set a small survey needs, from ID sheets to recording forms and a safety note.
- [Lost Ladybug Project: Participate](http://www.lostladybug.org/participate.php): a three-step "find, photograph, send" flow with the data fields listed in plain words.

<a id="280"></a>
#### 280 · Death Doula / End-of-Life Planning (`threshold`)
**For:** independent end-of-life doulas and planners who offer free first calls, session packages, planning guides and local Death Cafés.
**Real-world basis:** [Peaceful End of Life](https://www.peacefulendoflife.com/), [Dying Your Way: Book a consultation](https://dyingyourway.com/book-a-consultation/), [Dying Your Way: End-of-life plan](https://dyingyourway.com/end-of-life-plan/), [Death Cafe: What is Death Cafe](https://deathcafe.com/)
**Templates:** front-page · page-about · page-services (doula support, patient advocacy, advance planning) · page-book-a-consultation · page-fees · page-free-guides · page-resources · archive-post (articles) · page-death-cafe · page-testimonials · page-contact
**Patterns (~30):** three entry paths by situation (recently diagnosed / caring for someone / planning ahead), each with a free guide ("25 questions to ask", caregivers' guide, end-of-life planning guide), services list (doula support, patient advocacy, vigil support, advance planning), free 30-minute consultation booking, fees list (single session, 5- and 12-session packages, monthly on-call), service area ("virtual nationwide, in person around Sherman/Denison"), about the doula with training and years of practice, resources list (advance directives, funeral options, grief support), articles, Death Café dates with the host's approach, testimonials as quotations with context, podcast episodes.
**Content model:** `guide` (situation, PDF, email-gated yes/no); `service`; companion `event` for Death Cafés; posts for articles.
**Plugins:** Cal.com embed (free consultation), Jetpack Forms (guide requests and contact), Jetpack Newsletter (guides by email), The Events Calendar (Death Cafés, optional).
**Signature:** **three situation-based entry paths on the front page.** Visitors pick "I have just been diagnosed", "someone I care for is changing" or "I want to make my wishes clear", and each path leads to a matching free guide and then to a free consultation. (seen on: [Peaceful End of Life](https://www.peacefulendoflife.com/))
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Fees written out in full, with the free 30-minute call first and packages after (seen on: [Dying Your Way: Book a consultation](https://dyingyourway.com/book-a-consultation/))
- "What happens in the first call" paragraph beside the booking embed (seen on: [Dying Your Way: Book a consultation](https://dyingyourway.com/book-a-consultation/))
- Service-area line (online nationally, in person locally) set once and shown in the footer and on the booking page (seen on: [Peaceful End of Life](https://www.peacefulendoflife.com/))
- Death Café listing with date, time, cost ("free, donations welcome") and a link to the official listing (seen on: [Death Cafe](https://deathcafe.com/))
- Out-of-hours crisis and hospice numbers in the footer, and a "currently accepting new clients: yes / no" setting
**Style: Quiet editorial serif, warm**
- Type: headings Gupter 500 at 80–112px with generous line-height (1.1); body Libre Caslon Text 400/19px at 66ch; small meta (fees, times) in Libre Caslon Text italic, not caps.
- Palette: linen grey-white #F5F5F2 (bg), ink #22201E (text, 15:1), moss #4E5B45 (accent: "Book a free call" and links), stone #D9D6CF (rules), soft shadow grey #6B6862 (secondary text, 5.5:1).
- Layout: one reading column with wide left margin for small notes; the three entry paths are set as three short paragraphs with links, not cards; fees as a two-column price list; no hero image, the first thing on the page is one sentence in the doula's own words.
- Imagery: few photos: the doula's portrait in daylight, hands and objects from vigils (candles, blankets) with permission; no stock sunsets or butterflies.
- Motion: none. Content is static and calm by design.
- Why it fits now: the death-positive movement writes openly and plainly about dying, and its sites read like essays rather than service pages, e.g. [The Order of the Good Death](https://www.orderofthegooddeath.com/).
**Style variations:** Vigil (ink #22201E bg, warm white type) · Linen (white #FFFFFF, moss headings) · Garden (pale sage #E3E7DD bg, ink type)
**Refs:**
- [Peaceful End of Life](https://www.peacefulendoflife.com/): situation-based entry paths that lead to a guide and a free call.
- [Dying Your Way: Book a consultation](https://dyingyourway.com/book-a-consultation/): a transparent fee list with the free call first.
- [Death Cafe: What is Death Cafe](https://deathcafe.com/): the format and listing details to reuse for local Death Café events.

<a id="281"></a>
#### 281 · Literary Magazine (`lit`)
**For:** small print-and-web literary magazines (two to six editors, two issues a year) that publish fiction, poetry, essays and reviews, run open submission windows and live on subscriptions and stockists.
**Templates:** front-page (current issue) · archive-issue · single-issue (table of contents) · single (piece) · taxonomy-section (Fiction / Poetry / Essays / Reviews) · page-submissions · page-subscribe · page-stockists · page-about · 404
**Patterns (~45):** current-issue cover block with price and "buy this issue", issue table of contents grouped by section with author and first line, piece header (section, issue number, author, translator), contributor note, "from the print issue" / "web only" label, submissions window block (open or closed, categories, fees, payment rates per page), stockist list by country and city, library subscription note, gift subscription, back-issues grid, prize announcement, podcast episode row, newsletter sign-up.
**Content model:** `issue` CPT (number, season, year, price, cover, buy URL, in-print flag) with pieces as posts linked by `issue_id` meta; `section` taxonomy; `contributor` taxonomy with bio term meta; `stockist` CPT (name, city, country, URL). All bound to blocks with Block Bindings.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce (single issues, back issues), Subscriptions for WooCommerce, Jetpack Newsletter.
**Signature:** the issue page as a real table of contents: pieces grouped by section, each with author, opening line and a link to its own page, so an issue reads like the printed contents spread and every piece still has a permanent URL (seen on: [n+1: Issue 54](https://www.nplusonemag.com/issue-54/)). Built with a Query Loop filtered by `issue_id` and grouped by `section`.
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Submissions state block with open and close dates that flips its own copy from "Open until 31 May" to "Closed. Next window announced here", plus payment rates in a plain table (seen on: [The Stinging Fly: Submissions](https://stingingfly.org/submissions/))
- Stockist list grouped by country and state, printable for bookshop buyers (seen on: [n+1: Bookstores](https://www.nplusonemag.com/bookstores/))
- Library and institutional subscription page with invoice-friendly wording (seen on: [n+1: Libraries](https://www.nplusonemag.com/libraries/))
- Gift subscription product with a "start from next issue / current issue" choice and a gift note field
- Article schema.org on every piece and an OG image pattern that sets the issue cover and piece title in the magazine's type

**Style: Editorial serif revival**
- Type: headings Ibarra Real Nova 600, set large with normal tracking; body Ibarra Real Nova 400/19px, 1.55 line-height, 68ch measure; labels and section names Figtree 600 at 14px, sentence case.
- Palette: bg #F7F6F2 (uncoated paper white, cool) / text #1B1B1B / accent #9E1B32 (issue-number red, used only for section names and links) / surface #ECEAE3 / line #C9C5BA.
- Layout: 12-column grid with a narrow left margin column for section names and footnote numbers; pieces sit on columns 4–10. Home is the current issue: cover image left at 5 columns, the full contents list right. Nav is a single text row: Current issue · Archive · Submit · Subscribe. Hairline rules separate sections; corners stay square and content sits directly on the page.
- Imagery: covers shown flat at 3:4, no mock-up tilt; artist pages from the issue shown full-bleed with a caption line underneath, never cropped.
- Motion: none on scroll. Links underline on hover with a 120ms colour change; the contents list uses a View Transition when moving from issue to piece so the title lands in place. Reduced motion removes the transition.
- Why it fits now: independent magazines are moving back to reading-first sites with real contents pages after years of feed layouts, as on [The White Review](https://www.thewhitereview.org/).
**Style variations:** Winter issue: #EEF0F2 bg, slate-blue #2F4A6B accent · Proof: #FFFFFF bg, black text, red corrections · Night reading: #16181B bg, #E9E4D8 text.
**Real-world basis:** [n+1: Issue 54](https://www.nplusonemag.com/issue-54/), [The White Review: Issue No. 33](https://www.thewhitereview.org/issue/issue-no-33/), [The Stinging Fly: Submissions](https://stingingfly.org/submissions/), [n+1: Bookstores](https://www.nplusonemag.com/bookstores/), [n+1: Libraries](https://www.nplusonemag.com/libraries/)
**Refs:**
- [n+1: Issue 54](https://www.nplusonemag.com/issue-54/): contents grouped by section with author and opening lines; the model for `single-issue`.
- [The Stinging Fly: Submissions](https://stingingfly.org/submissions/): an honest closed-window notice, category rules and per-page payment rates.
- [The White Review: Issue No. 33](https://www.thewhitereview.org/issue/issue-no-33/): issue page that lists fiction, poetry, essays and artists with price and buy link.

<a id="282"></a>
#### 282 · Poet (`verse`)
**For:** working poets with one to five collections who give readings, teach, and need a place for poems published elsewhere, their books and their dates.
**Templates:** front-page · page-poems (published online) · archive-book · single-book · page-readings (upcoming and past) · page-prose · page-about · page-contact
**Patterns (~30):** selected poems list (title, magazine, year, external link), book entry (cover, publisher, year, prize shortlistings, press quotes, buy links), readings list (date, venue, city, "sold out", ticket link), past readings archive, prose and essays list, bio in short and long versions, contact split by purpose (readings, press, rights), audio track or recorded reading embed, newsletter.
**Content model:** `book` CPT (publisher, year, ISBN, prizes, buy links); `appearance` CPT (date, venue, city, ticket URL, status); "published elsewhere" list as a `link` post format with `venue` and `year` meta.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (upcoming vs past readings).
**Signature:** a "Poems" page that is a plain list of poems published online, each linking out to the magazine or newspaper where it first appeared, so the site sends readers to the poem's home instead of copying it (seen on: [Jericho Brown](https://www.jerichobrown.com/) and [Ross Gay: Writing](https://www.rossgay.net/writing)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- "Sold out" and "On sale 3 March" states on readings, with past dates moving to an archive page on their own (seen on: [Hollie McNish: Live dates](https://www.holliepoetry.com/livedates))
- Separate emails for readings, media and general post so bookers reach the right person (seen on: [Jericho Brown](https://www.jerichobrown.com/))
- Book page with prize shortlistings and two press quotes above the buy link (seen on: [Raymond Antrobus: Signs, Music](https://raymondantrobus.com/portfolio/signs-music/))
- Downloadable bio (50 words and 150 words) and author photo with credit, for festival programmes
- Line-break-safe poem template: preformatted whitespace preserved, no justified text, hanging indents kept on mobile

**Style: Web 1.0 revival (plain HTML poetry)**
- Type: everything in Radley 400/19px with italic for titles; headings are the same face at 28px, no second family except IBM Plex Mono 400/14px for dates.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #111111 / link #0000CC (unvisited) / visited #551A8B / rule #999999.
- Layout: one column, 36em wide, left-aligned, no header image. Nav is a line of text links at the top separated by middle dots. Home is the poet's name, one sentence, the next three readings and the newest book. Default-looking `<hr>`s, styled deliberately thin.
- Imagery: book covers at 180px wide, inline with text; one black-and-white author photo on the About page only.
- Motion: none. Visited-link colours are part of the design. Nothing to reduce.
- Why it fits now: poets and net artists are returning to hand-made HTML-looking pages that load instantly and last, as on [Olia Lialina's art.teleportacia.org](https://art.teleportacia.org/).
**Style variations:** Typescript: IBM Plex Mono throughout, #FAFAF7 bg · Chapbook: #F2EEE6 bg, oxblood #6B1E1E links · Blackout: #000000 bg, #F0F0F0 text.
**Real-world basis:** [Jericho Brown](https://www.jerichobrown.com/), [Ross Gay: Writing](https://www.rossgay.net/writing), [Ada Limón: Calendar](https://adalimon.com/calendar), [Hollie McNish: Live dates](https://www.holliepoetry.com/livedates), [Raymond Antrobus: Signs, Music](https://raymondantrobus.com/portfolio/signs-music/)
**Refs:**
- [Ross Gay: Writing](https://www.rossgay.net/writing): selected poems and essays as outbound links to where they were published, plus audio tracks.
- [Hollie McNish: Live dates](https://www.holliepoetry.com/livedates): a long readings list with clear SOLD OUT flags and "on sale" dates.
- [Ada Limón: Calendar](https://adalimon.com/calendar): short upcoming list with a separate past-events page.

<a id="283"></a>
#### 283 · Small Press Publisher (`imprint`)
**For:** independent presses publishing six to twenty titles a year (fiction, translation, poetry, essays) that sell direct, run reader subscriptions and deal with booksellers and rights buyers.
**Templates:** front-page · Woo shop · single-product (book) · archive-author · page-subscriptions · page-forthcoming · page-rights · page-booksellers · page-submissions · page-about
**Patterns (~50):** book page header (title, author, translator, format, pages, price, publication date), extract block, review quotes, ebook and audiobook retailer row, forthcoming list with publication dates, pre-order shipping note, subscription tiers (3 or 6 print books, ebook option), subscriber thank-you list, foreign rights contact, booksellers and distributors panel, catalogue PDF download, reading groups page, submissions policy.
**Content model:** Woo products with attributes (format, pages, ISBN, translator, publication date, series); `author` CPT linked to products; `catalogue` media item bound to a download button.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce, Subscriptions for WooCommerce, Advanced Query Loop (forthcoming vs published).
**Signature:** reader subscriptions where books ship before publication and subscribers are thanked by name in the back of the books they paid for; the site lists tiers and says how long the first book takes to arrive (seen on: [And Other Stories: Subscriptions](https://www.andotherstories.org/subscriptions/)). A companion block prints the subscriber list for a title from Woo subscription data.
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Pre-order note that says mixed orders ship together after the latest publication date (seen on: [Silver Press: Pre-orders](https://www.silverpress.org/collections/pre-orders))
- Booksellers page with UK and US distributor contacts in two lines (seen on: [Peninsula Press: Information for booksellers](https://peninsulapress.co.uk/pages/information-for-booksellers))
- Long extract on every book page, before the reviews (seen on: [Fitzcarraldo Editions: Helen of Nowhere](https://fitzcarraldoeditions.com/books/helen-of-nowhere/))
- Seasonal catalogue as a PDF download for bookshops and rights fairs
- Product and Book schema.org with ISBN so titles show properly in search

**Style: Swiss neo-grotesk index (catalogue numbers)**
- Type: headings Proza Libre 600, 40–72px, normal tracking; body Source Serif 4 400/18px for extracts; catalogue numbers and specs IBM Plex Mono 500/14px ("FE 214 · 160 pp · £12.99").
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #111111 / accent #1F3FA8 (single spot blue used for the series colour and links) / surface #F1F1EF / line #111111.
- Layout: strict 8-column grid, 1px black rules between rows; the shop is a numbered list (catalogue number, title, author, format, price) with a toggle to a covers grid. Home opens on the newest title's cover at half width with its catalogue line, then the forthcoming list. Nav is left-aligned text. Radius 0 everywhere.
- Imagery: flat cover scans at true proportion on white; author photos in black and white, 4:5, same size every time.
- Motion: list rows highlight in the accent blue on hover; the list/grid toggle uses a View Transition. No scroll animation.
- Why it fits now: small presses win shelf recognition with one typographic system across covers and site, as on [Fitzcarraldo Editions](https://fitzcarraldoeditions.com/).
**Style variations:** Fiction: #1F3FA8 blue · Essays: #FFFFFF bg with #111111 only · Poetry: #F3EFE6 bg, #7A1E1E accent.
**Real-world basis:** [And Other Stories: Subscriptions](https://www.andotherstories.org/subscriptions/), [Fitzcarraldo Editions: Helen of Nowhere](https://fitzcarraldoeditions.com/books/helen-of-nowhere/), [Silver Press: Pre-orders](https://www.silverpress.org/collections/pre-orders), [Peninsula Press: Information for booksellers](https://peninsulapress.co.uk/pages/information-for-booksellers), [Wave Books: Subscriptions](https://www.wavepoetry.com/collections/subscriptions)
**Refs:**
- [And Other Stories: Subscriptions](https://www.andotherstories.org/subscriptions/): subscription tiers, the "thanked by name" promise and an honest wait time.
- [Fitzcarraldo Editions: Helen of Nowhere](https://fitzcarraldoeditions.com/books/helen-of-nowhere/): book page order of format details, formats, extract, then reviews.
- [Silver Press: Pre-orders](https://www.silverpress.org/collections/pre-orders): a pre-order collection with a clear combined-shipping rule.
