#### 284 · Zine Library / Zine Fest (`zinefest`)
**For:** volunteer-run zine shops, libraries and annual zine fests that stock zines on consignment, run photocopiers and workshops, and publish an exhibitor list with table numbers.
**Templates:** front-page · page-fest (this year) · page-exhibitors · page-apply · page-stock-with-us · page-photocopying · page-workshops · page-safer-spaces · archive-post (news) · page-past-fests
**Patterns (~40):** fest date and venue block, exhibitor directory with table numbers and hall, table map image, youth exhibitors section, application with deadline and fee, consignment terms (copies taken, commission, payout timing), photocopier price table (A4/A3, B&W/colour, member rate), opening hours, workshop menu with what is provided, how-to-make-a-zine guide, safer spaces policy, volunteer call, poster artist credit, past fests archive.
**Content model:** `exhibitor` CPT (name, table, hall, URL, description, year taxonomy); `workshop` CPT; posts for news. Year taxonomy drives the archive.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (applications, stockist forms), Query Filter (exhibitors by hall and year), WooCommerce optional for a small zine shop.
**Signature:** an exhibitor directory listing every table number, hall, name, link and a short description, with table maps for each hall and a note that numbers can change before the fest (seen on: [Chicago Zine Fest: 2026 exhibitors](https://www.chicagozinefest.org/czf-2026-exhibitors.html)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Photocopier price list with member and non-member rates and paper rules ("bring your own, sealed, max 300gsm") (seen on: [Sticky Institute: Photocopying](https://stickyinstitute.com/photocopying))
- Consignment terms in plain numbers: up to 10 copies, 20% commission, paid when sold out or after six months (seen on: [Sticky Institute: Stock with us](https://stickyinstitute.com/stock-with-us))
- Safer spaces policy linked from the footer and the application form (seen on: [Chicago Zine Fest: Safer spaces](https://www.chicagozinefest.org/safer-spaces-policy.html))
- Workshop menu for schools and festivals with "all materials provided" and group size limits (seen on: [L.A. Zine Fest: Workshops](https://www.lazinefest.com/workshops))
- Printable one-page fold-a-zine template PDF, and an accessibility note for the venue (lifts, quiet room)

**Style: Riso zine**
- Type: headings Londrina Solid 900 at 64–120px, set slightly rotated (1–2deg) on the fest page only; body Work Sans 400/17px; table numbers and prices Space Mono 700.
- Palette: bg #FFFDF7 (newsprint) / text #1A1A1A / riso pink #FF48B0 / riso yellow #FFE800 / riso teal #00838A / line #1A1A1A.
- Layout: loose 6-column grid, blocks overlap by a few pixels as if misregistered; the exhibitor list is a two-column table with fat table numbers. Home is this year's fest poster at full width, then dates, then "Stock with us / Photocopy / Workshops" as three text links, not cards.
- Imagery: two-colour overprint duotones (pink over teal) made with CSS blend modes on photos; scanned zine covers as-is with staples visible.
- Motion: hover on exhibitor rows shifts the pink layer 2px to fake misregistration; nothing on scroll. Reduced motion removes the shift.
- Why it fits now: riso print culture is still the house style of zine and small-print communities, as on [Risotto Studio](https://risottostudio.com/).
**Style variations:** Pink/teal: #FF48B0 over #00838A · Fluoro orange: #FF6C2F with #0078BF · Photocopy: #FFFFFF bg, pure black toner only.
**Real-world basis:** [Chicago Zine Fest: 2026 exhibitors](https://www.chicagozinefest.org/czf-2026-exhibitors.html), [Sticky Institute: Photocopying](https://stickyinstitute.com/photocopying), [Sticky Institute: Stock with us](https://stickyinstitute.com/stock-with-us), [Barnard Zine Library: How to make a zine](https://zines.barnard.edu/zine-basics/how-make-zine), [L.A. Zine Fest: Workshops](https://www.lazinefest.com/workshops)
**Refs:**
- [Chicago Zine Fest: 2026 exhibitors](https://www.chicagozinefest.org/czf-2026-exhibitors.html): table numbers per hall, youth section, table maps and descriptions.
- [Sticky Institute: Stock with us](https://stickyinstitute.com/stock-with-us): consignment terms written so a first-time zinester understands them.
- [Sticky Institute: Photocopying](https://stickyinstitute.com/photocopying): the price table and house rules for a DIY copy shop.

<a id="285"></a>
#### 285 · Dancer / Choreographer (`move`)
**For:** independent choreographers and small dance companies that tour repertoire, run workshops and auditions, and need production pages that promoters, dancers and audiences all use.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-production · single-production · page-agenda (upcoming and past) · page-take-part · page-auditions · page-access · page-company · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** production header (title, year, premiere venue, running time), full credits block (choreography, created with, music, light, cast by year), tour dates for this production, video excerpt, press quotes, "learn the phrase" tutorial with public submissions, agenda row (date, production, venue, city, country, ticket link), past agenda by year, access provision icons as text (BSL, audio description, captions, relaxed), audition call with deadline, workshop list, touring and technical contact, support us.
**Content model:** `production` CPT (year, premiere, running time, credits repeater, cast by season); `performance` CPT (date, venue, city, country, ticket URL, access flags, `production_id`); `call` CPT for auditions with deadline meta.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (upcoming vs past, per production), Jetpack Forms (audition applications, submissions).
**Signature:** a participatory "learn the phrase" page for a signature work: a teaching video breaks down one movement, and the public upload their own filmed versions, which appear in a growing gallery on the production page (seen on: [Rosas: Rosas danst Rosas](https://www.rosas.be/en/productions/378-rosas-danst-rosas), which links its Re:Rosas! platform). Built as a video block, a Jetpack Form with video URL field, and a Query Loop of approved submissions.
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Agenda with an upcoming/past switch and year filter back to the company's first season (seen on: [Rosas: Agenda](https://www.rosas.be/en/agenda/))
- Access page listing which performances have audio description, BSL, captions or relaxed conditions (seen on: [Candoco: Accessibility](https://candoco.co.uk/accessibility/))
- Audition call with a hard deadline, invitation date and contract length, which hides itself after the deadline (seen on: [Wayne McGregor: Auditions and jobs](https://waynemcgregor.com/about/auditions-jobs))
- Technical riders page for promoters, with the head of touring's contact (seen on: [Hofesh Shechter Company: Technical riders](https://hofesh.co.uk/about-us/technical-riders/))
- Event schema.org on every performance

**Style: Kinetic variable-type maximalism**
- Type: headings Georama variable, width (62.5–150) and weight (200–800) animated on production titles; body Hanken Grotesk 400/18px; credits in Hanken Grotesk 500 small caps.
- Palette: bg #F4F4F0 / text #101010 / accent #E4002B (stage red, used for dates only) / surface #FFFFFF / line #101010.
- Layout: production pages open with the title filling the viewport width, then a 3:2 video still, then credits in a two-column list. The agenda is a dense table. Nav is a full-screen overlay with productions listed by year.
- Imagery: rehearsal and stage photos in full colour, cropped tight on bodies at 3:2 or 9:16; no stock silhouettes.
- Motion: production titles widen on scroll using scroll-driven animation (`animation-timeline: view()`) tied to font-variation-settings, once per page; reduced motion shows the static bold cut.
- Why it fits now: variable-font motion is how type foundries and performance makers show movement without video, as on [Dinamo](https://abcdinamo.com/).
**Style variations:** Studio: #F4F4F0 bg, #E4002B dates · Blackbox: #0F0F0F bg, #F4F4F0 text, no accent · Marley: #E9E2D0 bg, #1E3D59 accent.
**Real-world basis:** [Rosas: Rosas danst Rosas](https://www.rosas.be/en/productions/378-rosas-danst-rosas), [Rosas: Agenda](https://www.rosas.be/en/agenda/), [Candoco: Accessibility](https://candoco.co.uk/accessibility/), [Wayne McGregor: Auditions and jobs](https://waynemcgregor.com/about/auditions-jobs), [Hofesh Shechter Company: Technical riders](https://hofesh.co.uk/about-us/technical-riders/)
**Refs:**
- [Rosas: Rosas danst Rosas](https://www.rosas.be/en/productions/378-rosas-danst-rosas): credits, cast by year, tour dates, film excerpt and the participatory phrase project on one page.
- [Rosas: Agenda](https://www.rosas.be/en/agenda/): agenda rows with production, venue, city and a past archive with year filters.
- [Candoco: Accessibility](https://candoco.co.uk/accessibility/): plain list of access provision at performances.

<a id="286"></a>
#### 286 · Stand-up Comedian (`tightfive`)
**For:** touring stand-ups from club level to theatres who sell tour dates, run work-in-progress nights, sell specials and need a press pack.
**Templates:** front-page (next dates) · page-live-dates · single-show (tour show) · page-press-pack · page-watch (specials, clips) · page-merch · page-reviews · page-mailing-list · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** live dates table grouped by month (date, time, show, venue, town, status, ticket link), sold-out and extra-date flags, work-in-progress listing, show blurb with running time and age guidance, podcast recording dates, specials and DVDs with where-to-watch links, press pack with downloadable photos by show and photographer credit, bad reviews page, agent / publicist / tour booker contacts, mailing list.
**Content model:** `gig` CPT (date, time, venue, town, status: on sale / few left / sold out / extra date, ticket URL, `show_id`); `show` CPT (title, year, running time, age guidance); press photos as attachments grouped by show.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (upcoming only, grouped by month).
**Signature:** a reviews page that proudly collects the worst things ever said about the comedian online, attributed and uncorrected, next to the good press (seen on: [Stewart Lee: Online critiques](https://www.stewartlee.co.uk/online-critiques/)). A `quote` CPT with source and year, filtered by a "hostile" tag.
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Sold-out flags and "extra date added" labels on each row, set from one status field (seen on: [Stewart Lee: Live dates](https://www.stewartlee.co.uk/live-dates/))
- Press pack page with high-resolution photos grouped by show and photographer in the filename (seen on: [Stewart Lee: Press pack](https://www.stewartlee.co.uk/press-pack/))
- An honesty-box page for people who pirated the special, pointing them to a charity or the shop (seen on: [Stewart Lee: Did you illegally download my DVDs?](https://www.stewartlee.co.uk/did-you-illegally-download-my-dvds/))
- Recurring podcast recording nights listed with "guests TBA" until confirmed (seen on: [Richard Herring: Gigs](https://www.richardherring.com/gigs/))
- Age guidance and running time on every show ("14+, 90 minutes, no interval")

**Style: Utility / industrial signage (gig listing)**
- Type: headings Racing Sans One 400 for the name only; listings Overpass 700 (from Highway Gothic) at 20px, all dates in Overpass Mono 600 tabular figures; body Overpass 400/18px.
- Palette: bg #FFD200 (venue-sign yellow) / text #111111 / sold-out #D7261E / surface #FFFFFF / line #111111.
- Layout: the home page is the live dates table, full width, 2px black rules, one row per gig; month names as big left-hand labels. Show pages are single column. Nav is four words in a top bar.
- Imagery: black-and-white stage photos with hard flash, 3:2; tour poster art shown as-is.
- Motion: rows invert (black bg, yellow text) on hover; no animation otherwise.
- Why it fits now: listing-first sites that read like a venue board are back for live culture, as on [Cafe OTO: Event listings](https://www.cafeoto.co.uk/events/).
**Style variations:** Hazard: #FFD200 bg, #111111 text · Motorway: #00703C bg, #FFFFFF text · Night bus: #111111 bg, #FFD200 text.
**Real-world basis:** [Stewart Lee: Live dates](https://www.stewartlee.co.uk/live-dates/), [Stewart Lee: Online critiques](https://www.stewartlee.co.uk/online-critiques/), [Stewart Lee: Press pack](https://www.stewartlee.co.uk/press-pack/), [James Acaster: Gigs](https://www.jamesacaster.com/gigs), [Richard Herring: Gigs](https://www.richardherring.com/gigs/)
**Refs:**
- [Stewart Lee: Live dates](https://www.stewartlee.co.uk/live-dates/): month-grouped dates with sold-out flags and matinees.
- [Stewart Lee: Online critiques](https://www.stewartlee.co.uk/online-critiques/): the hostile-reviews page as a piece of comedy in itself.
- [James Acaster: Gigs](https://www.jamesacaster.com/gigs): a plain date / location / venue / tickets table with a work-in-progress banner.

#### 287 · Drag / Cabaret Performer (`cabaret`)
**For:** drag artists and cabaret singers who tour theatres and clubs, hold summer residencies and take bookings for private and corporate shows.
**Templates:** front-page · page-live-shows · single-show · page-residency · page-media (video, audio, photos) · page-about (short and long bio) · page-booking · page-shop · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** live show list (date, 12h and 24h time, venue, city, role: headline / support / host, ticket link, add-to-calendar), sold-out with waiting list link, tour show header with premiere venue, residency block (venue, season dates, nights, box office), characters gallery, media page with videos, audio downloads and photo sets, short bio and long bio, booking enquiry form, Patreon or supporter link, shop.
**Content model:** `show` CPT (title, premiere, blurb, running time, age guidance); `date` CPT (date, time, venue, city, role, ticket URL, status, `show_id`); `character` CPT for recurring personas.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop, Jetpack Forms (booking enquiries), WooCommerce optional (merch, recordings).
**Signature:** a residency page for a summer season: one venue, the show's title and description, the nights it runs and a direct box office link, kept separate from the touring list (seen on: [Paige Turner: Provincetown](https://www.paigeturnernyc.com/provincetown)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Add-to-calendar (ICS and Google) on every date, with times shown in 12h and 24h (seen on: [Joe Black: Live shows](https://www.misterjoeblack.com/liveshows))
- "Sold out: join the waiting list" state instead of a dead link (seen on: [Joe Black: Live shows](https://www.misterjoeblack.com/liveshows))
- Media page with downloadable tracks and a separate behind-the-scenes photo set for press (seen on: [Paige Turner: Media](https://www.paigeturnernyc.com/media))
- Booking form that asks for venue size, stage, sound, date and budget up front, plus a published tech rider PDF
- Age guidance (18+ / 16+) and content notes on each show; pronouns on the About page

**Style: Wood-type playbill revival**
- Type: headings Rye 400 and Ultra 400 mixed on the same line, set in big centred playbill stacks only on show headers; body Libre Caslon Text 400/18px; dates Alfa Slab One at 28px.
- Palette: bg #F3E9D2 (playbill buff, not cream-white) / text #1C1410 / accent #C8102E (show red) / second ink #1B4D89 / line #1C1410.
- Layout: show pages are poster-like stacks with mixed type sizes, framed by a 3px double rule; the dates page is a regular left-aligned table so it stays usable. Nav is a horizontal list with star separators.
- Imagery: full-colour costume photos cut out on flat red or blue, portrait 4:5; no glitter overlays.
- Motion: a small page-turn View Transition between show pages; buttons print-press down 2px on click. Reduced motion removes both.
- Why it fits now: letterpress and wood-type revivals are the go-to for live, human performance brands that want to look printed, as on [Hamilton Wood Type & Printing Museum](https://woodtype.org/).
**Style variations:** Music hall: #F3E9D2 bg, #C8102E and #1B4D89 · Weimar: #111111 bg, #E8D9B5 text, #B1002A accent · Seaside: #FDF1E4 bg, #0077A8 and #F28C28.
**Real-world basis:** [Joe Black: Live shows](https://www.misterjoeblack.com/liveshows), [Paige Turner: Provincetown](https://www.paigeturnernyc.com/provincetown), [Paige Turner: Media](https://www.paigeturnernyc.com/media), [Sasha Velour: Tickets](https://www.sashavelour.com/tickets), [Joe Black: About](https://www.misterjoeblack.com/about)
**Refs:**
- [Joe Black: Live shows](https://www.misterjoeblack.com/liveshows): each date says his role (host, support, headline), with calendar export and waiting lists.
- [Paige Turner: Provincetown](https://www.paigeturnernyc.com/provincetown): a residency page with the show, venue, reviews and box office link.
- [Sasha Velour: Tickets](https://www.sashavelour.com/tickets): theatre tour and club dates split into two lists under one show name.

#### 288 · Circus / Aerial School (`trapeze`)
**For:** aerial and circus studios running weekly classes in silks, hoop, trapeze and acrobatics, kids' circus, parties, open training and studio hire.
**Templates:** front-page · page-timetable · archive-class (by discipline) · single-class · page-new-to-aerial · page-prices · page-kids · page-hire · page-faq · page-contact
**Patterns (~45):** discipline index (silks, hoop, straps, static trapeze, flying trapeze, rope, acro, handstands, contortion), class card with level and prerequisites, weekly timetable by studio and day, new customer offer, credit packs with validity periods, memberships, open training / practice time, private lessons, kids and youth classes by age, holiday camps, birthday parties, tuition assistance, what to wear, code of conduct, studio hire rates.
**Content model:** `class` CPT (discipline, level 1–4, prerequisites, studio, duration); `discipline` taxonomy; `price` CPT for packs (classes, validity weeks, price). Live booking stays in the school's existing system (Mindbody, Momence, TeamUp) linked per class.
**Plugins:** Query Filter (classes by discipline, level, studio), Jetpack Forms (party and hire enquiries). WooCommerce only if the studio sells packs itself.
**Signature:** a "New to aerial?" route: which beginner classes to take, that you do not need to be strong or flexible, and an intro offer of three classes at a fixed price usable across disciplines and studios (seen on: [Flying Fantastic: New to aerial](https://www.flyingfantastic.co.uk/about/new-to-aerial-112/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Credit validity rules in one table: single class 6 weeks, 4 or 8 packs 8 weeks, bookings open 28 days ahead (seen on: [Flying Fantastic: Timetable](https://www.flyingfantastic.co.uk/timetable/class-timetable-87/))
- Need-based tuition assistance for youth classes with an application deadline and lottery note (seen on: [Circus Center: Tuition assistance](https://circuscenter.org/pages/tuition-assistance))
- "Updates coming soon: join the list" state for seasonal classes such as flying trapeze (seen on: [Circomedia: Flying trapeze](https://www.circomedia.com/flying-trapeze-classes/))
- What to wear and bring (leggings covering the knees, no jewellery, water), and a first-class checklist
- Gift cards, and a public accessibility note (step-free studio or not, accessible aerial class)

**Style: Soft neo-brutalism (hard shadows, pastel fills)**
- Type: headings Chango 400, 48–96px; body Figtree 400/17px; levels and times Figtree 700 at 15px.
- Palette: bg #FFF7EC / text #121212 / chalk blue #A9D6F5 / rosin pink #F7B2C4 / mat yellow #FFE27A / line #121212.
- Layout: timetable as a week grid with each class a flat pastel block, 2px black border and a 4px hard offset shadow; disciplines colour-coded by fill, never by colour alone (labels always visible). Home: a big "New to aerial? Start here" block, then this week's timetable. Radius 6px on blocks only, square buttons.
- Imagery: action photos shot from below against the rig, high shutter speed, 4:5 crops that keep hands and fabric in frame.
- Motion: blocks press into their shadow on hover and focus (translate 2px, shadow 2px); no scroll effects.
- Why it fits now: soft neo-brutalism is the friendly-but-bold look many small, class-based businesses use in 2025–26, as on [Gumroad](https://gumroad.com/).
**Style variations:** Chalk: #FFF7EC bg, pastel fills · Big top: #FFFFFF bg, #E63946 and #1D3557 fills · Night class: #1B1B1F bg, #F7B2C4 shadows.
**Real-world basis:** [Flying Fantastic: New to aerial](https://www.flyingfantastic.co.uk/about/new-to-aerial-112/), [Flying Fantastic: Timetable](https://www.flyingfantastic.co.uk/timetable/class-timetable-87/), [Circus Center: Tuition assistance](https://circuscenter.org/pages/tuition-assistance), [Circomedia: Flying trapeze](https://www.circomedia.com/flying-trapeze-classes/), [AirCraft Circus: FAQ](https://aircraftcircus.com/pages/frequently-asked-questions)
**Refs:**
- [Flying Fantastic: New to aerial](https://www.flyingfantastic.co.uk/about/new-to-aerial-112/): beginner route and intro offer written without jargon.
- [Circus Center: Tuition assistance](https://circuscenter.org/pages/tuition-assistance): a short, clear financial-aid notice with dates.
- [Circomedia: Flying trapeze](https://www.circomedia.com/flying-trapeze-classes/): how to present a seasonal class between runs.

#### 289 · Puppetry Company (`strings`)
**For:** puppet theatres and touring puppetry companies making family and adult shows, with schools work, birthday parties and a building or barge to visit.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-show · single-show · page-whats-on · page-visit (getting here, access) · page-schools · page-parties · page-touring · page-support · page-shop
**Patterns (~40):** show card with age range ("ages 2–5", "for everyone over 5"), running time and interval, relaxed and BSL performance rows, run dates per venue, show synopsis, puppet-making photos, schools workshops, birthday party packages, touring dates, access page (visual story, touch tours, seat sizes), getting here with photos, friends scheme, venue hire.
**Content model:** `show` CPT (age range, running time, puppetry type: glove / rod / shadow / marionette, synopsis); `run` CPT (venue or mooring, start, end, ticket URL, access performances repeater); `venue` taxonomy.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (current and next runs), Jetpack Forms (schools and party enquiries). Ticketing stays with the theatre's system.
**Signature:** a what's-on list split by location, for a company that plays in two places (or moves), each run showing age range, running time and the dates of relaxed and BSL-interpreted performances (seen on: [The Puppet Theatre Barge: Puppet shows](https://www.puppetbarge.com/puppet-shows), which moves between Little Venice and Richmond).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Age guidance on every listing, in words parents use ("Aimed at ages 2–5") (seen on: [Little Angel Theatre: What's on](https://www.littleangeltheatre.com/whats-on/))
- Access page covering relaxed events (lights stay on, no sudden sounds), visual stories, touch tours and seat dimensions (seen on: [Norwich Puppet Theatre: Accessibility](https://puppettheatre.co.uk/accessibility/))
- Birthday party packages with what is included and how many children (seen on: [Little Angel Theatre: Birthday parties](https://www.littleangeltheatre.com/hire-us/birthday-parties/))
- A cheap art shop with a short manifesto and low fixed prices (seen on: [Bread and Puppet: Cheap Art](https://breadandpuppet.org/cheap-art))
- "How to find us" photo directions for a hard-to-find entrance or mooring

**Style: Cut-paper collage**
- Type: headings Outward Block (Velvetyne) at 56–110px; body Literata 400/18px; ages and times Literata 700 italic.
- Palette: bg #F6F1E7 (sugar paper, unbleached) / text #1E1B18 / vermilion paper #E0452B / ultramarine paper #2A4DA8 / ochre card #D9A441 / line #1E1B18.
- Layout: show pages set on an asymmetric 10-column grid with cut-paper shapes (SVG, flat colour, hand-cut edges drawn once per theme) behind the show title; listings stay on a clean table. Home is the current show at full width, then a "This month" list. Nav is a vertical list on desktop, bottom sheet on phones.
- Imagery: puppets photographed on plain coloured card, lit from the side, 1:1 and 4:5; workshop photos of hands and materials.
- Motion: paper shapes shift a few pixels on pointer move (desktop only, respects reduced motion); no scroll animation.
- Why it fits now: hand-made, cut-and-painted visuals have returned as a direct answer to glossy digital branding in theatre and family arts, as on [Bread and Puppet Theater](https://breadandpuppet.org/).
**Style variations:** Shadow play: #111111 bg, #F2C14E light, paper cut-outs in black · Nursery: #FDF6EC bg, #E0452B and #2A4DA8 · Marionette: #F4EFE8 bg, #5B2A86 accent.
**Real-world basis:** [The Puppet Theatre Barge: Puppet shows](https://www.puppetbarge.com/puppet-shows), [Little Angel Theatre: What's on](https://www.littleangeltheatre.com/whats-on/), [Norwich Puppet Theatre: Accessibility](https://puppettheatre.co.uk/accessibility/), [Bread and Puppet: Cheap Art](https://breadandpuppet.org/cheap-art), [Handspring Puppet Company: Our work](https://www.handspringpuppet.com/handspring-puppet-company-productions)
**Refs:**
- [The Puppet Theatre Barge: Puppet shows](https://www.puppetbarge.com/puppet-shows): shows grouped by mooring, with age ranges, running time and relaxed and BSL dates.
- [Little Angel Theatre: What's on](https://www.littleangeltheatre.com/whats-on/): age ranges, two venues and relaxed performance listings.
- [Norwich Puppet Theatre: Accessibility](https://puppettheatre.co.uk/accessibility/): a thorough, practical access page for a small venue.

#### 290 · Art-Book Fair (`bookfair`)
**For:** independent art-book and self-publishing fairs (one to three editions a year) with a few hundred exhibitors, a talks programme and an application round.
**Templates:** front-page (this edition) · page-exhibitors · single-exhibitor · page-programme · page-apply · page-access · page-community-agreement · page-archive · page-about
**Patterns (~40):** edition block (dates, venue, opening hours, free entry), exhibitor index A–Z with city and country, filters by type (publisher, artist, zine, distributor, magazine, rare and out of print) and by country, floor plan PDF, exhibitor profile, talks and launches programme by day, application call with deadline, grants for exhibitors, access and directions (stations, walking minutes, parking), community agreement, archive by year.
**Content model:** `exhibitor` CPT (city, country, type taxonomy, URL, table, `edition` taxonomy); `event` CPT for talks (day, time, room); `edition` taxonomy for year and city.
**Plugins:** Query Filter (type, country, edition), Advanced Query Loop (programme by day), Jetpack Forms (applications).
**Signature:** an exhibitor index with A–Z grouping plus filters for exhibitor type and country, a gallery view toggle, a downloadable floor plan, and every past edition one click away (seen on: [Miss Read: Exhibitors 2026](https://missread.com/exhibitors/2026/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Community agreement page linked from tickets and applications, with a reporting email (seen on: [Tokyo Art Book Fair: Community agreement](https://tokyoartbookfair.com/community-agreement/))
- Access page listing every station exit with walking minutes, parking and accessible spaces (seen on: [Tokyo Art Book Fair: Access](https://tokyoartbookfair.com/access/))
- "Call for applications open until 16 August" line on the participants page, switching off after the date (seen on: [Offprint: Participants Paris 2026](https://www.offprint.org/participants-paris-2026))
- Archive of every edition by year and city (seen on: [Printed Matter Art Book Fairs: Archive](https://printedmatterartbookfairs.org/archive))
- Exhibitor grant label (for example BIPOC grants) on profiles, and a printable exhibitor list for the door

**Style: Exposed-grid floor-plan index**
- Type: headings Apfel Grotezk (Collletttivo) Regular at 48–96px; lists and body Hanken Grotesk 400/16px with tabular figures; table numbers IBM Plex Mono 500.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #0D0D0D / accent #FF5A1F (signage orange for table numbers and the "you are here" dot) / surface #F3F3F3 / line #0D0D0D.
- Layout: the exhibitor index is a dense four-column list that reads like a directory; the home page shows the floor plan as the hero, with table numbers clickable to profiles. Visible column rules only where they separate data, never as decoration. Nav: Exhibitors · Programme · Visit · Apply · Archive.
- Imagery: book spreads and covers photographed flat from above on grey, 4:3; no people-at-a-table stock shots.
- Motion: hovering an exhibitor highlights its table on the plan (Interactivity API); filter changes use a View Transition. Reduced motion drops the transition.
- Why it fits now: fairs and publishers use index-style directories because visitors come to find names fast, as on [Miss Read: Exhibitors 2026](https://missread.com/exhibitors/2026/).
**Style variations:** Hall: #FFFFFF bg, #FF5A1F numbers · Newsprint: #F2F0EA bg, #0D0D0D only · After hours: #121212 bg, #F2F0EA text, #FFB000 numbers.
**Real-world basis:** [Miss Read: Exhibitors 2026](https://missread.com/exhibitors/2026/), [Offprint: Participants Paris 2026](https://www.offprint.org/participants-paris-2026), [Tokyo Art Book Fair: Community agreement](https://tokyoartbookfair.com/community-agreement/), [Tokyo Art Book Fair: Access](https://tokyoartbookfair.com/access/), [Printed Matter Art Book Fairs: Archive](https://printedmatterartbookfairs.org/archive)
**Refs:**
- [Miss Read: Exhibitors 2026](https://missread.com/exhibitors/2026/): A–Z list, type and country filters, floor plan PDF and year filter.
- [Tokyo Art Book Fair: Access](https://tokyoartbookfair.com/access/): station-by-station directions and parking in one page.
- [Offprint: Participants Paris 2026](https://www.offprint.org/participants-paris-2026): a long participant list with the next application deadline.

#### 291 · Community Choir (`chorus`)
**For:** non-audition community choirs and amateur choral societies with one weekly rehearsal, two or three concerts a year and member subs.
**Templates:** front-page · page-join · page-concerts · single-concert · page-past-concerts · page-rehearsals · page-members (password-protected) · page-faq · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** "no auditions" join block with voice parts, rehearsal night, time and address, term dates, subs with concession rate and payment options, free taster session booking, concert card (date, venue, programme with works and composers, conductor, soloists, orchestra, tickets), past concerts poster archive, members area with learning tracks and scores, FAQ (can I read music, what if I can't come every week), newsletter.
**Content model:** `concert` CPT (date, venue, programme repeater of work and composer, conductor, soloists, ticket URL, poster); `term` CPT (start, end, half-term); members page is a password-protected page with audio blocks.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (upcoming vs past concerts), Jetpack Forms (join and taster requests).
**Signature:** a concert page that lists the full programme (work, composer, catalogue number), conductor, soloists and orchestra, with every past concert since the choir began kept as a poster archive (seen on: [Hackney Singers: Concerts](https://www.hackneysingers.org.uk/concerts)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Join page with fees, a concession rate, the option to pay in two instalments and "new members usually join after concerts in April, October and January" (seen on: [Hackney Singers: Join](https://www.hackneysingers.org.uk/join))
- Free first rehearsal / taster, with monthly subs and 30 days' notice to cancel (seen on: [Some Voices: Bristol](https://somevoices.co.uk/bristol))
- FAQ for nervous beginners: no need to read music, what to wear for concerts, missing rehearsals (seen on: [Some Voices: FAQ](https://somevoices.co.uk/faq))
- Password-protected learning tracks per voice part, and a printable term card with dates
- Accessible venue note (step-free hall, hearing loop) on the rehearsals page

**Style: Sheet-music engraving**
- Type: headings Bona Nova 400 at 56–88px; body Bona Nova 400/18px; programme lines in Bona Nova italic for works and small caps for composers; musical symbols set in Bravura (SMuFL, OFL) for dynamics used as section markers.
- Palette: bg #FBFAF7 (engraved-score white) / text #141414 / accent #7D1F2A (hymn-book red for concert dates) / surface #F0EEE8 / line #141414.
- Layout: five fine horizontal rules (a stave) used once, under the choir name in the header; concert programmes set like a printed programme, centred only on the concert page, left-aligned everywhere else. Home: next concert, then "Join us on Thursdays".
- Imagery: concert photos in black and white from the back of the hall, 3:2; scanned past posters in a grid.
- Motion: none beyond link underlines. The audio player for learning tracks uses the core Audio block.
- Why it fits now: music publishers and choirs lean on engraved, programme-like typography to feel serious without being stiff, as on [G. Henle Verlag](https://www.henle.de/).
**Style variations:** Evensong: #FBFAF7 bg, #7D1F2A accent · Pops choir: #FFF3E0 bg, #0A6E6E accent · Winter concert: #1C2230 bg, #F2EEE4 text.
**Real-world basis:** [Hackney Singers: Concerts](https://www.hackneysingers.org.uk/concerts), [Hackney Singers: Join](https://www.hackneysingers.org.uk/join), [Some Voices: Bristol](https://somevoices.co.uk/bristol), [Some Voices: FAQ](https://somevoices.co.uk/faq), [Streetwise Opera: What's on](https://streetwiseopera.org/whats-on/)
**Refs:**
- [Hackney Singers: Concerts](https://www.hackneysingers.org.uk/concerts): full programmes and a poster archive going back to 1973.
- [Hackney Singers: Join](https://www.hackneysingers.org.uk/join): "no auditions", voice parts, fees, concessions and rehearsal address in one short page.
- [Some Voices: Bristol](https://somevoices.co.uk/bristol): local choir page with terms, monthly price and free taster.

#### 292 · Youth Music Project / Charity (`bandroom`)
**For:** small youth music charities and projects running mentoring, band sessions, rock camps and studio time for young people, often funded by grants.
**Templates:** front-page · page-what-we-do · page-take-part · page-refer (for professionals) · page-stories · page-find-a-session (map) · page-support · page-safeguarding · page-team · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** programme block (ages, where, when, cost or free), referral form route for teachers and youth workers, eligibility list, "what happens next" steps, young people's stories with tracks, session finder map, safeguarding and safer spaces policies, funders row as plain text, paid traineeships, volunteer musicians call, donation block, annual report download.
**Content model:** `programme` CPT (ages, location, cost, dates, status); `story` CPT (participant first name or alias, track embed, consent flag); `site` CPT for session locations with lat/long.
**Plugins:** Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (session finder), Jetpack Forms (enquiries), GiveWP (donations).
**Signature:** a referral page for professionals: who can refer, eligibility (age, no experience needed), the two details that are essential (young person's phone and email), and what happens after the referral is sent (seen on: [Noise Solution: Referral](https://www.noisesolution.org/referral)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A map of sessions or funded projects filterable by age group and local area (seen on: [Youth Music: Projects map](https://www.youthmusic.org.uk/community/organisations-and-projects/projects-map))
- "Find a camp near you" list for a network of rock camps (seen on: [Girls Rock Camp Alliance: Find a camp](https://www.girlsrockcampalliance.org/findacamp))
- Stories page with young people's own tracks and words, published with consent (seen on: [Noise Solution: Our stories](https://www.noisesolution.org/our-stories))
- Policies page (safeguarding, safer spaces, complaints) linked in the footer (seen on: [Youth Music: Policies and procedures](https://www.youthmusic.org.uk/about/policies-and-procedures))
- "No sessions planned right now: email us" state for programmes between funding rounds, and a plain-language version of the referral page

**Style: Photocopied punk flyer / DIY collage**
- Type: headings Knewave 400 at 72–140px, uppercase for programme names only; body Atkinson Hyperlegible 400/18px for readability; stickers and labels Rubik Mono One at 14px.
- Palette: bg #F4F2EE (photocopy grey-white) / text #111111 / highlighter #FFF200 / sticker red #E0301E / tape blue #2F6FDE / line #111111.
- Layout: collage blocks on an 8-column grid, each with torn-tape corners drawn in CSS (not image masks), stacked slightly off-axis; forms and policies are plain and straight. Home: one big "Want to make music? Here's how" block with two routes: young person / professional.
- Imagery: high-contrast black-and-white photos of real sessions, photocopied look via CSS threshold filter, with one flat colour behind; faces only with consent.
- Motion: highlighter swipe under links on hover (background-size transition); nothing on scroll.
- Why it fits now: zine and flyer aesthetics speak to young people and grassroots music scenes without looking corporate, as on [Sticky Institute](https://stickyinstitute.com/).
**Style variations:** Gig flyer: #F4F2EE bg, #FFF200 highlighter · Studio: #111111 bg, #F4F2EE text, #E0301E stickers · Summer camp: #FFFFFF bg, #2F6FDE and #FF8A00.
**Real-world basis:** [Noise Solution: Referral](https://www.noisesolution.org/referral), [Noise Solution: Our stories](https://www.noisesolution.org/our-stories), [Youth Music: Projects map](https://www.youthmusic.org.uk/community/organisations-and-projects/projects-map), [Girls Rock Camp Alliance: Find a camp](https://www.girlsrockcampalliance.org/findacamp), [Spark the Noise: Take part](https://www.sparkthenoise.com/take-part/)
**Refs:**
- [Noise Solution: Referral](https://www.noisesolution.org/referral): referral route written for busy professionals, with what happens next.
- [Youth Music: Projects map](https://www.youthmusic.org.uk/community/organisations-and-projects/projects-map): map and list with filters by age and population served.
- [Spark the Noise: Take part](https://www.sparkthenoise.com/take-part/): how a small charity says "nothing running right now, email us" honestly.

#### 293 · Roller Derby League (`jam`)
**For:** amateur flat-track roller derby leagues with home teams, travel teams, juniors, a fresh-meat intake and bouts that sell tickets.
**Templates:** front-page (next bout) · page-schedule · single-bout · page-standings · archive-team · single-team (roster) · page-basic-training · page-juniors · page-rules · page-press-kit · page-code-of-conduct · page-sponsors
**Patterns (~45):** next bout block (teams, date, doors, venue, tickets), season schedule with scores, standings table (W-L, win %, streak), team page with roster (derby name, number, position), all-time finishes table by season, rules explainer (jammer, blockers, pivot, scoring), basic training intake (dates, price, gear list, insurance, skills needed), junior league, tryouts, fan code of conduct, press kit, sponsor list, volunteer officials call.
**Content model:** `bout` CPT (date, home team, away team, scores, venue, ticket URL); `team` CPT; `skater` CPT (derby name, number, position, team); standings computed by the companion plugin from bout scores.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (upcoming vs played), Jetpack Forms (volunteers, officials).
**Signature:** a season standings table for the home teams (record, win percentage, current streak) with the schedule and scores below, and a history table of every team's final place since the league began (seen on: [Rose City Rollers: Standings](https://rosecityrollers.com/standings/)). The companion plugin totals bout scores into a standings block.
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Basic training intake with session dates, price, mandatory insurance cost, full gear list and "loaner gear not available" note (seen on: [Gotham Roller Derby: Basic training](https://www.gothamrollerderby.com/basic-training))
- Press kit with league facts, team lists, abbreviations glossary and photo release rules (seen on: [Rose City Rollers: Press kit](https://rosecityrollers.com/about/press-kit/))
- Fan code of conduct linked from every ticket button (seen on: [Rose City Rollers: Fan code of conduct](https://rosecityrollers.com/fan-code-of-conduct/))
- Tryouts page with dates and minimum skills (seen on: [Texas Rollergirls: Tryouts](https://www.texasrollergirls.org/get-involved/tryouts/))
- SportsEvent schema.org on bouts, and pronouns on skater profiles

**Style: Sports-kit athletic type (varsity numerals)**
- Type: skater numbers and scores in Graduate 400 (collegiate block) at 80–200px; headings Graduate 400; body Work Sans 400/17px; stats Chivo Mono 500 with tabular figures.
- Palette: bg #F5F5F2 / text #101418 / team colour A #D1003F / team colour B #0057B8 / track grey #8A8F98 / line #101418.
- Layout: team pages use a kit-number hero (huge number, derby name beside it); standings as a heavy-ruled table; home is the next bout as a fixture card with both team colours split diagonally in flat colour, then schedule. Nav: Schedule · Standings · Teams · Join · Tickets.
- Imagery: action photos at track level, fast shutter, 16:9; roster headshots in helmets, 1:1, same background.
- Motion: score numbers count up once when a finished bout loads (tabular figures, no layout shift); disabled under reduced motion.
- Why it fits now: grassroots sport is using kit-number typography and fixture-first home pages instead of generic club templates, as on [Rose City Rollers](https://rosecityrollers.com/).
**Style variations:** Home kit: #F5F5F2 bg, #D1003F · Away kit: #101418 bg, #F5F5F2 text, #0057B8 · Juniors: #FFFFFF bg, #FF8A00 and #00A19A.
**Real-world basis:** [Rose City Rollers: Standings](https://rosecityrollers.com/standings/), [Rose City Rollers: Press kit](https://rosecityrollers.com/about/press-kit/), [Gotham Roller Derby: Basic training](https://www.gothamrollerderby.com/basic-training), [Rose City Rollers: Fan code of conduct](https://rosecityrollers.com/fan-code-of-conduct/), [Texas Rollergirls: Tryouts](https://www.texasrollergirls.org/get-involved/tryouts/)
**Refs:**
- [Rose City Rollers: Standings](https://rosecityrollers.com/standings/): standings, streaks, scores and a 20-year finishes table.
- [Gotham Roller Derby: Basic training](https://www.gothamrollerderby.com/basic-training): intake dates, prices, insurance and gear rules stated plainly.
- [Rose City Rollers: Press kit](https://rosecityrollers.com/about/press-kit/): a press kit a local reporter can use without phoning anyone.

#### 294 · DIY Skatepark Campaign (`diyspot`)
**For:** volunteer groups that build or save a concrete skatepark, raise money for materials, run build days and then keep the park going with sessions and loaner boards.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-build (projects) · single-build · page-volunteer · page-donate · page-sessions · page-about · page-reports · page-sponsors
**Patterns (~35):** build header (place, year, surface area in m², volunteers, status: planning / building / open), build diary posts with dated photos, what your money buys (bags of cement, a coping block, a day of machine hire), volunteer call with dates and skills, local crew and who runs the park now, weekly sessions and loaner boards, girls-only and beginners sessions, press mentions, annual report PDF, sponsors as a plain list, site map.
**Content model:** `build` CPT (location, country, year, surface m², volunteers count, status, lat/long, press links); posts tagged by build for the diary; `session` CPT (day, time, who it is for).
**Plugins:** GiveWP (donations with a materials goal), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (map of builds), Jetpack Forms (volunteer sign-up).
**Signature:** a project page per build with hard facts (surface area, number of volunteers, year built, who runs it now) above the photo diary, so donors see what the money became (seen on: [Make Life Skate Life: Iraq, Suli](https://www.makelifeskatelife.org/iraq-suli)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Projects index as a map and a country list, with "construction: 2026, surface: 450m²" on each (seen on: [Make Life Skate Life: Projects](https://www.makelifeskatelife.org/projects), [Uganda](https://www.makelifeskatelife.org/uganda))
- "Who runs it now" section naming the local crew or organisation after the build crew leaves (seen on: [Skateistan: Palestine's largest concrete skatepark at 10](https://www.skateistan.org/blog/celebrating-10-years-of-palestines-largest-concrete-skatepark))
- Donation amounts tied to materials, with a live total of bags and blocks funded
- Build-day checklist: boots, gloves, tetanus jab, what to bring, where to park
- Session times with "boards and helmets to borrow" and a beginners-only slot

**Style: Raw concrete web brutalism**
- Type: headings Zina 400 (Fontshare, grunge poster) uppercase at 64–120px with tight but readable leading (1.0); body IBM Plex Sans 400/18px; measurements IBM Plex Mono 600 ("450 m² · 45 volunteers · 2018").
- Palette: bg #D9D7D2 (wet concrete) / text #121212 / hi-vis #FF6A13 / surface #BDBAB3 / line #121212.
- Layout: full-width blocks with visible 1px borders, no padding theatre; build facts in a monospace spec strip under every title. Home: the current build status in huge type ("POURING: WEEK 3"), a donation total, then the build diary.
- Imagery: grainy photos of forms, rebar, wet concrete and first sessions, 4:3 and 1:1, uncorrected colour; no drone-shot gloss.
- Motion: none except the donation total updating. Links are underlined and turn hi-vis on hover.
- Why it fits now: raw HTML brutalism fits DIY builders who distrust polish, as collected on [Brutalist Websites](https://brutalistwebsites.com/).
**Style variations:** Wet pour: #D9D7D2 bg, #FF6A13 · Night session: #1A1A1A bg, #D9D7D2 text, #FFD500 · Chalk mark: #FFFFFF bg, #1A1A1A, #2BB673 marks.
**Real-world basis:** [Make Life Skate Life: Iraq, Suli](https://www.makelifeskatelife.org/iraq-suli), [Make Life Skate Life: Projects](https://www.makelifeskatelife.org/projects), [Make Life Skate Life: Uganda](https://www.makelifeskatelife.org/uganda), [Skateistan: 10 years of Palestine's largest concrete skatepark](https://www.skateistan.org/blog/celebrating-10-years-of-palestines-largest-concrete-skatepark), [Skateistan: Free Movement](https://www.skateistan.org/location/free-movement)
**Refs:**
- [Make Life Skate Life: Iraq, Suli](https://www.makelifeskatelife.org/iraq-suli): the build facts, local crew and weekly programme on one page.
- [Make Life Skate Life: Projects](https://www.makelifeskatelife.org/projects): a map of builds by country since 2013.
- [Skateistan: 10 years of Palestine's largest concrete skatepark](https://www.skateistan.org/blog/celebrating-10-years-of-palestines-largest-concrete-skatepark): how a park is handed over to local organisers.

#### 295 · Architecture School Studio Unit (`unit`)
**For:** design units and studio chairs inside architecture schools (a tutor or two, 12–20 students a year) that publish a yearly brief, site trip, references and the students' projects.
**Templates:** front-page (current brief) · archive-brief (by year or semester) · single-brief · archive-project · single-project · page-references · page-electives · page-people · page-contact
**Patterns (~35):** brief page (title, semester code, site, text, key quote, reading list), site trip block (dates, cost range), student list per brief, project page (student, title, drawings, model photos, short text), reference library (building or artwork, architect or artist, year, place, image), filters for references by architect, building type, place and era, electives list, past semesters archive, contact for applicants.
**Content model:** `brief` CPT (semester, year, site, trip dates, trip cost); `project` CPT (student, `brief_id`, drawings gallery); `reference` CPT (architect, year, place, type, era taxonomies).
**Plugins:** Query Filter (references by architect, type, place, era).
**Signature:** a reference library: every building, painting or photograph the unit has used as a precedent, filed by semester theme and filterable by architect, building type, location and era (seen on: [Studio A. Caruso: References](https://caruso.arch.ethz.ch/archive/references)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Brief page that states the site, trip dates and the trip's cost range so students can plan (seen on: [Studio Tom Emerson: Bricolage London](https://emerson.arch.ethz.ch/design-studio/bricolage-london))
- An index of every semester's brief back to the unit's first year (seen on: [Studio Tom Emerson: Design studio](https://emerson.arch.ethz.ch/design-studio/))
- Student project archive by theme (seen on: [Studio A. Caruso: Student projects](https://caruso.arch.ethz.ch/archive/student-projects))
- Reading list per brief with library shelfmarks, and a printable A4 brief PDF
- Credit line and permission note on every student drawing

**Style: Architectural drawing / technical orthographic**
- Type: headings Sedan SC 400 at 32–56px (like a drawing title block); body Sedan 400/18px; captions and scales IBM Plex Mono 400/13px ("1:200 · FS 2026").
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #111111 / line #111111 / red line (revision) #C8102E / surface #F4F4F4.
- Layout: every page has a title block in the bottom-right corner (unit, semester, sheet number) as a real sticky element; drawings shown large on a white field with generous margins; lists as numbered sheets only where the order is real. Home: the current brief's title and site plan, then the index of past briefs.
- Imagery: line drawings and model photos on white, never cropped; black-and-white site photos; no renders with glossy skies.
- Motion: none. Hovering a reference shows its caption in the title block (Interactivity API).
- Why it fits now: architecture studios and chairs keep choosing plain, drawing-led academic sites over portfolio templates, as on [Studio Tom Emerson](https://emerson.arch.ethz.ch/).
**Style variations:** Blueline: #F2F6FA bg, #1F4E8C lines · Trace: #FAF8F2 bg, #3A3A3A lines · Crit night: #121212 bg, #EDEDED lines.
**Real-world basis:** [Studio A. Caruso: References](https://caruso.arch.ethz.ch/archive/references), [Studio A. Caruso: Student projects](https://caruso.arch.ethz.ch/archive/student-projects), [Studio Tom Emerson: Bricolage London](https://emerson.arch.ethz.ch/design-studio/bricolage-london), [Studio Tom Emerson: Design studio](https://emerson.arch.ethz.ch/design-studio/)
**Refs:**
- [Studio A. Caruso: References](https://caruso.arch.ethz.ch/archive/references): a precedent library with semester themes and four filters.
- [Studio Tom Emerson: Bricolage London](https://emerson.arch.ethz.ch/design-studio/bricolage-london): a brief page with site, method, student list and trip dates.

#### 296 · Camera Club / Photography Society (`shutter`)
**For:** local camera clubs and photographic societies (30–120 members) with a weekly meeting, a season of talks, internal competitions, inter-club entries and an annual exhibition.
**Templates:** front-page · page-programme · archive-competition · single-competition (results) · page-join · page-galleries · page-exhibition · page-rules · page-history · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** season programme (date, speaker or competition, hand-in date), competition results post (judge with distinctions, trophy name, 1st/2nd/3rd, highly commended, commended, with titles and authors), members' galleries, annual exhibition dates and venue, how to join (fees, junior rate, visitors free for three nights), competition categories (open colour, mono, nature, PDI, print), rules PDF, federation and PAGB links, club history since founding, summer photo walks.
**Content model:** `competition` CPT (date, judge, category, trophy, results repeater: place, title, author, image); `meeting` CPT (date, type: talk / competition / members' night, speaker); member galleries as posts by author.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (programme upcoming vs past), Jetpack Forms (joining enquiries).
**Signature:** a results page for each competition night: judge and distinctions, trophy, and the placed images with titles and authors from first place down to commended (seen on: [Ilkley Camera Club: 20 March 2026 annual print competitions](https://ilkleycameraclub.co.uk/20-march-2026-annual-print-competitions/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Visitors attend free, speaker nights by £5 donation, and after three visits you join, with mid-season reduced fees (seen on: [Leeds Photographic Society: How to join](https://lps1852.org/how-to-join/))
- Programme with "subject to change" note and an iCal feed members can subscribe to (seen on: [Hebden Bridge Camera Club: Programme](https://hebdenbridgecc.co.uk/programme/))
- Inter-club entry results and rules downloads (seen on: [PAGB: Inter-club print](https://thepagb.org.uk/events/inter-club-print/))
- Hand-in deadline banner for the next competition that switches off after the date
- Alt text required on every gallery image, written by the photographer

**Style: Quiet luxury mono / darkroom**
- Type: headings Fanwood Text 400 at 40–72px; body Hanken Grotesk 400/17px; exposure data and scores IBM Plex Mono 400 ("1st · 20 pts · Open Mono").
- Palette: bg #F5F4F1 (fibre paper) / text #161616 / safelight #B3261E (used once per page for the current competition) / surface #E7E5E0 / line #9A9893.
- Layout: galleries on a strict 3-column grid with consistent white mats around images; results page is a ranked list with images at 2:3 and 3:2 kept in their own orientation. Home: next meeting, latest results, then "Visitors welcome on Tuesdays".
- Imagery: members' work only, shown uncropped with a thin keyline; no stock cameras on desks.
- Motion: lightbox via core "Expand on click"; nothing else.
- Why it fits now: photobook publishers and photographers favour quiet, white-matted layouts that let prints carry the page, as on [MACK](https://www.mackbooks.us/).
**Style variations:** Fibre: #F5F4F1 bg, #B3261E once · Darkroom: #111111 bg, #E9E7E2 text, #B3261E · Contact sheet: #FFFFFF bg, #000000, orange #FF7A00 grease-pencil marks.
**Real-world basis:** [Ilkley Camera Club: 20 March 2026 annual print competitions](https://ilkleycameraclub.co.uk/20-march-2026-annual-print-competitions/), [Leeds Photographic Society: How to join](https://lps1852.org/how-to-join/), [Hebden Bridge Camera Club: Programme](https://hebdenbridgecc.co.uk/programme/), [PAGB: Inter-club print](https://thepagb.org.uk/events/inter-club-print/), [PAGB: Find a club](https://thepagb.org.uk/repagb/find-a-club/)
**Refs:**
- [Ilkley Camera Club: 20 March 2026 annual print competitions](https://ilkleycameraclub.co.uk/20-march-2026-annual-print-competitions/): judge, trophy and placed images as a results post.
- [Leeds Photographic Society: How to join](https://lps1852.org/how-to-join/): fees, venue, visitor rules and mid-season rates.
- [Hebden Bridge Camera Club: Programme](https://hebdenbridgecc.co.uk/programme/): a season programme with talks, members' nights and an iCal feed.

### XXXI. Odd formats & single-purpose sites

<a id="297"></a>
#### 297 · Documentary Impact Campaign (`impactdoc`)
**For:** independent documentary teams running an impact campaign after release: community and school screenings, discussion guides, calls to action and partner organisations.
**Templates:** front-page · page-the-film · page-host-a-screening · page-find-a-screening · page-take-action · page-resources (guides by audience) · page-press · page-impact (report) · page-contact
**Patterns (~40):** film header (runtime, year, director, trailer), host-a-screening flow (licence types, what hosts get, lead time, steps), screenings table (date, city, host, public or private, ticket link), take action section by audience (individuals, families, educators, youth), discussion guide and facilitator guide downloads, poster and social assets pack, partner organisations list, impact highlights by year, press kit, subtitles and languages available.
**Content model:** `screening` CPT (date, city, country, host, public flag, ticket URL, lat/long); `resource` CPT (audience taxonomy, file, language); impact posts by year.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (screening enquiries), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (screenings map), Advanced Query Loop (upcoming screenings only).
**Signature:** a "Host a screening" page that explains the licence options (one-off event or year-round for schools), lists what hosts receive (facilitator guide, discussion questions, posters, social assets, subtitles), recommends 3–4 weeks' lead time and ends in an enquiry form (seen on: [Screenagers: Host a screening](https://www.screenagersmovie.com/host-a-screening)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Take-action page split by audience, with a free classroom pack for educators (seen on: [The Social Dilemma: Take action](https://thesocialdilemma.com/take-action/))
- Public screenings table fed by approved enquiries (seen on: [Screenagers: Find a screening](https://www.screenagersmovie.com/find-a-screening))
- Impact report posts ("2020 impact highlights") for funders (seen on: [The Social Dilemma: Impact highlights](https://thesocialdilemma.com/2021/01/07/the-social-dilemma-2020-impact-highlights/))
- Minimum bandwidth and tech check for streamed screenings (20+ Mbps), and a printable host checklist
- Content warnings and a support-line list at the end of the take-action page when the subject is heavy

**Style: Documentary lower-thirds cinematic**
- Type: headings Heebo 800 at 48–96px; body Source Serif 4 400/18px; lower-third labels (name, role, place) in Heebo 600 on a solid bar, like broadcast captions.
- Palette: bg #0E0F10 (screening-room black, used only on the film page) and #F4F3EF elsewhere / text #F4F3EF on dark, #111213 on light / accent #F2B705 (caption bar amber) / line #3A3C40.
- Layout: the film page opens on a 2.39:1 still with a lower-third caption; resource pages switch to light and work like a library, two columns: audience list left, downloads right. Nav: The film · Host · Screenings · Act · Press.
- Imagery: frame grabs from the film at true aspect ratio, never cropped to square; stills from real screenings with audiences.
- Motion: trailer uses core Video with poster; captions slide in once on the film page only (transform, 200ms) and are static under reduced motion.
- Why it fits now: documentary producers present work with film-grammar typography rather than marketing layouts, as on [Field of Vision](https://fieldofvision.org/).
**Style variations:** Festival: #0E0F10 bg, #F2B705 bars · Classroom: #F4F3EF bg, #0B6E4F bars · Archive: #EDE6D8 bg, #7A2E1E bars.
**Real-world basis:** [Screenagers: Host a screening](https://www.screenagersmovie.com/host-a-screening), [Screenagers: Find a screening](https://www.screenagersmovie.com/find-a-screening), [The Social Dilemma: Take action](https://thesocialdilemma.com/take-action/), [The Social Dilemma: Host a screening](https://thesocialdilemma.com/the-film/virtual-tour/host-a-screening/), [Doc Society: Films](https://docsociety.org/films/)
**Refs:**
- [Screenagers: Host a screening](https://www.screenagersmovie.com/host-a-screening): licence types, host materials and steps from enquiry to event.
- [The Social Dilemma: Take action](https://thesocialdilemma.com/take-action/): actions and resources grouped by audience.
- [Doc Society: Films](https://docsociety.org/films/): how a large catalogue of impact films is filtered by theme, region and year.

<a id="298"></a>
#### 298 · Crowdfunded Product Pre-order Campaign (`backer`)
**For:** small hardware and object makers running their own pre-order campaign (or continuing one after Kickstarter / Crowd Supply) who need a campaign page, production updates and order status.
**Templates:** front-page (campaign) · single-product (pre-order) · archive-update (production log) · single-update · page-specs · page-faq · page-shipping · page-order-status · page-press
**Patterns (~40):** campaign header (raised vs goal, backers, days left or "now in stock"), pre-order product options with price and shipping per region, estimated ship date per item or batch, production updates log (date, stage, photos), spec table, comparison table against alternatives, open-source files link, FAQ, sizing guide, order status lookup link, shipping and returns policy, press quotes.
**Content model:** Woo products (backorders allowed, "ships from" date meta); `update` CPT (date, stage taxonomy: design / tooling / mass production / shipping); `campaign` options (goal, raised, backers) bound to a progress block.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce.
**Signature:** a production updates log that moves the campaign through named stages (prototype, testing, mass production, shipping) with dated posts, and each post says which batches ship when and what buyers must do now (seen on: [Pebble: Index 01 is in mass production](https://repebble.com/blog/index-01-is-in-mass-production), [Crowd Supply: Haasoscope Pro](https://www.crowdsupply.com/andy-haas/haasoscope-pro)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- "Raised $97,708 of $50,000 · 68 backers" block that becomes "In stock, ships in 3 business days" after the campaign (seen on: [Crowd Supply: Haasoscope Pro](https://www.crowdsupply.com/andy-haas/haasoscope-pro))
- Per-item ship dates when pre-order and in-stock items mix in one basket
- Sizing warning and "recheck your size, no exchanges" note before the order locks (seen on: [Pebble: Index 01 is in mass production](https://repebble.com/blog/index-01-is-in-mass-production))
- Comparison table against named alternatives, plus a link to design files for open hardware (seen on: [Crowd Supply: Haasoscope Pro](https://www.crowdsupply.com/andy-haas/haasoscope-pro))
- Product schema.org with `availability: PreOrder` and a shipping-by-country table

**Style: Engineering spec-sheet / tactile skeuo 2.0**
- Type: headings Aldrich 400 at 40–80px; body Karla 400/17px; specs, part numbers and dates JetBrains Mono 500/14px.
- Palette: bg #ECEBE7 (powder-coat grey) / text #151515 / signal orange #FF5F00 / surface #FFFFFF / line #B8B6B0 / status green #2E8540 (only where a real status exists).
- Layout: spec sheets as two-column tables with 1px rules; the campaign page has a progress rail showing the real stages with the current one filled; product renders sit on flat grey plinths with real soft contact shadows. Buttons look physical: 1px darker bottom edge, pressed state on click.
- Imagery: studio product photos on a grey paper backdrop, 1:1 and 4:3; factory and PCB photos in production updates, unedited.
- Motion: progress rail fills to the current stage once on load; buttons depress 1px; nothing else.
- Why it fits now: makers lean on product-manual and spec-sheet aesthetics to signal that the object is real and engineered, as on [teenage engineering](https://teenage.engineering/).
**Style variations:** Lab: #ECEBE7 bg, #FF5F00 · Anodised: #1E2124 bg, #D6D6D1 text, #3DA5D9 · Beige box: #E8E1D3 bg, #151515, #C0392B.
**Real-world basis:** [Crowd Supply: Haasoscope Pro](https://www.crowdsupply.com/andy-haas/haasoscope-pro), [Pebble: Index 01 is in mass production](https://repebble.com/blog/index-01-is-in-mass-production), [Flipper Zero: product page](https://flipper.net/products/flipper-zero), [Playdate](https://play.date/)
**Refs:**
- [Crowd Supply: Haasoscope Pro](https://www.crowdsupply.com/andy-haas/haasoscope-pro): funding block, options with shipping, ship dates, updates and comparison table.
- [Pebble: Index 01 is in mass production](https://repebble.com/blog/index-01-is-in-mass-production): a production update that tells buyers exactly what happens next.

<a id="299"></a>
#### 299 · One-Product Brand Store (`single`)
**For:** companies that sell one main object (a device, a tool, a bag, a lamp) plus a few accessories, and want a long product page instead of a catalogue.
**Templates:** front-page (the product) · single-product · page-specs · page-accessories · page-faq · page-support · page-shipping-returns · page-press · Woo cart · Woo checkout
**Patterns (~35):** product hero with price, colour and "ships in 3–5 business days", use-case sections, "in the box" list, spec table (dimensions, weight, battery, materials), accessories row, FAQ (returns, warranty, where we ship), support and manuals, press quotes as short attributed lines, editions or colourways, out-of-stock state with notify-me.
**Content model:** one Woo variable product (colour, edition) plus accessory products; spec rows as product meta bound to a table pattern; FAQ as Details blocks.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce.
**Signature:** one long product page that runs from the object to the full spec table to "what's in the box", with price, availability and shipping time repeated at the bottom next to accessories (seen on: [Analogue: Pocket](https://www.analogue.co/pocket), [Playdate](https://play.date/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- "Ships in 3–5 business days" stated beside the price and repeated in the FAQ (seen on: [Daylight: Product](https://daylightcomputer.com/product))
- FAQ covering returns, warranty, where we ship and the EU withdrawal policy (seen on: [Daylight: FAQ](https://daylightcomputer.com/faq))
- "In the box" list including the cable and user guide, and what comes free after purchase (seen on: [Playdate](https://play.date/))
- Out-of-stock button that turns into "notify me" with the next batch month
- Downloadable manual PDF and a size comparison photo against a hand or an A4 sheet

**Style: Museum object-label minimal**
- Type: headings Sarabun 600 at 32–64px; body Sarabun 400/17px; object labels (name, material, dimensions, year) in Newsreader 400 italic 15px, set like a museum caption.
- Palette: bg #F7F7F5 / text #121212 / accent: the product's own colour (for example #F2C500 for a yellow device) used only on the buy button / surface #FFFFFF / line #D6D6D2.
- Layout: the product shown as an exhibit: large image on a plain plinth, a caption label to one side with materials and dimensions, lots of empty wall. Spec table follows as a single long label. No feature-card grids; each section is one image and one paragraph.
- Imagery: object photographed from three fixed angles on the same background, plus one in-hand photo; 4:5 and 1:1.
- Motion: colourway switch swaps the image with a View Transition; nothing on scroll.
- Why it fits now: one-object brands borrow museum display conventions to make a product feel considered, as in collection pages like the [V&A: Explore the collections](https://www.vam.ac.uk/collections).
**Style variations:** Gallery: #F7F7F5 bg, product colour on button · Plinth: #E6E3DC bg, #121212 · Vitrine: #151618 bg, #F2F2EF text.
**Real-world basis:** [Analogue: Pocket](https://www.analogue.co/pocket), [Playdate](https://play.date/), [Daylight: Product](https://daylightcomputer.com/product), [Daylight: FAQ](https://daylightcomputer.com/faq)
**Refs:**
- [Analogue: Pocket](https://www.analogue.co/pocket): a single long page from hero to spec table to accessories and stock state.
- [Playdate](https://play.date/): one product, one page, with price, what is included and specs in plain words.
- [Daylight: Product](https://daylightcomputer.com/product): use-cases, full spec panel and shipping time next to the object.

<a id="300"></a>
#### 300 · Pop-up Shop / Temporary Retail (`popup`)
**For:** makers, brands and collectives running a shop for a fixed run (a weekend to three months) in a rented space, market hall or container park.
**Templates:** front-page (the run) · page-visit (address, hours, access) · archive-trader or page-line-up · single-trader · page-events · page-press · page-after (what happens when it closes) · page-contact
**Patterns (~30):** run dates banner ("Open 1–24 December"), daily opening hours, address with photo of the shopfront, map, step-free access note, line-up of makers or traders with a photo and link each, events during the run (launch night, workshops), what's in stock this week, card-only / cash note, "last days" state, after-the-run links to the online shop, press contact.
**Content model:** `run` options (start, end, hours per day, address) bound to header and banner; `trader` CPT (name, what they sell, photo, URL, days present); `event` CPT (date, time, RSVP).
**Plugins:** Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap, Jetpack Forms (RSVPs), WooCommerce optional for click-and-collect.
**Signature:** a traders or makers line-up page where each seller has a photo, what they sell and a link, so visitors know who is in the shop before they come (seen on: [Pop Brixton: Traders](https://www.popbrixton.org/traders)), with a run-dates banner that counts down "last 3 days" and then switches to "Closed. Thanks for coming" after the end date.
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Opening hours and check-in/out times per day, plus accessibility of the space (step-free, toilets) stated up front (seen on: [Appear Here: Kingsland Road, Dalston](https://www.appearhere.co.uk/spaces/kingsland-road-dalston-the-raw-glass-shop))
- What's on during the run as a simple dated list (seen on: [Pop Brixton: What's on](https://www.popbrixton.org/whatson))
- A "how we ran it" page and press kit after the run, following the pop-up guides format (seen on: [Appear Here: Guides](https://www.appearhere.co.uk/inspire/guides))
- Card-only / cash-welcome note, and "which maker is in on which day" for shared shops
- After closing, the site redirects the home page to an online shop pattern automatically

**Style: Hand-painted shop-window sign**
- Type: headings Rampart One 400 on the run dates only, Alfa Slab One 400 for other headings; body Figtree 400/17px; prices and hours Figtree 600.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #111111 / sign red #D62828 / gold leaf #C99A2E (text only on dark) / window green #1F4D3A / line #111111.
- Layout: the run banner is a shop-window strip at the top of every page, full width, dates painted large; the line-up is a two-column list like a shop directory board. Home: dates and hours, shopfront photo, line-up.
- Imagery: shopfront and interior photos taken straight on, 3:2; product shots by each trader kept in their own style; no lifestyle stock.
- Motion: the "last 3 days" banner swaps text on the day, no animation. Nothing else moves.
- Why it fits now: sign-writing and shopfront lettering have a strong revival among small retailers who want to look local, as documented by [Ghostsigns](https://ghostsigns.co.uk/).
**Style variations:** Signwriter: #FFFFFF bg, #D62828 and #1F4D3A · Market hall: #F1ECE2 bg, #1F4D3A · Late opening: #111111 bg, #C99A2E text.
**Real-world basis:** [Pop Brixton: Traders](https://www.popbrixton.org/traders), [Pop Brixton: What's on](https://www.popbrixton.org/whatson), [Appear Here: Kingsland Road, Dalston](https://www.appearhere.co.uk/spaces/kingsland-road-dalston-the-raw-glass-shop), [Appear Here: Guides](https://www.appearhere.co.uk/inspire/guides)
**Refs:**
- [Pop Brixton: Traders](https://www.popbrixton.org/traders): a trader directory where each stall gets its own page.
- [Appear Here: Kingsland Road, Dalston](https://www.appearhere.co.uk/spaces/kingsland-road-dalston-the-raw-glass-shop): the facts a temporary shop has to publish (size, hours, access, use).
- [Appear Here: Guides](https://www.appearhere.co.uk/inspire/guides): the stages of a pop-up (space, design, PR, running, measuring) that the page set follows.

<a id="301"></a>
#### 301 · Online Exhibition / Virtual Show (`onlineshow`)
**For:** curators, artist-run spaces and collectives that stage exhibitions online (net art, video, digital work) with an opening date, a run, artist pages and a statement.
**Templates:** front-page (current show) · archive-exhibition · single-exhibition · single-work (gate page) · page-artists · page-open-call · page-about · page-archive
**Patterns (~30):** exhibition header (title, dates, curator), curatorial statement, gate page for each work (artist, title, year, statement, "enter the work" link), artist list, works list with medium and year, opening event and livestream time, open call with dates (deadline, notification, programme announced, run), pavilion or partner list, archive by year, credits and colophon.
**Content model:** `exhibition` CPT (start, end, curator, statement); `work` CPT (artist, year, medium, external URL, `exhibition_id`); `artist` taxonomy.
**Plugins:** Advanced Query Loop (current, upcoming and past shows), Jetpack Forms (open call).
**Signature:** a gate page for each work: the artist's name, title, date and a short statement on a quiet page, with one link that leaves the site to enter the work itself (seen on: [Whitney Museum: artport](https://whitney.org/artport), which ran Gate Pages from 2001 to 2006).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Open call timeline with deadline, notification date, programme announcement and run dates (seen on: [The Wrong Biennale](https://thewrong.org/))
- Exhibition history by year with venue and link, online and offline mixed (seen on: [Rafaël Rozendaal: Exhibitions](https://www.newrafael.com/exhibitions))
- Opening time shown in the visitor's own time zone
- Browser and device notes per work ("best on desktop, sound on"), and a captured video fallback for works that break
- Image descriptions for every work, written with the artist

**Style: White-cube gallery minimal**
- Type: headings Lineal (Velvetyne) Regular at 28–48px; body Lineal Regular/17px (one family, Regular and Bold only, with the second voice coming from IBM Plex Mono 400 for dates and credits).
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #0A0A0A / caption grey #5B5B5B (passes AA on white) / line #E5E5E5 / accent: none.
- Layout: lots of white; one work per screen; captions bottom-left like wall labels; the exhibition index is a simple list with dates on the right. Nav is four words in the top-left corner.
- Imagery: screenshots and captures of works at native aspect ratio on white, never mocked up in browser frames.
- Motion: none. The only interaction is entering the work.
- Why it fits now: online exhibition platforms are settling on quiet gallery layouts that let digital work carry the page, as on [Feral File: Exhibitions](https://feralfile.com/exhibitions).
**Style variations:** White cube: #FFFFFF bg · Screening room: #0A0A0A bg, #F2F2F2 text · Project space: #EFEDE8 bg, #0A0A0A text.
**Real-world basis:** [Whitney Museum: artport](https://whitney.org/artport), [The Wrong Biennale](https://thewrong.org/), [Feral File: Exhibitions](https://feralfile.com/exhibitions), [Rafaël Rozendaal: Exhibitions](https://www.newrafael.com/exhibitions), [Olia Lialina: GRAVITY](https://art.teleportacia.org/exhibition/GRAVITY/)
**Refs:**
- [Whitney Museum: artport](https://whitney.org/artport): the gate page format and an archive of commissioned online works.
- [The Wrong Biennale](https://thewrong.org/): an online biennale made of independently organised pavilions with a public timeline.

<a id="302"></a>
#### 302 · Net-Art: the website is the artwork (`netart`)
**For:** artists who make websites as artworks, often one work per domain, and need a home that indexes the works, records collectors and exhibitions, and stays online for decades.
**Templates:** front-page · page-works (index of domains) · page-exhibitions · page-texts · page-info · page-editions (how to collect) · 404 (made as a work)
**Patterns (~20):** works index (title, domain, year), exhibitions list by year, texts and interviews, contact and gallery representation, collector credit line, how collecting a website works (the contract), plain navigation, animated GIF thumbnails, "back / next" links between sections.
**Content model:** `work` CPT (domain, year, collector name, collector visibility flag, status: live / archived / offline); `exhibition` CPT (year, venue, city, URL).
**Plugins:** none.
**Signature:** collector credit in the work itself: each site-artwork carries its owner's name in the page title ("collection of ..."), and the artist's index records which works are held by whom (seen on: [muchbetterthanthis.com](https://muchbetterthanthis.com/), whose browser title names its collectors, and [Rafaël Rozendaal: Internet](https://www.newrafael.com/internet)). The theme's `work` template writes the collector field into the document title and colophon.
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Works index with each work at its own domain and year (seen on: [Rafaël Rozendaal: Internet](https://www.newrafael.com/internet))
- Chronological list back to the first work, with small GIFs as the only images (seen on: [Olia Lialina: art.teleportacia.org](https://art.teleportacia.org/))
- A plain "How to collect a website" page with the sales terms and domain renewal responsibilities
- Status flags for works that are archived or need an old browser, with a captured video
- A colophon on every page listing the date made and the last date checked working

**Style: Dither / 1-bit bitmap (net-art raw)**
- Type: DotGothic16 400 for everything at 16px and 32px; headings are the same face at 2x; no second family, the bitmap face is the idea.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #000000 / link #0000FF / visited #800080 / selection #FFFF00.
- Layout: one column, no max-width on the index (it runs the full window like an early directory listing); works listed as text lines. Pixel borders (1px solid black) only around embedded captures.
- Imagery: every image dithered to 1-bit (Floyd–Steinberg) at build time with the companion image filter, which also keeps page weight tiny.
- Motion: none by default; artists can embed their own. The theme adds nothing that moves.
- Why it fits now: dithered 1-bit images and tiny pages are a live aesthetic and an energy argument at the same time, as on [Low-tech Magazine (solar)](https://solar.lowtechmagazine.com/).
**Style variations:** Paper white: #FFFFFF bg, #000000 · Newsprint: #EDEBE6 bg, #111111 text, #0000FF links · Desktop: #008080 bg, #FFFFFF windows.
**Real-world basis:** [Rafaël Rozendaal: Internet](https://www.newrafael.com/internet), [muchbetterthanthis.com](https://muchbetterthanthis.com/), [Olia Lialina: art.teleportacia.org](https://art.teleportacia.org/), [JODI](https://jodi.org/), [Windows93](https://www.windows93.net/)
**Refs:**
- [Rafaël Rozendaal: Internet](https://www.newrafael.com/internet): an index of websites-as-artworks, each at its own domain, with years.
- [Olia Lialina: art.teleportacia.org](https://art.teleportacia.org/): a plain HTML home for decades of net art, listed by year.
