<a id="303"></a>
#### 303 · Manifesto / Single-Page Statement (`manifesto`)
**For:** collectives, movements and practitioners who publish a short statement of principles that people cite, translate and sign.
**Templates:** front-page (the text) · page-principles (expanded) · page-signatories · page-translations · single-translation · page-history · page-about-the-authors · page-print (poster version)
**Patterns (~20):** the statement itself, numbered theses or principles (only where the numbering is real), permalink anchor per principle, expanded principle page with background and examples, signatories list with date, translations list by language, history of the text, authors, licence line ("may be freely copied in any form, but only in its entirety"), print and PDF versions, last edited date.
**Content model:** principles as pages with `order` meta; translations with Polylang or as child pages with `lang` meta; `signatory` CPT (name, affiliation, date, approved flag).
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (signing), Polylang (only if translations are maintained in-site).
**Signature:** a translations index listing the text in every language it has been translated into, each a full page, plus a short licence line that lets anyone copy it whole (seen on: [Manifesto for Agile Software Development](https://agilemanifesto.org/), with 70+ translations).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Permalink anchors on every principle so people can cite one line (seen on: [Brutalist Web Design](https://brutalist-web.design/))
- Each principle expanded on its own section with background and practical examples, plus a "last edited" date (seen on: [Permacomputing: Principles](https://permacomputing.net/principles/))
- Download as ASCII, PDF and HTML, with a Creative Commons licence (seen on: [The Cluetrain Manifesto](https://www.cluetrain.com/))
- Signatory list with moderation, sorted by date signed
- An A2 poster PDF set in the site's own type for printing and pasting

**Style: Protest-poster condensed type**
- Type: statement in Mohave 700 at 8–14vw, uppercase only for the title; principles in Public Sans 800 at 32–48px; supporting text Public Sans 400/19px.
- Palette: bg #F2EFE8 (poster stock) / text #111111 / accent #E3120B (one red block per page) / surface #FFFFFF / line #111111.
- Layout: the statement fills the first screen and wraps hard at word boundaries; principles follow as full-width bands, each with its permalink shown as text. No images. Nav hidden behind a text link "Principles / Sign / Translations".
- Imagery: none, apart from the poster PDF preview.
- Motion: none. The page must print well on A4 and A2.
- Why it fits now: condensed, poster-scale type is the common voice of current climate and civic campaigns, as on [Extinction Rebellion](https://rebellion.global/).
**Style variations:** Fly-post: #F2EFE8 bg, #E3120B block · Stencil: #FFFFFF bg, #111111 only · Night march: #111111 bg, #F2EFE8 text, #FFCC00 block.
**Real-world basis:** [Manifesto for Agile Software Development](https://agilemanifesto.org/), [Brutalist Web Design](https://brutalist-web.design/), [Permacomputing: Principles](https://permacomputing.net/principles/), [The Cluetrain Manifesto](https://www.cluetrain.com/), [EFF: A Declaration of the Independence of Cyberspace](https://www.eff.org/cyberspace-independence)
**Refs:**
- [Manifesto for Agile Software Development](https://agilemanifesto.org/): statement, signatories, principles and a long list of translations.
- [Brutalist Web Design](https://brutalist-web.design/): principles listed first with permalinks, then explained.
- [Permacomputing: Principles](https://permacomputing.net/principles/): each principle with context, actions and examples, openly edited.

<a id="304"></a>
#### 304 · Protest / Direct-Action Toolkit (`toolkit`)
**For:** legal support groups, trainers and campaign networks that publish know-your-rights guides, printable cards and tactic libraries for people going to protests.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-guide · single-guide · page-bustcard · archive-tactic (toolbox) · single-tactic · page-training (events) · page-translations · page-about · page-donate
**Patterns (~35):** printable card (single and 4-up), key advice list, what to do if stopped / searched / arrested, solicitor numbers by region, support line number in large type, guides by topic (facilitation, consensus, direct action), tactic cards by type (tactic, principle, theory, story), training dates, legal observer explainer, translations, anti-copyright licence note, last reviewed date.
**Content model:** `guide` CPT (topic, region, last reviewed, PDF); `tactic` CPT (type taxonomy: tactic / principle / theory / story / methodology); `card` CPT (region, language, PDF single, PDF 4-up).
**Plugins:** Query Filter (tactics by type), Advanced Query Loop (upcoming trainings).
**Signature:** a printable bust card: a pocket-size PDF in single and 4-per-page layouts, per region and in several languages, with key advice, arrest rights and solicitor numbers, plus "write the support line on your arm" (seen on: [Green and Black Cross: Bustcard](https://greenandblackcross.org/guides/bustcard/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A "print info as PDF" button and a Spanish version on every rights page (seen on: [ACLU: Protesters' rights](https://www.aclu.org/know-your-rights/protesters-rights))
- Toolbox of tactics, principles, theories and stories as filterable cards (seen on: [Beautiful Trouble: Toolbox](https://beautifultrouble.org/toolbox))
- Guides in PDF, audio and video, with an anti-copyright note that invites translation (seen on: [Seeds for Change: Resources](https://www.seedsforchange.org.uk/resources))
- "Last reviewed" date on every legal guide, with a banner when a law changes
- Plain-language summary box at the top of each guide, and a quick-exit link

**Style: Printable samizdat pamphlet (monospace)**
- Type: Inconsolata 400/17px for body and 700 for headings; the support line number in Inconsolata 800 at 48px; secondary voice Literata 400 italic for pull quotes from guides.
- Palette: bg #FFFFFF / text #000000 / accent #FFE600 (highlighter behind the one number that matters) / surface #F2F2F2 / line #000000.
- Layout: A5-proportioned pages centred on desktop with visible crop marks on print; every guide is one column, 64ch. Cards shown at real pocket size with a "print 4-up" button. Home: support line number, then "Before / During / After arrest".
- Imagery: none by default; diagrams drawn as simple line illustrations where they explain a process.
- Motion: none. Print CSS is the primary design target: black on white, no backgrounds.
- Why it fits now: small, fast, printable pages matter when networks are unreliable, and the permacomputing and low-tech scene has made that look intentional, as on [Permacomputing: Principles](https://permacomputing.net/principles/).
**Style variations:** Photocopy: #FFFFFF bg, #000000 · Highlighter: #FFFFFF bg, #FFE600 marks · Street: #111111 bg, #F2F2F2 text (screen only).
**Real-world basis:** [Green and Black Cross: Bustcard](https://greenandblackcross.org/guides/bustcard/), [Green and Black Cross: What is a legal observer?](https://greenandblackcross.org/guides/what-is-a-legal-observer/), [Beautiful Trouble: Toolbox](https://beautifultrouble.org/toolbox), [Seeds for Change: Resources](https://www.seedsforchange.org.uk/resources), [ACLU: Protesters' rights](https://www.aclu.org/know-your-rights/protesters-rights)
**Refs:**
- [Green and Black Cross: Bustcard](https://greenandblackcross.org/guides/bustcard/): regional printable cards in several languages, single and 4-up.
- [Beautiful Trouble: Toolbox](https://beautifultrouble.org/toolbox): a card library of tactics and principles with type filters.
- [Seeds for Change: Resources](https://www.seedsforchange.org.uk/resources): short guides by topic in several formats under an anti-copyright licence.

<a id="305"></a>
#### 305 · Countdown / Launch Event Microsite (`countdown`)
**For:** campaigns and organisations whose site is built around one clock or deadline (a climate deadline, an annual setting, a launch date) that people embed, quote and gather around.
**Templates:** front-page (the clock) · page-the-deadline (the science or reason) · page-use-the-clock (embeds, assets) · page-get-a-clock (physical clocks) · archive-statement (by year) · single-statement · page-press · page-faq
**Patterns (~25):** the live countdown (years, days, hours, minutes, seconds), what the number means in one paragraph with its source, secondary "lifeline" numbers, embeddable widget code, press and social assets, photography and video tips for actions, physical clock options (portable, exhibition, monumental), annual statement with date and PDF, timeline of past settings, FAQ, press contact.
**Content model:** `deadline` option (target datetime or rate model, source citation); `statement` CPT (year, setting, date announced, PDF); `setting` timeline as a repeater bound to a timeline pattern.
**Plugins:** none (the clock is a companion Interactivity API block rendered on the server with the current value, then ticking in the browser).
**Signature:** a free embeddable version of the clock with press templates and assets, so schools, newsrooms and campaigners put the same number on their own sites and screens (seen on: [Climate Clock: Use the clock](https://www.climateclock.world/use-the-clock) and [Get a clock](https://www.climateclock.world/get-a-clock)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- A page explaining exactly how the number is calculated and where the data comes from (seen on: [Climate Clock: One deadline](https://www.climateclock.world/one-deadline))
- Annual statement with a print/PDF version and a timeline of every previous setting (seen on: [Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists: 2026 Doomsday Clock statement](https://thebulletin.org/doomsday-clock/2026-statement/))
- The clock value rendered server-side so it reads correctly without JavaScript and in screen readers (as text, updated with `aria-live="off"`)
- OG image generated with the current value for sharing
- For launches: the page swaps itself to the "it's here" state at the target time without a redeploy

**Style: Split-flap departure board**
- Type: clock digits in Handjet 900 (OFL, a modular element-grid display face) at 10–18vw, tabular; headings Handjet 600; body Barlow 400/18px.
- Palette: bg #141414 (board black, only behind the clock) and #F4F2EC for reading pages / digits #F5F5F0 / accent #FFB400 (board amber for labels) / surface #262626 / line #3A3A3A.
- Layout: the clock occupies the first screen in a single row of flap cells with unit labels under each; the explanation sits directly below on a light page, one column, 66ch. Nav: The number · Use it · Statements · Press.
- Imagery: photographs of the clock in public places (on buildings, in classrooms), 16:9, credited.
- Motion: each flap cell flips when its digit changes (a 3D rotateX on the top half, 180ms). Under reduced motion the digits change without animation. No pulsing.
- Why it fits now: split-flap boards are a recognisable, calm way to show live numbers in public, which is why they are being revived as products, as on [Vestaboard](https://www.vestaboard.com/).
**Style variations:** Terminal: #141414 board, #FFB400 labels · Platform: #F4F2EC bg, #141414 board · Station: #0B3D91 board, #FFFFFF digits, #FFD100 labels.
**Real-world basis:** [Climate Clock: One deadline](https://www.climateclock.world/one-deadline), [Climate Clock: Use the clock](https://www.climateclock.world/use-the-clock), [Climate Clock: Get a clock](https://www.climateclock.world/get-a-clock), [Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists: 2026 Doomsday Clock statement](https://thebulletin.org/doomsday-clock/2026-statement/)
**Refs:**
- [Climate Clock: Use the clock](https://www.climateclock.world/use-the-clock): templates, assets and guides that turn one number into a shared tool.
- [Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists: 2026 Doomsday Clock statement](https://thebulletin.org/doomsday-clock/2026-statement/): annual setting, full statement, PDF and history of settings.

<a id="306"></a>
#### 306 · Community Cookbook Fundraiser (`cookbook`)
**For:** schools, churches, clubs, food charities and community kitchens collecting recipes from members to print and sell a cookbook for a cause.
**Templates:** front-page · page-submit-a-recipe · archive-recipe (online preview) · single-recipe · page-buy (pre-order) · page-sponsors (local business ads) · page-contributors · page-about-the-cause · page-events (launch, sales)
**Patterns (~35):** recipe submission form (name, recipe title, serves, ingredients, method, story, section), submission deadline, chapter dividers (Starters, Soups, Mains, Baking, Preserves, Drinks), recipe with "from the kitchen of" contributor credit, "in memory of" dedication page, pre-order with collection or post, price and "every copy raises £X", local business sponsor ads by size (booster line, eighth, quarter, half, full page), launch event, sales tally, recipe calendar alternative, where to buy locally.
**Content model:** `recipe` CPT (contributor, section taxonomy, serves, times, ingredients, method, story, in-print flag); `sponsor` CPT (business, ad size, artwork); Woo product for the book.
**Plugins:** Jetpack Forms (recipe submissions, sponsor ads), WooCommerce (pre-orders, local pickup).
**Signature:** an online recipe collection page where members submit their recipes into the book before a deadline, with contributor names kept on every recipe, followed by pre-orders so the print run is known before printing (seen on: [CreateMyCookbook: Fundraiser cookbooks](https://www.createmycookbook.com/inspiration/fundraiser)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Local business ad packages sold by page fraction to cover printing (seen on: [Fundcraft: Merchant advertising](https://fundcraft.com/fundraising-cookbooks/1-merchant-advertising.asp))
- Chapter divider tabs that match the printed book's sections (seen on: [Fundcraft: Divider tabs](https://fundcraft.com/fundraising-cookbooks/divider-tabs-publishing-cookbooks.asp))
- "100% of profits go to the kitchen" statement beside the buy button, plus a recipe calendar as a smaller product (seen on: [Refugee Community Kitchen: Shop](https://refugeecommunitykitchen.org/shop))
- Recipe schema.org on the online preview recipes, and allergen tags on each
- Printable A5 recipe-submission form for people who don't use email, with a drop-off address

**Style: Spiral-bound church-cookbook typewriter**
- Type: recipe titles Patua One 400 at 32–48px; body Courier Prime 400/17px (the typed-up recipe card voice); chapter headings Fraunces 900 at soft optical size, used only on divider pages.
- Palette: bg #FFFEF9 / text #1F1A17 / divider colours: tomato #D8412F, mustard #E1A626, bean green #5C8A3A, sky #3E7CB1 (one per chapter, as the printed tabs) / line #1F1A17.
- Layout: each chapter opens with a coloured divider tab on the right edge (a fixed vertical strip); recipes are single-column cards with "from the kitchen of" at the bottom. Home: the cause, the price, the deadline for recipes or the pre-order button, then chapter tabs.
- Imagery: real contributors' kitchen photos and hand-written recipe cards scanned as-is; food shot from above on the actual table it was cooked for, 1:1.
- Motion: none. The online preview prints cleanly, one recipe per page.
- Why it fits now: community cookbooks are having a revival as heritage and fundraising objects, and the look people remember is the typed, tabbed, spiral-bound book printed by firms like [Fundcraft: Cookbook covers](https://fundcraft.com/fundraising-cookbooks/covers-cookbooks.asp).
**Style variations:** Church hall: #FFFEF9 bg, four tab colours · School fete: #FFFFFF bg, #E1A626 and #3E7CB1 · Community kitchen: #F4F1EB bg, #D8412F and #1F1A17.
**Real-world basis:** [CreateMyCookbook: Fundraiser cookbooks](https://www.createmycookbook.com/inspiration/fundraiser), [Fundcraft: Merchant advertising](https://fundcraft.com/fundraising-cookbooks/1-merchant-advertising.asp), [Fundcraft: Divider tabs](https://fundcraft.com/fundraising-cookbooks/divider-tabs-publishing-cookbooks.asp), [Refugee Community Kitchen: Shop](https://refugeecommunitykitchen.org/shop), [Refugee Community Kitchen: Recipes](https://refugeecommunitykitchen.org/recipes)
**Refs:**
- [CreateMyCookbook: Fundraiser cookbooks](https://www.createmycookbook.com/inspiration/fundraiser): online recipe collection from contributors plus pre-orders.
- [Fundcraft: Merchant advertising](https://fundcraft.com/fundraising-cookbooks/1-merchant-advertising.asp): how local ads pay for the print run, by ad size.
- [Refugee Community Kitchen: Shop](https://refugeecommunitykitchen.org/shop): a recipe calendar and merch where every profit goes to the kitchen.

<a id="307"></a>
#### 307 · Dialect / Minority Language Archive (`dialect`)
**For:** dialect societies, minority-language centres and community archives that collect words, recordings and texts, publish a word of the week and keep a journal index.
**Templates:** front-page · archive-word · single-word (entry) · archive-recording · single-recording · page-listen (by area) · archive-article · page-journal-index · page-learn · page-join · page-events
**Patterns (~40):** word of the week (date, word, short definition, illustration), dictionary entry (headword, pronunciation in IPA, part of speech, definition, citations with source and year, area), recordings grouped by area (title, author, reader, audio), transcript beside audio, place-name notes, journal index by decade, learning resources, membership, events with iCal, shop for CDs and books, submit a word or recording form.
**Content model:** `word` CPT (IPA, part of speech, definition, citations repeater, area taxonomy, illustration); `recording` CPT (author, reader, area, audio file, transcript, year recorded); `area` taxonomy for regions or ridings.
**Plugins:** Query Filter (words and recordings by area), Jetpack Forms (submissions), Polylang (only if the site runs in the language and English).
**Signature:** a listening page that groups dialect recordings by historic area, each with its title, the author and the named reader, because "there is no substitute for hearing authentic voices" (seen on: [Yorkshire Dialect Society: Listen](https://www.yorkshiredialectsociety.org.uk/yorkshire-dialect/listen/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Word of the week archive in reverse date order, each with an illustration and a one-line meaning (seen on: [Dictionaries of the Scots Language: Scots Word of the Week](https://www.dsl.ac.uk/our-publications/scots-word-of-the-week/))
- Searchable index of the society's journal back to its first issue (seen on: [Yorkshire Dialect Society: Transactions index](https://www.yorkshiredialectsociety.org.uk/transactions-introduction-index/))
- "Submit a video / submit a resource" routes for community contributions (seen on: [Wikitongues: Archive](https://wikitongues.org/archive/))
- Events list with an iCal feed for members
- Plain-language explanation of the language's status ("is it a language or a dialect?") and consent notes for recordings

**Style: Scholarly dictionary / philological**
- Type: headwords Gentium Book Plus 700 at 40–64px; body Gentium Book Plus 400/18px; IPA and diacritics in Charis SIL (full phonetic coverage); labels (n., v., area) in Charis SIL small caps.
- Palette: bg #FBF9F4 / text #1A1A1A / accent #2F5D50 (bookbinding green, used for headwords and links) / surface #F0EDE4 / line #CFC9BA.
- Layout: dictionary two-column layout on desktop (entries left, citations right), one column on phones; hanging indents on citations; letter index A–Z sticky at the side. Home: word of the week in large type, then "Listen" and "Search the words".
- Imagery: illustrations commissioned for words (line art), black-and-white photos of speakers with consent, maps of the area in two colours.
- Motion: audio play buttons show progress along the transcript (Interactivity API highlights the current line); no other animation.
- Why it fits now: language archives are moving away from database screens to readable, citation-first pages, as on [Dictionaries of the Scots Language](https://dsl.ac.uk/).
**Style variations:** Glossary: #FBF9F4 bg, #2F5D50 · Field notebook: #F3EEDF bg, #6B3E26 · Reading room: #1D1F1E bg, #EDE8DC text.
**Real-world basis:** [Yorkshire Dialect Society: Listen](https://www.yorkshiredialectsociety.org.uk/yorkshire-dialect/listen/), [Dictionaries of the Scots Language: Scots Word of the Week](https://www.dsl.ac.uk/our-publications/scots-word-of-the-week/), [Yorkshire Dialect Society: Transactions index](https://www.yorkshiredialectsociety.org.uk/transactions-introduction-index/), [Wikitongues: Archive](https://wikitongues.org/archive/), [Scots Language Centre: Articles](https://www.scotslanguage.com/articles)
**Refs:**
- [Yorkshire Dialect Society: Listen](https://www.yorkshiredialectsociety.org.uk/yorkshire-dialect/listen/): recordings grouped by area with author and reader named.
- [Dictionaries of the Scots Language: Scots Word of the Week](https://www.dsl.ac.uk/our-publications/scots-word-of-the-week/): a dated word series with illustrations.
- [Wikitongues: Archive](https://wikitongues.org/archive/): language search and open community submissions.

<a id="308"></a>
#### 308 · Time Bank / Local Currency (`timebank`)
**For:** local time banks (one hour given = one hour received) and local paper or digital currencies that need to explain the system, sign people up and list where it can be used.
**Templates:** front-page · page-how-it-works · page-join · page-directory (offers or businesses) · single-listing · page-exchange-points · page-find-your-nearest · page-safeguarding · page-newsletter · page-faq
**Patterns (~35):** how it works in three sentences ("For every hour given, you earn an hour"), examples of real exchanges, directory of offers and requests or of businesses that accept the currency by category and town, exchange points (banks, shops) with hours, notes and denominations, exchange rate and cash-back fee, find-your-nearest search by postcode and radius, safeguarding and DBS guidance, member statement explainer, newsletter archive, printable directory PDF.
**Content model:** `listing` CPT (type: offer / request / business, category taxonomy, town taxonomy, contact method, accepted flag); `exchange_point` CPT (address, hours, lat/long); member accounts stay in the time bank's existing software (hOurworld, TimeOnline) and are linked, not rebuilt.
**Plugins:** Query Filter (category and town), Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap (exchange points and directory map), Jetpack Forms (joining).
**Signature:** a directory of everywhere the currency (or time credit) can be spent, organised by category (food, farms, services, arts) and town, with a downloadable PDF of the printed directory (seen on: [BerkShares: Directory](https://berkshares.org/directory/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Find-your-nearest search by postcode with a radius and a map or text list, and "choose one within a couple of miles" advice (seen on: [Timebanking UK: Find your nearest time bank](https://timebanking.org/find-your-nearest-time-bank/))
- How-to-use page: 1:1 rate, where to exchange, the fee to change back, note denominations and "no coins, change comes in dollars" (seen on: [BerkShares: Using BerkShares](https://berkshares.org/using-berkshares/))
- Safeguarding and DBS guidance page for coordinators (seen on: [Timebanking UK: How it works](https://timebanking.org/howitworks/))
- Offers and requests search and printable member statements via the linked time bank software (seen on: [hOurworld: Time and Talents](https://hourworld.org/_TimeAndTalents.htm))
- Easy-read version of "how it works" and a phone number for people who don't use the internet

**Style: Banknote engraving / guilloche**
- Type: headings Luxurious Roman 400 at 40–72px; body Source Serif 4 400/18px; denominations and figures Luxurious Roman 400 with lining figures; small print Source Serif 4 italic 14px.
- Palette: bg #F4F6F1 (note paper, faint green) / text #1B2A24 / note green #2E6B4F / note brown #7A4B2A / surface #E6EBE3 / line #2E6B4F.
- Layout: each page framed by a thin guilloche border (SVG pattern drawn once, used as a border only, never as a background texture); the directory is a dense two-column list with category heads like a printed trade directory. Home: "One hour = one hour" or "B$1 = $1" in the largest type, then join and directory.
- Imagery: portraits of real members or local businesses rendered in an engraving-style line filter; photos of the notes themselves.
- Motion: none.
- Why it fits now: local and community money projects lean on the trust signals of engraved banknotes and printed directories, as on [BerkShares: Using BerkShares](https://berkshares.org/using-berkshares/).
**Style variations:** Green note: #F4F6F1 bg, #2E6B4F · Brown note: #F6F1EA bg, #7A4B2A · Blue note: #F1F4F7 bg, #28527A.
**Real-world basis:** [BerkShares: Directory](https://berkshares.org/directory/), [BerkShares: Using BerkShares](https://berkshares.org/using-berkshares/), [Timebanking UK: How it works](https://timebanking.org/howitworks/), [Timebanking UK: Find your nearest time bank](https://timebanking.org/find-your-nearest-time-bank/), [hOurworld: Time and Talents](https://hourworld.org/_TimeAndTalents.htm)
**Refs:**
- [BerkShares: Directory](https://berkshares.org/directory/): accepting businesses by category and town with a printed-directory PDF.
- [Timebanking UK: How it works](https://timebanking.org/howitworks/): the hour-for-an-hour idea explained with real exchange examples.
- [Timebanking UK: Find your nearest time bank](https://timebanking.org/find-your-nearest-time-bank/): postcode and radius search with a map or list.

#### 309 · Community-Supported Shares: bakery or brewery (`shares`)
**For:** co-operative bakeries and breweries that raise money from their community (community shares, bonds or pre-paid "shares" of bread or beer) and then keep those members involved.
**Templates:** front-page · page-invest (share or bond offer) · page-offer-document · page-faq · page-subscribe (bread or beer share) · page-members · page-about-the-co-op · page-find-us · page-news
**Patterns (~35):** offer block (target, stretch target, raised to date, minimum and maximum, interest, term), offer document PDF, risk statement, "what is a co-operative" explainer, one member one vote note, subscription share (weekly loaf or monthly box, commitment length, discount), loyalty stamp card, member updates, AGM date, where your money goes (ovens, fermenters, fit-out), opening hours and market days, wholesale.
**Content model:** `offer` CPT (target, raised, minimum, maximum, interest, closes, PDF, status: open / closed / oversubscribed) bound to a progress block; subscriptions as Woo subscription products; `update` posts for members.
**Plugins:** WooCommerce, Subscriptions for WooCommerce, Jetpack Forms (expressions of interest in the share offer).
**Signature:** an investment page with the target, the amount raised so far, the terms and the offer document as a PDF, so the community can see progress and read the small print in one place (seen on: [Stirchley Co-operative Development: Invest](https://www.stirchley.coop/invest/), the building co-op that houses Loaf bakery).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Subscription with discounts that grow with commitment (5% for 2 months, 10% for 6, 15% for 12) and pause or cancel after the minimum (seen on: [Stroud Brewery: Subscribe and save](https://stroudbrewery.com/pages/subscribe-save))
- Stamp-card loyalty that lives in the phone wallet, ten stamps for a free drink or loaf (seen on: [Stroud Brewery: Loyalty programme](https://stroudbrewery.com/pages/stroud-brewery-loyalty-programme))
- "We are a workers' co-operative: all permanent staff are directors" statement on the About page (seen on: [Loaf: About](https://loaf.coop/about/))
- Closed-offer archive showing each raise's target and final percentage (seen on: [Ethex: Investments](https://www.ethex.org.uk/investments))
- Risk statement and "this is not a savings account" wording beside every invest button, and an AGM date banner for members

**Style: Co-op share-certificate ledger**
- Type: headings Cinzel 600 at 40–64px; body Public Sans 400/18px; figures, share numbers and amounts IBM Plex Mono 500 in ledger columns.
- Palette: bg #FAF8F2 (ledger paper) / text #1D1D1B / ledger red #B3261E (rule lines and totals only) / ledger blue #2B5F8A (column rules) / surface #EFEBE0 / line #2B5F8A.
- Layout: the offer page is laid out like a ledger: date / description / amount columns with red double rules under totals; the raised-to-date number is the biggest thing on the page. A certificate-style border frames the offer summary only. Home: today's bread or beer, then the offer progress.
- Imagery: photos of the bakery or brewhouse at work, 3:2, early light; members' photos at the AGM; no piles-of-coins stock.
- Motion: none. The progress figure is text, updated from the offer meta.
- Why it fits now: co-ops and community-owned businesses want the look of a well-kept ledger rather than a startup pitch, as on this listing of closed raises at [Ethex: Investments](https://www.ethex.org.uk/investments).
**Style variations:** Ledger: #FAF8F2 bg, #B3261E and #2B5F8A · Flour: #FFFFFF bg, #1D1D1B, #C28E2B · Cellar: #1E1B18 bg, #EFE7D6 text, #C28E2B.
**Real-world basis:** [Stirchley Co-operative Development: Invest](https://www.stirchley.coop/invest/), [Loaf: About](https://loaf.coop/about/), [Stroud Brewery: Subscribe and save](https://stroudbrewery.com/pages/subscribe-save), [Stroud Brewery: Loyalty programme](https://stroudbrewery.com/pages/stroud-brewery-loyalty-programme), [Ethex: Investments](https://www.ethex.org.uk/investments)
**Refs:**
- [Stirchley Co-operative Development: Invest](https://www.stirchley.coop/invest/): target, raised to date, terms and offer PDF on one page.
- [Stroud Brewery: Subscribe and save](https://stroudbrewery.com/pages/subscribe-save): commitment-based discount tiers for a beer share.
- [Ethex: Investments](https://www.ethex.org.uk/investments): how community share and bond offers show target and percentage raised.

#### 310 · Street Tree Map / Guerrilla Gardening (`streettree`)
**For:** street tree action groups, tree-sponsorship schemes and guerrilla gardeners who map trees and beds, log digs and defend or plant trees street by street.
**Templates:** front-page (map) · archive-tree · single-tree · page-sponsor-a-tree · archive-dig (log) · single-dig · page-join-a-group · page-campaign · page-foi (documents) · page-how-to
**Patterns (~35):** tree map with species and status, tree page (species, street, age, status: saved / felled / threatened / planted, photos, story), notable trees list, sponsor-a-street-tree steps (check your council, choose a spot, council checks, planting next winter), dig log (date, place, plants, who came, before and after photos), join your local group by area, petitions, FOI documents list, campaign leaflets to print, how-to (seed bombs, tree pit planting), events.
**Content model:** `tree` CPT (species taxonomy, street, lat/long, planted year, status, photos); `dig` CPT (date, location, plants list, participants count); `group` CPT (area, contact).
**Plugins:** Out of the Block: OpenStreetMap, Query Filter (status and species), Jetpack Forms (sponsorship requests, group sign-up).
**Signature:** a notable trees page and map where each tree has its species, street, age, story and a status that campaigners update (saved, felled, threatened), turning a map into a record of the fight (seen on: [Sheffield Tree Action Groups: Notable trees](https://savesheffieldtrees.org.uk/notable-trees/)).
**Nice-to-haves:**
- Sponsor-a-street-tree steps with which councils take part and "planting happens the following winter" (seen on: [Trees for Cities: Trees for Streets](https://www.treesforcities.org/our-work/trees-for-streets))
- Dated dig log with before and after photos and the plants used (seen on: [Guerrilla Gardening: Blog](http://www.guerrillagardening.org/ggblog.html))
- "Join your local tree group" list by area with contacts (seen on: [STAG: Join your local tree group](https://savesheffieldtrees.org.uk/join-your-local-tree-group/))
- Printable campaign leaflet and street-by-street letter template
- Watering-season banner ("new trees need 50 litres a week, June to September") that appears and disappears on set dates

**Style: Botanical field-guide cartography**
- Type: headings Mate 400, 40–64px (one display voice); body Libre Franklin 400/17px; species names in Mate italic; map labels and coordinates IBM Plex Mono 400/12px.
- Palette: bg #F3F1E8 / text #1F2A1F / leaf green #3F6B3A / bark brown #6B4F36 / felled red #B23A2E (status only, always with a text label) / line #A9B29C.
- Layout: map-first home with a side list of notable trees; tree pages set like a field-guide plate: species name large, a botanical line drawing or photo, a facts column (planted, girth, street, status). Dig log as a dated diary list.
- Imagery: tree portraits shot from across the street in full leaf and bare, 4:5; before and after photos of the same framing; line drawings of leaves for species.
- Motion: map markers highlight when the matching list item is hovered (Interactivity API); no scroll effects.
- Why it fits now: map-led, species-first community mapping is how people now find and care for city trees, as on [Falling Fruit: Map](https://fallingfruit.org/map).
**Style variations:** Summer canopy: #F3F1E8 bg, #3F6B3A · Autumn: #F5EEE3 bg, #B5652B · Winter branches: #EDEFF0 bg, #3B4A55.
**Real-world basis:** [Sheffield Tree Action Groups: Notable trees](https://savesheffieldtrees.org.uk/notable-trees/), [STAG: Join your local tree group](https://savesheffieldtrees.org.uk/join-your-local-tree-group/), [Trees for Cities: Trees for Streets](https://www.treesforcities.org/our-work/trees-for-streets), [Guerrilla Gardening: Blog](http://www.guerrillagardening.org/ggblog.html), [Falling Fruit: Map](https://fallingfruit.org/map)
**Refs:**
- [Sheffield Tree Action Groups: Notable trees](https://savesheffieldtrees.org.uk/notable-trees/): individual trees with species, age, story and saved or felled status.
- [Trees for Cities: Trees for Streets](https://www.treesforcities.org/our-work/trees-for-streets): a three-step sponsorship process residents can follow.
- [Guerrilla Gardening: Blog](http://www.guerrillagardening.org/ggblog.html): dated troop digs with photos of real sites.

## Part 5: Shared companion blocks (from the nice-to-haves)

The 310 ideas list 1,574 nice-to-haves between them. The same small touches keep coming back across unrelated trades: a plumber and a bakery both need a "closed for the holidays" bar, and a tattoo studio and a therapist both need "books open / closed". Building each one once, in the `wp-oss-companion` plugin, gives every theme these features at no extra cost and keeps the themes free of functionality code (which the WordPress.org rules require anyway).

Counts are how many nice-to-haves across the 310 ideas each block would cover, from a keyword pass over every Nice-to-haves list. They are approximate, and there is overlap between rows.

| Block | Covers | Count | How it works |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Printable view** | printable menus, price lists, CVs, programmes, care sheets, PDFs | 156 | Print stylesheet per template plus a "Print / Save as PDF" button. No PDF library: the browser does it. |
| **Access info** | step-free access, BSL and captioned sessions, relaxed performances, sensory-friendly hours | 66 | Structured fields (step-free, toilet, hearing loop, quiet hours) rendered as a plain list, with schema.org `accessibilityFeature`. |
| **Customer / community wall** | customer photos, member galleries, "happy tails" | 60 | Query Loop over a `submission` type with moderation, fed by a Jetpack Form with file upload. |
| **Scheduled notice** | holiday closures, announcements, sale notices | 54 | Group block with start and end dates; server-side render skips it outside the window, so no flash of stale content. |
| **FAQ per item** | product and service FAQs | 52 | Core Details blocks in a pattern plus FAQPage schema. |
| **Find us** | directions, parking, bus stops, photo directions | 43 | Pattern: address, OpenStreetMap block, numbered photo steps, transport lines. |
| **Gift options** | gift cards, vouchers, gift notes | 35 | WooCommerce gift note field on checkout and a voucher product pattern. |
| **Credentials row** | registration numbers, insurance, licences | 34 | Repeater of name + number + verify link (e.g. Gas Safe, BACP, Ofsted) rendered as text, not badge images. |
| **Policies** | deposits, cancellations, returns in one paragraph | 28 | Bindable fields shown on booking and product templates. |
| **Aftercare / first visit** | aftercare guides, "what to expect" | 28 | Numbered steps pattern with a printable view. |
| **Stockists / map** | stockists, locations, murals | 28 | `place` type + OpenStreetMap + Query Filter by region. |
| **Structured data** | LocalBusiness, Product, Event, Recipe, Course | 24 | One schema generator reading the same fields the blocks use. |
| **Availability state** | commissions, books, new clients, places, waitlist | 22 | One toggle (open / closed / waitlist) in Site Editor settings. Any block can bind to it, e.g. to swap a form for a waitlist line. |
| **Price list** | rate cards, fee tables, service menus | 19 | Table pattern with tabular figures and a printable view. |
| **Cut-off banner** | "Order by 15 Dec for Christmas", per-region dates | 18 | Scheduled notice with a list of region + date rows; hides each row after its date. |
| **Stock state** | sold out, low stock, back in stock, "N left" | 14 | Woo stock status bound to labels, with honest "Sold out" kept visible. |
| **Lead time** | "booking 3 days ahead", turnaround | 14 | One editable field, shown in header or near forms. |
| **Local units** | cm/in, currency note, time zones for livestreams | 14 | Interactivity API toggle stored in localStorage. |
| **Open now** | hours today, open/closed now | 14 | Hours table with holiday exceptions; the "open now" label is computed in the browser in the site's time zone. |

Nine of these (scheduled notice, cut-off banner, availability state, lead time, open now, stock state, local units, printable view, credentials row) cover roughly a third of all nice-to-haves. **Build those first.**

## Part 6: How the library fits together

### Structure
- **Standalone block themes**, one per idea, as Automattic ships them. No parent-child chain, so each can be submitted to WordPress.org on its own.
- **One companion plugin** (`wp-oss-companion`): opt-in content types (Work, Project, Exhibition, Event, Release, Episode, Book, Place, Person, Listing…), the shared blocks above, Block Bindings sources, and schema. Themes check for it and degrade gracefully without it.
- **A shared pattern source**, maintained in the monorepo and copied into each theme at build time, not loaded at runtime. It covers roughly 40% of each theme's patterns: FAQ, find us, price list, policies, credentials, legal pages. Each theme restyles them through its own `theme.json`, so shared structure never means shared look.
- **Monorepo**: `/themes/<slug>`, `/companion`, `/shared-patterns`, `/research`, `/tools`.

### Release gates (CI)
Every theme must pass all of these before release:
1. `copylint` (see `ANTI-AI-WRITING.md`): zero severity-5 findings in patterns, templates, demo content and readme.
2. Anti-vibe lint (see `ANTI-VIBE.md` and the field study): banned fonts, banned hex ranges near Tailwind indigo/violet, gradient text, one global radius, banned section order.
3. **Font registry check** (`FONT-REGISTRY.md`): the display font is unique across the library.
4. The 53-question sniff test, answered in the theme's README by a person.
5. WordPress Theme Check plus the theme review requirements (no functionality in themes, escaping, i18n).
6. Accessibility: axe on every template, keyboard pass, 4.5:1 contrast on every surface token pair, `prefers-reduced-motion` honoured.
7. Performance: no render-blocking web fonts over 2 families, images lazy-loaded, LCP under 2.5s on the demo.
8. Screenshot diff of the demo against the style brief (catches accidental default styling).

### Per-theme build steps
1. Claim a display font in `FONT-REGISTRY.md`.
2. Fill in `docs/voice.md` (the voice sheet in `ANTI-AI-WRITING.md`, section 6).
3. Study the Real-world basis sites and screenshots in `research/screenshots/`.
4. Build `theme.json` tokens from the Style block, then the templates, then the patterns.
5. Write demo content in the owner's voice, then run copylint.
6. Run the release gates.

## Part 7: Suggested first wave (20 themes)

Chosen to cover the widest spread of sectors, plugins and companion blocks early, so the shared layer gets tested by very different businesses before scaling up.

| # | Idea | Why in the first wave |
|---|---|---|
| 001 | Illustrator: portfolio + shop | The founding example; WooCommerce, originals with RESERVED state, cut-off banner |
| 016 | Architecture studio | Index/table views, Query Filter, the most typographic of the set |
| 022 | UX designer case studies | Pattern overrides for case-study blocks |
| 038 | Band / solo musician | Events via Advanced Query Loop, EPK, embeds |
| 053 | Hyperlocal news | Editorial layouts, donations, heavy Query Loop use |
| 059 | Coffee roaster | Subscriptions, product attributes, filters |
| 066 | Bakery pre-order | Pickup dates, cut-off timer, allergen matrix |
| 083 | Neighbourhood restaurant | Menu patterns, printable view, open now |
| 091 | Guesthouse / B&B | Booking plugin, rooms, find us |
| 097 | Plumber & heating engineer | Trades pattern set: credentials row, lead time, quote form with photos |
| 111 | Therapist / counsellor | Availability state, calm style, crisis footer |
| 113 | Independent dental practice | Health and trust patterns, access info |
| 119 | Yoga studio | Timetable, class booking |
| 141 | Forest school | Education: term dates, inspection report, parent pages |
| 151 | Indie SaaS | Tests the anti-vibe rules where they are most at risk |
| 168 | Food bank / community pantry | Civic: plain-language, multilingual, "what we need this week" |
| 173 | Amateur football club | Fixtures and results, league tables |
| 205 | Wedding (couple's site) | RSVP, countdown, personal voice |
| 219 | Small museum | Heritage: collections, visit info, accessibility |
| 233 | Niche job board | Directory/board mechanics and front-end submissions |

Once these 20 ship, the shared blocks and patterns will have been used by a shop, a restaurant, a tradesperson, a clinic, a school, a club, a charity, a newsroom, a museum and a person. The next 290 are mostly new content models and new styles on top of a proven base.

## Open follow-ups

- **Web search budget.** The session hit its 200-search cap partway through the research. Later batches found sites by following links from verified sites, so some ideas rest on fewer or larger reference sites than intended (noted per batch). Raising `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION` and re-running a grounding pass on the thinner entries (pets 245–248, handyman 108, reunion 210, cookbook fundraiser 306) would help.
- **Repeated style direction names.** A few direction names were copied from the spec's examples and appear up to five times ("Warm Scandi minimal", "Soft neo-brutalism"). The briefs underneath differ, but the names should be made unique when each theme is built.
- **Shared accent colours.** 171 unique accents across 201 parsed palettes. `#C8102E` appears seven times. With unique display fonts no two themes share the font + accent + radius combination, but a colour registry alongside the font registry is worth adding.
- **Warm off-white grounds.** The field study found warm off-white + serif heading is now the most common AI-built look. The 310 ideas were checked: Fraunces (018) and Cormorant (019) were replaced, and the four ideas pairing a warm off-white ground with a serif display face (002, 032, 119, 223) were moved to cooler grounds. 57 ideas still use a warm off-white background with a sans or slab display face. That is fine on its own, but each should have a reason in the brief (paper stock, plaster, stone), not a default.
- **Fonts.** `FONT-REGISTRY.md` gives every idea a unique display family (310 of 310, checked by family, not only by name; 213 ideas were reassigned). Before building, look at specimens for the 17 Fontshare faces picked by category tag (listed in the registry notes), and reconsider the weaker fits (146 Press Start 2P, 206 Yanone Kaffeesatz, 175 BenchNine, 298 Aldrich). Another theme's display face still appears as a body or label face in 86 places; that is allowed, but should be reduced where a theme's look depends on it.
- **Screenshots.** A few reference pages sit behind bot checks or age gates. Those captures are marked as blocked in `screenshots/manifest.json` and left out of this document.
